results.title: ISIA Intelligenza artificiale generativa come nuovo modello di servizio pubblico alle imprese
results.proposal: ISIA Intelligenza artificiale generativa come nuovo modello di servizio pubblico alle imprese. The Irpinia Sannio Chamber of Commerce carries out its functions in a territory that clearly illustrates a challenge common to much of Europe. Almost ninety thousand businesses, predominantly micro and small enterprises, are distributed across two provinces characterised by a high proportion of inland areas and served by only two Chamber of Commerce offices. For many of these businesses, access to a public service has never been a question of whether the service is available, but rather of compatibility: between office opening hours and working hours, between the institutional office and the distance separating it from the municipality where the business is located, and between the language of administrative procedures and that of those who must navigate them without qualified intermediaries. The proposed solution addresses this gap. ISIA is the organisation’s virtual assistant, operational since 29 May 2025 and migrated to a generative artificial intelligence-based architecture in May 2026, representing the first such case within the Italian Chamber of Commerce system. It queries the institutional knowledge base to provide contextualised answers, guides users through access to the eight active Online Services, and enables appointments to be booked directly: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=pbVtQO1rWyA. What distinguishes the case, however, is not the technology adopted, which is widely available, but the decision to use it to adapt the administration to the user rather than requiring the user to adapt to the administration. First and foremost, this concerns language: following the migration to generative AI, requests asking users to rephrase their questions fell from 4.0% to 0.3% of messages, providing a measure of how significantly the terminology barrier has been reduced. It also concerns time: more than half of interactions take place outside public opening hours, and during evening and night-time hours the assistant is not merely an alternative channel but the only one available. Finally, it concerns channels: no function can be accessed through only one route, ensuring that users who are unable to use one channel are not excluded from the service. Human support has not been removed, but rather repositioned towards higher-value activities. Artificial intelligence is placed at the entry point of a four-level service pathway that always ultimately leads to a person: from independent access to information to assisted conversation, from online transactions to an interview with an operator, either in person or via video call, including document exchange and payments. Content remains under the responsibility of the competent offices; the system provides information and guidance without adopting administrative decisions, while responsibility for the administrative procedure remains with a natural person. By diverting from the service desk those requests that can be resolved upstream, automation has made operators more available for cases that genuinely require human expertise, while also making them accessible without requiring users to travel. The institutionally decisive step took place on 27 July 2026: through an administrative order issued by the Secretary-General, access to the five services involving the highest level of direct interaction was made subject to appointment booking, which can be completed either through the website or directly through a conversation with the virtual assistant, complemented by a remote service desk via videoconference. The virtual assistant does not simply operate alongside the service desk: it orchestrates access to the different service channels while ensuring that human support remains available at all times: https://www.irpiniasannio.camcom.it/notizie/nuova-modalita-accesso-agli-sportelli-prenotazione. The project forms part of “Le Camere del Futuro” (“The Chambers of the Future”), a national programme promoted by Unioncamere for the digital transformation of the Chamber of Commerce system. Irpinia Sannio is the first Chamber to integrate generative artificial intelligence into this framework: what has been implemented is therefore not an isolated experiment, but a prototype embedded within an architecture already shared by all Italian Chambers of Commerce. Alongside this transformation, the organisation has implemented a structured capacity-building programme targeting both its own staff and businesses operating in the territory, based on the principle that public technology that nobody knows how to use cannot generate public value. The solution was designed in accordance with the European and national accessibility framework: Directive (EU) 2016/2102 on the accessibility of the websites and mobile applications of public sector bodies; the harmonised EN 301 549 standard incorporating WCAG 2.1 Level AA criteria; and the relevant Italian implementing legislation (Law No 4/2004, as amended by Legislative Decree No 106/2018), together with the AgID Guidelines on the Accessibility of ICT Tools. The new institutional website, launched as part of the project, is built on the reference model for Italian public administration websites, which incorporates accessibility requirements into its navigation structure, colour contrasts and markup semantics. The organisation publishes its accessibility statement in accordance with the AgID model and maintains an active feedback mechanism through which users can report accessibility difficulties. Accessibility, however, has been interpreted more broadly than technical compliance alone, because the divide affecting businesses in this territory is not solely related to sensory accessibility. **Channel redundancy.** No function is accessible through only one route. An appointment can be booked through the website, in conversation with the virtual assistant, or at the reception desk, which schedules the first available appointment for anyone arriving without a prior booking. Information about an administrative requirement is available as a structured information sheet that can be browsed by category or keyword, as a conversational response, or through a discussion with an operator. Users who are unable to use one channel are therefore not excluded from the service. **Cognitive and linguistic accessibility.** The assistant responds in natural language to questions formulated in natural language, without requiring users to know administrative terminology. The reduction in requests for users to rephrase their questions from 4.0% to 0.3% of messages, measured following the technological upgrade, indicates the extent to which this barrier has been lowered: it is the administration that adapts to the user’s language, rather than the other way around. **Physical and temporal accessibility.** The remote service desk via videoconference, including document exchange and online payments, enables users to access Chamber of Commerce services without travelling. This is particularly relevant for people with reduced mobility and for businesses located in inland municipalities far from the two physical offices. More than half of interactions with the assistant take place outside public opening hours: service availability is therefore no longer dependent on compatibility between office opening hours and entrepreneurs’ working schedules. **Economic accessibility.** All components — the virtual assistant, specialist support, online services and the training programme — are provided to users free of charge. Accessibility is also one of the topics covered by the training programme offered to businesses, through a dedicated corporate case study. Accessibility is therefore not only a requirement applied to the service itself, but also knowledge transferred to the local business community. The solution was not acquired through a procurement procedure to which the EU standard contractual clauses would have been applicable. By means of a managerial decision dated 7 February 2025, the Irpinia Sannio Chamber of Commerce joined “Le Camere del Futuro”, the national programme promoted by Unioncamere for the digital transformation of the Italian Chamber of Commerce system. The solution is developed and operated by InfoCamere, an in-house company owned by the Chambers of Commerce, within the service relationship connecting the infrastructure operator with the entire Chamber system. Consequently, there was no competitive procurement procedure for acquiring an artificial intelligence system from an external supplier; rather, the Chamber joined a system configuration that had already been designed and made available to participating Chambers. Nevertheless, the safeguards that the model contractual clauses are intended to ensure are addressed through other mechanisms. The operator is a publicly owned entity controlled by the contracting administrations and subject to their equivalent control: data, infrastructure and service continuity therefore remain within the public-sector perimeter. Ownership of and responsibility for information content remain with the competent Chamber offices. Traceability of system use is ensured through structured reporting covering the entire period of operation, which is available for audit and internal control purposes. The quality of responses is subject to systematic assessment, with documented results. The system performs an information and guidance function and does not adopt administrative decisions: responsibility for the administrative procedure remains with a natural person, as required by Italian rules governing the use of artificial intelligence within public administration. The organisation nevertheless considers the EU standard contractual clauses to be a useful reference and intends to examine them in connection with future developments of the solution, including as a framework for verifying the safeguards already in place within its relationship with the infrastructure operator. **Technology Partner:** InfoCamere S.C.p.A., the in-house company of the Italian Chamber of Commerce system. **Scientific Partners:** Societing Lab — an action-research programme of the University of Naples Federico II; Giustino Fortunato Telematic University (e-learning platform and issuance of Open Badges).

results.company: Università degli Studi di Urbino Carlo Bo
results.title: Memento — auditable AI-assisted drafting of administrative documentation
results.proposal: Memento — auditable AI-assisted drafting of administrative documentation. A method for producing and reviewing complex administrative documentation with AI: vendor-neutral, at near-zero marginal cost, placing human-model collaboration inside a Git-versioned workflow that is traceable, reproducible and adoptable with tools an administration already owns. Four written registers, including a deterministic archive of the interactions, keep the work portable across people, offices and models. Applied twice by the university's administrative offices, to a technical manual required by national guidelines and to an internal regulation: about 1,370 pages of sources analysed, some 214,000 words produced, 13 effective working days, against the months of expert work a comparable document had previously required. Beyond drafting, the model reviews: examining the whole corpus it surfaced coverage gaps that human review had missed. Human validation and editorial responsibility remain with the officers. Published in full in English and Italian under CC BY 4.0.

results.proposal: Marche Region’s AI Use Cases related to public procurement, implemented within the projects: “#REG4IA - AI Hubs for PAs”, “ERDF 1.2.2.1 Advanced AI Solutions for public services”, “TrasparenzAI”. Marche Region uses AI to streamline administrative procedures through three converging public-procurement initiatives. Under the nationally funded interregional project #Reg4IA, Marche runs a PoC using generative and ontology-based AI to assist contracting officers with tender-idcode requests, compliance checklists, drafting of contracts and payment decrees, and timeline planning, under strict human-in-the-loop oversight. This builds on Marche's own AI platform (AIMA, ERDF 2021-27, measure 1.2.2.1), offering customised agent-automation tools and innovative features - including contextual know-how enrichment - reusable in multi-tenant mode by other PAs. Lastly, under an ANAC-CNR protocol and an agreement now being signed with ANAC, the "TrasparenzAI" project will test AI web-scraping to verify public-contract data PAs must publish in the "Transparent Administration" and "Public Customer's Profile" website sections, standardising data collection and strengthening transparency nationwide.

results.title: IRIS Navarra: Turning Frontier Technologies into a Shared Public Resource for Regional Innovation
results.proposal: IRIS Navarra: Turning Frontier Technologies into a Shared Public Resource for Regional Innovation. IRIS Navarra is a regional public innovation ecosystem promoted by the Government of Navarra and formally supported by a collaboration agreement involving 40 leading public and private organisations. Recognised as a European Digital Innovation Hub since 2023, IRIS has evolved into a permanent regional capability backed by €13 million in public investment. It gives companies and public organisations access to more than 220 services, 104 regional technology providers and advanced experimentation facilities in AI, supercomputing, synthetic biology, genomics, IoT, robotics and advanced manufacturing. More than 3,000 companies have already benefited from the Polo, while over 200 have used IRIS Lab infrastructures. By reducing the cost and risk of experimentation, IRIS enables organisations to test before investing and increasingly positions Navarra as a real-world testbed for frontier technologies.

results.title: SIO: AI-enabled evidence infrastructure for Italy's Observatory on Artificial Intelligence and Labour
results.proposal: SIO: AI-enabled evidence infrastructure for Italy's Observatory on Artificial Intelligence and Labour. Evidence on artificial intelligence and work evolves rapidly and remains fragmented across public institutions, research bodies, firms, workers and social partners. SIO (Sistema Intelligente dell’Osservatorio, the Intelligent System of the Observatory) is the AI-enabled evidence infrastructure of Italy’s Observatory on Artificial Intelligence and Labour, established within the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies. It combines a curated, source-linked knowledge base, a public conversational interface and an adaptive consultation environment for the Observatory’s bodies. Its governed architecture separates orchestration from generation, applies differentiated access and keeps validation and institutional responsibility with the Ministry and the Observatory. SIO supports a more structured, comparable and traceable evidence-to-policy cycle and provides a transferable model for public institutions addressing fast-moving technological change.

results.title: The Semantic Intelligence Services
results.proposal: The Semantic Intelligence Services. The SIS project, developed by ISTAT with DXC Technology and Lutech, addresses the semantic gap in public sector interoperability. By integrating the transactional Piattaforma Digitale Nazionale Dati (PDND) and the authoritative National Data Catalog (schema.gov.it), SIS supports data providers, consumers, and governors by automating the verification and discovery of data meaning in API specifications and API-based exchanges to enhance ecosystem semantic quality. SIS deploys a collaborative Agent Crew orchestrated by a central Semantic Broker and supported by specialized agents like the Schema Assistant and API Catalog Assistant. These agents dynamically query technical API specifications and map fields onto standardized ontologies and vocabularies. The pilot demonstrates that public sector data can transition from machine-readable to machine-comprehensible, establishing the foundation for trust, automated semantic quality assurance, and seamless cross-border e-Government.

results.title: LExIA - AI-assisted regulatory screening for early detection of competition restrictions.
results.proposal: LExIA - AI-assisted regulatory screening for early detection of competition restrictions. LExIA (“Lectura Experta con IA”) is an AI-based internal solution developed by the CNMC to support early detection of public regulatory restrictions to competition in Spanish official gazettes. It addresses a high-volume, time-sensitive process: thousands of legal texts are published across multiple official sources and must be screened quickly when they may require competition advocacy or, ultimately, legal action. LExIA combines preliminary filters, key information extraction, preliminary assessment of restrictions, retrieval of CNMC precedents through Retrieval Augmented Generation –RAG–, legal analysis against related official sources, prioritisation and automatic generation of Word reports and e-mail alerts. The system runs on real regulatory publications and sends daily results and filtering statistics for expert review. It does not replace legal or economic judgement; it structures, documents and prioritises cases, enabling CNMC to identify cases to challenge in court and engage authorities to amend anti-competitive rules, and has already helped remove restrictive regulation.

results.title: Simple: A Semantic, Voice-Driven Procurement Intelligence and Training System for Auditing and Decision Support in Public Administration
results.proposal: Simple: A Semantic, Voice-Driven Procurement Intelligence and Training System for Auditing and Decision Support in Public Administration. Simple is a semantic, graph-based procurement intelligence system developed within a university-led public sector innovation context and currently in pilot phase. It integrates European (TED) and national (KIMDIS) procurement data into a unified knowledge graph aligned with the eProcurement Ontology (ePO), enabling large-scale audit and analysis across contracting authorities, time periods and CPV categories. The system supports automated generation of structured audit reports and provides multi-layer diagnosis of procurement markets (macro–meso–micro) through explainable indicators, enhancing audit, policy analysis and decision-making. It also incorporates legal knowledge into a graph-based reasoning framework, enabling structured interpretation within the regulatory context. A voice-driven interface allows non-technical users to interact naturally, while a human-supervised self-correction mechanism ensures continuous refinement and transparency. The solution improves efficiency, compliance and data-driven policymaking in public procurement.

results.company: Luxembourg Office of Accreditation and Surveillance (OLAS)
results.title: Legal and normative text analyser
results.proposal: Legal and normative text analyser. Accreditation bodies must work with complex and frequently updated legal, technical and normative materials, including national laws, EU law, international standards and accreditation requirements. The Legal and Normative Text Analyser supports the Luxembourg Office of Accreditation and Surveillance by automating parts of this documentation analysis. The operational challenge is that OLAS needs to identify, collect and interpret relevant documents from recognised sources such as Legilux, EUR-Lex, ISO, CEN, EA, ILAC and IAF, as well as locally stored files, in order to determine applicable requirements for the accreditation of specific activities. Manual review can be time-consuming and requires specialist knowledge across multiple sources and standards. The tool analyses reliable databases and local files, identifies relevant documents or information demonstrating compliance, extracts applicable requirements and generates detailed reports based on the results. At operational level, it functions as a regulatory and normative intelligence assistant for accreditation workflows. It helps staff move more quickly from a broad documentation search to a structured understanding of which requirements apply to a conformity assessment body or activity. The expected impact is faster accreditation preparation, more consistent identification of applicable requirements, reduced manual effort and improved traceability in the analysis of legal and normative sources. The initiative is relevant because it applies AI to a highly specialised compliance function where reliability, source quality and structured reporting are essential for institutional credibility and for the proper supervision of accredited activities.
results.memo: Proceed. Legal and normative text analyser is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Generative AI Assistant PARLA for the City of Berlin
results.proposal: Generative AI Assistant PARLA for the City of Berlin. Public administrations and political institutions generate thousands of documents, but finding the right information quickly across parliamentary papers, committee procedures, and written questions can be time-consuming for civil servants, journalists, associations, and citizens alike. In Berlin, PARLA was developed to make this documentary landscape more searchable and intelligible by supporting research across a large corpus of public documents. The objective is to reduce the effort involved in navigating administrative and parliamentary records, improve access to public information, and provide answer suggestions that remain traceable to their documentary sources. The implementation uses AI to search and synthesise information from more than 10,000 public documents, including answers to written parliamentary questions and main committee procedures, and presents results through a question-answer interface. The system generates proposed answers based on the underlying text and cites the documents used, while also warning users that generated responses are not legally binding and should be checked against the linked sources. At a conceptual level, PARLA combines retrieval, synthesis, and source referencing in one research assistant for public documentation. The impact includes quicker information retrieval, improved transparency through traceable sourcing, and better support for daily work in parliament and administration, while also making complex documentary repositories more usable for external stakeholders.

results.title: Deliberations @ Scale: Large-scale high-engagement citizen participation with generative AI
results.proposal: Deliberations @ Scale: Large-scale high-engagement citizen participation with generative AI. Municipal decision-making often struggles to engage large numbers of citizens in meaningful deliberation processes. The Common Ground mobile application, developed in Eindhoven through a consortium of start-ups and local institutions, aims to scale citizen consultations using digital facilitation. The platform integrates an automated moderation system that structures discussions, summarises viewpoints and prompts balanced exchanges among participants. Natural language processing models analyse contributions in real time, grouping similar arguments and identifying emerging themes. The application has been tested in three consultation processes, evaluating usability and engagement levels. By lowering participation barriers and structuring dialogue, the system supports inclusive and organised civic debate. Future plans include national expansion and integration of moderated consultations into formal decision-making workflows. The initiative demonstrates how digital facilitation tools can enhance democratic participation, increase transparency and strengthen evidence-based policymaking through large-scale, structured citizen input.
results.memo: Proceed. Deliberations @ Scale: Large-scale high-engagement citizen participation with generative AI is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Titormos - the citizens assist chatbot in the Municipality of Agrinio
results.proposal: Titormos - the citizens assist chatbot in the Municipality of Agrinio. Titormos addresses limited accessibility and inefficiencies in citizen engagement with municipal services, where requests could previously only be submitted via phone during restricted hours. This constrained responsiveness and excluded citizens with limited availability or access to traditional channels. The objective is to provide a more accessible, efficient, and inclusive interface for citizens to obtain information and submit service requests. The solution implements a conversational interface capable of handling structured requests and free-form queries, supported by natural language processing and integration with municipal service databases. It captures user inputs, generates request tickets, and provides confirmations, while also enabling future integration with administrative and HR systems for analytics and reporting. A voice-based interface extends accessibility to users without digital access. The impact includes improved accessibility, faster response times, and enhanced citizen satisfaction. It also enables better data collection, operational efficiency, and scalability of municipal services, supporting more responsive and data-informed governance.

results.proposal: Provinc.IA: a provincial AI governance and pilot framework for trustworthy, reusable and interoperable AI adoption in local governments. Provinc.IA is the Artificial Intelligence Strategy of the Provincial Council of Castellón, Spain. It provides a provincial governance and pilot framework to help small and medium-sized municipalities adopt AI in a trustworthy, legally sound, useful and reusable way. The case addresses a structural public sector challenge: many local governments lack the technical, organisational and legal capacity to deploy AI safely. Provinc.IA combines strategic planning, multi-level governance, stakeholder mapping, ethical and legal safeguards, pilot projects, monitoring mechanisms and capacity-building. Its aim is to make AI adoption feasible for local administrations with limited resources, while supporting better services, administrative innovation and evidence-informed policy-making across the province.

results.title: AppLI: AI-powered guidance and skills development for professional transitions
results.proposal: AppLI: AI-powered guidance and skills development for professional transitions. AppLI is a national public platform created by the Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies to support citizens in skills development and professional transitions. Integrated into Italy’s public ecosystem for employment, training and social inclusion, it uses multi-agent generative AI to transform needs expressed in natural language into personalised pathways for guidance, learning and professional preparation. AppLI helps users define goals, identify learning needs, access regional, digital and AI training opportunities, undertake microlearning, prepare and edit CVs and cover letters, and practise for interviews. Citizens access the service securely through Italy’s national digital identity schemes and interact through a conversational interface. Operational nationwide since September 2025, AppLI is free and voluntary and works alongside Public Employment Services, combining public governance, user control and continuous support for skills development.

results.proposal: ASTRA: unlocking Italy's major terrorism-related and criminal case files through AI. ASTRA is an AI-powered system developed by the Emilia-Romagna Region to enhance access to digitized judicial records relating to some of Italy’s most significant terrorism-related cases of the late 20th century, including the Bologna (1980) and Italicus Express (1974) massacres, and the crimes of the White Uno Gang. results.proposal: GovRadar – AI-assisted preparation of tender documents in North Rhine-Westphalia. North Rhine-Westphalia has established the first statewide digital standard for tender preparation in a large German federal state. The Ministry for Home Affairs, Local Government, Building and Digitalisation (MHKBD) concluded a framework contract with the Munich-based GovTech company GovRadar GmbH, opening access in April 2025 to all 427 municipalities and extending it in July 2025 to all state authorities, agencies, higher education institutions and state-owned undertakings. The cloud-based solution focuses on the content preparation phase of procurement rather than process administration. It supports the drafting of legally compliant technical specifications by generating text proposals from a continuously updated corpus of millions of existing German tender documents, provides semantic search and an AI assistant for targeted research, structures market data for digitalised market exploration across product categories, and guides the creation of contracts and standard documents without media discontinuity. By supporting product-neutral, unambiguous specifications, the tool reduces the scope for specifications tailored to a single supplier and improves the quality and comparability of bids. Authorities report time savings of up to 90% in the preparation of tender drafts. As of mid-2025, 166 municipalities had requested the municipal licence and 2,140 individual user licences had been issued.

results.company: Danish Competition and Consumer Authority (Konkurrence- og Forbrugerstyrelsen, KFST)
results.title: Bid Viewer – computational screening for bid rigging in public procurement
results.proposal: Bid Viewer – computational screening for bid rigging in public procurement. Bid rigging in public procurement is difficult to detect through conventional investigation, because collusive tenders are designed to appear competitive. The Danish Competition and Consumer Authority (KFST) developed Bid Viewer in-house to screen large volumes of tender data for signals of horizontal agreements between bidders. The tool computes a set of statistical indicators of non-competitive bidding behaviour — covering the number and pattern of tenders, the variance and distribution of bid prices, bid rotation and incumbency patterns — and feeds these indicators into machine learning screens that combine them into a single model. The models are trained and evaluated on tender data containing known cartel cases, and assign each tender a probability score reflecting its likelihood of collusion, allowing case handlers to prioritise the tenders most worth investigating. Artificial neural networks are used alongside the statistical screens to improve classification performance. Bid Viewer is used operationally by the Authority to support a range of investigations, specifically the identification of bid rigging. The tool has been developed in cooperation with the Spanish and Swedish competition authorities and has been transferred to counterpart authorities in other European countries, including the Estonian Competition Authority and the United Kingdom, making it a reference case for cross-border reuse of an anti-collusion analytics solution. Its public value lies in stronger enforcement capability, better allocation of scarce investigative resources, and protection of public spending against cartel overcharges.

results.title: REDOC - Digital Tutor to make easier learning the STEM subject
results.proposal: REDOC - Digital Tutor to make easier learning the STEM subject. REDOC, based on the Redooc learning platform, addresses the challenge of making mathematics and science education more engaging, accessible, and effective for students while also supporting teachers with structured digital resources. The problem it tackles is not only the difficulty many learners experience with STEM subjects, but also the need for educators to access exercises, explanations, simulations, and lesson materials in formats that are suitable for classroom and independent study. The stakeholders include students across different age groups, teachers, schools, families, and the start-up providing the service. The objective is to encourage learning through practice, motivation, and playful competition, helping students train their reasoning skills in a way comparable to regular physical exercise. The implementation uses a web-based educational platform combining video lessons, interactive exercises, tips, simulations, and game-like learning paths. Technology is applied through digital tutoring functions, adaptive content organisation, gamification mechanics, progress tracking, and online assessment features that allow learners to practise and receive structured feedback. Teachers can use the platform to complement classroom instruction, assign activities, and explain concepts through ready-made multimedia resources. The expected impact includes stronger learner engagement, greater continuity between school and home study, easier access to remedial materials, and improved support for teachers. By presenting STEM learning as an interactive and competitive experience, the platform can increase motivation and broaden participation in scientific and mathematical education.

results.title: Privacy-safe synthetic test data: AI-generated replicas of statistical microdata for software development and testing at Statistics Netherlands
results.proposal: Privacy-safe synthetic test data: AI-generated replicas of statistical microdata for software development and testing at Statistics Netherlands. Statistics Netherlands (CBS) builds and maintains the software pipelines that produce official statistics. New software is developed in an environment that is less strictly secured than production, so real microdata about citizens and businesses may not be used there. Dummy or rule-based test data cannot capture the complexity of the real data. Together with technology partner BlueGen, CBS generated a synthetic replica of a large, complex relational dataset using generative AI (a diffusion transformer) trained entirely inside CBS's secure, air-gapped environment. The synthetic data mirrors the structure, statistical patterns and business rules of the real microdata while containing no real records. It enabled a new statistical pipeline to be developed and tested on realistic data, surfaced real defects before production, and removed the risk of a data leak from the development environment. Resemblance and utility scores exceeded 85%; measured privacy risk was zero

results.title: INPS ISAC – Generative Artificial Intelligence applied to social security contribution compliance.
results.proposal: INPS ISAC – Generative Artificial Intelligence applied to social security contribution compliance. INPS, in agreement with the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies, the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF) and the National Labour Inspectorate (INL), has developed the Statistical Indicators of Contribution Reliability (Indicatori Statistici di Affidabilità Contributiva, known as ISAC) in order to promote preventive contribution compliance and to identify cases of under-declaration of employment, by means of indicators that compare tax and social security contribution data. The process provides for compliance letters to be sent to companies, setting out any deviations in the indicators, as determined by the Institute. Once the compliance letters have been sent, companies may justify and explain the deviations, including by attaching appropriate documentation, by submitting specific communications through the INPS channels. The generative AI component operates in the analysis of the communications submitted by companies: it analyses and assesses the replies and any attachments in line with the deviations determined by the Institute; it extracts the evidence provided by the company; it assigns the companies’ replies to specific clusters; it proposes an explainable justification of the analysis carried out and also prepares a draft reply to the company itself. INPS staff govern the entire process: they examine, modify, supplement and/or validate the output produced by the AI system, that is, they retain responsibility for the final decision in providing feedback to the company. The outcomes feed into monitoring, enabling continuous improvement of the system. The first application concerns the “Wholesale food trade” sector and the “Hotel and non-hotel accommodation facilities” sector, for a total of 35,491 companies analysed and 20,038 compliance letters sent. The solution improves consistency, timeliness and traceability and will be extended to six further production sectors, namely: - Bar, ice-cream parlour, pastry shop and confectionery production activities, for a total of 91,048 businesses; - Retail sale of medical and orthopaedic goods, for a total of 2,551 businesses; - Installation of electrical, plumbing and other building installations, for a total of 113,063 businesses; - Bespoke and mass production of clothing, accessories and household linen, and related processing, for a total of 17,543 businesses; - Hairdressing services, for a total of 38,794 businesses; - “Maintenance and repair of motor vehicles, motorcycles and mopeds”, for a total of 49,035 businesses. The legal entities affected will total 312,034, while approximately 176,000 letters will be sent. The proposed solution has been designed with features of flexibility and modularity that also allow it to be extended to further processes, promoting the standardisation of activities and the optimisation of the resources employed.

results.company: Italian Ministry of Labour and Social Policies (Ministero del Lavoro e delle Politiche Sociali)
results.title: Digital Supervisory Intelligence for Private Pension Schemes
results.proposal: Digital Supervisory Intelligence for Private Pension Schemes. The Ministry of Labour and Social Policies (MLPS) supervises pension and social security institutions, including private-law entities established under D.Lgs No. 509/1994 and No. 103/1996. Its responsibilities cover both legal-administrative and financial oversight, including the approval of resolutions on contributions, benefits, governance, and appointments; the review of budgets, financial statements, actuarial reports, and investment plans; the assessment of financial sustainability and regulatory compliance in cooperation with other authorities, including MEF and COVIP. These activities generate large volumes of documentation and complex procedures, while being managed by a limited number of officials. The resulting administrative burden has increased processing times and highlighted the need for advanced digital tools to improve efficiency, consistency, knowledge sharing, and decision-making. The platform represents the first integrated digital environment specifically designed to enhance, streamline, and accelerate the supervisory and monitoring activities carried out by the MLPS overseeing private pension schemes. The platform has been conceived to support the supervision of 20 private pension funds currently operating in Italy, providing a comprehensive digital environment for the analysis, management, and assessment of both financial and governance-related information. The system is structured around two integrated modules. 1. Document Management, Analysis, and Knowledge Discovery Module The first module is dedicated to the collection, storage, processing, indexing, and intelligent analysis of all documents periodically submitted by pension funds to their supervisory authority. Through a centralized and highly searchable repository, supervisory staff can rapidly retrieve relevant information, navigate large volumes of documentation, and perform cross-document analyses that would otherwise require significant manual effort. The platform manages a wide range of documents, including annual budgets, financial statements, actuarial balance sheets, investment plans, board resolutions, minutes, reports issued by the Board of Statutory Auditors, and other regulatory filings. Advanced indexing and semantic-search capabilities enable users to identify specific information within seconds, compare data across multiple reporting periods, and conduct in-depth analyses of financial, governance, and operational trends. The system also includes sophisticated analytical tools that allow supervisors to generate reports, perform data aggregations, visualize historical developments through comparative tables and time-series analyses, and monitor key indicators over extended periods. These functionalities significantly improve the efficiency and consistency of supervisory activities while reducing the operational burden on staff. A particularly valuable feature concerns the assessment of board resolutions submitted for approval. In addition to the resolutions themselves, the platform incorporates a comprehensive and constantly updated repository of applicable legislation, regulatory provisions, pension-fund statutes, internal regulations, and governance rules adopted by each scheme. By combining this legal and regulatory framework with the economic, financial, and actuarial information extracted from the funds' reports, the platform leverages advanced Artificial Intelligence algorithms to support supervisory decision-making. Users can interact with the AI engine either through predefined prompts tailored to specific supervisory tasks or through a free-form conversational interface. The system can identify relevant regulatory references, highlighting potential inconsistencies or compliance issues, assessing the coherence of proposed decisions with applicable rules, and providing reasoned analyses to support the approval or rejection of board resolutions. Furthermore, it assists supervisory personnel in drafting technical opinions, advisory reports, and formal assessments, substantially reducing preparation time while improving the quality, consistency, and traceability of regulatory evaluations. 2. Appointment Management and Eligibility Assessment Module The second module issues invitations to complete application forms for appointments to the audit bodies of 20 pension schemes, the 36 administrative committees responsible for managing INPS (National Institute of Pension Schemes) funds, and four private complementary pension funds. Applications are transmitted to and verified by the Supervisory Authority’s staff. The module manages the full initial submission workflow, from the invitation sent to the candidate through the transmission of the completed application and supporting documents to the competent supervisory staff. This also supports efficient handling of each individual appointment procedure. Through a certified authentication system, selected individuals can complete an online form, upload a CV and an ID document and, after confirming the accuracy of the information entered, automatically generate the documents that the Administration must publish on its transparency portal. After applicants review and verify the submitted information, the platform performs a preliminary formal review using an artificial intelligence algorithm. It provides feedback indicating, for example, whether a document is expired, a file has the wrong format, a file submitted as a CV is not a curriculum vitae, the CV contains a name different from the applicant’s, or the CV lacks the declarations required for self-certifications and sworn statements. When formal errors are detected, the platform alerts applicants, enabling them to correct the issues and upload the appropriate documentation. This initial phase reduces completion errors and processing times. Consequently, applications reach the competent authority complete and formally compliant, allowing its staff to focus on substantive rather than formal checks. Immediately after submission, an officer of the Supervisory Authority can review the documentation and initiate automated checks to verify its completeness and formal correctness and, within the information available on the platform, identify potential risks concerning conflicts of interest, incompatibility, or ineligibility for appointment. For example, the platform examines candidates’ CVs and the positions they declare they currently hold or have held during the previous two years, to identify companies affiliated with or controlled by the pension institution concerned. This assessment is conducted by analysing the notes to the institution’s financial statements. If an officer needs to clarify additional issues, an AI-powered free-text chat function is available. It enables the officer to query all documentation stored on the platform, including declarations and supporting documents, conduct further analysis, and investigate matters requiring additional scrutiny. *** A core innovation of the platform is the transformation of previously siloed information into a shared institutional knowledge base. Historically, supervisory processes were managed by different offices, resulting in fragmented information, duplicated activities, and limited knowledge transfer. The platform overcomes these constraints by integrating documents, data, regulatory sources, and procedural information within a single digital environment. This substantially reduces the effort required to store, analyze, and retrieve relevant information, while enhancing collaboration, preserving institutional knowledge, and improving the overall effectiveness and efficiency of supervisory activities

results.proposal: BärGPT: An Open-Source AI Assistant for a Sovereign Public Administration. results.title: Automatic detection of impervious surfaces using AI
results.proposal: Automatic detection of impervious surfaces using AI. In the context of progressing climate change, a precise and up-to-date overview of impervious surfaces in municipalities is essential. Impervious surfaces (approximately 45% of settlement and transport areas in Germany) reduce rainwater infiltration and contribute to the formation of urban heat islands by acting as heat storage. To date, imperviousness has mainly been determined using: - Cadastral data, which only partially reflect the actual on-site situation. - Manual mapping, which is highly time-consuming, costly, and difficult to maintain. At the same time, AI-based methods—particularly deep convolutional neural networks for image analysis—have made significant performance advances. In parallel, the availability of high-resolution georeferenced data has increased, such as annual digital orthophotos (DOPs) with a ground resolution of up to 10 cm (RGB and near-infrared/NIR). These developments make the automated detection of impervious surfaces using AI a promising approach. The district of Recklinghausen, in cooperation with the Westphalian University of Applied Sciences, initiated a project to automatically detect and classify impervious surfaces.

The results support more accurate identification of drought-prone areas, zones at risk of subsidence, and regions vulnerable to high groundwater levels. results.proposal: KI4LSA – Artificial Intelligence for Adaptive Traffic Signal Control. Increasing urban traffic congestion leads to longer travel times, higher fuel consumption, and increased noise and air pollution. Optimising traffic signal systems is a critical lever for improving traffic flow in dense city environments, yet conventional control strategies struggle to adapt to dynamic traffic conditions. The KI4LSA project addresses this challenge by exploring adaptive control of traffic lights in inner-city areas. Stakeholders include transport authorities, municipalities, and road users seeking smoother traffic flow and reduced environmental impact. The objective is to optimise traffic signal behaviour in real time to minimise congestion and unnecessary stopping. The solution uses reinforcement learning, a data-driven control approach trained in detailed traffic simulations. Traffic signal controllers learn optimal strategies by observing traffic states and evaluating outcomes such as queue length and waiting time. After training, the learned control policies are evaluated against conventional approaches. The project demonstrates improved traffic flow, reduced stop-and-go behaviour, and lower emissions resulting from fewer accelerations and idling periods. The results highlight the potential of adaptive signal control to improve urban mobility efficiency and environmental performance, while providing a transferable framework for future smart traffic management systems.

results.title: AI-for-Søren: AI for work injuries
results.proposal: AI-for-Søren: AI for work injuries. Work-related injuries and eye injuries involve specific reporting obligations, rights, responsibilities and procedural steps that can be difficult for employees and managers to understand quickly. AI-for-Søren addresses this problem by providing an AI assistant that answers questions about municipal procedures for handling occupational injury cases. The operational problem is that different users need different kinds of guidance: an injured employee may need to know what to do immediately, a manager may need to understand reporting obligations, and HR or working-environment staff may need consistent procedural information. The assistant communicates the municipality’s procedures and links users to supplementary information from relevant Danish authorities and professional sources, including the Danish Working Environment Authority and the National Board of Industrial Injuries. At a conceptual level, the tool functions as a specialised knowledge assistant for a narrow administrative domain. It does not decide whether an injury is compensable or replace formal case handling; instead, it helps users find correct guidance and understand the steps involved. The expected impact is easier access to accurate information, fewer procedural mistakes, more consistent handling of work-injury cases and reduced workload for staff who otherwise answer recurring questions manually. The intended users include managers, working-environment representatives, injured employees, HR staff, MED organisation representatives and the municipality’s occupational-injury function. The case is relevant because it shows how a municipality can create a focused AI assistant for a specific internal governance and employee-support process, where a well-defined knowledge base can reduce uncertainty and improve procedural compliance.
results.memo: Proceed. AI-for-Søren: AI for work injuries is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

The operational problem is that legal professionals spend substantial time locating relevant provisions, guidance, case law and arguments before they can apply them to a concrete case. KAILA is designed to accelerate this research and drafting process while preserving source verification. It can help generate legal text, gather relevant sources and arguments, provide new perspectives and assist preparation for meetings or case discussions. At a conceptual level, the system works as a retrieval and drafting assistant for legal work: it uses AI to interpret the user’s question, search trusted legal materials and produce a response with references that the legal professional can verify. This is important because legal AI must not be treated as an uncheckable answer generator; the value lies in combining speed with transparent source grounding. results.title: Pluto – Road Analysis and Maintenance
results.proposal: Pluto – Road Analysis and Maintenance. results.title: Fasit Dialogstøtte – AI Assistant for Conversation Notes
results.proposal: Fasit Dialogstøtte – AI Assistant for Conversation Notes. Caseworkers in employment and social-service settings must listen carefully to citizens while also documenting conversations accurately for case files. This creates a practical tension: manual note-taking can reduce presence in the conversation, while incomplete documentation can weaken case quality and increase the risk of mistakes. Fasit Dialogstøtte addresses this problem by integrating an AI assistant into the Schultz Fasit case-management environment. The operational objective is to support caseworkers by automatically transcribing conversations with citizens and generating draft summaries, minutes or journal notes. At a conceptual level, the assistant acts as a documentation support tool rather than a case-decision system. It captures the spoken conversation, converts it to text and prepares a draft that the caseworker can review, correct and approve before it becomes part of the case record. This allows the professional to remain responsible for the final documentation while reducing the repetitive burden of manual note-taking. The expected impact is more focused citizen dialogue, more consistent records, reduced administrative workload and stronger documentation quality. The system may also support accuracy because key points from the conversation can be captured systematically rather than reconstructed from memory after the meeting. results.title: OS2ai - Open-source AI solution in Danish municipalities
results.proposal: OS2ai - Open-source AI solution in Danish municipalities. Danish municipalities are exploring generative AI, but many want solutions that preserve public ownership, reduce dependency on large proprietary providers and allow shared development across authorities. OS2ai addresses this need by providing an open-source AI platform for the public sector, built around common governance, shared costs and stronger ownership control. Randers Municipality participates in this wider public-sector AI community. The operational problem is that individual municipalities may not have the resources to build secure, reusable AI infrastructure alone, while proprietary tools can raise concerns about data control, vendor lock-in and long-term costs. OS2ai offers a shared platform that can be used for both everyday AI support and more specialised municipal applications. At a conceptual level, OS2ai is an enabling layer: it makes it easier for municipalities to integrate AI into workflows, develop assistants, automate tasks and reuse components developed by other public authorities. The platform builds on work initiated by Aarhus Municipality and is further developed through the OS2 community, which has long focused on shared open-source public-sector software. The expected impact is faster AI adoption, lower duplicated development costs, greater transparency, improved public control over data and models, and more scalable experimentation across municipalities and regions. The case is relevant because it treats AI infrastructure as a shared public-good approach rather than a set of isolated local procurements. This is particularly important where municipalities face similar tasks and can benefit from common technical foundations.

results.title: MARVEL project in Trento: monitoring crowd in the city
results.proposal: MARVEL project in Trento: monitoring crowd in the city. This use case addresses these needs by supporting the municipality and local police in monitoring public spaces such as streets, squares, subways, and parking areas, with the objective of identifying anomalous or risky situations, including fights, robberies, drug dealing, and traffic accidents, and enabling timely operational responses. The solution is implemented through a smart monitoring platform that analyses video and audio streams from distributed sensors and cameras across the city, applying advanced pattern recognition and anomaly detection techniques to identify events of interest within crowds and specific locations. Detected incidents trigger automated alerts to the police operational centre and generate a customised visual interface that highlights relevant camera feeds, supporting situational awareness and rapid decision-making. The system is tested across five trial cases, including crowd monitoring, detection of criminal or anti-social behaviour, subway monitoring, parking surveillance, and focused analysis of specific areas. The use case enhances public safety by enabling faster detection and response to incidents, improving coordination between monitoring systems and law enforcement, and increasing the effectiveness and scalability of urban surveillance, while supporting safer and more resilient city environments.

results.title: Dublin to host AI-powered e-scooter research project
results.proposal: Dublin to host AI-powered e-scooter research project. Dublin faces growing challenges in managing shared micro-mobility services, particularly e-scooters, as their rapid adoption raises concerns around road safety, pavement congestion, parking compliance, and integration with existing transport systems. City authorities, transport planners, mobility operators, researchers, and citizens all have a stake in ensuring that e-scooters contribute positively to sustainable urban mobility rather than creating new risks or inefficiencies. The objective of this use case is to improve how e-scooters are deployed, used, and regulated across the city by generating evidence-based insights that support safer operations, better infrastructure planning, and more effective policy decisions. The project applies advanced data analytics and machine learning techniques to data collected from e-scooters, including location, speed, braking events, trip duration, and interaction with the urban environment, combined with contextual data such as road layouts, traffic conditions, and weather. Computer vision and predictive models are used to analyse rider behaviour, identify unsafe patterns, optimise parking zones, and simulate different regulatory or infrastructure scenarios. These models are integrated into a research platform that connects mobility operators, city systems, and analytical tools to enable continuous experimentation and evaluation. The initiative supports improved rider safety, reduced pavement clutter, and more efficient use of public space, while providing the city with robust evidence to guide regulation and investment. It enhances service reliability and user experience, enables scalable management of micro-mobility, and delivers long-term value by helping Dublin design safer, more sustainable urban transport systems.

results.proposal: AI-SCORE, a project to calculate prognostic risk from Covid-19. The AI-SCORE project (Artificial Intelligence – SARS-CoV-2 Risk Evaluation) is an Italian research initiative led by IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital in Milan, developed in collaboration with academic and industrial partners. Its goal is to build an AI-based system capable of predicting the risk of severe outcomes in COVID-19 patients. The platform uses machine learning to analyze a combination of clinical data, laboratory results, and medical imaging to estimate the probability that an infected patient will develop serious complications. This helps doctors identify high-risk patients early, improve triage decisions, and optimize hospital resource allocation during the pandemic. Beyond COVID-19, the project is designed as a broader model for predictive medicine, showing how artificial intelligence can support clinical decision-making in future infectious disease outbreaks and other high-risk health conditions.

results.title: Data-Driven Risk Analysis to Prevent Tax Evasion in Italy
results.proposal: Data-Driven Risk Analysis to Prevent Tax Evasion in Italy. Tax authorities face persistent challenges in identifying and preventing tax evasion, particularly as economic activities and financial relationships become increasingly complex. Traditional risk assessment methods often struggle to detect sophisticated patterns of non-compliance early enough to support effective enforcement and voluntary compliance. This use case addresses these challenges by modernising tax evasion risk analysis for the Italian Revenue Agency, involving the Ministry of Finance, its in-house technology partner SOGEI, and European Union funding bodies, with the objective of strengthening preventive identification of taxpayers at high risk of non-compliance and improving the effectiveness of fiscal oversight. The initiative is implemented through a data-driven system that applies machine learning, network analysis, and advanced data visualisation techniques to large volumes of fiscal, administrative, and economic data. Analytical models examine relationships between individuals, companies, and transactions to uncover hidden networks and anomalous behaviours associated with evasion risks, while visualisation tools support analysts in interpreting complex results and prioritising cases. The system integrates with existing tax administration processes and information infrastructures, enabling experimentation, validation, and gradual operational adoption. The project enhances the accuracy and timeliness of risk assessments, enabling more targeted controls and more efficient use of investigative resources. By shifting towards preventive and evidence-based analysis, it supports reduced tax evasion, improved compliance, and stronger public finances, while increasing the transparency, scalability, and analytical capacity of the Revenue Agency’s risk management processes.

results.title: Self-driving buses roll into Gothenburg
results.proposal: Self-driving buses roll into Gothenburg. Cities seeking to modernise public transport must balance sustainability goals, service accessibility, and the safe introduction of new mobility technologies. In Gothenburg, local authorities and transport operators aimed to explore innovative solutions that could enhance connectivity within key employment and innovation districts while reducing environmental impact. This use case focuses on the trial deployment of autonomous electric shuttles to provide public transport services within the Lindholmen Industrial and Science Park, involving the city, the transport operator Keolis, and passengers, with the objective of assessing the feasibility, safety, and operational value of self-driving buses in an urban setting. The service is implemented through autonomous electric shuttle vehicles operating on a dedicated 1.8-kilometre route, using onboard sensors, navigation systems, and control software to perceive their environment and drive without direct human control. The shuttles operate under supervised conditions during a 4.5-month trial period that began on 18 January, allowing for real-world testing, data collection, and system validation while ensuring passenger safety and regulatory compliance. The trial provides insights into the performance, reliability, and user acceptance of autonomous public transport, demonstrating the potential for low-emission, flexible mobility services in urban areas. It supports evidence-based decision-making on future deployments, contributes to innovation in public transport provision, and helps position Gothenburg as a testbed for sustainable and scalable autonomous mobility solutions.

results.title: Artificial intelligence dives into thousands of WWII photographs
results.proposal: Artificial intelligence dives into thousands of WWII photographs. Researchers in history, computer science, and the social sciences face significant challenges when analysing large collections of historical photographs, as manual examination is time-consuming and limits the scale of inquiry. Understanding patterns of authorship, perspective, and visual style in wartime imagery is important for historical interpretation, archival research, and cultural analysis. This use case addresses these challenges through an interdisciplinary study that examines thousands of Second World War photographs, involving academic researchers and cultural heritage institutions, with the objective of uncovering latent patterns in visual content and advancing new methods for large-scale historical image analysis. The study is implemented using computer vision and pattern recognition techniques applied to extensive datasets of digitised wartime photographs, with models trained to extract visual features related to composition, subject matter, and contextual elements. These models analyse similarities and recurring visual signatures across images, enabling the system to distinguish and attribute photographs to individual photographers based solely on image content, without relying on metadata. The results demonstrate that large-scale automated image analysis can reveal meaningful stylistic and contextual patterns in historical archives, including the ability to identify photographers with a high degree of accuracy. This approach significantly expands the analytical capacity of historical research, supports more systematic exploration of visual archives, and opens new opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration and data-driven insights in the study of cultural heritage.

results.title: AI technology speeds up historical image handling at Hungary's National Archive
results.proposal: AI technology speeds up historical image handling at Hungary's National Archive. Hungary’s National Audiovisual Archive (NAVA) faced the challenge of organising and preserving millions of historical images and audiovisual records forming the country’s twentieth-century cultural memory. Manual classification was slow, costly, and unable to keep pace with digitisation efforts. Stakeholders included archivists, historians, public broadcasters, and citizens, with the objective of accelerating cataloguing while maintaining archival quality. Between 2019 and 2021, a pilot deployed cloud-based image analysis services to classify large image collections automatically. Visual recognition models were trained to detect objects, scenes, and contextual features, generating metadata to support indexing and retrieval. The system integrated with existing archive databases and digitisation workflows, enabling human archivists to validate and refine outputs rather than start from scratch. The pilot significantly reduced processing time for image classification, allowing millions of records to be indexed efficiently. It improved searchability and long-term preservation planning while lowering operational costs. Archivists retained editorial control, ensuring trust and reliability. The approach demonstrated strong scalability and laid the foundation for sustainable management of national audiovisual heritage.

results.proposal: Sohjoa - Baltic Sea Region transitioning into eco-friendly autonomous last mile public transport. The service is implemented through autonomous driving technologies that enable small electric buses to operate on predefined demonstration routes, using a combination of sensors such as cameras, lidar, and radar to continuously scan their surroundings, detect obstacles, and make driving decisions including slowing down or stopping when required. Control software processes sensor data in real time to support safe navigation in mixed traffic environments, while a trained operator remains on board during all pilot operations to supervise the system, intervene if necessary, and ensure compliance with safety regulations, with operational data collected to support system evaluation and refinement. The pilots provide valuable insights into the technical, operational, and regulatory aspects of autonomous public transport, demonstrating potential reductions in environmental impact, improved last-mile connectivity, and increased efficiency in urban transport networks, while the supervised deployment model helps build public confidence and supports the development of scalable, low-emission mobility solutions for cities planning future autonomous transport services.

results.proposal: AI-for-Covid Predictive diagnostics made in Italy. The platform is integrated into existing radiology and hospital information systems, enabling seamless access for clinicians without disrupting established diagnostic workflows. The solution improves the timeliness and consistency of clinical decision-making by providing early insight into disease progression risk. This supports more effective allocation of intensive care resources, reduces uncertainty in patient triage, and enhances overall care quality. By enabling earlier interventions for high-risk patients, the platform contributes to better patient management, increased operational efficiency, and improved resilience of healthcare services during periods of high demand.

results.proposal: Artificial intelligence and video surveillance to control the distance at the airport. COVID-19 restrictions severely limited in-person contact in hospitals, isolating patients from families and complicating communication between healthcare staff. Hospitals in Turin launched a pilot to explore how remote presence technologies could mitigate social isolation while maintaining safety protocols. Stakeholders included patients, relatives, healthcare professionals, hospital administrators, and telecom providers, with the objective of preserving human interaction and collaboration despite physical distancing requirements. From 2020 to 2021, the pilot deployed Double Robotics Double3 mobile robots connected via a 5G network. These remotely controlled robots enabled high-definition video communication and autonomous movement within hospital wards. Secure network connectivity ensured low latency and reliable audio-visual interaction, while simple user interfaces allowed staff and families to connect without specialised training. The robots integrated with hospital connectivity infrastructure and operated under strict data protection policies. The pilot improved patient well-being by restoring contact with families and supported collaboration among medical staff across wards. It reduced unnecessary physical movement within hospitals and demonstrated the value of high-bandwidth connectivity for healthcare environments. The solution proved reliable and scalable, highlighting potential long-term applications for telepresence in clinical care, training, and hospital operations beyond emergency contexts.

results.proposal: Poverty prevention - Identification of poverty and debt early. The pilot improved the timeliness and targeting of interventions, reducing long-term social and financial costs. Qualitative impacts include stronger inter-agency collaboration, increased trust from citizens and full compliance with data protection requirements. results.title: Decide Madrid - Citizen Participation and Machine Learning
results.proposal: Decide Madrid - Citizen Participation and Machine Learning. Large-scale online participation platforms can suffer from information overload: thousands of proposals and comments make it difficult for citizens to find relevant initiatives, build consensus, and understand debates, while public officials struggle to synthesise input into actionable insights. Research using Madrid’s Decide Madrid platform (built on Consul) examined how to improve discovery, deliberation, and responsiveness so that participation remains meaningful as volume grows. Stakeholders include citizens submitting proposals and comments, city administrators responsible for engagement and policy feedback, and platform maintainers seeking scalable moderation and analysis tools, with the objective of improving user experience and the quality of participation outcomes. The approach applies natural language processing and machine learning to suggest proposals users may wish to support, cluster citizens by shared interests, summarise comment threads, and assist with drafting or aggregating responses and refined proposals. This is achieved by processing the text corpus of proposals and comments, extracting semantic representations, and using similarity, clustering, and summarisation techniques that can be integrated into the platform interface as recommender, navigation, and analyst-support features. Reported evaluations indicate these methods can address participation barriers by reducing noise, improving navigability, and helping users and administrators focus on salient themes, thereby increasing the practicality of digital democracy tools without requiring proportional increases in staffing.

These tools are evaluated using harmonised imaging datasets and clinical data, and assessed across multiple dimensions, including technical robustness, algorithmic fairness, clinical usability, and acceptance by healthcare professionals, with integration into existing clinical workflows. The project strengthens confidence in data-driven imaging tools, supports more precise treatment decisions, and aims to reduce over-treatment while improving patient outcomes. results.title: Piedmont harnesses AI to bring healthcare to every corner
results.proposal: Piedmont harnesses AI to bring healthcare to every corner. Piedmont’s AI-healthcare initiative focuses on using artificial intelligence, diagnostics and telemedicine to improve healthcare access across a region where more than 40% of the territory is mountainous. The operational challenge is territorial inequality in access to care: residents in peripheral or mountain areas may need to travel long distances for diagnostic examinations or specialist medical consultations, creating delays and barriers to timely treatment. The initiative proposes an extended system of telemedicine cabins where patients can undergo examinations with the support of a trained health or social-care operator while a doctor connects remotely from a hospital. Artificial intelligence is positioned as a support layer for diagnostics, organisational efficiency and telemedicine workflows, helping clinicians interpret information, monitor patients and manage remote-service delivery more effectively. At operational level, the system decentralises access to diagnostic services by bringing examination capacity closer to residents while keeping specialist medical expertise connected through video and digital tools. This helps shift healthcare from a hospital-centred model towards more distributed territorial care. The expected impact is improved healthcare coverage for remote communities, faster access to diagnostic support, reduced travel burden for patients, more efficient use of medical resources and stronger resilience of the regional health system. The initiative is particularly relevant because it links AI not only to clinical innovation, but also to equity of access and territorial cohesion, using telemedicine to make the right to health more practical in peripheral areas.

AI Reader supports the Commissariat aux affaires maritimes by automating the extraction of predefined information from documents such as visas, whether they are submitted as text-based PDFs, image PDFs or JPEG files. The operational challenge is that customers and agents otherwise need to enter and verify data manually, creating delays, avoidable errors and repetitive administrative work. In the Seafarers’ service, this can affect the efficiency of document handling and the quality of information injected into administrative systems. AI Reader reads incoming documents, identifies the relevant fields and extracts the required information without manual intervention. At operational level, the tool reduces the amount of data that customers must provide directly, limits errors at the point of entry and reduces the need for later verification and correction by CAM agents. The extracted information can then be automatically integrated into the relevant internal systems, improving workflow continuity between document submission and case processing. The expected impact is faster handling of seafarer-related services, fewer data-entry mistakes, reduced administrative burden and a more streamlined user experience for applicants. The initiative is relevant because it applies AI to a common but important public-administration bottleneck: transforming unstructured or semi-structured documents into reliable data that can be reused in business processes. This type of document automation creates practical efficiency gains while preserving administrative control over final validation and service delivery.
