results.company: Zenter fir d'Lëtzebuerger Sprooch (ZLS – Centre for Luxembourgish Language)
results.title: "Iwwersetzungskorpus fir d'Lëtzebuergescht" - multilingual parallel corpus
results.proposal: "Iwwersetzungskorpus fir d'Lëtzebuergescht" - multilingual parallel corpus. High-quality machine translation and language AI depend on structured parallel datasets that show how the same content is expressed across different languages. Luxembourgish remains under-represented in such resources, creating barriers for translation technologies, language-model training and computational linguistics research. “Iwwersetzungskorpus fir d’Lëtzebuergescht” addresses this need by establishing a multilingual parallel corpus centred on Luxembourgish as the source language, with translations into German, French and English. The operational problem is that AI systems cannot provide reliable translation or language support for Luxembourgish unless they are trained on high-quality aligned texts that reflect real usage, terminology and linguistic variation. The corpus creates a reusable linguistic dataset that connects Luxembourgish with three major languages used in Luxembourg’s administrative, legal, educational and social environment. At operational level, the corpus provides the foundation for advanced machine translation, language-model training and multilingual public-service applications. It can also support researchers working on computational linguistics, language preservation and multilingual communication. The expected impact is improved digital treatment of Luxembourgish, better translation quality, stronger support for multilingual administration and greater inclusion of the national language in future AI systems. The initiative is particularly important because language technologies shape how citizens interact with public services, access information and participate in digital life. By building structured Luxembourgish-centred data, the project strengthens linguistic sovereignty and reduces dependence on datasets designed primarily for larger language markets.
results.memo: Proceed. "Iwwersetzungskorpus fir d'Lëtzebuergescht" - multilingual parallel corpus is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Zenter fir d'Lëtzebuerger Sprooch (ZLS – Centre for Luxembourgish Language)
results.title: "Sproocherkennung fir d'Lëtzebuergescht": improving schreifmaschinn.lu, an AI-based speech-to-text tool in various languages
results.proposal: "Sproocherkennung fir d'Lëtzebuergescht": improving schreifmaschinn.lu, an AI-based speech-to-text tool in various languages. Luxembourgish is central to the country’s linguistic identity, but speech-recognition technologies often perform better for larger languages with more abundant training data. “Sproocherkennung fir d’Lëtzebuergescht” addresses this gap by improving the speech-to-text capabilities of schreifmaschinn.lu, an AI-based transcription tool developed by the Zenter fir d’Lëtzebuerger Sprooch. The operational problem is that accurate speech recognition requires high-quality synchronised audio and text data, representing different speakers, accents, contexts and recording situations. The existing dataset already provides a foundation for Luxembourgish transcription, but broader and more diverse training material is needed to improve recognition quality and spelling accuracy. The initiative expands the hypersynchronised audio-text dataset from 55 hours to 80 hours, with two main objectives: diversifying the range of speakers and situations represented in the data, and improving orthographic accuracy in the generated transcription. At operational level, the project strengthens the data foundation behind Luxembourgish speech technology, enabling better automatic transcription for public, educational, cultural and administrative uses. It also supports digital inclusion by making spoken Luxembourgish more usable in digital environments, from accessibility tools to language-learning resources and public-service interfaces. The expected impact is more accurate Luxembourgish speech-to-text, stronger support for multilingual digital services and greater visibility of Luxembourgish in AI-enabled communication systems. The initiative is relevant because it treats language resources as strategic digital infrastructure for public-sector innovation and linguistic diversity.

evidence.quote: It also supports digital inclusion by making spoken Luxembourgish more usable in digital environments, from accessibility tools to language-learning resources and public-service interfaces.

results.title: UrbIA - AI for cadastral data
results.proposal: UrbIA - AI for cadastral data. Luxembourg’s cadastral data contain a long historical record of property information, including graphic materials such as cadastral plans and sketch maps and tabular records documenting changes in property rights. UrbIA supports the Land Registry and Topography Administration in making this historical information more usable by applying AI and data-interpretation methods to old handwritten cadastral registers. The operational challenge is that property-rights information from 1824 to 1972 was recorded manually in structured tables, creating a large archive that is valuable but difficult to exploit efficiently in modern digital workflows. Manual interpretation of these registers is time-consuming, specialist-dependent and not easily scalable across municipalities. UrbIA compares different technical approaches for interpreting selected registers in a given municipality, identifies the most effective method and then prepares implementation within the Administration. At operational level, the tool strengthens the digital transformation of cadastral management by converting historical handwritten information into data that can be searched, structured and reused more easily. The initiative helps preserve the continuity between historical land records and modern cadastral systems, improving access to information on property rights and supporting more efficient administrative processing. The expected impact is faster interpretation of historical registers, better integration of legacy cadastral data into contemporary systems, reduced manual workload and improved reliability of property-related public records. UrbIA is particularly relevant because it applies AI to a long-term institutional archive that remains essential for land administration, legal certainty and territorial information management.
results.memo: Proceed. UrbIA - AI for cadastral data is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Assitance in drafting judgments JUAIDE
results.proposal: Assitance in drafting judgments JUAIDE. Judicial drafting requires rapid access to legal texts, previous court decisions and accurate references while the judge is developing the reasoning of a decision. JUAIDE supports this work by integrating an artificial intelligence component into the drafting process for legal documents. The system analyses the context of the text being written in real time and identifies legal sources that may be relevant to the point under development. Instead of requiring the judge to interrupt drafting in order to conduct separate legal research, JUAIDE brings potentially applicable legal texts and case law directly into the workflow. This reduces the time spent searching for references, strengthens the accuracy of citations and helps ensure that judicial reasoning is supported by relevant legal material. At operational level, the tool acts as a drafting and research assistant: it does not replace judicial reasoning, but helps the judge identify and verify sources more efficiently while preparing legal documents. Its value lies in combining contextual analysis with immediate access to authoritative legal information, allowing drafting to become more fluid and better supported. The expected impact is faster preparation of judgments, improved quality of legal references, reduced repetitive research work and greater efficiency in the judicial process. The initiative is relevant for digital justice because it applies AI to a core professional task in a controlled way, preserving the judge’s responsibility while improving access to the legal materials needed for high-quality decision-writing.

results.title: AmigaAI - Chatbot for the legal sector
results.proposal: AmigaAI - Chatbot for the legal sector. AmigaAI is an Austrian legal-AI initiative designed to improve access to legal information and increase the efficiency of legal workflows through a domain-specific large language model. Legal language is highly specialised, context-dependent and difficult for non-experts to understand, while legal professionals also spend considerable time searching, interpreting and structuring complex information. General-purpose AI models are not always suitable for this environment because they may fail to capture the nuances, terminology and legal context of Austrian law. AmigaAI addresses this by developing a legal-specific language model capable of understanding and interpreting Austrian legal language more accurately. The initiative is led by the Vienna-based legal-tech company GesetzeFinden.at and brings together an interdisciplinary consortium including the Psychological Faculty of Sigmund Freud Private University, CERHA HEMPEL and Fraunhofer Austria. The project combines legal expertise, psychological research on human-machine interaction and technology acceptance, and applied technical development. A distinctive feature is the “Society of Minds” approach, in which several AI chatbots communicate internally and collaborate on the answer before presenting a result to the user. This design aims to improve output quality while allowing the use of smaller and more resource-efficient models. At operational level, AmigaAI is intended to support both professionals and the wider public by making legal information easier to retrieve, understand and apply, while maintaining reliability, usability and alignment with European AI governance expectations.

results.title: Microsoft Copilot in Cyprus' Public Administration
results.proposal: Microsoft Copilot in Cyprus' Public Administration. Cyprus is introducing Microsoft 365 Copilot across public administration to accelerate routine work, improve productivity and support the wider digital modernisation of government services. Public officials manage large volumes of written material, administrative data, reports and internal processes, much of which requires drafting, summarisation, analysis and coordination. Copilot provides an AI assistant integrated into the Microsoft 365 environment, enabling civil servants to draft reports, manage routine tasks, analyse large information sets and automate simple actions while remaining within the productivity tools already used by the administration. The first phase provides 350 user licences and dedicated training, ensuring that public servants can use the tool safely and effectively. The initiative also includes data-security considerations and is connected to a wider EUR 5 million “AI in Government” programme, which seeks to encourage AI-driven solutions for state challenges such as labour-market matching and climate response. At operational level, the rollout helps public officials complete repetitive knowledge-work tasks more quickly, freeing staff capacity for higher-value work and direct service improvement. At strategic level, it creates an initial public-sector user base for generative AI and helps the administration develop the skills, governance practices and organisational experience needed for broader AI integration across government.

results.company: Ministry of Justice, Paris Public Prosecutor's Office
results.title: Mon parquet assistant - My assistant prosecutor
results.proposal: Mon parquet assistant - My assistant prosecutor. Mon parquet assistant supports criminal-case processing in the courts under the Paris Court of Appeal by helping magistrates review, search and analyse procedural files more efficiently. Criminal files can be lengthy, heterogeneous and administratively demanding, particularly in high-volume proceedings where magistrates need to identify the nature of offences, locate relevant information and understand the structure of a case quickly. The tool is designed to allow users to upload one or more procedures, whether natively digital or scanned, into a dedicated interface. It then supports the detection of the offence types under investigation, offers a rapid view of the case by answering predefined questions linked to the relevant offence category, and enables deeper review by displaying source passages in a PDF reader and highlighting relevant sections. Users can also interrogate the procedure directly, making it easier to search through large files without manually reading every page in sequence. At operational level, the tool reduces repetitive, low-value document-handling tasks and gives magistrates faster access to the information needed for procedural analysis. It supports both overview and detailed review, while preserving the magistrate’s responsibility for legal assessment and prosecutorial decision-making. The initiative forms part of the Justice incubator approach to building practical digital tools around real professional workflows in the justice system.

results.title: Introduction of Microsoft 365 Copilot within the public sector
results.proposal: Introduction of Microsoft 365 Copilot within the public sector. Malta’s public-sector rollout of Microsoft 365 Copilot introduces generative-AI productivity support across the administration to reduce routine workload and modernise daily work practices. The initiative responds to a common administrative challenge: public officers spend significant time drafting documents, summarising information, preparing communications, managing email and performing repetitive knowledge-work tasks that can be accelerated with AI support. Through a EUR 4 million investment, Microsoft 365 Copilot is being made available to more than 8,000 public officers over a two-year period, with direct deployment on employees’ laptops and structured training to support effective use. The initiative also includes a Centre of Excellence operated through collaboration between Microsoft, the Government and MITA, providing a hub for guidance, best practice, governance and innovation. A distinctive feature is the integration of Maltese-language support, enabling public officers to use Copilot across core Microsoft applications in Maltese as well as English. This improves accessibility, reinforces the use of Maltese in digital administration and supports language inclusion within the public-sector workforce. At operational level, Copilot assists with drafting, summarisation, document preparation and routine administrative work, while employees remain responsible for reviewing and validating outputs. The initiative is part of Malta’s broader digital-transformation agenda and is positioned as a workforce-empowerment measure rather than a replacement for public officials.

results.title: Bilingual AI Chatbot and Mobile Robot
results.proposal: Bilingual AI Chatbot and Mobile Robot. Malta’s Life Events Robot provides AI-supported assistance for citizens dealing with major civil life events, including marriage, birth, divorce and other registration-related procedures. These services generate high volumes of recurring questions, and citizens often need clear guidance in both Maltese and English. The Life Events Robot addresses this challenge through a bilingual conversational assistant that combines retrieval-augmented generation, curated public-service information and natural-language interaction. The system retrieves relevant administrative and legal content from authoritative life-event datasets and presents it in a conversational format that is easier for users to understand than navigating multiple web pages or contacting a helpdesk. It also supports speech-to-text and text-to-speech functions, enabling voice-based interaction and improving accessibility for users who may find written digital services difficult to use. The mobile-robot component extends the same assistance into physical service environments, allowing citizens to receive on-site guidance through a Temi V3 robot in government service centres. At operational level, the solution reduces repetitive demand on staff, improves consistency of answers, supports 24/7 availability and creates a reusable platform that can later be extended to other public-service domains. Its bilingual design is particularly important in Malta’s administrative context, where digital public services must remain accessible in both national service languages.

results.title: Greek Government and Sword Health team up for AI-driven initiative
results.proposal: Greek Government and Sword Health team up for AI-driven initiative. Greece’s partnership with Sword Health uses AI to strengthen the national healthcare access pathway, starting from the National Health Information Line 1566. The initiative addresses a common public-health challenge: citizens often need guidance on where to seek care, which service to contact, or how to navigate the health system, while frontline teams face high volumes of routine and urgent enquiries. By integrating AI into triage and coordination processes, the programme aims to increase the capacity of the health information line, improve response times and provide more consistent support across the country. The AI layer is designed to work alongside healthcare professionals rather than replace them, absorbing repetitive and high-volume tasks, helping direct citizens towards appropriate services and giving health-system leaders better visibility over emerging needs. This is particularly relevant for a national system that must serve urban, rural and remote populations with different levels of access to healthcare resources. At operational level, the initiative creates an AI-enabled “front door” to healthcare: citizens can be guided more efficiently, hospitals can face lower avoidable pressure, and frontline staff can focus on cases requiring human judgement or clinical escalation. The wider ambition is to build a more responsive and resilient public-health access model that combines AI-based coordination with human care.

results.title: Digital Doctor Assistant
results.proposal: Digital Doctor Assistant. Greece’s Digital Doctor Assistant introduces artificial intelligence into the national electronic health-record environment to help doctors access, interpret and use patient information more efficiently. Public health systems generate large volumes of clinical data, including histories, medications, laboratory results, diagnostic information and previous treatments, but this information is not always easy to retrieve quickly during a consultation. The Digital Doctor Assistant addresses this challenge by allowing healthcare professionals to interact with the patient record through natural-language queries, including spoken interaction. Through the MyHealthDoc system, doctors can request summaries of a patient’s medical history, ask which medicines were administered over a given period, retrieve personalised results and navigate clinical information without manually searching across the full record. The tool is intended to reduce bureaucracy, shorten the time needed to access relevant information and support medical decision-making inside the National Health System. Its value lies in improving the clinical information workflow: doctors remain responsible for diagnosis and treatment, while the assistant helps surface relevant data faster and in a more usable form. The initiative also supports broader digital-health transformation by embedding AI directly into a national public-health platform rather than treating it as a separate experimental application.

results.title: OpenAI For Greece - Greek AI Accelerator to support local AI‑focused start‑ups
results.proposal: OpenAI For Greece - Greek AI Accelerator to support local AI‑focused start‑ups. Greece’s AI Accelerator is designed to strengthen the country’s start-up ecosystem by helping local founders build, test and scale AI-driven products in sectors aligned with national priorities. The programme responds to a structural innovation challenge: Greece has a strong base of STEM graduates and technical talent, but many highly skilled professionals pursue opportunities abroad, weakening the domestic pipeline for advanced digital entrepreneurship. The accelerator creates a pathway for AI-focused start-ups to access technical resources, international expertise and investor networks while remaining connected to the Greek innovation ecosystem. Selected companies receive access to OpenAI technology and credits, technical mentorship from OpenAI engineers and global experts, tailored workshops on scaling, compliance and safety-by-design, and international exposure, including links to leading investors and innovators. The programme gives particular attention to education, public services, healthcare and climate, where AI can generate both economic and public-interest value. At an operational level, the accelerator helps start-ups move from prototype development to scalable products by combining model access, technical advice, policy alignment and market visibility. At ecosystem level, it supports talent retention, creates stronger links between Greek founders and global AI networks, and contributes to the government’s wider objective of positioning Greece as a competitive hub for applied artificial intelligence.

results.title: OpenAI For Greece - ChatGPT Edu in Secondary Education
results.proposal: OpenAI For Greece - ChatGPT Edu in Secondary Education. Education systems need to prepare teachers and students for AI while ensuring that adoption is structured, responsible and aligned with pedagogical goals. OpenAI for Greece addresses this challenge through a partnership between OpenAI, the Government of the Hellenic Republic, the Onassis Foundation and Endeavor Greece, with an education component centred on ChatGPT Edu in upper-secondary schools. The operational problem is that generative AI is already entering learning environments informally, but teachers need training, secure tools and clear guidance if they are to integrate AI constructively into classroom practice. Greece’s pilot will start with teachers from upper-secondary schools selected to reflect regional and socio-economic diversity. The first phase focuses on AI literacy, teacher productivity and responsible integration of AI into education. ChatGPT Edu is described by OpenAI as a version of ChatGPT built for academic institutions, offering access to OpenAI’s latest models with enterprise-grade security and controls that support GDPR compliance. The Onassis Foundation will lead implementation with local partners, including The Tipping Point, while OpenAI will co-design teacher training, provide technical support and share best practices for safe classroom use. At a conceptual level, the initiative treats AI not merely as a student tool, but as a system-level capacity for teacher training, lesson support, responsible use and national skills development. The expected impact is improved AI literacy, more confident teacher adoption, support for classroom innovation and a pathway to wider national rollout if the pilot demonstrates successful outcomes
results.memo: Proceed. OpenAI For Greece - ChatGPT Edu in Secondary Education is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Sovereign AI for Public Administration in Germany
results.proposal: Sovereign AI for Public Administration in Germany. Germany’s sovereign AI initiative with France, Mistral AI and SAP SE is intended to create a trusted European framework for applying AI in public administration while preserving digital sovereignty and institutional control. The operational problem is that German administrations, like their French counterparts, increasingly require AI-enabled enterprise systems and digital agents for financial workflows, compliance support, drafting, service guidance and internal productivity. However, deploying such systems in government requires interoperability with existing administrative architecture, secure handling of public data, explainability, auditability and long-term resilience. The announced partnership focuses on a sovereign ERP platform with embedded AI, AI-supported financial management, digital agents for public services and shared training and innovation capacity. In the German context, SAP’s role is particularly relevant because of its long-standing presence in enterprise software used by public and private organisations, while Mistral AI contributes European model capabilities. At a conceptual level, the initiative aims to place AI inside the administrative operating system rather than deploying isolated chatbots. It is designed to create tools that help civil servants classify invoices, check audits, draft documents, simulate scenarios, justify budgets and guide citizens through forms or eligibility checks. The expected impact is more efficient administration, stronger interoperability, lower dependence on non-European providers and better alignment with European sovereignty objectives

results.title: Sovereign AI for Public Administration in France
results.proposal: Sovereign AI for Public Administration in France. France’s sovereign AI partnership with Germany, Mistral AI and SAP SE is designed to address a strategic public-administration challenge: how to adopt AI at scale while preserving European control over data, infrastructure, governance and critical digital dependencies. The operational problem is that public administrations need AI tools for productivity, decision support, financial management, service guidance and compliance, but reliance on non-European technology stacks can create concerns around sovereignty, interoperability, security and long-term control. The planned partnership focuses on four pillars: an intelligent sovereign ERP platform tailored to French and German administrative requirements; AI-augmented financial management, including invoice classification and audit checks; digital agents for civil servants and citizens; and joint training and innovation capacity through AI-ERP labs. For France, the initiative is framed as a strategic shift towards more efficient, resilient and sovereign public administration, enabling civil servants to use generative agents for drafting, scenario simulation, budget justification, compliance support and eligibility guidance. At a conceptual level, the partnership aims to create a European-controlled AI stack that combines Mistral AI’s models with SAP’s enterprise systems and sovereign infrastructure principles. The expected impact is improved public-sector efficiency, stronger auditability and traceability of AI systems, better service responsiveness and reduced dependence on external technology providers
results.memo: Proceed. Sovereign AI for Public Administration in France is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: KarolAIna - petascale EuroHPC supercomputer in Czechia
results.proposal: KarolAIna - petascale EuroHPC supercomputer in Czechia. The Czech AI Factory is intended to strengthen the Czech Republic’s ability to develop, test and deploy artificial intelligence across industry, research, public administration and start-ups. The operational challenge is that many AI applications require specialised computing resources, secure data environments, software tools, expert teams and training that are difficult for individual organisations to access alone. CZAI addresses this by establishing a national AI Factory led by VSB – Technical University of Ostrava, with a consortium that includes the Czech Technical University in Prague, Charles University, the International Neurodegenerative Disorders Research Center, the Institute of Organic Chemistry and Biochemistry of the Czech Academy of Sciences and Brno University of Technology. At the centre of the initiative is KarolAIna, a new AI-optimised supercomputer building on the Karolina EuroHPC petascale system at IT4Innovations. results.title: Drones and AI to tackle congestion
results.proposal: Drones and AI to tackle congestion. Urban mobility around major transport hubs is difficult to manage because cars, trams, buses, bicycles, electric scooters, pedestrians and ferry passengers interact dynamically, particularly during peak arrival and departure periods. Helsinki’s drone- and AI-supported traffic-monitoring initiative addresses this problem by collecting high-resolution mobility data around the West Harbour, one of Europe’s busiest ferry-port areas. The operational challenge is that transport planners need to understand not only aggregate traffic volumes, but also how passengers move between ferries, trams, metro lines, trains, taxis, scooters, bicycles and walking routes. Since 2023, drones have been used above the harbour area to collect bird’s-eye-view video of multimodal traffic. AI systems process the footage to detect and classify vehicles and track movement patterns, including speed, direction and interaction between transport modes. These outputs are then converted into anonymised trajectory data and integrated into AI-powered digital twins, allowing city regulators and engineers to test traffic-management strategies virtually before implementing them in the real world. At a conceptual level, the initiative turns temporary aerial observations into simulation-ready data for urban planning. It also raises important governance questions, since even GDPR-compliant drone monitoring can create public concerns about surveillance, transparency and cybersecurity. The project aims to test soft measures such as route recommendations and incentives to travel at off-peak times, and to trial an app suggesting alternative routes or modes. The wider expected impact is reduced peak congestion, smoother intermodal connections, better planning evidence and support for sustainable urban mobility

results.proposal: CostAI Kalundborg. Staff had to navigate too many links, tools and interfaces, which risked reducing the productivity benefits that AI was supposed to deliver. In response, the municipality worked with the Danish technology start-up Promte, formerly Applai, to develop a user-friendly platform for municipal AI assistants. The app is designed to work across PC, tablet and mobile devices and to bring together tools such as intranet chat, specialised professional-domain assistants, interpretation or translation support, meeting transcription and minute-generation functions. This supports safer and more coherent organisational adoption, because employees can access AI services through an approved municipal channel rather than through dispersed, informal solutions. results.title: Robotic technologies for the construction industry
results.proposal: Robotic technologies for the construction industry. Renovation, repair and deconstruction of masonry buildings are labour-intensive activities that can expose workers to repetitive strain, dust, noise and physically demanding manual work. The Danish project on robotic removal of masonry joints addresses this problem by developing and testing robotic technologies that can remove mortar joints in masonry more precisely and efficiently. The operational challenge is that brick buildings often have long potential lifetimes, but repairing or selectively dismantling them requires careful removal of joints without damaging reusable materials. Conventional manual methods can be slow and physically demanding, while demolition may lead to unnecessary material loss and reduce the possibility of circular reuse. The project therefore focuses on full-scale development, testing, dissemination and implementation of robotic technologies for the construction sector, with specific attention to extending building lifetime and enabling more effective deconstruction. At a conceptual level, the solution combines robotics, sensing and control methods to identify and remove joints accurately, supporting both selective repair and recovery of building materials. The expected impact is improved productivity in construction and renovation, reduced wear and tear on craft workers, better occupational safety, longer building lifetimes and increased reuse of masonry materials in the circular economy. The case is relevant because it shows how automation can support the green transition in construction not only through new materials, but also by making repair and deconstruction more practical. The official project page describes the initiative as an environmental-technology development, testing and demonstration project within the MUDP programme.

results.title: HabitAi - intelligent data to support sustainable decisions for homeowners
results.proposal: HabitAi - intelligent data to support sustainable decisions for homeowners. Renovation and maintenance decisions in residential buildings have a major influence on resource use, emissions and the long-term sustainability of the construction sector. HabitAi addresses this challenge by exploring how dynamic and contextual building data can be collected, structured and made usable for homeowners and construction-sector actors. The operational problem is that many decisions about single-family homes are still taken on the basis of fragmented, static or siloed data. Information about building characteristics, condition, maintenance needs, climate impact and renovation options may exist across different registries or professional assessments, but it is not necessarily available in a form that supports practical decision-making by the homeowner. The HabitAi preliminary project examined whether it is technically possible to carry out cross-cutting data collection and digitalisation of currently locked or fragmented building data for Danish single-family houses. The intended outcome is a digital toolbox that can help homeowners and the building sector decide when maintenance, renovation or preservation is preferable to demolition, and how to achieve the greatest environmental benefit within the homeowner’s financial constraints. At a conceptual level, the project is about converting building data into decision support: rather than treating each renovation as an isolated case, data can help identify sustainable pathways for preserving resources, extending building lifetimes and reducing climate impact. The case is relevant because it focuses on the residential building stock, where individual decisions collectively have large environmental consequences. results.company: Danish Ministry of Climate, Energy, and Utilities
results.title: Energy-efficient de-icing with camera detection and artificial intelligence
results.proposal: Energy-efficient de-icing with camera detection and artificial intelligence. Ventilation systems are critical for energy-efficient buildings because heat exchangers can recover a large share of the heat from exhaust air, reducing the need for additional heating. However, ice formation on heat exchangers can reduce efficiency, increase energy consumption and damage the system if not managed correctly. The Danish AICID project addresses this problem by developing an AI-based control algorithm for more precise de-icing in ventilation systems. The operational challenge is that conventional de-icing methods often rely on indirect external indicators, such as temperature and humidity, which may trigger de-icing even when ice formation is not actually present. This leads to unnecessary energy use and higher operating costs. AICID uses camera detection together with humidity and temperature sensors to identify real ice formation more accurately and control de-icing cycles only when needed. The project includes analysis of camera and sensor technologies, testing, development and implementation of the algorithm on EXHAUSTO ventilation systems, demonstration in homes managed by Haderslev Boligselskab and lifecycle assessment to confirm environmental benefits. The expected results are substantial: the project aims to reduce heat loss in ventilation systems by at least 40%, reduce de-icing periods from around 40% to between 5% and 0.5% annually, and lower the temperature threshold for de-icing from 5°C to between -5°C and -10°C. The wider expected impact is improved building energy efficiency, lower operational costs, longer equipment lifetime and significant national energy-saving potential.
results.memo: Proceed. Energy-efficient de-icing with camera detection and artificial intelligence is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI Assisted Process Understanding for Management of N2O Reduction from Wastewater Treatment Plants (AIAP-N2O)
results.proposal: AI Assisted Process Understanding for Management of N2O Reduction from Wastewater Treatment Plants (AIAP-N2O). Wastewater treatment plants can emit nitrous oxide, a greenhouse gas with a high climate impact, but emissions are difficult to manage because they depend on complex biological and operational conditions inside process tanks. AIAP-N2O addresses this challenge by using sensor data, AI, data analysis and process knowledge to understand and reduce N₂O formation in wastewater treatment. The operational problem is that treatment plants need practical control strategies that can be implemented across different hardware and software environments, rather than solutions that work only in one specific plant or vendor system. The project will collect data from three wastewater treatment plants over one to one and a half years, including measurements from two types of N₂O sensor technologies. These data will be used to develop an open and detailed description of how process-tank control can avoid or reduce nitrous oxide formation. At a conceptual level, the project converts plant-level measurements into generalisable process knowledge: AI helps identify the conditions and parameters that drive emissions, while the resulting guidance can be used by treatment plants or third-party control providers to build their own control strategies. The expected impact is lower greenhouse-gas emissions, better environmental performance in water and wastewater management, and easier adoption of N₂O reduction practices across the sector. The case is relevant because it uses AI not simply to optimise efficiency, but to make climate mitigation operational in public environmental infrastructure. The project is led by Duotec A/S with the Danish Technological Institute, DTU Sustain and several wastewater utilities.

results.title: AI-based feed optimisation – real-time processing of large amounts of data in pig production
results.proposal: AI-based feed optimisation – real-time processing of large amounts of data in pig production. Pig production depends heavily on feed efficiency because feed composition affects productivity, animal growth, production costs and the climate footprint of meat production. The Danish AI-based feed-optimisation project addresses the challenge of continuously identifying optimal feeding strategies for growing pigs using real-time data from across the production chain. The operational problem is that traditional feed trials can be slow and may struggle to keep pace with rapid genetic development in slaughter pigs. Producers need more dynamic tools that can account for changing growth patterns, feed composition, herd performance and commercial conditions. The project will develop an advanced AI-based system that integrates data from feed suppliers, slaughterhouses and pig producers, enabling real-time monitoring and continuous calculation of optimal feed compositions. At a conceptual level, the system works as a data-driven alternative or supplement to conventional feed trials: instead of relying only on periodic experimental results, the model learns from large-scale operational data and updates recommendations as conditions change. The expected impact is higher productivity, reduced feed costs, better feed utilisation and lower greenhouse-gas emissions from food production through more efficient resource use. The case is relevant because it applies AI to a concrete environmental and economic bottleneck in agriculture, where small improvements in feed efficiency can have significant aggregate effects. The project is led by IQinAbox ApS with the University of Copenhagen and is supported by Denmark’s Green Development and Demonstration Programme.

results.title: Digitalised Yellow Book
results.proposal: Digitalised Yellow Book. Citizen complaints, suggestions and compliments are a critical source of feedback for improving public services, but paper-based or handwritten submissions can be slow to process, difficult to classify and harder to analyse systematically. Portugal’s Digitalised Yellow Book initiative addresses this problem by modernising the traditional Livro Amarelo, the formal channel through which citizens provide feedback on public services. The broader electronic service is already available through gov.pt, where citizens can submit complaints about public services or public entities, and the complaints are sent directly to the responsible entity with legal value equivalent to the physical complaints book. The AI-specific project described by OECD.AI focuses on digitising handwritten complaint reports. The operational problem is that handwritten submissions require manual transcription and interpretation before they can be evaluated, routed and analysed. By applying AI to recognise and classify handwritten text, the initiative can convert unstructured citizen input into structured data more quickly and consistently. At a conceptual level, the system supports administrative accountability by improving the data pipeline behind complaints management: it does not replace the citizen’s right to complain or the authority’s duty to respond, but helps process and evaluate submissions more efficiently. The expected impact is shorter processing times, improved evaluation standards, more consistent support for users and better analytical insight into recurring service problems. The case is relevant because it applies AI to a foundational accountability mechanism in public administration.

results.title: Virtual civil servant - Galati City Hall
results.proposal: Virtual civil servant - Galati City Hall. Municipal service desks often receive recurring questions about planning, taxes, fees, local revenues and procedural requirements, creating pressure on front-office staff and delays for citizens. Galați City Hall’s virtual civil servant initiative addresses this problem by testing an AI-based assistant that can provide information to citizens on local administrative topics. The operational challenge is that local public-service information can be fragmented across departments and written in technical or legal language, while citizens need immediate and understandable answers about what applies to their situation. The Galați virtual assistant is intended to offer a conversational interface for common enquiries, particularly in areas such as town planning, taxes, fees and other local revenues. According to the OECD.AI entry, the assistant was launched after the Cluj initiative and was still being trained and tested at the time of reporting. At a conceptual level, the tool functions as an AI-supported public-information assistant: it can help users navigate administrative topics, but it should not be treated as making binding administrative decisions or replacing official case handling. The expected impact is easier access to municipal information, reduced workload for employees handling routine questions and faster guidance for citizens who otherwise need to search across web pages or contact offices directly. The case is relevant because it reflects the early diffusion of “virtual civil servant” models across Romanian local government. It also shows that municipal AI adoption is still at an experimental stage, where training, testing and content validation are central before wider citizen-facing use.

results.title: Virtual civil servant - Local public administration in Cluj
results.proposal: Virtual civil servant - Local public administration in Cluj. Local public administrations face increasing pressure to provide faster, more accessible and more responsive services while managing repetitive administrative procedures with limited staff capacity. The Cluj virtual civil servant initiative explores how AI-based assistants can support the digitisation of local administrative processes and improve interactions between citizens and municipal services. The operational problem is that many citizen requests require basic information, document verification, routing to the correct office or guidance through procedures that can be repetitive for staff but confusing for users. An AI-based “virtual civil servant” can act as a first-line interface, helping citizens understand procedures, prepare requests and obtain information without immediately requiring direct human intervention. At the same time, it can support civil servants by reducing repetitive workloads and enabling staff to focus on more complex cases requiring judgement, legal interpretation or personal assistance. The OECD.AI entry states that the initiative began in Cluj as part of the digitisation of procedures and citizen services, before similar experimentation appeared in Galați. At a conceptual level, the Cluj model represents a conversational administrative support layer, not an autonomous public authority: the system can provide guidance and process support, while public officials remain responsible for formal decisions. The expected impact is shorter response times, better service accessibility, more efficient administrative workflows and increased user-friendliness in local government. The case is relevant because it shows how Romanian municipalities are experimenting with natural-language AI in everyday public governance rather than only in national digital strategies.

results.title: Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) - AI for urban mobility
results.proposal: Intelligent Transport Systems (ITS) - AI for urban mobility. Transport authorities need integrated data and digital infrastructure to manage congestion, public transport, road safety, emissions and multimodal travel information. Malta’s Integrated Transport Management Systems initiative addresses this need by developing an ITMS platform that will support the country’s National Access Point and interact with existing intelligent transport systems. The operational problem is that transport data are often distributed across traffic-management tools, travel-information services, infrastructure systems and policy-planning processes. Without an integrated communication layer, it is difficult to provide interoperable mobility information, coordinate traffic management or prepare for more advanced forms of automated decision support. Transport Malta describes the ITMS platform as part of an effort to improve the safety and efficiency of road-based transport systems by making better use of digital technologies and information services, while encouraging a shift to lower-emission transport modes. The platform is intended to integrate with existing intelligent transport systems and accommodate future systems deployed under Malta’s National Transport Strategy and Transport Master Plan. Importantly, the source frames AI as a future capability: the communication layer may later enable advanced computer analysis and automated decision support using AI to simulate, predict and plan traffic-management operations in a multimodal environment. The expected impact is better mobility-data interoperability, stronger traffic-management capability and a foundation for future AI-enabled planning. The case should therefore be presented as a digital transport infrastructure project with potential AI functionality, not as a confirmed operational AI deployment.

results.title: agrifoodTEF - innovative AI and robotics applications for the Austrian agricultural and food industry
results.proposal: agrifoodTEF - innovative AI and robotics applications for the Austrian agricultural and food industry. Agriculture and food production are facing simultaneous pressure from climate change, biodiversity loss, labour shortages, resource constraints, animal-health needs and increasing demands for sustainability. agrifoodTEF addresses these challenges by providing testing and experimentation facilities where companies, start-ups, researchers and users can test AI and robotics solutions under real or realistic conditions. The operational problem is that many AI and robotics tools for agriculture remain stuck between laboratory development and market adoption because they need validation in heterogeneous field, farm and food-production environments. agrifoodTEF provides physical and digital test environments that help developers assess whether their technologies work reliably in practice before wider commercial deployment. In Austria, the initiative creates national test environments for innovative AI and robotics applications tailored to the needs of the agricultural and food sectors. The Austrian consortium includes Josephinum Research, Raumberg-Gumpenstein Research & Development and the University of Applied Sciences Wiener Neustadt. At a conceptual level, agrifoodTEF is an innovation infrastructure rather than a single AI product: it helps validate tools for precision agriculture, food-quality monitoring, robotics, animal-health applications and resource optimisation. The expected impact is stronger collaboration between users, technology providers and research centres, improved competitiveness of the agri-food sector and more sustainable production processes. The case is relevant because it shows how public-sector innovation policy can support AI adoption by reducing the testing and validation gap between prototype and market readiness.

results.title: A chatbot to protect the identities of those reporting school bullying
results.proposal: A chatbot to protect the identities of those reporting school bullying. School bullying is often under-reported because victims and witnesses fear reprisals, social exposure or being identified indirectly through the details of their report. The Petscraft project led by Inria addresses this problem by exploring an AI-based chatbot capable of receiving reports while protecting the identity of the person submitting them. The operational challenge is subtle: anonymity is not achieved simply by removing a name, because free-text reports can contain clues about a pupil’s class, schedule, relationship network, writing style, location or personal circumstances. A large language model might also infer personal traits or identity markers from apparently harmless text. The project therefore focuses on privacy-enhancing technologies that can filter, rewrite or transform the report so that the school receives useful information about the incident while reducing the risk that the reporter can be identified. The approach is first tested on public datasets before being applied to sensitive bullying-reporting material, which is important given the vulnerability of minors and the seriousness of the information involved. At a conceptual level, the chatbot acts as an anonymisation layer between the reporter and the institution: it encourages disclosure, protects the person raising the alert and helps schools detect and respond to bullying more effectively. The case is relevant because it applies AI not to surveillance or discipline, but to safer reporting and privacy-preserving child protection. Petscraft itself is an Inria project team created with INSA Centre Val de Loire and the University of Orléans, focused on privacy-enhancing technologies.

results.title: AI4CCAM - Trustworthy AI for Connected, Cooperative and Automated Mobility
results.proposal: AI4CCAM - Trustworthy AI for Connected, Cooperative and Automated Mobility. Connected, cooperative and automated mobility depends increasingly on AI systems that must interpret complex road environments, anticipate the behaviour of vulnerable road users and support safe vehicle decision-making. AI4CCAM addresses the problem that automated-vehicle AI cannot be evaluated only on technical performance: it must also be explainable, robust, unbiased, secure and acceptable to users, pedestrians, cyclists and other road actors. The project develops an open environment for integrating trustworthy-by-design AI models into CCAM scenarios, with particular attention to vulnerable road-user behaviour anticipation in urban traffic conditions. At a technical level, AI4CCAM works on AI-based scenario management, pedestrian and cyclist behaviour anticipation using elements such as visual-gaze estimation, explainable ego-car trajectory prediction and simulation of ethical dilemmas. The project also uses generative adversarial networks and metamorphic testing techniques to multiply and stress-test scenarios. At a governance level, it includes a participatory space where stakeholders and the public can explore risks, biases, cybersecurity issues and ethical questions related to automated driving. The expected impact is safer and more socially acceptable deployment of AI in automated mobility, supported by validated use cases and evidence on user acceptance. The case is significant because it treats AI for automated vehicles as a socio-technical system: the model must not only predict movement, but also operate transparently in environments where people need to trust and understand automated behaviour.

results.title: DVPS ('Diversibus Viis Plurima Solvo') - creating a new generation of artificial intelligence models
results.proposal: DVPS ('Diversibus Viis Plurima Solvo') - creating a new generation of artificial intelligence models. Current artificial-intelligence systems remain strong at processing digital representations such as text, images and video, but they are still limited when they need to understand real-world context across several sensory channels at once. DVPS, or “Diversibus Viis Plurima Solvo”, addresses this limitation by developing multimodal foundation models that combine linguistic, visual, auditory and sensory inputs to build more grounded representations of the physical world. The operational challenge is that many high-value applications require contextual awareness rather than isolated signal processing: simultaneous translation in a noisy environment requires knowing who is speaking; cardiology applications may require linking imaging data with physiological patterns; disaster-management tools may need to combine satellite, drone and environmental signals. DVPS therefore focuses on models that can learn across modalities, transfer knowledge between domains and adapt more efficiently when labelled data are limited. The project will develop AutoDVPS, an open-source toolkit for multimodal foundation-model design, pre-training, fine-tuning and modality expansion, as well as DVPSBench, a benchmarking suite for assessing performance, robustness and ethical implications. The expected impact is to strengthen Europe’s capacity in next-generation AI by producing reusable methods, open assets and demonstrators in language communication, cardiology and geo-intelligence. The case is relevant because it goes beyond language-model deployment and targets foundational AI capabilities for real-world interaction. Translated announced the initiative with EUR 29 million in backing and 20 partners across nine countries, while CORDIS lists the Horizon Europe grant agreement as running from 1 July 2025 to 30 June 2029.

evidence.quote: The case is relevant because it goes beyond language-model deployment and targets foundational AI capabilities for real-world interaction.

results.memo: Proceed. DVPS ('Diversibus Viis Plurima Solvo') - creating a new generation of artificial intelligence models is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Roboref - Generative AI in the Randers Municipality
results.proposal: Roboref - Generative AI in the Randers Municipality. Meeting documentation is a persistent administrative burden in public organisations, particularly where staff must record decisions, action points and discussion summaries while also participating actively in the meeting itself. Roboref addresses this problem by using speech-to-text and generative AI to record, transcribe and draft meeting summaries. In Randers Municipality, the tool is being tested by a selected group of employees for internal meetings. The operational problem is that manual note-taking can be time-consuming, uneven in quality and potentially distracting for employees who need to listen, contribute and capture key points at the same time. Roboref automates the first draft of meeting documentation by recording the meeting, converting speech into text and generating structured summaries or notes. At a conceptual level, the tool acts as an AI notetaker: it does not replace human validation, but produces a draft that can be reviewed, corrected and finalised by staff. The expected impact is time savings, more consistent meeting records, better objectivity in documentation and improved ability for employees to focus on the substance of meetings rather than on note-taking. The case is relevant because it represents one of the most common practical uses of generative AI in public administration: reducing documentation work without transferring decision-making authority to the system. It also requires clear governance on consent, recording, data protection and the handling of confidential meeting content. RoboRef is described elsewhere as a collaboration involving more than 20 municipalities, organisations, ATP and Droids Agency. (offentlig-ai.dk
results.memo: Proceed. Roboref - Generative AI in the Randers Municipality is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Implementation of AI in the knowledge database in Topdesk
results.proposal: Implementation of AI in the knowledge database in Topdesk. Municipal employees need fast access to internal guidance on IT, accounting, procurement and support processes, but knowledge is often spread across previous tickets, helpdesk articles and staff experience. Randers Municipality’s Ebbot use case integrates an AI chatbot into TOPdesk, the municipality’s IT service-management system, to improve internal support. The operational problem is that employees often submit recurring questions to support teams, while the relevant answer may already exist in a knowledge article or previous case. This creates avoidable workload for support staff and delays for the employee waiting for help. Ebbot acts as a conversational layer over the TOPdesk knowledge base: employees can ask questions in ordinary language, and the chatbot searches previous support cases and knowledge articles to produce a relevant answer. When the system cannot find a suitable response, it helps the user create a support ticket, preserving the escalation route to human support. At a conceptual level, the solution combines chatbot interaction, retrieval from structured knowledge articles and case-history reuse. The expected impact is faster first-line support, more consistent answers, reduced repetitive workload and improved use of existing organisational knowledge. The case is relevant because it applies AI to internal municipal productivity rather than citizen-facing services. By supporting staff with routine administrative and technical questions, the municipality can improve operational continuity and allow specialist support teams to focus on more complex or exceptional issues.

results.title: Gismap AI model for land cover analysis
results.proposal: Gismap AI model for land cover analysis. Municipal planning, biodiversity policy, climate adaptation and environmental reporting require accurate and up-to-date information on land cover, but producing this information manually can be time-consuming and inconsistent. The Gismap use case in Ballerup Municipality applies an AI model to generate land-cover data and combine it with environmental and spatial datasets. The operational problem is that municipalities need to understand how areas are distributed between buildings, roads, vegetation, water, bare ground and other land-cover categories, but traditional mapping may depend on periodic surveys or manual GIS updates. Gismap supports this work by using AI-based classification, editing tools and integration with public geospatial sources. The solution draws on publicly available datasets from Danish authorities, including the Danish Climate Data Agency, GeoDanmark, the Danish Environmental Portal and the Ministry of Environment. At a conceptual level, the model converts aerial, map and environmental data into structured land-cover layers that can support analysis across multiple municipal functions. These outputs can be used for biodiversity registration, operational optimisation, ESG reporting, strategic planning and spatial planning. The expected impact is faster production of land-cover information, better evidence for green-space management, improved environmental reporting and more efficient use of GIS capacity. The case is relevant because it shows how AI can strengthen ordinary planning and environmental administration by converting existing public data into decision-ready spatial information. It should be seen as a municipal geospatial-AI support tool rather than an autonomous planning decision system.
results.memo: Proceed. Gismap AI model for land cover analysis is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Paris Hospitals Use AI for ICU Bed Allocation and Mortality Prediction
results.proposal: Paris Hospitals Use AI for ICU Bed Allocation and Mortality Prediction. Intensive-care coordination becomes especially difficult when hospitals face sudden surges in critically ill patients, as happened during the COVID-19 crisis. The Paris hospitals use case concerns the reported use of AI to support ICU bed planning, patient transfer decisions and mortality-risk prediction across Assistance Publique – Hôpitaux de Paris. The operational problem is that ICU capacity depends on rapidly changing factors: bed availability, ventilator use, staff capacity, laboratory results, patient comorbidities, ambulance flows and local disease pressure. If these data are outdated or fragmented, hospitals may lose valuable time when deciding where a patient should be treated. The reported system uses federated learning so that predictive models can be trained across hospitals without centralising sensitive patient data. LSTM-based forecasting models are described as predicting ICU occupancy from clinical and operational indicators, while a triage module ranks patients according to survival probability and expected resource need. At a conceptual level, the system combines capacity forecasting, mortality-risk modelling and operational coordination, allowing emergency departments, ambulance dispatch and hospital managers to align transfers more effectively. The expected impact is faster ICU transfers, better use of beds, staff and ventilators, more accurate planning during surges and clearer information for families. However, this case should be handled cautiously: the available source is a secondary article, and I did not find an official AP-HP source confirming the exact metrics or system architecture. results.title: EDF Leverages AI to Predict Grid Stress During Heatwaves
results.proposal: EDF Leverages AI to Predict Grid Stress During Heatwaves. Electricity systems face increasing stress during extreme heat, when cooling demand rises, grid components operate under thermal constraints and localised overloads may develop quickly. The EDF use case described in the available secondary source concerns an AI system intended to predict grid stress during heatwaves and help operators prepare corrective actions before outages occur. The operational problem is that conventional monitoring can be reactive: operators may detect stress once transformers, substations or local networks are already close to operational limits. The reported system combines weather forecasts, consumption patterns, transformer loads and local events to model stress on high-voltage and regional grids, using transformer-based forecasting and graph neural networks. At a conceptual level, the model treats the electricity grid as a spatial and temporal system: network components influence one another, while weather and demand conditions evolve over time. Forecasts can then be presented through GIS-enhanced dashboards, allowing operators to identify vulnerable areas and consider mitigation measures such as demand shedding, battery dispatch or industrial load adjustment. The expected impact would be faster response, reduced outages, better voltage stability and more targeted protection of ageing grid assets during heatwaves. However, the evidence for this specific deployment is weak. The main source is DigitalDefynd, and I did not find an EDF source confirming the reported Rhône-Alpes results, the exact modelling architecture or the stated impact figures. EDF does publicly describe AI as a major part of its R&D strategy, but not this specific heatwave-stress system in the sources found.

results.title: ChatPat - Virtual assistant
results.proposal: ChatPat - Virtual assistant. Citizens, businesses and professionals often need to identify the correct public service, understand eligibility requirements and access online forms without knowing the internal administrative terminology used by public bodies. ChatPaT addresses this problem by providing a virtual assistant for the public services of the Autonomous Province of Trento. The operational objective is to reduce search time and make provincial services easier to find, understand and use. The assistant allows users to ask questions in natural language and receive immediate answers based on official information from the Province’s Service Catalogue, including direct links to detailed pages and online forms. It supports Italian, English, German, French, Spanish and Portuguese, and is available every day at any time. At a conceptual level, ChatPaT uses retrieval-augmented generation to connect colloquial user questions with the formal taxonomy of administrative services. The technical architecture is based on Microsoft Azure, including Azure AI Search, Azure Document Intelligence, Azure Functions and Azure AI Foundry, with production infrastructure hosted on an ACN-qualified cloud environment. The service includes privacy safeguards: conversations are anonymised, personal data are not intentionally requested or stored, and any personal data provided accidentally are removed before saving the conversation. The expected impact is improved access to digital public services, reduced burden on information offices, better multilingual support and continuous refinement through anonymised feedback and usage metrics. The case is significant because it combines generative AI, official-source retrieval, privacy-by-design and public-service usability in a controlled provincial-government setting.

results.title: AI Mobility Challenge - Dynamik Allocator
results.proposal: AI Mobility Challenge - Dynamik Allocator. Mobile workers such as service technicians, inspectors, maintenance staff and field personnel often travel between multiple tasks during the day, and inefficient scheduling can create unnecessary driving, fuel use, emissions and lost working time. Dynamik Allocator, developed by Paavo Kytölä and Anita Kuitunen, addresses this problem by using AI to optimise daily routes and task allocation for mobile workers. The operational problem is that manual scheduling may not fully account for geography, time windows, task duration, staff availability and route efficiency. Even small inefficiencies repeated across many workers and days can produce significant emissions and costs. Dynamik Allocator proposes to arrange job sequences and schedules more intelligently, minimising redundant travel while preserving operational requirements. At a conceptual level, the tool treats field-service work as a routing and allocation optimisation challenge: AI can analyse tasks, locations and constraints to recommend sequences that reduce unnecessary kilometres. The expected impact is lower work-related travel emissions, reduced fuel consumption, time savings for organisations and more predictable field operations. The case is relevant because it connects climate objectives with internal organisational logistics, showing that emission reductions can come not only from major infrastructure projects but also from smarter allocation of everyday work. In a municipal context, such tools could support maintenance crews, social-service visits, inspection units or other teams that move across the city. The available source describes the solution within Espoo’s AI Mobility Challenge, so it should be framed as challenge-stage development or potential pilot rather than an implemented municipal routing system.

results.title: AI Mobility Challenge - Traffic Info
results.proposal: AI Mobility Challenge - Traffic Info. Mobility information is only useful if people can access it quickly, understand it and apply it to their journey decisions. In multilingual urban environments, standard traffic bulletins or map-based alerts may not be equally accessible to all residents, commuters or visitors. Traffic Info, presented by Cadweiser during Espoo’s AI in Mobility Challenge, addresses this issue by using AI to generate traffic updates and announcements in natural language, both written and spoken. The operational problem is that traffic data may exist in structured systems, but users need understandable messages in the language and format most convenient to them. Traffic Info proposes a multilingual AI layer that can transform transport information into accessible announcements, improving communication about disruptions, congestion, route changes or travel conditions. At a conceptual level, the system connects mobility data with language generation: raw traffic information is translated into user-facing communication that can be delivered through speech or text. The expected impact is better access to real-time mobility information, improved inclusion for residents and visitors with different language backgrounds, smoother journey planning and potentially more efficient traffic flow as users adjust behaviour based on clearer information. The case is significant because it focuses on communication as a mobility intervention. Better transport systems do not only require sensors and infrastructure; they also require people to receive the right information in a usable form. Like the other Espoo challenge entries, Traffic Info should be classified as a solution in development or pilot preparation rather than a confirmed deployed municipal service.

results.title: AI Mobility Challenge - 0Flow
results.proposal: AI Mobility Challenge - 0Flow. Urban freight and service logistics generate emissions when vehicles travel with unused capacity, poorly coordinated routes or unnecessary trips. 0Flow, presented by Finnish Logistics Group during Espoo’s AI in Mobility Challenge, addresses this problem by using AI and data to improve utilisation of transport capacity. The operational problem is that many freight trips are not fully loaded or are planned without a complete view of available capacity, demand and routing possibilities. This creates avoidable traffic, emissions and operating costs. 0Flow proposes to optimise freight loads and route planning so that vehicles make better use of available space and reduce underutilised movements. At a conceptual level, the system treats urban logistics as an optimisation problem: available vehicles, parcels, destinations, time windows and route constraints can be analysed together to identify more efficient combinations. AI can support matching demand with capacity, grouping deliveries, reducing empty or partially empty trips and improving operational planning. The expected impact is lower transport-related emissions, fewer unnecessary kilometres, improved logistics efficiency and better use of existing vehicle fleets. The case is relevant because city climate strategies often focus on passenger mobility, while freight and service traffic also contribute materially to emissions and congestion. 0Flow shows how AI can support the less visible logistics layer of urban mobility. However, it should be framed as a challenge-stage solution under development, not as an already implemented citywide freight-optimisation platform.
results.memo: Proceed. AI Mobility Challenge - 0Flow is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI Mobility Challenge - CamTalks
results.proposal: AI Mobility Challenge - CamTalks. Smart-city cameras can support traffic and public-space management, but they also raise privacy concerns if raw images are transmitted, stored or analysed centrally. CamTalks, presented by NinjaLabo during Espoo’s AI in Mobility Challenge, addresses this tension by using edge computing to analyse camera feeds locally. The operational problem is that city authorities may want information such as how many people are present in a scene, whether a space is crowded, or whether mobility conditions are changing, but they do not necessarily need to retain identifiable images. CamTalks processes video data on site rather than sending raw footage to the cloud, allowing users to ask simple questions such as “how many people are in the picture?” and receive an answer based on local AI analysis. At a conceptual level, the system turns camera feeds into metadata while reducing exposure of personal data. This is important because urban AI systems must balance situational awareness with citizens’ rights to privacy and proportionality. The expected impact is improved real-time understanding of urban movement, better support for transport or event management, and reduced data-protection risks compared with centralised video analytics. The case is relevant because it shows a privacy-preserving design principle for AI-enabled cities: computation can be moved to the edge, and only necessary outputs can be shared. It should be treated as a challenge-stage or potential pilot solution, since the available source describes it as one of several ideas being refined within Espoo’s AI Mobility Challenge.

results.title: AI Mobility Challenge - DataTalks
results.proposal: AI Mobility Challenge - DataTalks. Cities increasingly collect mobility, parking, weather and infrastructure data, but much of this information remains difficult for residents and visitors to use in everyday decisions. DataTalks, presented by NinjaLabo during Espoo’s AI in Mobility Challenge, addresses this problem by creating a natural-language interface to urban data. The operational problem is that users may need to combine several sources of information before making a simple mobility choice: whether there is parking available, whether weather conditions make walking or cycling practical, or whether a trip can be planned more efficiently. DataTalks connects to different data interfaces and allows users to ask ordinary-language questions such as whether there is space in a specific parking garage and whether they need an umbrella outside. At a conceptual level, the service acts as a conversational data broker: it translates a user’s practical question into queries against parking, weather and potentially other urban datasets, then returns an integrated answer. The expected impact is easier access to city data, reduced unnecessary driving, smarter journey planning and better use of existing infrastructure. The case is significant because it demonstrates how AI can make open or municipal data more actionable for non-technical users. Rather than presenting a dashboard that requires interpretation, the tool provides answers in a form closer to how people make daily travel decisions. It remains a challenge-stage solution rather than a confirmed deployed municipal service, but it illustrates a promising direction for AI-enabled citizen mobility support.

results.title: Similis: for the identification of similar and identical amendments
results.proposal: Similis: for the identification of similar and identical amendments. Parliamentary amendment procedures can generate very large numbers of texts, many of which are identical or highly similar. This creates a practical burden for legislative offices, committees and parliamentary staff who must organise, compare and process amendments efficiently. Similis was developed by the IT Department of the Italian Senate in collaboration with the Institute of Legal Informatics and Judicial Systems of the National Research Council to calculate similarity between Senate amendments. The operational problem is that duplicate or near-duplicate amendments can slow legislative analysis, make debates harder to organise and reduce the transparency of the amendment-review process. Similis addresses this by automatically comparing amendment texts and grouping those with similar wording. The system is oriented towards syntactic similarity rather than full semantic interpretation, meaning that it is particularly useful for identifying amendments with similar structure, vocabulary and phrasing. At a conceptual level, each amendment is represented computationally and compared against others so that clusters of similar texts can be identified. The GitHub repository indicates that the tool can be invoked either through a REST interface or from the command line using a JSON file containing amendments. The expected impact is more efficient parliamentary document management, faster identification of duplicated proposals, better organisation of legislative work and support for transparency in amendment handling. The case is relevant because it demonstrates a focused, explainable and open-source digital tool for legislative support, rather than a broad autonomous AI system.
