results.title: AI4grids - AI - based planning and operational management of distribution grids
results.proposal: AI4grids - AI - based planning and operational management of distribution grids. Electricity distribution networks face increasing pressure from renewable generation, electric vehicles, heat pumps and changing consumption patterns. AI4Grids developed AI-based methods to support the planning and operational management of medium- and low-voltage distribution grids and microgrids. The operational problem is that solar and wind generation fluctuate, while new flexible loads can create local congestion or instability if not coordinated intelligently. The implementation develops algorithms for grid-state monitoring, load forecasting, renewable-generation prediction and operational recommendations. At a conceptual level, the system combines automated network-structure monitoring with weather and consumption data to build a more complete picture of grid conditions. In the event of a fault or abnormal operating state, AI-based control logic can generate recommendations for the control centre, helping operators restore stability more quickly. The expected impact is better integration of renewable energy, reduced need for costly grid over-dimensioning, improved reliability and more efficient use of existing infrastructure. The case is significant because it applies AI to a concrete energy-transition bottleneck: distribution grids must become more intelligent if decentralised generation and flexible demand are to be integrated at scale.

results.title: AI Model Combining Speech and Brain Activity for Depression Diagnosis
results.proposal: AI Model Combining Speech and Brain Activity for Depression Diagnosis. Depression diagnosis often relies on interviews, questionnaires and clinical judgement, which can be affected by subjectivity, limited appointment time and differences in how symptoms are expressed. Researchers at Kaunas University of Technology developed a multimodal AI model that combines speech patterns and brain activity to support more objective recognition of major depressive disorder. The operational problem is that single-source diagnostic signals may be insufficient: speech can capture changes in pace, intonation and energy, while EEG data can reflect brainwave activity under controlled conditions. The implementation uses voice recordings and EEG signals converted into spectrograms, then analysed through a modified DenseNet-121 deep-learning architecture. At a conceptual level, the model treats audio and brain signals as complementary representations of mental-state information, using deep learning to classify whether a person is healthy or affected by depression. The expected impact is faster assessment, potential support for remote screening and reduced reliance on purely subjective interpretation. The case should be framed as research rather than clinical deployment, because further clinical trials, explainability improvements and validation are required before such a system could be used safely in healthcare settings.

results.title: INCISIVE - Improving cancer diagnosis and prediction with AI and big data
results.proposal: INCISIVE - Improving cancer diagnosis and prediction with AI and big data. Cancer diagnosis increasingly depends on combining imaging, clinical information and specialist interpretation, but medical data are often fragmented across institutions and difficult to reuse securely for AI development. INCISIVE addressed this challenge by developing AI-based decision-support tools and a federated data repository for cancer imaging and associated clinical data. The operational problem was to improve the accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, interpretability and cost-effectiveness of cancer-imaging methods while respecting data-protection requirements. The implementation created an interoperable repository of anonymised medical images and clinical data, allowing AI models to be trained and validated across distributed European datasets without relying on a single centralised data pool. At a conceptual level, INCISIVE combines federated data governance, explainable AI services and clinical decision-support pipelines for breast, lung, prostate and colorectal cancer. The expected impact is better detection, staging, monitoring and risk assessment, as well as stronger European capacity to develop reliable AI tools for oncology. The use case is significant because it links AI performance to trustworthy data infrastructure, recognising that clinical AI depends as much on secure, representative and interoperable datasets as on model design.

results.title: Estonia to give citizens Alexa-like access to public services
results.proposal: Estonia to give citizens Alexa-like access to public services. Digital public services can still be difficult to use when citizens must navigate multiple portals, forms and institutional websites to complete a life event or obtain an answer. Estonia’s Bürokratt initiative aims to create a network of public-sector virtual assistants that allow people to interact with the state in natural language. The operational problem is that even highly digital government systems can remain fragmented from the user’s perspective, especially when a request requires cooperation between different agencies. The implementation concept connects chatbots across public-sector institutions into a shared assistant network. At a conceptual level, a citizen can ask a question or request a service through a conversational interface, while the system identifies the relevant institution, retrieves information and, where possible, supports service routing or administrative action. The longer-term vision is for personalised AI agents to cooperate across domains and help citizens solve problems without navigating complex portals or repeating information. The expected impact is simpler access to public services, better customer support, reduced administrative friction and more human-centred digital government. The initiative is significant because it moves beyond isolated chatbots towards an interoperable assistant layer for the public sector, building on Estonia’s wider digital-state infrastructure.

results.title: Automatic identification of individual risk factors in social care and healthcare
results.proposal: Automatic identification of individual risk factors in social care and healthcare. Social exclusion among young adults can arise from interacting health, social, educational and economic factors, making it difficult for professionals to identify early patterns using service records in isolation. Eksote, the South Karelia social and healthcare district, worked with Fujitsu on an AI model to identify factors associated with social exclusion and related risks. The operational problem was to understand which combinations of service-use patterns, health records or social-care indicators were associated with later adverse outcomes, so that welfare professionals could improve prevention. The implementation used pseudonymised data from Eksote services and machine-learning methods to identify risk factors defined by professionals. At a conceptual level, the model analyses historical service data, identifies statistical relationships with social-exclusion outcomes and produces an overview of factors associated with increased risk. Its expected value is to support service planning, professional awareness and research on early intervention. Importantly, the system was constrained by Finnish rules on secondary and combined use of healthcare data: the model could not be used to identify individual young adults at risk without additional legal or consent arrangements. The case is therefore best framed as a modelling and risk-factor analysis project rather than a fully operational individual risk-identification system.

results.title: WIL Leak Current - Discover abuse and improper use of benefits
results.proposal: WIL Leak Current - Discover abuse and improper use of benefits. Welfare administrations need to ensure that people who are entitled to benefits receive support while also detecting improper use or abuse of public funds. WIL Lekstroom, a cooperation of municipalities in the Utrecht region, was reported as using algorithms to support detection of abuse and improper use of social-assistance benefits. The operational problem is that benefit-control processes are labour-intensive, and staff may need to identify which cases deserve additional review without checking every file manually. At a conceptual level, the system would use historical benefit, case-management or administrative data to detect patterns associated with previous improper use, then generate signals or risk scores for officials. The expected impact is more targeted investigation, reduced unnecessary checks, improved administrative efficiency and better protection of public resources. However, welfare-fraud prediction is a high-risk area because historical data may reflect biased enforcement patterns and flagged residents may not know that an algorithm influenced additional scrutiny. The system should therefore be understood as decision support only, not as automatic sanctioning or benefit withdrawal. Any responsible use would require clear documentation, explainability, human review, appeal routes and monitoring for discriminatory impact, especially because the affected population may already be socio-economically vulnerable.

results.title: Early school leavers in the municipality of Amersfoort - Estimation of students at risk
results.proposal: Early school leavers in the municipality of Amersfoort - Estimation of students at risk. Preventing early school leaving requires timely identification of pupils whose educational trajectory suggests a higher risk of dropping out before completing their programme. The Amersfoort and Dordrecht use case concerns the use of an algorithm to estimate which students may be at risk of becoming early school leavers. The operational problem is that schools and municipalities may hold relevant signals, such as school changes, grade repetition or attendance-related patterns, but these signals may not be systematically combined for early intervention. At a conceptual level, the algorithm compares current pupils with patterns observed among previous early school leavers and assigns an indication of risk. Professionals can then decide whether additional guidance, counselling or follow-up is appropriate. The intended value is preventive: the model is meant to help education and youth-support services act before disengagement becomes irreversible. The expected impact is better targeting of support, lower dropout rates, more efficient use of guidance capacity and improved educational outcomes. However, the case also raises important governance issues because educational-risk profiling can affect young people’s opportunities and may be difficult to understand or contest. It should therefore be presented as decision support for human professionals, with transparent explanation of the indicators used and safeguards against discriminatory effects.

results.title: Predict which residents have a higher risk of care or debt problems in Twenterand (SyRI)
results.proposal: Predict which residents have a higher risk of care or debt problems in Twenterand (SyRI). Residents experiencing debt, care needs or social vulnerability often interact with multiple services, but early warning signs may remain fragmented until problems become acute. Twenterand’s reported use case concerns profiling residents to map debt and care-related problems, with the aim of identifying people who may need help earlier. The operational problem is that social problems often develop gradually and may only become visible once enforcement, crisis care or intensive support is required. A predictive system can bring together administrative indicators and historical patterns to identify households or individuals whose situation resembles earlier cases of debt escalation or care need. At a conceptual level, the system would classify or prioritise residents according to risk signals, enabling municipal professionals to consider preventive outreach or support. The expected impact is earlier intervention, better coordination between social services, reduced crisis escalation and more efficient targeting of limited municipal capacity. The use case must be handled carefully because it involves potentially sensitive social and financial data, and because predictive profiling can unintentionally stigmatise residents or neighbourhoods. Its legitimacy depends on clear purpose limitation, strong human oversight, transparency to affected people and safeguards ensuring that the system is used to offer support rather than punishment.

results.title: Detection of crime and subversion in the municipality of Nederweert (SyRI system)
results.proposal: Detection of crime and subversion in the municipality of Nederweert (SyRI system). Smaller municipalities can face complex enforcement challenges when criminal or improper activity is hidden behind legal-looking administrative structures, property records or business registrations. Nederweert was reported as using algorithmic methods to support detection of subversive crime. The operational problem is that municipal datasets may contain weak signals of irregularity, but individual records may not be meaningful unless combined with other information. A risk-based system can help identify buildings or cases where paperwork “smacks of suspicious cases”, allowing limited inspection capacity to be focused where further review appears justified. At a conceptual level, such a system would aggregate administrative indicators, score or classify cases and provide signals to officials for follow-up. The expected impact is more efficient local enforcement, earlier identification of hidden misuse of property and better support for multi-agency responses to organised crime. However, the system can also create legal and ethical risks if residents, owners or businesses are profiled through opaque combinations of data. The case therefore needs to be presented as an enforcement-support system requiring human verification, rather than an automated determination of criminal conduct. Transparency and safeguards are particularly important because flagged persons may not know that algorithmic profiling influenced official attention.

results.proposal: Detection of crime and subversion in the municipality of Maastricht (SyRI system). At a conceptual level, the system would process administrative records and other available indicators to flag addresses or cases where the combination of data points appears unusual or suspicious. The expected impact is more targeted inspection, earlier detection of hidden criminal structures and better coordination between municipal services and enforcement partners. The system’s role should be framed as risk signalling for human review, not as automatic proof of wrongdoing. This distinction is important because the consequences of being flagged can be significant, including inspections, enforcement attention or reputational harm. The use case therefore raises strong requirements around explainability, proportionality, auditability and safeguards against discriminatory targeting of neighbourhoods, businesses or residents.

results.title: Using smart algorithms to map whether building or demolishing certain homes improves liveability
results.proposal: Using smart algorithms to map whether building or demolishing certain homes improves liveability. Housing policy can affect liveability through tenure mix, housing type, density, neighbourhood composition, public-space quality and access to services, but the relationship between physical interventions and social outcomes is difficult to assess with simple indicators. Breda’s use case concerns the application of machine-learning methods to investigate whether building or demolishing certain types of homes could improve neighbourhood liveability. The operational problem is that urban-planning decisions often involve long-term effects and many interacting variables, making it hard for decision-makers to isolate which housing interventions are likely to improve local conditions. The implementation concept uses historical and spatial data to detect patterns between housing stock, neighbourhood characteristics and liveability outcomes. At a conceptual level, the model would compare combinations of housing and contextual indicators, identify correlations with liveability measures and support planners in evaluating possible redevelopment scenarios. The expected impact is more evidence-based housing policy, better targeting of regeneration measures and stronger analytical support for decisions on demolition, new construction or housing mix. The system should be understood as a planning-support tool rather than a substitute for political, social and participatory decision-making. Its value depends on combining model outputs with local knowledge, resident engagement and policy judgement.
results.memo: Proceed. Using smart algorithms to map whether building or demolishing certain homes improves liveability is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Identifying people at risk of falling into large debts
results.proposal: Identifying people at risk of falling into large debts. Municipal debt-prevention services increasingly try to intervene before financial problems become unmanageable, because late intervention can lead to enforcement costs, housing insecurity, health impacts and long-term dependence on social support. The Amsterdam use case concerns the use of predictive or data-driven methods to identify residents who may be at risk of accumulating large debts, so that support can be offered earlier. The operational problem is that signs of debt distress may be distributed across different municipal or service-provider datasets, while front-line staff may only become aware of the situation once arrears have already escalated. At a conceptual level, the system would combine available administrative signals, risk indicators and historical patterns to prioritise cases for preventive outreach. The intended value is not to automate sanctions, but to surface possible vulnerability so that human professionals can offer assistance, advice or referral to debt-support services. The expected impact is earlier identification of residents in financial difficulty, better targeting of municipal support, reduced long-term debt escalation and more efficient use of social-service capacity. However, such systems require careful safeguards because financial-risk profiling can reproduce biases in historical data, affect vulnerable households and create opacity around why a person is flagged.

results.title: IT4LIA – Italy for Artificial Intelligence
results.proposal: IT4LIA – Italy for Artificial Intelligence. Advanced AI development requires large-scale computing infrastructure, high-quality data services and technical support that many public administrations, SMEs, start-ups and research organisations cannot build independently. IT4LIA is Italy’s AI Factory initiative, designed to provide national and European users with AI-optimised supercomputing capacity, data-processing tools and related services. The operational problem is that AI adoption in strategic sectors depends on access to high-performance infrastructure and expert support, not only on algorithms. The implementation centres on the CINECA data centre in Bologna, where a new AI-optimised supercomputer is being integrated with existing high-performance computing and cloud systems. At a conceptual level, the factory provides a shared infrastructure layer for developing, training, testing and deploying AI applications in sectors such as agritech, cybersecurity, manufacturing, climate, earth sciences and public administration. The expected impact is stronger Italian and European AI competitiveness, wider access to advanced computing, accelerated innovation by SMEs and start-ups, and better translation of research into operational AI services. The initiative is significant because it treats AI capacity as public strategic infrastructure, linked to EuroHPC and national industrial-policy objectives.

results.title: RePAIR – Reconstructing the Past: Artificial Intelligence and Robotics meet Cultural Heritage
results.proposal: RePAIR – Reconstructing the Past: Artificial Intelligence and Robotics meet Cultural Heritage. Archaeological restoration can involve thousands of damaged fragments whose manual reassembly is extremely slow, uncertain and resource-intensive. RePAIR addresses this problem by combining artificial intelligence, computer vision and robotics to support the reconstruction of fragmented artefacts such as frescoes, vases and amphorae. The operational challenge is that many cultural objects are excavated as large collections of worn, incomplete or irregular pieces, making traditional puzzle-solving methods impractical at scale. The implementation develops technologies that digitise fragments, analyse their shape and visual features, identify possible matches and physically assist reconstruction through robotic systems. At a conceptual level, the project creates a human-in-the-loop restoration workflow: AI helps reduce the search space and propose fragment relationships, while archaeologists and conservators retain expert control over interpretation and validation. The expected impact is faster restoration, recovery of artefacts that would otherwise remain inaccessible, improved documentation and new research capacity for cultural heritage institutions. The project’s significance lies in bringing together advanced robotics and archaeological expertise, demonstrating how automation can support restoration without replacing scholarly judgement or conservation ethics.
results.memo: Proceed. RePAIR – Reconstructing the Past: Artificial Intelligence and Robotics meet Cultural Heritage is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: SNCF collect 3x more customer feedback with AI
results.proposal: SNCF collect 3x more customer feedback with AI. Railway operators need timely and detailed customer feedback to understand service quality, detect weak signals and respond to dissatisfaction before it damages trust. SNCF used AlloReview to improve the collection and analysis of passenger feedback across TER services, particularly in the Grand Est region. The operational problem was that traditional satisfaction surveys were not capturing enough qualitative information, while unsolicited passenger experiences were difficult to process at scale. The implementation combines QR codes, phone numbers, business cards and post-journey feedback mechanisms, allowing travellers to leave comments orally or in writing at different moments of the customer journey. AI-supported real-time analysis processes the resulting verbatims, identifies satisfaction levels and topics raised, and supports scenario-based follow-up. At a conceptual level, the system transforms open-ended voice and text feedback into structured customer intelligence, enabling SNCF to re-engage dissatisfied passengers, reward loyal customers and identify improvement opportunities. The expected impact is richer customer listening, faster detection of recurring problems, better segmentation of passenger satisfaction and stronger customer relationship management. The case demonstrates how AI can be used in transport not only for operations or mobility flows, but also for continuous service-quality improvement through large-scale qualitative analysis.

results.title: Finland Tax Agency AI support
results.proposal: Finland Tax Agency AI support. Tax administrations process large volumes of returns, declarations, payments, risk signals and taxpayer interactions, making them natural candidates for automation and data-driven decision support. The Finnish Tax Administration use case concerns the controlled use of artificial intelligence in taxation, within the legal framework governing tax assessment and administrative procedure. The operational problem is that taxation requires both efficiency and legal certainty: AI can support risk selection, classification, service delivery or internal analysis, but the consequences for taxpayers mean that each use must be assessed separately. The implementation approach is therefore governance-led rather than based on one single model. Different AI solutions may be used for different functions, and the degree of automation depends on the purpose, legal basis and procedural safeguards of each system. At a conceptual level, AI can either generate recommendations for tax officials or, where legally permitted, support more automated processing. The expected impact is more efficient tax administration, improved targeting of checks, better consistency in routine processing and faster taxpayer service. The case is significant because it emphasises that AI in taxation is not merely a technical matter: it must be aligned with administrative-law principles, taxpayer rights, transparency, accountability and the distinction between decision support and independent automated decision-making.

results.title: ChatGPT as a tool for Education
results.proposal: ChatGPT as a tool for Education. Schools and higher-education institutions face a pedagogical challenge when generative AI can produce coherent written answers, summaries and draft texts in response to ordinary prompts. This use case concerns the educational use of ChatGPT not as an autonomous teaching system, but as a tool for critical collaboration between students, teachers and AI-generated text. The operational issue is that students may use the system to produce assignments mechanically, while educators can instead redesign activities so that learners interrogate, verify, contextualise and improve AI outputs. The implementation is therefore mainly pedagogical: ChatGPT can be used to generate examples, draft outlines, propose questions, create exercises, provide writing models, support translation, or produce material that students then analyse against sources and disciplinary knowledge. At a conceptual level, the tool offers syntactically coherent and semantically connected responses, but it does not independently establish a situated, critical or interpretative perspective. The expected impact is a shift from banning AI to teaching students how to question it, evaluate its limitations and use it to accelerate constructive thinking. The case is particularly relevant in arts and humanities education, where human contextualisation, semiotic reading and critical interpretation remain central to the learning process.

results.title: EBB_AI : Co-creation-as-a-Service
results.proposal: EBB_AI : Co-creation-as-a-Service. Cultural institutions and artists face growing demand to use generative AI creatively while protecting copyright, attribution and fair compensation. EBB_AI proposes a Co-creation-as-a-Service platform that allows museums, art schools, contemporary artists, film producers and other cultural partners to create AI-assisted outputs while maintaining rights-holder traceability. The operational problem is that generative AI can remix or derive value from cultural datasets without clear governance, making it difficult for institutions and artists to control use, monetise outputs or ensure recognition. The implementation combines co-creation tools, cultural partner databases, AI content-generation workflows and a blockchain- or NFT-based copyright-management layer. At a conceptual level, users interact with curated cultural assets through AI tools, while the platform records rights information, supports automated compensation and enables digital merchandise or poster creation under controlled conditions. The expected impact is more responsible use of AI in the cultural sector, new revenue models for institutions and artists, improved user engagement and stronger safeguards against untraceable reuse of protected works. The case is important because it addresses one of the central tensions in creative AI: enabling experimentation while embedding mechanisms for copyright, inclusivity, bias reduction and stakeholder compensation.

results.title: DESIGN-IT (DEcision Science desIGN platform for digItal Twins)
results.proposal: DESIGN-IT (DEcision Science desIGN platform for digItal Twins). Industrial organisations increasingly need to model products, machines and processes while integrating simulation, optimisation, machine learning and predictive maintenance into operational decision-making. The implementation aims to provide a drag-and-drop platform where users can combine modelling, simulation, data management, optimisation and explainable AI components. At a conceptual level, the system acts as a configurable environment for creating digital twins at product, component and process levels, then connecting them with AI pipelines for prediction, maintenance and operational optimisation. The expected impact is faster development of industrial AI applications, greater accessibility for non-programmers, improved human-machine collaboration and smarter decision-making in automated manufacturing and robotics contexts. results.title: Digital twins in cultural heritage conservation: Notre-Dame Cathedral
results.proposal: Digital twins in cultural heritage conservation: Notre-Dame Cathedral. Major heritage monuments require detailed documentation for conservation, maintenance and public interpretation, especially where restoration history, structural complexity and visitor pressure create long-term management challenges. The Notre-Dame digital twin project aims to create a highly detailed virtual replica of the cathedral using AI-supported processing of imagery and spatial data. The operational objective is to build an accurate digital record of the cathedral’s interior and exterior, including roof, vaults, stonework, stained glass and architectural details, so that heritage professionals can support conservation and future maintenance. The implementation combines drone imagery, laser scanning, photogrammetry, high-resolution photographs and AI algorithms to integrate the data into a coherent digital model. At a conceptual level, the digital twin acts as both a conservation record and an immersive access tool: it can document physical condition, support analysis of the building fabric and allow remote users to explore the monument virtually. The expected impact is improved heritage preservation, more informed maintenance planning, broader public access and stronger resilience against future damage or loss. The case illustrates how AI and digital twins can support cultural heritage by making complex architectural information usable for both specialists and the public.

results.title: Air quality sensors in Trim (Ireland)
results.proposal: Air quality sensors in Trim (Ireland). Meath County Council’s Trim air-quality project installed sensors in the town to generate hyperlocal environmental information and make it visible through a public dashboard. The operational problem was to provide residents and decision-makers with more granular evidence on pollutants, traffic-related exposure and the health implications of air quality. The implementation combines air-quality sensors, the Meath Environment Platform and Trilateral Research’s STRIAD:AIR platform. At a conceptual level, sensors collect local readings, the platform stores and displays the data, and analytical tools help identify trends and potential health impacts. The expected impact is better public understanding of local air quality, stronger evidence for environmental policy, support for behaviour change and improved ability to assess whether local interventions are working. The use case is relevant because it makes environmental data directly available to residents rather than keeping it only inside council systems. It also supports a more participatory model of climate and air-quality governance, where local evidence can inform both public debate and operational decisions.

results.title: Graz outfits intersection with smart sensors to improve cyclist commute
results.proposal: Graz outfits intersection with smart sensors to improve cyclist commute. The operational problem was that conventional sensor systems can struggle to distinguish between cars, mopeds, bicycles, scooters and other users, limiting the usefulness of traffic data for active-travel policy. The implementation uses light-mounted smart sensors and a GDPR-compliant video analytics platform that applies AI algorithms at the edge to classify traffic and detect behaviours such as bus-lane use by passenger vehicles, illegal turns and red-light violations. At a conceptual level, the system analyses video streams, categorises road users, measures traffic patterns and produces data that can inform future junction design or enforcement priorities. The expected impact is better safety analysis, more evidence-based cycling infrastructure, improved understanding of violations and a lower-cost alternative to infrastructure-heavy monitoring systems. The case is relevant because it shows how AI-enabled sensing can be deployed quickly at existing street infrastructure to support urban mobility and climate-policy goals.

Licensed clinicians then review the recommendations and develop final plans in collaboration with the system, ensuring that professional judgement remains central. The expected impact is reduced administrative planning time, more consistent rehabilitation recommendations, better use of historical data and improved support for patients moving from hospital to municipal rehabilitation services. The case is important because it applies AI to a care-planning workflow where recommendations are decision-support outputs, not automated treatment decisions. results.title: Semantic Analyser – Smart Text Search Engine
results.proposal: Semantic Analyser – Smart Text Search Engine. The operational problem is to help officials analyse collections of laws, proposals, vocabularies and other public-administration texts by identifying key concepts and relationships between them. The implementation uses natural-language processing to extract characteristic concepts from documents, identify concepts that co-occur, group texts with related content and visualise semantic relationships. At a conceptual level, the tool turns terms into links between documents, enabling users to find related materials, identify missing concepts in vocabularies and compare texts across collections. Users can also search by a set of terms and discover documents connected by synonyms, broader terms or related concepts. The expected impact is more efficient document analysis, better management of legal and administrative knowledge, improved development of public-sector vocabularies and stronger reuse of textual data. The use case is important because it shows how AI can support everyday knowledge work in government, especially in smaller-language contexts where off-the-shelf NLP tools may be less mature.

results.title: Forecasting Sweeish GDP with Explainable AI
results.proposal: Forecasting Sweeish GDP with Explainable AI. Macroeconomic forecasting is essential for public financial management, but machine-learning models can be difficult for officials to trust if their predictions are not interpretable. The Swedish National Financial Management Authority developed an explainable-AI application to improve GDP forecasting and help analysts understand the behaviour of black-box models. The operational problem was not only to produce accurate forecasts, but also to make visible which variables influenced a prediction and how their importance changed over time. The implementation used machine-learning forecasting models alongside explainability tools developed in collaboration with a scholar from KTH Royal Institute of Technology. At a conceptual level, the web application analyses the contribution of individual variables to GDP predictions, showing both temporal variation and aggregated effects over longer periods. This allows economists to inspect model behaviour, compare it with domain knowledge and improve forecasting practice. The expected impact is more accountable use of AI in public financial management, better integration of machine learning into economic forecasting and stronger confidence among officials who must interpret forecasts for policy and budgetary purposes. The use case is significant because it focuses on explainability as a core requirement for government AI, rather than treating predictive accuracy alone as sufficient.

results.title: Assisted Living and Safe Aging Services in the Region of Central Macedonia (Greece)
results.proposal: Assisted Living and Safe Aging Services in the Region of Central Macedonia (Greece). Ageing populations create increasing demand for social-care models that help people remain independent at home while reducing isolation and improving safety. The Region of Central Macedonia introduced Assisted Living and Safe Aging Services as a telecare model for elderly people who live alone, have chronic conditions, face health risks or are socially isolated. The operational problem is that older people may need rapid help after a fall, health incident or emergency, but cannot always rely on family members or nearby carers. The implementation combines a 24-hour call centre with trained social workers and psychologists, home monitoring devices, fall-detection systems, panic buttons, outdoor tracking and locator devices. At a conceptual level, the service links personal devices, monitoring infrastructure and human support teams so that alerts can be assessed and responded to quickly. The expected impact is safer independent living, reduced loneliness, faster response to emergencies and greater confidence for elderly people and their families. The service is also important as a preventive social-care intervention: rather than waiting for institutionalisation or crisis, it provides continuous, personalised support that can help people remain in familiar home environments while still being connected to public care services.

results.title: Speeding up judicial proceedings with Transkit, an AI-based tool that transcribes trials
results.proposal: Speeding up judicial proceedings with Transkit, an AI-based tool that transcribes trials. Court proceedings generate large volumes of spoken material that may later need to be searched, quoted, reviewed or used in higher-instance appeals. In the Basque Country, Transkit was developed to reduce the burden of manually reviewing court-session videos and preparing transcripts. The operational problem is that legal staff may need to locate exactly where a phrase was said, who said it, or which named entities were mentioned, but manual video review is slow and does not create searchable text. The implementation uses neural-network-based speech-to-text technology capable of transcribing Spanish, Basque and bilingual Spanish-Basque audio or video content. At a conceptual level, the system converts recorded proceedings into timestamped text, links speech with searchable terms and allows staff to focus on correction, validation and completion rather than full manual transcription. The expected impact is faster judicial administration, improved productivity for clerks and court staff, easier review of appeal material, better searchability of proceedings and more efficient preparation of judgments or records. The tool does not replace official legal validation of transcripts; it provides a draft and search layer that supports human professionals in managing recorded procedural content more efficiently.

results.title: Procurement data quality and CPV improvement for TED data
results.proposal: Procurement data quality and CPV improvement for TED data. European public procurement transparency depends on high-quality, standardised data, but procurement notices can contain missing, inconsistent or incorrectly classified information. The TED data-quality and CPV improvement use case focuses on using AI and natural language processing to improve the quality of Tenders Electronic Daily data and generate more reliable procurement statistics. The operational problem is that Common Procurement Vocabulary codes and notice metadata are essential for search, monitoring, analytics and expenditure analysis, but they may be incomplete or inaccurate when submitted. The implementation concept includes extracting or validating CPV codes from procurement documents, detecting inconsistencies, deriving missing fields, harmonising data and producing improved statistics on expenditure, contractors and contracting authorities. At a conceptual level, NLP models read tender text and metadata, infer likely classifications or corrections, and support data-quality auditing. More advanced analytical objectives include identifying patterns in awards and forecasting likely bidders or awardees under certain tender characteristics. The expected impact is better procurement transparency, more accurate public spending analysis, improved searchability of tenders and stronger evidence for policy, audit and market-intelligence work. The use case is important because high-quality procurement data is a foundation for accountability, competition analysis and anti-corruption monitoring across the EU.
results.memo: Proceed. Procurement data quality and CPV improvement for TED data is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: 5G test field planned in the Port of Duisburg
results.proposal: 5G test field planned in the Port of Duisburg. Inland ports need low-latency, high-capacity connectivity to support automation, traffic control and real-time logistics coordination. The Port of Duisburg 5G test field was designed to explore how private or local 5G infrastructure can improve port operations, especially the partially automated control of container cranes and future smart logistics applications. The operational problem is that conventional connectivity may not provide the responsiveness, reliability or flexibility needed for semi-automated equipment, sensor networks, drones and real-time traffic-management systems. The implementation established a 5G test environment in Europe’s largest inland port, with support from North Rhine-Westphalia’s 5G.NRW funding framework and technology partners including Deutsche Telekom. At a conceptual level, cameras, sensors, industrial equipment and control systems communicate over the 5G network, enabling data to be collected and interpreted rapidly for operational decisions. The expected impact is higher container-handling capacity, more flexible port operations, better congestion prevention and a foundation for future AI- and IoT-enabled logistics use cases. The project illustrates how next-generation connectivity can be a prerequisite for more advanced automation: AI-driven prediction or control depends on timely data transmission from distributed port assets.
results.memo: Proceed. 5G test field planned in the Port of Duisburg is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Intelligent traffic control in the port of Hamburg - various applications
results.proposal: Intelligent traffic control in the port of Hamburg - various applications. Ports are complex logistics ecosystems in which road, rail, vessel, terminal and warehouse operations must be synchronised to avoid congestion, emissions and wasted capacity. Hamburg Port Authority’s smartPORT approach applies digital intelligence to improve the efficiency and sustainability of port operations. The operational problem is that freight movement and traffic flows depend on many actors and real-time conditions, including vessel arrivals, truck movements, parking availability, road capacity, environmental constraints and terminal operations. The implementation uses sensor technology, analysis, forecasting and information systems to support intelligent traffic and goods management. At a conceptual level, data from infrastructure, vehicles, logistics systems and operational platforms are integrated to produce traffic information, forecasts and decision support for port users and managers. This can improve routing, parking, congestion management and the utilisation of existing infrastructure. The expected impact is reduced delays, lower greenhouse-gas and air-pollutant emissions, fewer unnecessary vehicle kilometres, better reliability for logistics operators and stronger environmental performance. The case is important because it treats port digitalisation as a system-level optimisation problem: AI and analytics do not only improve one process, but help coordinate the port as an urban-industrial infrastructure.

results.title: Venice Smart Control Room
results.proposal: Venice Smart Control Room. Managing Venice requires coordination across pedestrian flows, water traffic, road access, tourism pressure, public transport, weather, tides, security and parking. The Venice Smart Control Room was developed as an integrated urban “control tower” to aggregate information from sensors, video feeds, municipal systems and service operators. The operational problem is that Venice’s urban mobility is unusually complex: boats, pedestrians, road transport and tourist flows interact with weather and tidal risks in a fragile historic environment. The implementation, developed by the Municipality of Venice with TIM and local public-safety stakeholders, brings together data on people present in the city, types of boats in canals, water and road transport movement, tourist flows, forecasts and parking. At a conceptual level, the platform combines sensor networks, camera feeds, telecommunications data, urban analytics and predictive modelling to support monitoring and decision-making. It can help detect mobility issues, identify congestion, support public safety and provide evidence for planning. The expected impact is improved city management, faster operational coordination, better regulation of water and land mobility, and more informed decisions during high-pressure events. The case is significant because it combines heritage-city governance with smart-city operations in a territory where urban management has both everyday and exceptional-risk dimensions.

results.title: ‘Outpost’ autonomous towers to monitor Greek islands for threats
results.proposal: ‘Outpost’ autonomous towers to monitor Greek islands for threats. Remote island monitoring requires persistent situational awareness across land, sea and air, but continuous human surveillance can be costly, difficult and operationally limited. “Outpost” is an autonomous surveillance tower concept developed by Lambda Automata for monitoring Greek islands and other remote or sensitive areas. The operational problem is to detect and track diverse possible threats, including people, drones, vessels, aircraft, vehicles and smoke columns, across locations where infrastructure and personnel may be limited. The implementation uses autonomous towers equipped with sensors and artificial-intelligence software for geolocation, classification and tracking. At a conceptual level, the system observes the surrounding environment, processes sensor inputs, classifies detected objects or events and supports operators with alerts or situational information. The expected impact is stronger border and island surveillance, earlier detection of threats, reduced reliance on continuous manual observation and improved response coordination. The use case is security-focused and therefore distinct from civilian smart-city monitoring, but it illustrates a broader pattern in public-sector AI: distributed sensor infrastructure combined with automated classification to provide decision support in environments where rapid detection matters. It also raises typical governance issues around surveillance, oversight, proportionality and the human role in interpreting alerts.
results.memo: Proceed. ‘Outpost’ autonomous towers to monitor Greek islands for threats is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI for Water in Garda Lake area
results.proposal: AI for Water in Garda Lake area. Wastewater-treatment and water-infrastructure operators need to manage variable inflows while controlling energy consumption, maintenance risks and service continuity. The Trentino / Garda-area AI for Water use case involved NIRIS and AI Challenge participants working on data from public water-treatment infrastructure to forecast incoming water variations using historical plant data and meteorological information. The operational problem is that treatment plants consume significant energy, and rainfall-driven changes in inflow can create operational peaks that are expensive or inefficient if not anticipated. The implementation used historical purifier data, weather data from the Stenico area and machine-learning methods to identify correlations between meteorological conditions, anthropic impact and plant behaviour. At a conceptual level, the system learns from past inflow, weather and operational patterns to forecast future water loads, enabling plant managers to prepare equipment and optimise energy use. The expected impact is lower energy consumption, better remote management, improved predictive maintenance and more resilient operation of depuration infrastructure. The use case is notable because it applies AI to a highly practical utility-management problem, where small percentage savings can matter because water-treatment systems operate continuously and at high energy intensity across many plants.
results.memo: Proceed. AI for Water in Garda Lake area is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI for Weather Forecast in Trentino
results.proposal: AI for Weather Forecast in Trentino. Local authorities need reliable warning systems for storms and fast-developing weather events because short lead times can affect emergency management, road safety, civil protection and public communication. In Trentino, the weather-forecasting AI use case focused on supporting MeteoTrentino and the Autonomous Province of Trento by improving the validation and use of weather-station data. The operational problem is that meteorological networks collect large volumes of real-time data from stations across the territory, but missing values, anomalous measurements and inconsistencies between nearby or similar-altitude stations can reduce the quality of warnings and forecasts. The implementation approach used artificial intelligence to identify errors or anomalies in weather data and improve the quality of archived and operational datasets. At a conceptual level, the system compares real-time station values with climatology, neighbouring stations and expected physical patterns, flagging values that may require correction or review before being used in alerts. The expected impact is more reliable weather warnings, better support for local administrators, improved emergency notifications and stronger data quality for climate and weather services. The use case is particularly relevant for mountain territories, where storms can develop rapidly and localised data quality is essential for timely action.
results.memo: Proceed. AI for Weather Forecast in Trentino is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: JustizOnline
results.proposal: JustizOnline. Access to justice can be hindered when citizens and organisations must physically attend court offices or navigate several separate portals to find information, forms and register services. JustizOnline was created as Austria’s digital gateway to the judiciary, bringing together online information, procedural services and access to registers in a single service environment. The operational objective is to reduce unnecessary court visits and help users find relevant functions more quickly, whether they need information on proceedings, court services, forms, the Companies Register, the Land Register or judicial announcements. The implementation includes the chatbot “Justitia”, which guides users to the relevant information and can answer simple justice-related questions. At a conceptual level, the platform combines digital self-service, secure authentication, linked e-government interfaces, register access and conversational navigation. Integration with other Austrian e-government portals reduces duplication by allowing representation and authorisation information to be managed consistently across connected services. The expected impact is easier access to justice, faster completion of routine interactions, fewer administrative barriers and more efficient communication between the judiciary and the public. JustizOnline is important because it treats digital justice as a service ecosystem rather than a single online form, supporting both information needs and transactional access to judicial services.

results.title: Facial and official document recognition to deliver digital identities
results.proposal: Facial and official document recognition to deliver digital identities. Digital public services require reliable remote identification, but traditional identity enrolment can depend on face-to-face registration that is inconvenient for citizens and difficult to scale. The Open Administration of Catalonia developed video-identification capabilities for obtaining digital identity credentials such as idCAT, using facial recognition and official-document recognition. The operational problem is to verify that the person applying remotely is the legitimate holder of the identity document and that the document is genuine, while maintaining security and privacy guarantees equivalent to in-person processes. The implementation asks the user to show both sides of an identity document, performs document checks, captures a selfie and compares the facial image with the image extracted from the document. The process also includes mobile-phone verification and later review by a trained operator. At a conceptual level, the system combines document image analysis, facial comparison, liveness or video evidence, consent capture, audit recording and human validation. The expected impact is easier access to digital identity credentials, reduced need for physical registration, improved inclusion for users who cannot attend offices and stronger uptake of digital public services. The case is relevant because it applies biometric matching in a controlled enrolment process, rather than in open-ended public-space surveillance.

results.title: EUIPO  eSearch Plus
results.proposal: EUIPO  eSearch Plus. Trade mark clearance depends on identifying earlier similar marks, including figurative marks whose similarity may arise from shapes, colours, textures and visual composition rather than text alone. EUIPO’s eSearch Plus image-search functionality supports users searching for similar-looking trade marks and designs in the European Union Intellectual Property Office’s databases. The operational problem is that manual image comparison and Vienna Classification searches can be time-consuming and may miss visually similar marks where keywords or classifications are incomplete. The implementation uses AI-based image-recognition technology to analyse uploaded or selected images and return visually similar trade marks or designs, which users can combine with criteria such as Nice and Vienna classifications. At a conceptual level, the system extracts visual features from an image, compares them with stored intellectual-property images and ranks results by similarity. The expected impact is more efficient trade mark clearance, better support for applicants and representatives, improved monitoring of potentially conflicting marks and stronger quality in IP-search workflows. The tool does not make legal decisions about likelihood of confusion or registrability; it supports human users by surfacing relevant prior rights and visual similarities for further legal assessment.
results.memo: Proceed. EUIPO  eSearch Plus is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: City Shark - Keeping Aarhus harbor clean with a robot
results.proposal: City Shark - Keeping Aarhus harbor clean with a robot. Harbours and urban waterways collect floating waste that is difficult to remove continuously through manual cleaning alone. Aarhus Municipality developed the City Shark project to test robotic and drone-based methods for keeping the harbour cleaner. The operational problem was to collect waste from the water surface efficiently while also exploring how autonomous technology could support environmental management. The core solution was a WasteShark, a sailing drone designed primarily to collect floating rubbish. The project was organised in phases by Aarhus Municipality’s ITK department in collaboration with the Agency for Data Supply and Efficiency, the Port of Aarhus, the City of Aarhus and external suppliers. At a conceptual level, the water drone navigates the harbour, collects waste from the surface and can be combined with other sensor or drone systems to detect pollution such as oil or petrol from the air and guide the water drone to the affected area. The expected impact is cleaner harbour water, reduced manual cleaning effort, greater public visibility of marine litter problems and a testbed for autonomous environmental robotics. The use case demonstrates how relatively small autonomous systems can support municipal environmental services in constrained urban-water settings.

results.title: Urban Intelligence-as-a-Service model for smart lighting upgrade
results.proposal: Urban Intelligence-as-a-Service model for smart lighting upgrade. results.title: Rüsselsheim am Main enforces truck ban with AI to abate pollution
results.proposal: Rüsselsheim am Main enforces truck ban with AI to abate pollution. Air quality and traffic-management measures can be difficult to enforce when they depend on distinguishing specific vehicle types without creating intrusive surveillance. Rüsselsheim am Main introduced an AI-enabled intelligent-infrastructure solution to support enforcement of a ban on trucks weighing 7.5 tonnes or more when they originate outside city limits. The operational problem was to identify vehicles subject to the ban at roads entering and exiting the city while protecting privacy and avoiding manual monitoring. The implementation installed sixteen Velodyne Ultra Puck lidar sensors on street lights along relevant routes. These sensors collect anonymised three-dimensional traffic data that allow an AI-enabled platform to distinguish heavy trucks from other vehicles. At a conceptual level, the system analyses vehicle shape, size and movement patterns rather than relying on facial recognition or licence-plate identification. This enables local officials to understand whether restricted vehicles are entering the city and to generate evidence for traffic-control and environmental-management decisions. The expected impact is improved enforcement of the truck restriction, reduced pollution and noise, better data on freight movement and a foundation for wider traffic and air-quality analytics. The same infrastructure can also support prediction-based traffic management and environmental monitoring, making it a broader smart-city tool rather than a single-purpose enforcement device.

results.title: Municipality of Cologne improves the accuracy of its wastewater taxation system with a geospatial AI system
results.proposal: Municipality of Cologne improves the accuracy of its wastewater taxation system with a geospatial AI system. Wastewater taxation often depends on the amount of impervious surface on private property, because paved or sealed areas increase rainwater runoff into the drainage system. Cologne’s municipal wastewater authority, Stadtentwässerungsbetriebe Köln, worked with Hexagon to improve the accuracy and efficiency of this process using a GeoAI solution. The operational problem was that earlier methods relied heavily on manual inspections and property-owner self-reporting, which made it difficult to detect changes in paved surfaces consistently across the city. The implementation uses aerial imagery, LiDAR mapping and AI-based classification to identify sealed and unsealed surfaces on private land. At a conceptual level, the platform analyses high-resolution geospatial data, detects changes since previous surveys and classifies surfaces that affect drainage-fee calculations. This provides a more accurate basis for wastewater-tax assessment and can also support simulations related to climate adaptation, such as renaturalisation or de-sealing of paved areas. The expected impact is fairer taxation, lower manual workload, improved data quality and better environmental planning. The case shows how GeoAI can support municipal finance and climate resilience at the same time: a taxation dataset becomes useful not only for billing, but also for understanding urban runoff and planning greener surfaces.

results.title: School choice preferences algorithm in the Federation Wallonie-Bruxelles
results.proposal: School choice preferences algorithm in the Federation Wallonie-Bruxelles. Allocating pupils to secondary schools is a sensitive administrative process because families express preferences, schools have limited capacity and authorities must apply common rules fairly. The Federation Wallonie-Bruxelles uses an automatic allocation algorithm in the secondary-school enrolment procedure to rank applications and assign available places. The operational problem is that many pupils apply to multiple schools, and each school may receive more applications than available seats. The implementation uses a preference-optimisation procedure based on deferred acceptance, where pupils list preferred schools, schools rank applicants according to the applicable rules, and the algorithm iteratively assigns places while respecting pupil preferences as far as possible. At a conceptual level, the system creates ordered applicant lists for schools, allocates provisional seats, removes duplicate allocations where pupils receive a place in more than one school, and reassigns freed places to the next pupils on waiting lists. The expected impact is a more transparent, rule-based and consistent enrolment process, reducing ad hoc allocation and making the treatment of preferences more systematic. The algorithmic nature of the procedure also makes it important that families can understand the ranking process, the role of preferences and the avenues for appeal or correction.

results.title: Flora Incognita app – recognise wild plants using an app
results.proposal: Flora Incognita app – recognise wild plants using an app. Biodiversity awareness depends on people being able to recognise the plants around them, but botanical identification can be difficult without specialist knowledge. Flora Incognita addresses this gap through a free mobile application that uses artificial intelligence to identify wild plants from images taken with a smartphone or tablet. The objective is both educational and scientific: users receive immediate help identifying species, while the observations generated through the app can contribute to research on plant distribution, biodiversity change and environmental monitoring. The implementation applies deep-learning models to photographs of plant parts such as flowers, leaves, bark or fruit. At a conceptual level, the app analyses the visual characteristics of the plant, compares them with learned species patterns and returns a likely identification together with supporting information on characteristics, distribution and protection status. Its expected impact is wider public engagement with nature, easier access to botanical knowledge, increased participation in citizen science and better data for conservation research. The app is especially useful for schools, universities, nature-protection initiatives and individual users who want to learn more about local flora. By combining image recognition with educational content and observation recording, Flora Incognita turns everyday encounters with plants into structured biodiversity data and public learning opportunities.

The implementation uses voice-recognition technology to transform speech into text, reducing the need for purely manual typing and helping legal-administrative staff prepare records more efficiently. results.proposal: ITA.CA (Italian Case-Law On Private Antitrust Enforcement ). Private antitrust enforcement depends on access to specialised case law, but judgments in this field can be difficult to locate, compare and analyse across courts. ITA.CA was developed to collect and systematise Italian case law on private enforcement of competition law, initially around the Milan courts and later with broader contributions. The operational problem is that practitioners, judges, scholars and public stakeholders need a coherent view of decisions relating to damages actions, competition infringements and related civil litigation. The implementation uses a structured online database hosted by the Eurojus scientific journal, collecting judgments and organising them so that users can search and analyse relevant material. At a conceptual level, the system combines legal information retrieval, classification, expert curation and rule-based structuring of case-law content. It is not an autonomous legal decision-maker; rather, it supports legal knowledge management by making decisions easier to find and compare. The expected impact is improved legal transparency, better access to antitrust jurisprudence, stronger doctrinal analysis and more consistent understanding of private enforcement across Italy. The case is relevant to digital justice because curated and searchable databases are a foundation for more advanced legal analytics, even when the underlying technology is primarily rule-based or expert-system oriented.

results.title: Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR)
results.proposal: Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR). Road-policing and law-enforcement operations often require rapid identification of vehicles without manual reading or recording of registration plates. Ireland’s Automatic Number Plate Recognition use case concerns deployment of ANPR technology by justice and policing authorities to support traffic and law-enforcement operations. The operational problem is that officers may need to identify vehicles of interest, verify registration information or process large numbers of passing vehicles quickly and accurately. The implementation uses optical character recognition, later capable of being augmented by artificial-intelligence techniques, to read and record vehicle registration plates automatically from camera feeds. At a conceptual level, the system captures an image of a vehicle plate, converts it into text, compares it with relevant records or alert lists, and produces information for policing or administrative follow-up. The expected impact is faster identification of vehicles, more efficient enforcement, reduced manual input, and stronger operational capacity in roads policing. The technology also raises privacy and governance questions because vehicle movements can reveal sensitive information about individuals’ behaviour. For that reason, legal authorisation, retention rules, access controls and oversight are important elements of responsible deployment. The tool should be understood as an investigative and traffic-management support capability rather than an autonomous sanctioning system.

results.title: AI to anonymise judicial courts in Denmark
results.proposal: AI to anonymise judicial courts in Denmark. Judicial transparency depends on publishing court judgments in a form that is accessible to the public, while privacy law requires that parties and other individuals are protected from unnecessary identification. Denmark’s court judgment anonymisation project supports publication of decisions in Domsdatabasen, the Danish courts’ judgment database, by using machine learning to pseudonymise judgments before they are made public. The operational problem is that judgments contain names, pronouns, descriptions, contextual details and other linguistic elements that can reveal identity directly or indirectly. The implementation uses a machine-learning system to pre-screen documents and suggest text passages that may need anonymisation or pseudonymisation. At a conceptual level, the solution combines named-entity recognition, privacy-risk detection, text marking and human quality control. Each judgment is reviewed by human participants after the software has identified potentially sensitive content, creating a hybrid workflow in which AI accelerates the process but does not make publication decisions alone. The expected impact is faster preparation of judgments, more consistent protection of personal data, broader access to case law and better public understanding of judicial practice. The system is particularly important because anonymisation quality affects both privacy and the usefulness of judgments for legal analysis.

The operational challenge is that courts produce large volumes of decisions, and manual anonymisation can be slow, inconsistent and resource-intensive. Its purpose is not only to remove personal data, but also to preserve the legal meaning of the decision so that judges, lawyers, researchers, businesses and citizens can search and understand case law. The expected impact is greater transparency, faster publication of judgments, improved consistency in anonymisation and stronger public access to judicial information. The initiative also sits within a wider digital-justice agenda, including e-communication between courts, prosecutors, litigants and other justice stakeholders.

results.title: Crowdsorsa - City of Helsinki
results.proposal: Crowdsorsa - City of Helsinki. Municipalities need up-to-date information on the condition of roads, cycle lanes, public infrastructure and environmental assets, but comprehensive field surveys can be costly and slow. Crowdsorsa applies gamification and crowdsourcing to urban data collection, allowing citizens to complete location-based missions through a mobile app while collecting GPS-tagged photos or videos. In Helsinki, the approach has been used for tasks such as surveying road and cycle-lane conditions, mapping infrastructure assets and supporting environmental missions. The implementation turns data collection into a game: participants move through assigned areas, collect virtual objects, record evidence and upload material for analysis. At a conceptual level, the system combines citizen participation, location tracking, smartphone sensing, AI-based asset analysis and municipal asset-management workflows. Data gathered by participants can be evaluated by AI and converted into condition assessments or maintenance intelligence. The expected impact is faster infrastructure inventories, lower survey costs, improved coverage of physical assets and more participatory maintenance of the urban environment. The model also creates a direct incentive for residents to contribute, because missions can include monetary rewards. Its value lies in combining human mobility, local knowledge and automated analysis to update infrastructure data at a scale that would otherwise require dedicated survey teams.

results.proposal: Virtual assistant equipped with artificial intelligence for Parkinson's patients and their families. The service was designed to improve access to reliable information and strengthen continuity between specialist expertise and patients’ day-to-day needs. The implementation used IBM Watson Assistant, configuring a conversational interface around clinically relevant content prepared for people affected by Parkinson’s, caregivers and family members. At a conceptual level, the system interprets user questions, matches them to a structured knowledge base and returns answers in natural language, reducing the need for users to search manually through multiple sources or wait for routine information. Its expected impact is easier access to medical guidance, stronger patient and caregiver support, reduced burden on staff for repetitive questions and a more responsive digital communication channel around chronic neurological care. The case also illustrates how conversational AI can be used in hospital services when the subject matter requires a careful balance between accessibility and clinical reliability: the bot supports information delivery but does not replace medical evaluation or personalised decisions by clinicians.

results.title: Chatbot - City of Vienna
results.proposal: Chatbot - City of Vienna. Residents and visitors often need quick answers to practical city questions while on the move, such as where to find a service, how long parking rules apply, when public transport departs or where the nearest public facility is located. Vienna developed WienBot as a digital assistant that complements the city website by providing concise answers through chat and voice. The objective is to make municipal information easier to consume in everyday situations, without requiring users to navigate long web pages or search-result lists. The implementation connects the chatbot to city information and open government data, including geospatial data, the city events database and real-time public-transport interfaces from Wiener Linien. At a conceptual level, the bot interprets a user’s question, retrieves relevant structured or editorial information and returns a direct answer, sometimes supported by map or route data. It can answer in standard language and has also been known for a local Viennese tone. The expected impact is faster access to municipal information, improved usability on mobile devices, greater accessibility through voice search and reduced friction for routine enquiries.

results.title: Swedish municipality deploys robots for safer recruitment
results.proposal: Swedish municipality deploys robots for safer recruitment. Recruitment processes can reproduce unconscious bias when candidates are screened through CVs, informal impressions or inconsistent interview questions. Upplands-Bro Municipality used Tengai’s AI interview system to support more structured and resume-free candidate screening, particularly during urgent recruitment needs in care and welfare roles during the COVID-19 period. The objective was to scale early-stage recruitment while reducing the influence of irrelevant background characteristics and ensuring that applicants were asked comparable questions. The implementation uses a conversational AI interview tool that conducts structured screening interviews, asking candidates identical or standardised questions and producing information for recruiters to review. At a conceptual level, the system separates initial candidate assessment from CV cues, applies consistent interview protocols and provides structured data that HR staff can use in later selection stages. The expected impact is faster screening of large applicant pools, reduced unconscious bias at the early interview stage, greater consistency across applicants and more time for HR staff to focus on qualitative follow-up and final hiring decisions.
