results.title: IVDP DATA+ - AI models for processing relevant data for the economy of the Douro Wine Region.
results.proposal: IVDP DATA+ - AI models for processing relevant data for the economy of the Douro Wine Region. IVDP DATA+ addresses the need to strengthen data-informed decision-making for the Douro Wine Region, an economically and culturally significant territory where public and sectoral authorities must manage complex information on production, markets and regional dynamics. The project is based on a new model of experimentation developed in close collaboration with the scientific community, with the aim of promoting knowledge transfer and adopting advanced tools and techniques from artificial intelligence and data science. The objective is to support decisions by processing existing data more effectively and transforming them into useful analytical insights for the region’s economy. The emerging technology implementation consists of artificial intelligence models and data-science methods applied to relevant datasets held or used in the Douro wine-sector context. At conceptual level, the models process existing information to identify patterns, generate forecasts or support scenario-based understanding of variables affecting the regional wine economy. The source description does not specify the exact datasets, models or operational modules, so the implementation should be recorded at a high level. The expected impact is improved analytical capacity, stronger collaboration between public institutions and scientific actors, and better evidence for strategic decisions affecting the Douro Wine Region. By creating a data-driven experimentation model, IVDP DATA+ can support more informed governance, improve planning and contribute to the competitiveness and resilience of the regional economy.

results.title: RELIABLE - Building occupant risk warning panel during extreme weather events
results.proposal: RELIABLE - Building occupant risk warning panel during extreme weather events. RELIABLE addresses the need to protect building occupants during extreme weather events, particularly heat and cold waves. Such events can create significant health risks, especially for vulnerable populations, and public authorities need timely, spatially detailed information to identify where risks are concentrated. Conventional warning systems may not provide sufficiently granular information on building-level or localised exposure, limiting the ability to target prevention and response measures. The project, led by the Associação do Instituto Superior Técnico para a Investigação e o Desenvolvimento, aims to develop a public geographic dashboard providing real-time information and high spatial resolution on the health risks faced by building occupants during extreme weather events. The emerging technology implementation consists of a geographic dashboard supported by real-time data processing and spatial risk modelling. At conceptual level, the system would combine environmental, geographic and building-related information to estimate occupant health risk during heat and cold waves and present it through an accessible public interface. The expected impact is improved situational awareness for authorities and citizens, more targeted risk communication and better prioritisation of preventive measures during extreme weather. By making high-resolution risk information available in real time, RELIABLE can support public-health preparedness, improve the user experience of warning services and strengthen resilience to climate-related hazards.

results.title: AI-4-MUFF - AI for the management of the degree of readiness in urban firefighting
results.proposal: AI-4-MUFF - AI for the management of the degree of readiness in urban firefighting. AI-4-MUFF addresses the challenge of improving strategic decision-making for urban firefighting. Fire services must maintain an appropriate degree of readiness while facing uncertainty regarding incident occurrence, resource availability, operational priorities and urban risk conditions. Decisions on preparedness and response capacity need to be based on empirical evidence and must balance multiple objectives, such as response time, coverage, resource use and operational resilience. The project, led by NOVA.ID.FCT, intends to develop a strategic decision-support system for combating urban fires. The emerging technology implementation combines machine-learning techniques, multi-objective optimisation models and an agent-based simulation environment. At conceptual level, machine-learning methods can be used to extract patterns from historical or operational fire-service data, while optimisation models support the allocation of resources across competing objectives. Agent-based simulation allows the modelling of interactions between units, incidents, urban environments and decision rules, enabling the testing of different preparedness scenarios. The expected impact is improved evidence-based planning for urban firefighting, better readiness management and stronger capacity to evaluate strategic options before they are implemented. By integrating prediction, optimisation and simulation, AI-4-MUFF can support more efficient resource deployment, increase service reliability and improve the ability of fire authorities to respond effectively to urban fire risks.

results.title: GrassData - Identification, verification and quantification of CO2 sequestration in pastures
results.proposal: GrassData - Identification, verification and quantification of CO2 sequestration in pastures. GrassData addresses the need to monitor and verify land-management practices that improve soil protection and carbon sequestration in pastures. Public authorities and environmental programmes require reliable evidence to confirm whether declared practices, such as bush management or the existence of harrows, are actually being implemented and producing the expected environmental benefits. Manual verification can be costly, time-consuming and difficult to scale across extensive pasture areas. The project, led by the Associação do Instituto Superior Técnico para a Investigação e o Desenvolvimento, aims to develop algorithms that support monitoring, verification and compliance assessment in relation to soil and carbon-related practices. The emerging technology implementation consists of automated algorithms designed to verify the results of pasture-management practices that contribute to carbon sequestration. At conceptual level, the system would analyse relevant data on land conditions, management activities and environmental indicators to detect whether required practices are present and to support quantification of CO2 sequestration outcomes. The exact datasets and model architecture are not specified in the source description, so the implementation should be understood as an algorithmic monitoring and verification capability. The expected impact is more efficient compliance control, stronger evidence for climate and land-management policies, and improved capacity to scale verification across pasture areas. By automating parts of the monitoring process, GrassData can reduce administrative burden and support more credible environmental reporting.

results.title: MATISSE - Bivalve health: predictive and early warning system
results.proposal: MATISSE - Bivalve health: predictive and early warning system. MATISSE addresses the environmental, public-health and economic risks created by harmful algal blooms and shellfish biotoxin contamination. Under favourable climate and oceanographic conditions, toxin-producing microalgae can proliferate, reach high concentrations in seawater, accumulate in shellfish and threaten seafood consumers. These events can also cause significant economic losses for shellfish farmers when harvesting or production must be restricted. The project, linked to Universidade Nova de Lisboa, responds to the need for more effective tools that help shellfish producers and public environmental authorities anticipate harmful algal bloom events and manage contamination risks. The emerging technology implementation focuses on statistical and machine-learning forecasting tools for predicting harmful algal blooms and shellfish biotoxin contamination. The reviewed approaches include autoregressive models, support vector machines, random forests, probabilistic graphical models and artificial neural networks, with more complex models increasingly supported by multi-source data. At conceptual level, these models analyse environmental, oceanographic and biological information to forecast bloom events or contamination risks and support early warning. The expected impact is improved decision-making for harvesting, production management and mitigation measures. By providing earlier and more accurate warnings, MATISSE can help reduce production losses, protect consumer health and strengthen the evidence base used by governmental agencies with environmental responsibilities.

results.title: PAMWater: Analytical and Predictive Models for Optimization of Multimunicipal Water Systems
results.proposal: PAMWater: Analytical and Predictive Models for Optimization of Multimunicipal Water Systems. PAMWater addresses the need to improve the efficiency, resilience and sustainability of multimunicipal water systems. Water utilities and public decision-makers must manage complex infrastructures where demand, supply, operational constraints and environmental pressures vary over time and across territories. Inefficient planning can increase costs, reduce service reliability and limit the capacity of water systems to respond to stress events or long-term sustainability objectives. The project, led by the University of Minho, aims to create a predictive and analytical platform that supports decision-makers by giving them access to a broad set of descriptive and predictive information. The emerging technology implementation consists of deep-learning models embedded in a decision-support platform for multimunicipal water systems. At conceptual level, the platform would process operational, temporal and system-level data to identify patterns, forecast relevant variables and provide analytical outputs for planning and optimisation. The use of predictive models can support decisions on resource allocation, infrastructure management, demand anticipation and operational performance. The expected impact is improved decision-making, stronger system resilience and more sustainable management of water resources. By consolidating descriptive and predictive information in a single platform, PAMWater can help public and utility stakeholders anticipate operational needs, reduce inefficiencies and improve the reliability and scalability of water-system management across multiple municipalities.
results.memo: Proceed. PAMWater: Analytical and Predictive Models for Optimization of Multimunicipal Water Systems is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: iLU: Advanced Learning in Urban Data with Situational Context for Optimizing Mobility in Cities
results.proposal: iLU: Advanced Learning in Urban Data with Situational Context for Optimizing Mobility in Cities. The iLU project addresses the challenge of optimising urban mobility in Lisbon by making better use of heterogeneous data stored in the city’s Intelligent Management Platform. Urban traffic management requires real-time understanding of mobility conditions, but relevant data are often distributed across different sources and may not be systematically connected with situational context. The project aims to consolidate multiple mobility data sources in the Plataforma de Gestão Inteligente de Lisboa, ensure their real-time updatability, discover actionable spatio-temporal patterns and anticipate congestion. The emerging technology implementation combines advanced predictive modelling with deep reinforcement learning. At conceptual level, the system analyses heterogeneous mobility data to detect non-trivial correlations between road traffic and contextual variables, forecast traffic congestion and support real-time mobility decisions. Deep reinforcement learning is intended to help condition city traffic positively by supporting interventions such as traffic-light control and road-message panels. The system therefore connects data integration, pattern discovery, prediction and operational decision support within an urban mobility-management environment. The expected impact is improved traffic anticipation, more responsive mobility management and better use of city infrastructure. By enabling real-time, data-driven interventions, iLU can contribute to reduced congestion, improved reliability of urban travel, more efficient traffic-control operations and stronger strategic capacity for mobility planning in Lisbon.
results.memo: Proceed. iLU: Advanced Learning in Urban Data with Situational Context for Optimizing Mobility in Cities is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: MOPREVIS - Modeling and prediction of traffic accidents in the district of Setúbal
results.proposal: MOPREVIS - Modeling and prediction of traffic accidents in the district of Setúbal. MOPREVIS addresses the need to improve road-safety planning in the district of Setúbal by understanding where traffic accidents occur, why they happen and which locations are most likely to present future risks. The project aimed to create an information system combining several sources of information on accidents, traffic intensity and climatic conditions. The objective was to classify accident hotspots, identify determinant factors influencing the occurrence and severity of accidents, draw profiles of individuals involved, compare accident types such as collisions, pedestrian accidents and scraping incidents, and construct predictive models for both the number and severity of accidents. The emerging technology implementation consists of a digital platform with distributed architecture for storage, large-scale data processing and management. It includes a data-acquisition module that extracts information from accident documents using natural language processing and artificial intelligence techniques, as well as interfaces for automatic data collection from other systems, including traffic-intensity data in adjacent streets and climate data. An information-retrieval module supports access to the processed results. The expected impact is improved capacity for evidence-based traffic-safety interventions, more accurate identification of high-risk locations and better prioritisation of prevention measures. By integrating multiple data sources and predictive models, MOPREVIS can help authorities anticipate accident risks, allocate resources more effectively and design targeted actions to reduce accident frequency and severity.

results.title: LAB BUPi - Creation of the Single Counter Laboratory Simplified Cadastral Information System
results.proposal: LAB BUPi - Creation of the Single Counter Laboratory Simplified Cadastral Information System. LAB BUPi seeks to resolve the long-standing challenge of identifying land structure and ownership in rural territories in Portugal. Incomplete or fragmented cadastral information can create difficulties for land registration, territorial planning, property management and interaction between citizens and public administration. The reform consists of a pilot project for a simplified national cadastral information system, combined with the entry into operation of the Land Cover Monitoring System and the development of the BUPi digital land registry platform. The objective is to aggregate the information necessary for property registration and provide citizens with a physical and virtual counter that simplifies interaction with public services in the land-register domain. The emerging technology implementation centres on a digital platform using geo-referenced property information. At conceptual level, BUPi consolidates cadastral, registration and land-related data in a single service environment, allowing citizens and authorities to identify, record and manage rural properties more effectively. The reform also establishes the legal framework needed to operationalise the rural property registry and land-cover monitoring investment. The expected impact is improved accuracy and accessibility of property information, easier registration procedures, stronger territorial knowledge and better interaction between citizens and the administration. By combining digital services with geo-referenced data and a simplified counter model, LAB BUPi can improve scalability, reduce administrative barriers and support more coherent land-governance policies.

results.title: PAGIRAA - Analytical Platform for the Intelligent Management of Water Supply Networks
results.proposal: PAGIRAA - Analytical Platform for the Intelligent Management of Water Supply Networks. Water utilities and public administrations need reliable operational intelligence to manage supply networks, reduce losses and anticipate service problems across complex infrastructure. The context was public-sector digital transformation in Portugal, with the aim of applying advanced analytics to a critical municipal and regional service. Water networks generate large volumes of operational data from meters, network assets, consumption records and maintenance activity, but this information is often fragmented across systems and difficult to translate into timely management decisions. The platform was designed to consolidate and analyse such data so that authorities and operators could better understand water-flow behaviour, identify irregularities and support planning. Although the available source provides limited operational detail, the case fits within a wider pattern of using data analytics to modernise essential infrastructure and support more proactive public-service management.

results.title: Sia - Online notification system of the municipality of Amsterdam
results.proposal: Sia - Online notification system of the municipality of Amsterdam. The Municipality of Amsterdam must respond to a high volume of reports about public-space issues, ranging from street cleaning and repairs to unsafe traffic situations, nuisance and problems in parks or around restaurants. Sia provides a digital channel through which residents and other users can submit notifications when something in the public space needs attention. The core operational problem is that urban maintenance and enforcement services depend on timely, structured and actionable information from the public, while fragmented reporting channels can make it harder to prioritise, route and resolve issues efficiently. SIA enables reports to be made for several types of situations, including objects or areas that need to be repaired or cleaned, dangerous traffic conditions and nuisance caused by people or establishments. The technology implementation consists of an online reporting platform that captures user-submitted information and supports its classification and routing within municipal workflows. Where algorithmic support is used, incoming reports can be categorised, prioritised or assigned to the appropriate service teams based on the content and type of notification. The main impact is a more accessible reporting route for citizens, better structuring of municipal case handling, faster allocation of tasks to relevant departments and improved oversight of recurring public-space problems. For the municipality, SIA contributes to more responsive local service delivery and a stronger evidence base for managing urban maintenance and liveability.

results.title: Scan car for checking group formation and complying with corona measures
results.proposal: Scan car for checking group formation and complying with corona measures. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the municipality of Rotterdam needed ways to monitor compliance with public-health measures in urban space, particularly rules concerning group formation and distancing. Manual enforcement alone could be difficult to scale across a large city, especially when conditions changed quickly and authorities needed timely information about where crowding or non-compliance might be occurring. The use case therefore focused on supporting oversight of coronavirus measures in public areas, with the objective of improving situational awareness and helping the municipality respond more effectively to risky gatherings. The stakeholders include the municipality, enforcement and public-safety teams and people using public space, with the wider aim of reducing infection risk during the emergency period. The solution was implemented through a scan car used to observe public-space conditions and check for group formation linked to corona rules. At a conceptual level, the system combined mobile sensing and automated analysis to identify patterns of crowding or gathering while moving through the city, creating a more mobile form of monitoring than fixed observation points alone. This allowed the municipality to gather information on compliance across different locations and support operational responses where required. The expected impact was improved visibility of non-compliant situations, more efficient deployment of enforcement attention and stronger support for pandemic management. More broadly, the use case created value as an example of crisis-time urban monitoring, showing how mobile automated observation could support local public-health enforcement in exceptional circumstances.

results.title: Rijkswaterstaat vital assets - Predictive maintenance on bridges
results.proposal: Rijkswaterstaat vital assets - Predictive maintenance on bridges. The Dutch Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management needs to maintain bridges and hydraulic civil-engineering works in a way that prevents failures, reduces unnecessary interventions and uses maintenance budgets more efficiently. Rijkswaterstaat vital assets - Predictive maintenance on bridges supports this objective by using data to estimate when maintenance should be carried out on critical infrastructure assets. The operational challenge is that bridges and related water-management structures are subject to wear, environmental pressure and intensive use, while traditional maintenance planning can be either reactive or based on fixed schedules that do not always reflect the actual condition of the asset. The initiative, funded by the Dutch Ministry of Infrastructure and developed with Vitale Assets and the Water cluster of the CAMINO Smart Industry Field Lab, explores how predictive maintenance can be applied to hydraulic civil-engineering works. results.proposal: Remote sensing for monitoring nature reserves on the Frisian Wadden Islands. results.title: Project Jurisprudence Robot -  AI tool to support prosecutors and investigators
results.proposal: Project Jurisprudence Robot -  AI tool to support prosecutors and investigators. Public prosecutors and investigators face growing volumes of legal material and case law, making it increasingly difficult to identify relevant jurisprudence efficiently and consistently. To address this challenge, the Dutch Public Prosecution Service collaborated with the legal technology company LexIQ to develop the Jurisprudence Robot, a tool designed to support daily prosecutorial work by improving access to relevant judicial decisions. The main stakeholders include prosecutors, investigators, and judicial support staff, with the objective of reducing time spent on legal research while improving consistency in legal reasoning. The solution processes large collections of court rulings and legal texts and matches them to case-specific queries using automated text analysis techniques. The system structures legal documents, extracts relevant concepts, and presents ranked jurisprudence results to users through an interface integrated into existing prosecutorial workflows. Human decision-making remains central, with the tool acting strictly as an advisory aid rather than an automated decision-maker. According to publicly available judicial documentation, the Jurisprudence Robot has been tested in controlled environments and limited operational settings, with no evidence of nationwide deployment or discontinuation. Reported benefits include faster legal research, improved consistency in case preparation, and reduced administrative burden, while maintaining judicial accountability and professional autonomy.

results.proposal: Pilot Youth Policy Rotterdam - Influencing factors socio-emotional development of young people. The policy challenge is that youth outcomes are shaped by multiple interacting variables across education, family context, neighbourhood conditions, health, welfare and social participation. Local authorities need stronger evidence on these relationships to design interventions that are preventive, targeted and proportionate. The stakeholders included the Municipality of Rotterdam, TNO, the Dutch Ministry of the Interior and Kingdom Relations, young people, families, youth-service professionals and policymakers. The implementation links datasets and applies a combination of statistical analysis and machine learning to examine which factors are associated with socio-emotional development. Conceptually, the pilot functions as a data-driven policy lab: it integrates relevant administrative or research data, tests associations, identifies patterns and supports policy learning rather than producing a direct automated decision on individual young people. The expected impact is improved understanding of risk and protective factors, better targeting of youth policies and stronger evidence for preventive interventions. Its usefulness depends on data quality, careful interpretation, privacy protection and avoiding deterministic conclusions about individual young people based on statistical correlations.

The impact is faster, more efficient and more complete processing of referrals, allowing law-enforcement officers to focus their attention on high-priority cases, victim identification and perpetrator detection. results.title: Passer-by count
results.proposal: Passer-by count. City centres increasingly require reliable insights into pedestrian flows to support economic development, urban planning and public safety. The municipality of Nijmegen introduced passer-by counting to better understand how people move through the city centre, how busy specific areas are at different times, and how these patterns relate to retail performance and public space use. The sensors process visual or signal data locally to extract movement counts and directional flows, which are then aggregated and transmitted to municipal dashboards. Data is anonymised at source and integrated with other urban indicators, such as time of day, weather and events. results.title: Parking control in various Dutch municipalities - Parking control by means of scan cars
results.proposal: Parking control in various Dutch municipalities - Parking control by means of scan cars. Large municipalities need to enforce parking rules across dense urban areas efficiently, while limiting manual checks and maintaining consistent treatment of vehicles using paid or restricted parking spaces. Parking control in various Dutch municipalities - Parking control by means of scan cars supports parking enforcement in Amsterdam, The Hague, Rotterdam and Utrecht through vehicles equipped with cameras that inspect parked cars while driving through city streets. The operational problem is that conventional on-foot inspection can be labour-intensive and difficult to scale across large numbers of parking spaces, particularly in cities with high vehicle turnover and complex parking regimes. The scan cars capture licence plates and use an image-recognition algorithm to identify registration numbers. These readings can then be checked against parking-payment or permit databases to determine whether a vehicle appears to be compliant. Cases that require further verification can be reviewed before enforcement action is taken, depending on local procedures. The technology therefore combines mobile sensing, automated number-plate recognition and integration with municipal parking-administration systems. Its impact is greater inspection coverage, faster detection of possible parking violations, more efficient deployment of enforcement staff and improved consistency in parking control. For municipalities, the approach can also generate better operational data on parking behaviour and support more responsive management of urban parking policy.

results.proposal: Detection of crime and subversion in the municipality of Dronten (SyRI system). The municipality therefore explored how algorithmic analysis could support earlier detection and prioritisation of cases requiring further attention. The implementation is described as an experiment using algorithms to detect subversive crime. Risks include opaque criteria, inaccurate suspicion, disproportionate targeting of specific groups or areas, and weak routes for contesting decisions. The pilot therefore needs careful legal, ethical and operational governance if algorithmic signals are used to trigger further enforcement action.

The stakeholders included the municipalities of Deventer and Goirle, welfare recipients, municipal social-service staff, enforcement teams and citizens affected by decisions based on risk scores. The implementation generated risk profiles for welfare recipients, with the resulting score used to decide whether a dossier should be examined more closely. results.proposal: Inspection bridges with drones. The bridge-inspection drone pilot explores how unmanned aerial vehicles can reduce reliance on manual inspection capacity for bridges and viaducts. Public infrastructure managers need reliable ways to detect deterioration, document structural conditions and prioritise maintenance without closing assets unnecessarily or deploying extensive human resources for every inspection. The implementation uses drones to capture visual data from bridges and viaducts, allowing inspection teams to review high-resolution imagery of structural elements that would otherwise require physical access. At a conceptual level, the approach can combine UAV-based image capture, georeferenced inspection records, visual analytics and, where developed further, computer-vision models for recognising cracks, corrosion, deformation or other signs of damage. The expected impact is faster inspection, lower operational burden, improved safety for inspection staff and more consistent documentation of asset condition. If validated, the pilot could support more risk-based infrastructure maintenance by helping authorities identify which structures require closer expert review and which can be monitored remotely.

evidence.quote: Public infrastructure managers need reliable ways to detect deterioration, document structural conditions and prioritise maintenance without closing assets unnecessarily or deploying extensive human resources for every inspection.

results.title: HKV Eye - Line in Water
results.proposal: HKV Eye - Line in Water. HKVEYE supports the inspection and monitoring of dikes, water defences and water systems by adding data-driven visual analysis to water-management practice. The operational challenge is that water authorities and infrastructure managers face expanding management areas while staffing capacity for inspection can be limited. Manual inspection of dikes, structures and water systems can be time-consuming, and early recognition of deterioration is essential for flood safety and maintenance planning. HKV Lijn in Water developed HKVEYE to provide additional “eyes” on water infrastructure, using visual data to examine the condition of dikes and related assets in more detail. The implementation applies data-science techniques to interpret images and other visual data, supporting questions such as monitoring vegetation quality, assessing revetment condition, detecting sand-carrying boils and conducting difference analyses over time. Conceptually, the system combines visual monitoring, data interpretation, anomaly detection and inspection-support workflows. The expected impact is more precise, efficient and evidence-based inspection, helping managers focus attention on areas that require intervention. By extracting useful information from increasingly available visual data, HKVEYE can improve maintenance prioritisation, support flood-risk management and strengthen the reliability of water-safety monitoring.

results.title: Hansken - Recognizing images of narcotics in digital seizure
results.proposal: Hansken - Recognizing images of narcotics in digital seizure. Criminal investigations increasingly involve very large volumes of seized digital material, making it difficult for forensic experts and investigators to manually review every phone, computer, hard drive or storage device in time-sensitive cases. Hansken - Recognizing images of narcotics in digital seizure responds to this challenge by helping the Netherlands Forensic Institute and investigative authorities identify relevant visual or textual evidence more quickly within large datasets. The operational aim is to accelerate the discovery of incriminating or case-relevant material while reducing the burden of exhaustive manual review. The technological implementation uses a self-learning algorithm integrated into the Hansken digital-forensics environment. The system can be trained to recognise specific categories of images, such as weapons or drugs, and to detect text elements appearing in images, including licence plates or account numbers on stolen bank cards. At a conceptual level, image-recognition and pattern-detection techniques classify visual content and highlight items that may deserve closer examination by experts. The tool supports forensic prioritisation rather than replacing evidentiary assessment, which remains subject to professional and legal review. Its impact is faster search across seized data, better use of investigative capacity, improved ability to find hidden or dispersed evidence and stronger support for serious-crime investigations where digital material is extensive and operational timelines are demanding.
results.memo: Proceed. Hansken - Recognizing images of narcotics in digital seizure is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority (NVWA)
results.title: Graasdierpremie - Use of drones in counting animals
results.proposal: Graasdierpremie - Use of drones in counting animals. The Graasdierpremie pilot examines whether drones and automated image analysis can improve the counting and monitoring of grazing animals. The operational problem is that animal-distribution and abundance monitoring is traditionally carried out manually on foot or through aerial recording from manned aircraft, both of which can be costly, slow and labour-intensive. For public authorities such as the NVWA, more efficient monitoring can support nature conservation, agricultural control and subsidy-related verification. The implementation uses drone imagery to collect visual data on animals in the field, combined with computer-vision methods that detect, classify and count animals automatically. Conceptually, the system replaces broad manual observation with aerial data capture, image-processing pipelines and automated counting models, while still requiring quality checks and validation by competent staff. The expected impact is faster monitoring of animal populations, reduced inspection costs, improved geographical coverage and more consistent evidence for administrative or conservation decisions. If validated, the approach could make field verification more scalable and less dependent on resource-intensive manual methods. It may also support more timely insights into animal distribution, enabling better planning and more targeted follow-up inspections.
results.memo: Proceed. Graasdierpremie - Use of drones in counting animals is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: GEO reference of documents - Gaining more insight into data on nitrogen emissions and soil pollution
results.proposal: GEO reference of documents - Gaining more insight into data on nitrogen emissions and soil pollution. The GEO reference of documents project supports the Province of Gelderland in analysing large volumes of unstructured information related to nitrogen emissions and soil pollution. The policy and administrative challenge is that environmental files, permits, reports and technical documents may contain relevant evidence, but their unstructured format makes it difficult for officials to extract patterns, locations and relationships efficiently. Bolesian developed an application to help the province gain more insight from this dispersed information base. The implementation uses natural language processing, document analytics and geographic referencing to process unstructured text and connect relevant information to territorial or environmental contexts. Conceptually, the system can identify key entities, themes, locations and relationships within documents, then structure them so that policymakers and specialists can examine nitrogen and soil-pollution issues more systematically. The expected impact is improved environmental intelligence, faster review of complex documentation and stronger evidence for policy, permitting and enforcement decisions. By converting unstructured material into more usable data, the application can support more transparent and data-informed environmental governance in a policy field where decisions are often technically complex and politically sensitive.

results.title: Forensic Image Recognition (FIRE) -  Recognition of containers that have illegal cargo
results.proposal: Forensic Image Recognition (FIRE) -  Recognition of containers that have illegal cargo. FIRE is an experimental forensic image-recognition system developed to reduce the manual burden on detection staff when analysing large volumes of visual material. The operational problem is that forensic and investigative services may need to inspect extensive image datasets, including data carriers and other visual sources, to identify objects that could be relevant to criminal investigations. In this framed pilot area, the Netherlands Forensic Institute examines whether the system can learn to recognise sea containers that may contain illegal cargo. The implementation uses automatic image recognition, drawing on large datasets to train or test models capable of identifying relevant visual patterns. Conceptually, FIRE combines computer vision, dataset preparation, model training, image classification and explainability requirements, particularly because forensic applications must be legally robust and understandable. The expected impact is a substantial reduction in the time required for image-based screening, allowing staff to focus on higher-value forensic analysis. If the approach succeeds, work that might otherwise require extensive manual review could be narrowed to a more manageable set of flagged images. However, before broader use, the project must address dataset compilation, storage, lawful use and inter-agency sharing.

results.title: FlowCube - a picture of the traffic of cyclists, vehicles and pedestrians
results.proposal: FlowCube - a picture of the traffic of cyclists, vehicles and pedestrians. Street managers need reliable information on how different road users move through public space, especially where cyclists, pedestrians and vehicles interact in ways that are not fully captured by traditional traffic counts. FlowCube responds to this need by using compact camera-based modules to generate traffic intelligence for local mobility management. The system is intended to give authorities and transport planners a clearer picture of flows, routes and travel times without relying on manual observation or intrusive data collection. Its implementation combines compact video sensors with image-recognition algorithms that distinguish cyclists, pedestrians and, where configured, other types of traffic. At a conceptual level, the modules detect objects, classify road-user categories, track local movement and aggregate observations into usable mobility data. Multiple FlowCubes can also combine data to infer commonly used cycling routes and corresponding travel times. The expected impact is more accurate insight into active mobility, better evidence for infrastructure planning, improved monitoring of cycling and walking policies, and safer management of mixed-use streets. Technolution presents FlowCube as an operational product and emphasises privacy compliance, because the system generates mobility indicators rather than functioning as an identity-based surveillance tool. This makes it relevant for municipalities seeking granular traffic intelligence while remaining within data-protection constraints.
results.memo: Proceed. FlowCube - a picture of the traffic of cyclists, vehicles and pedestrians is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT: A Pre-trained Transformer Language Model for Italian Law
results.proposal: ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT: A Pre-trained Transformer Language Model for Italian Law. Legal language differs substantially from general Italian because it contains technical terminology, Latin expressions, formulaic constructions and domain-specific references that general-purpose language models may not represent well. ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT addresses this gap by adapting transformer-based natural language processing to the Italian legal domain. The model was introduced by researchers at the Sant’Anna School of Advanced Studies to improve performance on downstream legal NLP tasks where generic Italian BERT models lose accuracy. The implementation starts from an Italian BERT architecture and performs additional pre-training on Italian civil-law corpora. At a conceptual level, the model learns contextual representations from legal texts, making it better suited to tasks such as legal classification, retrieval, information extraction or document analysis. This approach is important because many public-sector legal applications require high sensitivity to legal wording and cannot rely solely on models trained on Wikipedia, news or other general corpora. The expected impact is improved performance in Italian legal AI systems, stronger foundations for legal analytics, and a reusable research resource for courts, public administrations, legal publishers and academic projects. The published paper reports that ITALIAN-LEGAL-BERT outperforms the general-purpose Italian BERT in domain-specific tasks, while a public Hugging Face entry indicates the model remains available as an open machine-learning resource.

results.title: Syddjurs, DK and neighboring cities map employment service processes with AI-powered platform
results.proposal: Syddjurs, DK and neighboring cities map employment service processes with AI-powered platform. Employment services often involve complex citizen journeys across unemployment benefits, municipal departments, job-search support and follow-up activities, making it difficult for caseworkers and managers to see which pathways are effective. Syddjurs Municipality and four partner municipalities used AI-based process mining to analyse how citizens move through employment-service systems and where delays, detours or inefficient steps occur. The objective was to create a more holistic and effective employment effort by turning administrative process data into maps of real user experiences and predictive insights. The implementation combines municipal data on unemployment benefits, service contacts and departmental interactions with process-mining and predictive-monitoring techniques. At a conceptual level, the platform reconstructs actual citizen pathways, identifies patterns in service sequences and recommends the most suitable route for each resident’s employment search. This allows municipalities to understand not only which services are provided, but how citizens experience the sequence of interventions. The expected impact is better prioritisation of employment support, improved coordination between municipal teams, faster identification of bottlenecks and more personalised guidance for jobseekers. The participating municipalities received DKK 4.1 million from a national innovation fund, and the dedicated project site remains active with resources on process mining, data strategy and evaluation.

results.company: Aarhus University, Municipality of Aalborg and DigiRehab
results.title: AI-enabled Rehabilitation in danish municipalities
results.proposal: AI-enabled Rehabilitation in danish municipalities. Municipal rehabilitation for older citizens requires caseworkers to assess training needs, assistive aids, fall-prevention measures and expected self-sufficiency, often under pressure from ageing populations and limited care resources. The AIR project was designed to support these professional assessments with data-driven decision support rather than replace municipal judgement. With Aalborg Municipality as project owner, Aarhus University, DigiRehab, Syddjurs Municipality and Viborg Municipality collaborated on one of Denmark’s municipal AI signature projects. The implementation uses models and statistical analysis based on municipal rehabilitation data, including information on granted assistive devices and completed training pathways, to support decisions about which rehabilitation measures may be most appropriate for older citizens. At a conceptual level, the system analyses patterns in previous rehabilitation cases and translates them into recommendations or decision support for case managers, with performance measured through improved self-sufficiency and reduced reliance on home help. The expected impact is more consistent rehabilitation planning, better use of assistive aids, earlier fall-prevention attention and improved targeting of training resources. A proof-of-concept was conducted in 2018–2019, while the AIR signature project ran from 2020 to 2022 and delivered a prototype by the end of the project period.
results.memo: Proceed. AI-enabled Rehabilitation in danish municipalities is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI-assisted diagnostic and rehabilitative tools for personalised support of children with cerebral palsy
results.proposal: AI-assisted diagnostic and rehabilitative tools for personalised support of children with cerebral palsy. Children with unilateral cerebral palsy require highly personalised assessment and rehabilitation because motor impairments, upper-limb function and treatment response vary substantially across individuals. The AInCP project, led by the University of Pisa, addresses this need by developing clinical decision-support tools that can help clinicians provide functional diagnosis, prognosis and tailored home-based intervention for children with unilateral cerebral palsy. The operational problem is that conventional care can rely on fragmented clinical observations, periodic assessments and limited real-time information on how children use their upper limb outside the clinic. The implementation uses a multimodal approach that combines clinical phenotyping, advanced brain imaging and real-time monitoring of upper-limb function. Artificial intelligence methods are used to integrate these sources into personalised assessment and rehabilitation tools, supporting both clinical interpretation and home-based treatment planning. At a conceptual level, the system links diagnostic data, imaging features, movement monitoring and intervention recommendations in an evidence-based decision-support framework. The expected impact is more precise functional profiling, better prediction of rehabilitation needs, improved personalisation of therapy and stronger continuity between clinical and home settings. The project also aims to validate the tools through observational and rehabilitation studies, making clinical reliability and trustworthiness central to its development. CORDIS lists AInCP as running from 1 June 2022 to 31 May 2027.

evidence.quote: The expected impact is more precise functional profiling, better prediction of rehabilitation needs, improved personalisation of therapy and stronger continuity between clinical and home settings.

results.title: The Hague uses AI to reduce laughing gas nuisance
results.proposal: The Hague uses AI to reduce laughing gas nuisance. Urban enforcement teams in busy nightlife and tourist areas must respond to nuisance quickly, but reports may arrive too late or lack precise location information. In Scheveningen, The Hague tested whether smart cameras could help detect nitrous oxide, or laughing gas, abuse around the boulevard, where nuisance was linked to parking problems, traffic violations, noise and other undesirable behaviour. The objective was to give municipal enforcement staff timely information while avoiding unnecessary collection of identifiable footage. The implementation used AI-enabled cameras from Avutec trained to recognise nitrous oxide balloons and related paraphernalia, with Monotch’s TLEX platform forwarding detection data to the enforcement organisation. At a conceptual level, the system combines video analytics, object recognition, privacy-preserving event reporting and real-time notification workflows. Smart Cities World reports that no footage was sent because of privacy considerations; only detection data were forwarded. The pilot assessed algorithm functionality, camera accuracy, notification speed and privacy protection during a test day on the Scheveningen boulevard. The expected impact is quicker enforcement response, better targeting of patrols and reduced nuisance linked to laughing gas use, without creating a general-purpose surveillance stream. The test confirmed the algorithm’s functionality and gave a “green light” for refinement, but public sources describe it as a trial rather than full deployment.

results.title: Artificial Intelligence and advanced Data Analytics for Law Enforcement Agencies
results.proposal: Artificial Intelligence and advanced Data Analytics for Law Enforcement Agencies. Law-enforcement agencies investigating cybercrime and terrorism must process large, heterogeneous and fast-moving datasets, including online content, digital traces, multilingual material, network information and intelligence records. AIDA was created to provide European law-enforcement bodies with a modular platform for descriptive and predictive analytics that could support investigation and proactive prevention while operating in a secure environment. The objective was to improve the full analytical workflow, from content acquisition and information extraction to fusion, knowledge management, enrichment, visual analytics and operational decision support. The implementation combines big-data processing, machine learning, deep learning, predictive analytics, multilingual scene-text recognition and task-specific analytical tools for cybercrime and terrorism investigations. At a conceptual level, AIDA integrates data ingestion, automated mining, entity and relationship extraction, knowledge representation and visual interfaces so that analysts can identify patterns, links and risks across large datasets. The tools were intended to be made available to law-enforcement agencies through a secure sandbox environment using real data, raising the technological readiness level towards TRL 7. The expected impact is faster intelligence analysis, more efficient investigations, improved situational awareness and stronger ability to detect complex criminal activities. The project also produced work on safeguards and citizen perspectives, reflecting the sensitivity of AI use in policing.

evidence.quote: At a conceptual level, AIDA integrates data ingestion, automated mining, entity and relationship extraction, knowledge representation and visual interfaces so that analysts can identify patterns, links and risks across large datasets.

results.title: Evaluate science and business cooperation in terms of knowledge usage efficiency
results.proposal: Evaluate science and business cooperation in terms of knowledge usage efficiency. Public innovation agencies need to understand whether scientific knowledge generated by universities and research institutions is effectively used by businesses and economic sectors. In Lithuania, GovTech Lab supported a challenge to create an AI-enabled tool for evaluating science-business cooperation and knowledge-use efficiency. The operational problem is that data on publications, graduates, joint projects and institutional knowledge-transfer activities can be dispersed, delayed or difficult to compare across sectors. This limits the ability of public authorities to assess which forms of cooperation produce value and where additional policy support is needed. The implementation develops an innovative, user-friendly tool to collect, process, classify and systematise relevant data from institutions of science and studies. At a conceptual level, the solution combines data integration, automated classification, interactive visualisation and analytical summaries, allowing users either to compare information quickly through diagrams or conduct deeper cross-sectional analysis. The expected impact is more transparent monitoring of knowledge-transfer effectiveness, better evidence for science and innovation policy, and improved capacity to identify sectors where scientific knowledge is being underused.
results.memo: Proceed. Evaluate science and business cooperation in terms of knowledge usage efficiency is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Fondo Caproni Project (AI for Culture)
results.proposal: Fondo Caproni Project (AI for Culture). Large cultural collections can become difficult to preserve and make accessible when the volume of material exceeds the capacity of manual cataloguing teams. The Caproni Collection contains approximately 200,000 historic photographs and aviation-related assets, including valuable images, memorabilia and documentation linked to Italian aeronautical history. The administrative challenge is to count, catalogue, classify, preserve, assess image quality and prepare selected materials for public exposure without imposing unsustainable labour requirements on cultural staff. The implementation explored the use of artificial intelligence to automate parts of the catalogue-building process, with particular emphasis on image-quality assessment and primary thematic classification. At a conceptual level, computer-vision models can identify damaged, blurred or low-quality photographs, group images into broad themes, support metadata generation and prioritise items requiring human review or conservation attention. This does not remove curatorial responsibility, but it can shift expert effort towards validation, interpretation and public presentation. The expected impact is faster digitisation, improved quality control, better searchability and broader public access to the Caproni heritage. Provincial material also confirms that the wider Caproni archive is being digitalised using PNRR funding, making the AI challenge part of a larger cultural-heritage digitisation trajectory. The case demonstrates how AI can support public cultural institutions when archive scale makes purely manual processes impractical.
results.memo: Proceed. Fondo Caproni Project (AI for Culture) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI for Monitoring Glacier water flows
results.proposal: AI for Monitoring Glacier water flows. Mountain water management depends on understanding how glacier melt contributes to downstream reservoirs, especially as climate change alters snow, ice and seasonal runoff dynamics. In Trentino, the Public AI Challenge applied artificial intelligence to the Careser Glacier in the Dolomites to reconstruct and forecast water flows towards reservoirs located downhill. The operational problem is that environmental monitoring datasets can contain gaps, missing measurements or discontinuities, making it harder for public authorities to understand hydrological conditions and anticipate changes in water availability. The implementation used dense neural-network techniques to estimate and reconstruct missing flow-rate data by learning relationships between available observations and expected water-flow patterns. At a conceptual level, the model supports prediction-measurement comparison: where sensor or historical data are incomplete, the neural network can infer plausible values and help reconstruct the hydrological series needed for environmental assessment. This creates a decision-support layer for monitoring glacier-fed systems, reservoir inflows and broader environmental status. The expected impact is improved continuity of hydrological monitoring, better evidence for water-resource planning and stronger public-sector capacity to use existing environmental datasets. The case is also relevant because it shows how an open-innovation challenge can introduce AI methods into provincial administration without requiring a full internal AI development team. Trentino Innovation describes the Public AI Challenge as a mechanism through which students develop predictive models and intelligent systems for public-administration needs.
results.memo: Proceed. AI for Monitoring Glacier water flows is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: AOC Consorci Administració Oberta de Catalunya
results.title: Automating the energy poverty report
results.proposal: Automating the energy poverty report. Energy-poverty protection in Catalonia requires municipalities to determine whether households with unpaid utility bills are socially vulnerable before suppliers can cut off gas, water or electricity. This legal safeguard is essential for vulnerable citizens, but the administrative process is burdensome: utility companies send monthly lists in different formats, and municipal staff must manually check whether each person or household is at social or economic risk. AOC developed a pilot cloud service to standardise and automate the preparation of energy-vulnerability reports, improving interoperability between suppliers, municipalities and other administrations. The implementation validates and cross-checks data, manages requests through a single point and helps municipal social services process supplier consultations more efficiently. At a conceptual level, the system combines data reception, identity or case matching, rule-based verification, workflow automation and administrative interoperability to produce or support the required report. The expected impact is shorter processing time, fewer manual checks, more consistent treatment of households and better prevention of unlawful supply cuts. AOC reports that the pilot began in 2023 in the social-services areas of El Prat de Llobregat, Granollers and Amposta and validated technical and organisational feasibility in a real environment. The initiative’s public value is significant because it converts a rights-protection obligation into a more scalable and less error-prone administrative process.
results.memo: Proceed. Automating the energy poverty report is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: LEOS Case 4: Checking for digital readiness
results.proposal: LEOS Case 4: Checking for digital readiness. Digital-ready legislation is increasingly important because laws and policies must be implementable through digital-by-default public services, data exchange and automated administrative processes. This LEOS case study investigates how smart drafting support could assess whether a legal act enables smooth digital implementation. The operational problem is that digital readiness is often assessed late or inconsistently, even though legislative wording can determine whether services can be automated, data can be reused and citizens can interact digitally with administrations. The proof of concept has three linked goals: calculate a digital-readiness index for a document, assess how normative citations and definitions propagate through the legal system, and develop a predictive model that estimates the index of new text fragments during drafting. The implementation uses legal-text analysis, citation analysis, modelling of definitions and predictive scoring. At a conceptual level, the system examines how a draft refers to other norms, how definitions affect implementation, and whether textual features support or hinder digital administration. The expected impact is earlier identification of provisions that may block digital-by-default services, better alignment between legal drafting and digital policy implementation, and more actionable feedback for drafters. The European Commission’s later LEOS work frames these cases as part of a broader move towards AI-based microservices that assist lawyers and policy developers while preserving human legal control.
results.memo: Proceed. LEOS Case 4: Checking for digital readiness is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: LEOS Case 3: Derogations and transitory provisions
results.proposal: LEOS Case 3: Derogations and transitory provisions. Derogations and transitional provisions are essential in legislation, but they can make legal obligations difficult to understand because they modify when, where or under what conditions a rule applies. This LEOS case study explores how classification and legal-text analysis can help identify derogations, connect them to the obligations they modify, and extract temporal or conditional parameters. The operational problem is that drafters and users may struggle to trace the relationship between a general rule and exceptions that appear elsewhere in a legal act or in related legislation. The implementation uses AI classification, legal annotation and structured analysis of normative text. At a conceptual level, the system detects clauses that create derogations or transitional regimes, identifies the initial obligations affected, and extracts information such as dates, durations, conditions and applicability criteria. These outputs can then support drafting review, legal navigation and clearer presentation of exceptions. The expected impact is improved legal clarity, fewer interpretative errors, better traceability of temporal rules and stronger support for digital legal services. For policy and drafting teams, the value is not automatic legal interpretation but earlier visibility of how exceptions interact with obligations. The use case was included in the European Commission’s LEOS smart-functionality study alongside pilots on corrigenda, transposition and digital readiness.
results.memo: Proceed. LEOS Case 3: Derogations and transitory provisions is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: LEOS Case 2: Transposition of EU directives
results.proposal: LEOS Case 2: Transposition of EU directives. Transposing EU directives into national law is legally complex because Member States must ensure that domestic provisions correctly reflect EU obligations while adapting them to national legal structures. This LEOS case study examines how AI-supported analysis could document and compare transposition more systematically. The pilot focuses on comparing selected directives with Italian domestic legislation to identify relationships between articles and detect where texts converge, diverge or omit relevant obligations. The implementation uses legal-text processing, similarity analysis, document comparison and visualisation tools within the broader LEOS smart-functionality framework. At a conceptual level, the system represents EU and national provisions, measures semantic or structural relationships between them, and highlights possible correspondences or gaps for legal experts to review. The expected impact is faster transposition analysis, improved documentation of legal implementation, better support for consolidation work and reduced risk that obligations are overlooked. Such functionality would not replace legal assessment, since transposition depends on legal interpretation, institutional context and national drafting conventions. Its value is to make comparison more systematic and navigable, helping experts focus on legally meaningful divergences. The European Commission’s LEOS smart-functionality study presents this case as one of four pilots exploring how hybrid AI can enhance legislative drafting and analysis.
results.memo: Proceed. LEOS Case 2: Transposition of EU directives is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: LEOS Case Study 1: Learning from examining corrigenda
results.proposal: LEOS Case Study 1: Learning from examining corrigenda. Legislative corrigenda reveal recurring drafting, formatting or reference problems that can undermine legal clarity and create costs when acts must be corrected and republished. This LEOS case study explored whether patterns in corrigenda could be identified and used to improve future legal drafting. The operational objective is to help drafters avoid avoidable errors, produce clearer legislation and reduce the administrative burden associated with post-publication corrections. The implementation uses legal-text analysis and hybrid AI methods applied to corpora of EU legislation and corrigenda, with particular attention to pattern detection and visualisation. At a conceptual level, the system clusters corrigenda, identifies recurring error types and translates those findings into possible smart functionalities for the LEOS legal drafting editor. These functionalities could warn drafters about risky structures, problematic references or repeated drafting patterns before publication. The expected impact is better regulation, clearer legislative texts, lower republication costs and faster availability of updated legislation. The case is part of a wider European Commission study on smart functionalities for LEOS, which piloted four use cases including corrigenda analysis, transposition, derogations and digital readiness. Public material describes the work as proof-of-concept research rather than a fully integrated production feature available across all EU legal drafting workflows.
results.memo: Proceed. LEOS Case Study 1: Learning from examining corrigenda is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: TrueBee (Digital forensics and blockchain tech against deceptive deepfake imaging in social media)
results.proposal: TrueBee (Digital forensics and blockchain tech against deceptive deepfake imaging in social media). Synthetic and manipulated images can support fraud, harassment, disinformation and other harms, especially when they circulate rapidly on social platforms and users lack tools to assess provenance. TrueBees was created to help distinguish trustworthy images from deceptive deepfake or AI-generated visual content by combining forensic analysis with blockchain-based traceability. The project originated in 2022 through collaboration between U-Hopper and researchers from the University of Trento, with support from TruBlo, an EU-funded Next Generation Internet initiative. The implementation combines an AI module based on image-forensics methods with a blockchain registry. Users can upload an image through a web interface, receive a TrueBees score indicating trustworthiness, and have the image hash and corresponding score stored on a blockchain. At a conceptual level, the system links media-forensic classification, provenance recording, immutable timestamping and consultation of prior assessments. The expected impact is improved detection of deceptive images, stronger evidential trails for journalists or fact-checkers, and more trust in media verification workflows. The project white paper reports a prototype architecture and cites high classification performance, including a 97.99% figure in the publicly indexed summary, while the current TrueBees website presents the work as moving from research into a practical solution for AI-generated image detection.

results.title: AI for Ethically Responsible Big Open Data (ETAPAS Case 1)
results.proposal: AI for Ethically Responsible Big Open Data (ETAPAS Case 1). Publishing open datasets from public administration can create transparency and research value, but it can also expose privacy, fairness and re-identification risks when datasets are sensitive or can be combined with other information. The ETAPAS NoiPA use case examines these risks in relation to Italy’s NoiPA platform, which provides HR shared services to around 100 central and local administrations and is used by approximately 2.2 million civil servants. The objective is to identify ethical issues, legal risks and possible negative impacts linked to the analysis and publication of anonymised open datasets, then define mitigation actions consistent with the GDPR and public-sector accountability. The implementation applies the ETAPAS responsible-disruptive-technology framework to NoiPA open-data publication processes, focusing on privacy, fairness, transparency and risk management. At a conceptual level, the use case analyses how dataset combinations, proxy variables, biased sampling or apparently anonymised aggregates could reveal personal information or discriminatory patterns. The expected impact is a more robust procedure for publishing open data, stronger safeguards against re-identification, and better institutional awareness of ethical risks in public-data analytics. The use case is particularly relevant because it treats open-data governance not as a purely technical anonymisation task, but as an organisational process requiring continuous assessment, mitigation and documentation.
results.memo: Proceed. AI for Ethically Responsible Big Open Data (ETAPAS Case 1) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Ministerium der Justiz und für Europa (JUM)
results.title: Machine translation service of the justice system - Developing translation memory
results.proposal: Machine translation service of the justice system - Developing translation memory. Judicial authorities often need to understand foreign-language documents quickly, but legal translation is sensitive, time-critical and unsuitable for generic public translation platforms when quality, confidentiality and data protection are required. In the German justice context, the project responds to the recurring need for rapid work translations across many languages, where in-house expertise may not be available and manual translation can be too slow or costly for initial case assessment. The objective is to help justice staff search and understand foreign-language material more effectively, while preserving control over legal data. The implementation uses neural machine translation trained on translated texts relevant to the judicial environment. At a conceptual level, foreign-language documents are processed through a secure translation system that produces immediate work translations, enabling users to obtain an overview, search documents more precisely and decide whether certified or expert translation is needed. A further development goal is translation memory: texts already processed as input or output are recognised and reused, improving consistency and efficiency over time. In regular operation, the system is intended to shift towards a central translation platform. The expected impact is faster access to multilingual legal material, lower thresholds for preliminary translations, reduced dependence on external platforms and better support for time-critical judicial workflows. Because legal meaning is context-dependent, the service remains a support tool rather than a substitute for authoritative legal translation.

results.title: The LOVOT social AI robot in nursing homes to help people with dementia
results.proposal: The LOVOT social AI robot in nursing homes to help people with dementia. Dementia care often involves residents who experience loneliness, high arousal, withdrawal or difficulty sustaining social interaction, while care staff must balance emotional support with limited time and resources. Aalborg, Viborg and Skive municipalities piloted LOVOT in Danish nursing homes to investigate whether a social robot could contribute to quality of life for people with dementia. The target group includes residents in care centres who may benefit from comforting interaction, sensory stimulation or a non-demanding social presence. The implementation uses LOVOT, a small social robot designed to respond to touch, speech and eye contact through sensors, movement, warmth, sounds, facial expression and body language. At a conceptual level, the robot detects social cues, reacts in ways that resemble a living companion, and develops interaction patterns that may encourage residents to engage, calm down or seek contact. The technology does not replace professional care or relational work by staff; rather, it provides an additional welfare-technology tool that can be introduced where a resident’s needs and preferences make it appropriate. The expected impact is improved wellbeing, reduced loneliness or agitation, and richer activity options in dementia care. Ethical attention remains necessary, especially because lifelike robots can blur emotional boundaries for people with cognitive impairment, making staff assessment and transparent use essential.

results.title: AI-enabled system for assistive technology requests
results.proposal: AI-enabled system for assistive technology requests. Municipal welfare services must process large volumes of applications for assistive technologies while ensuring that urgent cases receive attention quickly and that documentation is complete. Sønderborg Municipality handles around 5,000 annual requests for body-worn aids, including items such as corsets, diabetes materials and orthopaedic footwear, with 15 to 20 applications arriving each day. The operational objective is to reduce processing time and improve prioritisation without weakening the individual assessment that each citizen’s situation requires. The implementation tests an AI-enabled system that reviews whether the necessary medical or administrative documentation is present and sorts applications according to urgency and condition. At a conceptual level, the system analyses application content, checks completeness against case requirements, identifies missing information and supports triage so that caseworkers can focus on the most urgent or complex files first. The expected impact is faster case handling, fewer delays caused by missing documents, better allocation of caseworker time and a more reliable application pathway for citizens needing assistive technology. GovLaunch reports that the municipality received a DKK 3.2 million grant for a pilot of AI-supported application review, indicating that the initiative was designed as a funded test rather than a fully mature service.

results.title: AI-enabled platform for reduced hospitalizations among senior residents
results.proposal: AI-enabled platform for reduced hospitalizations among senior residents. Municipal eldercare services need to identify health deterioration early enough to prevent avoidable hospital admissions, while also allocating limited staff and resources where they are most needed. Køge Municipality’s planned AI-enabled platform uses information from municipal caregiver notes to support earlier disease detection among senior residents. The objective is to complement staff training in early diagnosis and patient communication with a data-supported tool that can detect warning signs in everyday care documentation. The implementation analyses text notes and care observations, looking for patterns that may indicate emerging illness or increased risk. At a conceptual level, the system processes caregiver documentation, identifies clinically relevant signals, and provides recommendations on local resource deployment so that officials and care managers can respond earlier. The expected impact is fewer preventable hospitalisations, better targeting of municipal care resources, improved continuity for older citizens and stronger evidence for preventive eldercare. The Danish Digitisation Agency funded the project and intended to use the Køge platform as a model for other municipalities, showing its role as a public-sector AI signature initiative. However, available public sources describe it as planned or project-based rather than as a fully embedded operational service, so the current maturity should be treated cautiously.
