results.title: Aarhus Municipality creates an AI-enabled analytical tool for sustainable procurement decisions
results.proposal: Aarhus Municipality creates an AI-enabled analytical tool for sustainable procurement decisions. Public procurement has a major climate footprint, because everyday purchases of goods and services generate indirect emissions across large supplier chains. Aarhus Municipality worked with the local company Konsido to make these impacts more visible and actionable, helping public buyers understand how purchasing patterns could be redirected towards more sustainable options. The objective was to move sustainable procurement from broad policy ambition to concrete decision support, using municipal expenditure data to identify where emissions reductions might be achieved. The implementation developed Konsido CPO, an AI-based analytical tool that processes purchasing behaviour, supplier expenditure and climate-emissions information. GovLaunch reports that the tool divided municipal purchases into around 1,000 categories based on invoice analysis, while Aarhus describes the project as further developing Konsido CO2-focused Procurement Optimisation for automated Scope 3 climate accounting. At a conceptual level, the system links e-invoices, financial systems, supplier registers, category structures and emissions estimates to produce procurement intelligence. The expected impact is better prioritisation of green purchasing measures, more continuous follow-up on whether interventions work, and stronger ability to align procurement with climate-reduction targets. Konsido now presents itself as providing AI-based consumption and climate-emission analytics for public authorities and private companies, suggesting that the solution has moved beyond an isolated municipal experiment.
results.memo: Proceed. Aarhus Municipality creates an AI-enabled analytical tool for sustainable procurement decisions is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Ghent turns downtown traffic data into predictions during three-month pilot
results.proposal: Ghent turns downtown traffic data into predictions during three-month pilot. Busy city centres need better information on how pedestrians, cyclists and vehicles move through streets, especially when congestion affects shops, public space, safety and accessibility. Ghent’s three-month pilot tested whether anonymised traffic data from downtown streets could be converted into predictions about when and where crowding or congestion would occur. The municipality’s objective was both analytical and practical: to understand high-traffic areas better, provide useful intelligence for city officials and businesses, and identify which sensing technology would be most suitable for possible wider deployment. The implementation tested four types of cameras and sensors, each collecting anonymised counts or movement data on pedestrians, cyclists and vehicles. At a conceptual level, the system combined urban sensing, data anonymisation, time-series analysis and predictive modelling, using several months of observations to forecast likely pressure points in the city centre. These insights could support decisions on mobility management, public-space planning and retail-area operations. The expected impact was earlier anticipation of congestion, more evidence-based traffic and crowd management, and better understanding of sensor performance before scale-up. Ghent has since continued to experiment with data-driven mobility tools, including EIT Urban Mobility-supported work using AI and drones for road-safety analysis, indicating an ongoing smart-mobility trajectory beyond the initial pilot.

The chatbot draws from official knowledge bases and guides users through common issues in a conversational format. It operates alongside existing support channels, offering immediate assistance through a widely used social platform. The service improves accessibility, reduces call centre workload, and speeds up resolution of simple enquiries. results.company: City of Wien - Municipal Directorate of Strategic ICT
results.title: A DIGITAL BUILDING PERMIT SYSTEM FOR THE SMART CITY in Wien
results.proposal: A DIGITAL BUILDING PERMIT SYSTEM FOR THE SMART CITY in Wien. Building-permit procedures are often slow, document-heavy and difficult for applicants and administrations to navigate, especially in a growing city that receives high volumes of construction applications. Vienna’s BRISE project rethinks this process by replacing paper-based, two-dimensional submissions with a more integrated digital workflow for construction approvals. The City of Vienna’s objective is to make permit procedures faster, more transparent and less costly, while creating a model that can later be transferred to other fields of public administration. The implementation combines Building Information Modelling, artificial intelligence, augmented reality and robotic process automation. Instead of submitting 2D plans, applicants use digital 3D building models that can be checked against relevant building regulations. At a conceptual level, the system connects BIM data, automated rule checking, administrative workflows, AR-supported inspection and digital collaboration between applicants, experts and public officials. This creates an end-to-end basis for managing a construction project from planning and submission to site inspection and acceptance of the completed structure. The expected impact is faster processing, improved project quality, greater transparency and reduced administrative effort. OECD OPSI reports 50% time savings, while Vienna’s project material notes approximately €4.8 million in EU Urban Innovative Actions funding and implementation by March 2023.
results.memo: Proceed. A DIGITAL BUILDING PERMIT SYSTEM FOR THE SMART CITY in Wien is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Flemish Employment and Vocational Training Service (VDAB)
results.title: Managing vacancies - Recommender: the amazon of the labour market
results.proposal: Managing vacancies - Recommender: the amazon of the labour market. Public employment services face challenges in efficiently matching jobseekers with suitable vacancies, particularly as labour markets become more dynamic and digitally mediated. Traditional keyword-based search functions often fail to capture skills proximity, transferable competences and evolving job profiles. Stakeholders include jobseekers, employers and public employment agencies. The objective is to enhance matching quality and labour market efficiency through personalised vacancy recommendations. The system leverages big data analytics to process vacancy descriptions, candidate profiles and historical placement data. Collaborative filtering, content-based recommendation algorithms and skills ontology mapping are used to infer relevance scores and suggest vacancies aligned with a jobseeker’s competences and preferences. Integration with the public vacancy platform enables real-time recommendations upon user login, supported by feedback loops to continuously refine model accuracy. Expected benefits include improved placement rates, reduced job search duration, better utilisation of transferable skills and enhanced user experience comparable to leading e-commerce recommendation systems.

results.company: Flemish Employment and Vocational Training Service (VDAB)
results.title: Competence based matching - a success story from Flanders to Malta
results.proposal: Competence based matching - a success story from Flanders to Malta. Public employment services often struggle to match jobseekers and vacancies accurately due to vague job descriptions and inconsistent skill profiling. This leads to inefficient labour market matching and prolonged unemployment. This use case involves the Flemish employment service (VDAB), employers, jobseekers, and later the Maltese Public Employment Service, with the objective of improving match quality and labour market efficiency. The system is implemented through structured competency frameworks that require employers to define vacancies in detailed, standardised skill terms, while jobseekers build equally comprehensive competency profiles. Matching algorithms compare these profiles to generate higher-quality matches based on skills rather than job titles alone. The concept was successfully transferred from Flanders to Malta in 2016, demonstrating cross-border applicability. The solution improves placement accuracy, reduces mismatch, and shortens recruitment times. It supports mobility of best practices across Europe and delivers measurable value through more effective employment services and better labour market outcomes.

results.title: Driving collective data governance through smart engagement platforms (COLLIBRA)
results.proposal: Driving collective data governance through smart engagement platforms (COLLIBRA). Data governance often remains distant from the everyday contexts in which business users create, interpret and reuse data, leading to weak adoption, unclear ownership and limited trust in datasets. This project sought to bring governance closer to actual workplaces by embedding support into the systems of engagement where decisions are already discussed, such as boardrooms, design workshops, Confluence, Slack and other collaboration tools. The objective was to help users make better low-level decisions when interacting with data, while generating richer contextual information on how datasets are used. The implementation developed a platform that uses artificial intelligence to learn bottom-up data-usage context and provide reliable, machine-accurate recommendations for the next best action inside core business applications. At a conceptual level, the system combines data-governance metadata, engagement traces, workflow context, recommendation logic and integration with collaboration environments. This allows governance guidance to appear at the point of use rather than as a separate administrative obligation. The expected impact is better data stewardship, stronger trust in datasets, more efficient governance decisions and more time for users to focus on substantive business problems. The project also supports dataset promotion by helping users build credibility around data generated through collaborative engagements, making governance more participatory and embedded in practice.

results.title: EV Charging Optimiser
results.proposal: EV Charging Optimiser. The rapid electrification of vehicle fleets creates a practical energy-management problem: charging many vehicles at the same time can overload local capacity, increase costs and make operations difficult to coordinate, especially in unpredictable real environments. VUB and Energis developed the EV Charging Optimiser to test how an entire fleet of electric vehicles could be charged in a coordinated and controlled way, both in laboratory settings and in operational contexts. The objective is to move beyond static charging schedules and create a controller that remains robust when vehicles arrive late, leave early, require different charging levels or face changing electricity and infrastructure constraints. The implementation applies reinforcement learning to charging scheduling, allowing the system to learn policies that balance fleet requirements, grid constraints and operational uncertainty. At a conceptual level, the controller observes charging demand, vehicle availability, battery states and environmental constraints, then selects charging actions that improve long-term outcomes rather than optimising only the immediate moment. The expected impact is more efficient fleet charging, lower peak demand, improved use of charging infrastructure and better integration of electric mobility into energy systems. By testing the approach in real environments, the project emphasises robustness and practical viability, which are critical for fleet operators that cannot rely on perfectly predictable charging behaviour.

evidence.quote: The objective is to move beyond static charging schedules and create a controller that remains robust when vehicles arrive late, leave early, require different charging levels or face changing electricity and infrastructure constraints.

results.title: CSAI: Cyber Security Artificial Intelligence
results.proposal: CSAI: Cyber Security Artificial Intelligence. Cybersecurity teams operate in environments where attacks evolve quickly, alerts are numerous and purely rule-based systems may struggle to distinguish meaningful threats from routine activity. CSAI responds to this challenge by exploring how more intelligent models and techniques can support cybersecurity technology beyond automated analytics alone. The project, funded by Flanders’ innovation and entrepreneurship agency, brings research and industry actors together to investigate methods that can improve detection, reasoning and response across cybersecurity contexts, from devices and networks to compliance. The implementation combines symbolic and sub-symbolic approaches, using domain-specific cybersecurity knowledge, mechanisms to acquire new knowledge and techniques that can apply that knowledge to operational tasks. At a conceptual level, CSAI seeks to connect machine-learning models, knowledge representation, threat intelligence and security workflows so that systems can reason more effectively about risks and incidents. The expected impact is stronger cyber-threat detection, more robust decision support for analysts, and improved ability to apply research advances in practical security products and services. By focusing on hybrid intelligence rather than only statistical detection, the project aims to make cybersecurity tools more explainable, adaptable and aligned with professional expertise. Its public value lies in strengthening digital resilience in a domain where both technical sophistication and trustworthiness are essential.
results.memo: Proceed. CSAI: Cyber Security Artificial Intelligence is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: EPD: Employability in programme development
results.proposal: EPD: Employability in programme development. Higher education institutions increasingly need reliable labour-market intelligence to ensure that courses and programmes equip students with skills that employers actually demand. The EPD project addresses this gap by helping participating universities understand what information on skills demand is available, what programme designers and employability practitioners need, and how this evidence can be incorporated into curriculum development. The objective is to establish a feedback loop between the labour market and higher education, so that programme design is informed not only by academic expertise but also by evolving employment patterns and employer expectations. The implementation uses artificial intelligence and natural language processing to analyse labour-market data, identify skills signals and support the development of a prototype dashboard for higher education staff. Secondary data sources are complemented by employer input, while the project also curates European best practices in employability through case studies. At a conceptual level, the system combines skills extraction, labour-market intelligence, dashboard visualisation and stakeholder feedback to make employability evidence usable for institutional decision-making. The expected impact is better alignment between curricula and labour-market needs, more evidence-based course design, and improved graduate employability. By translating complex labour-market information into a practical dashboard, EPD helps universities move from general employability ambitions to concrete, data-supported programme-development choices. The project was funded under Erasmus+ for 2021–2023 with a grant of €433,771.
results.memo: Proceed. EPD: Employability in programme development is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Healthy Food production with AI
results.proposal: Healthy Food production with AI. Food manufacturers face a difficult product-development problem when they try to make bakery and patisserie products healthier without compromising taste, texture, functionality or consumer acceptance. The Healthy Food R&D project brings Puratos together with the Artificial Intelligence Lab at Vrije Universiteit Brussel to support recipe development with data-driven prediction rather than relying only on repeated trial-and-error experimentation. The objective is to identify healthier ingredients, understand how they behave during and after baking, and recommend recipes with a more balanced nutritional profile while maintaining the product characteristics expected by consumers and industrial processes. The implementation develops a multi-objective predictive model that can evaluate several goals simultaneously, such as nutritional improvement, ingredient behaviour, sensory properties and technical performance. At a conceptual level, the system links ingredient data, processing conditions, product characteristics and predictive modelling to generate recommendations for recipe development. This makes it possible to explore trade-offs between health, quality and manufacturability before committing to extensive physical testing. The expected impact is faster R&D cycles, lower development cost, more systematic formulation of healthier products and improved capacity to innovate in bakery and patisserie. Although the public VUB material describes the project clearly as an R&D collaboration, I found no evidence that the specific model has been released as a standalone commercial tool.

results.title: Webapp L15 - digital ecosystem of Lombardy Region
results.proposal: Webapp L15 - digital ecosystem of Lombardy Region. Regional digital ecosystems can help public and private actors expose services through APIs, creating reusable building blocks for transport, tourism, healthcare, mobility and other domains. Lombardy’s E015 digital ecosystem was designed as a platform where public and private providers could publish APIs and combine them into user-facing services. The Webapp E015, also referred to as L15 in some catalogues, demonstrated the potential of this ecosystem by bringing together multiple services in a single digital environment, including information such as healthcare-unit availability in regional hospitals and parking availability. The implementation was based on a customisation developed by ARIA S.p.A. using Open 2.0, the open-source application made available by Regione Lombardia for collaborative tools. At a conceptual level, the platform operated as an API aggregation and service-composition environment: providers exposed data or functions, while applications could reuse them to create integrated services for citizens, businesses or institutions. Its expected impact was to demonstrate interoperability, stimulate reuse of regional digital assets, support service innovation and show how a mature API ecosystem could generate practical applications. The webapp was ultimately discontinued in January 2024 because it had completed its demonstrative role. The wider E015 initiative was considered mature, with multiple success stories showing that the ecosystem model had been validated beyond the original demonstrator.

results.title: iBeacon Living Lab
results.proposal: iBeacon Living Lab. Urban Internet of Things ecosystems require open test environments where developers, citizens, businesses and public authorities can experiment with sensors and location-based services in real streets. Amsterdam’s iBeacon Living Lab, including the Beacon Mile, was created as a public demonstrator for beacon and LoRa-enabled sensor applications. The initiative gave tourists and other users location-based information during city walks, while also serving as a testbed for Amsterdam’s broader IoT economy. The implementation used beacons and long-range sensor-beacon infrastructure deployed in the city, with Glimworm and KPN playing key roles alongside the City of Amsterdam. At a conceptual level, beacons transmit proximity signals to nearby mobile devices, enabling context-specific information delivery, while LoRa-enabled components support wider sensor-network experimentation. The expected impact was to stimulate IoT innovation, provide real-life conditions for developers, improve visitor information and demonstrate how public urban infrastructure can host digital services. The project also helped connect beacon experimentation with smart-city policy discussions, open innovation and sensor-network deployment. Available public evidence points to a pioneering mid-2010s living-lab initiative rather than a currently active citywide service. Its lasting value is therefore as an early urban IoT test environment that helped familiarise Amsterdam with beacon-guided services and public sensor experimentation.

results.title: MyHelsinki Open API
results.proposal: MyHelsinki Open API. Tourism, event promotion and city discovery services depend on high-quality local data that can be reused by developers, businesses and public-sector actors. The MyHelsinki Open API was created to provide structured access to information about places, events and activities in Helsinki and the surrounding region. The objective was to make city-curated content available as open data, encouraging reuse in digital services while maintaining quality standards and multilingual accessibility. The implementation exposed three databases through an application programming interface, allowing users to query and filter content by location, category, time and other criteria. At a conceptual level, the API turned Helsinki Marketing’s curated destination information into machine-readable resources that third-party applications could integrate into websites, mobile apps or digital services. Content was maintained by experts, updated regularly and made available in Finnish, Swedish, English and Chinese, improving both local and international reuse. The expected impact was stronger tourism innovation, easier development of city-service applications, improved visibility of Helsinki’s events and attractions, and reduced duplication of content maintenance across public and private platforms. The case illustrates how open APIs can serve as public digital infrastructure, enabling an ecosystem of services around trusted municipal data. Although not an AI use case in itself, it was an important example of data-driven public-service enablement and reuse.

results.title: ARMAR-6 – Cooperative robot in industrial environments
results.proposal: ARMAR-6 – Cooperative robot in industrial environments. Industrial maintenance often requires workers to perform varied physical tasks in environments where tool use, unexpected situations and human cooperation are central. ARMAR-6 was developed by Karlsruhe Institute of Technology as a humanoid assistance robot able to support people in industrial contexts, especially where tasks cannot be fully anticipated at programming time. The objective is to create a robot that can recognise when a human partner needs help, use human-designed tools and perform or assist with maintenance activities. The implementation combines a human-like upper body, bimanual manipulation, mobile movement, perception, action planning and interaction capabilities. At a conceptual level, the robot observes the work situation, interprets human activity, identifies opportunities to assist and executes tasks such as handing tools, holding components or operating equipment. Its human-like morphology allows it to interact with objects and tools designed for people, such as drills or hammers. The expected impact is safer and more flexible industrial support, reduced physical burden on workers and better handling of tasks that are difficult to automate with fixed machinery. ARMAR-6 remains primarily a research platform for collaborative humanoid robotics, but it is important because it demonstrates how industrial assistance can move from pre-programmed automation towards proactive, context-aware cooperation with human workers.

results.title: FlatFish - Autonomous inspections in the deep sea
results.proposal: FlatFish - Autonomous inspections in the deep sea. Inspection of offshore oil and gas infrastructure is expensive, technically complex and risky when it depends on remotely operated vehicles, support vessels and specialist divers. FlatFish was developed to simplify repeated subsea inspection by using an autonomous underwater vehicle capable of operating for extended periods around underwater structures. The objective is to reduce inspection cost and risk while improving the frequency and quality of monitoring for industrial assets. The implementation combines autonomous navigation, acoustic and optical sensors, subsea docking concepts and robotic inspection capabilities. At a conceptual level, the vehicle maps and localises itself underwater, follows inspection missions, collects visual and sensor data, and performs tasks such as structure and pipeline inspection without continuous tethered control. Original research involved DFKI, the Brazilian Institute of Robotics and Shell, while later industrial development connected FlatFish to Saipem’s Hydrone underwater robotics programme. The expected impact is lower reliance on maintenance ships, reduced exposure of personnel to hazardous offshore work, better repeatability of inspections and more efficient asset monitoring. Recent public information indicates that FlatFish has advanced beyond laboratory research: Saipem reported successful functional testing with Petrobras in 2026, including autonomous inspection missions, cathodic-protection measurements and wall-thickness assessments.

results.title: PhenoRob proejct - Fertilise crops more specifically
results.proposal: PhenoRob proejct - Fertilise crops more specifically. Crop production must become more resource-efficient while maintaining yields under climate, biodiversity and environmental pressures. PhenoRob, the Cluster of Excellence led by the University of Bonn with Forschungszentrum Jülich, addresses this challenge by combining robotics, phenotyping, digitalisation and machine learning for sustainable crop production. The objective is to understand plant growth, nutrient use and water efficiency more precisely so that fertiliser and crop-protection measures can be applied only where and when needed. The implementation uses ground robots, drones, sensor-based phenotyping, field monitoring and large-scale data analysis. At a conceptual level, robotic platforms collect high-resolution data on crop growth, soil, canopy structure and field conditions, while machine-learning models transform these observations into knowledge about plant performance and resource needs. This supports more targeted agronomic interventions and helps researchers explore crop adaptability to climate conditions and biodiversity-preserving practices. The expected impact is lower input use, reduced environmental burden, better yield stability and more robust evidence for sustainable farming systems. PhenoRob is not a single deployed product but a major interdisciplinary research cluster whose work feeds methods, prototypes and scientific knowledge into future agricultural practice. In 2025, the cluster received further funding for a second phase extending to 2032, confirming continued institutional support.

results.title: Ion - the world's first government advisor
results.proposal: Ion - the world's first government advisor. Governments increasingly seek tools to understand public concerns in real time, but turning large volumes of citizen expression into reliable policy insight raises questions about transparency, representativeness and accountability. Romania’s ION was launched in March 2023 as an artificial-intelligence government adviser, presented as a system that could collect and synthesise citizens’ opinions and concerns for public officials. The objective was to enhance citizen-government communication by receiving direct submissions through an official platform and monitoring public online content to identify issues that mattered to the population. The implementation combined an AI-branded public interface with sentiment or topic-analysis ambitions, aiming to generate a real-time snapshot of public mood and communicate it to government decision-makers. At a conceptual level, the system was intended to aggregate citizen messages, detect recurrent topics, summarise concerns and support public officials with a non-traditional channel of feedback. Its expected impact was more responsive government, broader participation and faster awareness of social priorities. However, the project soon faced criticism over transparency, data collection and unclear evidence of meaningful functionality. Later reporting indicated that ION had been reduced to a simple informational chatbot, and subsequent accounts suggested that it was removed from government premises after administrative change. The case is therefore best understood as an ambitious but short-lived experiment in AI-mediated civic listening.

results.title: Artificial intelligence finds disease-related genes
results.proposal: Artificial intelligence finds disease-related genes. This use case addresses a central challenge in biomedical research: disease mechanisms are often distributed across large numbers of interacting genes, making it difficult for researchers to identify meaningful patterns in high-dimensional gene-expression data. Scientists at Linköping University led a study exploring how these complex datasets could be used to discover groups of genes associated with disease and, in the longer term, support more precise diagnosis and treatment. The objective was not to replace biological interpretation, but to give researchers a stronger exploratory method for finding structures that may otherwise remain hidden in very large molecular datasets. The implementation used an artificial neural network trained on extensive gene-expression information, allowing the system to learn patterns without relying only on predefined disease categories or manually selected markers. At a conceptual level, the model processed expression profiles, detected relationships between genes and organised them into groups that could reveal disease-relevant biological signals. The expected impact is improved discovery of candidate genes, better understanding of disease pathways and stronger foundations for precision medicine and individualised treatment. Although the work remains research-oriented, its value lies in showing how neural-network methods can support biomedical knowledge discovery by extracting interpretable signals from datasets that exceed the capacity of conventional manual analysis.

results.title: Housing Assistance Payment Robotics Pilot
results.proposal: Housing Assistance Payment Robotics Pilot. The Housing Assistance Payment Robotics Pilot addressed the operational pressure faced by the HAP Shared Service Centre, operated by Limerick City and County Council on behalf of the local government sector. The centre manages very large payment and tenancy volumes, including more than 47,000 tenancies, 27,000 landlords, over €400 million in payments and more than €100 million in rent collection, with projected growth to 80,000 tenancies, 55,000 landlords and €600 million in payments by 2021. These volumes create substantial administrative workload and a strong incentive to identify processes that can be automated safely. In 2018, Agilisys carried out a proof-of-concept pilot examining three micro-processes within the centre. The implementation used robotic process automation to test whether repeatable, rule-based activities could be executed by software robots across existing business systems. Conceptually, the pilot assessed process suitability, automation feasibility, savings potential and opportunities for wider business-system integration. The results demonstrated that efficiencies and savings could be achieved, and the subsequent business case suggested that replacing 10 complex processes with RPA could generate considerable savings while improving services for tenants, landlords and administrative stakeholders. The use case therefore provided a practical basis for identifying further immediate automation opportunities within the HAP SSC.

results.title: DPER Robotic Process Automation (RPA) Pilot
results.proposal: DPER Robotic Process Automation (RPA) Pilot. The DPER Robotic Process Automation pilot examined whether routine, stable and fully computer-based administrative processes in Irish central government could be automated to improve efficiency and service delivery. Public bodies often manage high-volume tasks that require staff to copy, check or transfer information between digital systems, even when the rules are clear and human judgement is limited. In 2017, the Department of Public Expenditure and Reform coordinated a pilot in which four government departments selected suitable processes to test the potential of robotic process automation. The implementation used software robots to operate existing applications at user-interface level, automating labour-intensive, rules-based tasks without requiring wholesale replacement of legacy systems. Conceptually, RPA was applied as a non-invasive automation layer that could log into systems, follow predefined steps, transfer data, validate entries and generate outputs consistently. The expected impact was improved accuracy, fewer manual errors, faster processing and the release of staff time for higher-value work. The pilot also helped the Irish public service understand which process characteristics make automation feasible and what governance, procurement and implementation arrangements would be needed for wider adoption. A later government RPA framework indicates that the pilot contributed to a broader national approach to automation services.

results.title: WELCOME(Multiple Intelligent Conversation Agent Services for Reception, Management and Integration)
results.proposal: WELCOME(Multiple Intelligent Conversation Agent Services for Reception, Management and Integration). WELCOME focused on supporting the reception and integration of third-country nationals, migrants and refugees through personalised digital assistance for both newcomers and public administrations. Reception and integration processes often involve complex registration steps, orientation needs, language barriers, civic education, access to local services and social inclusion challenges, while administrations must provide guidance across diverse profiles and contexts. The project aimed to create a psychologically and socially competent support environment that could help users navigate these processes in a more accessible and personalised way. Its implementation developed intelligent multilingual conversational agents, including embodied assistants, designed for contexts such as registration, orientation, language learning, civic education and community integration. The system used personalisation techniques so that agent behaviour could adapt to the user’s profile and situation, and it also explored immersive virtual and augmented reality technologies to make interaction more realistic and engaging. Conceptually, WELCOME combined conversational interfaces, multilingual processing, user profiling, interaction adaptation and immersive service design. The expected impact was better access to integration guidance, reduced pressure on frontline administrations, more consistent information provision and improved user experience for migrants and refugees. The services were validated through pilot use cases in Catalonia, Spain, Germany and Greece.

results.title: NADINE -  platform to promote migrant inclusion
results.proposal: NADINE -  platform to promote migrant inclusion. NADINE was designed to support migrant inclusion by improving the way public authorities and guidance professionals understand skills, needs and available services. Migration brings significant human capital to Europe, yet integration systems may struggle to match people’s abilities, career ambitions, educational requirements and social or cultural needs with real opportunities in host societies. The project therefore aimed to build a platform that could support employability, career guidance and service matching on the basis of richer evidence about both migrants and local environments. Its implementation used open data, large-scale data repositories and analytical tools to create two main information banks: one concerning host societies and services, and another concerning migrants’ profiles, needs and skills. As users interacted with the platform, further data could be collected to refine the system and improve recommendations. Conceptually, NADINE combined skills assessment, labour-market intelligence, local-service mapping, guidance tools and personalised support interfaces. The expected impact was more tailored assistance for migrants, better use of skills, improved decision support for professionals and stronger alignment between integration services and actual needs. By linking social, educational, cultural and employment dimensions, NADINE approached inclusion as a multidimensional process rather than only a labour-market matching exercise.

results.title: REBUILD -  ICT toolbox providing support to both migrants and refugees
results.proposal: REBUILD -  ICT toolbox providing support to both migrants and refugees. REBUILD aimed to improve how migrants and refugees access services in Europe while helping local service providers manage integration support more effectively. The operational challenge was two-sided: newcomers often face fragmented information, language barriers, unfamiliar administrative systems and difficulties identifying relevant opportunities, while public authorities and support organisations need better tools to understand needs, coordinate services and evaluate impact. The project adopted a user-centred and participatory design approach, involving migrants, refugees and service providers from the early stages so that ethical, cultural and practical requirements could shape the solution. Its implementation developed an ICT toolbox using user profiling, skills-and-needs matching, chatbot functions and accessible service interfaces. Conceptually, the ecosystem connected information about individuals’ needs, skills and preferences with local service offers, guidance pathways and administrative workflows. It also included mechanisms to monitor and validate socio-economic impact. The expected value was more personalised support, easier access to services, improved communication between users and administrations, and better evidence for integration policies. By combining digital tools with co-design, REBUILD sought to avoid imposing a generic integration platform and instead build services around the lived experience of migrants and refugees and the operational realities of local providers.

results.title: WeGovNow: Collective and participative approaches for addressing local policy challenges
results.proposal: WeGovNow: Collective and participative approaches for addressing local policy challenges. WeGovNow explored how local public services and policy challenges could be addressed through collaborative digital participation, treating citizens as partners in public-service delivery rather than passive users or customers. Local authorities often need to respond to issues such as neighbourhood improvement, service quality, environmental concerns or community planning, but conventional consultation channels can be fragmented, episodic and disconnected from day-to-day civic action. The project therefore aimed to provide public administrations, citizens, civil-society organisations and local businesses with digital tools for co-production, collective proposition development and shared problem-solving. Its implementation integrated emerging civic technologies into a pilot platform tested under day-to-day conditions in the London Borough of Southwark, the City of Turin and San Donà di Piave. Conceptually, the platform combined participatory mapping, issue reporting, discussion, collective proposal development and community coordination functions. The project also examined legal, ethical and organisational conditions to ensure democratic legitimacy and practical exploitability. The expected impact was stronger citizen engagement, more responsive local services and improved evidence on how digital co-production works in real administrative contexts. During the final project year, 9,976 pilot user accounts were registered across the three pilot municipalities, showing meaningful uptake in real-life settings.

results.title: SIMPATICO - Platform for PS - Italian Usecase
results.proposal: SIMPATICO - Platform for PS - Italian Usecase. SIMPATICO was developed to improve the way citizens and companies interact with online public services, addressing a common weakness in digital administration: many services are standardised replicas of offline procedures, designed mainly around internal organisational logic rather than the needs, language and behaviour of users. In the Italian use case, the Municipality of Trento provided a public-service context in which administrative procedures could be simplified and adapted through continuous feedback. The objective was to make digital services easier to understand, reduce the distance between users and administrations, and identify why online procedures remain difficult or underused. Public administrations supplied formal knowledge about procedures, while citizens, companies, civil servants and professionals contributed questions, doubts, explanations and improvement suggestions. At a conceptual level, the platform linked service interfaces, text simplification, workflow guidance, user feedback and collaborative knowledge creation, allowing interactions to be progressively refined. The expected impact was improved usability of online services, fewer errors during administrative procedures, better citizen satisfaction and stronger capacity for administrations to learn from recurring difficulties. By combining institutional knowledge with bottom-up input, SIMPATICO treated service improvement as a continuous, participatory process rather than a one-off redesign of digital forms.

results.title: RECAP - Reliable Capacity Provisioning and Enhanced Remediation for Distributed Cloud Applications
results.proposal: RECAP - Reliable Capacity Provisioning and Enhanced Remediation for Distributed Cloud Applications. RECAP supported the implementation of the Common Agricultural Policy by developing personalised public services for farmers, agricultural consultants and administrations responsible for monitoring compliance. CAP rules create complex obligations, particularly around cross-compliance, and public authorities need efficient ways to monitor whether requirements are being met across diverse agricultural contexts. Farmers and consultants also benefit from clearer, more transparent information on obligations and potential breaches. The project implemented a cloud-based Software-as-a-Service platform using open Earth Observation data, user-generated information and geospatial data to support compliance monitoring. Conceptually, the system extracted relevant features from satellite and other open data, correlated them with information available to public organisations and modelled potential breaches of CAP requirements. This enabled authorities and inspectors to focus attention on likely non-compliance while giving users more personalised support. The expected impact was more efficient administrative control, lower monitoring burden, greater transparency for farmers and better targeting of inspections. By combining Earth Observation with cloud services and user-generated data, RECAP demonstrated how agricultural public services can shift from document-heavy compliance checks towards more continuous, data-supported monitoring.

Its implementation used Linked Open Statistical Data technologies and ran pilot studies in six countries, testing how structured, interoperable data could support new public-service models. Conceptually, the project combined linked data, semantic technologies, statistical datasets, co-creation methods and public-administration process redesign. It followed an iterative approach, using development and evaluation cycles to refine the OpenGovIntelligence framework and associated tools. The expected impact was greater transparency, more innovative public services, improved reuse of official statistics and stronger collaboration between administrations and external stakeholders. By treating data as a shared resource for service design, the project aimed to stimulate innovation and creativity while strengthening evidence-based administration.

results.title: ENLARGE - ENergies for Local Administrations: Renovate Governance in Europe
results.proposal: ENLARGE - ENergies for Local Administrations: Renovate Governance in Europe. ENLARGE examined how public authorities, experts and civil society can work together to design and deliver more effective public policies and services, with a particular focus on sustainable energy. Local administrations often face complex energy-transition challenges that require public acceptance, technical expertise and coordinated action across stakeholders. Traditional top-down policy design may not capture local knowledge or ensure long-term legitimacy, especially when energy measures affect daily life, costs and public-service delivery. The project therefore used intense policy dialogue to analyse existing models of co-design and co-production, drawing lessons on how collaborative governance can improve both sustainable-energy policies and broader public-administration performance. Its implementation relied on comparative analysis, case-study work, deliberative processes and structured engagement between policymakers, experts and civil-society actors. Conceptually, ENLARGE was less about a single digital tool and more about a governance methodology for identifying conditions under which co-production can increase policy quality, efficiency and public value. The expected impact was improved capacity of local administrations to involve stakeholders, stronger evidence on participatory energy governance and better guidance for designing public services that are both effective and legitimate. By focusing on co-design, the project supported administrative innovation in the energy-transition field.

evidence.quote: Local administrations often face complex energy-transition challenges that require public acceptance, technical expertise and coordinated action across stakeholders.

results.title: CITADEL - Empowering Citizens to TrAnsform European PubLic Administrations
results.proposal: CITADEL - Empowering Citizens to TrAnsform European PubLic Administrations. CITADEL focused on helping public administrations understand why citizens do not always use digital public services and how those services can be redesigned to become more inclusive, efficient and citizen-centred. Good public services are central to quality of life, regional competitiveness and entrepreneurship, but digital uptake may be limited by lack of skills, fear of errors, low trust, service complexity or poor alignment with user needs. The project therefore aimed to provide public authorities with tools, recommendations and methods to identify barriers to use and bring citizens back into digital service channels. Its implementation combined ICT-enabled service analysis, citizen engagement, public-sector transformation methods and evidence-based recommendations. CITADEL created an ecosystem of best practices and tools that allowed administrations to use existing knowledge and new data to shape services around what matters to users. Conceptually, it linked service-design insight, administrative data, stakeholder feedback and co-creation approaches to support better digital public services. The expected impact was improved digital-service adoption, more inclusive access, greater administrative responsiveness and better alignment between public services and citizen expectations. By examining not only technology but also trust, skills and usability, CITADEL treated digital transformation as an organisational and social challenge as much as a technical one.
results.memo: Proceed. CITADEL - Empowering Citizens to TrAnsform European PubLic Administrations is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Institute for Computer Science and Control
results.title: ADVANCE - Advanced predictive-analysis-based decision-support engine for logistics
results.proposal: ADVANCE - Advanced predictive-analysis-based decision-support engine for logistics. ADVANCE was designed to help logistics operators make better decisions in transport planning, dispatching and strategic network management. Logistics environments generate large volumes of data on routes, orders, partners, traffic conditions, capacity constraints and delivery performance, yet operational decisions are often made under uncertainty and with incomplete visibility. The project therefore sought to provide a decision-support platform capable of combining the most recent operational information with higher-level intelligence derived from longer-term data analysis. Its implementation used predictive analytics, data mining, machine learning and optimisation techniques, including heuristics, ant colony optimisation and evolutionary algorithms. The platform was intended to analyse massive datasets, including 50 million or more data elements, and to process new information rapidly for real-time or near-real-time decisions. Conceptually, it linked structured logistics data, forecasting models and optimisation routines to support tasks such as local dispatching, deadheading reduction, early detection of missed due dates and partnership planning. The expected impact was improved transport efficiency, more competitive logistics strategies, lower operational waste and better responsiveness to changing conditions. By making the software framework available as open source, the project also aimed to reduce initial investment barriers and encourage smaller logistics actors to exploit predictive decision-support tools.
results.memo: Proceed. ADVANCE - Advanced predictive-analysis-based decision-support engine for logistics is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: DE-ENIGMA (Multi-Modal Human-Robot Interaction for Teaching Social Imagination in Autistic Children)
results.proposal: DE-ENIGMA (Multi-Modal Human-Robot Interaction for Teaching Social Imagination in Autistic Children). DE-ENIGMA focused on the use of robot-based interaction to support social imagination and social communication skills among autistic children. Many children with autism spectrum conditions may find social cues, imaginative interaction and reciprocal communication challenging, while therapists, educators and families need tools that can provide structured, engaging and repeatable support. The project aimed to create and evaluate technology that could help children practise social interaction in a controlled and motivating environment. The implementation used multi-modal human-robot interaction, combining robotic behaviour, sensors, affective computing, speech or gesture processing and adaptive interaction design. At a conceptual level, the robot acted as an interactive teaching partner, recognising child responses and supporting exercises designed to expand social understanding and imaginative engagement. The expected impact was more personalised therapeutic support, increased child engagement, improved consistency of social-skills training and new evidence on the role of robots in autism interventions. By combining robotics with behavioural and educational expertise, DE-ENIGMA sought to support professionals rather than replace them, offering an additional tool for structured learning. Its value lies in creating repeatable, measurable and potentially scalable interaction scenarios for children who may respond positively to predictable robotic partners.
results.memo: Proceed. DE-ENIGMA (Multi-Modal Human-Robot Interaction for Teaching Social Imagination in Autistic Children) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: FLOBOT - Floor Washing Robot for Professional Users
results.proposal: FLOBOT - Floor Washing Robot for Professional Users. FLOBOT addressed the difficulty of cleaning very large indoor surfaces in professional environments such as supermarkets, airports, trade fairs, hospitals and industrial or commercial premises. These facilities often require floor washing every day, and sometimes several times during the day, creating repetitive, physically demanding and time-consuming work for cleaning staff. Existing robotic solutions did not meet the standards expected by professional cleaning-service providers, particularly in relation to performance, safety, reliability and usability in busy environments. The project therefore developed and validated a professional robotic scrubber-dryer capable of washing and drying large floor areas. Its implementation combined robotics, autonomous navigation, floor-cleaning hardware, perception systems, safety controls and user interfaces suitable for professional operators. At a conceptual level, the robot needed to map and move through large premises, avoid obstacles, apply brushes and suction effectively, and operate in spaces shared with people and equipment. The expected impact was reduced manual effort, improved cleaning productivity, more consistent service quality and better scalability for cleaning operations across large buildings. By automating repetitive floor-maintenance tasks, FLOBOT could allow cleaning staff to focus on supervision, detailed tasks and service quality. The project also offered business value to cleaning providers by addressing labour intensity and operational efficiency.

results.title: HoPE - Holistic Personal public Eco-mobility
results.proposal: HoPE - Holistic Personal public Eco-mobility. HoPE was conceived as a user-centred mobility platform intended to encourage more conscious, convenient and sustainable use of public transport and eco-mobility services. Urban and regional travellers often face fragmented information across transport modes, ticketing systems, payment channels and journey-planning tools, which can make sustainable transport less attractive than private car use. The project therefore aimed to bring together mobility information and service functions in a single platform that could support greener travel choices while improving the user experience. The implementation combined info-mobility, trip planning, ticket reservation, fare calculation and mobile payment functions within a digital platform oriented around individual users. Conceptually, it integrated transport data, journey-planning algorithms, payment services, user-interface design and personalised mobility information to help people compare and access transport options more easily. The expected impact was greater awareness of public transport and eco-mobility, smoother journey planning, better access to multimodal services and increased attractiveness of low-emission travel. By combining information, reservation and payment capabilities, HoPE sought to reduce friction in everyday mobility decisions and create value for both users and transport providers. Its broader contribution lies in demonstrating how digital platforms can support behavioural change towards more sustainable transport systems.

Conceptually, it integrated transport data, journey-planning algorithms, payment services, user-interface design and personalised mobility information to help people compare and access transport options more easily.

results.title: eNest solution
results.proposal: eNest solution. Finland’s eNest solution was designed to simplify supplier verification during public procurement by reducing the need for bidders to submit official records manually. In tendering processes, contracting authorities must check that suppliers meet legal and administrative requirements, while companies often need to gather and attach documents that already exist in official databases. This creates duplication, administrative burden and avoidable friction for both public buyers and service providers. eNest aims to make the tendering process more efficient by automatically verifying information submitted by suppliers against official records. The implementation relies on the European Single Procurement Document as a standardised structure for supplier declarations, allowing the system to connect tender information with authoritative public registers. At a conceptual level, the solution combines procurement workflow integration, automated data checks, standardised supplier self-declarations and register-based verification. By replacing repeated document submission with automated confirmation, the system can improve reliability, reduce processing time and make participation easier for companies. The expected impact is lower administrative cost, fewer errors in tender documentation, faster assessment of suppliers and a better user experience for both contracting authorities and bidders. It also supports interoperability in public procurement by aligning national processes with European procurement standards.
results.memo: Proceed. eNest solution is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Predicting youth problems - Identifying youth problems and providing support
results.proposal: Predicting youth problems - Identifying youth problems and providing support. In South Karelia, Eksote developed a predictive welfare model to help social, health and education professionals identify children and young people who might need support before difficulties became more severe. The operational problem was that warning signs are often dispersed across maternity clinics, kindergartens, schools, healthcare, mental healthcare and social services, making it difficult for authorities to intervene early and coordinate support for families. The objective was to detect emerging risks linked to school performance, attendance, behavioural issues, psychiatric care, custody decisions and substance abuse, so that preventive action could be taken sooner. The implementation used a model developed with the Finnish IT firm Avaintec, combining administrative data from several public-service systems and analysing predefined undesirable outcomes. It identified 1,340 risk factors, including examples such as dental problems, missed maternity-clinic appointments by parents and bullying behaviour among siblings. At a conceptual level, the system used cross-sector data integration, pattern detection and risk-factor modelling to follow indicators at individual level. The expected value was earlier identification of children requiring support, better coordination between services and more targeted preventive intervention. However, the use case also raised serious questions about proportionality, data quality, family profiling and whether administrative indicators can reliably capture complex social and educational needs.

results.title: FOLDOUT - Through-foliage detection, including in the outermost regions of the EU
results.proposal: FOLDOUT - Through-foliage detection, including in the outermost regions of the EU. Border surveillance in forested, remote or extreme-climate areas is difficult because people and vehicles can move under dense vegetation where conventional sensors often produce unreliable detections or high false-alarm rates. FOLDOUT was developed as a Horizon 2020 project to improve through-foliage detection in both inner and outermost EU regions, supporting border guards with faster and more reliable situational awareness. The objective was to detect, locate, track and classify people, vehicles and other objects in challenging terrain while reducing operational workload and improving border-management efficiency. The implementation integrates ground, aerial and satellite data with specialised sensors, machine-learning algorithms and multi-sensor fusion. At a conceptual level, the platform combines data from several sensing modalities, applies detection and classification models, and presents near-real-time information to operators. FOLDOUT also developed performance-evaluation approaches to assess how well the system works under different environmental and weather conditions. The expected impact is improved detection in foliated areas, reduced false alarms, better allocation of border-guard resources and enhanced safety in difficult environments. The project produced research outputs on hyperspectral surveillance, sensor fusion and object tracking, and its own platform material describes demonstrations at end-user sites using an intelligent and robust detection system.
results.memo: Proceed. FOLDOUT - Through-foliage detection, including in the outermost regions of the EU is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Use of IoT technologies to gather data from the City of Ferrara
results.proposal: Use of IoT technologies to gather data from the City of Ferrara. Cities that manage tourism, air quality, shared mobility and public-space use need timely information from many urban systems, but these data are often fragmented across departments, platforms and service providers. Ravenna’s smart-city work has explored the use of IoT technologies to monitor sensitive urban indicators, including air quality, tourist flows and mobility-sharing patterns. The operational objective is to help the municipality understand how people move through the city, how tourism affects local areas and where environmental or mobility pressures require intervention. The implementation is based on connected sensors, data collection from urban infrastructure and analytical platforms that support monitoring and planning. At a conceptual level, IoT devices and digital services collect local observations, which can then be integrated into dashboards or planning tools to inform mobility, tourism and environmental policies. This approach is consistent with Ravenna’s wider digital transition trajectory, including the DARE programme and the more recent FOOTPRINTS initiative, which focuses on sustainable tourism, accessibility, mobility, digital facilities and flow management. The expected impact is improved situational awareness, better management of tourist pressure, more evidence-based mobility planning and stronger capacity to reduce the ecological footprint of visitors. Current public information suggests that Ravenna continues to develop smart mobility and sustainable destination tools, although the precise status of the individual IoT pilots described in the original source is not fully specified.
results.memo: Proceed. Use of IoT technologies to gather data from the City of Ferrara is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Georg-August University of Göttingen (UGOE) and Julius Kühn Institute (JKI
results.title: NOcsPS (Agriculture 4.0 without chemical-synthetic crop protection)
results.proposal: NOcsPS (Agriculture 4.0 without chemical-synthetic crop protection). Pressure to reduce chemical-synthetic plant protection products is reshaping agricultural research, because farmers still need systems that protect yields, manage weeds and diseases, and remain economically viable. NOcsPS develops a cultivation model that sits between conventional and organic farming: it avoids chemical-synthetic crop protection while retaining mineral fertilisation and using new cultivation measures, data-driven monitoring and agronomic optimisation. The initiative brings together the University of Hohenheim, the University of Göttingen and the Julius Kühn Institute to test whether more sustainable cropping systems can be designed without seriously impairing yield performance. The implementation combines field trials, crop-rotation design, soil and fertilisation strategies, digital monitoring and Agriculture 4.0 methods. At a conceptual level, data from experimental plots, crop growth, management practices and environmental conditions are used to compare production systems and support decisions on how to control pests, weeds and diseases without conventional pesticides. Initial research indicates that systems without chemical-synthetic plant protection generally achieve lower yields than conventional systems, but considerably higher yields than organic systems, suggesting a potential middle path for sustainable intensification. The expected impact is reduced pesticide dependency, improved evidence for future farming systems, and better support for farmers facing regulatory and environmental pressure. NOcsPS has moved into a second phase, with 18 scientific consortium partners working across cropping systems, sustainability and transformation.
results.memo: Proceed. NOcsPS (Agriculture 4.0 without chemical-synthetic crop protection) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Wearable exoskeleton for stroke patients
results.proposal: Wearable exoskeleton for stroke patients. Stroke and other neurological conditions can leave patients with severe movement limitations, creating a need for intensive, repetitive and adaptive rehabilitation that is difficult to provide continuously through therapist-led sessions alone. In Bremen, DFKI’s Robotics Innovation Center developed Recupera REHA as a mobile whole-body exoskeleton and modular assistance system for robot-supported rehabilitation. The aim was to expand therapy options by helping patients practise gripping, arm movement, standing or walking with robotic support adapted to their impairment. The implementation uses a metal exoskeleton structure with modular actuators, sensor systems and control software. Individual actuator modules can support the body directly or be reconfigured as gripper arms attached to a wheelchair, enabling assistance for different mobility needs. At a conceptual level, the system combines rehabilitation robotics, biosignal analysis, sensor fusion and adaptive “assist-as-needed” control so that support can match the patient’s capability and therapy goals. The expected impact is more intensive rehabilitation, greater patient autonomy, reduced dependence on constant therapist assistance and new possibilities for home or near-home training. The project ran from 2014 to 2017, and later research continued to advance the Recupera-Reha exoskeleton’s modelling and control for actions such as sitting, standing and static walking. (dfki.de
results.memo: Proceed. Wearable exoskeleton for stroke patients is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI for predicting the climate change impact in RES and energy demand at regiona and local level
results.proposal: AI for predicting the climate change impact in RES and energy demand at regiona and local level. Regional energy planners need more precise information on how climate change will affect renewable-resource availability and local energy demand, because high-level climate projections are often too coarse for operational decisions. In Asturias, FAEN led a pilot focused on downscaling climate information to support regional and local energy planning. The problem is that changing weather patterns can alter heating and cooling demand, solar and wind generation potential, and the reliability of renewable-energy planning assumptions. Existing climate models may describe long-term trends, but their spatial resolution is often insufficient for local infrastructure, investment or policy decisions. The implementation uses artificial intelligence to connect broad climate projections with in situ data, producing finer-scale estimates of local climate impacts and their consequences for renewable energy and demand. At a conceptual level, the system combines climate-model outputs, local measurements, energy-demand data and renewable-generation indicators to generate geographically relevant forecasts. The expected impact is better regional energy planning, improved assessment of renewable potential, stronger adaptation strategies and more resilient investment decisions. By translating climate projections into actionable local energy intelligence, the use case supports public authorities and energy agencies in aligning climate adaptation, renewable deployment and demand management. (research.aiodp.eu

results.company: German Research Center for Artificial Intelligence
results.title: Planning and execution for a mobile indoor robot
results.proposal: Planning and execution for a mobile indoor robot. Indoor mobile manipulation requires a robot to act in environments where object positions, task conditions and execution outcomes may not be fully known in advance. This German use case explores how task planning and execution can control a mobile robot performing manipulation tasks in such settings. The practical challenge is that a robot may need to find boxes or other objects placed on tables, move through the environment, decide which actions to perform and adapt when observations differ from the initial model. The implementation combines task-planning methods with execution control on a mobile robotic platform. In the demonstration scenario, the robot starts without knowing where objects are located and must plan, perceive, move, manipulate and update its knowledge as the task progresses. At a conceptual level, symbolic planning represents goals, actions and preconditions, while execution modules dispatch actions to the robot, monitor results and trigger replanning if expected conditions fail. This creates a loop between high-level reasoning and low-level robotic control. The expected impact is more robust service robotics, improved ability to operate in uncertain indoor environments and a clearer path from planning research to physical deployment. The use case is valuable because it demonstrates not only plan generation, but also the operational challenge of making plans executable on real robots. (research.aiodp.eu

evidence.quote: The expected impact is more robust service robotics, improved ability to operate in uncertain indoor environments and a clearer path from planning research to physical deployment.

results.title: Planning for flexible manufacturing with robots
results.proposal: Planning for flexible manufacturing with robots. Heavy-vehicle axle production involves many machining stages, machine constraints, stock dependencies and planning decisions that are difficult to automate when they rely heavily on human expertise. In this Swedish use case, the challenge is to support flexible manufacturing of front axles by transforming expert production knowledge into a form that automated planning and scheduling systems can use. Human planners understand which operations are possible, which machines can perform them, how available stock affects production routes and how orders should be sequenced, but this knowledge is often implicit and hard to scale. The implementation combines planning and scheduling techniques to generate machining plans from three main inputs: expert knowledge extracted from human planners, incoming order requirements and available stock. At a conceptual level, the system formalises production rules, links them to machine capabilities and uses scheduling-based reasoning to identify feasible and efficient machining sequences. This allows planning decisions to be produced more systematically while remaining grounded in operational know-how. The expected impact is faster production planning, better use of machinery, reduced dependence on individual planners and improved ability to respond to changing orders or stock availability. By combining knowledge representation with automated scheduling, the use case demonstrates how industrial planning systems can support flexible, small-batch or variable manufacturing without requiring a complete redesign of production infrastructure. results.title: Scaviho: scalable vegetation index and harvesting forecaster
results.proposal: Scaviho: scalable vegetation index and harvesting forecaster. Precision agriculture already uses NDVI widely to monitor crop condition, but intermediate NDVI values during the growth stage can be difficult for farmers to interpret despite containing important information on crop development. In Spain, Scaviho was developed to make vegetation-index information more actionable for vineyards and other agricultural contexts, helping users assess growth evolution, anticipate hidden problems and forecast harvesting dates. The operational problem is not the absence of satellite data, but the difficulty of translating seasonal vegetation signals into practical decisions for field management and harvest planning. The implementation uses historical Sentinel-2 NDVI data, crop phenological information and artificial-intelligence methods to broaden the interpretation of intermediate vegetation-index values. At a conceptual level, the solution builds a scale that links NDVI patterns to crop-growth stages and uses past satellite observations to identify deviations or signals relevant to expected harvest timing. The project involves ENCORE LAB and Castillo de Maetierra, combining digital-agriculture capabilities with vineyard operational experience. The expected impact is better crop monitoring, earlier detection of hidden stress, improved harvest planning and more precise use of remote-sensing information in everyday farm decisions. AI4Copernicus and the AI-on-demand platform describe Scaviho as an Open Call success story whose results have been developed in a consortium already using satellite images in daily agricultural operations.
results.memo: Proceed. Scaviho: scalable vegetation index and harvesting forecaster is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Automatic Ship Classification from Optical Aerial Images with Convolutional Neural Networks
results.proposal: Automatic Ship Classification from Optical Aerial Images with Convolutional Neural Networks. Maritime surveillance, coastal monitoring and aerial reconnaissance generate large volumes of visible-spectrum imagery in which ships or small unidentified floating objects may be difficult to identify quickly and consistently. Traditional approaches to ship detection have often relied on manually designed image-processing features, followed by conventional supervised classifiers, which can be sensitive to changing image conditions and may not capture complex visual patterns. Researchers at the University of Alicante addressed this challenge by developing a method to determine whether an optical aerial image contains a ship. The implementation used a convolutional neural network architecture adapted to visible-spectrum aerial imagery. At a conceptual level, the model extracted neural visual codes from images and combined them with a k-nearest neighbour method to improve classification performance. This approach moved feature extraction away from manually engineered descriptors and towards representations learned from image data. The expected impact is faster and more accurate screening of aerial image collections, reduced manual inspection effort and stronger support for maritime monitoring applications such as traffic surveillance, search and rescue, environmental control or security tasks. The work is research-oriented, but it demonstrates how deep-learning methods can improve remote-sensing image interpretation when the operational question is binary and clearly framed: whether a ship is present or absent in the observed scene.
results.memo: Proceed. Automatic Ship Classification from Optical Aerial Images with Convolutional Neural Networks is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Predictive justice - a database to provide predictable guidelines and timing in particular areas
results.proposal: Predictive justice - a database to provide predictable guidelines and timing in particular areas. Judicial users, lawyers and citizens often need to understand how similar cases have been decided and how long proceedings may take, especially in areas where case-law orientation can affect litigation strategy and settlement decisions. In Brescia, the Court of Appeal developed a predictive justice initiative to organise selected decisions from the Brescia Court of Appeal and Ordinary Court into a navigable database. The objective was to provide predictable guidelines, relevant precedents and procedural orientation in particular legal areas, while supporting legal professionals rather than automating judicial decisions. The implementation uses a structured jurisprudence database supported by natural language processing and rule-based or expert-system logic. At a conceptual level, users choose a legal area and follow a guided path that progressively identifies the judicial situation most similar to their own issue, using essential linguistic and graphical presentation to make the case-law material easier to consult. The platform focuses on legal similarity, orientation and knowledge access rather than on generating binding outcomes. The expected impact is improved transparency of local case-law, faster retrieval of relevant decisions, better preparation by lawyers and parties, and greater consistency in understanding judicial tendencies. Current online material shows that the Brescia predictive justice platform remains publicly accessible and presents selected decisions grouped by thematic areas, notably labour and business law.
