results.title: Evaluate the potential of facial matching technologies as an aid to the intelligence gathering process
results.proposal: Evaluate the potential of facial matching technologies as an aid to the intelligence gathering process. Law-enforcement and justice authorities face recurring challenges in identifying persons of interest, comparing image material and supporting intelligence processes, but facial-matching technologies raise significant questions about accuracy, proportionality, bias and fundamental rights. In Ireland, the Department of Justice and Equality developed a 2019 project to evaluate whether facial matching could assist intelligence gathering as part of a broader European mapping of innovative technologies in justice. The objective was exploratory: to assess potential use rather than to present a fully deployed policing system. The implementation concerned facial-matching technologies, which compare facial images to identify possible similarities or candidate matches. At a conceptual level, such a tool would require image inputs, biometric feature extraction, similarity scoring, human review and governance controls to ensure that any result remains investigative support rather than automatic identification or evidentiary determination. The expected value would be faster screening of image material, better support for intelligence workflows and improved prioritisation where large visual datasets are involved. However, the use case also sits in a high-risk area, because biometric matching in justice and policing contexts requires a clear legal basis, strict necessity and proportionality assessment, data-protection safeguards and transparency. The European Commission study records the Irish project as an evaluation initiative, and I found no evidence that it progressed to full operational deployment.

results.title: Future criminal court rooms
results.proposal: Future criminal court rooms. Criminal proceedings increasingly rely on digital evidence, remote participation, audio-visual material and complex case records, while many courtrooms remain organised around paper-based or manually documented hearings. In North Rhine-Westphalia, the Central Cybercrime Department developed a pilot project aimed at modernising criminal courtrooms through technologies that could reduce the time and effort required to record, review and present proceedings. The objective was to create a courtroom environment in which hearings could be videotaped, speech could be converted into written transcripts, and participants could access both the transcription and embedded audio material. The implementation concept combined audio recording, video recording, speech-to-text recognition and digital document production inside the courtroom workflow. A further element under consideration was the 3D projection of crime scenes, which could support the presentation of spatially complex evidence in cybercrime or other criminal cases. The expected impact was reduced administrative effort, faster review of hearings, more accurate documentation and broader modernisation of criminal justice infrastructure. results.title: Application of AI for early recognition of criminal offences that relate to hate crime
results.proposal: Application of AI for early recognition of criminal offences that relate to hate crime. Online hate crime creates a difficult enforcement problem because potentially criminal content circulates at high volume, changes quickly and may be embedded in ambiguous linguistic, social or political contexts. In Germany, the Federal Criminal Police Office participated in a research project examining how police organisations could use automated support to detect, prevent and prosecute hate crime while respecting legal, ethical and organisational constraints. The objective was not only to classify online statements, but to define the conditions under which such tools could be responsibly adopted by law-enforcement bodies. The implementation investigated technical approaches for classifying hate speech according to criminal-law categories, hate-speech phenomena and thematic content. At a conceptual level, the project combined natural language processing, supervised classification, domain-specific annotation, organisational analysis and legal-ethical assessment. This holistic design was intended to ensure that any prototype would be evaluated not only for technical accuracy, but also for its suitability within police workflows and fundamental-rights safeguards. The expected impact was faster identification of potentially criminal hate messages, better prioritisation of police review, and stronger evidence on how automated tools can support, rather than replace, human legal judgement. FRA records the output as reports and a technical prototype to be evaluated by police, while later project reporting indicates that a tool recognising criminal hate messages from social media posts was developed through KISTRA.

results.title: Land register analysis component in the project Development of a federal database land register
results.proposal: Land register analysis component in the project Development of a federal database land register. Digitising land-register information requires converting legally important legacy documents into structured, accurate and reusable data without weakening the certainty attached to property records. In Germany, this project component focused on automating the analysis of existing PDF files containing land-register information so that their contents could be fragmented, interpreted and assigned to appropriate database fields. The operational problem is that land-register material may exist in document formats that are difficult to search, integrate or process electronically, creating manual workload for justice administrations and limiting interoperability between systems. The objective was to support the development of a federal land-register database by transforming unstructured or semi-structured documents into structured records. The implementation is based on expert systems and rule-based techniques, reflecting the formalised structure of land-register documents and the need for deterministic interpretation rather than open-ended prediction. At a conceptual level, the tool analyses document content and layout, separates relevant sections, recognises values according to predefined rules and maps them into corresponding database fields. The expected impact is reduced manual transcription, improved consistency of digitised records, faster migration of legacy information and stronger support for electronic workflows involving courts, land-registry authorities, notaries and other authorised users. The case demonstrates that rule-based automation remains valuable where legal formats are stable and accuracy requirements are high.

results.title: DataJust
results.proposal: DataJust. Compensation for bodily injury is a legally sensitive field because victims, parties, lawyers and judges need reliable information on comparable cases while preserving the independence and discretion of judicial decision-making. In France, the Ministry of Justice launched DataJust to explore whether past civil and administrative liability decisions could support a more consistent understanding of compensation levels. The project aimed to carry out retrospective and prospective evaluations of public policies, develop an indicative framework for bodily-injury compensation, inform parties during amicable settlement discussions and provide documentation for judges ruling on damages claims. The implementation was authorised by Decree No. 2020-356 of 27 March 2020, following CNIL review, and involved automated processing of personal data from relevant judicial decisions. At a conceptual level, the system was intended to extract compensation-related information, structure legal and factual variables, conduct statistical analysis and generate decision-support or information outputs. The expected value was greater transparency for parties, better-informed settlement negotiations and more documented policy evaluation in civil liability. However, the initiative raised concerns because it involved sensitive personal and judicial data and could influence perceptions of standardisation in damages assessment. The project ultimately did not reach operational deployment, showing the difficulty of applying algorithmic tools in domains where individual harm, legal nuance and institutional legitimacy are closely intertwined.

results.title: Automatic anonymisation and content description of documents containing personal data
results.proposal: Automatic anonymisation and content description of documents containing personal data. Judicial and administrative documents contain information that is valuable for transparency, research and decision-making, but wider electronic availability is constrained by the need to protect personal data. In Finland, the Ministry of Justice led the Anoppi project to address this challenge for court decisions and other official decisions issued by public authorities. Manual anonymisation can be slow, costly and inconsistent, particularly when large collections of documents must be prepared for publication, research use or legal-information services. The objective was therefore to provide tools that help authorities make documents more accessible while preserving privacy and legal safeguards. The implementation uses language-technology and semantic-computing methods to support two functions: automatic or semi-automatic anonymisation and pseudonymisation of personal data, and content description or annotation of legal documents. At a conceptual level, the system applies natural language processing, named-entity recognition, semantic annotation and document-structuring techniques to identify sensitive elements and generate metadata that improves searchability and reuse. The expected impact is faster document processing, broader access to legal information, improved support for research and more efficient publication workflows. By reducing the burden on courts and authorities, Anoppi strengthens digital justice services while maintaining data-protection requirements. It also supports the wider development of open, anonymised legal data for intelligent legal applications and the Semantic Finlex environment.

results.title: Tackling urban heat through data, paying attention to our citizens' perception
results.proposal: Tackling urban heat through data, paying attention to our citizens' perception. Rising urban temperatures require local authorities to understand not only where heat is physically concentrated, but also how inhabitants experience discomfort, exposure and relief in everyday public spaces. Bordeaux Métropole developed this initiative to support climate-adaptation policies with indicators that combine environmental measurement and citizens’ perceived thermal comfort. Technical services need evidence on the conditions under which trees, fountains, urban design or surface materials reduce heat-island effects, while elected officials and planners also need to know whether residents actually feel improvements in liveability. The project began with a data-collection phase across eight cities in the metropolitan area, installing sensors in places with varied topographical and urban characteristics, including public squares, alleys, dense districts and wooded areas. The implementation combines environmental sensing, spatial analysis and typologies of urban spaces to compare temperature differences and evaluate the effects of local interventions. It also incorporates subjective perceptions, recognising that physical measurements alone cannot capture vulnerability, behavioural adaptation or citizen satisfaction. The expected impact is better targeted climate-adaptation planning, stronger evidence on which measures work, and greater legitimacy for public investment in cooling strategies. By connecting measurable heat conditions with lived experience, the initiative helps Bordeaux Métropole design responses that are both technically informed and socially meaningful, with possible replication across the wider metropolitan territory.

results.title: Municipality of Palaio Faliro: Development of IOT Platform - Energy Upgrade
results.proposal: Municipality of Palaio Faliro: Development of IOT Platform - Energy Upgrade. Municipalities increasingly need continuous visibility over how buildings, facilities and urban assets consume energy and other resources, rather than relying on fragmented readings or periodic manual checks. In Palaio Faliro, the administration developed a centralised IoT management platform to monitor, control, record and analyse consumption data across municipal infrastructure. The local context includes a diverse estate of municipal buildings, schools, social facilities, sports facilities and street lighting, with further potential sources of data across urban services. The objective is to give the municipality a single operational layer for understanding its energy footprint and progressively improving the performance of public assets. The implementation uses the SenseOne IoT platform, connecting sensors, meters and infrastructure data sources so that information can be collected, processed and displayed through dashboards. At a conceptual level, the platform can extend beyond electricity monitoring to environmental indicators, waste bins, parking spaces, gas meters, smart water meters, tanks, wells and electric-vehicle chargers. This makes the system a scalable smart-city architecture rather than a narrow energy-accounting tool. The expected impact is improved decision-making, lower consumption, earlier detection of anomalies and better prioritisation of energy-efficiency interventions. By consolidating operational data, Palaio Faliro can shift from reactive infrastructure management to continuous, evidence-based monitoring of its municipal footprint.

results.company: Rheinische Friedrich-Wilhelms-Universität Bonn, Faculty of Agriculture, Institute for Agricultural Engineering
results.title: WeedAI – promoting non-chemical weed control in sugar beet cultivation
results.proposal: WeedAI – promoting non-chemical weed control in sugar beet cultivation. WeedAI responds to the growing need for reliable evaluation of non-chemical weed-control technologies, especially in sugar beet cultivation. Mechanical and robotic weeding methods are increasingly important as agriculture seeks to reduce herbicide use, but assessing their effectiveness usually requires extensive field trials and labour-intensive manual ground-truthing. This slows innovation and makes it harder to compare tools, field conditions and weed-management strategies. The project therefore develops automated methods to assess how well weeding operations remove weeds while preserving crops. Its implementation is based on deep-learning methods for plant recognition, using image data to detect and distinguish sugar beet plants and weeds, estimate their position and size, and evaluate treatment outcomes. Conceptually, WeedAI links field imagery, crop-weed segmentation, object recognition and performance assessment into a system that can quantify both crop and weed responses after intervention. The expected impact is faster evaluation of weeding systems, lower trial costs, better evidence for non-chemical crop protection and more rapid development of sustainable weed-control technologies. Project outputs indicate that the system can make precise predictions on individual sugar beet and weed positions, even in fields unknown to the model, provided that high-quality drone and camera data are available.

results.proposal: RoLand - how to achieve low-cost automation in agriculture. RoLand develops a low-cost robotic harvesting system for fruit production, with particular attention to open-field strawberry harvesting. Fruit farms face labour shortages, rising production costs and time-sensitive harvesting windows, while robotic harvesting solutions have historically been concentrated in greenhouse environments or designed at cost levels unsuitable for smaller farms. The project therefore aims to create a semi-autonomous mobile system that can harvest fruit independently under real outdoor conditions, including changing weather, uneven terrain and variable crop presentation. Its implementation combines a mobile robotic platform, fruit-recognition systems, an end-effector for harvesting, autonomous navigation and perception technologies. DFKI’s SHIVAA robot, developed in the project, is designed to identify ripe fruit and pick it in open fields, with the possibility of scaling work output through multiple compact units. Conceptually, the system integrates visual detection, motion planning, manipulation and field mobility in a platform intended to remain economically viable for smaller producers. The expected impact is reduced dependence on seasonal labour, improved supply security, more flexible harvesting by time of day and stronger competitiveness for regional fruit production. Public demonstrations indicate that RoLand has moved from design towards field-tested prototype capability, including public strawberry-field testing.

results.title: Movi-Q – optimize visual quality controls intelligently
results.proposal: Movi-Q – optimize visual quality controls intelligently. Movi-Q addresses a persistent quality-control problem in the food industry: fruit, vegetables, meat and other natural products vary widely in appearance, while defects are often detected manually by visual inspection. This makes sorting resource-intensive, inconsistent and prone to human error, and it can contribute to unnecessary rejection of usable products or failure to remove defective material. The project, led through the DIL German Institute of Food Technologies in Quakenbrück, aimed to develop a mobile and modular prototype for visual quality detection that could be used by companies in different food-processing contexts. Its implementation combines image acquisition hardware, machine-vision methods, artificial intelligence and software modules able to identify defects and trigger downstream processes such as sorting. A key component is the creation of high-quality training data through a mobile image-capture unit that can be adapted to different products and application scenarios. Conceptually, Movi-Q links visual sensing, defect classification, process integration and practical guidelines for food companies. The expected impact is more reliable quality assurance, lower reject rates, reduced manual sorting effort and better resource efficiency. By demonstrating transferable application scenarios, the project helps food businesses assess where automated visual inspection can improve productivity, quality standards and sustainability.

results.company: Justus Liebig University Giessen, Institute for Animal Breeding and Domestic Animal Genetics
results.title: mAInZaun – the intelligent fence that recognizes animal species
results.proposal: mAInZaun – the intelligent fence that recognizes animal species. mAInZaun was created to improve herd protection in areas where grazing animals are exposed to predators, especially wolves. Livestock owners need effective protection, but conventional electric fences and deterrent systems may lose effectiveness when predators become habituated, and remote grazing sites often lack permanent infrastructure. The project therefore developed a modular, autonomous and intelligent protective fence able to recognise approaching animals and trigger appropriate deterrence measures. Its implementation combines sensors, local power supply, animal-species recognition and dynamic deterrent responses, including stimuli such as ultrasonic signals. The system is designed not only for integration into existing fences, but also for independent deployment in temporary safety zones, for example near roads, settlements, railways, hiking trails, tourist areas or landscape-conservation projects. Conceptually, mAInZaun links edge sensing, classification of approaching animals, automated alerting and context-specific deterrence. It can also integrate police, road-maintenance departments or railway authorities into the alert system where relevant. The expected impact is stronger protection of grazing animals, reduced economic losses for farmers, improved coexistence between livestock farming and wildlife conservation, and more flexible management of temporary risk areas. By reacting dynamically rather than relying on static barriers, the system seeks to maintain deterrent effectiveness over time.

results.title: KRIBL - affordable robotics also for small businesses
results.proposal: KRIBL - affordable robotics also for small businesses. KRIBL focuses on making agricultural robotics accessible to smaller farms, which may otherwise be excluded from advanced automation because current systems are often large, specialised and expensive. Organic and biological farming businesses need practical tools for monitoring, plant care and field operations, but the economics of highly automated machines tend to favour very large agricultural enterprises. The project therefore aims to develop compact, affordable and flexible robot systems that can be used in everyday agricultural settings without requiring excessive investment. Its implementation combines small mobile robots, sensor technology, field robotics, modular software and intelligent data processing to support precision tasks in biological agriculture. Conceptually, KRIBL explores how lightweight robotic platforms can perceive their environment, support crop and weed-related operations, and operate as part of a broader digital farming workflow. Recent project material also links KRIBL to containerised AI deployment and reproducible weed-detection workflows on mobile agricultural robots, showing how software modularity can improve maintainability and transferability. The expected impact is broader access to automation, reduced labour intensity, more precise field operations and improved competitiveness for smaller farms. By lowering the economic and technical threshold for robotics, KRIBL contributes to a more inclusive model of agricultural innovation rather than concentrating advanced technology only in large-scale operations.

results.title: AI-Breeding – find the highest yielding strains quickly and accurately
results.proposal: AI-Breeding – find the highest yielding strains quickly and accurately. AI-Breeding addresses the need to accelerate plant breeding by identifying high-performing lines and hybrids more quickly, accurately and resource-efficiently. Breeders working on important crops must combine yield potential, environmental adaptation and genetic diversity, but conventional selection can require long cycles of field testing and complex interpretation of genome, phenotype and environmental information. The project brings together practical plant breeding, breeding theory, quantitative genetics, genome analysis and advanced prediction methods to improve selection success across different breeding stages. Its implementation develops and applies machine-learning methods for pattern recognition in highly complex genome, phenome and environmental datasets. These methods are used to predict performance-related and environment-dependent genetic structures in breeding populations, extracting data attributes that can support better decisions on combination ability, line selection and hybrid performance. Conceptually, the approach links genomic markers, phenotypic observations, environmental conditions and predictive modelling to support “big data”-based breeding. The expected impact is faster breeding progress, improved yield security and better use of large-scale biological datasets in practical breeding programmes. Rather than relying only on traditional trial-and-error selection, the project aims to make breeding decisions more evidence-driven and scalable, helping to develop crop varieties that remain productive under changing environmental conditions.

results.title: KIdetect - Reliable detection of weed growth centers
results.proposal: KIdetect - Reliable detection of weed growth centers. KIdetect tackles a practical limitation in mechanical weed control: as weed infestation becomes denser, it becomes harder for camera-guided hoeing systems to identify where tools should act precisely. Farmers and agricultural-technology providers need methods that can target weeds selectively without damaging crops and without relying excessively on herbicides. The project therefore aims to detect weeds reliably and in real time, with particular attention to the spatial location of their growth centres, which may be hidden by leaves or neighbouring plants. The implementation uses image processing supported by artificial intelligence together with multispectral camera systems in the visible and short-wave infrared ranges. It also creates 3D reconstructions of weed areas so that growth centres can be located even under heavy infestation. Testing takes place in a controlled vertical-farming stand, where weed image data can be generated under adjustable lighting, wavelength and camera conditions before being processed with specialised methods. The expected impact is more accurate activation of hoeing devices, improved selective weed removal, lower chemical input and more reliable smart-farming equipment. By linking multispectral sensing, 3D reconstruction and real-time interpretation, KIdetect strengthens precision agriculture’s ability to manage weeds sustainably.

By enabling continuous and objective monitoring without attaching devices to animals, KAMI offers a more scalable route to precision livestock management and more informed herd-care decisions.

results.title: HEB KI– Artificial intelligence searches to improve barley variety
results.proposal: HEB KI– Artificial intelligence searches to improve barley variety. HEB KI focuses on improving plant-breeding decisions by increasing genetic diversity in barley while reducing the resources required to identify promising crosses. Barley breeders need to introduce useful traits from wild or diverse accessions, but selecting which genetic material should be crossed and tested can be expensive, slow and uncertain. The project therefore aims to expand the HEB-25 barley population towards HEX-35 by selecting suitable accessions from a wild barley population in a more targeted way. The implementation further develops and adapts the XSeedScore algorithm for barley, combining genome and phenome datasets to prioritise breeding material with the highest expected value. Conceptually, the system links genetic information, observed plant traits and predictive scoring so that breeders can focus field trials and controlled experiments on the most promising candidates. This enables a more systematic approach to introducing novel alleles into barley breeding. The expected impact is faster and more resource-efficient variety development, improved breeding diversity and better selection of lines with agronomically useful traits. By reducing trial-and-error, HEB KI can help breeders use limited experimental capacity more effectively while strengthening the resilience and adaptability of future barley varieties.

results.title: SKRINJA 2.0 - Business Intelligence in the civil service (BI)
results.proposal: SKRINJA 2.0 - Business Intelligence in the civil service (BI). SKRINJA 2.0 provides Slovenia’s public administration with a horizontal data warehouse and business-intelligence service hosted on the Government Computer Cloud. The administrative problem is that ministries and public bodies often need better access to structured data, analytical tools and shared reporting capabilities to support evidence-based decisions, but such functions can be fragmented across institutions. The main stakeholders include the Ministry of Public Administration, its ICT department, government bodies, civil servants, procurement officials and policy managers using data for planning or oversight. The system was implemented as a cross-government service to promote data-driven decision-making in the civil service. Its implementation combines data warehousing, business-intelligence tools, cloud infrastructure and horizontal service configuration, enabling different parts of the administration to store, process, analyse and visualise data. Since the Ministry of Public Administration also handles national procurement activities, the system may also be used to support procurement procedures in the future. Conceptually, SKRINJA 2.0 provides common analytical infrastructure rather than a single sector-specific application, allowing public institutions to reuse data capabilities across policy areas. The expected impact is improved analytical capacity, more consistent reporting, reduced duplication of BI infrastructure and stronger support for strategic management in government. By centralising business-intelligence functions in the public cloud, the solution can enhance efficiency and create a foundation for broader data-driven governance.
results.memo: Proceed. SKRINJA 2.0 - Business Intelligence in the civil service (BI) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Lombardia Chatbot Coronavirus
results.proposal: Lombardia Chatbot Coronavirus. The Lombardia Coronavirus Chatbot was developed during the COVID-19 emergency to respond to the urgent need for clear, accessible, and structured public information on symptoms and appropriate behavioural measures. The operational problem was the rapid increase in citizen enquiries during a public health crisis, which placed pressure on regional information channels, healthcare services, and emergency communication systems. The stakeholders included residents of Lombardy, the regional administration, ARIA SpA as the Regional Company for Innovation and Purchasing, healthcare authorities, and public health bodies responsible for issuing guidance. The objective was to provide a guided self-orientation tool that helped users understand which actions to take based on their selected symptoms and official recommendations. The implementation consisted of an automated information chatbot that led users through predefined interaction paths, using symptom selection, rule-based decision flows, natural language interaction elements, and curated guidance from the Ministry of Health and relevant international organisations. The service was made available through a digital channel and integrated conceptually with regional communication infrastructure and authoritative public health content. The impact was immediate and visible, as the tool generated very high access numbers shortly after launch. Its main value was the ability to scale public communication rapidly, reduce repetitive enquiries to human operators, improve consistency of advice, and support citizens in navigating uncertainty during the emergency. The chatbot also strengthened the user experience by offering a simple, guided route to trusted information.

results.title: MIREL - Mining and reasoning with legal text
results.proposal: MIREL - Mining and reasoning with legal text. MIREL was established to advance the mining and formal reasoning of legal texts by creating an international and inter-sectoral network across law, artificial intelligence and computational modelling. The central problem is that legal materials are complex, interpretative and difficult to translate into structured representations that can support querying, compliance checking and decision support. Researchers, legal experts, SMEs, industrial partners and academic institutions are therefore brought together to address both conceptual and computational barriers. The project develops a formal framework and tools for transforming legal texts into representations that machines can process, compare and reason over. Its implementation connects natural language processing, legal ontologies, computational argumentation, formal logic and reasoning methods. It also considers the role of legal interpretation, the handling of large legal datasets and the complexity of regulatory compliance. A distinctive feature is its effort to bridge communities that often work separately: those developing legal ontologies and NLP parsers, and those focused on formal reasoning and logic. Through mobility and staff exchange between SMEs and academia, MIREL aims to build an interdisciplinary and inter-continental knowledge base. Its expected impact is stronger legal technology research, improved foundations for compliance tools and future market-oriented services in legal reasoning.
results.memo: Proceed. MIREL - Mining and reasoning with legal text is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: iBorderCtrl: Virtual Policeman
results.proposal: iBorderCtrl: Virtual Policeman. iBorderCtrl, the Intelligent Portable Control System, was designed to address the operational challenge of conducting thorough yet faster border checks for third-country nationals crossing the land borders of EU Member States. Border authorities must balance security, legal compliance, traveller facilitation, and resource efficiency, particularly at road crossings, pedestrian routes, and train stations where flows can be complex and time-sensitive. The stakeholders include border guards, national authorities, EU-level border management actors, travellers, technology suppliers, and backend system operators. The objective was to create a comprehensive and mobile two-stage procedure capable of reducing the time and cost associated with checks while maintaining the depth of control required under Schengen border management. The implementation combined portable readers and scanners, automatic control subsystems, wireless networking, secure backend storage, and processing infrastructure. At a conceptual level, the system brought together hardware for document and biometric capture, software modules for verification and risk-related processing, mobile connectivity for field operations, and centralised data services for secure storage and decision support. The intended impact was to make border control more scalable, consistent, and efficient, particularly in land-border environments where fixed infrastructure may be limited. Expected results included reduced processing time per traveller, lower operational costs, improved mobility for border teams, and more reliable information flows between frontline officers and backend systems. The use case also illustrates the importance of safeguards, transparency, and proportionality in sensitive border-management technologies.

results.company: ISS- ITALY Istituto Superiore di Sanità
results.title: EU-JAV European Joint Action on Vaccination
results.proposal: EU-JAV European Joint Action on Vaccination. The EU-JAV vaccine conversation monitoring platform was developed to help public health actors understand how vaccination-related narratives circulate online across different countries and languages. The policy problem is that vaccine debates unfold rapidly through social media and web platforms, making it difficult for health authorities to detect emerging concerns, influential actors and misinformation dynamics in real time. Stakeholders include the Istituto Superiore di Sanità, EU-JAV partners, public health authorities, researchers, online communities and citizens exposed to vaccine information. In its initial phase, the platform operated in Italian, French and Spanish and was accessible via credentials. It monitored information flows from Twitter, Reddit, Wikipedia and Google Trends through a three-layer architecture: a Data layer, an Analysis layer and a Visualisation layer. The Data layer collected and cleaned raw information through platform APIs and keyword filters validated using recurrence and relevance criteria. The Analysis layer generated graphs, geolocated tweets and applied machine-learning processes for influencer analysis and early-signal detection, including the identification of active or influential users and emerging vaccine-related hashtags. The Visualisation layer presented results in an accessible way. The expected impact is stronger real-time monitoring of vaccine conversations, earlier detection of changing narratives, and better evidence for public communication strategies. By structuring online data into interpretable outputs, the platform supports more responsive vaccination policy and communication.

results.title: Respondus:  assessment software for remote management of students (university)
results.proposal: Respondus:  assessment software for remote management of students (university). Respondus is a remote proctoring solution used by several Italian universities to supervise online examinations and identify behaviour considered unusual or suspicious during tests. The educational challenge is to preserve exam integrity when assessments are conducted remotely, where universities cannot rely on traditional in-person invigilation. Stakeholders include universities, students, teaching staff, examination offices, technology providers and data-protection authorities or officers responsible for oversight. The software monitors the student’s device and collects visual data during the examination process. Its implementation includes video recording, facial image capture, periodic snapshots and algorithmic flagging of moments that may indicate abnormal conduct. These signals are intended to support decisions on whether a student may have copied, used unauthorised materials or violated examination rules. Conceptually, the system combines device monitoring, identity verification, behavioural analysis, video analytics and automated risk flagging, with human review normally needed to interpret the results. The expected benefits for universities are more scalable remote assessment, reduced need for live invigilators and stronger deterrence against fraud. However, the impact is contested because proctoring systems can affect privacy, create stress for students, and generate false or ambiguous alerts. The use of such tools therefore requires clear rules, proportionality, transparency, human oversight and accessible procedures for students to challenge contested findings.

results.title: Shareart: measure the public's satisfaction in front of the works of art exhibited in museum
results.proposal: Shareart: measure the public's satisfaction in front of the works of art exhibited in museum. ShareArt explores how museums can better understand visitors’ engagement with artworks by analysing behaviour during observation. The cultural-management problem is that museums often rely on indirect indicators, surveys or attendance numbers to assess how the public experiences exhibitions, whereas curators and administrators may need more granular evidence on attention, satisfaction and interaction with specific works. Stakeholders include ENEA’s Sustainability Department of Production and Territorial Systems, the Bologna Museums Institution, museum managers, visitors, curators and cultural-policy actors. The system uses a camera positioned near artworks to detect faces looking towards the piece and collect information about observation behaviour. Its implementation draws on big-data techniques and convolutional neural networks to correlate data on the use and enjoyment of artworks with characteristics inferred from visitors and their behaviour. Conceptually, the tool combines computer vision, behavioural analytics, image processing and data aggregation to infer patterns of public engagement. The expected impact is a more evidence-based understanding of museum experience, helping institutions assess which works attract attention, how visitors interact with exhibitions and how displays might be improved. It may support curatorial planning, audience development and cultural-service evaluation. At the same time, the use of cameras and inferred personal characteristics in a museum setting requires careful attention to transparency, proportionality, anonymisation and visitor privacy.

results.title: Seamless Flow: facial recognition of airport passengers
results.proposal: Seamless Flow: facial recognition of airport passengers. Seamless Flow supports automated passenger processing in airports by using biometric identification to manage travellers’ digital identities and reduce repeated document checks. The operational issue is that airports must process large passenger flows while maintaining security, identity verification and efficient movement through controlled areas. Passengers, airport operators, border or security authorities, airlines and the technology provider Vision-Box are the central stakeholders. The solution is used in several airports, including Fiumicino, Malpensa and Linate, and aims to allow passengers to move through airport procedures without repeatedly presenting passports and tickets. The implementation uses IoT-enabled access gates equipped with cameras and facial recognition software. These devices capture the passenger’s face and associate it with passport and ticket data, creating a temporary digital identity that is maintained for the duration of the passenger’s stay at the airport. Conceptually, the system combines biometric enrolment, document-data verification, facial matching, passenger-flow management and integration with airport access-control infrastructure. The expected impact is smoother passenger circulation, shorter queues, reduced manual document checks and more consistent identity verification across airport touchpoints. For airport operators, it can improve throughput and service quality, while supporting security objectives. However, because the system relies on biometric data, its use requires strict safeguards on consent, retention, accuracy, access control and proportionality.

results.title: Trentino Salute 4.0: TREC+
results.proposal: Trentino Salute 4.0: TREC+. TreC+ brings together the digital health trials carried out in Trentino with citizens and health professionals, turning them into a single operational ecosystem for online health services. The service challenge is to guarantee citizens continuous, safe and integrated access to healthcare functions through one platform and one app, while maintaining the quality and reliability of care. The main stakeholders include the Autonomous Province of Trento, APSS, citizens, doctors, health professionals and the FBK research centre. The platform is designed around a constant exchange of data produced by patients and clinicians, with health information remaining under public control in APSS archives. Its implementation is based on open-source technologies and an open architectural model that allows proprietary tools and external solutions to be connected without moving health data away from the public system. The more advanced components, developed and experimented with FBK, explore virtual coaches, predictive models, chatbots and other intelligent applications. TreC+ can also integrate with existing healthcare-management systems, including booking services, electronic health records, payment systems and telemonitoring tools. The expected impact is broader access to digital health services, improved continuity of care, stronger data protection, and greater reusability in other regional, provincial, local health authority or hospital contexts. By combining public governance with modular integration, the ecosystem supports scalable digital healthcare while keeping citizens’ data central, protected and available.

results.title: YUCCA-Smart Data Platform
results.proposal: YUCCA-Smart Data Platform. YUCCA Smart Data Platform offers Regione Piemonte and other public or private entities an open, pre-competitive cloud environment for experimenting with data-driven solutions. The policy and operational problem is that organisations often hold or generate valuable data from sensors, social sources, public datasets and private systems, but lack a shared infrastructure for aggregation, selective sharing, real-time processing and advanced analysis. Stakeholders include Regione Piemonte, public administrations, private organisations, developers, data users, IoT operators and citizens who may benefit from new digital services. The platform aggregates information from the Internet of Things, including cameras, sensors and weather stations, from the Internet of People, such as tweets, and from public and private datasets. It supports selective data sharing, self-service real-time processing, advanced analytics and access to data and metadata through APIs. Conceptually, YUCCA functions as a data platform that enables ingestion, governance, processing, analysis, visualisation and reuse of heterogeneous information. The expected impact is the creation of value-added services across multiple policy areas, easier experimentation with innovative technologies, and better interoperability between data producers and service developers. By providing end-to-end capabilities, the platform can reduce barriers to data innovation, support evidence-based decision-making and help public and private actors develop scalable solutions using shared digital infrastructure.
results.memo: Proceed. YUCCA-Smart Data Platform is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: LombardiaInforma: proactive Citizen Communication
results.proposal: LombardiaInforma: proactive Citizen Communication. LombardiaInforma supports Regione Lombardia in managing personalised communications to citizens through a multi-channel and multi-service approach. The organisational need is to help editorial and communication teams disseminate information more effectively, while ensuring that citizens receive relevant content according to their interests and contact preferences. The stakeholders include Regione Lombardia, citizens, editorial staff, communication offices, service managers and data-protection functions responsible for GDPR-compliant profiling. The implementation is based on an omnichannel customer-experience architecture and a public portal, Lombardia Informa, which centralises citizens’ contact data and declared topics of interest. The platform enables the creation and management of personalised communication campaigns across different channels, harmonising data from heterogeneous systems and supporting a coherent browsing experience. It also allows the development of integrated communication tools such as landing pages and surveys, and supports enriched content through image slideshows, videos and PDF attachments. User management and profiling are designed to operate in line with GDPR requirements. The expected impact is more targeted public communication, reduced fragmentation across channels, improved editorial efficiency and a better user experience for citizens receiving regional information. By centralising contact management and campaign delivery, the solution strengthens the region’s capacity to communicate proactively, consistently and in a way that is more responsive to citizens’ interests.

results.title: Alexacert: Voice application on Alexa for requesting a birth certificate
results.proposal: Alexacert: Voice application on Alexa for requesting a birth certificate. Alexacert was developed by the Municipality of Turin as a proof of concept to test whether citizens could request registry certificates through a voice assistant rather than through traditional online portals or physical offices. The administrative problem is that even standard registry procedures can create friction for users, particularly when they require navigation across multiple interfaces, authentication steps and back-office systems. The prototype focuses on birth certificates, which are well suited to experimentation because they are exempt from stamp duty. The solution uses an Alexa voice application activated through the phrase “Alexa, speak with Torino certificates”. The user is identified once by linking the Amazon account with a recognised digital identity, such as SPID, and this authorisation remains valid until explicitly revoked. After recognition, the system uses the email address associated with the Amazon profile, asks the user to confirm the request and, once consent is given, retrieves the PDF certificate from the Registry or ANPR and sends it to the registered inbox. The expected value is a simpler, faster and more accessible interaction with municipal registry services. The prototype also demonstrates how voice interfaces, digital identity, consent management and public back-office integration can be combined in a citizen-facing service.

results.title: IBM Watson Content Hub
results.proposal: IBM Watson Content Hub. IBM Watson Content Hub provides a centralised environment for managing web content and digital assets across multiple digital channels. The operational need is to help organisations organise editorial materials, images, documents and other assets in a consistent way, while reducing duplication, improving searchability and supporting coherent publication across websites, applications and other online services. Stakeholders include content editors, digital service teams, communications departments, IT administrators, end users accessing digital channels, and organisations using the service through the public cloud catalogue. The implementation combines a content-management interface with IBM Watson services for automatic asset tagging, allowing digital materials to be categorised and retrieved more efficiently. A SOLR-based search engine supports asset and content discovery, while image rendition and sizing functions help adapt visual materials for omni-channel use. The system also offers REST APIs for editorial functions and content-model reuse, enabling integration with IBM and third-party solutions. Delivery through Akamai’s Content Delivery Network supports reliable digital distribution, while the SaaS model reduces infrastructure-management burdens and allows IBM to maintain updates, enrichment and security levels. The expected impact is lower operating cost, better content reuse, more consistent digital presence, faster asset discovery and improved editorial productivity. By combining centralised content governance, automated cataloguing and API-based distribution, the platform supports scalable management of digital communication services.

results.title: ConsolONE: proactive monitoring and management system for real-time control of all company resources
results.proposal: ConsolONE: proactive monitoring and management system for real-time control of all company resources. ConsolONE is presented in the AgID data catalogue as a proactive monitoring and management system for real-time control of organisational resources, including technological infrastructure, buildings, IoT devices, environmental systems, data centres, assets, vehicles and people. The operational issue addressed is the fragmentation of monitoring across different technical domains, where organisations may need separate tools for IT infrastructure, building management, environmental control, cloud systems, asset management and safety-related traceability. The stakeholders include public or private organisations using the platform, IT managers, facility managers, security and safety teams, asset-management staff and AgID as the catalogue authority. The solution aims to provide a reliable, intuitive and integrated environment for supervising resources in real time. Its implementation covers monitoring and proactive management of IT infrastructure, BMS and home-automation systems, IoT sensors using IP, radio frequency, LoRaWAN and Narrowband technologies, environmental control systems, on-premise, cloud and hybrid-cloud data centres, and company assets such as PCs, servers, tablets and smartphones. It also supports traceability of vehicles and people within company premises for security and safety purposes. The expected impact is improved operational visibility, faster detection of anomalies, more coordinated infrastructure management and reduced complexity in controlling heterogeneous systems. By integrating multiple monitoring domains, ConsolONE can enhance reliability, support preventive maintenance and strengthen organisational control over critical resources.

results.title: Brain4it : monitoring the SmartCity
results.proposal: Brain4it : monitoring the SmartCity. Brain4it was developed by the City Council of Sant Feliu de Llobregat as an open-source expert-system platform for managing Smart City infrastructure and supporting Internet of Things applications. The operational problem is that connected urban infrastructures generate diverse data flows and require remote, flexible and secure management across multiple municipal systems. City administrations need tools that can automate infrastructure control, support data governance and adapt to new use cases without relying on fragmented or closed technical environments. The stakeholders include the City Council, municipal technical teams, Smart City operators, residents and developers working with urban IoT services. The platform runs as a network service and provides a REST API, enabling remote control and programming of the City-OS platform. It uses a functional language designed to facilitate the implementation of expert systems and machine-learning applications. Conceptually, Brain4it supports modular automation, rules-based reasoning, IoT integration, infrastructure monitoring, security management and adaptable service development. Its open-source character allows the municipality and wider developer community to reuse and extend the platform for different Smart City needs. The expected impact is more efficient infrastructure management, easier integration of IoT services, reduced dependence on proprietary solutions and greater flexibility in developing new municipal applications. By combining expert-system logic with programmable interfaces, Brain4it strengthens the city’s capacity to manage urban systems in a scalable and adaptable way.

results.title: Extended Situational and Operational Knowledge Management Service for National Cyberspace
results.proposal: Extended Situational and Operational Knowledge Management Service for National Cyberspace. Portugal’s Extended Situational and Operational Knowledge Management Service for National Cyberspace forms part of a broader effort to strengthen national cybersecurity capacity and improve the country’s resilience against digital threats. The policy and operational problem is that public authorities require timely, structured and actionable knowledge about risks, incidents, vulnerabilities and trends affecting national cyberspace. Without an integrated situational-awareness capability, cybersecurity actors may struggle to coordinate responses, prioritise threats and support strategic decision-making. The main stakeholders include the National Cybersecurity Centre, AMA as the Portuguese Agency for Administrative Modernisation, public institutions, critical-service operators, businesses and citizens who depend on secure digital infrastructure. The implementation is centred on a knowledge-management service intended to support situational and operational awareness in cybersecurity. Conceptually, this may involve the collection, organisation and analysis of cybersecurity information, integration of threat data, dashboards for operational monitoring, incident-support workflows and mechanisms for sharing relevant knowledge among competent actors. The objective is to contribute to a safer, more prosperous and more resilient Portugal through innovative and inclusive action. The expected impact is improved capacity to monitor national cyberspace, support faster and better-informed responses to cyber risks, strengthen coordination among institutions and enhance trust in digital public services. Its value lies in transforming fragmented cybersecurity information into usable operational intelligence.
results.memo: Proceed. Extended Situational and Operational Knowledge Management Service for National Cyberspace is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: MILITARY CARE  (improve customer satisfaction through cognitive models of text and voice)
results.proposal: MILITARY CARE  (improve customer satisfaction through cognitive models of text and voice). MILITARY CARE, also referred to as AIcare, focuses on improving the quality and responsiveness of interactions between public service users and the organisations responsible for handling their requests. The operational issue concerns the management of customer communication across text and voice channels, where high volumes of enquiries, inconsistent responses, and delays can negatively affect satisfaction and internal efficiency. In the Portuguese national context, the initiative is associated with AMA, the Agência para a Modernização Administrativa, and is relevant to public administrations, service agents, end users, and managers responsible for service performance. The objective is to enhance customer and business satisfaction by making service interactions more accurate, faster, and easier to manage. The implementation uses cognitive models for text and voice, combining natural language processing, speech recognition, intent classification, sentiment analysis, and automated response-support capabilities. These models can process written and spoken interactions, identify the subject and urgency of requests, route cases to appropriate channels, and support staff with suggested answers or structured information. Integration would take place at the level of contact-centre systems, knowledge bases, customer relationship management tools, and service dashboards. The expected results include shorter response times, improved consistency of information, better allocation of human operators, and a more seamless user experience. The business value lies in increasing service capacity without proportionally increasing staffing costs, while improving reliability and user satisfaction.

results.title: Mobilità Integrata Trentino Trasporti (MITT)
results.proposal: Mobilità Integrata Trentino Trasporti (MITT). MITT was designed to improve the management of public transport in the Autonomous Province of Trento by making services more integrated, responsive and user-oriented. The operational challenge is that regional transport systems must coordinate tariffs, vehicles, passenger information and service planning across different routes and mobility needs. Citizens require reliable information on travel times, while transport operators need real-time visibility over vehicles and tools to support scheduling decisions. The main stakeholders include Provincia autonoma di Trento, Trentino Trasporti, passengers, transport planners and public-service managers. The project introduces smart cards for integrated and differentiated tariffs, with the possibility of extending their use in a multiservice logic. The technological implementation also includes real-time monitoring of local public transport vehicles, travel-time management and predictive support for bus scheduling. Positioning data from buses are detected and transmitted to provide passengers with information on journey times, while analytical tools can support planning and operational optimisation. At a conceptual level, the system combines smart-ticketing infrastructure, vehicle-location data, passenger information services, scheduling support and transport-management systems. The expected impact is a more efficient public transport network, better passenger experience, improved reliability of travel information and stronger capacity for transport planning. By linking fare integration with real-time operational intelligence, MITT can help the province deliver a more coordinated and effective mobility service.

results.title: ANCI Lombardia - CVqui-Jobiri
results.proposal: ANCI Lombardia - CVqui-Jobiri. The CVqui-Jobiri initiative was created to modernise youth information and employment-support services across parts of Lombardy, helping citizens, public institutions and companies interact within a more integrated labour-market ecosystem. The operational problem is that young people and jobseekers often need guidance on career planning, CV preparation, applications, interviews and access to vacancies, while local public services may lack scalable digital tools to provide personalised support. Employers, in turn, require more effective channels to reach candidates and communicate labour-market needs. The solution developed by Jobiri, in collaboration with the Informagiovani services of Cremona, Crema, Lodi, Novate Milanese and Bergamo, provides an intelligent career-service platform. Citizens can develop a professional project, consult job opportunities, create CVs using thousands of examples, access cover-letter templates, practise interviews through video simulations and improve their CVs through automated suggestions. The implementation combines digital self-service tools, recommendation functions, job-matching capabilities, automated CV analysis, interview-training simulations and employer-branding features. Public institutions can use the ecosystem to expand employment services for citizens and businesses, while companies can publish vacancies, manage selection processes and collaborate with institutions to share employment trends. The expected impact is broader access to employability support, improved quality of job applications, stronger matching between candidates and employers, and more efficient delivery of local employment services.

results.title: CEF Data Marketplace
results.proposal: CEF Data Marketplace. The CEF Data Marketplace responds to a structural problem in the translation and language-technology sector: the fragmented availability of high-quality, domain-specific, and reusable language data across different languages, sectors, and use contexts. Organisations developing translation services, public bodies, language service providers, technology companies, and data owners often face difficulties in finding trustworthy datasets that meet their linguistic, legal, and technical requirements. The objective of the use case is to create a broader and more sustainable market that serves the data needs of stakeholders operating in the global translation ecosystem, while supporting multiple language combinations and specialist domains. The implementation consists of a universal and secure trading platform for language data, designed to facilitate the discovery, exchange, licensing, and controlled reuse of datasets for machine translation and other machine learning applications. At a conceptual level, the platform relies on data cataloguing, metadata standards, secure transaction mechanisms, access controls, quality assessment processes, and integration interfaces that allow suppliers and users to interact within a trusted digital environment. The expected impact is the creation of a continuous and long-term supply of language resources, reducing search and transaction costs while improving access to data for smaller and larger market participants alike. By strengthening data availability and interoperability, the marketplace can improve translation performance, accelerate innovation, and increase the economic value of language assets

results.title: Geo Machine Learning for Health
results.proposal: Geo Machine Learning for Health. Regione Lombardia’s Geo Machine Learning for Health project applies territorial analysis to respiratory care, with a focus on patients affected by respiratory insufficiency, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and asthma. The planning challenge is that health needs are not distributed evenly across the territory, and regional authorities require more precise ways to identify areas where patients share similar healthcare characteristics, service demand and clinical profiles. The main stakeholders include Regione Lombardia, ARIA SpA, the Regional Epidemiological Observatory, healthcare planners, providers and patients living with chronic respiratory diseases. The project aims to support more granular population analysis by defining what is described as the UMTA, or Minimum Unit Territorial Aggregation: a geographical area grouping assisted individuals with homogeneous health properties connected to the respiratory tracers identified by the regional observatory. The implementation uses machine-learning techniques applied to health and territorial data, combining information on chronic respiratory conditions, patient characteristics, healthcare consumption and geographical distribution. Conceptually, the model supports spatial clustering, population stratification and predictive territorial planning. The expected impact is a more accurate understanding of where respiratory care needs are concentrated, allowing the region to plan services, allocate resources and design interventions with greater territorial precision. By linking clinical indicators with geographical aggregation, the project can improve evidence-based planning, strengthen chronic disease management and support more targeted healthcare policies across Lombardy.

results.title: Finding the ‘next-best-clinical-action"
results.proposal: Finding the ‘next-best-clinical-action". The “next-best-clinical-action” project in Regione Lombardia focuses on improving the understanding of care pathways for patients affected by cognitive dementia. The clinical and organisational challenge is that chronic patients often experience complex sequences of health events, service contacts, and care needs over time, making it difficult for healthcare planners and clinicians to anticipate the most appropriate subsequent intervention. Stakeholders include Regione Lombardia, ARIA SpA, healthcare professionals, patients with cognitive dementia, carers, and institutions responsible for chronic care planning. The objective is to analyse and predict the patient journey following the onset of dementia, year by year, over a five-year period. The implementation uses data and process mining techniques to study the characteristics of the pathology and reconstruct the sequence of medical events, consumption patterns, and healthcare interactions among the chronic population affected by cognitive dementia. Conceptually, the project combines longitudinal health data, pathway modelling, event-sequence analysis, predictive analytics, and process mining to identify the likely next clinical step in a patient’s pathway. The expected impact is better anticipation of care needs, more informed clinical and organisational planning, and stronger evidence for designing pathways around real patient trajectories. The solution can support healthcare services in identifying recurrent patterns, improving continuity of care, and aligning resources with expected demand. Its broader value lies in moving from retrospective observation to more proactive management of chronic neurodegenerative conditions.

results.title: Predictive Healthcare Assistance DB (BDA) in Regione Lombardia
results.proposal: Predictive Healthcare Assistance DB (BDA) in Regione Lombardia. Regione Lombardia’s predictive evolution of the Assisted Database focuses on improving population stratification and healthcare planning for chronic disease management. The health-system problem is that regional authorities need to understand the complexity, care needs, and service consumption of a large population affected by chronic conditions in order to plan assistance more effectively. Stakeholders include Regione Lombardia, ARIA SpA, the regional epidemiological observatory, healthcare providers, patients with chronic diseases, and policy-makers responsible for resource allocation. The objective is to move from descriptive stratification towards predictive assistance, enabling the region to anticipate needs and better organise care pathways. The implementation builds on the existing Assisted Database, which has classified the Lombardy population according to healthcare consumption and 62 chronic pathologies, using variables such as tracer conditions, complexity level, territory, gender, age group, and type of assistance. The project operates under the scientific direction of the regional epidemiological observatory and applies predictive analytics to administrative and healthcare data. At a conceptual level, the system may combine population stratification, risk modelling, longitudinal consumption data, and regional health-service information to identify groups requiring different levels of care. The expected impact is improved planning of chronic care, more accurate targeting of resources, and better understanding of territorial differences in healthcare needs. By strengthening predictive capacity, the database can support more proactive assistance models and improve the reliability of regional health policy decisions.

results.company: Department of Hygiene and Epidemiology - University of Thessaly
results.title: Efficient and targeted COVID-19 border testing via reinforcement learning
results.proposal: Efficient and targeted COVID-19 border testing via reinforcement learning. Greece’s Eva system was deployed during the summer of 2020 to improve the allocation of limited COVID-19 tests at national borders and reduce the risk of asymptomatic infected travellers entering the country undetected. The public health challenge was that uniform or country-wide testing rules could not make optimal use of constrained testing capacity, particularly when traveller flows and infection prevalence changed rapidly. Border authorities, incoming travellers, public health officials, epidemiologists, and policy-makers were directly involved. The objective was to use available testing resources more strategically while generating real-time estimates of COVID-19 prevalence to inform border policy. The implementation relied on a reinforcement learning system that allocated tests using incoming travellers’ demographic information and results from previous travellers. Unlike static protocols, Eva updated its testing strategy as new evidence became available, learning which traveller profiles or routes were associated with higher positivity risk. Conceptually, the system combined sequential decision-making, adaptive risk estimation, epidemiological data, and border-testing operations into a single allocation mechanism. The reported impact was a more targeted testing approach, allowing Greece to prioritise higher-risk arrivals despite limited resources. The system also provided policy-relevant information on prevalence among travellers, supporting more responsive border management during the pandemic. Its value lay in improving public health surveillance, making testing more efficient, and enabling decisions to adjust as conditions evolved.

results.title: Automated processes Uddevalla - AI to internal processes
results.proposal: Automated processes Uddevalla - AI to internal processes. Uddevalla municipality has pursued internal process automation to release administrative capacity within municipal services, particularly in the social administration. The organisational problem was the presence of repetitive, rules-based tasks that absorbed staff time and limited the ability to respond to growing service volumes in areas such as childcare and home care. Municipal employees, service managers, residents relying on welfare services, and the technology provider supporting automation are the principal stakeholders. The objective is to streamline back-office workflows and redirect staff capacity towards frontline and higher-value public service tasks. The implementation involves automated processes across several administrative areas, including compensation, sick pay costs, authorisation administration, IT group activities, planning systems, financial aid, automatic closing, accounting with Försäkringskassan, lunch boxes, absence, extra time, new decisions, income changes, and resource allocation. These workflows likely combine robotic process automation, rule-based processing, data extraction, system integration, and automated handovers between municipal applications. The municipality had 10 automated processes underway, corresponding to the annual work of 20 full-time positions. By 2021, further automation was expected to release capacity equivalent to another 20 full-time positions. The impact is both operational and financial: automated processes can handle increased volumes without additional resources, reduce repetitive manual work, and allow freed-up capacity to be redirected towards childcare, home-care demand, and other social administration priorities.
results.memo: Proceed. Automated processes Uddevalla - AI to internal processes is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Checks for financial support - AI for checking companies requesting support
results.proposal: Checks for financial support - AI for checking companies requesting support. Sweden’s Public Employment Service has experimented with automated decision-making to assess companies applying for financial support linked to the employment of long-term unemployed people. The administrative challenge is to verify eligibility efficiently while processing applications in a consistent way and protecting public funds. The system rates whether a company can receive support using a traffic-light logic: green indicates eligibility, yellow means that an additional manual check is required, and red indicates non-eligibility. Its implementation uses automated checks against relevant company and eligibility data, translating administrative rules and risk indicators into a structured rating that guides case handling. Conceptually, the tool combines data validation, rule-based decision support and automated classification within the grant-assessment workflow. The expected impact is faster processing, reduced workload for caseworkers and more uniform treatment of standard applications. At the same time, the use case raises concerns because caseworkers reportedly have limited possibilities to challenge the automated decision in this area. This is particularly sensitive because access to employment-support funding can affect employers’ incentives to hire long-term unemployed people and can indirectly influence labour-market inclusion outcomes.
results.memo: Proceed. Checks for financial support - AI for checking companies requesting support is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Ministry of Education, Science and Sport
results.title: Detect early learning problems in primary schools (METS)
results.proposal: Detect early learning problems in primary schools (METS). METIS was developed in Slovenia to test whether an intelligent educational support system could help identify early learning difficulties among primary-school pupils. The policy and pedagogical problem is that schools may need earlier warning of pupils who are struggling, but teachers require reliable, context-sensitive indicators rather than narrow administrative signals. The system was designed to monitor grades and absences, search for specific learning patterns and support teachers in identifying pupils who might need additional attention. Its implementation uses artificial intelligence and machine-learning methods based on indicators of educational success, with pupils assessed as being at increased risk of developing learning difficulties and then referred to an education professional for consultation and an action plan. The expected benefit is earlier intervention, more structured support for pupils and improved use of school data in educational planning. However, the project was criticised by educational experts who argued that grades and absences alone were not sufficient to detect learning problems reliably. Further concerns related to limited budget, interpolated data, methodological shortcuts and the role of a private commercial contractor holding substantial school data. These issues make the case important not only as an educational innovation, but also as an example of the governance risks of predictive systems in schools.
results.memo: Proceed. Detect early learning problems in primary schools (METS) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Detecting tax evasion schemes - Machine learning to detect tax evasion
results.proposal: Detecting tax evasion schemes - Machine learning to detect tax evasion. In Slovenia, the financial administration under the Ministry of Finance applies machine-learning techniques to strengthen tax compliance and identify behaviour that may indicate evasion, fraud, or reporting errors. The policy problem is the difficulty of detecting irregular fiscal conduct across large volumes of tax declarations, transactions, and administrative records using only manual checks or traditional rule-based controls. The key stakeholders are the Ministry of Finance, the financial administration, taxpayers, auditors, and citizens whose fiscal data may be processed. The objective is to improve the authority’s ability to uncover tax evasion schemes, detect inaccurate tax reports, and prioritise cases that warrant closer examination. The implementation uses machine learning to analyse tax data and identify patterns associated with fraud or non-compliance. According to the information provided, the ministry also ranks citizens considered “risky” because they are thought to be more likely to become tax evaders. Conceptually, the system may combine anomaly detection, predictive risk scoring, historical compliance data, classification models, and automated case selection to support audit targeting. The expected benefits include more efficient allocation of inspection resources, faster detection of suspicious schemes, and improved consistency in identifying reporting anomalies. However, citizen risk-ranking raises important concerns around transparency, accuracy, contestability, and possible unfair treatment if individuals are prioritised for scrutiny on the basis of opaque or weakly explained statistical signals.
