results.title: AI in e-Sociala program - Optimization of the social benefits tranfers
results.proposal: AI in e-Sociala program - Optimization of the social benefits tranfers. Slovenia’s e-Sociala programme was introduced to improve the administration of social transfers across the welfare system, including social assistance, unemployment benefits, child benefits, subsidies, and related entitlements. The administrative challenge was to manage complex benefit applications more efficiently while supporting social workers in checking eligibility, reducing errors, and handling large volumes of interconnected information. Citizens, social workers, welfare authorities, and the Ministry of Public Administration are the main stakeholders, as the programme affects both service delivery and access to social rights. The system is built around multiple connected databases and has progressively incorporated automated decision-making, machine-learning and predictive capabilities. Citizens can use automated tools to understand possible social rights and estimate benefit payments before submitting an application, while certain application processes for social rights are fully automated. The platform can retrieve previous benefit decisions, generate informative decisions for specific applicants, identify people belonging to the same family, and access relevant financial data to simplify case handling. Its longer-term objective is to create a complete “social rights profile” for each applicant, showing eligibility, duration, and payment amounts. The expected impact is faster processing, fewer administrative mistakes, improved support for social workers, and greater predictability for citizens. Human intervention remains necessary for legal reasons, as social workers still evaluate, print, sign, and send applications, with manual actions recorded and analysed to improve the system.

results.title: Proof of life recognition - Audio or video recognition
results.proposal: Proof of life recognition - Audio or video recognition. The proof-of-life recognition pilot aims to simplify pension verification for Portuguese retired citizens living abroad. Each year, approximately 11,000 retired Portuguese citizens abroad must demonstrate that they are alive in order to continue receiving their pension, a process that can be burdensome when it requires physical documentation or interaction with consular or administrative offices. Caixa Geral de Aposentações, the welfare institution for civil servants, launched a pilot to allow pensioners to provide proof of life through face or voice recognition. The pilot began in Macau, where hundreds of people were already using the system. The implementation relies on biometric verification through audio or video recognition, enabling remote confirmation of a pensioner’s identity and liveness. Conceptually, the system combines identity verification, facial or voice biometrics, secure submission and pension-administration workflows. The expected impact is reduced administrative burden for pensioners abroad, faster verification, fewer physical procedures and stronger continuity of pension payments. For the administration, it can reduce manual processing and improve assurance that benefits are paid only to eligible recipients. Because the process involves biometric data and elderly users, it requires careful safeguards for accessibility, consent, data security and alternative channels for those unable to use digital verification.

results.title: Catch facial recognition software
results.proposal: Catch facial recognition software. The Dutch police’s Catch system is a facial recognition tool used to support the identification of suspects in serious criminal investigations. The operational need is to compare images obtained during police work against an existing database of persons suspected of serious offences, thereby helping investigators establish possible identities more rapidly than through manual comparison alone. Stakeholders include the Dutch police, suspects whose images are stored or searched, victims of serious crime, investigators, oversight bodies, and the wider public concerned with biometric surveillance. The implementation relies on facial recognition software that compares submitted images against a database containing police-held facial images. An investigation published by VICE in July 2019 reported that Catch contained more than 2.2 million images relating to 1.3 million individuals who may have been suspected of committing serious criminal offences. In November 2019, the police confirmed that the facial recognition system had access to a complete database of people suspected of serious crimes. The national police also introduced a smartphone application allowing officers to send images to Catch. Conceptually, the system combines image capture, facial feature extraction, biometric matching, database search, and investigator review. Its expected impact is faster suspect identification, improved investigative capacity, and easier submission of images from operational settings. In 2017, 93 suspects were reportedly identified using the system. At the same time, the scale of the database and mobile access raise significant issues concerning legality, necessity, accuracy, retention, and safeguards against misuse.

results.company: Department of Public Security Central Anti-Crime Directorate
results.title: XLAW - Trends and pattern discovery in crimes
results.proposal: XLAW - Trends and pattern discovery in crimes. XLAW is an Italian predictive policing system used to support the detection of crime trends and the anticipation of offences in urban areas. The system was developed by a law-enforcement official and has been deployed in several cities, including Naples, Modena, Prato, Salerno, Livorno, Trieste, Trento, and Venice. The operational problem is that police forces need to identify where and when certain offences are likely to occur, so that patrols can be positioned more effectively before crimes take place. Stakeholders include law enforcement agencies, the Department of Public Security’s Central Anti-Crime Directorate, local police services, residents, potential victims, and persons who may be affected by predictive policing practices. The implementation is described as a probabilistic, machine-learning-powered solution for discovering trends and patterns in crime. It relies on the analysis of criminal history in specific locations over time, reportedly drawing on 20 years of data and the developer’s field experience. The system can alert officers and support deployment before an offence is expected to happen, and it has been reported to provide details such as gender, height, citizenship, distinguishing features, and biometrics of a potential suspect. Reported accuracy figures include 87–93% in Naples, 92–93% in Venice, and 94% in Prato, while the Venice State Police stated that 84% of attempted or committed felonies had been foreseen. However, no independent public audit or fact-checking appears available for these trials, making external validation essential before treating these results as conclusive.

results.company: Polizia di Stato - Questura di Milano
results.title: KeyCrime - Crime Analysis for the next generation (Predictive Policing)
results.proposal: KeyCrime - Crime Analysis for the next generation (Predictive Policing). KeyCrime was developed from operational policing experience in Milan to support the analysis of thefts and robberies and help investigators identify offences that may have been committed by the same person or group. The policing problem is that serial crimes can appear as separate incidents when data are fragmented across reports, locations and investigative files, making it difficult to detect recurring patterns quickly. Stakeholders include the Polizia di Stato, the Milan Police Headquarters, investigators, victims of robbery, local communities and the KeyCrime company. The software, later associated with the company KeyCrime and the product Delia, analyses thousands of data points to compare different crimes and identify possible relationships between them. Conceptually, the system supports crime-linkage analysis by examining variables such as modus operandi, location, timing, target type, behavioural features and other investigative information. Its purpose is not only to support enforcement after offences occur, but also to assist prevention by helping police understand serial patterns and prioritise operational responses. The solution was tested in production in Italy by the State Police in Milan to combat robberies. The expected impact is faster recognition of crime series, more focused investigative work, better allocation of police resources and improved capacity to anticipate repeated offending. By transforming large volumes of case data into structured operational intelligence, the tool can strengthen investigative effectiveness, although its accuracy and governance arrangements require careful validation.
results.memo: Proceed. KeyCrime - Crime Analysis for the next generation (Predictive Policing) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Evasometro Anonimizzato - Big data analysis of taxpayer behaviour
results.proposal: Evasometro Anonimizzato - Big data analysis of taxpayer behaviour. Italy’s Evasometro Anonimizzato was created to help the tax administration detect inconsistencies in taxpayer behaviour by analysing large volumes of fiscal and financial information. The underlying administrative problem is tax evasion, particularly cases where declared income, consumption patterns, or financial transactions appear misaligned. For the Agenzia delle Entrate, the objective is to acquire a broader evidence base for understanding taxpayers’ fiscal conduct and identifying situations that may merit further scrutiny. Stakeholders include the Italian Tax Authority, taxpayers, financial institutions, public bodies holding relevant records, and individuals whose data may be analysed. The implementation is described as using specific algorithms to cross-check databases held by the fiscal authorities and detect anomalies in consumption or financial operations. These “digital eyes” flag inconsistencies, after which tax officials may summon individuals for additional checks. The system is also intended to be combined with monitoring of open sources, including news articles, websites, and social media, to enrich the authority’s understanding of potentially relevant behaviour. Conceptually, the solution combines big-data analytics, anomaly detection, database matching, risk scoring, and open-source intelligence. The expected impact is stronger targeting of tax controls, better use of existing administrative data, and potentially higher efficiency in identifying suspicious cases. However, the tool also raises questions about transparency, proportionality, data protection, and the risk that automated flags may place burdens on taxpayers without sufficient contextual explanation.
results.memo: Proceed. Evasometro Anonimizzato - Big data analysis of taxpayer behaviour is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Tribunal of Pisa (and EMbeDS, KDD Lab)
results.title: Predictive Jurisprudence - Tribunale di Pisa
results.proposal: Predictive Jurisprudence - Tribunale di Pisa. Predictive Jurisprudence is a long-term research and development initiative aimed at applying data science, natural language processing and legal analytics to judicial materials. The operational challenge is that courts and researchers handle large volumes of legal texts that require anonymisation, annotation, querying and analysis before they can support research, decision support or institutional knowledge management. The project started in 2019 at LIDER Lab, Scuola Superiore Sant’Anna, in collaboration with EMbeDS, KDD Lab and the Tribunal of Genoa, and was later followed by an agreement with the Tribunal of Pisa for anonymisation and pseudonymisation protocols of case-law materials. The implementation follows a modular, interdisciplinary approach, combining legal expertise, software pipelines, pseudonymisation tools, automatic annotation, data mining and predictive models. Conceptually, the project aims to build enabling technologies for legal analytics while remaining coherent with regulatory and ethical constraints. The expected impact is improved management of legal documents, better access to structured judicial knowledge, more efficient anonymisation of case law and stronger foundations for explainable legal analytics. The project’s own website still describes it as a commitment towards a fully automated data-driven platform for legal analytics.

results.proposal: Predicting chronic pathologies and post-surgery complications. The Vimercate hospital initiative applies predictive analytics to clinical and organisational decision support within the Lombardy public health system. The operational problem is that hospitals need to manage patients more efficiently, anticipate chronic disease risks and identify post-surgical complications early, while also reducing costs and improving logistics. ASST Vimercate adopted open-source cloud solutions developed by Almaviva, building on a long digitisation process of medical records. The implementation uses algorithms and machine-learning analytics to develop predictive models for chronic diseases and post-operative complications, supporting the hospital’s broader precision-medicine objectives. Conceptually, the system combines digitised clinical records, cloud infrastructure, predictive modelling, patient-risk stratification and decision-support tools for healthcare professionals. The expected impact is earlier identification of risk, more personalised treatment planning, improved allocation of hospital resources and stronger preventive care. Almaviva describes the wider platform as supporting prognoses in areas ranging from chronic diseases to post-operative infection risk and drug-therapy outcomes. The available sources present the initiative as a structured experimentation and adoption of predictive AI in a hospital setting, but not as a replacement for clinicians.

results.company: Hellenic Police and the Hellenic Ministry of Citizen Protection
results.title: Smart policing software - Development an integrated information system for police
results.proposal: Smart policing software - Development an integrated information system for police. Greece’s Smart Policing project was conceived as an integrated information system to support police checks in real time during stops and field operations. The operational problem was that officers needed mobile access to identity, document and database-verification capabilities, while existing checks could require slower, less integrated procedures. Under a €4 million contract signed in 2019, Intracom Telecom was to develop and supply a system for the Hellenic Police and the Ministry of Citizen Protection, including 1,000 portable devices and 500 external fingerprint scanners. The planned implementation combined facial recognition, automated fingerprint identification, document authentication, vehicle and object identification, and complex searches across existing databases. Conceptually, the system linked portable biometric devices, identity-verification workflows, document scanning, police databases and real-time mobile checks. The expected operational impact was faster field identification, more integrated access to law-enforcement information and greater efficiency during police stops. However, the project raised significant legality and data-protection concerns because it involved biometric processing in public policing contexts. In 2026, the Greek Data Protection Authority warned that activating the system’s biometric functions would constitute unlawful data processing, following an investigation initiated after a complaint by Homo Digitalis.

results.title: ANPR Greece
results.proposal: ANPR Greece. Greece introduced Automatic Number Plate Recognition cameras in 2019 to strengthen police capacity to identify vehicles linked to theft or criminal activity. The operational challenge was to enable officers to check large volumes of moving vehicles more rapidly than would be possible through manual observation, particularly in situations where police cars need to operate across roads and public spaces. The relevant stakeholders include the Hellenic Police, vehicle owners, road users, victims of vehicle-related crime, and public authorities responsible for law enforcement and traffic security. The objective is to provide mobile police units with a rapid detection capability that can compare observed licence plates against relevant records and alert officers when a match is found. The implementation consists of ANPR cameras installed on 50 Hellenic Police vehicles. These cameras capture licence plate images, convert them into readable alphanumeric data, and compare the results with databases of stolen vehicles or vehicles associated with criminal offences. The system is capable of recognising 15,000 licence plates per hour and can detect plates on vehicles travelling above 170 km per hour. Future functionality was expected to include identification of uninsured vehicles. The impact is increased operational reach for police patrols, faster detection of vehicles of interest, and improved capacity to act in real time. The system can also reduce reliance on manual checks, though its use requires appropriate data-retention, accuracy, and oversight safeguards.
results.memo: Proceed. ANPR Greece is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: DyRiAS potential to go on a school shooting rampage.
results.proposal: DyRiAS potential to go on a school shooting rampage. Within the Federal State Education Agency of Saxony-Anhalt, DyRiAS-Schule is deployed to help assess whether a student may present a serious threat of school violence, including the potential to carry out a shooting rampage. The problem addressed is the difficulty of identifying credible warning signs in highly sensitive situations where schools and authorities must act quickly, but also avoid disproportionate or discriminatory responses. Stakeholders include students, school staff, education authorities, families, psychological or security professionals, and the assessed individuals themselves. The purpose of the system is to support threat management by giving education authorities a structured framework for evaluating risk signals and deciding whether preventive intervention is required. Technically, the tool appears to operate through a standardised assessment process focused on observable behaviour, contextual information, and indicators associated with severe targeted violence. It can be understood as a structured risk-analysis instrument that organises case data, applies predefined criteria, and produces a threat-level assessment for professional review. The intended impact is to improve consistency in how schools and authorities interpret warning signs, reduce the likelihood of overlooked high-risk cases, and support earlier coordination of prevention measures. Its use may also help document why certain interventions were considered or initiated. However, because the system concerns minors and potentially life-altering assessments, its deployment requires careful governance, transparent procedures, proportionality, and safeguards against stigmatisation or inaccurate labelling.

results.title: DyRiAS threat levels of abusive male partners
results.proposal: DyRiAS threat levels of abusive male partners. In Singen and Weimar, women’s protection centres use DyRiAS-Intimpartner to support the assessment of risks posed by abusive male partners. The operational need arises in domestic violence contexts, where professionals must identify whether a perpetrator may represent an escalating threat and determine what protective measures may be required for the victim. The main stakeholders include women experiencing intimate partner violence, protection-centre staff, local authorities, police or support services that may act on the assessment, and the individuals being assessed. The objective is to provide a structured method for evaluating threat levels so that practitioners can prioritise cases, document risk factors, and coordinate appropriate responses. The implementation relies on a specialised risk-assessment tool for intimate partner violence, likely using standardised questions, behavioural indicators, case information, and scoring rules to generate a threat classification. Rather than replacing professional judgement, the system appears to support staff by organising relevant data and producing an assessment that can inform further action. Its value lies in creating a more consistent approach to risk identification, particularly where fragmented information or subjective interpretation could otherwise affect decision-making. The expected impact is earlier recognition of serious threats, better allocation of protective resources, and more systematic support for victims. At the same time, such a tool requires strong safeguards, because errors or over-reliance on automated risk categories could have serious consequences for safety, rights, and accountability.
results.memo: Proceed. DyRiAS threat levels of abusive male partners is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.proposal: ALLEGRO - administer unemployment benefit. The Bundesagentur für Arbeit (Federal Labor Agency) uses an IT-system called ALLEGRO to administer unemployment benefit. results.company: Agency for Labor, Social Affairs, Family and Integration
results.title: JUS-IT -  Child Care Service
results.proposal: JUS-IT -  Child Care Service. JUS-IT is a case-management and administrative software system used in Hamburg for the General Social Service, the Child Care Service, and the Economic Help for Youths Programme. The operational problem is that child and youth welfare services require the coordinated handling of sensitive cases, payments, records, and inter-agency information flows, often involving vulnerable children, families, social workers, police information, and health insurance data. The objective is to support case administration and automate certain payment-related processes within the Agency for Labour, Social Affairs, Family and Integration. The implementation is based on Cúram, a modular off-the-shelf IBM product that can be adapted to specific welfare-administration needs. At a conceptual level, the system combines case records, workflow management, payment automation, data interfaces, and administrative reporting functions. Its interfaces connect to police reports and health insurance funds, enabling caseworkers to draw on external information sources within welfare-related procedures. The expected benefits include more centralised case handling, reduced duplication of administrative tasks, improved continuity of records, and more efficient payment administration. Nevertheless, the system appears to have faced serious concerns regarding performance, suitability, or governance, since a major revision or complete shutdown was recommended in 2019. In a child welfare context, these issues are especially significant because system reliability, data quality, and clear accountability directly affect sensitive decisions and service delivery.

results.title: Identity Check of Migrants - Analysis of content and language of phones
results.proposal: Identity Check of Migrants - Analysis of content and language of phones. This use case concerns the use of automated text, speech, and device-analysis tools by Germany’s Federal Office for Migration and Refugees to support identity checks in asylum procedures. The operational problem is that applicants may arrive without valid identity documents, requiring authorities to assess claims about country or region of origin through alternative evidence. Stakeholders include asylum seekers, BAMF employees, migration authorities, technology providers, legal representatives, and civil society organisations concerned with procedural rights and privacy. The objective is to provide officials with additional indications that may support verification of an applicant’s stated background. The implementation includes software capable of extracting and analysing data from mobile phones, tablets, or laptops when access is requested, presenting employees with a limited overview of device content and language patterns found in text. A separate tool analyses a two-minute voice recording in which the applicant describes a picture in their mother tongue, calculating how closely the speech matches a particular dialect. Conceptually, the system combines mobile forensics, text recognition, language detection, speech analysis, and probabilistic dialect classification. The expected administrative value is faster access to supporting information in cases where documentary evidence is missing. However, the use case involves significant risks relating to consent, privacy, evidential reliability, linguistic accuracy, and the potential consequences of automated indications in asylum decisions.

results.title: Suicide Prevention in Jail - Detecting of suspicious objects in a cell
results.proposal: Suicide Prevention in Jail - Detecting of suspicious objects in a cell. North Rhine-Westphalia’s prison suicide-prevention programme was launched to reduce suicide risk among detainees classified as medium to high risk. The operational problem is that conventional in-person checks at 15-minute intervals can be resource-intensive and may increase emotional strain on inmates, while prison staff still need reliable ways to detect dangerous objects or situations promptly. The Ministry of Justice of North Rhine-Westphalia commissioned FusionSystems GmbH to build a video surveillance system able to identify suspicious objects in a cell, such as a knotted rope or a firelighter, and alert officers on duty. The implementation uses video analytics and object-recognition techniques to monitor defined visual indicators associated with suicide risk. Conceptually, the system combines camera-based observation, automated object detection, risk-specific alerting and staff response workflows. The expected impact is earlier warning of potential self-harm situations, reduced need for intrusive repeated checks and better allocation of staff attention towards cases requiring intervention. However, because the system operates in a prison environment and concerns highly vulnerable individuals, it requires strict safeguards around privacy, necessity, accuracy, proportionality and human oversight. Its value depends on whether automated alerts can improve safety without creating excessive surveillance or false reassurance.

results.title: RADAAR-iTE Predictive policing - risk assessment of militant Salafitsts
results.proposal: RADAAR-iTE Predictive policing - risk assessment of militant Salafitsts. RADAR-iTE is a German risk-assessment tool used to support police evaluation of persons already known to the authorities in relation to militant Salafist extremism. The operational problem is that security agencies must prioritise attention and resources across individuals who may present different levels of threat, while ensuring that assessments are structured, documented, and comparable. Stakeholders include the Bundeskriminalamt, caseworkers, other security authorities, assessed individuals, and the research partner involved in development. The objective is to classify known persons into threat levels that can inform subsequent operational decisions. The implementation is based on a standardised questionnaire completed by a caseworker using observable behaviour and data already gathered by the police, as well as information the police are legally authorised to access. The system then produces a categorisation into three levels: high, conspicuous, or moderate. Conceptually, RADAR-iTE functions as a structured professional judgement and risk-scoring tool, combining behavioural indicators, case information, and predefined assessment criteria rather than acting as a fully autonomous policing system. Once the threat level is generated, the responsible caseworker or department decides what action should follow. The expected impact is greater consistency in risk classification, clearer prioritisation of security resources, and more systematic documentation of assessments. However, the use case also requires careful safeguards due to its sensitivity, including legality, proportionality, non-discrimination, and accountability for decisions based on risk categorisation.
results.memo: Proceed. RADAAR-iTE Predictive policing - risk assessment of militant Salafitsts is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Face recognition at schools - Face recognition at the building’s entrance
results.proposal: Face recognition at schools - Face recognition at the building’s entrance. The use case concerns a proposed access-control system for selected high schools in Nice and Marseille, where local authorities sought to manage entry to school buildings more efficiently while strengthening perimeter security and monitoring the flow of pupils. The operational issue was centred on verifying that only authorised students could enter school premises, with school administrations, municipal authorities, students, parents, and technology providers all affected by the initiative. The intended objective was to replace or complement existing manual checks at the building entrance with a faster identity-verification process. The proposed implementation relied on facial recognition technology installed at school entrances, under a programme to be funded and delivered by Cisco. In conceptual terms, the system would have compared live facial images captured at entry points against enrolled biometric templates associated with authorised pupils, using image-processing models, biometric matching algorithms, controlled access infrastructure, and secure storage mechanisms. Integration would likely have involved entry gates, local school databases, and identity-management workflows. The expected benefits included shorter queues, more consistent access control, reduced administrative burden for staff, and improved perceived security. However, the project was placed on hold after the French data protection authority considered it illegal, underlining that operational efficiency gains could not outweigh concerns around proportionality, consent, children’s rights, and compliance with data protection rules.

results.title: Checking entitlement of umemployment aid
results.proposal: Checking entitlement of umemployment aid. This use case concerns the use of automated decision-making by Estonia’s Unemployment Insurance Fund to determine what unemployed persons are entitled to receive, including the amount and duration of unemployment aid or unemployment insurance benefits. The operational problem is that benefit entitlement assessment requires the processing of eligibility rules, personal employment histories, insurance records, and other administrative data, often under time pressure and with direct consequences for citizens’ income security. Stakeholders include unemployed applicants, the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund, public employment-service staff, and the wider social protection system. The objective is to accelerate and standardise the calculation of benefit rights while reducing manual workload in routine cases. The implementation uses automated systems to assess entitlement on the basis of available applicant data and predefined legal or administrative criteria. At a conceptual level, the system likely combines data retrieval from official registers, rule-based eligibility checks, automated calculation modules, and case-routing functions for decisions requiring further review. The information provided indicates that 50% of these decisions are made entirely through automated means. The expected impact includes faster processing, improved administrative scalability, and more uniform application of entitlement rules. At the same time, because the decisions affect access to financial support, the use case raises important requirements around explainability, contestability, accuracy, and human oversight, especially where applicants may need to challenge or correct the data used in the assessment.

The key stakeholders are unemployed citizens, the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund, public databases holding relevant administrative records, and case officers responsible for employment services. The objective is to make registration faster and more standardised by allowing the system to verify the applicant’s data after online submission and determine which document should be sent to the person concerned. results.title: Prediction model for the healthcare needs of patients with chronic illnesses
results.proposal: Prediction model for the healthcare needs of patients with chronic illnesses. This use case addresses the need to strengthen primary care in Estonia by helping family physicians identify patients with selected chronic conditions who are at higher risk of hospital admission or other adverse health outcomes. The operational challenge is that health systems often hold substantial administrative and billing data but may struggle to use it proactively to support prevention, care planning, and earlier intervention. Stakeholders include the Estonian Health Insurance Fund, family practitioners, patients with chronic illnesses, the World Bank, and international partners contributing comparative data. The objective is to provide a practical prediction model that can support physicians in prioritising patients who may require closer monitoring or tailored care. The implementation draws on medical invoice data held by the Estonian Health Insurance Fund to identify relevant diagnoses and patient characteristics. The pilot also involved Costa Rica, which provided access to its medical billing database to examine clinical and socio-economic data not included in EHIF datasets. At a conceptual level, the model applies predictive analytics to administrative health records, seeking the algorithm that best estimates the likelihood of hospital admission or further health problems. Training and reinforcement were supported through webinars for family practitioners, led by a local pilot coordinator acting as a World Bank consultant. The expected impact is better targeting of primary care, earlier identification of high-risk patients, and improved use of existing health data for prevention-oriented service planning.

results.title: Exam control in schools: fighting fraud or profiling students?
results.proposal: Exam control in schools: fighting fraud or profiling students?. This use case concerns the use of digital examination-monitoring tools in Denmark to detect suspected exam fraud in schools and universities. The operational problem is the need to protect the integrity of assessments while managing large numbers of students and increasingly digital forms of examination. Education authorities and institutions sought ways to identify plagiarism, unauthorised collaboration, or manipulation of exam conditions more efficiently than through manual review alone. However, students, schools, universities, and public authorities became involved in a wider debate about proportionality, privacy, accuracy, and fairness. The implementation relied on digital monitoring and analytical tools designed to observe or assess student behaviour, device activity, and written submissions. One strand involved The Digital Exam Monitor, while another example came from students at Copenhagen University, who developed a machine-learning system for plagiarism detection using around 130,000 student assignments. Such systems can conceptually combine text comparison, behavioural monitoring, statistical similarity detection, and data-driven anomaly identification. The expected impact would be stronger fraud detection, more consistent enforcement, and reduced administrative effort in checking exams. Nevertheless, the use case generated substantial resistance because students considered the tools invasive and potentially discriminatory. Concerns also emerged around the unauthorised use of assignment data, the risk of false positives, and the profiling of particular groups of students.

results.title: Taxation and the automatization of property evaluation
results.proposal: Taxation and the automatization of property evaluation. Denmark’s automated property valuation initiative addresses a long-standing administrative challenge in tax governance: how to assess property values consistently, efficiently, and at national scale. Property valuation is central to taxation, but manual or fragmented approaches can be slow, costly, uneven, and difficult to update across large numbers of properties. The Danish government has therefore sought for several years to centralise and automate parts of tax administration, with property assessment becoming one of the key initiatives. The relevant stakeholders include the Danish Tax Authority, property owners, taxpayers, legislators, administrative law experts, and system developers. The objective is to establish a more standardised valuation process capable of calculating property values through a national automated system. The legal basis is the Ejendomsvurderingslov, the 2017 law on property assessment, which mandates the use of an automated valuation system. The planned implementation is expected to use machine learning to develop a statistical predictive model, drawing on property characteristics, market information, geographic variables, and other administrative datasets to estimate values. At a system level, this requires integration with tax databases, cadastral information, valuation workflows, and channels for administrative review. The intended impact is greater scalability, more consistent assessments, lower long-term processing costs, and faster updates. However, the system has faced delays, rising cost concerns, doubts about accuracy, and questions over compatibility with Danish administrative law, meaning that the expected benefits remain dependent on technical reliability and legal robustness.

results.title: Predictive ADM systems for healthcare and upbringing
results.proposal: Predictive ADM systems for healthcare and upbringing. This use case brings together two related applications of predictive automated decision-making in Belgium: health risk prediction and possible future support for child-related public services. In healthcare, the operational problem concerns the early identification of atrial fibrillation, a heart rhythm disorder associated with serious cardiovascular events, including heart attacks. Earlier detection could support preventive care, clinical prioritisation, and better risk management. Stakeholders include patients, clinicians, researchers, healthcare providers, and technology developers such as the Brussels start-up Kantify and the AI Lab at Université Libre de Bruxelles, Iridia. The implementation described for atrial fibrillation involves a predictive model trained to identify patterns linked to the condition, using health-related data and machine-learning techniques to estimate risk. A second, less concrete strand concerns the Flemish Agency for Upbringing, where public discussion indicated interest in using predictive systems to anticipate whether problems may emerge for a particular child, based on existing information. However, the Agency stated that there were no concrete plans at that stage and that it was preparing a policy note. The potential impact in healthcare includes earlier detection, better targeting of interventions, and improved clinical efficiency. In child and family services, possible benefits could include earlier support and more proactive case management, but the absence of a defined implementation makes results uncertain. The use case therefore illustrates both the promise of predictive tools and the need for caution, legal clarity, transparency, and strong safeguards in sensitive domains.

results.title: Algorithmic school registrations
results.proposal: Algorithmic school registrations. Algorithmic school registration systems in Belgian cities emerged in response to persistent problems in allocating school places fairly when demand exceeded capacity, particularly where parents sought admission to the same popular schools. In some cases, families spent nights in tents outside schools to secure early registration, which was widely seen as inequitable and administratively unsustainable. The stakeholders include children, parents, schools, municipalities, education authorities, and communities concerned with equal access to education. The objective was to replace first-come, first-served practices with centralised online registration procedures capable of allocating places according to defined criteria. In primary education, the Leuven system considers variables collected from parents, including the mother’s education level and whether the student receives a grant, to classify children as “indicator” or “non-indicator” students. Further allocation is based on distance between home and school and the stated school preference, with schools able to assign different weights to these two criteria, such as 30%, 50%, or 70%. In Antwerp, distance must receive at least 50% weight. For secondary schools, some cities use a different algorithm because distance can be discriminatory where not all municipalities have secondary schools; instead, priority students and indicator students are considered, with random allocation based on first choice across three rounds. The expected benefits include less queuing, greater procedural order, and more transparent allocation. Yet the system has also produced contested outcomes, such as pupils living near a school not receiving a place while others from farther away were admitted.

results.title: Briefcam - Smart video surveillance by the local police
results.proposal: Briefcam - Smart video surveillance by the local police. The Briefcam use case concerns the adoption of smart video surveillance by the local police serving Kortrijk, Kuurne, and Lendelede, known as VLAS, from 2019 onwards. The operational issue was the need to process large amounts of video footage more efficiently, particularly when police services had to search for people, vehicles, animals, or other objects appearing in recorded images. Traditional manual review of surveillance footage can be slow, resource-intensive, and inconsistent, especially where many cameras or long recordings are involved. The stakeholders include local police forces, municipal authorities, residents, people captured by surveillance systems, and the technology provider. The objective was to make video analysis faster and more searchable for policing and security purposes. The implementation uses Briefcam’s video analytics system, which stores objects detected in footage and classifies them into categories such as people, small vehicles, large vehicles, and animals. The system then performs additional categorisation: for people, it may distinguish between men, women, and children, and further identify visual attributes such as sleeve length, trousers, clothing colour, hats, handbags, or backpacks; comparable categorisation is applied to vehicles. At a conceptual level, the system combines object detection, image classification, metadata extraction, and searchable video indexing. The expected impact is faster investigation support, improved ability to identify relevant footage, and reduced time spent on manual review. However, the use case also raises important issues regarding proportionality, accuracy, transparency, and the monitoring of people in public spaces.
results.memo: Proceed. Briefcam - Smart video surveillance by the local police is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: IBM Watson: Automated assistance in tax filing in Spain
results.proposal: IBM Watson: Automated assistance in tax filing in Spain. The Spanish Tax Authority’s use of IBM Watson responds to a specific administrative challenge in VAT filing, particularly for large companies dealing with complex reporting obligations. Before the deployment, civil servants received a substantial volume of email enquiries related to VAT issues, creating repetitive workload and slowing down support for taxpayers. The operational context therefore involved a national tax administration seeking to provide more continuous, consistent, and scalable assistance, while reducing the burden on staff responsible for answering technical questions. The objective was to offer automated support on a defined aspect of VAT filing, allowing companies to obtain guidance outside standard office hours and helping public servants concentrate on more complex cases. The implementation used IBM Watson as an automated assistance tool, applying natural language processing and question-answering capabilities to interpret written queries, retrieve relevant information, and provide responses linked to tax-filing requirements. At system level, the solution would rely on curated tax knowledge, structured guidance, conversational interfaces, and integration with the Tax Authority’s service channels. Public communications emphasised its 24/7 availability and its capacity to absorb repeated enquiries. Reported results indicate a marked operational effect: between July 2017 and February 2018, weekly emails to civil servants on VAT matters fell from 900 to 165, while the assistant’s use rose from around 200 questions per week at launch in July 2017 to approximately 2,000 by November 2017. These figures suggest improved scalability, lower administrative pressure, and greater availability of taxpayer support.

results.title: Introduction of autonomous electric vehicles for urban transport
results.proposal: Introduction of autonomous electric vehicles for urban transport. Rzeszów’s autonomous electric vehicle pilot focuses on connecting different transport nodes through driverless public transport vehicles. The mobility challenge is to improve first- and last-mile connectivity between local, long-distance, railway and air stations, where passengers often need convenient transfers across different transport modes. The Municipality of Rzeszów and MPK are associated with the planned introduction of autonomous, driverless electric vehicles that would carry passengers between these transfer points. The implementation is based on autonomous electric shuttle technology, combining vehicle automation, electric propulsion, route planning, passenger-transfer management and integration with the wider urban transport network. Conceptually, such a system uses sensors, navigation software, control systems and predefined operating routes to move passengers safely between nodes without a conventional driver. The expected impact is improved intermodal connectivity, reduced dependence on private cars for short transfer journeys, lower local emissions and a more innovative public transport offer. If successfully tested, the pilot could provide evidence on the feasibility of autonomous shuttles in Polish urban mobility, including their operational reliability, passenger acceptance and integration with existing public transport services. Its long-term value would depend on safety performance, regulatory approval, infrastructure readiness and clear service integration.

results.title: Poznan: Improving the flow of electric bus traffic
results.proposal: Poznan: Improving the flow of electric bus traffic. Poznań’s electric-bus traffic-flow pilot was designed to support the introduction of electric buses on route No. 174 by improving bus priority at traffic lights. The transport-management problem is that electric buses require reliable scheduling and sufficient charging time at terminal loops, while delays caused by traffic signals can reduce operational efficiency and affect service regularity. The Municipality of Poznań therefore equipped traffic lights along the route with signal receivers from buses and adjusted signal programmes to prioritise bus movement. The implementation combines vehicle-to-infrastructure communication, traffic-signal priority and timetable-sensitive operational planning. Conceptually, buses transmit their presence or approach to the signal system, which can then adapt traffic-light phases to improve journey smoothness and reduce unnecessary waiting time. The objective is not simply to reduce travel time, but also to maximise the time available for vehicle charging at the end loop, which is critical for electric-bus reliability. The expected impact is smoother public transport operation, improved punctuality, better energy-management conditions and stronger passenger service quality. By aligning traffic-control infrastructure with the needs of electric fleets, the pilot supports the transition to cleaner public transport while reducing the operational risks associated with battery charging and route delays.
results.memo: Proceed. Poznan: Improving the flow of electric bus traffic is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: The use of game theory in the process of modeling the development of smart city
results.proposal: The use of game theory in the process of modeling the development of smart city. The Warsaw smart-city modelling pilot aims to represent the development and functioning of a smart city through a participatory game based on game-theory principles. The policy and planning problem is that urban development involves multiple actors with different objectives, resources and constraints, including city authorities, developers, environmental organisations and residents. A conventional planning model may struggle to capture these interactions, particularly where cooperation, conflict, negotiation and shared benefits influence outcomes. The implementation seeks to develop a participatory game model using artificial intelligence methods, with cooperative game theory providing the formal basis for representing smart-city processes. A key element is parameterisation: defining the number of players, assigning their roles and modelling how their decisions affect urban development scenarios. Conceptually, the system combines simulation, stakeholder modelling, strategic interaction and AI-supported analysis to illustrate how smart-city choices may evolve under different assumptions. The expected impact is better understanding of urban governance dynamics, stronger support for participatory planning and improved capacity to test policy options before implementation. By translating complex city-development processes into a structured game model, the pilot can help public authorities explore trade-offs, incentives and cooperation mechanisms in smart-city policy design.

results.title: Viralcom Egg - accidents in the water
results.proposal: Viralcom Egg - accidents in the water. Viralcom Egg is a prototype designed to detect accidents in water and communicate relevant alerts to rescue services. The safety problem is that drownings or underwater incidents can be difficult to identify quickly, especially where visual monitoring from the shore is limited or delayed. The Municipality of Dordrecht is linked to the pilot context, with Viralcom seeking to test the Egg remotely from the quay in Zwijndrecht to the opposite quay in Dordrecht. The implementation uses artificial intelligence and neural networks for pattern recognition and drowning detection. Conceptually, the system monitors activity in or around the water, analyses visual or sensor patterns that may indicate an accident, and sends information to emergency or rescue services when a potential incident is identified. The expected impact is faster detection of water accidents, shorter response times and improved public safety in areas where people may fall into or become distressed in water. The prototype’s value depends on reliable detection under varying environmental conditions, low false-alarm rates and effective integration with rescue-service workflows. If validated, it could strengthen prevention and emergency response in urban waterfront areas.

results.title: Movable Traffic Predictor
results.proposal: Movable Traffic Predictor. The Movable Traffic Predictor pilot was designed to support traffic-management decisions by forecasting traffic conditions before congestion becomes visible in real time. The operational problem is that traffic-control centres often react to current data, while non-recurrent congestion caused by incidents, sudden bottlenecks or unusual flows may require earlier warnings to deploy effective measures. File radar B.V. developed a new type of AI-based traffic forecaster capable of predicting traffic up to about one hour ahead, with testing carried out in collaboration with traffic-control centres, particularly the national VCNL centre near Utrecht. The implementation applies predictive analytics to traffic data to generate short-term forecasts in the range of approximately 20 to 60 minutes. Conceptually, the system analyses current and historical traffic conditions, identifies emerging disruptions and provides predictive information for operational decisions such as congestion detection, deployment of mobile assets or traffic-management measures. The expected impact is earlier intervention, improved traffic flow, reduced delay and better use of transport-management resources. By shifting traffic control from purely real-time monitoring to anticipatory decision support, the pilot can improve resilience to irregular and incident-driven congestion.

evidence.quote: The operational problem is that traffic-control centres often react to current data, while non-recurrent congestion caused by incidents, sudden bottlenecks or unusual flows may require earlier warnings to deploy effective measures.

Conceptually, the system analyses current and historical traffic conditions, identifies emerging disruptions and provides predictive information for operational decisions such as congestion detection, deployment of mobile assets or traffic-management measures.

results.memo: Proceed. Movable Traffic Predictor is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Dutch Police, with Speech lab B.V.
results.title: Speaker Tracking in Time and Space
results.proposal: Speaker Tracking in Time and Space. Speaker Tracking in Time and Space supports police analysis of audio recordings by separating and labelling speech from different speakers. The operational issue is that investigations can involve lengthy recordings with multiple voices, requiring officers or analysts to listen manually to identify who is speaking and when. This is time-consuming and can also expose investigators to conversations unrelated to the subject of interest, creating unnecessary privacy intrusion. Spraaklab develops technology that can largely disassemble, distinguish and label speech from different speakers, allowing police teams to work more efficiently and with higher analytical quality. The implementation uses speech-processing techniques, likely including speaker diarisation, voice-separation, audio segmentation and speaker-labelling models. Conceptually, the tool structures raw audio into speaker-specific segments, helping analysts locate relevant parts of recordings without reviewing unrelated material repeatedly. The expected impact is faster audio review, improved investigative productivity, better-quality evidence handling and stronger privacy protection for people whose conversations are not relevant to the investigation. Its value depends on accuracy in difficult acoustic conditions, careful validation and appropriate human review, since mistaken speaker attribution could affect investigative interpretation.
results.memo: Proceed. Speaker Tracking in Time and Space is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: UWV, SVB, the Tax And Customs Administration, DUO, Justid, CJIB and RDW
results.title: Enforcement of social policy laws with AI
results.proposal: Enforcement of social policy laws with AI. This national Dutch pilot concerns the use of data analysis to support enforcement of social-security legislation, particularly in relation to fraud detection and compliance with the duty to inform. The administrative problem is that several public bodies are responsible for schemes, payments, registrations and enforcement processes that may involve overlapping information on citizens, benefits, education, taxation, vehicles and justice-related records. Coordinated analysis can help authorities understand enforcement risks, identify inconsistencies and evaluate how social-security rules are implemented. The implementation involves organisations including UWV, SVB, the Tax and Customs Administration, DUO, Justid, CJIB and RDW. Conceptually, the system can combine cross-agency data analysis, risk indicators, policy evaluation and compliance monitoring to support enforcement of social-policy laws. The expected impact is more structured insight into enforcement practice, better targeting of checks and improved understanding of where errors, omissions or potential fraud may occur. However, because the use case involves sensitive personal and administrative data across multiple bodies, it requires strong safeguards on legality, purpose limitation, transparency, proportionality and independent oversight. The business value for public administration depends on using analytics to improve fairness and efficiency without creating opaque or discriminatory risk profiling.

results.title: Smart lampposts for combating burglaries - Detection of suspicious movements and audio
results.proposal: Smart lampposts for combating burglaries - Detection of suspicious movements and audio. Rotterdam’s smart lampposts pilot in the Lombardijen district was introduced to test whether street infrastructure could support earlier detection of burglary-related signals. The public-safety problem is that burglary attempts may occur before residents, police or municipal services become aware of suspicious activity, limiting the opportunity for rapid intervention. The Municipality of Rotterdam installed lampposts equipped with sensors able to record suspicious movements and microphones able to detect sounds such as tapping on a window. The implementation combines urban sensor infrastructure, motion detection, audio analysis and alerting logic to identify patterns that may suggest attempted burglary or abnormal activity. Conceptually, the lampposts function as distributed detection points in the neighbourhood, using environmental signals to support situational awareness. The expected impact is faster recognition of possible incidents, improved capacity to deploy security or police resources and stronger deterrence in areas affected by burglary risk. The pilot also illustrates the governance challenges of sensor-based urban safety systems, as microphones and movement detection in public or semi-public spaces require careful safeguards, transparency, proportionality and clear limits on data use.

evidence.quote: The expected impact is faster recognition of possible incidents, improved capacity to deploy security or police resources and stronger deterrence in areas affected by burglary risk.

results.memo: Proceed. Smart lampposts for combating burglaries - Detection of suspicious movements and audio is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Detection of aggression, panic and abnormal behaviour with smart cameras
results.proposal: Detection of aggression, panic and abnormal behaviour with smart cameras. This pilot investigates whether smart-camera analytics can support earlier recognition of aggression, panic and abnormal behaviour in crowded public environments. The operational problem is that incidents in stations, airports, city centres or entertainment districts can escalate quickly if security teams identify them too late. Traditional monitoring relies heavily on human operators observing multiple camera feeds, which can be demanding, inconsistent and slow. ViNotion develops technology that analyses the behaviour of individuals and detects signs of panic, aggression or deviant conduct at an early stage. The implementation uses video analytics and behaviour-recognition models to process visual information from cameras, identify movement or interaction patterns associated with abnormal events, and generate alerts for security or assistance personnel. Conceptually, the system combines computer vision, behavioural classification, anomaly detection and real-time alerting. The expected impact is faster deployment of staff, reduced harm to the public, more efficient incident response and better management of safety risks in large public areas. Its value depends on accuracy, proportionality and careful governance, because behavioural interpretation in public spaces can raise concerns around false positives, surveillance intensity and the treatment of individuals whose conduct is incorrectly flagged.

evidence.quote: The expected impact is faster deployment of staff, reduced harm to the public, more efficient incident response and better management of safety risks in large public areas.

results.memo: Proceed. Detection of aggression, panic and abnormal behaviour with smart cameras is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Agent system
results.proposal: Agent system. ProRail’s agent system is designed to support train traffic controllers when disruptions or delays occur on the Dutch rail network. The operational challenge is that small delays can propagate quickly through interconnected railway services, requiring rapid decisions on routing, prioritisation and recovery measures. Train traffic controllers must assess complex operational conditions under time pressure, balancing passenger disruption, infrastructure capacity and the need to prevent knock-on effects. The agent functions as an autonomous computer programme that operates with defined goals and associated actions, providing advice to controllers on how to respond to delays and reduce further disruption. At a conceptual level, the system can be understood as a decision-support agent that analyses traffic conditions, expected train movements, available infrastructure and possible operational choices, then proposes interventions for human operators to consider. The expected impact is improved punctuality, better use of available rail capacity and more consistent support during disruption management. By assisting controllers rather than replacing them, the system can help preserve human responsibility while improving the speed and quality of operational advice in complex traffic situations.

results.company: 8Ting, business office Work & Income of the municipality of Enschede
results.title: 8TING - Analysis of drivers to keep people in class
results.proposal: 8TING - Analysis of drivers to keep people in class. 8TING was used in Enschede to apply psychology and web technology to support people participating in municipal work-and-income or training pathways. The operational problem is that people may drop out of programmes when support is not aligned with their personal motivation, behaviour, context or barriers. The system seeks to make clear who needs what type of attention by monitoring and adjusting more than 80 factors related to internal drivers. Its implementation uses profiles, behavioural data and contextual indicators to plan automatic or semi-automatic interventions, such as measurements, encouragement and targeted support activities intended to keep people engaged in class or training. Conceptually, the tool combines behavioural profiling, motivation analysis, web-based interaction, programme planning and adaptive support. The expected impact is better retention in training, more personalised support, earlier identification of disengagement risks and improved effectiveness of municipal activation services. At the same time, because the tool analyses behavioural and psychological drivers, careful safeguards are needed around transparency, consent, proportionality and the avoidance of overly deterministic profiling of participants.

results.title: 3D scan underground infrastructure - Prevention damage of critical infrastructure
results.proposal: 3D scan underground infrastructure - Prevention damage of critical infrastructure. Arnhem’s 3D scan project focuses on preventing accidental damage to critical underground infrastructure during construction work. The operational issue is that sewer infrastructure is often located below ground in ways that may be difficult for construction teams to visualise accurately from the surface, creating a risk of costly damage, service disruption and safety hazards. The municipality’s approach combines a precise 3D scan of the main sewer with an application that visualises the sewer’s location above ground. The implementation therefore links geospatial surveying, three-dimensional infrastructure modelling and field-based visualisation, allowing users to understand the position of underground assets before or during works. Conceptually, the system turns hidden sewer infrastructure into a digital and spatially interpretable layer that can be consulted by staff or contractors. The expected impact is fewer accidental strikes, better planning of construction activities, reduced repair costs and improved protection of essential municipal infrastructure. By making underground assets more visible and usable in operational settings, the project supports safer, more data-driven public works management.

results.title: Impulsa Autónomo: Intelligent Platform to Personalise Grants and Subsidies for the Self-Employed in Galicia through AI
results.proposal: Impulsa Autónomo: Intelligent Platform to Personalise Grants and Subsidies for the Self-Employed in Galicia through AI. Impulsa Autónomo was developed by the Xunta de Galicia to simplify how self-employed professionals identify and access grants, subsidies and support measures. The administrative problem is that funding opportunities are often dispersed across different portals, calls and institutional sources, making it difficult for autónomos to understand which schemes are relevant to their activity, situation and eligibility profile. The platform consolidates this information into a single intelligent portal and widget, reducing fragmentation and improving the user journey. Its implementation uses Retrieval-Augmented Generation–based generative AI, connected to official databases, to provide personalised recommendations rather than static lists of subsidies. The system combines official information retrieval, conversational guidance, personalised publication of subsidies, automatic alerts, BI dashboards, satisfaction monitoring and two-way feedback channels. Early results indicate reductions in search time of more than 60% and over 100 hours of integrated specialised advisory services. The expected impact is faster access to relevant support, lower administrative costs through automated responses, more transparent communication of available aid, and stronger interaction between the administration and self-employed workers. Its design also supports interoperability and regulatory alignment, making it a potentially replicable model for digital public services. The Xunta’s official Oficina Virtual do Autónomo is currently online and provides information on support and grants for self-employment.

results.company: Secretary of State of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg (Senatskanzlei)
results.title: KIRA - AI research assistant
results.proposal: KIRA - AI research assistant. Hamburg’s KIRA Research Assistant was developed to help public administration staff manage large volumes of legal and social-services documentation more efficiently. The administrative challenge is that employees handling social benefits requests must interpret complex legislation, locate relevant guidance and provide consistent answers under time pressure. This can slow case processing and create uneven service quality if information is difficult to retrieve. The main stakeholders include the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg, the Senatskanzlei, public administration staff, social-benefit applicants and the InnoTecHH Fonds supporting the project. KIRA operates as an AI-driven knowledge tool and chatbot that retrieves relevant documentation and provides accurate answers to staff queries. Conceptually, it combines document retrieval, question answering, knowledge-base search and conversational access to legal and administrative information. Pilot results indicate strong performance, with an 87% top-k accuracy rate, a usability score of 9.75 out of 10 on the SUS measure, and high satisfaction among staff. The expected impact is shorter research time, more reliable processing of social benefits requests, reduced pressure on employees and more consistent service delivery. By supporting staff rather than replacing their judgement, KIRA improves the administrative knowledge workflow and directly benefits citizens through faster and more dependable handling of requests.

results.title: Identification of flammable dwellings
results.proposal: Identification of flammable dwellings. Estonia’s flammable-dwellings project aims to support fire prevention by identifying residential buildings that may present elevated fire risk. The public-safety problem is that fire services need to prioritise prevention activities, inspections and awareness measures, but risk factors may be distributed across building characteristics, location, past incidents, socio-demographic indicators and other administrative records. The Estonian Fire Department is developing an AI-based solution to detect dwellings that are more likely to be flammable or vulnerable to fire-related incidents. The implementation is described as an AI project under development, likely combining risk indicators, building or housing data, historical fire information and classification models to support prioritisation. Conceptually, the system would produce risk signals for fire-safety professionals, helping them decide where preventive outreach or inspection should be directed. The expected impact is better targeting of prevention resources, earlier identification of risky dwellings, fewer fire incidents and improved protection of residents. Because the system may concern private homes and potentially sensitive household data, its value depends on transparent criteria, appropriate legal basis, careful validation and use as a support tool rather than a fully automated enforcement mechanism.
results.memo: Proceed. Identification of flammable dwellings is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Identification of forest tree species, forest clearing and forest height
results.proposal: Identification of forest tree species, forest clearing and forest height. Estonia’s remote forest monitoring information system was created to improve how forest resources are recorded, monitored and shared in georeferenced form. The forestry-management problem is that national forest assessment requires up-to-date spatial information on tree species, forest clearings, forest height and other structural characteristics, but traditional methods can be slow, fragmented or dependent on manual inspection. The Environmental Agency and KEMIT developed a system that supports the collection and sharing of operational forest information, using remote sensing as the main data source. The implementation is semi-automatic, combining machine-learning algorithms, visual inspection of remote-sensing data and third-party software tools. Inputs include satellite or other remote-sensing data, forest notifications, soil maps and teaching and validation datasets. The outputs include nationwide map layers for key assessment features, such as raster maps identifying dominant tree species. Conceptually, the system integrates geospatial data processing, classification models, human validation and forest-resource mapping. The expected impact is more consistent national forest monitoring, better evidence for forest management, improved detection of changes such as clearing, and more efficient sharing of forest data among competent bodies.
results.memo: Proceed. Identification of forest tree species, forest clearing and forest height is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: INDOOR – usINg Drones fOr Organ tRansportation
results.proposal: INDOOR – usINg Drones fOr Organ tRansportation. INDOOR tests whether drones can improve medical logistics for the transport of organs and biological material in urban areas. The operational challenge is that transplant logistics are extremely time-sensitive, while road-based transport can be affected by traffic, distance between hospital sites and coordination constraints. In Turin, the project demonstrated a drone connection between two hospital facilities, aiming to create a replicable model for faster and safer transport of organs, blood, medicines and biological samples. The experimental flight on 1 October 2024 covered around 500 metres between the CTO helipad and the Molinette Genetics building, crossing an urban section of the city and part of the Po river. The drone, developed by ABzero, used a dedicated smart capsule able to maintain appropriate transport conditions. Its implementation combines automatic drone navigation, protected biomedical transport, capsule-based monitoring and integrated AI for continuous control of temperature, humidity and material integrity. The expected impact is shorter medical transport times, improved reliability of transplant logistics and stronger capacity to manage urgent biological deliveries across dense urban environments. In Piedmont, the potential beneficiaries include transplant patients, with 496 organ transplants reported in 2024, 449 of them in Turin.

results.title: Navigard: the future of road safety on Italian motorways
results.proposal: Navigard: the future of road safety on Italian motorways. Navigard is an advanced motorway safety platform developed by Autostrade per l’Italia and the Italian State Police to improve traffic monitoring, enforcement and incident detection on Italian highways. The operational challenge is that motorway safety depends on rapidly identifying risky behaviours and conditions, including dangerous overtaking by heavy vehicles, wrong-way driving, overloaded vehicles, accidents and abnormal traffic situations. The system integrates radars, high-definition cameras, sensors and centrally processed data to monitor traffic and driver behaviour in real time. Its implementation relies on complex algorithms, advanced sensing infrastructure and a central platform able to communicate with competent authorities. Conceptually, Navigard combines real-time data acquisition, automatic risk detection, vehicle monitoring, enforcement support and road-safety intelligence. The expected impact is faster identification of dangerous events, better coordination between infrastructure operators and police, improved road safety and more proactive management of motorway risks. Autostrade per l’Italia also frames Navigard within a broader “intelligent motorway” strategy involving connected roads, smart service areas, drones, infrastructure monitoring and sensor-enabled maintenance.
results.memo: Proceed. Navigard: the future of road safety on Italian motorways is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Helpme.ai - assisting asylum seekers with AI
results.proposal: Helpme.ai - assisting asylum seekers with AI. Helpme.ai addresses the information barriers faced by refugees and asylum seekers who need reliable, understandable, and context-specific guidance when navigating administrative procedures, social services, accommodation, rights, and local support options in Germany. The operational problem is that relevant information is often dispersed across official websites, service providers, assistance organisations, and informal experiences, making it difficult for users to identify accurate answers in a language they understand. Stakeholders include asylum seekers, refugees, public administrations, social service providers, civil society organisations, and the Helpme.ai platform team. The objective is to provide a centralised, accessible support channel that can respond to user questions and guide people towards relevant resources. The implementation uses Large Language Models to deliver multilingual chatbot functionality, supported by advanced natural language processing and a privacy-conscious configuration. The system draws on an information vector database containing material from official websites, social service providers, assistance resources, and positive experiences shared by previous refugees and asylum seekers. Through retrieval-based techniques, the chatbot can search relevant content, generate contextual answers, and present information through a web interface. The expected impact includes improved access to support, reduced confusion, faster orientation, and better user experience for vulnerable groups. For service providers, the platform can reduce repeated enquiries, scale multilingual assistance, and improve the consistency of information delivered across different user situations.
