results.company: Dutch Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management
results.title: Consultation AI
results.proposal: Consultation AI. ConsultationAI was developed to improve how governments analyse and respond to public consultation input. The administrative problem is that public consultations can generate large volumes of written feedback, making it difficult for authorities to process responses efficiently, identify recurring themes and close the feedback loop with citizens. The tool was created during the OECD Co-Creation Bootcamp in Lisbon, which focused on improving civic participation with emerging technologies. Its implementation uses AI-driven analytics to support the analysis, synthesis and reporting of consultation responses, while preserving a human decision-making role for policymakers and public officials. Conceptually, the system combines text classification, clustering, summarisation, theme extraction and reporting support to help governments understand citizen input at scale. The expected impact is lower analysis costs, faster consultation reporting, better traceability of public feedback and more meaningful civic engagement. By helping authorities respond more effectively to citizens’ contributions, ConsultationAI aligns with the wider CivicAI objective of scaling participation through responsible digital public goods. The OECD bootcamp took place on 26–27 February 2025 in Lisbon under an initiative involving Portugal, Spain and the Netherlands.
results.memo: Proceed. Consultation AI is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: CORRECTIV.Faktenforum - AI to combat disinformation
results.proposal: CORRECTIV.Faktenforum - AI to combat disinformation. CORRECTIV.Faktenforum is Germany’s first fact-checking community, created to involve citizens in identifying, discussing and countering false claims. The societal problem is the rapid spread of disinformation online, which can outpace traditional journalistic fact-checking and undermine public debate. The platform therefore combines community participation, civic technology and professional guidance to scale prebunking and debunking activities. Stakeholders include CORRECTIV, participating citizens, journalists, online communities, civic-tech actors and the wider public exposed to misleading information. The implementation enables people, regardless of journalistic experience, to contribute from anywhere by identifying suspicious claims, collecting evidence, discussing facts and sharing findings under CORRECTIV’s guidance to maintain journalistic standards. AI technologies support the workflow through data analysis, machine learning and generative AI, while human-in-the-loop tools such as CORRECTIV.Checkbot assist community efforts. Conceptually, the system combines collaborative fact-checking, automated claim-support tools, content analysis, community moderation and editorial oversight. The expected impact is increased capacity to detect and respond to false claims, stronger public participation in information integrity and improved resilience against disinformation campaigns. By combining automation with human review and journalistic standards, the project can expand fact-checking capacity without fully outsourcing judgement to machines. Its value lies in linking civic engagement with structured, technology-supported verification processes.
results.memo: Proceed. CORRECTIV.Faktenforum - AI to combat disinformation is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: BeReady - AI to enhance Air Raid Warning System
results.proposal: BeReady - AI to enhance Air Raid Warning System. Estonia’s BeReady initiative strengthens national air-threat detection by involving citizens in the reporting of suspicious aerial activity through a mobile application. The defence and civil-protection challenge is that traditional surveillance systems may benefit from additional distributed observations, especially where rapid reporting and corroboration can support situational awareness. Stakeholders include the Estonian Air Force, citizens using the application, Estonia-based IT companies, national-security authorities and communities relying on timely air-raid warnings. The implementation integrates an AI-powered air-threat identification feature into the BeReady mobile app. Citizens can capture and submit photos of suspicious aerial activities, while the system processes the inputs and consolidates data from multiple users to generate real-time, actionable intelligence for the Air Force. Conceptually, the solution combines mobile crowdsourcing, image analysis, threat classification, data aggregation and operational intelligence workflows. The system was successfully tested during Spring Storm 2024, Estonia’s largest annual joint military exercise. The expected impact is an expansion of surveillance capacity through citizen participation, faster collection of relevant observations and improved support for air-threat assessment. By connecting public reporting with automated analysis, the application can strengthen national security and resilience. Its deployment also requires safeguards to manage false reports, data quality, privacy and the appropriate use of citizen-generated information in defence contexts.

evidence.quote: Its deployment also requires safeguards to manage false reports, data quality, privacy and the appropriate use of citizen-generated information in defence contexts.

results.memo: Proceed. BeReady - AI to enhance Air Raid Warning System is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Bronia.AI - acoustic technology
results.proposal: Bronia.AI - acoustic technology. Bronia.AI is a Bulgarian start-up established in 2024 to develop intelligent acoustic signal-processing technology for complex sound-related applications. The business and technical problem addressed is that many sectors require more advanced tools for managing audio signals, reducing noise, optimising sound quality and extracting usable information from acoustic environments. Stakeholders include Bronia.AI, potential industrial clients, technology partners, sectors using acoustic systems and end users benefiting from improved sound processing. The company’s objective is to build a cutting-edge platform that can transform how sound signals are processed and applied across different business domains. The implementation is centred on AI-powered acoustic technologies, including sound optimisation, noise reduction and advanced signal processing. Conceptually, the platform may combine machine-learning models for audio enhancement, signal separation, pattern recognition, acoustic modelling and real-time processing. Its value lies in addressing situations where conventional audio-processing methods may be insufficient, particularly in complex, noisy or data-rich environments. The expected impact is improved sound quality, more reliable acoustic analysis, new product possibilities and efficiency gains for organisations using audio technologies. As a young company, Bronia.AI’s broader market impact will depend on product maturity, sector adoption and demonstrable performance in real-world settings. Its positioning suggests a focus on innovation in a specialised technological field with potential cross-sector applications.
results.memo: Proceed. Bronia.AI - acoustic technology is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: PERKS - AI for industrial operational efficiency
results.proposal: PERKS - AI for industrial operational efficiency. PERKS, formally “Eliciting and Exploiting Procedural Knowledge in Industry 5.0”, addresses the difficulty industrial organisations face in capturing, managing and reusing procedural knowledge. The operational problem is that know-how related to processes, safety procedures, system configuration and energy-management practices is often tacit, poorly digitalised or difficult for workers to access at the moment of need. The project therefore aims to improve industrial efficiency by developing modular, AI-based tools and methodologies that support the full lifecycle of procedural knowledge, from elicitation and management to access and exploitation. Its implementation combines symbolic and subsymbolic AI, data technologies, knowledge-management methods and worker-centred digital tools. The solutions are tested in three industrial scenarios: a white-goods production plant, computer numerical control machines and a microgrid testbed, each presenting different procedural-knowledge requirements. The expected impact is improved productivity, fewer operational errors, better knowledge transfer, stronger worker safety and more efficient energy-related practices. With an overall budget of €3.55 million, the project contributes to Industry 5.0 by prioritising human-centric, flexible and accepted tools for industrial workers rather than automation alone.

results.title: Automatic Detection of Impervious Surfaces
results.proposal: Automatic Detection of Impervious Surfaces. Recklinghausen developed this software to give municipalities a more precise basis for monitoring sealed surfaces and planning climate-adaptation measures. The environmental problem is that impervious surfaces prevent rainwater infiltration and contribute to urban heat accumulation, increasing risks related to drainage, flooding and heat islands. In Germany, around 45% of settlement and transport areas are sealed, according to the Federal Environmental Agency statistics cited in the source material. Stakeholders include the District of Recklinghausen, participating cities, the Westphalian University of Applied Sciences, land registry and geo-information staff, environment and climate-protection departments and local residents. The implementation uses artificial intelligence, deep learning and computer vision to derive maps of impervious surfaces from aerial images and aggregate the results to different area divisions. The project was carried out over 12 months with funding of just under €100,000 for a research associate at the university’s Department of Electrical Engineering and Applied Natural Sciences. Regular meetings between the university and participating cities defined objectives and monitored progress. The expected impact is more detailed assessment of urban land conditions, improved evidence for drainage control, stronger planning of climate-effective measures and better evaluation of municipal land-management interventions. By automating surface classification, the tool helps local authorities move towards more systematic, data-based environmental and climate planning.

results.title: Enhancing healthcare policy evaluation through AI-driven analytics platform for the National Public Administration
results.proposal: Enhancing healthcare policy evaluation through AI-driven analytics platform for the National Public Administration. Bulgaria’s National Council on Prices and Reimbursement of Medicinal Products initiated this project to improve how public authorities evaluate the real-world value of innovative and high-cost medicines. The policy challenge is that reimbursement decisions require evidence on clinical effectiveness, patient outcomes and budget impact, yet traditional evaluation processes may not fully exploit large-scale health data. Stakeholders include the National Council, healthcare policymakers, patients, clinicians, pharmaceutical companies, reimbursement authorities and public-finance actors responsible for sustainable spending. The objective is to support more informed decisions on whether and how medicines should be reimbursed, while balancing patient access with cost-effectiveness. The implementation uses artificial intelligence and big-data analytics to assess the real-world effectiveness of medicines after they enter clinical use. Conceptually, the platform can combine reimbursement records, treatment data, patient outcomes, medicine-cost information and analytical models to compare expected and observed performance. This enables decision-makers to identify which therapies deliver measurable value in practice and where public expenditure may need adjustment. The expected impact is stronger evidence for reimbursement policy, more efficient allocation of public funds, improved accountability for high-cost therapies and better patient care. By linking analytics with reimbursement governance, the project supports a more data-driven and outcome-oriented healthcare administration.

results.title: AID HCH – Advancing Humanities and Cultural Heritage with Artificial Intelligence
results.proposal: AID HCH – Advancing Humanities and Cultural Heritage with Artificial Intelligence. AID HCH is a Slovenian research initiative designed to advance the use of artificial intelligence in humanities research and cultural-heritage preservation. The strategic problem is that AI has been widely applied in natural sciences, engineering and medicine, but less systematically in humanities and heritage contexts, where digitised sources, archives, objects and conservation data require specialised methods and ethical safeguards. The project aims to establish Slovenia’s first comprehensive data space for humanities and heritage, strengthening cooperation with infrastructures such as E-RIHS, CLARIN and DARIAH. Its implementation combines AI tools, data-space development, digitised cultural and historical sources, predictive conservation methods, heritage storytelling and interdisciplinary frameworks for legal and ethical use. Conceptually, the project creates shared infrastructure and methodologies for analysing cultural-heritage data, supporting research collaboration and improving protection of heritage assets. The expected impact is stronger digital transformation in humanities research, better access to structured heritage data, improved conservation planning and greater international interoperability. The project also has a capacity-building function by connecting universities, libraries, heritage institutions and technical partners around common data and AI standards.

results.title: PLLuM - Polish Large Language Model
results.proposal: PLLuM - Polish Large Language Model. PLLuM, the Polish Large Language Universal Model, was launched to strengthen Poland’s capacity to develop open and responsible language technologies primarily trained on Polish text. The problem it addresses is the limited availability of high-quality, open-access language models designed around the linguistic, cultural and administrative needs of Polish users. The main stakeholders include Wrocław University of Science and Technology, the wider consortium of six Polish institutions, researchers specialising in artificial intelligence and linguistics, public-service providers, developers and citizens, including those at risk of digital exclusion. The project aims to create the first open Polish large language model and a related smart assistant that can support access to public services electronically and in person. The implementation involves large-scale Polish-language model training, dataset preparation, linguistic expertise, evaluation and the development of assistant functionalities aligned with ethical and responsible AI principles. These include attention to data representativeness, transparency and fairness. Conceptually, PLLuM can support natural-language interaction, information retrieval, text generation and user guidance in public-service contexts. Its expected impact is broader access to digital services, improved quality of Polish-language AI applications and reduced dependence on models developed primarily for other languages. By targeting digitally excluded users, the smart assistant also has potential to improve administrative accessibility and inclusion.

results.title: SmartDriveAI - digitising accident reporting
results.proposal: SmartDriveAI - digitising accident reporting. SmartDriveAI was developed to modernise accident reporting in public transport by replacing slow, paper-based processes with real-time digital reporting and predictive safety insights. The operational problem is that conventional accident documentation can delay response, fragment evidence and limit authorities’ ability to identify recurring safety patterns. In Graz, the project involved Graz Linien and Mapular, with drivers equipped to submit GPS-tagged reports, photographs and incident details through a multilingual digital interface. The implementation integrates external data such as weather conditions and uses analytics to generate proactive safety alerts and insights for city authorities and operators. Conceptually, the platform combines mobile accident reporting, geodata technologies, real-time data capture, predictive modelling and safety-dashboard functionality. Pilot results reported by Mapular indicate a 90% reduction in reporting time, 100% data integrity during the pilot phase and identification of three key accident patterns. The expected impact is faster reporting, better data quality, improved resource allocation, stronger road-safety analysis and more proactive prevention of recurring incidents. The initiative also demonstrates how public transport operators can use structured operational data to move from reactive accident handling to evidence-based safety management.

results.proposal: LUCID – Data intelligence for cities and urban logistics. LUCID develops a data-driven platform to improve urban logistics by optimising routes, reducing congestion and improving the use of loading and unloading spaces. The operational challenge is that freight and last-mile logistics contribute significantly to urban congestion, emissions and fuel consumption, while cities and operators often lack a shared evidence base for managing delivery flows. The project integrates public city data and private logistics-operator data to provide real-time insights for both city planners and logistics actors. Its implementation uses advanced analytics and machine-learning methods to support route planning, operational decision-making and more efficient allocation of urban logistics infrastructure. Pilot testing is foreseen in Madrid, Las Rozas and Prague, with logistics operators involved to validate the platform in real-world settings. Conceptually, LUCID combines data integration, predictive analytics, route optimisation, loading-space intelligence and city-dashboard functionality. The expected impact is lower delivery costs, reduced environmental footprint, less congestion and better planning capacity for local authorities. By bringing together public and private data, the project supports a more coordinated model of urban logistics management in rapidly growing cities.

results.title: iTranSys - Public Transport Optimisation Powered by AI
results.proposal: iTranSys - Public Transport Optimisation Powered by AI. Považská Bystrica adopted iTranSys to improve the planning and operation of public transport in a town of around 40,000 residents. The main operational pressure was the combination of driver shortages and inefficient scheduling, which can increase costs, reduce service reliability and negatively affect passenger satisfaction. The stakeholders include the City of Považská Bystrica, public transport operators, drivers, passengers, municipal planners and residents who rely on local mobility services. The objective is to make route and timetable planning more efficient while maintaining or improving service quality. The implementation uses an AI-powered optimisation tool that automates aspects of public transport planning, including timetable generation and route scheduling. Conceptually, the system can analyse passenger demand, operational constraints, available drivers, route structures and service-frequency requirements to generate more efficient transport plans. By supporting automated scenario analysis and schedule optimisation, it reduces dependence on manual planning and allows the municipality to respond more flexibly to capacity constraints. The reported impact includes significant annual financial savings, improved passenger satisfaction and reduced per capita CO₂ emissions. These results suggest that the tool delivers both operational and environmental value by using resources more efficiently, improving service attractiveness and supporting more sustainable urban mobility.

The regional problem is that SMEs across the Danube area face uneven digital maturity, labour shortages, cost pressures, industrial transformation and limited internal capacity to adopt advanced technologies. The project therefore focuses on knowledge transfer, skills development and targeted transnational interventions in sectors such as manufacturing, agrofood, healthcare and sustainable energy. The implementation is structured as an Interreg Danube Region project that equips stakeholders and SMEs with AI-related knowledge, supports pilot solutions and builds on previous regional innovation results. Conceptually, the initiative combines capacity building, technology transfer, pilot experimentation, stakeholder networking and sector-specific AI adoption support. The expected impact is improved SME competitiveness, stronger readiness for Industry 5.0, more balanced regional development and better alignment between AI adoption and economic, environmental and social sustainability. By working across the Danube Region, BrAIn addresses the fact that AI capability gaps are not only technological, but also organisational, skills-based and territorial.

results.title: LifeSaver - enhancing medical services
results.proposal: LifeSaver - enhancing medical services. The operational challenge is that emergency medical systems must respond quickly under uncertain and changing demand, while ensuring that ambulances, staff, dispatch arrangements and service areas are organised effectively. The project focuses on modernising life-saving assistance by using predictive analytics, real-time monitoring and transparent system insights to support faster and more effective emergency responses. The implementation includes the LifeSaver Intelligence Platform and a comprehensive review of Estonia’s emergency medical system by international experts. The platform supports analysis of response patterns, demand forecasting, resource optimisation and identification of improvement projects. The LifeSaver programme identified ten potential innovation projects, from which the Estonian government selected five for future implementation. Conceptually, the initiative combines operational EMS data, predictive modelling, service-area analysis, monitoring dashboards and strategic planning for emergency care. The expected impact is better allocation of emergency resources, faster response capability, improved patient outcomes and stronger public-sector innovation capacity. Estonia was the first country to work with International SOS and Airbus Helicopters on the LifeSaver programme.

results.title: Smart Public Lighting in City of Sveta Nedelja (Croatia)
results.proposal: Smart Public Lighting in City of Sveta Nedelja (Croatia). The Sveta Nedelja smart public lighting pilot tested how existing public lighting infrastructure could become a platform for energy management, environmental monitoring and urban sensing. The municipal problem is that public lighting is a major operational asset, but conventional lighting systems offer limited remote control, monitoring or capacity to generate wider city data. The pilot aimed to improve energy efficiency, quality of life, public safety and reduction of light pollution. The implementation, developed with HT Group, connected 80 control and communication modules to existing lighting poles. The solution can operate across several network technologies, including 3G, 4G, 5G and NB-IoT, and is applicable to different types of public lighting. The smart poles enabled remote wireless monitoring and control of lamps, measurement of energy indicators, and additional sensing functions such as temperature, humidity, pressure, UV radiation, air quality, pedestrian passage and traffic noise. Conceptually, the system combines IoT connectivity, smart lighting control, environmental sensing, remote monitoring and city-data collection. The expected impact is reduced energy use, better maintenance insight, improved environmental monitoring and a foundation for broader Smart City services using existing infrastructure.

BgGPT is intended to make these materials easier to understand and use. The implementation has two main functions. Conceptually, the system combines Bulgarian-language generative AI, document summarisation, topic indexing, conversational interaction and service-routing functions. The expected impact is improved transparency of local-government decisions, easier access to administrative services, better-informed residents and reduced pressure on staff handling repetitive information requests. By applying a national-language model in a municipal setting, the pilot also demonstrates how locally developed AI can be adapted to public-service delivery.

results.proposal: AI-enabled speech-to-text in the health and elderly area. Denmark’s speech-to-text initiative aims to reduce the documentation burden for staff working in health, home care and elderly services. The operational problem is that employees spend substantial time producing care records and placing documentation correctly in municipal IT systems, which can reduce time available for direct citizen care. The initiative focuses on developing and testing an AI-supported solution that converts audio recordings into medical-record text and helps staff decide where the generated content should be placed in the municipal system. It builds partly on experience from Thisted Municipality and will involve Copenhagen, Aarhus, Aalborg and other municipalities. Conceptually, the system combines speech recognition, natural language processing, documentation assistance and workflow guidance for municipal care records. The expected impact is faster record creation, improved documentation quality, less administrative pressure on care staff and more consistent placement of information in municipal systems. The initiative receives DKK 8.5 million in funding and forms part of Denmark’s wider effort to scale practical AI solutions across municipalities. A related Danish TALT speech-recognition project has reportedly shown time savings and is ready for national roll-out, suggesting that the policy area is moving from testing towards broader implementation.

results.title: AI4POL: Using Artificial Intelligence to Support Regulators & Policy Makers
results.proposal: AI4POL: Using Artificial Intelligence to Support Regulators & Policy Makers. Its implementation combines AI tools, policy research, human-centred analysis and stakeholder engagement. AI systems may help summarise complex legal or contractual information in simpler language, while the broader project develops tools, insights and frameworks aligned with European values, human rights and citizens’ needs. The consortium is led by Tilburg University and includes TUM and other research partners, with an advisory board involving regulators, policymakers, consumer-protection bodies, civil-society organisations and AI firms. The expected impact is stronger evidence for regulation, better consumer understanding and more effective oversight of AI and digital markets.

results.title: GPT@JRC: Generative AI Tool to support Science for Policy at JRC
results.proposal: GPT@JRC: Generative AI Tool to support Science for Policy at JRC. GPT@JRC was developed inside the European Commission’s Joint Research Centre to give staff a secure environment for experimenting with large language models in science-for-policy work. The operational challenge is that JRC staff routinely handle complex knowledge tasks, including summarising evidence, translating material, drafting briefings, proofreading, classification, sentiment analysis and preparing analytical inputs for policy processes. Using external generative tools can create confidentiality and compliance risks, particularly where internal documents or sensitive policy material are involved. GPT@JRC therefore provides controlled access to language-model capabilities within a secure platform. The implementation allows JRC staff to use LLMs for day-to-day productivity tasks and to test how generative functions can be embedded into existing tools and workflows through automated access and processing. Conceptually, the platform combines secure model access, experimentation facilities, internal governance, prompt-based interaction and potential integration with other JRC systems. The expected impact is improved productivity, faster document handling, enhanced quality of drafts and summaries, and better understanding of how generative AI can support science-for-policy work. It also served as an important precursor to broader Commission-level tools, helping the institution test safe adoption patterns before wider deployment.

results.title: GPT@EC: Generative AI Tool to support EC administrative task
results.proposal: GPT@EC: Generative AI Tool to support EC administrative task. GPT@EC is the European Commission’s secure general-purpose generative AI tool for supporting administrative and knowledge tasks across Commission departments and executive agencies. The organisational challenge is that staff regularly need to draft texts, summarise documents, develop code and process internal information, but using external third-party tools can create risks for confidentiality and compliance. GPT@EC was developed by DG DIGIT as an internal corporate tool adapted to the Commission context, allowing staff to process internal Commission information without sharing it with external parties. The implementation provides access to several large language models, including models suitable for different tasks and sensitivity levels, with the possibility of using open-source and sovereign models. Conceptually, the tool combines secure model access, internal governance rules, compliance controls and task-oriented generative functions such as drafting, summarisation and coding assistance. The expected impact is improved productivity, greater creativity, reduced dependency on unmanaged external tools and safer experimentation with generative AI in the EU administration. The Commission presents the roll-out as aligned with its AI@EC approach for lawful, safe and trustworthy AI, with staff feedback used to improve the tool.

evidence.quote: The organisational challenge is that staff regularly need to draft texts, summarise documents, develop code and process internal information, but using external third-party tools can create risks for confidentiality and compliance.

results.memo: Proceed. GPT@EC: Generative AI Tool to support EC administrative task is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Curve Real Time - Monitoring TV Audience
results.proposal: Curve Real Time - Monitoring TV Audience. Curve Real Time is part of RAI’s broader strategy to become a more data-driven public broadcasting organisation. The operational problem is that broadcasters need timely insight into audience reactions, content performance and viewer behaviour in order to improve programming, personalise services and manage increasingly complex media environments. The use case focuses on tracking TV audiences and analysing real-time reactions to broadcast content, while RAI’s wider AI agenda includes data governance, production-process automation, metadata enrichment, recommendation engines and entity recognition. The implementation uses descriptive, predictive and generative AI methods to process audience-related data and support both content creation and content consumption. Conceptually, Curve Real Time combines real-time audience monitoring, reaction analysis, data analytics and decision-support dashboards for editorial and operational teams. The expected impact is better understanding of audience engagement, more responsive content strategies, improved operational efficiency and stronger user-centricity in public broadcasting. The available public material confirms that RAI presented AI-supported processes, including this type of use case, in the context of the Politecnico di Milano Artificial Intelligence Observatory, but I did not find detailed evidence of the current operational maturity of Curve Real Time specifically.
results.memo: Proceed. Curve Real Time - Monitoring TV Audience is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Elsa - AI-assisted spreading decisions
results.proposal: Elsa - AI-assisted spreading decisions. Elsa addresses the need for more consistent winter-service decisions across Flemish road districts. The Agency for Roads and Traffic is responsible for controlling slippery road conditions on the roads it manages, but spreading decisions depend on local interpretation of real-time measurements, weather forecasts and staff experience. Because expertise varies across districts and road networks do not stop at administrative boundaries, inconsistent spreading policies can affect safety, environmental impact and operational efficiency. Elsa is intended to support district employees in deciding whether, when and how to spread de-icing material. The implementation combines physical rules and machine-learning techniques with data from AWV’s smoothness measurement system, which already integrates real-time measurements from monitoring points and stations with forecasts from the Royal Meteorological Institute. Conceptually, the system assesses road and weather conditions, estimates the risk of slipperiness and recommends the type of spreading material, quantity and timing needed to keep roads ice-free. The expected impact is more uniform decision-making, better road safety, reduced unnecessary salt use, lower environmental burden and stronger support for staff during winter operations.
results.memo: Proceed. Elsa - AI-assisted spreading decisions is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Smart regulation - Using Artificial Intelligence to train computers to interpret regulation
results.proposal: Smart regulation - Using Artificial Intelligence to train computers to interpret regulation. Smart Regulation responds to the difficulty of navigating fragmented, divergent and incoherent regulatory information. Regulations are essential for citizens, administrations, businesses and software systems, yet relevant provisions are often spread across basic laws, amendments, additions and corrections, making it hard to retrieve the exact rule that applies to a given situation. The Flemish Domestic Governance Agency and Information Flanders aim to create an engine that can process unstructured legal and regulatory sources and provide users with targeted data and insights according to their needs. The implementation uses artificial intelligence to train computer systems to interpret regulation, extract relevant information and make it available for specific target groups, including people, applications and machines. Conceptually, the solution combines natural language processing, legal text mining, semantic structuring, regulatory knowledge extraction and subscription-based access to structured outputs. The expected impact is faster access to applicable rules, reduced information silos, better reuse of regulatory data and stronger support for digital public services that depend on machine-readable legislation. By turning complex legal texts into more structured and queryable information, the project can improve administrative efficiency and regulatory transparency.
results.memo: Proceed. Smart regulation - Using Artificial Intelligence to train computers to interpret regulation is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: CATE - Continuous Auditing based on Technological Evolution and Data Mining
results.proposal: CATE - Continuous Auditing based on Technological Evolution and Data Mining. CATE was developed to rethink how the Flemish Audit Authority audits projects subsidised through European Structural Funds and Flemish co-financing. The operational problem is that a significant share of audits must be outsourced, often at high cost and with uneven added value, while the Flemish Audit Authority still needs to spend substantial time on quality control when external auditors lack sufficient expertise in public procurement or state aid. The project aims to redesign the audit process methodologically and technologically so that audits can provide greater assurance, lower costs, shorter turnaround times, higher added value and reduced loss of European resources. The implementation is based on continuous auditing, data mining and technological evolution, with an innovation partnership structured in phases from proof of concept to increasingly mature functionality. Conceptually, the system uses data-driven risk analysis, audit-process automation, analytical models and continuous monitoring of subsidised projects to identify where audit attention is most needed. The expected impact is a more efficient and targeted audit function, stronger detection of irregularities, better use of audit capacity and improved protection of public funds.
results.memo: Proceed. CATE - Continuous Auditing based on Technological Evolution and Data Mining is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: DigiPolis, IT provider for the City of Antwerp
results.title: ALTRUIS - Alternative Use of Imaging Systems through Artificial Intelligence
results.proposal: ALTRUIS - Alternative Use of Imaging Systems through Artificial Intelligence. ALTRUIS was launched to help Antwerp respond to severe mobility pressures by extracting useful traffic and mobility insights from existing camera footage. The operational context was particularly challenging because Antwerp already experienced heavy congestion, while major infrastructure works placed additional pressure on mobility and quality of life. Digipolis sought to turn street images, which have limited value in raw form, into mobility intelligence for the city, especially in the Smart Zone. The implementation explored alternative use of imaging systems through artificial intelligence, initially focusing on anonymisation of visual material and then on image recognition and algorithms for mobility insights. The procurement later combined these phases into a single assignment and shifted the technological scope towards edge AI, meaning that interpretation would occur closer to the camera instead of relying only on cloud or on-premise GPU processing. The expected impact was better understanding of movement patterns, more responsive mobility management and support for smart-city traffic solutions. The case also highlights the importance of anonymisation, privacy-by-design and careful governance when repurposing urban camera infrastructure.
results.memo: Proceed. ALTRUIS - Alternative Use of Imaging Systems through Artificial Intelligence is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Henchman - contract drafing with AI support
results.proposal: Henchman - contract drafing with AI support. Henchman supports legal professionals in drafting and improving contract clauses by extending the range of available drafting options during contract preparation. The practical challenge in legal work is that lawyers frequently need to adapt existing clauses to specific transactional contexts, client preferences or drafting conventions, while maintaining consistency, precision and speed. The platform is therefore relevant to law firms, in-house legal teams, contract managers and clients relying on efficient document production. Its objective is to make contract drafting more agile by helping users refine language, adjust wording and introduce clause-level variations without starting from scratch. The implementation uses GPT-3.5 to assist with targeted drafting operations, such as changing a clause from singular to plural or adding a new element to an existing provision. Conceptually, the system combines large language model functionality with contract-drafting workflows, allowing users to generate or modify text within a controlled legal-document environment. The expected impact is faster clause adaptation, reduced repetitive editing, improved consistency across contract drafts and greater productivity for legal teams. By supporting incremental drafting rather than replacing legal judgement, the tool can help professionals focus on negotiation strategy, legal risk and client-specific tailoring. Its value depends on appropriate human review, since AI-generated legal text must be checked for accuracy, enforceability and alignment with the intended contractual position.

results.title: Predictice - Summaries of Court Decisions
results.proposal: Predictice - Summaries of Court Decisions. Predictice uses generative language technology to make legal research more efficient by producing automatic summaries of court decisions. The practical challenge for legal professionals is that judicial documents can be long, technical and time-consuming to read, while some decisions may prove irrelevant only after several minutes of review. Predictice provides access to a large legal corpus of around 26 million documents, including court decisions, and aims to help users assess relevance more quickly. The implementation applies GPT-3 and ChatGPT-style language-model capabilities to the task of document synthesis. Rather than asking the model to produce legal advice, the tool focuses on summarising existing decisions, a use case considered more reliable by the Predictice team than generating autonomous legal answers. Conceptually, the system combines large-scale legal-document retrieval, generative summarisation, natural language processing and user-facing legal search functions. The expected impact is faster review of case law, reduced time spent on irrelevant documents, improved productivity for lawyers and legal researchers, and easier navigation of large legal databases. By providing concise summaries of lengthy decisions, Predictice can support legal professionals in prioritising which documents deserve closer reading. However, because legal interpretation remains sensitive, summaries should be treated as decision-support outputs and checked against the original court text.

results.company: Flemish Agency for Persons with Disabilities
results.title: Remote interpreting services - Communicating in Flemish sign language
results.proposal: Remote interpreting services - Communicating in Flemish sign language. The remote interpreting services project aims to improve communication between deaf and hearing people in Flanders by making Flemish Sign Language interpretation available more flexibly and consistently. The service problem is that several comparable services currently operate side by side, creating fragmentation and confusion for users, while existing technical and organisational arrangements do not yet ensure access anytime and anywhere. The project seeks to harmonise and scale remote interpreting so that deaf users can contact everyone by telephone, including emergency services, and can also be contacted by others such as colleagues or doctors in their preferred communication mode. Implementation requires innovation in hardware, software, service organisation, privacy protection and interoperability between existing systems. Conceptually, the solution combines video-remote interpreting, user authentication, service-routing, privacy safeguards and platform harmonisation. The expected impact is improved accessibility, lower organisational costs through consolidation, greater use of remote interpreting and stronger inclusion of deaf users in public, professional and personal communication. Its public value lies in treating language accessibility as an essential service rather than a fragmented accommodation.

results.company: Athens university of economics and business
results.title: LEGAL-BERT: The Muppets straight out of Law School
results.proposal: LEGAL-BERT: The Muppets straight out of Law School. LEGAL-BERT was developed to improve the application of transformer-based language models to legal-domain tasks, where general-purpose models may not perform optimally because of specialised vocabulary, reasoning patterns and document structures. The research problem is that BERT had achieved strong results across many natural language processing tasks, but guidance on how to adapt it to specialised domains had not been sufficiently tested for legal materials. The project therefore evaluates different strategies for applying BERT to legal downstream tasks, including using the original model directly, adapting it through additional pre-training on legal corpora and pre-training models from scratch on domain-specific legal data. The implementation also explores a broader hyper-parameter search space for fine-tuning, recognising that standard configurations may not generalise well to law. The resulting LEGAL-BERT family of models is intended to support legal NLP research, computational law and legal technology applications. Conceptually, the project combines domain-specific pre-training, transformer architectures, legal corpora and systematic evaluation across datasets. Its expected impact is improved model performance for legal text classification, retrieval and analysis, as well as more reliable methodological guidance for researchers and developers working in specialised domains. By releasing LEGAL-BERT, the project provides reusable infrastructure for legal AI experimentation and application development.
results.memo: Proceed. LEGAL-BERT: The Muppets straight out of Law School is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Legislab - monitoring legislative quality with GenAI
results.proposal: Legislab - monitoring legislative quality with GenAI. Legislab is designed to support analysis of the Italian legislative system and assist parliamentary offices in monitoring legal quality. The institutional problem is that new legislative proposals must be assessed against a large and continuously evolving corpus of laws, from the Constitution onwards, making it difficult to identify relevant precedents, overlaps, inconsistencies or references. The project, developed by the Politecnico di Milano and the Istituto Einaudi, is intended for the offices of the Chamber of Deputies and combines a database of Italian laws with analytical and generative functions. Its implementation allows users to input a topic or draft title and receive relevant articles and laws that may need to be considered. The system is deliberately constrained to reduce hallucination risks: it relies on existing legal data, objective information and linguistic metrics from scientific literature rather than generating free-form legal text. The expected impact is stronger legislative quality monitoring, faster identification of relevant legal sources and better support for expert legislative drafting, while preserving the role of legal professionals and parliamentarians in writing the law.
results.memo: Proceed. Legislab - monitoring legislative quality with GenAI is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Supporting Civil Servant with Generative AI
results.proposal: Supporting Civil Servant with Generative AI. France’s experiment on generative artificial intelligence in public services was launched to assess how such tools could support civil servants in responding to users more efficiently. The administrative problem is that public agents handle large numbers of online opinions, comments and procedural interactions, many of which require clear written replies but can be repetitive and time-consuming. The initiative involved 1,000 volunteer agents equipped with a tool to help draft responses to users during online procedures, while preserving a human-in-the-loop model: agents supervise, modify and approve responses before they are sent. The experiment is led by the Interministerial Directorate for Public Transformation and the Interministerial Digital Directorate, with a solution provided by Allobrain. The system uses generative language technology to propose draft responses based on anonymised data, meaning confidentiality is intended to be preserved. The model supports response writing rather than replacing the public official, and the approach is framed as a way to save time on specific tasks while strengthening human contact between public services and citizens. The planned extension to France services counters would broaden the support to agents assisting users face to face. The expected impact is faster response preparation, reduced administrative burden, improved consistency in written replies and more time for personalised support where human judgement is most valuable.

results.memo: Proceed. Supporting Civil Servant with Generative AI is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: ‘Democratic Engagement through a Public Chatbot’ (DepuChat) - How GenAI can increase transparency
results.proposal: ‘Democratic Engagement through a Public Chatbot’ (DepuChat) - How GenAI can increase transparency. DepuChat proposes a public chatbot to make information on the Italian Chamber of Deputies more accessible, usable and transparent for citizens. The democratic problem is that parliamentary information is often technically complex, dispersed across institutional documents and difficult for non-specialist users to interpret. The project, developed by the IDEAS Research Centre at Roma Tre University in collaboration with the Department of Legal Sciences at the University of Florence, aims to bring citizens closer to institutions by allowing them to query information on the Chamber, its bodies and procedures, individual MPs, and political positions expressed by MPs and the Government. The implementation uses generative AI to create a conversational and potentially graphical interface over parliamentary data. Conceptually, the system combines institutional data retrieval, natural-language interaction, summarisation and visual presentation to help users explore parliamentary activity more easily. The expected impact is improved transparency, broader civic access to legislative information and stronger democratic engagement. The project was announced in July 2024 as a winner of the Chamber of Deputies’ call for ideas, so its current form appears to be a selected proposal or prototype rather than a fully operational public service.

results.company: Roads and Traffic Agency of the Flemish Government
results.title: Creation and management of semantic OTL relationships
results.proposal: Creation and management of semantic OTL relationships. The Flemish Roads and Traffic Agency’s semantic OTL project supports its transition towards data-driven infrastructure management. The operational problem is that road infrastructure assets, including roads, cycle paths, tunnels, bridges and related equipment, generate information across design, construction, maintenance and replacement phases, but this information must be standardised to remain usable throughout the asset lifecycle. The project aims to develop a tool for creating and managing semantic relationships in the Object Type Library, allowing asset data to be collected once, structured consistently and exchanged across models, databases and software systems. Its implementation builds on BIM and semantic data-management methods, defining relationships between infrastructure object types so that asset information can be shared uniformly among project partners. The expected impact is improved data quality, more efficient collaboration, reduced duplication and stronger lifecycle management of public infrastructure. By embedding semantic standards into asset management, AWV can strengthen interoperability and make infrastructure information more reliable for planning, maintenance and operational decisions.
results.memo: Proceed. Creation and management of semantic OTL relationships is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: FinGPT-3 - The open Finnish LLM
results.proposal: FinGPT-3 - The open Finnish LLM. FinGPT-3 was created to expand the availability of generative language models for Finnish, a language that is less represented than English in many large-scale model ecosystems. The research challenge is to build models that can handle Finnish linguistic structures effectively and support applications in language technology, digital linguistics and natural language processing. The project is led by the TurkuNLP Group at the University of Turku, whose work spans corpus annotation, analysis, machine learning theory and applied language technologies. The National Library of Finland collaborated on the model development, and the project received support from the European Union’s Horizon Europe research and innovation programme under grant agreement No 101070350. In 2023, the team trained GPT-3-like generative models for Finnish. The implementation involves assembling and processing Finnish-language corpora, training large generative architectures, evaluating linguistic performance and making model outputs available for research or downstream application. Conceptually, FinGPT-3 provides foundational language-model capacity that can support Finnish text generation, summarisation, classification, information extraction and other NLP tasks. The expected impact is stronger technological coverage for Finnish, improved resources for researchers and developers, and reduced dependence on multilingual systems that may underperform for smaller language communities. By combining university expertise, national library resources and EU funding, the project contributes to Europe’s capacity for language-specific AI development.
results.memo: Proceed. FinGPT-3 - The open Finnish LLM is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: GenAI-based chatbot to help the public access services on official websites
results.proposal: GenAI-based chatbot to help the public access services on official websites. Ireland’s GenAI chatbot initiative was designed to test how generative AI could help members of the public find information on government supports and services through official digital channels. The administrative problem is that citizens and businesses often need to navigate multiple public websites, schemes and eligibility pages, which can create friction and increase demand for direct assistance. The initial project aimed to deliver a “chat agent” able to provide information on business supports offered by the Government, with pilot funding from Microsoft and delivery in collaboration with the Office of the Government Chief Information Officer. Conceptually, the service uses generative AI to interpret user questions, retrieve relevant official content and provide conversational answers, while requiring safeguards around accuracy, transparency, human oversight and data protection. The expected impact is easier access to public information, reduced search burden for users, and better scalability for high-volume enquiries. A related public-facing Irish implementation is now visible through AskCI, an AI-powered chatbot on Citizens Information that uses generative AI to answer questions based on citizensinformation.ie content and was developed with the OGCIO.

results.company: POLITEHNICA Bucharest, the University of Bucharest and the Institute of Logic and Data Science
results.title: OpenLLM-Ro - The first LLM in Romanian language
results.proposal: OpenLLM-Ro - The first LLM in Romanian language. OpenLLM-Ro was developed to address the limited availability of large language models specifically trained for Romanian, a gap that can constrain the quality of digital services, research tools and language technologies for Romanian-speaking users. The initiative brings together academic actors seeking to strengthen national language-technology capacity and provide an open model that can be further refined for different applications. The main stakeholders include POLITEHNICA Bucharest, the University of Bucharest, the Institute of Logic and Data Science, researchers working pro bono, developers, public or private organisations that may reuse the model, and Romanian-speaking end users. Starting in the second half of 2023, the research team worked on developing and training the model, with POLITEHNICA Bucharest also providing the computing power needed for training. The implementation involves large-language-model development, corpus preparation, training infrastructure, model evaluation and ongoing fine-tuning. Conceptually, the project creates a foundational Romanian-language model that can support downstream tasks such as text generation, summarisation, question answering, classification or conversational interfaces. Its expected impact is to reduce dependence on models optimised primarily for larger languages, improve Romanian-language processing quality, and support innovation in education, administration, business and research. The model’s online availability and continued fine-tuning indicate an evolving resource for the Romanian digital ecosystem.

results.title: Qra - The first  Polish open-source LLM
results.proposal: Qra - The first  Polish open-source LLM. Qra was developed to provide a strong Polish-language generative model trained specifically on Polish text, responding to the limited availability of open large language models optimised for Polish. The research and technology problem is that models primarily trained on English or multilingual corpora may underperform in Polish-language understanding, question answering and coherent text generation. Gdańsk University of Technology and the AI Lab at the National Information Processing Institute developed Polish generative neural language models using approximately a terabyte of Polish-language data. The implementation involved training open-source models on Polish text, with the Hugging Face model card noting that published versions were based on Llama 2 checkpoints and further trained on a cleaned, filtered and deduplicated Polish corpus of about 90 billion tokens. The models were trained using infrastructure from the PG TASK Computing Centre with 21 Nvidia A100 cards. The expected impact is improved Polish-language AI capacity, broader reuse by researchers and developers, and reduced reliance on foreign-language models for Polish applications. Because the models are open-source, users can download and adapt them to specific domains or tasks, including question answering and text generation.

results.title: Amsterdam: Generating sustainable materials with Generative AI
results.proposal: Amsterdam: Generating sustainable materials with Generative AI. The University of Amsterdam’s AI4SMM initiative applies artificial intelligence to the design of sustainable molecules and materials, shifting generative techniques from language to chemistry and materials science. The research challenge is that developing new materials for energy storage, industry, food and plastics can be slow, costly and experimentally intensive, while sustainability transitions require faster discovery of safer and lower-impact alternatives. The initiative is led by Bernd Ensing at the Faculty of Science and connects expertise in computer science, chemistry, ecology, physics and biology. The implementation uses machine-learning and generative approaches to model molecules and materials, replacing word-based associations with relationships between molecular structures and properties. Initial projects focus on areas such as energy-storage salts, sustainable steel, safe plastic and new plant proteins. Conceptually, the approach combines molecular data, computational chemistry, generative modelling, property prediction and experimental validation to propose promising candidates for further study. The expected impact is faster discovery of sustainable materials, better targeting of laboratory work and stronger integration between AI and sustainability research. By applying generative methods to molecules rather than text, the initiative can support innovation in sectors where material performance and environmental impact are central.

results.title: Open Spanish LLM model in collaboration with IBM
results.proposal: Open Spanish LLM model in collaboration with IBM. The Spanish Government and IBM collaboration aims to develop open-source foundation models in Spanish and Spain’s co-official languages, including Catalan, Basque, Galician and Valencian. The strategic challenge is that Spanish and Iberian-language communities require generative AI systems that reflect their linguistic diversity, cultural context and public-interest requirements, rather than relying mainly on models optimised for English. The initiative was launched through a Memorandum of Understanding discussed in April 2024 between the Spanish Government and IBM. The implementation draws on IBM’s open-source AI framework and AI stack, with an emphasis on ethical, sustainable and community-driven model development. Conceptually, the project combines large and small language models, open-source development, AI supercomputing, multilingual training and community contribution mechanisms. The expected impact is stronger national and international Spanish-language AI capacity, improved access to generative AI tools for nearly 500 million Spanish speakers, and better support for co-official languages in digital services and innovation. The collaboration also aims to advance responsible generative AI technologies in Spain and support practical deployment in public and private contexts.

results.title: ALEIA digital assistant - Generative AI at the Île-de-France Regional Council
results.proposal: ALEIA digital assistant - Generative AI at the Île-de-France Regional Council. The ALEIA digital assistant responds to the difficulty citizens face when trying to identify the regional aid schemes for which they may be eligible. Île-de-France has around 350 aid schemes, and this breadth of provision can make access confusing for residents, associations or other potential beneficiaries. The Regional Council therefore sought a tool that could guide users through the available support landscape and provide clear answers based on the region’s own documentation. Developed by the start-up Aleia, the solution combines a search engine and a conversational agent. It uses the French Mistral language model to formulate responses grounded in the region’s corpus of documents, while data are hosted in France and answers are continuously improved. The system is also designed to recognise when a user asks about support that falls outside the region’s responsibilities and to respond negatively rather than providing irrelevant guidance. Conceptually, the assistant combines document retrieval, generative language modelling, conversational interaction, controlled knowledge sources and French-hosted data infrastructure. The expected impact is simpler access to regional support, reduced user confusion, more efficient routing towards relevant schemes and less pressure on administrative staff handling repetitive eligibility questions. By linking conversational access with an official documentary corpus, the system can improve transparency and make regional aid more navigable.

results.title: F13, the LLM used by the State of Baden-Württemberg in collaboration with Aleph Alpha
results.proposal: F13, the LLM used by the State of Baden-Württemberg in collaboration with Aleph Alpha. Baden-Württemberg introduced F13 to support employees of the state administration in drafting, summarising and processing textual information more efficiently. The administrative challenge is that civil servants work with large volumes of documents, cabinet templates, notes and research material, which can slow workflows and reduce time available for substantive policy or service tasks. F13 is designed to relieve staff by providing text assistance functions tailored to administrative routines. The system was developed primarily by the Heidelberg-based company Aleph Alpha and presented by the Innovation Lab Baden-Württemberg, InnoLab_bw. Its implementation uses generative language-model technology to support several functions: a summary tool with selectable compression levels for pasted texts, a Cabinet Template Note function that converts uploaded cabinet templates into summarised note templates, a research assistant for preparing large volumes of information, and the “Vermerkomat”, which creates comprehensive flow text. At a conceptual level, F13 combines large language models, document processing, summarisation, text generation and workflow-oriented user interfaces within the state administration network. The expected impact is faster preparation of administrative documents, reduced repetitive writing work, improved handling of information-intensive tasks and more consistent support for employees. Since 2024, all staff with access to the state administration network can use F13, indicating a move beyond experimentation into full administrative deployment.

results.title: GENAI4LEX-B
results.proposal: GENAI4LEX-B. GENAI4LEX-B was developed to support parliamentary work in Italy by using generative AI for the preparation of legislative initiative acts. The institutional problem is that parliamentarians and parliamentary staff must navigate complex regulatory sources, amendments, policy objectives and legislative drafting requirements under time and information constraints. The project won the “Supporting the preparation of initiative acts” area in a call promoted by the Italian Chamber of Deputies, which selected three winning projects from 28 proposals. Its three prototypes are designed to help users explore regulatory sources, simplify and summarise amendments, and measure the alignment between bills and the policies they intend to pursue. The implementation combines generative AI, legal informatics, regulatory-source analysis, summarisation and legislative-support functions. The consortium is coordinated by Alma Mater Studiorum – University of Bologna / ALMA-AI and includes CNR-Igsg with Aptus.AI, Luiss Guido Carli University with Asimov AI, the University of Turin and the University of Verona. The expected impact is more efficient legislative preparation, improved access to regulatory context, clearer amendment analysis and stronger evidence on whether proposed bills match policy goals. Its value depends on careful human oversight and constitutional safeguards in parliamentary processes.

results.title: TrustLLM - Democratise trustworthy and efficient LLM technology for Europe
results.proposal: TrustLLM - Democratise trustworthy and efficient LLM technology for Europe. TrustLLM is a Horizon Europe project designed to develop open, trustworthy and sustainable large language models for European languages, with an initial focus on Germanic languages and underrepresented linguistic communities. The strategic problem is that Europe needs language-model infrastructure that is transparent, reliable, energy-conscious and less dependent on closed non-European systems. Coordinated by Linköping University, the project brings together partners across Europe with expertise in natural language processing, high-performance computing, trustworthy AI, model evaluation and downstream deployment. The implementation will develop large language models trained on substantial multilingual European text resources, while addressing reliability, bias, hallucination, sustainability and accessibility. Conceptually, the project combines large-scale model training, exascale computing, trustworthiness research, open model development and ecosystem-building for modular and extensible European LLMs. The expected impact is stronger European capacity in language technologies, improved human-machine interaction across applications, wider access to open models and better support for industry, public services and research. TrustLLM is explicitly positioned as a response to the need for reliable generative models and mitigation of risks such as hallucinations and bias.

results.title: MitosLOD: Exporting Linked Open Data from the Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services
results.proposal: MitosLOD: Exporting Linked Open Data from the Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services. MitosLOD enhances the Greek National Registry of Administrative Public Services by making information on public services easier to search, retrieve and understand. The operational issue is that administrative service catalogues can be difficult for citizens, businesses and public officials to navigate when information is structured around formal terminology rather than the way users naturally express their needs. The project therefore aims to improve access to the MITOS registry through more intuitive, accurate and multilingual search functions. Its implementation combines Linked Open Data, semantic technologies, natural language processing and artificial intelligence techniques to interpret the meaning and intent behind user queries. Instead of relying only on keyword matching, the semantic search engine analyses relationships between public-service descriptions and translates natural-language questions into structured, machine-readable formats. This allows the system to return more relevant results and support multilingual access to registry content. Conceptually, the solution links public-service metadata, semantic relationships, NLP query interpretation and structured retrieval over the registry. The expected impact is a better user experience, more effective discovery of administrative services and improved reuse of public-sector information. By transforming registry data into semantically searchable content, MitosLOD supports transparency, accessibility and more efficient interaction with public administration.

results.title: Chaos - Analysis of multiple data sources to forecast property market performance
results.proposal: Chaos - Analysis of multiple data sources to forecast property market performance. CHAOS provides AI-driven location intelligence for the real-estate sector by analysing multiple data sources to forecast property-market performance and generate actionable insights. The business problem is that investors, property developers, cities and retail operators need to understand how neighbourhood dynamics, service accessibility, demographics, mobility and local amenities affect real-estate value and urban development potential. Traditional property analysis can be fragmented, slow and insufficiently sensitive to changes in urban environments. CHAOS addresses this by combining data analytics, AI and built-environment expertise to support more informed decision-making. Conceptually, the platform integrates heterogeneous urban and market datasets, models location attractiveness and produces insights that can guide investment, development and planning choices. The expected impact is faster property analysis, more evidence-based investment decisions, improved understanding of local demand and support for more liveable urban development. Recent company information indicates that CHAOS has moved beyond an experimental phase and is scaling its AI-driven location-intelligence platform across the Nordics and DACH region.

results.title: Prediction supply of trucks - Machine Learning to predict truck scheduling
results.proposal: Prediction supply of trucks - Machine Learning to predict truck scheduling. La Poste’s truck-scheduling use case addresses the difficulty of managing loading operations when incoming trucks arrive early, on time or late because of congestion and other disruptions. The operational problem is that uncertain arrival times reduce loading-bay utilisation and force logistics operators to make costly rescheduling decisions. The solution combines a machine-learning classifier with an optimisation model: the classifier estimates the probability that each truck will arrive early, on time or late, and these probabilities are then used to proactively adjust loading slots. At a conceptual level, the system links real-time truck-location information, historical traffic data, predictive classification and mathematical rescheduling. The expected impact is more efficient loading-bay management, lower disruption costs and better transport-flow optimisation. Research on the case reported that the combined predictive and proactive approach reduced rescheduling costs by around 42% compared with a baseline schedule without real-time arrival predictions. This indicates that predictive information can materially improve operational planning when integrated with optimisation rather than used only as a passive forecast.
results.memo: Proceed. Prediction supply of trucks - Machine Learning to predict truck scheduling is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Anomaly detection in e-government administration
results.proposal: Anomaly detection in e-government administration. Hungary’s anomaly-detection initiative focuses on protecting the reliability and availability of critical digital public services. The operational challenge is that modern e-government systems generate large volumes of technical and usage data, while service disruptions or misuse can affect citizens’ ability to complete administrative procedures. IdomSoft, a state-owned company responsible for a wide range of Hungarian digital government services, is introducing machine-learning techniques to predict future system loads and identify abnormal use of public-service systems. The implementation applies anomaly-detection algorithms to data generated by administrative digital services, enabling the authority to analyse usage patterns and detect possible service corruption, overload or misuse. Conceptually, the system combines monitoring data, predictive modelling, anomaly detection and operational alerting to support service continuity. The expected impact is improved resilience of e-government platforms, lower risk of disruption, better targeting of technical interventions and reduced operational costs. By moving from reactive maintenance to predictive monitoring, the initiative can strengthen the dependability of digital administration and improve the user experience for citizens relying on online public services.

results.title: MLOps platform for classification purposes - Developing classification models
results.proposal: MLOps platform for classification purposes - Developing classification models. Statistics Finland’s MLOps platform is designed to make the development, deployment and maintenance of machine-learning classification models more robust within official statistics production. The operational problem is that statistical organisations increasingly use models in internal workflows, but each project can otherwise require separate decisions on architecture, security, deployment, monitoring and maintenance. This creates duplication and weakens consistency across statistical processes. The platform supports expert users working with internal data or statistical production pipelines, where classification models may operate either in batch mode or as online prediction services. Its implementation defines common architecture and security policies for model development, reducing the need to redesign governance and technical arrangements case by case. Conceptually, the system covers the machine-learning lifecycle, from model construction and deployment to monitoring and operational maintenance, while ensuring that outputs remain internal intermediate products before aggregation and publication as official statistics. The expected impact is improved reliability, easier model reuse, stronger governance, reduced operational risk and more efficient development of classification models. By standardising MLOps practices, Statistics Finland can scale machine-learning use while preserving statistical quality and confidentiality requirements.

results.title: Integrated Public Transport Management System - ITS
results.proposal: Integrated Public Transport Management System - ITS. Public transport networks require reliable passenger information, safety monitoring and coordination with wider traffic-management systems to maintain service quality and user confidence. Integrated Public Transport Management System in Lublin complements the existing traffic-management system by adding functions that support travellers, operators and municipal transport management. The operational challenge is to provide timely information and improve safety at stops and interchange points, particularly where passengers depend on accurate updates to plan journeys and where public transport infrastructure must be monitored continuously. The system includes an information service for travellers, such as electronic information boards and online systems, as well as safety-monitoring systems installed at stops and transfer hubs. Technologically, it combines digital passenger-information displays, online data services, monitoring devices and integration with the city’s traffic-management environment. These components allow transport information to be communicated more clearly and enable responsible services to observe conditions at key public-transport locations. The expected impact is improved passenger experience, better access to real-time or updated transport information, enhanced safety at stops and hubs, and stronger operational coordination within the urban mobility system. For the municipality, the project supports a more integrated approach to public transport management and helps align passenger services with broader traffic-control capabilities.
