results.title: Bridge sensors to control car and boat traffic
results.proposal: Bridge sensors to control car and boat traffic. The Province of South Holland introduced this use case to address the operational challenge of keeping both roads and waterways safe, accessible and efficient in an area where bridge openings directly affect two interconnected transport systems. Through the Smart Shipping programme, developed with the Directorate-General for Public Works and Water Management and the Ministry of Infrastructure and Water Management, the province aims to improve the use of inland waterways while reducing unnecessary disruption for road users. The central objective is to coordinate bridge operations more intelligently, so that vessels can pass with less waiting time and road traffic remains manageable when bridges open. The implementation relies on a network of sensors installed across 55 provincial bridges to detect whether each bridge is open or closed, combined with induction loops placed in roads to measure traffic volumes. These data streams are used by a mobility application that supports operational decisions on bridge openings by balancing vessel movements with road traffic conditions. By integrating bridge-status data and traffic-flow measurements, the system enables more responsive planning and contributes to smoother multimodal transport management. The expected value lies in reducing waiting times for ships, limiting avoidable congestion for cars and other road users, improving safety around bridge operations, and supporting the wider competitiveness of waterborne transport as a reliable alternative to road-based logistics.
results.memo: Proceed. Bridge sensors to control car and boat traffic is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: MasterMind - Southern Denmark
results.proposal: MasterMind - Southern Denmark. MasterMind in Southern Denmark addressed the same broader European objective of making high-quality depression treatment more widely available through ICT-enabled care. Adults with mild and moderate depression may face barriers to accessing regular therapy, including service availability, travel, stigma or scheduling constraints. The Region of Southern Denmark participated in the European MasterMind project, which involved 23 partners and focused on implementing Computerised Cognitive Behaviour Therapy as a scalable form of supported treatment. The emerging technology implementation centred on the web application “Overcome your depression”, which can be used through a computer, tablet or smartphone. The application delivers therapy in six modules using text, videos, images, graphs and other structured materials. Patients complete tests during the programme, allowing their progress and condition to be communicated to healthcare professionals. Clinicians review the results periodically and receive alarms when responses indicate a cause for concern. The expected impact is improved access to treatment, reduced reliance on face-to-face appointments and more efficient monitoring of patient progress. By enabling remote therapy while maintaining professional involvement, the solution can help mental-health services reach more patients, use clinical resources more effectively and provide a flexible pathway for people with mild or moderate depression. The case demonstrates how digital therapy can be integrated into regional healthcare provision.

results.company: Osakidetza (Servicio Vasco de Salud/Basque Health System)
results.title: MasterMind - Basque Country
results.proposal: MasterMind - Basque Country. MasterMind in the Basque Country addressed the need to make high-quality treatment for depression more widely available to adults with mild and moderate depression. Access to psychological therapy can be constrained by limited professional capacity, distance, waiting times and the need for repeated face-to-face appointments. The project, involving Osakidetza within a broader European collaboration of 23 partners, aimed to use ICT to expand access while maintaining professional oversight. The emerging technology implementation consisted of Computerised Cognitive Behaviour Therapy delivered through the web application “Overcome your depression”, accessible by computer, tablet or smartphone. At conceptual level, the application provides therapy through six modules combining text, videos, images, graphs and interactive tasks. Patients complete tests within the platform, and these results communicate the evolution of their condition to health professionals. Clinicians periodically review the outputs and receive alerts when a patient’s results indicate possible concern. The expected impact is wider availability of depression treatment, fewer required face-to-face appointments and better continuity of monitoring between patients and professionals. By combining structured digital therapy with clinical supervision, MasterMind can improve service accessibility, support efficient use of healthcare resources and provide patients with a flexible treatment pathway that complements conventional mental-health services in the Basque health system.

results.title: Track AI
results.proposal: Track AI. Track AI addresses the difficulty of assessing visual function in children and other non-collaborative patients who may be unable to complete conventional ophthalmological examinations. Reliable early detection of visual impairment is essential for timely intervention, but clinical assessment can be challenging when patients cannot follow instructions or communicate clearly. The project, linked to Miguel Servet Hospital in Zaragoza, uses the DIVE medical device and aims to help physicians determine whether a patient has a visual impairment and, in some cases, estimate the probability of a specific pathology. The emerging technology implementation integrates artificial intelligence into the DIVE device through a dedicated app running on a Huawei P30 mobile phone. The app analyses data from visual explorations, especially patient gaze patterns, and compares them with a database generated from previous diagnoses, available both online and offline. At conceptual level, the system uses pattern comparison and probabilistic classification to support clinical interpretation of visual behaviour. Although focused on non-collaborative patients, it can also be used with collaborative patients. The expected impact is improved support for clinicians, faster and more accessible screening, and better identification of patients who may require further assessment or treatment. By combining portable technology with diagnostic-support capabilities, Track AI can strengthen paediatric and inclusive eye-care services.

results.title: AI4EU-TAILOR
results.proposal: AI4EU-TAILOR. TAILOR addresses the strategic objective of advancing trustworthy artificial intelligence in Europe by integrating reasoning, learning and optimisation. The project responds to the need for research and innovation that is not only technically advanced, but also human-centred, responsible and aligned with European values. Coordinated through a consortium including Linköping University, TAILOR is committed to demonstrating that expertise, cooperation and diversity can support the European vision of trustworthy AI and position Europe as a global role model for responsible development. The emerging technology implementation focuses on the foundations of trustworthy AI, particularly the integration of symbolic reasoning, machine learning and optimisation methods. At conceptual level, the project brings together research communities that address different aspects of intelligent systems, seeking approaches that are more robust, explainable, reliable and suitable for human-centred applications. Rather than a single operational tool, TAILOR functions as a research network and capability-building initiative that supports methods, knowledge exchange and innovation pathways. The expected impact is stronger European excellence in trustworthy AI, improved collaboration among researchers and better foundations for future applications in public and private sectors. By advancing methods that combine reasoning, learning and optimisation, TAILOR can contribute to systems that are more transparent, dependable and aligned with governance expectations for high-impact digital technologies.
results.memo: Proceed. AI4EU-TAILOR is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: National Center for Scientific Research Demokritos
results.title: AI4EU-AICopernicus
results.proposal: AI4EU-AICopernicus. AI4Copernicus addresses the need to connect artificial intelligence capabilities with Earth observation data, particularly data generated through the Copernicus programme. Researchers, innovators and public-sector users often face technical and organisational barriers when trying to combine satellite and geospatial data with advanced analytical methods. The project, associated with the National Center for Scientific Research Demokritos, aims to make the AI4EU AI-on-demand platform the digital environment of choice for users working with Copernicus data. The emerging technology implementation focuses on bridging the AI4EU platform with the Earth observation ecosystem. At conceptual level, AI4Copernicus supports access to tools, resources and services that enable users to apply artificial intelligence methods to Copernicus data for research and innovation purposes. This may include support for data discovery, model development, experimentation and reuse of analytical components in geospatial applications. The expected impact is stronger uptake of Earth observation data, improved innovation capacity and easier development of AI-enabled services based on Copernicus resources. By linking two major European digital assets, AI4Copernicus can support applications in areas such as environmental monitoring, climate services, land management and emergency response. The project contributes to a more integrated European data and AI ecosystem, making advanced analysis more accessible to both specialists and applied users.

results.company: Centre for Research and Technology Hellas (CERTH)
results.title: AI4EU-AI4Media
results.proposal: AI4EU-AI4Media. AI4Media addresses the need to strengthen Europe’s research and innovation capacity in artificial intelligence for the media sector while ensuring that future deployments reflect European values of ethics, trustworthiness and responsibility. The media sector faces rapid technological change, including new forms of content production, distribution, verification and personalisation, requiring advanced tools and specialised expertise. Funded under the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme, AI4Media is structured as a Network of Research Excellence Centres and is associated with the Centre for Research and Technology Hellas. The objective is to become a Centre of Excellence engaging a wide network of researchers across Europe and beyond. The emerging technology implementation consists of research, training and development activities focused on the next generation of core artificial intelligence advances for media applications. At conceptual level, the network brings together scientific expertise, technical tools and sector-specific challenges to support responsible innovation in media technologies. It also emphasises the embedding of ethical and trustworthy AI principles in future deployments. The expected impact is improved European capacity to develop and apply advanced media technologies, stronger research collaboration and better alignment between innovation and public-interest values. By linking technical excellence with ethical governance, AI4Media supports a more responsible and competitive European media-technology ecosystem.

results.title: AI4EU-AIPlan4EU
results.proposal: AI4EU-AIPlan4EU. AIPlan4EU addresses the need to make automated planning technologies more accessible and usable for European innovators, practitioners and public or private organisations using the European AI On-Demand Platform. Planning technologies can support decision-making where actors must sequence actions, optimise resources or coordinate complex processes, but they are often difficult for non-specialists to access and apply. The project, coordinated through LAAS-CNRS, aims to bring AI planning into the AI4EU platform as a first-class capability by creating a uniform, user-centred framework for accessing existing planning technologies. The emerging technology implementation focuses on integrating planning tools, methods and guidance into the European platform environment. At conceptual level, the framework provides common access routes to established planning technologies and supports users in selecting, understanding and applying these tools to concrete innovation problems. The project also develops practical guidelines for innovators and practitioners, helping translate research outputs into usable solutions. The expected impact is broader adoption of planning technologies, reduced barriers between research and application, and improved capacity for organisations to use advanced decision-support methods. By embedding planning capabilities in AI4EU, AIPlan4EU strengthens the platform’s value as a shared European resource and supports more scalable use of intelligent planning across sectors and use cases.

results.title: CityFlows-Milano
results.proposal: CityFlows-Milano. CityFlows-Milano addresses the challenge of managing busy pedestrian spaces in Milan by improving public authorities’ capacity to monitor crowding, assess risks and support operational decisions. Dense urban areas require tools that can help maintain comfort and safety, especially in places affected by high footfall, public events, commuting flows and changing mobility patterns. CityFlows, an EIT Urban Mobility flagship project, brought together a diverse consortium of partners to launch a state-of-the-art Crowd Management Decision-Support System. The Municipality of Milan is identified as the local public stakeholder. The emerging technology implementation is based on the CityFlows CM-DSS, a decision-support software later licensed to government authorities through City Analytics, a dedicated start-up. At conceptual level, the system combines pedestrian-flow data, urban analytics and decision-support functions to help public authorities interpret crowd conditions and plan responses. It supports the connection between monitoring information and operational management of public space. The expected impact is better safety, comfort and responsiveness in pedestrian areas, with authorities able to rely on more structured information when managing crowd-related risks. The City Analytics licensing model also increases the potential for replication beyond the original project, allowing municipalities and public-space managers to adopt a scalable tool for crowd management, including during crisis situations or periods of unusual pressure on public space.
results.memo: Proceed. CityFlows-Milano is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: CityFlows-Barcelona
results.proposal: CityFlows-Barcelona. CityFlows-Barcelona addresses the need to improve the safety and comfort of busy pedestrian spaces in Barcelona. High-density urban areas face operational challenges related to crowding, public-space management, mobility flows and emergency preparedness, particularly in locations affected by tourism, events and changing patterns of pedestrian movement. The CityFlows initiative, developed as an EIT Urban Mobility flagship project, brought together a diverse consortium of partners to create a Crowd Management Decision-Support System for public authorities and managers of pedestrian spaces. The Municipality of Barcelona is identified as the local public stakeholder. The emerging technology implementation centres on the CityFlows CM-DSS, a software solution later licensed through City Analytics, a start-up created to provide the system to government authorities. At conceptual level, the platform uses urban analytics and pedestrian-flow information to support the monitoring, assessment and management of crowded spaces. It can help authorities understand crowd conditions, assess potential risks and select appropriate operational measures. The expected impact is improved situational awareness, safer and more comfortable pedestrian environments, and stronger capacity to manage public spaces during normal operations and periods of disruption. The creation of City Analytics also supports scalability, enabling the solution to be reused by other authorities seeking reliable tools for evidence-based crowd management.

results.title: GAIA-X: Predictive maintenance for the road infrastructure in South Tyrol
results.proposal: GAIA-X: Predictive maintenance for the road infrastructure in South Tyrol. This GAIA-X use case addresses the challenge of helping public administrations make better-founded decisions on road maintenance and budget planning. Road authorities must manage large infrastructure networks with limited resources, while poor road-surface quality can increase maintenance costs, congestion, downtime and costs for road users. In South Tyrol, GAIA-X is described as a data lake and scalable infrastructure for storing and processing heterogeneous data sources relevant to road-surface quality and maintenance needs. DataPort GmbH is identified as the associated stakeholder. The emerging technology implementation aggregates data from different sensors and other sources useful for assessing road conditions and identifying potential maintenance issues. At conceptual level, the platform processes large volumes of heterogeneous information to generate evaluations within response times suitable for public-administration budget planning. Predictive maintenance methods can then support targeted interventions by estimating where maintenance is most needed and when it should be prioritised. The expected impact includes better management of public funds, more efficient and targeted maintenance, improved road-surface quality, reduced disruption from roadworks, lower agency costs for the administration and lower road-user costs for citizens and infrastructure users. The cloud-based approach is potentially reusable by other European public administrations facing similar road-maintenance challenges.

results.title: GAIA-X: Digital public administration – Chatbot
results.proposal: GAIA-X: Digital public administration – Chatbot. The GAIA-X Digital Public Administration Chatbot use case addresses the need to develop and deploy digital assistants in public administration within a legally compliant and trustworthy cloud environment. Public bodies increasingly seek to use conversational services to guide citizens, answer questions and support administrative processes, but they must ensure that data storage, processing and software components comply with public-sector requirements. The project, associated with DataPort GmbH, aims to create the basis for a cloud environment in which digital assistants can be developed and used securely by administrations. The emerging technology implementation consists of modular functional AI building blocks offered as software-as-a-service components and linked with official infrastructure for data storage and processing. At conceptual level, the solution enables administrations to combine reusable chatbot capabilities, natural-language functions and compliant cloud infrastructure rather than building each assistant from scratch. This modularity can support faster deployment and more consistent service quality across public bodies. The expected impact is improved scalability of conversational public services, reduced technical barriers for administrations and a stronger compliance basis for cloud-based digital assistants. By connecting AI components with official infrastructure, the use case can support more accessible citizen services while preserving the governance, security and legal requirements expected in public administration.

results.title: GAIA-X: Data Science & Machine Learning (DSML) Hub
results.proposal: GAIA-X: Data Science & Machine Learning (DSML) Hub. The GAIA-X Data Science & Machine Learning Hub addresses the challenge of making public-administration data more accessible and usable for data-science and artificial intelligence applications while respecting data-protection requirements. Public-sector data are often stored in organisational silos, limiting their reuse by administrations, companies, start-ups and research institutions. The DSML Hub, associated with DataPort GmbH, aims to create a sustainable approach to the use of data science and AI in the public sector and to support innovation and value creation across the wider ecosystem. The emerging technology implementation consists of five building blocks: unlocking administrative data silos and enabling access for third parties; creating infrastructure for data science and AI with modern hardware and common software, including a DSML platform; expanding an ecosystem of start-ups, public IT service providers, regional SMEs, administrations, politics and research institutions; synchronising with GAIA-X; and implementing ten selected innovative projects in administrations and companies. At conceptual level, the Hub combines data access, technical infrastructure and ecosystem governance. The expected impact is improved reuse of public data, stronger innovation capacity and better conditions for public-sector digital transformation. By providing shared infrastructure and connecting diverse actors, the DSML Hub can reduce duplication, improve scalability and enable more evidence-based administrative services and policy applications.
results.memo: Proceed. GAIA-X: Data Science & Machine Learning (DSML) Hub is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: GAIA-X: AI-Marketplace: An Ecosystem For Artificial Intelligence
results.proposal: GAIA-X: AI-Marketplace: An Ecosystem For Artificial Intelligence. The GAIA-X AI Marketplace addresses the need to support manufacturing companies, solution providers and artificial intelligence experts in developing innovative applications for product development. Organisations seeking to apply advanced analytical tools in production contexts often face difficulties in finding appropriate partners, accessing relevant data environments and assembling reusable development components. The project establishes a digital platform that brings together AI experts, solution providers and manufacturing companies to promote joint innovation and build on existing infrastructure. Inno-focus Businessconsulting GmbH is identified as the stakeholder associated with the use case. The emerging technology implementation consists of a platform ecosystem providing essential tools for the development of AI solutions. Its core functions include an intelligent partner agency for AI use cases in production development, a data room for production-development data and a construction kit for AI development. At conceptual level, the platform supports matchmaking, data access and reusable development components, enabling actors to design and test solutions more efficiently. The expected impact is faster innovation, stronger collaboration and more scalable development of AI applications in industrial settings. By creating a structured marketplace, the use case can reduce fragmentation, facilitate knowledge exchange and support the emergence of a trusted European data and innovation ecosystem aligned with GAIA-X principles.

results.company: Lepida Spa (inhouse ICT of Regione Emilia Romagna)
results.title: RainBO (follow-up of BLUEAP Bologna Urban Environment Adaptation Plan for a resilient city)
results.proposal: RainBO (follow-up of BLUEAP Bologna Urban Environment Adaptation Plan for a resilient city). RainBO addresses the need to improve Bologna’s resilience to severe rainfall and sudden flooding, particularly in relation to the hydrological response of small watercourses within the urban area. Extreme rainfall can create fast-moving local risks for citizens, infrastructure and municipal services, especially where watercourses react quickly to intense precipitation. As a follow-up to the BLUEAP Bologna Urban Environment Adaptation Plan, the project focuses on improving methods and tools that allow authorities to predict severe rainfall events and assess their likely impact. Lepida Spa, the in-house ICT body of Regione Emilia-Romagna, is identified as the public technology stakeholder. The emerging technology implementation consists of a monitoring and modelling system designed to forecast sudden flooding events. At conceptual level, the system combines rainfall prediction, hydrological modelling and local monitoring data to understand how small urban watercourses may respond to severe weather. These outputs can support early warning, preparedness and operational decision-making by public authorities. The expected impact is higher resilience in vulnerable urban watercourses, improved situational awareness before and during heavy rainfall, and stronger capacity to anticipate flood risks. By connecting monitoring with predictive modelling, RainBO can help authorities move from reactive emergency response towards more preventive and evidence-based management of rainfall-related urban hazards.

results.title: DARE: Digital Environment for collaborative Alliances to Regenerate urban Ecosystems in middle-sized cities
results.proposal: DARE: Digital Environment for collaborative Alliances to Regenerate urban Ecosystems in middle-sized cities. DARE addresses the challenge of supporting urban regeneration in middle-sized cities through a citizen-centred and digitally enabled governance model. The project focuses on the Darsena area in Ravenna and aims to demonstrate an approach that can facilitate, support and accelerate the implementation and evaluation of the regeneration process, with potential replication in other European middle-sized cities. The policy challenge is not only technical, but also organisational: public administration must act as an enabler of collaboration between citizens, economic actors and strategic policy objectives. The emerging technology implementation consists of a three-layer digital environment composed of a data-management platform, an editorial content-management layer and a virtual-realm presentation layer. At conceptual level, this environment enables the collection, organisation and presentation of information needed to activate urban actors and support collaborative decision-making. The project also introduces a process-organisers team to connect strategy, economic opportunities and citizen needs, while promoting digital culture among residents so that they can become digitally aware city changers. The expected impact is improved coordination of urban-regeneration activities, stronger citizen participation and more transparent evaluation of interventions. By combining digital infrastructure with a revised public-administration role, DARE can increase the scalability and replicability of participatory regeneration models in other European urban contexts.

results.title: AI4EU: Boosting Europe’s artificial intelligence capacity
results.proposal: AI4EU: Boosting Europe’s artificial intelligence capacity. AI4EU addresses the strategic need to strengthen Europe’s artificial intelligence ecosystem by bringing together knowledge, algorithms, tools and resources in a common environment. European researchers, innovators, businesses and public-sector users often operate across fragmented communities, which can limit reuse, collaboration and access to technical assets. Launched in January 2019 as a €20 million European Union flagship project involving more than 70 partners across 21 countries, AI4EU aimed to unify Europe’s AI community and make capabilities more accessible to a broad range of users. The emerging technology implementation consists of a European platform designed to share expertise, knowledge, algorithms, tools and resources. At conceptual level, the platform provides an infrastructure for collaboration across research, innovation and business, enabling users to discover and reuse AI-related assets and contribute to collective work. The project was planned to run for three years, with the platform under development at the time described. The expected impact is increased European capacity in artificial intelligence, stronger collaboration across countries and sectors, and easier access to tools for organisations that may lack in-house capabilities. By consolidating resources and supporting a shared ecosystem, AI4EU can reduce duplication, promote innovation and strengthen Europe’s competitiveness and strategic autonomy in advanced digital technologies.

results.title: Citizen Conversational AI Platform
results.proposal: Citizen Conversational AI Platform. The Citizen Conversational AI Platform addresses the need to make digital public services more accessible through natural-language interaction. Citizens often need to navigate complex administrative information, and traditional interfaces may require users to understand service structures or search terms before finding the right answer. CSI Piemonte developed prototypes to explore how chatbots and conversational interfaces could support interaction with regional services in Piedmont. The objective was to engineer and automate bot production so that new services could be implemented quickly, while improving the effectiveness of conversations through context management and more fluid dialogue mechanisms. The emerging technology implementation consists of chatbot prototypes using conversational user-experience design, context management and artificial intelligence technologies. At conceptual level, the platform supports everyday natural-language requests, maintains elements of the current conversation, manages list references and provides refined responses. CSI Piemonte produced prototypes for searching general practitioners and paediatricians of the Piedmont Region through Alexa and Google Home, including search-refinement capabilities. The expected impact is improved user experience, faster access to information and increased scalability in the production of conversational public-service tools. By making services available through familiar voice assistants and conversational channels, the platform can reduce barriers for users, support more intuitive interaction with public administration and create reusable components for future chatbot-based services.

The platform uses multiple data sources, including Copernicus Sentinel satellite data, ad hoc monitoring cameras, social media, and mobile-phone inputs from professional users, volunteers and citizens. Citizens and field actors can report observed conditions through chatbots, enriching real-time situational awareness. At conceptual level, the system integrates earth observation, user-generated reports, sensor data and emergency-management workflows to support detection, assessment and response. The expected impact is improved forest-fire preparedness, faster access to operational information, better coordination among actors and stronger capacity to manage emergencies. By combining satellite monitoring with local observations and automated analysis, SAFERS can improve scalability, responsiveness and resilience in forest-fire governance.

results.title: FAITH - monitoring mental health with Artificial Intelligence - IRELAND Pilot
results.proposal: FAITH - monitoring mental health with Artificial Intelligence - IRELAND Pilot. The FAITH Ireland pilot addresses the need to integrate mental-health and well-being monitoring into cancer care for patients undergoing treatment or who have completed treatment. UPMC Waterford is the main Irish pilot test-trial site, focusing on breast-cancer patients as the selected use case and target group. The clinical rationale is that patient well-being and mental health are as important as access to advanced oncology care, particularly when patients may require follow-up from oncologists, general practitioners or local cancer-support services. The objective is to use FAITH to identify patients who would benefit from additional care and ensure that support needs are detected in a timely manner. The emerging technology implementation consists of an artificial intelligence application that identifies and analyses depression markers in people treated for cancer. At conceptual level, the tool processes patient-related information collected through monitoring and assessment to identify signals that may indicate psychological distress or aftercare needs. These outputs can help clinicians decide whether a patient should receive follow-up from the oncology team, a GP or a local Cancer Support Centre. The expected impact is improved identification of patients requiring psychosocial or clinical follow-up, better integration of mental-health support into oncology pathways and a more personalised care experience. By supporting earlier referral decisions, FAITH can contribute to more holistic cancer survivorship care.

The emerging technology implementation consists of an artificial intelligence application that identifies and analyses depression markers in people who have undergone cancer treatment. In the Portuguese pilot, patients receive psychological and cognitive assessments through psychosocial questionnaires, neuropsychological testing and other relevant constructs. At conceptual level, the system uses these data to detect patterns that may indicate aftercare needs or risks to mental well-being. By embedding structured monitoring into oncology follow-up, FAITH can support clinicians in improving continuity of care and enhancing quality of life for lung-cancer patients.

results.title: Deep Gravity: the algorithm that explains how people move
results.proposal: Deep Gravity: the algorithm that explains how people move. Deep Gravity addresses the limitations of traditional mobility-flow prediction models used to estimate how people move between places, both on foot and by vehicle. The conventional gravitational model, inspired by Newton’s law of universal gravitation, estimates flows between two locations as proportional to population and inversely proportional to distance. In practice, this approach is often inaccurate because it relies on only two variables and cannot capture complex relationships between the characteristics of places. The Institute of Science and Information Technologies of the Italian National Research Council, together with the Bruno Kessler Foundation and Argonne National Laboratory, developed Deep Gravity to improve mobility prediction. The emerging technology implementation extends the gravitational model by incorporating multiple variables that describe points of interest in each location, such as restaurants, hotels, hospitals and streets, and by using deep learning to capture complex relationships among these variables. At conceptual level, the algorithm learns how the attractiveness and structure of places influence mobility flows, improving predictions beyond distance and population alone. The expected impact is more accurate mobility-flow estimation, which can support public authorities in transport planning, urban policy, infrastructure design and emergency management. By better explaining how people move, Deep Gravity can improve decision-making in mobility-related public services and provide a more scalable analytical basis for understanding urban and regional movement patterns.

results.proposal: BALCAT – Project on ballistics analysis. BALCAT addresses the need for faster and more reliable access to information in serious-crime investigations involving firearms. Police authorities require rapid access to structured, accurate and searchable data so that forensic ballistics analysis can be connected with administrative information on weapons. This can improve investigative efficiency, support faster decision-making and strengthen the quality of forensic support in serious-crime cases. results.title: IRIS – Application of Artificial Intelligence Techniques in the Supreme Court of Justice
results.proposal: IRIS – Application of Artificial Intelligence Techniques in the Supreme Court of Justice. IRIS addresses the challenge of analysing, summarising and disseminating court decisions within the Supreme Court of Justice. Judicial decisions are complex documents that require careful study by legal professionals, but they are also increasingly relevant to citizens, researchers and other non-specialist users who need understandable access to legal information. The project has two main objectives: to develop automatic summarisation approaches for court decisions and to create a representation of judicial proceedings that can be browsed in a way that supports the decision process. The emerging technology implementation focuses on text-analysis and summarisation techniques applied to judicial documents. At conceptual level, the system is designed to generate both technical summaries, useful for legal study, processing and dissemination, and summaries that are more understandable for non-technical audiences. It also aims to represent the key elements of judicial proceedings in a structured, browsable format, making it easier to explore complex case materials. The expected impact is improved efficiency in analysing court decisions, better dissemination of jurisprudence and stronger support for judicial decision-making. By reducing the burden of navigating lengthy and complex documents, IRIS can enhance access to legal knowledge, improve usability for different user groups and support a more transparent and efficient justice system.

results.title: Decoding the Legislation
results.proposal: Decoding the Legislation. Decoding the Legislation addresses the difficulty citizens face when trying to understand and consult legal texts. The project sought to facilitate citizen consultation of legal information by improving how legislation from the Diário da República Eletrónico can be searched and interpreted. The selected case studies were Consumer Rights Legislation and the Retirement Statute, both areas where citizens may need practical answers to specific legal questions. The emerging technology implementation involved the creation of repositories containing data sources and metadata from the Diário da República Eletrónico, combined with natural language processing tools. At conceptual level, legal attributes were transformed into code language, and a web application was developed to allow intelligent queries on a given law. A proof of concept demonstrated an intelligent search mechanism through which citizens could ask questions about selected legislative sets and receive automatic answers. The expected impact is improved accessibility of legislation, a better user experience for citizens and reduced friction in finding relevant legal information. By making legal consultation more intuitive, the project can support transparency, legal empowerment and more efficient interaction between citizens and public legal-information systems. At conceptual level, the system analyses judicial texts and identifies relevant patterns, precedents or similarities that may assist magistrates when examining new inquiries or documents. It is not intended to replace judicial discretion, but to improve access to structured information and reduce the time needed to locate and interpret comparable cases. The expected impact is faster handling of legal materials, more efficient judicial workflows and improved responsiveness of the justice system. By enabling magistrates to reach well-supported conclusions more quickly, the project can contribute to shorter processing times and better service to citizens. The case is relevant as an example of how data-driven tools may support legal professionals while preserving the central role of human legal judgement.

results.title: LAIfeBlood - Artificial Intelligence for Blood Management
results.proposal: LAIfeBlood - Artificial Intelligence for Blood Management. LAIfeBlood addresses the operational challenge of improving the efficiency and resilience of Portugal’s blood supply chain. The Instituto Português do Sangue e da Transplantação is the public authority responsible for the collection and regulation of blood donation and transplantation at national level, including the quality and safety of donation, procurement, processing, storage, preservation and distribution of human blood, blood components, organs, tissues and human-origin cells. The emerging technology implementation focuses on extracting temporal and geographical patterns from historical collection and transfusion data, developing predictive models for expected collections and transfusions across different time periods and regions, and creating software tools to optimise national collection planning. At conceptual level, the system combines forecasting, optimisation and dynamic supply-chain management to help IPST plan collection events according to resource availability and demand expectations. The expected impact is improved blood-service effectiveness, reduced wastage and more efficient daily inventory rebalancing. The project also aims to generate implementable policies for IPST, strengthening national capacity to manage collections, allocate teams and respond to changing demand. By supporting evidence-based planning, LAIfeBlood can improve the reliability, scalability and sustainability of blood supply operations in Portugal.

By identifying high-risk patients earlier, IPOSCORE can help clinicians plan follow-up, allocate resources and adapt interventions more effectively. The case is particularly relevant for public healthcare settings seeking to improve oncology outcomes through data-driven risk stratification and more precise use of available clinical information.

By decreasing the time and number of activities dedicated to coding supervision, CliKode can reduce pressure on specialised human resources, improve hospital data quality and strengthen the reliability of administrative and clinical information.

results.title: AI4Life - Artificial intelligence as a tool to reduce Premature Mortality
results.proposal: AI4Life - Artificial intelligence as a tool to reduce Premature Mortality. AI4Life responds to the public-health objective of reducing premature mortality from non-communicable diseases, in line with the World Health Organization target of reducing such mortality by 25% by 2025. The project focuses on the infantile-juvenile population and responds to the need for a more complete understanding of the factors associated with health risks across several dimensions. Public-health authorities often hold relevant data in separate systems, limiting their ability to identify patterns and relationships that could support prevention. The project therefore aims to collect and integrate information from several data sources that had not previously been combined, in order to characterise young populations more comprehensively. The emerging technology implementation applies machine-learning techniques to discover patterns, relationships and knowledge from integrated datasets. The proposal aims to support the national upscaling of a telecare screening and intervention service connected to SNS24 for older people with frailty risk. Its objectives include monitoring a group of elderly citizens through a telecare service, preventing health occurrences, detecting emerging needs early, promoting integrated care and contributing to healthy and active ageing. The emerging technology implementation uses intelligent analysis of frailty trajectories to support screening, follow-up and intervention planning. At conceptual level, the system would combine telecare data with risk assessment and predictive modelling to identify changes in frailty status and guide the prioritisation of support. Integration with SNS24 would allow the approach to be embedded in a national public-service context, supporting remote monitoring and coordinated responses. The expected impact is improved early detection of needs, better continuity of care and greater scalability of frailty-related public services. By enabling proactive follow-up rather than relying only on reactive care, FrailCare.AI can contribute to healthier ageing, reduced avoidable health incidents and more efficient allocation of health and social-care resources.

The project, led by Associação para a Inovação e Desenvolvimento da FCT, aims to characterise potential work-related disorders in the Portuguese population and examine their relationship with professional categories and workplace risk situations. The emerging technology implementation applies artificial intelligence and data-science methods to profile workers, analyse daily activities and identify clusters of work activities associated with exposure to risk factors. At conceptual level, the system is intended to forecast the progression of occupational disorders, assess associated risk factors, and estimate socio-economic impacts linked to morbidity, mortality, reduced life expectancy and incapacity. It also supports the definition of national indicators to monitor and alert authorities to occupational risks in public administration. The expected impact is stronger preventive capacity, more targeted occupational-health policies and better evidence for managing workplace risks. By identifying risk clusters and forecasting disorder progression, PrevOcupAI can help public administrations reduce absenteeism, protect worker health and improve the sustainability and productivity of public-sector workplaces.

results.proposal: SNS24 Scout.AI - APPLICATION OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE AND NATURAL LANGUAGE PROCESSING METHODOLOGIES IN THE TRIAGE, COUNSELLING AND REFERRAL SERVICE OF SNS24. SNS24 Scout.AI addresses the operational challenge of supporting nurses working in the Triage, Counselling and Referral Service of SNS24, the telephone service provided by the Contact Centre of Portugal’s National Health Service. In this context, nurses must select the most appropriate clinical algorithm and referral pathway during interactions with citizens, often under time pressure and with significant implications for access to care. The project, involving the University of Évora, aims to improve decision support in the triage process and to help the Directorate-General of Health optimise the design of clinical algorithms and their referrals. The emerging technology implementation applies artificial intelligence and natural language processing methodologies to support the interpretation of user interactions and the selection of appropriate clinical pathways. At conceptual level, the system is intended to analyse information exchanged during telephone contacts, assist the nurse in identifying the most relevant clinical algorithm, and generate evidence that can inform improvements to the structure and performance of triage algorithms. The expected impact is a more consistent, efficient and evidence-informed triage process, improving support for health professionals and potentially enhancing the user experience for citizens contacting SNS24. The project also creates value for health-system governance by helping DGS review and refine clinical algorithms on the basis of operational data and observed referral patterns.

results.title: ICDS4IM - Intelligent Support for Clinical Decision in Intensive Care Medicine
results.proposal: ICDS4IM - Intelligent Support for Clinical Decision in Intensive Care Medicine. ICDS4IM addresses the need for timely, reliable and high-quality information in intensive care medicine, where professionals must make decisions in fast-changing environments marked by complex and unpredictable events. Intensive care units generate continuous streams of clinical data from bedside devices, including vital-sign monitors, but the value of these data depends on their availability, accuracy and integration into clinical workflows. The project aims to support intensive medicine professionals by ensuring that relevant information is available in useful time and can contribute to better-supported decisions. The emerging technology implementation consists of an intelligent clinical decision-support architecture connected to bedside devices. At conceptual level, the system provides a communication layer between vital-sign monitors and decision-support components, allowing clinical information to be collected, structured and made available to professionals. The architecture is designed to improve information quality and availability, supporting the interpretation of real-time data in a mutable clinical environment. The expected impact is improved support for intensive care teams, better situational awareness and stronger capacity to respond to rapidly evolving patient conditions. By reducing fragmentation between monitoring devices and clinical decision processes, ICDS4IM can contribute to more reliable decision-making, more efficient use of clinical information and improved operational resilience in intensive medicine. The case is primarily focused on architectural design and prototype development for intelligent decision support in high-risk healthcare settings.

results.title: P.IA.ES - Modeling and prediction of failure and school dropout in Higher Education
results.proposal: P.IA.ES - Modeling and prediction of failure and school dropout in Higher Education. P.IA.ES tackles the challenge of reducing academic failure in higher education by enabling institutions to identify students at risk at an early stage of their academic path. Higher education institutions often need to intervene before poor performance becomes irreversible, but early warning is difficult when decisions must rely on limited information available at enrolment. This work uses a dataset from a higher education institution containing information known when students enrol, including academic trajectory, demographic characteristics and socio-economic factors. The objective is to support timely student-success strategies by predicting academic performance and identifying learners who may require additional support. The emerging technology implementation formulates the problem as a three-category classification task, complicated by strong class imbalance towards one of the categories. The project tests synthetic oversampling methods to promote class balancing and trains classification models using both standard machine-learning algorithms and state-of-the-art boosting algorithms. The results show that boosting algorithms perform better than standard methods for this specific task, although they still fall short in correctly identifying most cases in one minority class. The impact is mainly methodological and operational: the project demonstrates the potential of predictive modelling for early intervention, while also clarifying its limitations. Future improvements include adding first-year performance data, such as grades from initial semesters, to improve accuracy and better support targeted measures against failure and dropout.
results.memo: Proceed. P.IA.ES - Modeling and prediction of failure and school dropout in Higher Education is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: CDAP@UP (Predictive Analysis to Promote Student Success and Fight School Dropout)
results.proposal: CDAP@UP (Predictive Analysis to Promote Student Success and Fight School Dropout). CDAP@UP addresses the challenge of identifying students at risk of academic failure or dropout at the University of Porto early enough to provide effective support. Universities need timely and reliable evidence to understand which students may require additional assistance and to design interventions that improve academic success and retention. The project, implemented through the Data and Predictive Analytics Centre of the University of Porto, aims to support institutional decision-making by combining student data from different sources. The emerging technology implementation uses data analysis and artificial intelligence techniques to develop predictive models based on academic, sociodemographic and behavioural data. At conceptual level, these models identify risk patterns associated with academic failure or dropout and generate early-warning information that can be used by university services. The outputs enable the university to implement personalised support actions, such as tutoring, psychological counselling, academic assistance or financial support, according to the nature of the identified risk. The expected impact is improved student success, reduced dropout rates and more efficient targeting of institutional support services. By enabling earlier intervention, CDAP@UP can enhance the student experience, strengthen educational outcomes and generate public value by helping the university allocate resources where they are most needed.

results.title: SARAI – Security Advanced Research with Artificial Intelligence
results.proposal: SARAI – Security Advanced Research with Artificial Intelligence. SARAI addresses the challenge faced by cybersecurity teams in obtaining accurate and timely information from large volumes of security-related data. Public organisations increasingly depend on digital infrastructures and must detect, correct and prevent the exploitation of computer and information-security flaws before they cause serious operational disruption. The objective of the project is to create a functional prototype capable of supporting cybersecurity teams in responding more effectively to threats and vulnerabilities. The emerging technology implementation explores artificial intelligence and data-science mechanisms for large-scale security analysis. At conceptual level, the prototype is intended to process high volumes of information produced by digital systems, identify relevant signals, support the detection of vulnerabilities or suspicious activity, and help teams prioritise corrective and preventive actions. The system therefore combines automated analysis with operational cybersecurity workflows, acting as a next-generation decision-support capability for security professionals. The expected impact is faster and more accurate identification of security weaknesses, improved prevention of exploitation, and better allocation of cybersecurity resources. By reducing the time needed to process large-scale information, SARAI can increase the reliability and resilience of public-sector digital systems. The case is particularly relevant for administrations seeking to strengthen cyber-defence capacity through scalable analytical tools that support, rather than replace, expert judgement.

results.title: HEALTHI.CO: Factors for promoting dialogue and healthy behaviors in online school communities.
results.proposal: HEALTHI.CO: Factors for promoting dialogue and healthy behaviors in online school communities. HEALTHI.CO addresses the growing importance of online interaction within school communities and the need to better understand the dynamics of digital conversations among secondary school students and teachers. Schools increasingly rely on online spaces for communication, learning and social interaction, but these environments can also reflect or amplify exclusion, incivility and unhealthy behaviours. The project, supported in Portugal through FCT, seeks to generate evidence that can inform long-term educational programmes promoting empathy, inclusion, civility and healthy dialogue. The emerging technology implementation is based on the use of data-science methods to analyse online social conversation within school communities. At conceptual level, the project would examine patterns in digital communication, identify factors associated with constructive or harmful exchanges, and generate insights into how students and teachers interact in online environments. These findings could then be used to design or adjust educational interventions aimed at improving the quality of dialogue and strengthening positive behaviours. The expected impact is improved understanding of online school-community dynamics and stronger evidence for preventive and educational programmes. By helping schools and policymakers identify the conditions that foster respectful and inclusive communication, HEALTHI.CO can support healthier digital learning environments, improve student well-being and contribute to more effective long-term strategies for online citizenship education.

results.title: Modeling student flow in the Portuguese education system
results.proposal: Modeling student flow in the Portuguese education system. The ModEst project addresses the challenge of estimating and forecasting how students move through the Portuguese education system across different regions and stages of learning. Public authorities need reliable information on admissions, progression and drop-outs in order to plan resources, anticipate demographic and educational pressures, and support more effective policy decisions. The project focuses on NUTS3 regional granularity and covers the six stages of education, providing annual estimates of key variables related to student flow. It uses data from the Directorate-General for Statistics of Education and Science, Statistics Portugal, PorData and other public sources. The emerging technology implementation combines machine-learning and simulation approaches to develop predictive models of student movements. At conceptual level, these models integrate historical and administrative data to estimate flows across education stages and generate projections under different conditions. A user-centred application is also built so that the Directorate-General for Statistics of Education and Science can specify input variables, produce projections and run conditional “what-if” scenarios, while updating the models year by year. The expected impact is improved strategic planning, stronger capacity to anticipate regional education needs and better evidence for policy formulation. By enabling scenario analysis and regular model updates, ModEst supports more scalable, transparent and adaptive management of the education system.

results.title: Understanding the determinants of academic performance from Portuguese secondary education system
results.proposal: Understanding the determinants of academic performance from Portuguese secondary education system. This project addresses the need to understand which factors influence student performance in Portuguese secondary education and how public authorities can use evidence to support better educational outcomes. The work used an anonymous dataset from the 2014–15 school year provided by the Directorate-General for Statistics of Education and Science of the Portuguese Ministry of Education. The policy context concerns student achievement, educational inequality and the identification of variables that may help explain differences in high-school performance. The objective was to compare the predictive power of traditional statistical modelling with more advanced computational methods in order to assess which approaches can better support analysis of academic performance. The emerging technology implementation consisted of a comparison between a classic multilinear regression model and several machine-learning algorithms, including random forest, support vector machine, artificial neural network and an extreme gradient boosting machine stacking ensemble. At conceptual level, the models processed educational data to identify patterns and estimate student performance outcomes. The impact is mainly analytical and methodological: the project provides evidence on the usefulness of different modelling approaches for education policy and planning. By improving the understanding of performance determinants, it can support more targeted interventions, better monitoring of educational systems and more robust evidence for decision-makers seeking to improve student success in Portuguese secondary education.

results.title: CEOS - Knowledge of the Evolution of Opportunities between the Genders
results.proposal: CEOS - Knowledge of the Evolution of Opportunities between the Genders. The CEOS project seeks to solve the need for public administrations to better understand how opportunities between genders have changed over time and how structural inequalities affect access to education, employment and social mobility. The policy problem concerns the persistence of unequal life chances and the difficulty of identifying where progress has occurred, where gaps remain and which factors may explain different outcomes for women and men. In Portugal, the project is linked to the Agência para a Modernização Administrativa and aims to provide evidence that can support more equitable public policies. The emerging technology implementation is based on the analysis of datasets covering education, labour-market participation and mobility trajectories. At conceptual level, the project uses data-science methods to examine patterns across time, identify changes in access to key opportunities and reveal relationships between gender and socio-economic outcomes. By structuring and analysing these data, the system can help transform dispersed administrative and social information into policy-relevant insights. The expected impact is improved analytical capacity for equality-oriented policymaking, allowing authorities to identify persistent barriers, monitor long-term developments and design more targeted interventions. The case supports evidence-based assessment of gender opportunities and can contribute to more transparent, data-informed strategies for reducing inequality and promoting fairer access to education, employment and social advancement.

results.title: MapIntel - Interactive Visual Analysis Platform for Competitive Intelligence
results.proposal: MapIntel - Interactive Visual Analysis Platform for Competitive Intelligence. MapIntel addressed the challenge of supporting strategic decision-making through better analysis of large collections of business and policy-relevant documents. Competitive intelligence requires gathering and analysing information on the business environment so that executives and decision-makers can identify trends, risks and opportunities. However, large text corpora are difficult to explore manually, particularly when documents are heterogeneous and relevant information is distributed across many sources. The project, involving Portugal’s Agency for Administrative Modernisation, proposed an interactive visual analysis platform to improve the organisation, retrieval and exploration of such information. The emerging technology implementation was based on a neural network document-clustering system using Self-Organising Maps. Documents were clustered and stored according to their content, creating a content-addressable memory system in which texts could be retrieved through semantic similarity rather than only by keywords. At conceptual level, documents were represented as points on a semantic map, arranged topologically so that proximity reflected similarity of content. This map then served as an interface for visual analytics, allowing users to explore the corpus through different but correlated views and iteratively select and examine documents. The expected impact was to improve the efficiency, transparency and usability of competitive-intelligence analysis. By turning complex text collections into navigable visual structures, MapIntel could support faster insight generation, better strategic planning and more informed decision-making within public administration and related policy contexts.

results.proposal: AICE (Data Science and Over-Indebtedness: Use of AI algorithms in Credit and Debts). The project, supported by FCT, aimed to improve understanding of the factors that contribute to consumer vulnerability and to support better regulation and financial empowerment policies. Public authorities require more precise evidence on how different groups are affected by debt-related risk, but traditional analysis may not fully capture the interaction between socio-economic profiles, financial events and behavioural patterns. The emerging technology implementation proposed the use of machine-learning methods to develop descriptive and predictive models of over-indebtedness. In particular, unsupervised learning algorithms such as Self-Organising Maps and Agglomerative Hierarchical Clustering would be used to identify consumer clusters and reveal patterns within the data. At conceptual level, the system would process financial and socio-economic variables to group consumers according to similarities in debt vulnerability, enabling policymakers to better understand risk profiles and influencing factors. The expected impact was to produce evidence that could inform guidelines for over-indebtedness regulation, consumer financial empowerment and preventive policy design. By identifying clusters and risk factors, the project could support more targeted interventions, improve analytical capacity and contribute to fairer and more effective consumer-protection strategies in the credit and debt domain.

results.title: GADgET: Detection of addition patterns in online game
results.proposal: GADgET: Detection of addition patterns in online game. The GADgET project addressed the public-policy and regulatory challenge of identifying risky behavioural patterns in online gambling. Gambling behaviour is dynamic and time-sensitive, meaning that harmful patterns may emerge through sequences of actions rather than isolated events. The project, supported in Portugal through FCT, proposed a system capable of analysing gamblers’ behaviour over time in order to detect common patterns, identify actions associated with risk and enable continuous monitoring of online gambling activity. The emerging technology implementation was based on recurrent neural networks, with the architecture optimised through a neuroevolution algorithm. This approach was designed to compare time series associated with different gamblers’ behaviours, while explicitly taking account of the temporal dimension of the problem. At conceptual level, the system would process behavioural sequences generated during online play, identify similarities across users, detect indicators of risky conduct and operate in real time so that gambling activity could be continuously assessed. The intended impact was to improve the capacity of regulators, operators or public authorities to detect addiction-related patterns within an acceptable timeframe and intervene more effectively where risk indicators are present. By supporting real-time analysis, the solution aimed to move beyond retrospective assessment and enable more proactive monitoring of gambling-related harm. The case is particularly relevant for public administrations exploring data-driven approaches to consumer protection, behavioural risk detection and responsible gambling oversight.

results.title: DANTE H2020
results.proposal: DANTE H2020. The DANTE project, Detecting and Analysing Terrorist-related Online Contents and Financing Activities, addressed the challenge of supporting law-enforcement and defence authorities in identifying terrorist propaganda, training and financing activities across complex online environments. Italy participated through the Ministry of Defence and the General Command of the Carabinieri, within a project involving 18 European countries. The operational problem concerned the difficulty of retrieving and analysing large volumes of heterogeneous, multilingual and unstructured online information, particularly across channels such as the open web, the deep web and the dark web. The emerging technology implementation consisted of an automated system for extracting and analysing data from unstructured sources. The system applied web-mining methods and advanced analytical techniques to identify, retrieve, collect and analyse online content linked to terrorist networks. At conceptual level, it combined multilingual information extraction, source monitoring, content analysis and investigative-support functions to help authorities trace financing, training and propaganda-related activities. The system was designed to process information from channels that are traditionally more difficult to investigate, thereby expanding the analytical reach of police and security authorities. Its expected impact was to improve the accuracy, speed and completeness of terrorism investigations by enabling investigators to handle larger volumes of online material and identify relevant patterns more effectively. The case provides an example of cross-border security research intended to strengthen investigative capabilities against online terrorist activity.

results.title: MATHISIS H2020 - Italian Pilot (MIUR)
results.proposal: MATHISIS H2020 - Italian Pilot (MIUR). The Italian pilot of the MATHISIS H2020 project addressed the need for more personalised educational support for students with autism spectrum disorder, ADHD and multiple disabilities in public schools. The public stakeholders involved were Italian first- and second-degree schools, with the project aiming to improve learning pathways by adapting teaching exercises to students’ attention levels, emotional states and interaction patterns. The objective was to support teachers and learners through a platform able to respond dynamically to individual learning conditions, particularly for students who may require more tailored pedagogical approaches. The emerging technology implementation consisted of a teaching support platform connected to a webcam, movement-recognition equipment and a gyroscope. Using affective computing techniques, the platform analysed signals related to mood, movement and attention, and adjusted the difficulty of didactic exercises accordingly. At conceptual level, the system combined sensor-based interaction data with adaptive learning logic to increase or decrease task complexity in response to the learner’s condition. The pilot was tested in a sample of Italian public schools, involving just under 100 students. Initial results indicated that use of the platform improved students’ learning paths by increasing concentration and attention levels. The case demonstrates the potential of adaptive educational technologies to support inclusive education, improve engagement and provide teachers with additional tools for differentiated learning in complex classroom contexts.

results.title: Financial Assistance Automation
results.proposal: Financial Assistance Automation. Nacka municipality introduced financial assistance automation to modernise social-service administration and reduce the administrative burden on caseworkers. The objective was to create a more efficient and customer-oriented process for residents applying for financial assistance, while allowing municipal staff to focus more on individual support and pathways towards self-sufficiency. Work began in 2017 with the introduction of an e-service, and in December of the same year the processing workflow was automated. Nacka became the second municipality in Sweden to automate the financial assistance process. The emerging technology implementation combined a digital application channel with automated processing of defined steps in the case-management workflow. At conceptual level, the system enabled applicants to initiate a case online at a time of their choosing, submit required information digitally and follow the progress of their application. Automation supported the structured handling of applications where relevant information could be processed according to predefined rules, while staff remained available for assessment, support and more complex situations. The reported impact was an increase in quality for residents applying digitally, as well as a more efficient and user-centred service. The process reduced reliance on manual administration, improved transparency for applicants and strengthened municipal capacity to allocate staff time to advisory and support functions rather than routine processing. The case illustrates how automation can improve both internal efficiency and the citizen experience in welfare administration.
results.memo: Proceed. Financial Assistance Automation is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

Two of these are in the so-called Establishment Unit (Etablering), and the other is in the Work and Business Unit. results.title: SPIRIT predictive policing  - privacy-preserving intelligence analysis for resolving identities
results.proposal: SPIRIT predictive policing  - privacy-preserving intelligence analysis for resolving identities. The SPIRIT project tackles the operational challenge faced by law-enforcement authorities when attempting to resolve identities and connect information across multiple investigative sources. The Hellenic Police participated alongside the West Midlands Police, the Police and Crime Commissioner for Thames Valley, the Serbian Ministry of Interior and the Police Academy in Szczytno. The objective was to support intelligence analysis by enabling investigators to correlate fragmented information, including material from social media and other sources relevant to criminal investigations, while framing the project around privacy-preserving analysis. The emerging technology implementation included tools for face extraction and matching, social-media data correlation and complex associative searches across different information sources. At conceptual level, the system aimed to connect identity-related signals and support investigators in identifying relationships, matches or links that would be difficult to detect manually. Greek trials involved the Hellenic Police Border Unit and were scheduled between January and August 2020, with deliverables expected in April 2020 and January 2021. Two Greek private companies, Singular Logic and Nydor System Technologies, were members of the consortium. The project was due to end in July 2021. Its expected impact was to improve investigative efficiency, support cross-source intelligence analysis and reduce manual processing burdens. At the same time, the case raises important governance questions around personal data, transparency, oversight and safeguards in law-enforcement use of identity-resolution technologies.

results.title: AVINT Trikala - Integration of a line of automated buses
results.proposal: AVINT Trikala - Integration of a line of automated buses. The AVINT project in Trikala responded to the challenge of integrating automated mobility into an existing urban transport environment. The City of Trikala participated in AVINT, Autonomous Vehicles Integrated within the Urban Context, to study how automated buses could operate safely and usefully within the city’s transportation network. The planned service consisted of three automated buses, each carrying up to 10 passengers, connecting Trikala city centre with the university campus. The objective was to assess the feasibility, safety and service value of autonomous public transport in a real urban setting, while exploring how such vehicles interact with passengers, road users, infrastructure and municipal transport planning. The emerging technology implementation centred on automated electric buses operating on a defined route within the city. At conceptual level, the system required integration between vehicle automation, route planning, traffic management, passenger service design and local operational supervision. The project started in January 2019 and was scheduled for completion in December 2021. Its expected impact included testing the reliability of automated buses in everyday urban conditions, improving knowledge of regulatory and operational requirements, and supporting future decisions on smart mobility deployment. For the municipality, the project offered a controlled environment to evaluate whether autonomous shuttles could complement existing public transport, provide a low-capacity link between key locations, and contribute to a broader transition towards innovative and sustainable urban mobility.

results.title: ROBORDER project
results.proposal: ROBORDER project. The ROBORDER project was designed to address border-surveillance challenges that require persistent monitoring across complex land, sea and air environments. The Hellenic Ministry of Defence participated in the consortium alongside the Centre for Research and Technology Hellas, the National and Kapodistrian University of Athens and partners from twelve other countries: Portugal, the United Kingdom, Romania, Germany, Italy, Switzerland, Bulgaria, Spain, Hungary, Belgium, Finland and Estonia. The objective was to deliver a fully functional autonomous border-surveillance system capable of supporting authorities in detecting and monitoring events across different border contexts. The emerging technology implementation consisted of an autonomous swarm of heterogeneous unmanned vehicles, including aerial, water-surface, underwater and ground robots. These vehicles were intended to operate both independently and collectively in coordinated swarms, combining multiple sensing platforms and mobility modes into a single surveillance architecture. At conceptual level, the system integrates robotics, autonomous navigation, sensor fusion and command-and-control functions to provide border authorities with wider coverage and more flexible monitoring capabilities. The project started in May 2017 and was scheduled to conclude in February 2021. Its expected impact was to improve situational awareness, extend surveillance reach, reduce the need for continuous human presence in difficult environments and enhance the scalability of border-monitoring operations. The case remains primarily a research and development initiative, with impact linked to prototype delivery and demonstration rather than confirmed routine operational deployment.
