At a conceptual level, the system combines robotic process automation with AI-enabled enterprise automation to move across institutional systems, collect the necessary records and reduce the amount of manual administrative intervention needed. AFIR stated in March 2024 that the initiative was expected to benefit more than 50,000 stakeholders, including both farmers and state institutions. The expected impact is shorter processing times, lower administrative cost and improved operational efficiency across the funding chain. More broadly, the project creates value by making public funding more accessible, increasing the efficiency of inter-institutional document handling and supporting a more user-friendly model of agricultural-support administration.

results.title: AI for certfied emails management in the Municipality of Cinisello Balsamo
results.proposal: AI for certfied emails management in the Municipality of Cinisello Balsamo. This manual work is repetitive, time-consuming and poorly suited to high-volume digital administration, yet it remains essential for ensuring timely response and orderly case handling. The solution was implemented in partnership with Make IT through a machine-learning-based platform for PEC management. At a conceptual level, the system automates the reading, classification and routing of certified emails, creating a structured intake workflow that can integrate with municipal operations while preserving attention to security, data protection and ethical considerations. Rather than replacing human oversight altogether, the platform aims to reduce the clerical burden at the front end of the process. The expected impact is faster handling of incoming PEC traffic, reduced manual effort and improved productivity for municipal teams. More broadly, the project creates value by modernising digital administration, supporting better use of staff time and demonstrating how local authorities can apply automation responsibly in document-heavy service environments.

results.proposal: Bikeability.AI to analise bikeability in Municipality of Dordrecht. The expected impact is clearer policy insight, better prioritisation of cycling interventions and more evidence-based urban mobility planning. results.title: Forecasting models Road Administration (Roads conditions and return of investments)
results.proposal: Forecasting models Road Administration (Roads conditions and return of investments). These outputs can then support prioritisation, maintenance scheduling and broader infrastructure strategy. The expected impact is better-targeted investment, improved road-condition management and more efficient use of public resources. results.title: Battling pandemics with the help of AI
results.proposal: Battling pandemics with the help of AI. The Lower Saxony State Health Office developed Nova to respond to a recurring public-health communication challenge: during major health events such as the COVID-19 pandemic, public enquiries can rise sharply, overloading staff and making it harder to provide quick, consistent answers through traditional channels alone. The organisation needed a way to offer reliable health information around the clock while preserving staff capacity for more complex work. The stakeholders include the health office, its service teams and citizens seeking guidance on diseases and health-related concerns, with the objective of improving access to official information, reducing pressure on employees and strengthening the administration’s ability to communicate under crisis conditions. The solution was implemented with Nortal using its Tark platform to create Nova, a virtual assistant available on the NLGA website. At a conceptual level, the system combines generative capabilities, large language models and a secure, NLGA-controlled knowledge base to interpret questions, understand contextual meaning and deliver rapid answers on topics such as COVID-19, measles and other public-health concerns. This architecture allows the tool to update quickly as information changes while keeping control of source content within the public authority. The impact includes faster access to health information, better service continuity and lower workload for staff. More broadly, Nova creates value by improving crisis communication, increasing scalability in citizen support and demonstrating a secure model for health-related virtual assistance in public administration.

results.title: 3DAI City Mobile Application - AI for Road Maintenance
results.proposal: 3DAI City Mobile Application - AI for Road Maintenance. MM Spa introduced the 3DAI City mobile application to address a practical infrastructure-management problem: maintaining Milan’s roads more efficiently by identifying defects earlier and improving the quality of maintenance planning. Since taking responsibility for routine road maintenance in July 2023, MM needed a scalable way to monitor a dense and heavily used urban network without relying solely on slower, labour-intensive manual inspections. The stakeholders include MM’s maintenance teams, city infrastructure managers and Milan’s road users, with the objective of reducing emergency repairs, improving visibility of road-surface conditions and making intervention planning more timely and cost-effective. The solution is implemented in collaboration with Univrses AB through a smartphone-based system mounted on MM vehicles’ windscreens. According to MM, the technology entered a nine-month trial in November 2024 and uses moving-vehicle image capture to detect cracks, potholes, other pavement defects and anomalies in vertical road signs, with outputs integrated into MM’s Web-GIS portal. At a conceptual level, the system combines mobile computer vision, georeferenced defect detection and GIS-based asset mapping to create an updated digital view of the city’s road infrastructure. The expected impact is earlier fault detection, fewer emergency interventions and more efficient allocation of maintenance resources. More broadly, the project creates value through lower operational cost, better planning accuracy and a scalable approach to urban road-condition monitoring.

results.title: Smart Assistant - Development of a chatbot for the municipalities of the LEADER Region Weinviertel Ost
results.proposal: Smart Assistant - Development of a chatbot for the municipalities of the LEADER Region Weinviertel Ost. Municipalities in the LEADER Region Weinviertel Ost needed a practical way to automate routine online interactions and improve digital service delivery without each authority having to build separate solutions from scratch. Smaller municipalities often face capacity constraints in maintaining responsive online communication, even though residents increasingly expect fast answers on common topics such as building permits and local administrative procedures. The project therefore set out to provide a shared digital assistant for 58 municipalities, with the objective of streamlining routine enquiries, improving access to information and supporting more efficient day-to-day online operations. The stakeholders include municipal administrations, residents and the regional bodies coordinating the initiative, with the aim of creating a reusable and locally relevant support tool across the whole region. The solution is implemented through a chatbot integrated into municipal websites and trained specifically for the needs of Weinviertel Ost. At a conceptual level, the system uses commercially available chatbot software, but its local effectiveness depends on targeted training using information drawn from publicly accessible databases through central interfaces and from a dedicated frequently asked questions database covering municipal competencies. This creates a shared but customisable knowledge base aligned with local administrative needs. The expected impact is faster handling of standard requests, lower administrative effort for routine digital communication and improved service consistency across municipalities. More broadly, the project creates value by giving smaller local authorities a scalable and regionally coordinated way to modernise citizen interaction.

results.company: RTVE – Radiotelevisión Española (Spanish Radio and Television Corporation)
results.title: AI-tool to cover local elections
results.proposal: AI-tool to cover local elections. RTVE developed this use case to solve a persistent media-coverage challenge: local elections in small municipalities generate official results that are highly relevant to residents, yet producing reliable and accessible reporting for every location can be difficult, especially where traditional newsroom resources are limited. The project aimed to ensure that no community would be left without election information, regardless of location, while also improving accessibility for people with visual impairments. The stakeholders include RTVE journalists, audiences in small municipalities and citizens requiring accessible electoral information, with the objective of expanding coverage, improving speed and maintaining trust by basing outputs strictly on official results. The solution is implemented through a tool that automatically drafts written and audio election content using official election data as its sole input source. At a conceptual level, the system combines automated text generation, structured result processing and editorial supervision so that informative, coherent and useful outputs can be produced quickly for municipalities with fewer than 1,000 inhabitants, while remaining extensible to broader electoral coverage. RTVE professionals train and supervise the system to maintain quality and editorial standards. The impact includes wider electoral coverage, faster production and improved information accessibility, especially in smaller localities that might otherwise receive limited attention. More broadly, the tool creates value by supporting public-service media, strengthening democratic information access and reducing the resource barrier to comprehensive local-election reporting.

results.company: Information System Authority of the Republic of Estonia
results.title: Bürokratt – a virtual assistant for the Public Administration
results.proposal: Bürokratt – a virtual assistant for the Public Administration. Estonia’s public sector has sought to simplify how people access government services by reducing the need to navigate multiple agencies, channels and digital systems separately. The underlying operational problem is that citizens and businesses often have to move between different websites, interfaces and institutions to complete related tasks, even when they experience them as part of one life event or administrative need. Bürokratt was conceived to address this fragmentation by creating a more unified service experience in which users can obtain information and complete actions through a single conversational entry point. The stakeholders include citizens, public authorities, national information-system operators and, in some cases, private-sector service providers, with the objective of making service access more seamless, reducing friction and improving the efficiency of digital public administration. The solution is implemented as an interoperable network of public-sector virtual assistants, or “kratts”, connected to national information systems and capable of acting together as one channel from the user’s perspective. At a conceptual level, the system combines conversational interfaces, service orchestration and interoperability across public and selected private systems so that multiple tasks can be handled within one communication session and across devices. The expected impact is a more coherent user experience, reduced channel fragmentation and stronger scalability in digital service delivery. More broadly, Bürokratt creates value by supporting a whole-of-government approach to virtual assistance and making public services more accessible, integrated and citizen-centred.

results.title: Automatic translation in the Land Register search portal and Commercial Register
results.proposal: Automatic translation in the Land Register search portal and Commercial Register. Estonia’s Centre of Registers and Information Systems introduced automatic translation in the e-Land Register and related registry environments to address a practical accessibility problem: non-Estonian speakers often found it difficult to understand detailed registry information, even when they needed only to read and interpret on-screen data rather than obtain a legally binding translation. Registry entries can contain highly technical content, such as information on easements and mortgages, and this can create barriers for foreign users engaging with official systems. The use case therefore involves citizens, businesses and other users of the e-Land Register and Commercial Register, with the objective of improving comprehension of registry data and making these digital public services more accessible internationally. The solution is implemented through a real-time machine translation tool launched in the e-Land Register web environment on 29 October 2021. At a conceptual level, the system uses neural-network-based translation methods that draw links across a large language database and improve over time as vocabulary and patterns are refined. The tool was developed in cooperation between Estonia, Latvia and Belgium, with middleware provided by the Latvian partner TILDE SIA. The translated text is explicitly informative and has no legal force, as Estonian remains the official language of the register. The impact includes improved usability for non-Estonian speakers, greater accessibility of registry information and a more inclusive digital-service experience.

results.proposal: Automatic translation of Riigi Teataja Ametlikud Teadaanded. Estonia’s Official Gazette introduced automated translation to make website content available in English, responding to the need for greater accessibility for foreign businesses and other international stakeholders while preserving Estonian as the only legally binding language. The use case therefore involved the publisher of the official notices service, external technology partners and users who require reliable access to administrative information in a language other than Estonian. Its objective was to support an open business environment and improve usability for non-Estonian speakers, while maintaining clear legal certainty about which language version is authoritative. The solution is implemented through a neural machine translation system developed with Tilde Eesti OÜ and Inversion OÜ and funded 80% by the European Commission. Quality is also monitored and adjusted by the publisher to maintain accuracy and fitness for use. The expected impact is lower translation cost, broader access to official information and improved convenience for foreign stakeholders. results.title: SAFELIGHT project: Analysis of visibility in roads and streets during the night to avoid accidents of vulnerable users
results.proposal: SAFELIGHT project: Analysis of visibility in roads and streets during the night to avoid accidents of vulnerable users. Many urban locations, such as pedestrian crossings, cycle lanes and narrow pavements near traffic, become especially hazardous at night when poor visibility increases the risk of accidents for vulnerable road users. Municipalities often struggle to identify these lighting-related risks systematically, and conventional inspection methods may not be frequent or detailed enough to support timely maintenance decisions. SAFELIGHT addresses this challenge by helping cities detect high-risk locations and improve illumination where it matters most for safety. The stakeholders include host cities, road-maintenance teams, mobility planners and vulnerable users such as pedestrians and cyclists, with the objective of reducing night-time accident risk through better-targeted lighting interventions that can be integrated into ordinary maintenance operations. The solution is implemented through the Autonomous Urban Inspector for Lighting, which analyses road and street visibility using data collected in the urban environment and automatically identifies locations where conditions are unsafe. At a conceptual level, the system combines automated inspection, risk assessment and recommendation functions, after which Flash Lighting proposes the most suitable technical responses for each site. A second inspection is then carried out once lighting changes are implemented in order to validate the improvement in visibility. The expected impact is more precise identification of dangerous locations, more efficient maintenance planning and better evidence for safety interventions. More broadly, SAFELIGHT creates value by providing a scalable, operationally usable method for improving urban lighting and helping reduce accidents involving vulnerable road users.

results.proposal: Customer call analysis -  Finding patterns in the reasons for customer inquiries. The Social Insurance Board needed a clearer understanding of why citizens were contacting its services and where recurring pain points in service delivery were causing confusion, delays or repeated enquiries. Traditional review methods made it difficult to obtain both a broad statistical overview and a detailed picture of issues emerging across multiple communication channels. This use case therefore focused on helping managers identify patterns in customer concerns more quickly so that services could be improved in a targeted and timely way. The pilot involved an information-line manager and two service managers, with the objective of generating insights that would support managerial decision-making and lead to faster, more convenient public services. The solution was implemented with Feelingstream, which analysed customer contacts across calls, emails and chatbot interactions. During the pilot, calls from May to August 2020 were transcribed in Estonian and Russian, enabling the system to detect themes and recurring reasons for contact across language groups. At a conceptual level, the approach combines transcription, multilingual text analysis and cross-channel pattern detection to turn customer-contact data into actionable service intelligence. The expected impact is faster identification of service problems, better prioritisation of improvements and more informed management decisions. In practice, this enhances efficiency, improves the citizen experience and creates value by linking everyday customer interactions directly to service redesign.

results.company: Department of Mobility and Public Works (MOW)
results.title: Clearance of dumped war ammunition in the North Sea
results.proposal: Clearance of dumped war ammunition in the North Sea. On the North Sea sandbank De Paardenmarkt near Knokke, around 35,000 tonnes of First World War ammunition, including both conventional and chemical munitions, remain buried beneath the seabed. Although the site is currently regarded as stable, long-term risks persist as corrosion progresses and external factors such as ship strikes could trigger severe pollution, threaten marine safety and constrain coastal and port development. The Flemish government’s Maritime Access department launched this use case to test practical methods for addressing the problem safely and cost-effectively, with the objective of evaluating whether a larger-scale clean-up could be undertaken without creating unacceptable risks for people or the marine environment. The solution is being trialled through a combination of precision detection, environmental monitoring, sediment removal, deepening operations and robotic recovery of buried ammunition. At a conceptual level, the approach integrates seabed sensing, risk monitoring, controlled excavation and remote-handling technologies to locate and retrieve hazardous objects while limiting direct human exposure and minimising ecological disturbance. The expected impact is better understanding of feasible remediation methods, reduced uncertainty around operational risk and stronger preparedness for a full-scale clean-up. In strategic terms, the project supports environmental protection, enhances coastal safety and may unlock future value by reducing obstacles to maritime infrastructure and port development.
results.memo: Proceed. Clearance of dumped war ammunition in the North Sea is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Naamsestraat - Reduce night noise through technology and nudging
results.proposal: Naamsestraat - Reduce night noise through technology and nudging. Naamsestraat in Leuven is a busy transit route for people returning home after a night out, and this regularly generates disturbance for residents through late-night noise. The City of Leuven is addressing this as part of a broader strategy on nightlife nuisance in which preventive and enforcement measures are intended to work together. The use case therefore focuses on making the street more liveable while preserving the vitality of the city centre, involving municipal authorities and a range of local partners with the objective of detecting disturbing noise more accurately, understanding when and where it occurs, and intervening at the right moment. The solution is being developed as a living lab combining real-time data capture, objectified recognition of disturbing night noise, nudging techniques and predictive intervention planning. At a conceptual level, the implementation uses automated sound recognition to define and map nuisance, links live detections to behavioural nudges in the street environment, and supports scheduling of interventions through predictive models that identify likely high-disturbance moments. This creates a dynamic feedback loop between monitoring and action rather than relying solely on retrospective complaint handling. The expected impact is reduced nuisance, more targeted deployment of municipal measures and an improved nighttime environment for residents. More broadly, the initiative enhances urban liveability, supports evidence-based public-space management and creates a scalable model for tackling nightlife-related disturbance.

results.title: Innovative functionalities and AI for energy saving in the public sector
results.proposal: Innovative functionalities and AI for energy saving in the public sector. The Flemish public sector manages a large and diverse portfolio of buildings and infrastructure, yet turning building and energy data into practical action remains a complex task. Within the Terra patrimony and energy database, substantial information already exists on asset characteristics and energy performance, but the challenge lies in using that information actively and systematically to identify savings opportunities, support renewable energy projects and guide long-term property strategy. This use case brings together VEB, Facilities and Services, and VEA, with the objective of improving how public-sector energy data is used to detect inefficiencies faster, plan interventions more effectively and monitor energy-saving measures with greater precision. The solution explores smart data use through advanced analytics, asset analysis and measurement models, while also assessing where algorithmic methods and a Software-as-a-Service model could add value. At a conceptual level, the approach uses the Terra database as the central information layer for identifying energy-saving potential, informing real-estate strategies, supporting the initiation and monitoring of OEPC contracts, and creating synergies with other digital and sustainability initiatives. The expected impact is earlier identification of savings opportunities, better-managed energy programmes and stronger evidence for investment decisions. In business and operational terms, the initiative supports cost reduction, improves the scalability of energy management and increases the long-term value of public assets through more informed and professionally managed interventions.

results.proposal: Smart Personalisation of the cultural offer in Antwerp Testing (SOCRATES). The City of Antwerp and Digipolis launched SOCRATES to address a growing challenge in cultural participation: citizens are exposed to a broad and fragmented cultural offer, yet it is often difficult to connect individuals with activities and content that genuinely match their interests. The project therefore focuses on whether a more tailored, user-driven cultural experience can increase engagement and improve how residents discover literature, events and other cultural opportunities. The stakeholders include the city, Digipolis, cultural users and the wider digital-services ecosystem around Antwerp’s public platforms, with the objective of testing the feasibility and usefulness of an individual cultural profile that can power more relevant recommendations. The solution is implemented through a Digital Experience Platform built around a personal culture profile and enriched by recommendation logic, described as a “wonder algorithm”, that can suggest suitable cultural content. At a conceptual level, the platform is designed modularly so that it can connect with existing and future architecture, especially Antwerp City Platform as a Service, which already offers reusable backend components. SOCRATES extends this model to application front ends and digital touchpoints, allowing the user’s “digital cultural DNA” to inform personalised suggestions. The expected impact is more relevant cultural discovery, better use of digital channels and stronger engagement with Antwerp’s cultural offer. More broadly, the project creates value by testing a scalable, interoperable model for citizen-centred cultural personalisation.

results.proposal: AI platform for agri-food applications from field to fork. The use case therefore focuses on helping ILVO researchers make better use of the information already being produced, while reducing the barriers that prevent advanced data methods from being used routinely in day-to-day work. Internal stakeholders across research and innovation teams were involved in defining the needs, with the objective of creating a platform that broadens access to data-driven methods and improves the speed and consistency of analysis from field to fork. results.title: NER-based extraction of contract data
results.proposal: NER-based extraction of contract data. Public bodies that handle large volumes of incoming correspondence and forms often face a difficult administrative problem: important information is buried in siloed documents and must be extracted manually before it can be reused in central systems. Smals, as an ICT provider for government, explored this challenge with public-sector partners such as the RSZ/ONSS, where the broader aim was to support data centralisation and reduce the effort required to process incoming material. The use case focused on extracting structured information from emails and forms, including names, roles and telephone numbers, so that staff could move faster from unstructured documents to usable records. The stakeholders include administrative teams, ICT specialists and the government bodies seeking to consolidate data sources, with the objective of improving efficiency while retaining sufficient control over data quality. The solution was implemented through named-entity recognition and related natural-language-processing techniques applied to scanned documents and digital correspondence. At a conceptual level, the system first converts paper-based material into machine-readable text through scanning and OCR, then applies entity-extraction models to identify specific data fields. The proof-of-concept work showed that highly structured information can be captured with reasonable effectiveness, while context-dependent elements such as job functions remain more difficult to interpret reliably. The impact lies in reduced manual effort and better support for mailroom and intake automation, but also in a clearer understanding of the limits of current extraction tools, including the need for human validation where full accuracy cannot be guaranteed.

results.title: Cultural Heritage Tools - AI tools integrated in the National Library of Finland
results.proposal: Cultural Heritage Tools - AI tools integrated in the National Library of Finland. Two AI tools have been integrated into the IT system of the National Library of Finland (digi.nationallibrary.fi): 1. Named entity recognition (NER) -Stanford NER software to recognize persons and place names from the Finnish historical newspapers. The first training and evaluation data set was created that consists of pages of both journals and newspapers from the time period 1836–1918. The Stanford NER system was trained using 220 annotated pages and evaluated using 34 pages. The results that were achieved were mostly good: 71 % of person names and 79 % of place names were recognized from the evaluation data. 2. Image classification -Google TensorFlow was used to classify images. A training dataset was created that was used to train the classifier model with TensorFlow. Using the trained model, it was possible to classify images into the following groups: advertisements, drawings, notes, pictures, paintings, maps or garbage. -The trained model was used to classify 50 000 images and its accuracy was about 70-75% when about 10 000 classified images were manually observed. -A graphical user interface was created that enabled an easier way to observe achieved results.

results.title: Tool to optimise self-consumption in residential sectors
results.proposal: Tool to optimise self-consumption in residential sectors. Households and residential communities increasingly want to make better use of locally generated renewable electricity, but optimising self-consumption is difficult because it depends on understanding both generation patterns and highly variable consumption behaviour. In practice, selecting the right system size and managing hourly distribution of photovoltaic output across users requires forecasting that most available tools do not support well. This use case was therefore designed to help residential users and energy planners develop more efficient self-consumption scenarios and better align local renewable generation with actual demand. The stakeholders include energy users, installers, planners and potentially grid operators, with the objective of improving self-consumption rates, supporting system sizing and enabling more efficient use of distributed renewable energy. The solution is implemented through a set of tools built around three modules: recruitment, planning and execution. At a conceptual level, the platform combines consumption forecasting, photovoltaic production forecasting and optimisation techniques to calculate hourly distribution coefficients and recommend self-consumption scenarios. In addition, automatically generated statistical profiles by user type help determine the optimal number of PV panels during earlier planning stages. The expected impact is better use of renewable generation, more accurate system sizing and reduced difficulty in planning residential self-consumption schemes. More broadly, the tool creates value by helping users adapt consumption habits, supporting future grid-stability services and enabling a more data-driven, scalable approach to distributed energy management.

results.title: IRIS - Support system for classification of citizen inquiries or complaints
results.proposal: IRIS - Support system for classification of citizen inquiries or complaints. Barcelona City Council relies on IRIS as the channel through which citizens report incidents, submit complaints and suggest service improvements, yet the effectiveness of the process depends heavily on the initial thematic classification chosen by the user. If an incident is assigned to the wrong category, it can be routed to the wrong department, causing delays and reducing service quality. The operational problem was therefore to simplify classification for citizens while improving routing accuracy inside the council. The use case involves residents, the IRIS service and the municipal departments responsible for resolving reported incidents, with the objective of speeding up response times, reducing classification errors and improving the overall quality of citizen service. The solution is implemented through MARIO, a machine-learning-based module developed as part of the IRIS update. At a conceptual level, the module analyses the free text entered by the user and suggests the most likely categories into which the incident fits, allowing the citizen to choose the most appropriate option with guidance from the system. This creates a more intelligent classification layer at the point of submission and reduces the reliance on later manual correction. The reported impact is substantial: whereas previously around 50% of communications had to be reassigned, MARIO now achieves a hit rate of over 85%. More broadly, the project creates value by improving routing efficiency, reducing rework and making citizen reporting more reliable and user-friendly.
results.memo: Proceed. IRIS - Support system for classification of citizen inquiries or complaints is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Federal Office for Security in Information Technology (Bundesamt für Sicherheit in der Informationstechnik - BSI)
results.title: Enhancing metadata for textual information - improving the quality of search and automatic reasoning
results.proposal: Enhancing metadata for textual information - improving the quality of search and automatic reasoning. Public organisations working with large volumes of unstructured information on IT security need better ways to search, interpret and reuse textual content that is often fragmented across news, reports and background material. The operational challenge is that pure text alone is difficult to query with precision, especially when words have multiple meanings or when users need systems to support more advanced reasoning rather than simple keyword lookup. This use case therefore focuses on improving the metadata attached to unstructured textual information so that search quality and automated reasoning can be strengthened. The stakeholders include the BSI, analysts and users of IT-security information, with the objective of creating cleaner, more structured and more semantically useful text resources for retrieval and analysis. The solution is implemented by first creating a corpus of publicly available IT-security news and background texts, pre-processing it to remove artefacts and technical noise, and then enriching it through a combination of semantic and statistical methods. At a conceptual level, manually created taxonomies and ontologies, using standards such as SKOS, are combined with machine-learning approaches that capture local context and support named-entity extraction, while transformer-based NLP models are applied to tasks such as entity recognition, classification and question answering. The impact is expected to include higher-quality search, more reusable metadata and better support for automated interpretation, creating value through improved information access and stronger analytical capability in cybersecurity knowledge management.
results.memo: Proceed. Enhancing metadata for textual information - improving the quality of search and automatic reasoning is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Assessment security properties of Symmetric Ciphers - Supporting assessment of security properties of cryptographic algorithms
results.proposal: Assessment security properties of Symmetric Ciphers - Supporting assessment of security properties of cryptographic algorithms. Assessing the security strength of cryptographic algorithms is a technically demanding task, yet it is essential for organisations that rely on encryption to protect sensitive information. In the case of symmetric ciphers, security assessment often requires specialised expertise and careful analysis of whether the cipher can be distinguished from random behaviour under different conditions. This use case was developed to support that evaluation process and to investigate whether advanced computational methods can assist experts in solving cryptographic problems more efficiently. The stakeholders include the BSI, cryptography specialists and organisations that depend on trustworthy encryption mechanisms, with the objective of improving the assessment of cipher security and strengthening the analytical basis for selecting secure algorithms. The solution is implemented through a tool based on deep neural networks. At a conceptual level, the model is trained to distinguish ciphertext pairs produced by round-reduced symmetric ciphers from random text, thereby producing a coarse estimate of the security level that a given cipher may provide. This allows the tool to act as an analytical aid within a broader cryptographic study rather than as a definitive replacement for expert evaluation. The expected impact is faster exploratory assessment, improved support for security analysis and a stronger evidence base for cryptographic review. More broadly, the project creates value by opening a new line of support for complex cipher evaluation within information-security research.
results.memo: Proceed. Assessment security properties of Symmetric Ciphers - Supporting assessment of security properties of cryptographic algorithms is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Detection causes early school leavers Kungsbacka - Analysing data of early school leavers
results.proposal: Detection causes early school leavers Kungsbacka - Analysing data of early school leavers. Each year in Kungsbacka, around 100 students move from primary school to upper secondary education without the eligibility required to continue successfully, creating a significant concern for educators and local authorities. The operational challenge is that current analysis of this problem has been limited largely to grades and has been carried out manually, which restricts the ability to uncover broader patterns and understand the full range of contributing factors. This use case was developed to help the organisation gain a deeper and more proactive understanding of why some students are at risk of early educational disengagement, with the objective of identifying underlying causes earlier and enabling preventive intervention. The stakeholders include school leaders, education staff and students at risk of exclusion from further education pathways, and the initiative also serves as a first step towards wider use of advanced analytical tools in the organisation. The solution is implemented through analytical technology applied to data on students transitioning without eligibility. At a conceptual level, the system is intended to move beyond manual grade-based review by examining a wider set of patterns and relationships in available student data, helping to surface contributing factors that may not be obvious through conventional analysis alone. The expected impact is better understanding of educational risk, stronger capacity for early intervention and a more evidence-based foundation for support measures. More broadly, the project creates value by improving educational planning and opening the way for broader data-driven improvement across other service areas.

results.title: Object Detection Kit Amsterdam - Automatic detection of garbage
results.proposal: Object Detection Kit Amsterdam - Automatic detection of garbage. Amsterdam introduced the Object Detection Kit to address a highly visible and operationally demanding urban-management issue: waste placed incorrectly in public space, especially near underground containers, was affecting street cleanliness and requiring frequent reporting and intervention. Manual reporting by residents and reactive clean-up processes created inefficiencies, delayed response and placed unnecessary burden both on citizens and municipal waste services. The use case therefore involves the municipality, waste-removal teams and local residents, with the objective of keeping public spaces cleaner while deploying removal services more efficiently and reducing the need for residents to report misplaced rubbish repeatedly. The solution is implemented through the open-source Object Detection Kit, a platform initiated by Amsterdam to detect rubbish in public space automatically. At a conceptual level, the system uses object-detection techniques to scan public areas, identify waste items visually and transmit this information directly to the service responsible for removing that category of rubbish. This creates an automated chain from detection to operational response, allowing waste issues to be addressed more proactively. The impact includes faster identification of rubbish hotspots, more efficient deployment of cleaning resources and less reliance on citizen reporting. More broadly, ODK creates value by improving the cleanliness of urban environments, reducing operational friction and offering a scalable open-source model that other municipalities can potentially adapt to their own waste-management challenges.

results.title: Calculemus FLINT - Ensuring understandability of normative law texts
results.proposal: Calculemus FLINT - Ensuring understandability of normative law texts. Legal and policy rules are often difficult to interpret consistently, particularly when different professional groups or affected citizens need to understand how norms should be applied in practice. This creates challenges not only for legislative drafting and legal analysis, but also for the legitimacy and acceptance of decisions made under complex regulatory frameworks. Calculemus FLINT was developed to address this problem by making normative legal texts more understandable, more formally interpretable and easier to test for executability. The stakeholders include policymakers, legislative lawyers and citizens subject to legal rules, with the objective of improving the exchange, interpretation and explanation of norms across different groups while supporting more transparent and accountable implementation. The solution is implemented through a paired method and language framework: Calculemus as a roadmap for solving normative questions, and FLINT as a formal domain-specific language for interpreting judicial and normative sources. At a conceptual level, the approach translates legal norms into structured formal representations that allow rules to be analysed, compared and tested more systematically. This can help explain whether laws are operationally executable and whether decisions made under them can be justified clearly. The impact is primarily qualitative, centred on greater interpretability, improved legal transparency and stronger normative grounding for automated or assisted decisions. More broadly, the method creates value by increasing confidence in rule-based public administration and supporting clearer communication between legal experts, policymakers and citizens.

results.title: Debt relief - Chatbot to assist people with debts
results.proposal: Debt relief - Chatbot to assist people with debts. Many people experiencing debt problems struggle to find the right form of help quickly, particularly when they do not know which service to contact or feel overwhelmed by the complexity of support pathways. This creates a significant access problem in debt relief, as delays in finding appropriate advice can worsen financial hardship and make later intervention more difficult. The project, developed through a collaboration between IBM and the Municipality of Rotterdam, was designed to make local debt-relief support easier and faster to reach. The stakeholders include debtors, municipal support services and debt-assistance providers, with the objective of lowering access barriers, guiding people to the most suitable support route and improving the overall responsiveness of debt-relief services. The solution is implemented partly through a chatbot that asks a series of key questions in order to determine the most appropriate next step for the person concerned. At a conceptual level, the system uses structured conversational triage and decision logic to assess the user’s situation and route them towards the correct entry path for debt support. This creates a more accessible first contact point than leaving individuals to navigate multiple service options unaided. The impact includes quicker orientation into support pathways, reduced confusion for users and a more efficient front door for debt-relief services. More broadly, the project creates value by improving early access to assistance and helping local authorities organise debt-support journeys more effectively.

results.title: AI for detecting illegal substances -  AI to index seized data carrier
results.proposal: AI for detecting illegal substances -  AI to index seized data carrier. The Netherlands Forensic Institute needed a faster and more effective way to review large volumes of seized digital material in investigations where images of illegal substances might be present. Manual searching through data carriers is time-consuming and can slow investigative progress, especially when detectives must examine extensive collections of low-quality or mixed-content images. The use case was therefore developed to support forensic and investigative teams by accelerating the indexing of seized data and helping them locate potentially relevant material more efficiently. The stakeholders include forensic analysts, detectives and criminal-investigation units, with the objective of reducing review time, improving search precision and increasing the effectiveness of digital evidence analysis. The solution is implemented through a workflow in which seized data carriers are indexed and their contents scanned for images likely to depict illegal substances. At a conceptual level, the development process involved labelling examples of illegal substances, selecting an appropriate model architecture based on pre-trained deep-learning methods and then fine-tuning the model to perform better on low-quality images. This creates a practical classification layer that can highlight potentially relevant material for further expert examination rather than requiring investigators to inspect all data manually. The impact includes faster evidence handling, improved investigative productivity and more efficient use of forensic resources. More broadly, the system creates value by strengthening digital-forensics capability and allowing law-enforcement teams to focus their efforts more effectively on high-priority material.
results.memo: Proceed. AI for detecting illegal substances -  AI to index seized data carrier is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Tracing potential victims of human trafficking and labour exploitation with AI
results.proposal: Tracing potential victims of human trafficking and labour exploitation with AI. Labour exploitation and human trafficking are difficult to detect because warning signs are often hidden within ordinary-looking financial activity, making traditional investigation methods slow and resource-intensive. To address this, the Inspectorate SZW collaborated with ABN AMRO and the University of Amsterdam to identify patterns in banking data that may indicate possible cases of labour exploitation. The use case does not aim to detect perpetrators directly at the initial stage, but to help authorities identify potential victims more effectively and trigger further investigation where justified. The stakeholders include labour inspectors, banks, researchers, the Financial Intelligence Unit and, ultimately, prosecutors and judges, with the objective of strengthening early detection while preserving human control over escalatory decisions. The solution is implemented through pattern-recognition scripts applied to banking data using risk patterns supplied by the Inspectorate. At a conceptual level, the scripts search for relevant transactional connections, after which human reviewers check the output for false positives. If a pattern is validated, it may justify a further FIU investigation into suspicious transactions, which can then support legal escalation and, where authorised, access to address and transaction details for tracing potential victims. Machine-learning refinement and expansion to four other major banks are under consideration. The impact lies in earlier and more targeted identification, improved investigative efficiency and stronger inter-institutional cooperation in combating labour exploitation.

results.title: Automation subsidy requirements - Application for a subsidy are examined by AI algorithm
results.proposal: Automation subsidy requirements - Application for a subsidy are examined by AI algorithm. The Province of South Holland introduced this use case to address a practical barrier to household sustainability: many homeowners wanted to make their homes more energy-efficient but lacked the financial means to do so. To support this group, the province offered subsidies of between EUR 300 and EUR 3,000 to homeowners whose property value was EUR 200,000 or less, provided that they had taken measures to improve the sustainability of their homes. The operational challenge was that reviewing applications manually was slow, costly and difficult to scale, which delayed support and limited administrative efficiency. The stakeholders therefore included homeowners, subsidy administrators and provincial programme managers, with the objective of accelerating application handling, reducing processing costs and ensuring that eligible applicants received support more quickly. The solution is implemented through automated assessment based on cluster data analysis and rule-based eligibility evaluation. At a conceptual level, the system analyses application data to identify likely eligible cases and processes them automatically, while directing uncertain cases to human staff for review so that applications are not rejected solely by the system. The project was delivered using an innovation-oriented methodology involving funnels, scrum and product owners. The impact includes a reduction in processing time from weeks to days, improved administrative scalability and lower handling costs. More broadly, the initiative creates value by speeding up access to sustainability support and making the subsidy scheme more efficient and citizen-friendly.
results.memo: Proceed. Automation subsidy requirements - Application for a subsidy are examined by AI algorithm is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Vegetation detection Friesland - Remote sensing and image recognition to interpret satellite images
results.proposal: Vegetation detection Friesland - Remote sensing and image recognition to interpret satellite images. The Province of Friesland needed a more efficient and timely way to monitor vegetation on the Dutch Wadden Islands, where traditional field-based registration had been carried out only once every six or twelve years by inspectors travelling to the islands. This approach was both labour-intensive and too infrequent to provide the up-to-date environmental insight needed for effective management. The use case therefore focused on improving how authorities assess the current state of vegetation, with the added importance that many plant communities in the area are sensitive to nitrogen, making accurate vegetation monitoring relevant for broader environmental modelling as well. The stakeholders include provincial authorities, environmental inspectors and ecological planners, with the objective of creating a more scalable and current monitoring method while retaining expert oversight for uncertain cases. The solution is implemented through remote sensing and image-recognition techniques applied to satellite imagery. At a conceptual level, the system analyses satellite data to classify vegetation patterns across the islands, while areas that are difficult to interpret automatically are flagged for manual review by inspectors. This creates a hybrid workflow that combines large-scale automated screening with targeted expert validation. The expected impact is more frequent and less labour-intensive vegetation monitoring, better environmental intelligence and stronger support for nitrogen modelling. More broadly, the approach creates value by improving ecological oversight, reducing fieldwork burden and enabling a more responsive approach to landscape management.
results.memo: Proceed. Vegetation detection Friesland - Remote sensing and image recognition to interpret satellite images is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Project ML-SAST - Machine Learning in the Context of Static Application Security Testing
results.proposal: Project ML-SAST - Machine Learning in the Context of Static Application Security Testing. The Federal Office for Information Security launched the ML-SAST project to address a pressing software-security problem: identifying vulnerabilities and coding errors early enough in the development process to reduce remediation effort, shorten delivery times and improve the overall security of software systems. Static Application Security Testing is already used to examine source code without executing it, but conventional approaches can struggle to recognise new or evolving error patterns efficiently. The use case therefore involves the BSI, software-security researchers and development teams, with the objective of strengthening automated code analysis and exploring whether more adaptive methods can make security testing more effective and less burdensome. The solution is implemented as a staged research and development effort focused on applying machine-learning techniques to static security testing. At a conceptual level, the project begins with a feasibility study and literature review to identify the most suitable model families for detecting code patterns associated with vulnerabilities. On the basis of those findings, an open-source prototype is then developed to demonstrate the method in practice. This combines pattern-recognition strengths from machine learning with the static-analysis context of software assurance. The expected impact is more secure software, lower manual workload for developers and shorter development cycles. More broadly, ML-SAST creates value by exploring a scalable route towards earlier and more autonomous vulnerability detection in software engineering.
results.memo: Proceed. Project ML-SAST - Machine Learning in the Context of Static Application Security Testing is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Scout.AI - Analyse the information recorded within the SNS 24 TAE Service
results.proposal: Scout.AI - Analyse the information recorded within the SNS 24 TAE Service. The SNS 24 Triage, Counselling and Referral Service handles a very large volume of calls across Portugal and plays an important role in ensuring equitable access to healthcare advice. In 2018 alone, more than 1 million calls were answered, each lasting on average seven to eight minutes, and nurses relied on one of 59 predefined clinical algorithms to triage callers and decide on the most appropriate referral. The operational challenge is that choosing the right algorithm is critical to both patient safety and service efficiency: the selected pathway must avoid missing urgent situations while also discriminating effectively between cases. The use case therefore involves nurses, the SNS 24 Contact Centre and the Directorate-General of Health, with the objective of improving algorithm selection in real time and strengthening the design of the clinical algorithms themselves. The solution is implemented through decision-support models trained on anonymised SNS 24 contact data from 2017 and 2018, representing around 2 million cases. At a conceptual level, the system uses classification methods to recommend the most appropriate clinical algorithms for a given symptom profile, adjusted for age and sex, and is then integrated into the TAE workflow as real-time support for nurses. The expected impact is safer and more consistent triage, reduced uncertainty in algorithm choice and better-informed optimisation of referral logic, creating value through improved clinical decision support and more effective telephone-based healthcare access.

results.title: Intelligent mechanisms for clinical evaluation - Facilitate the reconciliation of citizens
results.proposal: Intelligent mechanisms for clinical evaluation - Facilitate the reconciliation of citizens. Vimercate Local Health Authority sought to reconcile two competing pressures in hospital care: offering citizens the best possible treatment while reducing the time clinicians spend on administrative and forecasting tasks that take them away from patients. In departments such as diabetology, nephrology and internal medicine, doctors must assess patients daily in order to estimate likely discharge times, the risk of complications and the possibility of readmission, including urgent readmission, both for those currently in treatment and for those in protected discharge. The objective of this use case was therefore to improve clinical evaluation and operational planning at the same time, enabling the facility to maintain continuity of care while optimising resources and reducing costs. The solution is implemented through machine-learning mechanisms that support doctors by analysing larger volumes of clinical information and generating suggestions more quickly than manual review alone. At a conceptual level, the system processes patient conditions and historical treatment patterns to assist with predictions regarding discharge timing, complication risk and readmission likelihood, integrating these outputs into daily clinical assessment workflows. This does not replace medical judgement but augments it with faster, broader analytical support. The expected impact includes reduced administrative burden on doctors, more timely and informed clinical predictions, better bed and care-capacity planning and improved service continuity. More broadly, the initiative creates value through better operational efficiency, stronger patient management and a more sustainable balance between care quality and hospital resource use.

results.title: Decision on the Maternity Benefit (TÉBA) - The Family Support Scheme of the Hungarian State Treasury
results.proposal: Decision on the Maternity Benefit (TÉBA) - The Family Support Scheme of the Hungarian State Treasury. The Hungarian State Treasury introduced the TÉBA system to address a structural administrative problem in family support: benefits such as family and disability allowances were managed across different databases and processes, making it harder to deliver a unified, efficient and citizen-centred service. Fragmented data access can slow decision-making, increase duplication and make it more difficult for public bodies to manage entitlements consistently. This use case was therefore designed to improve the management of maternity-related and other family support benefits by integrating or guaranteeing access to the relevant information sources required for decision-making. The stakeholders include the State Treasury, benefit administrators and citizens applying for family-related support, with the objective of simplifying administration, improving coordination across databases and making benefits management more coherent and efficient. The solution is implemented through a system architecture that connects or provides access to multiple public databases involved in family and disability allowance administration. At a conceptual level, TÉBA functions as an integration layer that enables the Treasury to consolidate the information needed for benefit assessment and payment within a more unified workflow, reducing fragmentation in case handling. Although the source provides limited quantitative detail, the expected impact lies in faster processing, improved consistency and lower administrative overhead. More broadly, the system creates value by modernising benefits administration, supporting better data availability and enabling a more integrated public-service model for family support.

results.title: Véda-KAFIR-ROBOTZSARU (‘Robocop’) - System Operated by the Police for Traffic Safety Automated Processing
results.proposal: Véda-KAFIR-ROBOTZSARU (‘Robocop’) - System Operated by the Police for Traffic Safety Automated Processing. Hungary’s road-safety enforcement authorities needed a faster and more integrated way to process large volumes of traffic violations with minimal delay and consistent evidential handling. Manual processing of speeding and related road-traffic offences can be time-consuming and vulnerable to bottlenecks, particularly when evidence must be matched against vehicle registries and then transferred into case-management systems. This use case therefore aims to streamline enforcement by linking roadside capture, data verification and administrative processing in a single workflow. The stakeholders include the police, responsible enforcement authorities and road users, with the objective of improving traffic-safety enforcement, accelerating case handling and reducing administrative friction in the imposition of fines. The solution is implemented through the Véda intelligent camera network, which feeds data into KAFIR, the Traffic Safety Automated Processing and Information System, and then into the police’s broader Robotzsaru records and case-management platform. At a conceptual level, the cameras capture the vehicle registration number, speed, location coordinates, date and time, after which KAFIR cross-checks this information against the traffic registry, for example to determine whether a vehicle is stolen, and uploads the data into Robotzsaru. The files are then classified and sent to the competent authority without human intervention at that stage, followed by an ex post administrative check. results.title: Estimation of income of self-employed and SMES who pay taxes by module
results.proposal: Estimation of income of self-employed and SMES who pay taxes by module. In Spain, certain self-employed workers and small and medium-sized enterprises may opt to pay taxes under a modular system rather than declaring their exact income. While this simplifies compliance for taxpayers, it creates an analytical challenge for the tax administration because exact income figures are not directly available for this group, yet they are still needed for the calculation of ratios, statistics and broader economic analysis. This use case was designed to estimate the likely income of those taxpayers more accurately so that official statistical and analytical work can be based on more robust information. The stakeholders include the tax administration, statistical and analytical teams, and indirectly the wider policy community that relies on income-based indicators, with the objective of improving the quality of tax-based estimates without changing the underlying tax regime. The solution is implemented through predictive estimation based on a wider comparison population of taxpayers with similar characteristics who do declare exact income, as well as taxpayers who switch between the modular system and direct declaration from one period to the next. At a conceptual level, the system uses these comparable datasets to infer likely income levels for the target population and feeds the resulting estimates into the calculation of income-related indicators. The impact is improved statistical reliability, stronger analytical precision and better consistency in fiscal reporting, creating value through more accurate measurement and more useful evidence for policy and administration.

results.proposal: Notification procedure - Automatic control of accident occurring at the workplace. Previously, suspected cases were forwarded through a standardised document flow to a central office, where they were manually pre-checked, creating a slow and resource-intensive process across large case volumes. This use case was developed to improve prioritisation and support case handlers with more structured evidence before they decide whether to pursue recourse. The stakeholders include the insurance association, recourse departments and case officers, with the objective of increasing efficiency, improving the quality of triage and strengthening decisions on whether legal recovery is worthwhile. The solution is implemented using a model trained on around one million completed recourse and subrogation proceedings, both successful and unsuccessful. At a conceptual level, the system estimates the plausibility of a potential recourse action, forecasts the likely probability of success and predicts the level of total costs. In parallel, text-mining methods identify critical keywords, such as whether the police were called or whether an assault occurred, to provide additional decision support. These outputs are delivered through a web interface for the recourse department. The impact is faster pre-assessment, better-informed case selection and reduced manual effort, with broader value in improving consistency, focusing resources on higher-potential cases and making recourse management more scalable.

results.title: Study certificates - Automatic recognition for applying for child benefit
results.proposal: Study certificates - Automatic recognition for applying for child benefit. Family benefits offices in Germany face a recurring administrative burden because, to maintain eligibility for child benefit, a student’s current certificate of enrolment must be submitted twice a year. The problem is compounded by the lack of a uniform certificate format across German universities, which means that large volumes of heterogeneous documents must be checked manually. This use case was introduced to reduce processing effort, improve consistency and accelerate validation while retaining staff oversight. The stakeholders include applicants, family benefits offices and case-handling staff, with the objective of making the verification of study certificates faster, more reliable and less labour-intensive. The solution is implemented through a workflow in which the applicant uploads the certificate via a web portal, the text is extracted using optical character recognition, and the resulting content is classified automatically. At a conceptual level, the system checks four points: whether the document is a study certificate, whether it relates to the correct child, whether the semester or validity period is correct, and whether the issuing institution is a recognised German university. The result is displayed within the specialist procedure and must be actively accepted by an employee. The training base currently includes 60,000 semi-automatically annotated certificates, anonymised with a dedicated algorithm, and the classification combines Naive Bayes, Support Vector Machine, Logistic Regression, natural language processing and named-entity recognition. The impact is improved efficiency, reduced manual workload and more scalable certificate processing.

results.title: SKOSA - Interpreting medical information
results.proposal: SKOSA - Interpreting medical information. Administrators handling health-related casework often need to review large volumes of medical information and translate complex clinical material into structured assessments that support benefit or needs-related decisions. This is a demanding process because medical records can be detailed, inconsistent in format and difficult for non-clinical staff to interpret without support. SKOSA was developed to address this challenge by helping administrators analyse, structure and understand medical information more effectively when conducting needs assessments. The stakeholders include public administrators, medical experts and case-handling organisations responsible for decisions influenced by health information, with the objective of improving consistency, reducing interpretative burden and strengthening the quality of assessment processes. The solution is implemented as a general platform with a digital knowledge base built in collaboration with doctors and other subject-matter experts. At a conceptual level, the system combines expert-curated knowledge structures with analytical support tools that help caseworkers organise medical data, identify relevant information and interpret it within a decision-support context. Rather than replacing professional judgement, the platform is designed to make medical evidence more accessible and usable in administrative workflows. The expected impact is more efficient case handling, better-structured use of health information and improved consistency in needs assessments. More broadly, SKOSA creates value by reducing the cognitive load on administrators, supporting more reliable decisions and building a reusable infrastructure for interpreting complex medical evidence in public administration.

results.title: Tengai - Robot in recruitment processes
results.proposal: Tengai - Robot in recruitment processes. Upplands-Bro Municipality began using Tengai in June 2019 to address a persistent challenge in recruitment: reducing bias in candidate selection while maintaining a structured and efficient hiring process. Traditional interviews can be influenced by subjective impressions, inconsistent questioning and uneven evaluation practices, which may affect fairness and the quality of shortlist decisions. The use case therefore involved the municipality’s recruitment and staffing agency, hiring managers and job candidates, with the objective of making recruitment more impartial, standardised and evidence-based while preserving a final human assessment of motivation and fit. The solution was implemented through Tengai, one of the first social interview robots, developed in collaboration between municipal staff and Furhat Robotics. At a conceptual level, the system first identifies candidates with the highest general performance scores to create a shortlist, then conducts structured interviews in which it assesses behaviour, problem-solving ability and other competencies, including the ability to ask follow-up questions where needed. These interview outputs are combined with competency scores and passed on to recruiters, who then carry out the final interview stage. The first results were regarded as successful, and the service was adopted permanently within a week of release. The impact included a more standardised interview process, reduced exposure to bias in early screening and significant reputational value through national and international media attention to the municipality’s innovative recruitment approach.

results.title: Robotic System Da Vinci
results.proposal: Robotic System Da Vinci. Hospitals and surgical teams continually seek ways to perform delicate and complex operations with greater precision, less trauma to the patient and shorter recovery times, particularly in procedures where conventional open surgery may involve larger incisions and longer rehabilitation. The da Vinci Surgical System addresses this challenge by supporting minimally invasive surgery in situations where high dexterity and fine control are especially important. The stakeholders include surgeons, hospital teams and patients undergoing complex procedures, with the objective of improving surgical performance, reducing the physical burden of operations on patients and expanding the range of procedures that can be carried out through small incisions. The solution is implemented as a robotic-assisted surgical platform that enables surgeons to operate through a limited number of small entry points while controlling instruments with enhanced precision. At a conceptual level, the system combines robotic arms, surgeon-controlled interfaces and high-definition visualisation to translate the surgeon’s movements into highly controlled instrument actions inside the body. This allows intricate procedures to be performed with a level of stability and manoeuvrability that can exceed conventional laparoscopy in certain contexts. The impact includes more precise surgical intervention, reduced invasiveness and potential improvements in patient recovery and hospital efficiency. More broadly, the da Vinci system creates value by modernising the surgical theatre, improving the quality of complex operations and supporting a more advanced model of minimally invasive care.

results.title: VeriPol - Detect false police reports
results.proposal: VeriPol - Detect false police reports. False police reports, especially for low-level offences, consume investigative resources, distort crime recording and can be linked to wider fraudulent behaviour, making them a costly problem for law-enforcement agencies. In Spain, the National Police adopted VeriPol to help identify reports that may be fabricated and to improve the efficiency of case handling within existing policing workflows. The stakeholders include police officers, investigators and administrative staff, with the objective of reducing wasted effort, improving the quality of recorded complaints and supporting earlier detection of potentially fraudulent claims. The solution is implemented as a system integrated into SIDENPOL, the existing information system of the Spanish National Police, so that it can be used directly within standard reporting practices. At a conceptual level, VeriPol was trained on a dataset of 1,122 police reports, including 534 genuine and 588 false reports, and applies natural language processing together with classification models to estimate the probability that a report is false. In addition to producing a risk score, the system also provides insight into linguistic and structural differences between false and true reports, which can support professional understanding and review. The impact includes more efficient screening of complaints, better targeting of police attention and stronger integration into established operational systems. More broadly, VeriPol creates value by reducing misuse of police resources, improving investigative efficiency and supporting a more evidence-based response to fraudulent reporting.

results.title: VioGen - Forecast gender violence
results.proposal: VioGen - Forecast gender violence. Spain introduced VioGen to support one of the most sensitive and high-stakes areas of public protection: assessing the risk faced by victims of gender-based violence and determining the level of police protection required. The operational challenge is that risk can change across time and across judicial stages, and authorities need a more consistent basis for deciding how to prioritise resources before trial, after sentencing or even in situations where a trial does not take place. The stakeholders include victims, police forces and protection services, with the objective of improving risk assessment, tailoring police protection more effectively and reducing repeat violence. The solution is implemented through an algorithmic system that uses two assessment tests to evaluate the risk level associated with complainants or already sentenced offenders. At a conceptual level, the system processes case-related information and translates it into a graded risk classification, which then determines the level of police monitoring and protection to be applied. This embeds the tool directly into protection workflows rather than treating it as a separate analytical exercise. The reported results are significant: according to the source, recurrence of attacks has fallen by 25% since implementation, and whereas recidivism in comparable neighbouring countries reaches around 35%, in Spain it is reported at 15%. The impact therefore includes measurable reductions in repeat violence, more targeted protection and stronger operational consistency in safeguarding victims of gender violence.

results.proposal: Chatbot  - Boost relations with citizens. The use case therefore involved the city council, residents and frontline administrative teams, with the objective of speeding up access to services, improving communication with citizens and strengthening day-to-day relations between the administration and the local community. The solution is implemented through two initial chatbot services focused on arranging prior appointments with the City Council and supporting management of registration flyers. At a conceptual level, the system uses conversational interaction to guide users through these processes, capture their requests and route them into the relevant municipal workflow, reducing reliance on slower manual exchanges. This creates a more immediate digital access point for common tasks and helps the administration organise routine demand more efficiently. The impact includes shorter waits, smoother appointment handling and a more convenient experience for residents seeking municipal services. More broadly, the project creates value by improving responsiveness, supporting a more citizen-friendly local administration and demonstrating how targeted chatbot deployment can strengthen both efficiency and public engagement at municipal level.
