results.title: Bucharest airport Face recognition - Detection of wanted persons and unsafe situations
results.proposal: Bucharest airport Face recognition - Detection of wanted persons and unsafe situations. Bucharest Henri Coandă Airport sought to strengthen its security operations in a context where major transport hubs must identify wanted individuals, respond to terrorism-related risks and detect suspicious behaviour across fast-moving passenger flows. Conventional airport surveillance can struggle to process the scale and pace of activity effectively, particularly when security teams need to distinguish priority threats from routine movement in real time. This use case therefore involves airport authorities, security services and intelligence-linked stakeholders, with the objective of improving threat detection, supporting faster intervention and enhancing overall passenger and infrastructure safety. The solution is implemented through a facial-recognition-based security system designed both to identify persons on wanted or intelligence-service lists and to detect suspicious behaviour patterns. At a conceptual level, the platform combines live camera feeds with biometric matching and behavioural-analysis functions so that visual information from the airport environment can be screened automatically against relevant watchlists and risk indicators. This creates a dual-layer security capability focused on both person identification and situational anomaly detection. The expected impact is stronger surveillance coverage, faster recognition of high-risk individuals and improved capacity to spot unsafe situations before they escalate. More broadly, the system creates value by enhancing airport-security efficiency, supporting more targeted use of human security resources and contributing to a more proactive and technology-enabled approach to protecting a critical transport hub.

results.title: Home Quarantine - app on COVID-19 risk
results.proposal: Home Quarantine - app on COVID-19 risk. During the COVID-19 pandemic, the Polish government needed a way to monitor compliance with mandatory quarantine orders while limiting in-person checks and at the same time offering practical support to people confined at home. The operational challenge was to verify that quarantined individuals remained at the required location without relying solely on repeated police visits, which would have been resource-intensive and harder to scale during a public-health emergency. The use case therefore involved quarantined residents, police authorities and public-health institutions, with the objective of improving quarantine enforcement, reducing administrative burden and giving users access to relevant information and support. The solution was implemented through the free Home Quarantine app for iPhone and Android, connected to the official database of phone numbers associated with quarantine orders so that only eligible users could activate it. After registration using a phone number and SMS code, users submitted a reference photograph, and the app then sent unscheduled prompts requiring a new image within 20 minutes. At a conceptual level, the system combined facial-recognition checks with location verification to confirm identity and presence, effectively replicating the function of an in-person control. The app also included health information and access to a hotline. The impact was improved scalability in quarantine monitoring, reduced dependence on physical inspections and more integrated support for quarantined individuals, while also raising broader questions about proportionality, privacy and emergency digital enforcement.

results.company: Ministry of Social Affairs and Employment
results.title: SyRi - Detect welfare fraud
results.proposal: SyRi - Detect welfare fraud. SyRi was introduced by the Dutch government in 2014 to address a longstanding administrative challenge: municipalities wanted a more systematic way to identify possible welfare fraud and misuse of public benefits across fragmented public-sector datasets. Before SyRi, several municipalities had been developing their own approaches, creating inconsistency and duplication in fraud-detection practices. The use case involved municipalities, civil servants and national authorities, with the objective of improving the targeting of further investigations by identifying addresses considered at higher risk of irregularities in welfare claims. SyRi did not make formal decisions itself, but was designed to support civil servants by generating recommendations for additional scrutiny based on aggregated signals from existing governmental systems. The solution was implemented by combining risk indicators from multiple sources, including tax records, health-insurance data, residence information and education-related datasets, to generate risk profiles for possible fraud or misuse. At a conceptual level, the system used cross-dataset matching and risk-scoring techniques to highlight cases for further human review. However, the system became highly controversial because of concerns over privacy intrusion, lack of transparency and discriminatory effects on poorer and more vulnerable citizens. Following legal challenge, a Dutch court ruled in early 2020 that SyRi’s use breached Article 8 of the European Convention on Human Rights, and the system was prohibited. Its impact therefore includes not only lessons on administrative targeting, but also a major cautionary example regarding legality, transparency and rights-based governance.

results.title: viLTe' - Chatbot answering relevant questions regarding the COVID-19
results.proposal: viLTe' - Chatbot answering relevant questions regarding the COVID-19. Created during the “Hack the Crisis” hackathon, viLTe' was designed to address an urgent public-information problem during the COVID-19 pandemic: citizens needed fast, reliable and easy-to-understand answers about symptoms, restrictions and related public-health measures at a time of high uncertainty and rapidly changing guidance. The use case focused on supporting the general public by reducing confusion, improving access to essential information and easing pressure on traditional information channels that were likely to be overwhelmed during the health emergency. The stakeholders included citizens, public authorities and health-information providers, with the objective of offering an accessible and responsive digital point of contact capable of answering common pandemic-related questions quickly and consistently. The solution was implemented as a chatbot using conversational language-processing capabilities to interpret user queries and match them to relevant, pre-structured information on COVID-19 symptoms, rules and restrictions. At a conceptual level, the system combined question recognition, intent matching and automated response delivery so that users could receive immediate answers without navigating lengthy websites or waiting for human support. The expected impact was faster public access to critical information, reduced demand on manual support channels and a better user experience during a highly disruptive period. More broadly, viLTe' demonstrated the value of lightweight conversational tools in crisis communication by improving responsiveness, scalability and the accessibility of public-health information.

results.title: Voice-bot ACOSS - answering questions from users
results.proposal: Voice-bot ACOSS - answering questions from users. The Central Agency of Social Security Bodies developed the ACOSS voice-bot to answer questions from users of the Chèque Emploi Associatif, addressing a common service-delivery challenge in social-administration contexts: large volumes of routine enquiries can slow response times and place heavy demand on human support channels. The objective of the initiative was to provide faster, more accessible answers for users while easing pressure on administrative teams responsible for handling repeated questions. The stakeholders included ACOSS, users of the Chèque Emploi Associatif service and customer-support staff, with the intention of improving responsiveness and simplifying access to information by telephone. The solution was implemented as a conversational voice agent capable of interacting with callers and supplying responses automatically. At a conceptual level, the system used voice-based dialogue handling to recognise incoming questions, match them to relevant service information and deliver spoken answers within the call flow, creating an automated first-line support channel for the service. This allowed routine issues to be handled without immediate staff intervention and offered a more scalable way to provide information to users. While detailed performance figures are not provided in the source material, the expected benefits included faster access to answers, reduced administrative workload and more efficient handling of common queries. The voice-bot is no longer in use, but it remains a relevant example of how social-security institutions experimented with conversational voice technology to modernise user support.

results.title: Decidim - digital and democratic platform for citizen participation
results.proposal: Decidim - digital and democratic platform for citizen participation. Barcelona City Council created Decidim.Barcelona to address a core governance challenge: how to involve citizens more meaningfully, transparently and inclusively in municipal decision-making. Traditional participation processes can exclude parts of the population, limit visibility of how contributions are used and make it difficult for residents to engage consistently across different policy issues. The platform was therefore designed to give citizens a more direct role in shaping the city’s development by enabling debate, proposal submission and voting on public initiatives. The stakeholders include residents, municipal departments, civic organisations and elected representatives, with the objective of strengthening democratic engagement, improving transparency and making participation more accessible through a combination of online and in-person channels. The solution is implemented through an open-source digital participation platform that supports structured consultations, deliberation spaces, proposal management and voting mechanisms. At a conceptual level, the system integrates digital workflows with physical participation methods, allowing contributions gathered through different channels to be managed within a common and transparent framework. Because the software is open source, it can be continuously improved, adapted and reused according to changing civic and institutional needs. The impact includes broader citizen participation, greater visibility of decision-making processes and improved trust in municipal governance. More broadly, Decidim creates public value by supporting scalable, transparent and inclusive democratic participation while giving the city a flexible platform for long-term civic engagement.

results.title: Automated bus lane and bus stop enforcement pilot with Hayden AI
results.proposal: Automated bus lane and bus stop enforcement pilot with Hayden AI. Bus reliability in dense urban corridors is frequently undermined by vehicles that stop or park illegally in reserved bus lanes or at bus stops, disrupting service regularity and slowing public transport operations. In Barcelona, this creates an operational challenge for Transports Metropolitans de Barcelona, which must keep buses moving efficiently while also understanding how frequently such obstructions occur and where they have the greatest impact. The six-month pilot was therefore launched to improve evidence on bus-lane and bus-stop misuse and to assess whether a larger-scale monitoring approach could support future operational improvements. The stakeholders include TMB, bus operators, city mobility authorities and public transport users, with the objective of enhancing bus circulation, reducing interference with service and gathering robust information for possible future enforcement action. The solution is implemented on four buses running on the H12 and D20 routes through cameras mounted inside the front of the vehicles and supplied by Hayden AI. At a conceptual level, the system uses computer-vision techniques to identify static violations, such as unauthorised stopping or parking in restricted areas, while avoiding the recording of licence plates or people during the trial phase. No fines are issued; instead, the system collects statistical and contextual data for evaluation. The expected impact is improved understanding of obstruction patterns, better-informed decisions on rollout and a scalable model for supporting faster, more reliable bus services across the network.
results.memo: Proceed. Automated bus lane and bus stop enforcement pilot with Hayden AI is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Lab.ai: the heart of artificial intelligence in public administration
results.proposal: Lab.ai: the heart of artificial intelligence in public administration. Public administrations and local businesses increasingly need structured support to explore advanced digital solutions responsibly, yet innovation efforts are often dispersed across separate projects without shared coordination, training or ethical oversight. Lab.ai was launched by Informatica Alto Adige under a broader strategy for introducing advanced digital capabilities into public administration in South Tyrol. Based at NOI Techpark in Bolzano, the initiative addresses the need for a central coordination point capable of linking research, development and skills-building across both public-sector use cases and local economic actors. The stakeholders include public administrations, local businesses, research partners and innovation leaders, with the objective of accelerating practical adoption, strengthening organisational capability and ensuring that innovation proceeds under clear strategic and ethical guidance. The solution is implemented as a coordinated innovation hub, supported by partnerships with Microsoft and Eurac Research and reinforced by a dedicated competence centre for strategic oversight, compliance and capacity-building. At a conceptual level, Lab.ai connects experimentation, training and application development in a shared framework that allows public-sector and local-business use cases to benefit from common expertise and infrastructure rather than operating in isolation. The expected impact is stronger innovation coordination, improved institutional readiness and better-quality deployment of advanced digital solutions. More broadly, Lab.ai creates value by building a sustainable ecosystem for public-sector modernisation, strengthening skills and governance, and making innovation more structured, scalable and aligned with public interest.

results.company: Roma Tre University and the University of Florence
results.title: DEPUCHAT - chatbot to facilitate citizens' access to MPs' activities
results.proposal: DEPUCHAT - chatbot to facilitate citizens' access to MPs' activities. Citizens often find it difficult to obtain clear, trustworthy and easily searchable information about the work of Members of Parliament, even though much of that information is already published in official records. Parliamentary activity is spread across proposals, speeches, committee work, oversight acts and institutional roles, which can make it hard for non-specialists to understand what representatives are doing or to explore parliamentary action on a specific topic. DEPUCHAT was created to reduce that barrier and improve public access to parliamentary information. The stakeholders include citizens, parliamentary institutions and civic users interested in transparency and democratic participation, with the objective of providing fast, certified and intelligible access to MPs’ official activities while maintaining strict limits around the scope of the information provided. The solution is implemented as an experimental generative chatbot developed from a proposal by Roma Tre University and the University of Florence in response to a call from the Chamber of Deputies. At a conceptual level, it uses official parliamentary data, including roles, legislative proposals, speeches, committee work and oversight acts, to support topic-based, person-based and issue-based queries. The system is explicitly confined to parliamentary activity and excludes personal questions. Still in testing, it will undergo further data integration, stress testing and security checks before public release. The expected impact is improved transparency, easier public understanding of parliamentary work and stronger civic engagement through more direct and reliable access to institutional information.

results.title: MSE - assisted text system for parliamentary amendments
results.proposal: MSE - assisted text system for parliamentary amendments. Drafting parliamentary amendments is a technically demanding task because proposals must not only reflect the intended policy change, but also comply precisely with strict formal and syntactic rules. For deputies and parliamentary groups, this can make amendment preparation slow, error-prone and heavily dependent on specialist drafting expertise. MSE was designed to address this operational difficulty by supporting the preparation of formally correct amendments directly within the parliamentary drafting process. The stakeholders include deputies, parliamentary commissions and political groups, with the objective of reducing drafting friction, improving formal accuracy and making legislative work more efficient and accessible. The solution is implemented as an assisted drafting system developed by the Alma Human AI inter-university consortium, involving the Universities of Bologna, LUISS, the CNR, and the Universities of Verona and Turin. At a conceptual level, MSE provides a text-editor interface that works directly on draft bills and automatically converts modifications into correctly structured amendment proposals in real time. It also includes an internal chatbot that retrieves relevant supporting documentation, such as dossiers, hearing transcripts and deposited memoranda, and links these to official sources. A further module under development will suggest more refined technical phrasing through natural-language interaction. Currently used on a trial basis by parliamentary groups, MSE is expected to be officially rolled out by the end of 2025, with benefits in drafting speed, reliability and overall legislative workflow efficiency.

results.title: NORMA - virtual assistant for the analysis of legislative production
results.proposal: NORMA - virtual assistant for the analysis of legislative production. Accessing and interpreting parliamentary data can be complex, particularly when users need to navigate large volumes of legislative information spread across amendments, draft laws, procedural stages and official reports. For the Chamber of Deputies, this creates an operational challenge in making legislative production easier to explore, analyse and verify, both for institutional users and for those supporting parliamentary work. NORMA was developed to simplify that access by enabling more intuitive consultation of the Legislative Observatory. The stakeholders include parliamentary staff, researchers and institutional users who need reliable information on the lawmaking process, with the objective of improving the accessibility, clarity and analytical usability of legislative data. The solution is implemented as a natural-language virtual assistant developed from the Legislab proposal by the Polytechnic University of Milan and the Einaudi Institute for Economics and Finance. At a conceptual level, the system queries certified parliamentary archives and allows users to retrieve information on amendments, legislative texts and the parliamentary progress of bills through conversational interaction. It can also present outputs in charts and tables, making complex legislative information easier to interpret. Because it relies on official archival sources, results can be verified against certified documentation. The expected impact is faster access to legislative information, improved analytical capability and stronger support for the Chamber’s institutional work, while also creating value for statistical and research activities related to legislative production.

results.title: iMaging Project - EyeOnWater app
results.proposal: iMaging Project - EyeOnWater app. Marine oil spills are difficult to detect and track quickly across large sea areas, yet delays in identification can worsen environmental damage, complicate response planning and reduce the effectiveness of mitigation efforts. The Oil Spill Detection service within the EU-funded iMagine project addresses this operational problem by improving how spills are identified, monitored and modelled from satellite data. The stakeholders include researchers, environmental authorities and decision-makers responsible for marine protection and spill response, with the objective of strengthening early detection, improving situational awareness and making advanced monitoring tools easier to adopt in practice. The solution, also known as WITOIL, is implemented on the iMagine platform and uses deep-learning models trained on labelled imagery from Sentinel-1, Sentinel-2 and Landsat 8 satellites. At a conceptual level, the service combines satellite-image analysis, automated classification and spill-modelling functions to enhance the capabilities of existing systems such as OKEANOS. In addition to detection, it supports fuel-spill modelling, alert generation, documentation and training resources, allowing users to integrate the service more effectively into operational workflows. The prototype runs from September 2022 to August 2025. The expected impact is faster and more consistent spill detection, reduced manual screening effort and improved decision support for marine incidents. More broadly, the service increases scalability in environmental monitoring and strengthens the practical usability of Earth-observation data for pollution management.
results.memo: Proceed. iMaging Project - EyeOnWater app is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: SOCIB - Balearic Islands Ocean Observing and Forecasting System
results.title: iMaging Project - Beach Monitoring
results.proposal: iMaging Project - Beach Monitoring. Coastal authorities need timely and reliable information on beach conditions in order to protect the public, monitor environmental health and respond quickly to changing marine dynamics. Manual observation can be limited in speed, consistency and coverage, particularly when beach conditions change rapidly and multiple indicators must be tracked simultaneously. This use case, developed within the EU-funded iMagine project and led by SOCIB, addresses that challenge by improving the monitoring of beach environments through automated analysis of camera feeds. The stakeholders include coastal managers, environmental researchers and public-safety actors, with the objective of supporting near real-time understanding of shoreline conditions, strengthening beach safety and improving knowledge of ecologically significant coastal features. The solution is implemented through a prototype service that uses deep-learning image-segmentation techniques to analyse video from beach-monitoring cameras. At a conceptual level, the system processes visual data to detect and monitor Posidonia oceanica berms, which are relevant indicators of coastal health, and to identify rip currents, including their location and physical characteristics. These outputs provide actionable information for both environmental observation and risk management. Running from September 2022 to August 2025, the prototype demonstrates how automated image analysis can complement existing beach-monitoring practices. The expected impact includes faster interpretation of coastal conditions, improved support for beach management and stronger public-safety capability, alongside a more scalable approach to continuous shoreline observation.

results.title: Regional AI Hubs/Centres for Health and Tourism
results.proposal: Regional AI Hubs/Centres for Health and Tourism. Several Italian regions are facing similar operational pressures in two high-impact service areas: healthcare and tourism. In healthcare, long waiting lists, uneven demand and constrained resources make it difficult to plan appointments and allocate capacity fairly and efficiently. In tourism, fluctuating visitor numbers, seasonal concentration and rising expectations for personalised services place strain on destinations and reduce the quality of the visitor experience. This pilot was created to address those shared challenges through regionally coordinated innovation hubs that bring together public administrations, service providers and technology partners. Its objective is to test common approaches that improve planning, service efficiency and user experience across both domains, while building a framework that can be replicated across regions. The solution is implemented through analytical tools for healthcare demand forecasting, adaptive resource allocation, appointment scheduling and booking support, combined with tourism-flow management tools designed to personalise visitor experiences and distribute demand more evenly across destinations and seasons. At a conceptual level, the system uses predictive analysis, optimisation techniques and shared governance mechanisms, while embedding ethical and regulatory safeguards into implementation. Early results show improved planning accuracy, reduced bottlenecks in access to care and stronger coordination in tourism services. More broadly, the pilot supports greater service equity, better quality of care and visitor experience, and a resilient, citizen-centred model for cross-regional public-sector innovation.

results.title: Bike sharing availability optimisation in the City of Kuopio
results.proposal: Bike sharing availability optimisation in the City of Kuopio. Keeping shared bicycles available where and when users need them is a persistent operational challenge for cities, particularly when demand fluctuates sharply by area and time of day. In Kuopio, the electric bike-sharing scheme regularly faced shortages in high-demand zones and surpluses elsewhere, undermining reliability and limiting its effectiveness as a sustainable mobility option. The pilot was designed to address this imbalance by helping the city and service operators manage fleet distribution more intelligently. The stakeholders include mobility operators, logistics teams, municipal transport planners and users of the bike-sharing system, with the objective of improving service reliability, increasing user satisfaction and encouraging wider uptake of cycling as part of the urban transport mix. The solution is implemented through analysis of historical usage data to identify recurring demand patterns by location and time, followed by predictive forecasting of likely shortages. At a conceptual level, these forecasts feed into an operational system that sends real-time redistribution instructions to logistics operators via SMS or digital channels, guiding targeted rebalancing actions. A feedback loop records completed interventions and reported outcomes, allowing the predictive models to be refined continuously. The pilot resulted in more consistent bike availability, fewer service disruptions and better operational efficiency. More broadly, it improved the user experience, strengthened the attractiveness of sustainable transport and demonstrated a scalable, data-driven approach to managing shared mobility assets more effectively across a city.

results.proposal: AI-Tour guide in the City of Tampere. The pilot therefore focused on improving how people experience the city in real time, with the objective of delivering accessible, immersive guidance that helps visitors discover services, museums and points of interest more easily and enjoyably. The stakeholders include tourists, tourism authorities, museums and local businesses, all of whom benefit from a more dynamic visitor-information system. The solution is implemented through smart glasses equipped with a virtual assistant that delivers location-based information as visitors move through the city. At a conceptual level, the system combines wearable interfaces, contextual content delivery and continuously updated destination information supplied by tourism organisations and local businesses. This enables visitors to receive relevant guidance in situ rather than searching separately for information, while also allowing business and cultural content to remain current. The pilot improved visitor satisfaction and increased engagement with local services, while also opening new promotional opportunities for participating businesses. More broadly, the use case enhanced accessibility, supported a more interactive tourism experience and demonstrated a scalable smart-tourism model capable of combining user convenience, local economic value and richer destination storytelling.

results.title: Urban EVOLUTION (Earth obserVatiOn and nature-based soLUTions agaInst urban pollution)
results.proposal: Urban EVOLUTION (Earth obserVatiOn and nature-based soLUTions agaInst urban pollution). Urban EVOLUTION addresses a pressing urban-management challenge: how to reduce air pollution and urban heat-island effects in dense city environments while planning interventions that are practical, evidence-based and replicable. Piloted over 12 months in Naples, Catania and Perugia, the initiative brings together municipalities, research partners and technical specialists to test how Nature-Based Solutions can respond to different climatic and urban conditions. The operational objective is to help cities understand where green infrastructure can deliver the greatest value in lowering emissions, reducing particulate matter and improving thermal comfort, while supporting longer-term planning aligned with climate targets. The solution is implemented through a combination of geospatial analysis, remote sensing and analytical models developed with technological partner Latitudo 40 and supported by WiseTown, TeamDev’s R&D division, and the Universities of Perugia and Palermo. At a conceptual level, Earth-observation data and urban-environment indicators are processed to assess pollution levels, map spatial patterns and estimate the impact of green spaces on CO₂ reduction, particulate capture and temperature mitigation. These outputs provide a decision-support layer for Nature-Based Solution planning across diverse city contexts. The expected impact is improved urban-planning precision, stronger evidence for climate adaptation measures and a scalable model for greener cities. More broadly, the project supports Paris Agreement goals, with the broader ambition of cutting emissions by 50% by 2030 and reaching carbon neutrality by 2050, while showing that urban green spaces could offset up to 40% of city emissions and materially improve air quality.
results.memo: Proceed. Urban EVOLUTION (Earth obserVatiOn and nature-based soLUTions agaInst urban pollution) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AuroraAI - Ministry of Finance
results.proposal: AuroraAI - Ministry of Finance. AuroraAI was launched in Finland as a national service model intended to support more human-centric public services and more informed public-sector management. The underlying challenge was that services were often organised in silos, making it harder for citizens and businesses to receive timely support aligned with real-life situations and harder for authorities to allocate services in a coordinated way. AuroraAI sought to respond to this by creating a “well-being snapshot” and linking it to service provision across different life events, with the objective of improving relevance, timing and coordination in public support. The stakeholders included citizens, companies, responsible authorities and public-service organisations, with the broader aim of reshaping how government worked across institutional boundaries. The solution was implemented through a decentralised network architecture designed to connect service providers and allocate services more effectively based on identified needs. At a conceptual level, the model combined distributed data use, service-matching logic and ethical-governance principles, with responsible organisations coordinating the application of the model to selected life events. This was intended to enable knowledge-based management as well as more timely support for end users. The anticipated impact included better cross-service coordination, less fragmented service supply and stronger conditions for ethically functioning digital support in government. Although the service model is no longer in use, AuroraAI remains significant as an ambitious attempt to redesign public services around life events, wellbeing and coordinated digital governance.
results.memo: Proceed. AuroraAI - Ministry of Finance is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Chatbot Sigma
results.proposal: Chatbot Sigma. Sigma served as the chatbot for Portugal’s public-services portal, ePortugal.gov.pt, helping users navigate state services and complete certain simple interactions through a digital conversational interface. The operational challenge was that citizens often need quick answers about administrative procedures but may struggle to navigate large service portals or understand where to find the right transaction. Sigma was introduced to improve access to public-service information and make some routine interactions more convenient, such as changing an address on the Citizen Card or checking polling stations during elections. The stakeholders included portal users, public-service administrators and the teams managing the national digital-services platform, with the objective of simplifying first-line access to administrative information and tasks. The solution was implemented through a combination of three Microsoft technologies: LUIS for intent recognition, QnA for service and chat content, and Cognitive Services APIs for keyword-based interpretation. At a conceptual level, these components enabled the chatbot to recognise user questions, retrieve relevant content and guide people towards the appropriate service or action. This created a conversational access layer over the wider ePortugal portal rather than requiring users to rely solely on menus and static pages. The impact was improved convenience, quicker access to routine information and broader experimentation with conversational public services. Although Sigma is no longer in use, it remains a useful example of multi-platform chatbot deployment in government digital services.

results.title: Detection protective equipment
results.proposal: Detection protective equipment. University Hospital Olomouc tested this system during April and May 2021, at a time when hospitals and other indoor environments needed practical ways to monitor compliance with COVID-19 protective measures. The operational challenge was to observe whether visitors and others in indoor spaces were wearing respirator masks correctly, maintaining recommended distance and displaying possible signs of illness, while reducing the burden on staff responsible for supervision. The use case therefore involved hospital management, visitors and industry partners, with the objective of supporting safer indoor conditions and improving adherence to pandemic-related rules within the hospital environment. The solution was implemented as a system under development that combined detection of correct mask use, interpersonal distancing and coughing behaviour. At a conceptual level, it used visual and audio analysis technologies, reportedly alongside thermal-camera testing in the wider hospital effort, to identify whether personal protective equipment was being worn properly and whether distancing and symptom-related behaviours suggested heightened risk. This created a single monitoring framework intended to support public-health compliance in interior spaces. Because the system remained in testing, its impact was exploratory rather than fully operational, but its anticipated value lay in strengthening rule adherence, reducing manual checking and supporting safer movement through hospital facilities during the pandemic. The initiative is no longer in use, yet it illustrates the short-term experimentation that many health institutions pursued when trying to manage infection-control measures more effectively.

results.title: One and a half meter monitor - Monitor which automatically calculates the distance between people
results.proposal: One and a half meter monitor - Monitor which automatically calculates the distance between people. Amsterdam introduced the 1.5 metre monitor during the COVID-19 pandemic to support enforcement of public-health guidance on social distancing in busy public spaces. The operational problem was that authorities needed a way to observe crowd behaviour and communicate distancing risks in real time, particularly in locations where pedestrian density could change quickly and manual oversight alone was insufficient. The stakeholders included municipal authorities, public-space managers and pedestrians, with the objective of encouraging safer distancing behaviour, monitoring crowding and helping manage public areas under emergency regulations. The solution was implemented through camera-based monitoring that measured the distance between pedestrians and displayed anonymised visual feedback using green, orange and red smileys, accompanied by audio warnings. At a conceptual level, the system used computer-vision techniques to estimate interpersonal distance and produce immediate behavioural cues without storing photographs, while still recording pedestrian counts to track crowd levels. This allowed the city to test a form of real-time public-space monitoring that combined behaviour feedback with crowd measurement. The impact was primarily operational and situational: it offered a way to promote distancing and understand crowding patterns during the pandemic, while limiting data retention by avoiding image storage. Once COVID-19 restrictions ended, the monitor was discontinued. Although temporary, the case remains an important example of how public-health rules were supported through live behavioural monitoring in urban environments.

results.title: Home Quarantine App - Supporting the use of electronic control for home quarantine
results.proposal: Home Quarantine App - Supporting the use of electronic control for home quarantine. In early May 2020, a government decree enabled the use of electronic control to support home quarantine, responding to the practical challenge of monitoring compliance during the COVID-19 pandemic without relying solely on manual enforcement. The app was introduced in a context where authorities needed a scalable mechanism to check whether quarantined individuals remained at home, while also attempting to encourage uptake by linking participation to lower fines for breaches of quarantine rules. The stakeholders included quarantined citizens, state authorities and the developer company Asura Technologies, with the objective of strengthening compliance monitoring and supporting pandemic-control measures. The solution was implemented through a mobile application developed by Asura Technologies, a Hungarian company with experience in facial-recognition and GPS-location technologies. At a conceptual level, the system linked identity verification with geolocation checks, while personal data formally remained with the state and the company’s role was described as establishing the connection between the relevant data points rather than accessing the data itself. Although use of the app was voluntary, the incentive structure created practical pressure to adopt it. The impact lay in providing a digital alternative to more labour-intensive monitoring, but the case also raised broader issues around proportionality, governance and the role of private operators in public enforcement technology. The app is no longer in use, but it remains significant as a pandemic-era example of digitally supported quarantine control.

results.title: C-19 - Interdepartmental chatbot on the topic of Corona.
results.proposal: C-19 - Interdepartmental chatbot on the topic of Corona. During the early stages of the COVID-19 pandemic, German public services experienced a dramatic increase in citizen enquiries, with volumes reported to rise by up to ten times. This created an urgent operational need for a scalable way to answer common questions quickly and consistently without overwhelming public-service staff. The C-19 chatbot was introduced to address this surge by providing citizens with immediate access to information on coronavirus-related issues and directing them to further official sources where appropriate. The stakeholders included public administrations, service teams and the general public, with the objective of reducing pressure on frontline channels while maintaining accessible communication during a fast-moving crisis. The solution was implemented as an interdepartmental chatbot built from existing FAQ content, which was entered as modular dialogue components to generate automated responses. At a conceptual level, the system combined pre-formulated answer blocks with speech-recognition and dialogue-processing components so that citizens could ask questions in natural language and receive standardised replies. The chatbot also pointed users towards further sources of information, and future ambitions reportedly included support for application creation and status clarification. The impact was improved scalability in handling routine pandemic-related enquiries and faster dissemination of official information at a time of high uncertainty. Although no longer in use, the case remains relevant as an example of rapid chatbot deployment for crisis communication under exceptional service pressure.

results.title: Fuengirola Town Hall - measuring beach attendance
results.proposal: Fuengirola Town Hall - measuring beach attendance. During the COVID-19 pandemic, Fuengirola Town Hall needed a practical way to manage crowding on beaches and in public spaces so that residents and visitors could use these areas more safely while reducing the risk of infection. The operational challenge was that beach attendance changes constantly, and manual supervision alone could not provide timely, area-wide visibility of occupancy levels. The use case therefore focused on helping the municipality monitor capacity in real time and communicate crowding information clearly to the public. The stakeholders included town-hall representatives, local residents, visitors and public-space managers, with the objective of avoiding overcrowding, supporting safer use of public areas and improving situational awareness during the health emergency. The solution was implemented through a system developed by a local company using sensors installed in streetlights and virtual occupancy grids with defined maximum capacities. At a conceptual level, the system measured the three-dimensional movement of people entering and leaving monitored spaces and counted how many individuals were present in each measurement grid, producing real-time occupancy calculations. These results were then translated into public warnings using percentages and colour-coded alerts. The expected impact was better crowd management, improved public information and faster response to unsafe density levels. More broadly, the initiative created value by improving public-space management, supporting safer tourism and demonstrating a scalable model for real-time occupancy monitoring in high-footfall environments.

results.title: Robots - Automating Covid-19 tests
results.proposal: Robots - Automating Covid-19 tests. During the COVID-19 emergency, Spanish authorities faced the urgent challenge of scaling up testing capacity quickly enough to support public-health management and identify infections at a much larger volume than manual processes could comfortably handle. Traditional laboratory and sample-processing workflows risked becoming a bottleneck at a time when testing speed and throughput were critical to the national response. The use case therefore focused on increasing testing capacity in order to improve operational efficiency and strengthen the response to the spread of the virus. The stakeholders included health authorities, laboratory operators and the wider public, with the objective of processing far more tests per day while reducing dependence on slower, labour-intensive routines. The solution was implemented through the planned acquisition and testing of four robots designed to automate parts of the COVID-19 testing process. At a conceptual level, the system was intended to use robotic automation to handle repetitive steps within the testing workflow, allowing higher throughput and more consistent execution than purely manual operations. The target capacity reported was up to 80,000 tests per day, highlighting the scale of the ambition behind the project. The expected impact was significantly increased testing throughput, reduced operational pressure on staff and stronger capacity to manage pandemic surveillance. More broadly, the initiative illustrated how robotic automation could support rapid scaling in high-demand public-health operations, with value in speed, consistency and resilience during a crisis.

results.title: 060 Service - Answer FAQ from citizens and burocratic terms into informal language
results.proposal: 060 Service - Answer FAQ from citizens and burocratic terms into informal language. Spain’s 060 Service was created as a central contact point to help citizens navigate the complexity of central government services through one short number and a unified access channel. A key operational challenge for public administrations is that official terminology is often formal, technical and difficult for citizens to understand, while large volumes of routine questions can create pressure on service teams. This use case focused on improving clarity and accessibility by helping citizens obtain answers to frequently asked questions and by translating bureaucratic language into more informal, user-friendly terms. The stakeholders included Spanish citizens, central-administration service teams and public-service providers connected through the 060 channel, with the objective of making public information easier to access, easier to understand and more consistent across services. The solution was implemented using natural language processing to interpret citizen queries and match them to relevant answers, while also recognising formal administrative expressions and converting them into plainer language. At a conceptual level, the system combined FAQ retrieval, conversational query handling and terminology simplification so that citizens could interact more naturally with government information. The expected impact was faster access to answers, reduced friction in understanding public services and improved efficiency in handling common enquiries. More broadly, the 060 Service created value by simplifying interaction with central administration, improving the user experience and supporting a more citizen-centred model of public information delivery.

results.title: Blue Operational Prevention Service
results.proposal: Blue Operational Prevention Service. Flood prevention requires timely decisions based on changing risk conditions, available response resources and the practical question of what action is most useful in a given moment. In many cases, however, decision-makers must interpret large volumes of information under pressure, making it difficult to determine the optimal deployment strategy quickly and consistently. This use case addresses that challenge by helping users prevent flooding through more precise and operationally relevant guidance. The stakeholders include flood-risk managers, emergency planners and operational users responsible for preventive action, with the objective of minimising risk through better real-time deployment choices and more tailored decision support. The solution is implemented through smart algorithms that combine live risk information with knowledge of the resources available. At a conceptual level, the system analyses evolving conditions, evaluates feasible response options and translates them into a user-specific action perspective, rather than producing a generic warning alone. This means the output is not simply descriptive, but directly linked to the operational choices that can still be made in time. The expected impact is more effective preventive deployment, quicker and better-targeted decisions and improved use of limited resources in flood-risk situations. More broadly, the approach enhances reliability, supports scalability in operational prevention and creates value by turning real-time information into practical, context-sensitive action for those managing water-related threats.

results.title: Combating Online Child Abuse
results.proposal: Combating Online Child Abuse. Authorities and online-safety stakeholders face the urgent challenge of identifying illegal child sexual abuse imagery on the internet quickly enough to support removal and limit further harm. The scale of online content makes manual review alone difficult, slow and distressing for staff, while delayed detection can allow illegal material to remain accessible for longer. This use case addresses that problem by exploring whether a technical model can be created and deployed to recognise illegal images and support rapid action. The stakeholders include enforcement and online-safety actors, specialist investigators and platform or service partners involved in the detection and removal process, with the objective of strengthening identification capability and improving the speed and consistency of intervention. The solution is being developed through an SBIR project in collaboration with PwC to assess the feasibility of creating and implementing a model that recognises illegal image content. At a conceptual level, the system uses image-classification techniques to analyse visual material, distinguish unlawful content from non-relevant imagery and generate outputs that can support review and takedown processes. These capabilities are intended to complement, not replace, human oversight in highly sensitive decision-making. The expected impact is faster detection of illegal material, reduced manual burden on specialist teams and more effective support for online removal. More broadly, the approach improves scalability, strengthens digital safeguarding and creates public value through better protection of children online.

results.title: Asphalt scan - Detection of  damage to roads
results.proposal: Asphalt scan - Detection of  damage to roads. Road authorities need reliable and up-to-date information on pavement damage and declining visibility of signage in order to plan maintenance before defects become more severe, more expensive and more disruptive for road users. Traditional inspection methods can be time-consuming and difficult to scale across large networks, particularly when both road-surface condition and associated roadside assets must be monitored regularly. This use case addresses that operational need by improving how defects in infrastructure are identified and prioritised. The stakeholders include road-maintenance teams, infrastructure managers and public authorities responsible for transport safety and asset performance, with the objective of detecting deterioration earlier and supporting more efficient maintenance planning. The solution is implemented through the Asphalt Scan, which gathers data from satellites and scanning vehicles and then applies analytical models to identify road damage and reductions in signage brightness. At a conceptual level, the system combines remote and mobile sensing with automated classification and anomaly-detection techniques to convert raw imagery and scan data into actionable maintenance signals. These outputs can then feed into infrastructure-management workflows and inspection planning. The expected impact is earlier detection of deterioration, reduced reliance on manual inspection and better-targeted maintenance interventions. More broadly, the approach improves scalability, enhances asset reliability and creates value through more efficient road-network management and safer travel conditions.

results.title: AIDA (Artificial Intelligence Disaster Advisor), and Horizon 2020 project
results.proposal: AIDA (Artificial Intelligence Disaster Advisor), and Horizon 2020 project. During major incidents, control rooms are confronted with a flood of potentially relevant information arriving from social media, public channels and other data sources, yet it is rarely possible for emergency staff to collect, validate and assess all of it in real time. This creates an information paradox: there is abundant data, but not enough operational clarity, which can hinder decision-making, slow coordination and ultimately endanger lives. AIDA was developed to address this challenge by helping emergency services identify and use the most relevant information during a crisis. The stakeholders include control-room operators, emergency responders and coordinating authorities, with the objective of improving situational awareness and enabling faster, more informed action in high-pressure scenarios. The solution is implemented by combining big-data processing, data-science methods and streaming architectures to ingest and filter information from multiple public and non-public sources. At a conceptual level, the system analyses incoming data flows, evaluates relevance and rapidly distributes prioritised information to emergency services so that operational teams can focus on the most important signals. This supports live crisis management rather than retrospective analysis. The expected impact is better-informed emergency handling, faster access to critical intelligence and improved coordination across services. In practical terms, AIDA strengthens responsiveness, increases the usability of complex data in crisis settings and creates public value by supporting actions that can better save and protect human lives.

results.title: AI for fisheries inspections - Detecting illegal barrels
results.proposal: AI for fisheries inspections - Detecting illegal barrels. Inspection authorities face a recurring challenge when monitoring production and storage environments: potentially harmful anomalies may be difficult to identify quickly across large areas, yet delayed detection can weaken controls, increase operational costs and heighten risks to food safety. This use case, explored in a testing environment with the Netherlands Food and Consumer Product Safety Authority, focuses on improving inspection efficiency by identifying suspicious deviations that may indicate harmful organisms or other non-compliant conditions. The stakeholders include inspectors, laboratory teams and operational managers, with the objective of directing scarce inspection resources more effectively, strengthening control methods and improving the quality of oversight in high-risk contexts. The solution is implemented through image-analysis technology mounted on drones or other unmanned aerial vehicles, designed to detect anomalies from visual data gathered during inspections. At a conceptual level, the system combines aerial imaging, machine-learning-based pattern detection and inspection workflows so that unusual features can be highlighted and assessed for follow-up. These outputs can then support decisions on where to deploy staff, laboratory analysis or specialist equipment. The expected impact is more efficient use of inspection capacity, improved targeting of controls and stronger food-safety protection through earlier and more reliable anomaly detection. More broadly, the approach enhances scalability, reduces wasted effort and creates value by modernising field inspection methods in a resource-constrained regulatory environment.

results.title: AI for detecting Asian Hornbill
results.proposal: AI for detecting Asian Hornbill. Detecting the presence of the Asian hornet is a growing operational priority because this invasive species can threaten biodiversity, disrupt ecosystems and create risks for beekeeping and public safety. The challenge for inspectors is that suspected nests are not always easy to confirm quickly in the field, particularly across wide outdoor areas, and accurate species identification is essential to avoid unnecessary intervention. This use case, led by the NVWA, addresses that problem by improving how potential sightings and nest reports are verified. The stakeholders include inspectors, environmental authorities and members of the public reporting possible nests, with the objective of accelerating detection, improving species recognition and supporting more targeted intervention against the invasive hornet. The solution is implemented through two complementary tools: drone surveys equipped with thermal-imaging cameras for suspected nest areas, and an image-recognition application that helps distinguish between the Asian hornet and the European hornet. At a conceptual level, the system combines aerial thermal sensing with visual classification models to support both field detection and species verification. These capabilities can then be integrated into the NVWA’s inspection workflow to prioritise action and reduce uncertainty. The expected impact is faster confirmation of nest locations, more reliable differentiation between species and better use of inspection resources. More broadly, the approach enhances scalability, supports environmental protection and creates public value through a more responsive and accurate invasive-species control process.
results.memo: Proceed. AI for detecting Asian Hornbill is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI for detection of diseases in plants and trees
results.proposal: AI for detection of diseases in plants and trees. Plant and tree health monitoring is essential for protecting agriculture, biodiversity and wider environmental quality, yet disease detection across large areas can be difficult, time-consuming and dependent on scarce specialist expertise. The NVWA pilot addresses this challenge by exploring a more efficient way to identify signs of disease in plants and trees before problems spread or become more costly to manage. The stakeholders include inspectors, plant-health specialists and authorities responsible for biosecurity and environmental protection, with the objective of improving early detection, strengthening surveillance capacity and supporting more timely interventions. The use case responds to the practical need for broader, more scalable monitoring in contexts where manual inspection alone may not provide sufficient coverage or speed. The solution is implemented through a pilot that applies image-based analysis to detect disease-related patterns in vegetation. At a conceptual level, the system uses machine-learning techniques trained on visual indicators of plant or tree illness in order to distinguish healthy from potentially affected specimens and to support inspection prioritisation. These outputs can then be incorporated into plant-health workflows to guide follow-up checks and decisions. The expected impact is faster identification of potential disease outbreaks, better targeting of inspection resources and reduced reliance on purely manual screening. More broadly, the approach improves scalability, enhances the reliability of plant-health monitoring and creates value through stronger preventive action in environmental and agricultural protection.

results.title: AI machine learning supervised - Delivering learning reports
results.proposal: AI machine learning supervised - Delivering learning reports. Educational and public-service organisations often hold large amounts of administrative and performance data, yet turning those data into useful learning insights for internal improvement can be slow and resource-intensive. This use case, piloted internally by DUO, addresses the need to produce learning reports more efficiently and in a more structured way. The stakeholders include internal analysts, programme managers and decision-makers within DUO, with the objective of improving how organisational learning is captured, reported and used to inform future action. In this context, the challenge is not simply to collect information, but to derive coherent reporting outputs that support reflection, oversight and service improvement from existing internal data. The solution is implemented through a supervised machine-learning pilot designed to support the production of a learning report. At a conceptual level, the system uses labelled data and supervised modelling techniques to identify relevant patterns, classify information or structure insights that can feed into report generation and internal evaluation processes. Rather than replacing expert interpretation, the tool is intended to support analysts in assembling evidence more systematically and efficiently. The expected impact is quicker preparation of learning reports, reduced manual processing and stronger consistency in how findings are compiled. More broadly, the pilot offers a foundation for scalable internal reporting, improved organisational learning and better use of data in steering, evaluation and continuous improvement activities within DUO.
results.memo: Proceed. AI machine learning supervised - Delivering learning reports is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AICrimePrediction (AICP) - Prediction of  the risk of crime and terrorism
results.proposal: AICrimePrediction (AICP) - Prediction of  the risk of crime and terrorism. Police control rooms handle continuous streams of incident data and real-time reports, yet anticipating where risks may emerge remains a difficult task in fast-changing urban environments. The AICrimePrediction feasibility study, carried out by Amsterdam police and Ciphix, addresses the challenge of improving situational awareness and supporting earlier, better-informed deployment decisions in relation to crime and terrorism risks. The stakeholders include control-room staff, police planners and operational decision-makers, with the objective of understanding whether available data can be used to generate sufficiently accurate risk predictions to strengthen prevention and response. Rather than focusing only on historical review, the use case seeks to inform live operational choices by connecting past patterns with current signals. The solution is implemented by combining historical control-room data, including type of incident, time and location, with real-time reporting inputs. At a conceptual level, the system applies predictive modelling to spatio-temporal and incident-pattern data in order to estimate the likelihood of criminal or terrorism-related risk in particular contexts or locations. These predictions are intended to support operational awareness and resource allocation rather than replace police judgement. The expected impact is more targeted monitoring, improved readiness and better use of police capacity in high-risk situations. More broadly, the feasibility study explores whether data-driven forecasting can strengthen public-safety operations through greater precision, timeliness and coordination in risk assessment.

results.title: AI for public space notifications - Image recognition to analyse reports
results.proposal: AI for public space notifications - Image recognition to analyse reports. Municipalities receive many citizen reports about defects and inconveniences in public space, ranging from loose paving stones and broken streetlights to potentially dangerous situations requiring urgent intervention. Although these reports are valuable, they can vary greatly in clarity and completeness, which means staff must spend time interpreting the issue before deciding how to respond. This use case, explored by the municipality of Dordrecht, addresses that operational friction by seeking to make reporting easier for residents and the follow-up process more efficient for municipal teams. The stakeholders include citizens, municipal service staff and teams responsible for public-space maintenance, with the objective of improving intake quality, speeding up case assessment and supporting quicker resolution of local problems. The solution is implemented through image-recognition techniques applied to photographs submitted with defect reports. At a conceptual level, the system analyses the uploaded image to identify the type of issue reported, extract relevant visual cues and support routing or prioritisation within the municipal workflow. This gives staff a clearer starting point for action and may reduce the need for repeated clarification. The expected impact is faster processing of public-space notifications, reduced administrative effort and a smoother user experience for residents. More broadly, the approach improves service responsiveness, enhances consistency in case handling and creates value by linking citizen reporting more directly to operational action.
results.memo: Proceed. AI for public space notifications - Image recognition to analyse reports is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: CLAVIS project - Automatic recognition of old handwritten documents
results.proposal: CLAVIS project - Automatic recognition of old handwritten documents. Historical archives contain vast quantities of handwritten material that remain difficult to exploit because older manuscripts are often challenging to read, search and interpret at scale. For the Luxembourg National Archives, this limits the accessibility of important seventeenth- and eighteenth-century sources and constrains the extent to which researchers can use them effectively. The CLAVIS project addresses this documentary bottleneck by improving the legibility and usability of digitised manuscript collections. The stakeholders include archivists, historians, researchers and cultural-heritage institutions, with the objective of making historic documents more accessible, searchable and useful for future generations while also improving archival description processes. The solution is implemented by submitting digitised manuscript images to Transkribus, a platform for automated handwriting recognition, transcription and search in historic documents. At a conceptual level, the system processes scanned archival pages, converts handwritten text into machine-readable transcriptions and enables downstream uses such as content search, structured retrieval and the automated generation of inventories or indexes of people and places. This transforms previously difficult-to-use archival sources into a more navigable digital resource. The expected impact is greatly improved accessibility to historical records, reduced manual transcription effort and stronger support for archival research and discovery. More broadly, the project improves the scalability of document processing, enriches cultural-heritage services and creates value by opening complex manuscript collections to much wider scholarly and public use.
results.memo: Proceed. CLAVIS project - Automatic recognition of old handwritten documents is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Extraction of topographical objects - AI to extract topographical objects from aerial images
results.proposal: Extraction of topographical objects - AI to extract topographical objects from aerial images. Updating national topographic and land-registry databases is labour-intensive, particularly when officials must identify newly built structures, new roads and emerging construction areas from large volumes of aerial imagery. This creates delays in keeping official spatial records current and can limit the quality and timeliness of services that depend on accurate geographic information. The use case therefore addresses the need to modernise how the Land Registry and Topography Administration detects changes in the built environment and maintains its databases. The stakeholders include mapping specialists, cadastral officials and public bodies that rely on up-to-date territorial information, with the objective of reducing manual workload, accelerating updates and improving the overall quality of topographical data. The solution is implemented through automated extraction of topographical objects from aerial images using computer-vision and object-detection techniques. At a conceptual level, the system analyses imagery to identify features such as buildings and roads, distinguishes new elements from the existing mapped environment and feeds these outputs into the database-update process. This creates a more efficient workflow for detecting construction areas and for enriching official geospatial records. The expected impact is faster database maintenance, improved data quality and lower administrative effort for State officials. More broadly, the initiative enhances scalability, supports the creation of new data and services, and strengthens the public value of official geospatial infrastructure through more timely and reliable mapping.
results.memo: Proceed. Extraction of topographical objects - AI to extract topographical objects from aerial images is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Ministry of Ecological and Inclusive Transition - Météo France
results.title: Expert systems in meteorology and climate to better forecasting
results.proposal: Expert systems in meteorology and climate to better forecasting. Weather and climate services must produce forecasts that are not only scientifically robust but also understandable, timely and useful for a wide range of users affected by meteorological risks. For Météo-France, this means continually improving predictive capability while also adapting communication tools and workforce practices to new operational realities. This use case addresses that dual challenge by modernising forecasting methods and supporting the organisation’s staff as their professional roles evolve alongside new technologies. The stakeholders include meteorologists, climate specialists, operational forecasters and end users of weather information, with the objective of improving the prediction of meteorological phenomena and their impacts while making forecast outputs more actionable and easier to communicate. The solution is implemented through expert systems and machine-learning-based approaches that enhance the modelling and interpretation of weather and climate data. At a conceptual level, these methods are used to refine forecasting processes, support impact-oriented analysis and integrate more effective communication tools into operational workflows. At the same time, the project supports staff in adapting to new modes of work and decision support. The expected impact is better forecasting performance, clearer communication of risks and stronger operational efficiency within the forecasting chain. More broadly, the initiative increases institutional resilience, improves the usefulness of meteorological services and creates value by combining technical innovation with organisational transformation.
results.memo: Proceed. Expert systems in meteorology and climate to better forecasting is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Ministry of Solidarity and Health - DREES
results.title: Health data hub - Creation of a big data infrastructure in health
results.proposal: Health data hub - Creation of a big data infrastructure in health. Health systems produce vast quantities of information, yet the value of these data is often constrained by fragmentation, inconsistent access and a shortage of shared tools and expertise to make them usable for research and operational decision-making. This use case addresses that structural problem by creating a health data infrastructure capable of supporting analysis at scale and improving how data are mobilised across the healthcare ecosystem. Led by the Department of Research, Studies, Evaluation and Statistics of the Ministry of Solidarity and Health, the initiative involves researchers, policymakers, planners and healthcare stakeholders, with the objective of strengthening clinical research, improving support for resource-allocation decisions and enabling more predictive and effective forms of medicine. The solution is implemented through a big-data infrastructure in health that brings together datasets, analytical tools and specialist capabilities within a common framework. At a conceptual level, the platform is designed to facilitate secure data use, support large-scale analysis and provide the technical and organisational foundation needed for data-driven research and decision support. This creates an environment in which health information can be used more systematically to generate evidence and operational insight. The expected impact is improved efficiency in the health system, stronger support for clinical and policy analysis and better conditions for innovation in care and research. More broadly, the initiative enhances scalability, strengthens the value extracted from health data and creates public benefit through a more informed, coordinated and forward-looking healthcare system.

results.title: Datascience
results.proposal: Datascience. The Ministry of the Interior carries out a wide range of missions, from security and territorial administration to crisis management and public-policy coordination, all of which generate substantial volumes of data. The operational challenge is to turn that information into structured insight that can support strategic analysis consistently across the ministry rather than in isolated, ad hoc exercises. This use case focuses on expanding the activity of the scientific laboratory, or datalab, created in 2016 so that data-driven methods can be embedded more systematically across the organisation. The stakeholders include ministry analysts, operational departments and senior decision-makers, with the objective of strengthening strategic analysis, improving cross-cutting understanding of complex issues and enabling broader adoption of advanced analytical methods in support of ministerial missions. The solution is implemented by enlarging the datalab’s role, capabilities and analytical reach, creating a shared environment for data exploitation and the emergence of more advanced modelling approaches. At a conceptual level, this involves structuring data-science practices, developing reusable analytical workflows and promoting the use of predictive and exploratory techniques across multiple business areas of the ministry. The expected impact is better-informed decision-making, stronger analytical consistency and greater capacity to address diverse operational questions at scale. More broadly, the initiative improves institutional agility, supports innovation in public administration and creates value by making strategic analysis more systematic, reusable and relevant to the full range of the Ministry of the Interior’s responsibilities.
results.memo: Proceed. Datascience is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Ministry of Action and Public Accounts - DGFIP
results.title: AI for targeting fraud and valuing requests (CFVR) to improve the efficiency of tax audits
results.proposal: AI for targeting fraud and valuing requests (CFVR) to improve the efficiency of tax audits. Tax administrations must process very large volumes of information from multiple public sources in order to identify cases where individuals or companies may not be complying with their fiscal obligations. The difficulty lies in distinguishing the truly high-risk situations from the mass of ordinary declarations, especially where discrepancies may result from error, omission or deliberate fraud. This use case addresses that challenge by helping the Directorate General of Public Finances target tax audits more effectively and allocate investigative resources where they are most justified. The stakeholders include tax auditors, compliance teams and public-finance authorities, with the objective of improving the efficiency, fairness and consistency of fiscal controls. The solution is implemented within the CFVR system through large-scale processing and cross-checking of data collected by different administrations. At a conceptual level, the system analyses patterns such as abrupt changes in income, inconsistencies between declared situations and other indicators of risk in order to generate prioritised signals for tax-control teams. These signals support audit selection and case valuation while leaving the final judgement to tax professionals. The expected impact is more accurate targeting of audits, reduced time spent on low-yield controls and better recovery of irregular situations. In operational and public-value terms, the approach increases scalability, strengthens the credibility of tax enforcement and creates value through more efficient use of control resources and fairer treatment of compliant taxpayers.
