results.company: Departmental Directorate of Territories and the Sea (DDTM) of L'Hérault
results.title: Automatically detecting irregularities in occupancy soils
results.proposal: Automatically detecting irregularities in occupancy soils. Monitoring land use across a territory is a complex responsibility, particularly when authorities need to identify irregular developments such as illegal construction, unauthorised land occupation or waste dumping over large areas. Manual inspection alone is costly, slow and often unable to provide timely visibility of emerging problems. This use case, developed by the Departmental Directorate of Territories and the Sea of Hérault, addresses that operational challenge by improving the detection of irregularities in land occupation and use. The stakeholders include territorial authorities, environmental and planning officers and inspection teams, with the objective of strengthening oversight, accelerating detection and improving the protection of land and natural environments. The solution is implemented through the analysis of aerial and satellite imagery to identify patterns that may indicate unlawful or abnormal land-use activity. At a conceptual level, image-analysis and classification techniques are applied to large-scale geospatial data in order to detect changes or anomalies associated with illegal constructions, dumping or other irregular uses of land. These findings can then be routed into administrative and inspection workflows for verification and follow-up. The expected impact is quicker identification of suspect sites, reduced reliance on labour-intensive visual review and better prioritisation of field controls. More broadly, the approach improves scalability in territorial monitoring, enhances the reliability of detection and creates public value by supporting more effective environmental and land-use enforcement.
results.memo: Proceed. Automatically detecting irregularities in occupancy soils is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Better guide environmental police checks
results.proposal: Better guide environmental police checks. Environmental police services must decide where to direct limited inspection resources across large territories and a wide variety of ecological risks, from habitat degradation to unlawful activities affecting protected areas. Without strong targeting, inspections may be dispersed too broadly, reducing their deterrent effect and limiting the capacity of authorities to intervene where environmental harm is most likely or most severe. This use case addresses that challenge by helping the French Biodiversity Agency improve how controls are planned and prioritised. The stakeholders include environmental inspectors, biodiversity-protection teams and public authorities responsible for safeguarding natural ecosystems, with the objective of making inspections more efficient and strengthening the effectiveness of environmental enforcement. The solution is implemented through analytical methods that help identify patterns of risk and guide control activity towards higher-priority locations or situations. At a conceptual level, the system combines available environmental, territorial and operational information to support risk-based targeting of checks, enabling inspectors to focus attention where potential infringements or ecological pressures are more likely to occur. These outputs complement, rather than replace, field expertise and enforcement judgement. The expected impact is better allocation of inspection effort, more targeted interventions and stronger protection for vulnerable ecosystems. In operational terms, the approach improves efficiency, supports scalability in environmental policing and creates value by increasing the effectiveness of public controls without requiring a proportional increase in field resources.
results.memo: Proceed. Better guide environmental police checks is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Hydrographic and Oceanographic Service of the Navy
results.title: Automating coastline correction work - Improve coastal mapping
results.proposal: Automating coastline correction work - Improve coastal mapping. Maintaining an accurate national coastline repository is a demanding task because shorelines change over time and raw observation data often require careful correction before they can be used in official mapping. For the Hydrographic and Oceanographic Service of the Navy, this creates a significant operational burden, as agents must review large volumes of coastal measurements to ensure that reference data remain reliable for navigation, planning and environmental management. The use case therefore addresses the need to speed up and standardise coastline correction work while preserving the quality of the French coastal reference base. The stakeholders include hydrographic specialists, cartographic teams and public authorities that depend on precise coastal information, with the objective of improving production efficiency and reducing the manual effort involved in updating shoreline data. The solution is implemented using laser remote-sensing measurements collected through lidar surveys along the coast. At a conceptual level, analytical models are applied to these geospatial point clouds to detect the relevant coastal contours and automate part of the correction work previously carried out by agents. The resulting outputs are then integrated into the production chain for the national coastline repository, where they support validation and refinement. The expected impact is faster updating of coastal maps, greater consistency in correction processes and better use of expert staff time. More broadly, the approach improves scalability, strengthens the reliability of coastal reference data and creates public value through more efficient management of a critical national geospatial asset.
results.memo: Proceed. Automating coastline correction work - Improve coastal mapping is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Identify divergences in case law - Detection of divergent interpretations of the law
results.proposal: Identify divergences in case law - Detection of divergent interpretations of the law. Courts and legal institutions depend on a coherent interpretation of the law, yet divergences can arise when decisions on the same theme evolve differently across jurisdictions or judicial levels. Detecting these discrepancies early is difficult when case law volumes are high and legal reasoning is dispersed across multiple databases and courts. This use case addresses that problem by helping identify decisions that deal with comparable legal issues but may reflect differing interpretations. The stakeholders include magistrates, legal researchers and institutions responsible for ensuring consistency in jurisprudence, with the objective of improving visibility over divergent case law and supporting a more appropriate and harmonised interpretation of legal rules. The solution is implemented using case law data from the Court of Cassation’s Jurinet database and the Courts of Appeal’s JuriCA database. At a conceptual level, the system reconciles decisions dealing with the same subject through thematic comparison and legal-similarity analysis, then highlights areas where the reasoning or legal outcome appears to diverge. These outputs can support expert review, doctrinal analysis and judicial oversight rather than replacing legal interpretation itself. The expected impact is earlier identification of inconsistent jurisprudence, better support for legal harmonisation and more efficient navigation of large case law collections. More broadly, the approach improves reliability in legal analysis, strengthens institutional coherence and creates public value by supporting clearer and more consistent application of the law.

results.company: National Institute for Geographic and Forest Information
results.title: AI to identify breaks in antenna's positioning of terrestrial reference points from satellite data
results.proposal: AI to identify breaks in antenna's positioning of terrestrial reference points from satellite data. Permanent GNSS antennas are essential to the quality of terrestrial reference systems, but interruptions or breaks in their position measurements can degrade the reliability of the data used for geodetic calculations and international reference frameworks. Detecting these discontinuities is technically important because unrecognised shifts may distort downstream analyses, yet manual identification can be difficult across large volumes of satellite-derived positioning data. This use case therefore focuses on improving the monitoring of reference-point measurements so that anomalies can be recognised and incorporated into quality control more systematically. The stakeholders include geodesy specialists, reference-system managers and institutions responsible for maintaining positioning infrastructure, with the objective of preserving the accuracy and consistency of the international terrestrial reference system. The solution is implemented by analysing satellite-based measurements from permanent antennas in order to identify breaks in the observed position series automatically. At a conceptual level, the system uses time-series analysis and anomaly-detection techniques to distinguish genuine discontinuities from normal variation and to flag measurement segments requiring adjustment or expert review. These results can then be integrated into geodetic processing workflows so that identified breaks are taken into account appropriately. The expected impact is improved quality of reference-point data, more reliable maintenance of positioning systems and reduced manual effort in monitoring. In broader terms, the approach enhances precision, supports scalability in geodetic operations and creates value by strengthening a foundational layer of spatial and navigation infrastructure.
results.memo: Proceed. AI to identify breaks in antenna's positioning of terrestrial reference points from satellite data is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Directorate-General for Competition, Consumer Affairs and Fraud Control
results.title: AI for detecting mandatory information and unfair terms in contracts, quotes and invoices
results.proposal: AI for detecting mandatory information and unfair terms in contracts, quotes and invoices. Consumer-protection authorities must examine contracts, quotations and invoices to verify whether mandatory information is present and whether contractual terms may be unfair, misleading or detrimental to consumers. This work is legally important but highly document-intensive, especially when investigators recover large numbers of business records during controls and must compare them with prior decisions, opinions and recommendations. The use case therefore addresses the need to strengthen consumer-market oversight while reducing the manual burden involved in document review. The stakeholders include DGCCRF investigators, legal analysts and market-regulation teams, with the objective of improving the detection of non-compliance, enhancing consumer protection and supporting fairer competition. The solution is implemented by analysing reports and documents collected during controls together with the decisions, opinions and recommendations of the Unfair Terms Commission. At a conceptual level, the system uses information extraction, clause classification and thematic analysis to detect mandatory information, identify the subject matter of contract clauses and flag terms that may be unfair according to existing regulatory and interpretative sources. These outputs support investigators in targeting the most problematic documents for closer review. The expected impact is quicker identification of unlawful or problematic contractual content, more consistent enforcement activity and better use of investigative capacity. More broadly, the approach improves reliability, increases scalability in market controls and creates value through stronger consumer protection and more effective competitive regulation.
results.memo: Proceed. AI for detecting mandatory information and unfair terms in contracts, quotes and invoices is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Group disputes together with AI for a joint decision
results.proposal: Group disputes together with AI for a joint decision. Administrative courts receive large numbers of claims, and many disputes may concern the same issue, legal basis or factual pattern even if they are filed separately. When these related cases are not identified early, judges and court staff may process them individually, increasing workload, delaying resolution and missing opportunities for more coherent treatment of series litigation. This use case addresses that operational inefficiency by helping courts detect disputes that should be grouped together for joint handling or harmonised decision-making. The stakeholders include administrative judges, court clerks and justice-system managers, with the objective of improving the efficiency of administrative justice while preserving consistency across similar cases. The solution is implemented by analysing the body of requests submitted to administrative courts in order to identify recurring themes and detect case series automatically. At a conceptual level, the system uses document comparison, clustering and thematic similarity techniques to reconcile claims dealing with the same matter and highlight groups of disputes that are likely to benefit from coordinated review. These groupings can then support judicial organisation and case-management decisions. The expected impact is faster processing of repetitive litigation, better consistency in decisions and more efficient allocation of judicial resources. In operational terms, the approach improves scalability in court administration, reduces duplicated effort and creates value by supporting a more streamlined and coherent handling of high-volume administrative disputes.

results.company: Directorate-General for Enterprises - Strategic Information and Economic Security Service
results.title: AI to identify entities presenting a risk to economic interests
results.proposal: AI to identify entities presenting a risk to economic interests. Authorities responsible for reviewing foreign investment requests must assess not only the immediate transaction but also the broader profile of the entities involved, including whether they may present risks to national economic interests. This is a complex task because the relevant signals may be dispersed across investment files and external information sources, making manual assessment time-consuming and potentially uneven across cases. The use case therefore focuses on improving the processing of foreign investment dossiers and reinforcing economic intelligence capabilities. The stakeholders include public officials reviewing investments, economic-security specialists and decision-makers concerned with strategic assets and national interests, with the objective of identifying higher-risk entities earlier and supporting more consistent risk analysis in investment screening. The solution is implemented by combining information from foreign-investment requests in France with external data sources to detect and characterise entities that may warrant closer examination. At a conceptual level, the system uses entity analysis, cross-source matching and risk-scoring techniques to surface patterns, links or attributes associated with potential threats to France’s economic interests. These outputs are then used to support file processing and prioritisation rather than replace expert judgement. The expected impact is faster and more focused treatment of investment files, improved detection of strategic risks and better use of specialist review capacity. More broadly, the approach strengthens economic-security oversight, improves analytical consistency and creates public value through more informed handling of sensitive foreign investments.

results.company: National Institute for the Industrial Environment and Risks
results.title: AI to Identify molecules contaminating the environment and the sources of pollution
results.proposal: AI to Identify molecules contaminating the environment and the sources of pollution. Environmental monitoring depends on the ability to identify contaminating substances accurately and to understand whether different samples point to the same pollutant source or to distinct pollution events. In practice, chemical analyses generate complex spectral outputs whose similarities and differences can be difficult to assess consistently at scale, especially when many compounds or trace signatures must be compared across multiple samples. This use case addresses that challenge by improving how analysts detect polluting molecules and interpret the relationships between molecular spectra. The stakeholders include environmental laboratories, pollution-monitoring authorities and investigators responsible for tracing contamination sources, with the objective of strengthening environmental surveillance and making the identification of pollutants more precise and operationally useful. The solution is implemented by applying analytical models to the results of chemical analyses in order to compare spectra and objectify their proximity or divergence. At a conceptual level, the system uses pattern-recognition techniques on molecular signatures to highlight recurring forms, distinguish substances more reliably and support the identification of contaminants present in environmental samples. This can also help investigators infer whether pollution may stem from similar or distinct origins. The expected impact is more accurate detection of polluting molecules, faster interpretation of analytical results and stronger support for source identification. In practical terms, the approach improves the reliability and scalability of environmental analysis and creates value by enabling more targeted pollution control and remediation efforts.
results.memo: Proceed. AI to Identify molecules contaminating the environment and the sources of pollution is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: New Aquitaine Chambers of Trades and Crafts
results.title: Develop a tool to help the establishment of craft businesses
results.proposal: Develop a tool to help the establishment of craft businesses. Choosing the right location is a decisive factor for the viability of a new craft business, yet artisans often have limited access to clear, evidence-based information on the characteristics of a territory before committing to an installation decision. Local demand, demographic structure and the existing economic fabric can all influence whether a craft activity is likely to thrive, but assessing these elements in a systematic way is difficult for individual entrepreneurs and for the public bodies that advise them. This use case therefore addresses the need to support craftsmen more effectively when selecting where to establish their business. The stakeholders include artisans, local economic-development actors and advisory services, with the objective of improving business-location decisions, reducing the risk of failure and strengthening the fit between craft activity and territorial opportunity. The solution is implemented by combining data on craft businesses with population data in order to estimate the likelihood of success for a given type of activity in a given area. At a conceptual level, the system uses predictive modelling and territorial analysis to relate business characteristics, local market conditions and demographic patterns, then translates these into decision-support outputs for advisers and business founders. The expected impact is better-informed establishment choices, improved quality of support to craftsmen and more efficient local economic guidance. More broadly, the approach can enhance business survival prospects, reduce wasted investment and create value through smarter alignment between entrepreneurship and territorial demand.
results.memo: Proceed. Develop a tool to help the establishment of craft businesses is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies
results.title: Improve the identification of the employing establishment in the population census
results.proposal: Improve the identification of the employing establishment in the population census. In population-census processing, accurately identifying a respondent’s employing establishment is essential for producing reliable statistics on commuting and home-to-work patterns. However, declarations provided in census data may be incomplete, ambiguous or inconsistent with the official business register, creating a manual correction burden for agents and introducing inefficiencies into the production chain. This use case addresses that problem by helping staff reconcile census declarations with the SIRENE database of companies and establishments more accurately and efficiently. The stakeholders include census-processing agents, statistical-production teams and data users who depend on robust mobility and labour-market statistics, with the objective of improving data quality and streamlining correction work. The solution is implemented through a recommendation engine built on census declarations and the SIRENE register. At a conceptual level, the system compares the establishment information entered by respondents with relevant entities in the business database and proposes likely matches to support agent review and correction. This creates a decision-support layer that helps standardise identification work while preserving human validation of the final result. The expected impact is greater precision in the home-to-work statistics produced by INSEE and improved efficiency across the data-production process. More broadly, the approach enhances reliability, reduces manual effort and creates value by strengthening the quality and timeliness of official census-based statistics.
results.memo: Proceed. Improve the identification of the employing establishment in the population census is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: General Directorate of Customs and Indirect Duties
results.title: Identify false customs declarations using text mining
results.proposal: Identify false customs declarations using text mining. Customs authorities must review product descriptions in administrative documents to ensure that imported goods are declared under the correct nomenclature, particularly where some classifications attract more favourable tax treatment. The difficulty is that misleading or inaccurate descriptions can be used to place goods in a tax-advantaged category improperly, and manual detection of such cases is challenging across high volumes of declarations. This use case therefore focuses on improving the fight against customs-duty fraud by helping inspectors identify potentially false declarations more efficiently. The stakeholders include customs officers, fraud investigators and revenue authorities, with the objective of strengthening detection capability, improving prioritisation of controls and protecting public revenue. The solution is implemented by applying text-mining techniques to product descriptions contained in single administrative documents. At a conceptual level, the system analyses language patterns in the declared goods, compares them with expected nomenclature characteristics and flags cases where the textual description appears inconsistent with the claimed product category. These outputs can then support targeted inspection and further verification by customs staff. The expected impact is more accurate detection of suspicious declarations, reduced manual screening effort and better targeting of enforcement resources. In practical and financial terms, the approach enhances scalability, improves reliability in fraud detection and creates value by supporting more effective customs control and reducing losses linked to incorrect duty classification.

results.company: General Directorate of the National Gendarmerie
results.title: Improve the online pre-complaint system - Detecting infringements automatically
results.proposal: Improve the online pre-complaint system - Detecting infringements automatically. Online pre-complaint services help citizens begin reporting offences before direct contact with law-enforcement officers, but these submissions are not always complete or sufficiently precise to be treated immediately as fully qualified complaints. As a result, complainants may need to repeat information and gendarmerie staff must spend additional time clarifying the nature of the infringement and collecting missing details. This use case addresses that inefficiency by improving the quality of online pre-complaints from the start. The stakeholders include complainants, gendarmerie officers and administrative staff, with the objective of transforming initial digital submissions into better-qualified complaints, reducing duplication and accelerating downstream case handling. The solution is implemented through automated infringement detection and question-generation capabilities applied to online pre-complaint data. At a conceptual level, the system analyses the content entered by the user, identifies the likely type of offence and determines which additional questions should be asked to complete the complaint in a structured way. By dynamically enriching the submission, the tool helps convert a preliminary account into a more usable case file before officer review. The expected impact is time savings for both citizens and law-enforcement personnel, better-quality complaint information and smoother intake processing. More broadly, the approach improves service responsiveness, enhances the user experience and creates operational value through more efficient digital complaint management.
results.memo: Proceed. Improve the online pre-complaint system - Detecting infringements automatically is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Slovenia - Pilot3)
results.proposal: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Slovenia - Pilot3). National strategies on advanced digital technologies are now widespread, but understanding how these policy documents address issues such as bias, fairness and responsible governance remains a complex analytical task. The OECD AI policy-analysis pilot addresses this challenge by helping institutions examine national strategies in a more systematic way, with particular attention to how bias is treated in policy frameworks. The stakeholders include policymakers, governance researchers and organisations interested in responsible digital regulation, with the objective of improving understanding of policy quality, highlighting best practices and supporting more informed development of future governance approaches. The solution is implemented through analytical and visual tools that examine national policy documents and generate comparative summaries of how bias-related questions are addressed. At a conceptual level, the pilot combines policy-text analysis, thematic categorisation and visual presentation methods to reconcile large numbers of documents and make differences in emphasis, completeness and good practice easier to identify. These outputs can then support reflection and policy learning rather than replacing expert interpretation. The expected impact is clearer visibility of policy strengths and gaps, better benchmarking across national strategies and stronger support for more ethical policy development. More broadly, the pilot creates value by improving the transparency and usability of policy analysis, helping decision-makers move from broad strategy statements towards more concrete, informed and responsible approaches to governance.
results.memo: Proceed. AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Slovenia - Pilot3) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Slovenia - Pilot2)
results.proposal: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Slovenia - Pilot2). Policymakers and researchers need accessible ways to monitor progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals, yet relevant indicators are often dispersed across different sources and not always presented in a form that supports rapid understanding or action. The JSI SDG Observatory pilot addresses this challenge by creating a clearer and more usable evidence base for tracking sustainability progress. The stakeholders include researchers, policymakers and institutions working on SDG implementation, with the objective of making indicators easier to gather, visualise and interpret so that they can inform strategy, monitoring and public decision-making more effectively. The solution is implemented as a web-based toolkit that aggregates and displays SDG-related indicators in a structured and accessible format. At a conceptual level, the observatory combines data collection, harmonisation and visual analytics so that users can explore trends, compare indicators and identify areas requiring policy attention. This turns fragmented sustainability information into a more coherent monitoring environment and supports more timely use of evidence in governance. The expected impact is better visibility of SDG progress, improved usability of indicator data and stronger support for evidence-based policy discussions. More broadly, the pilot creates value by enhancing transparency in sustainability monitoring, reducing friction in the use of complex datasets and giving policymakers and researchers a more practical tool for understanding where action is succeeding and where additional intervention may be needed.
results.memo: Proceed. AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Slovenia - Pilot2) is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Slovenia - Pilot1)
results.proposal: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Slovenia - Pilot1). Many promising initiatives claim to contribute to the Sustainable Development Goals, but comparing them systematically and evaluating their ethical quality and practical impact at a global level is difficult. The Top100 Projects pilot, led by the Jožef Stefan Institute in partnership with UNESCO’s IRCAI, addresses this challenge by strengthening the application and evaluation process behind IRCAI’s annual showcase of one hundred initiatives linked to the 17 UN Sustainable Development Goals. The stakeholders include researchers, project applicants, evaluators and policymakers interested in socially beneficial innovation, with the objective of creating a more robust global platform that highlights projects not only for technical novelty but also for ethical practice and real-world value. The solution is implemented by enhancing the digital system through which initiatives are submitted, assessed and compared. At a conceptual level, the pilot applies structured analysis and evaluation support to make project selection more transparent, consistent and evidence-based, while giving greater visibility to considerations such as impact, fairness and responsible implementation. This transforms the showcase from a listing exercise into a stronger governance and learning instrument. The expected impact is improved quality and comparability of applications, better visibility for ethically grounded initiatives and more useful insights for organisations tracking innovation for the SDGs. More broadly, the pilot creates value by supporting a more credible and globally relevant framework for recognising technology-enabled projects with genuine societal benefit.

results.company: Diputación Provincial de Badajoz (DPB) is a local government body coordinating municipalities to promote economic and social development across the province. As part of the AI4Gov project, the DPB pilot focuses on sustainable water cycle management, covering both drinking and wastewater. The council oversees 63 drinking water treatment plants serving 137,910 residents, along with wastewater treatment. The pilot aims to develop intelligent tools that leverage existing water management systems and data to identify inefficiencies—such as leaks, water losses, or off-hour energy use—enabling technicians to implement non-obvious, day-to-day solutions. The insights will also support policymakers in infrastructure planning, budget allocation, and optimising water services by training AI models to detect system malfunctions.

results.proposal: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values (Spain). In the province of Badajoz, water-cycle management spans both drinking water and wastewater services, creating an operational challenge in identifying inefficiencies across a distributed infrastructure of treatment plants and networks. The provincial council oversees 63 drinking-water treatment plants serving 137,910 residents, alongside wastewater responsibilities, and needs better ways to detect leaks, losses, malfunctioning equipment and avoidable energy use. This pilot addresses that problem by helping technicians and policymakers use existing operational data more effectively in day-to-day management and long-term planning. The stakeholders include technical staff, infrastructure planners and provincial decision-makers, with the objective of improving service efficiency, targeting investment more intelligently and strengthening sustainable water management. The solution is implemented by building intelligent tools on top of existing water-management systems and datasets. At a conceptual level, the pilot uses analytical models to identify non-obvious inefficiencies, abnormal patterns and possible system malfunctions, translating these findings into operational insights for maintenance and service optimisation. The same evidence base can also inform budget allocation and infrastructure planning decisions. The expected impact is earlier detection of leaks and losses, more efficient energy use and better-informed technical interventions. More broadly, the pilot creates value by improving reliability in public water services, supporting sustainable infrastructure management and showing how existing municipal data can be turned into practical governance and operational benefits.

results.title: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values
results.proposal: AI4Gov - Trusted AI for Transparent Public Governance fostering Democratic Values. Public administrations are increasingly interested in using advanced analytical systems to improve policy design and service delivery, yet this raises difficult questions around transparency, bias, discrimination, legality and public trust. AI4Gov addresses this governance challenge by helping policymakers and public institutions develop tools and frameworks that support automated, evidence-based decision-making while protecting democratic values and fundamental rights. The stakeholders include public authorities, policymakers, researchers and citizens, with the objective of making technological adoption in government more trustworthy, interpretable and aligned with frameworks such as GDPR and the EU AI Act. The solution is implemented through a European programme that develops governance models, practical tools and pilot use cases to improve transparency, explainability and ethical oversight in public-sector applications. At a conceptual level, the project combines technical methods for trustworthy systems with policy-oriented design and user-friendly interfaces, enabling public bodies to test how advanced automation can be introduced without sacrificing accountability or fairness. This also supports greater citizen understanding and confidence in the use of digital systems in governance. The expected impact is better-quality public decision support, reduced risk of harmful bias and improved institutional readiness for responsible adoption. More broadly, AI4Gov creates value by strengthening democratic legitimacy, supporting more transparent public innovation and helping governments modernise in a way that is both effective and rights-conscious.

results.title: Acts - Develop Artificial Intelligence in dematerialised legality control
results.proposal: Acts - Develop Artificial Intelligence in dematerialised legality control. Prefectures receive large volumes of administrative acts through the @ctes (Acts) application as part of the legality-control process, and agents must determine which acts are transmissible, which are not, and which elements merit priority review. This creates a substantial operational burden, particularly where routine sorting and first-level screening absorb time that could otherwise be dedicated to the most sensitive or legally significant cases. The use case therefore addresses the need to make dematerialised legality control more efficient and better targeted. The stakeholders include prefecture agents and supervisory authorities responsible for legality review, with the objective of simplifying intake, improving prioritisation and strengthening the consistency of initial case handling. The solution is implemented using data from the @ctes system to automate sorting and highlight information requiring closer inspection. At a conceptual level, the system combines classification techniques with information-extraction models to distinguish transmissible from non-transmissible acts and to identify the legal or administrative features that should be checked as a priority. These results are integrated into the agents’ workflow as decision-support outputs rather than replacing legal judgement. The expected impact is reduced manual workload, faster processing of incoming acts and more focused allocation of expert attention. In operational terms, the approach improves scalability, enhances reliability in triage and creates value by making legality control more efficient without weakening oversight.

results.company: Institute for Radiation Protection and Nuclear Safety
results.title: Ionising radiation exposure monitoring information system (SISERI)
results.proposal: Ionising radiation exposure monitoring information system (SISERI). Monitoring occupational exposure to ionising radiation is a critical public-health and workplace-safety responsibility, particularly for workers whose roles involve repeated or potentially high-risk exposure. The challenge is not only to collect exposure data, but also to interpret it in a way that supports personalised follow-up and allows unusual patterns or potential anomalies to be detected early. This use case therefore focuses on strengthening the SISERI monitoring system so that exposure oversight becomes more targeted, responsive and effective. The stakeholders include occupational-health professionals, radiation-protection specialists, regulatory bodies and exposed workers, with the objective of improving individual monitoring and supporting earlier identification of cases that may require investigation or intervention. The solution is implemented using data from the ionising radiation exposure monitoring information system itself. At a conceptual level, the system applies analytical models to historical and current exposure records in order to profile normal and abnormal patterns, support personalised monitoring of worker exposure and flag cases that diverge from expected ranges or trajectories. These outputs can then feed into occupational-health and regulatory workflows for review and follow-up. The expected impact is improved detection of anomalies, more tailored exposure monitoring and better use of specialist oversight capacity. More broadly, the approach strengthens safety governance, improves the reliability of monitoring processes and creates value by enabling a more scalable and preventive model of radiation-risk management.

results.title: Facilitate access to patient information - Semantic search in patient records
results.proposal: Facilitate access to patient information - Semantic search in patient records. In hospitals and care settings, clinicians and nursing staff often lose valuable time searching through lengthy electronic patient records to locate relevant information needed for treatment, coordination or follow-up. Although the information exists within the record, it may be scattered across notes, reports and historical documentation, making it difficult to retrieve quickly in a busy clinical environment. This use case addresses that practical problem by improving how healthcare staff access and visualise patient information, with the aim of reducing time spent on searching and allowing more attention to be devoted to care delivery. The stakeholders include nurses, physicians and other healthcare professionals who rely on the computerised patient record, with the objective of making clinically relevant information easier to find and use at the point of care. The solution is implemented through a semantic-search prototype for electronic patient records. At a conceptual level, the system uses language-processing techniques to interpret the meaning of search queries and match them to relevant content across structured and unstructured patient data, rather than relying only on exact keyword matching. Results are then presented in a way that helps staff navigate the record more efficiently. The expected impact is quicker access to information, reduced administrative friction and improved workflow efficiency for clinical teams. In practical terms, the use case enhances the user experience, supports more reliable information retrieval and creates value by reducing wasted time in healthcare processes.

results.title: Optimize the processing of reports of adverse health events
results.proposal: Optimize the processing of reports of adverse health events. Health authorities receive large numbers of adverse health event reports, and each submission may contain a mixture of structured details, free-text descriptions and signals of varying relevance or urgency. Processing these reports efficiently is difficult because staff must classify cases, identify the medically significant elements and spot unusual patterns, all while maintaining speed and consistency across a high-volume workflow. This use case therefore addresses the operational need to strengthen pharmacovigilance and health-safety monitoring by helping analysts and case handlers prioritise their effort more effectively. The stakeholders include health-agency professionals, safety-monitoring teams and decision-makers responsible for the assessment of reported incidents, with the objective of improving the speed, quality and consistency of report handling while preserving human oversight of the final assessment. The solution is implemented using the full body of adverse-event reports as a data source for automated classification, concept extraction and anomaly detection. At a conceptual level, the system applies natural language processing and classification models to identify relevant business concepts within reports, categorise incoming cases and highlight submissions that deviate from expected patterns and may require closer attention. These outputs can then be integrated into existing review workflows to support prioritisation and triage. The expected impact is faster case handling, more reliable identification of significant signals and reduced manual burden on specialist teams. More broadly, the approach improves scalability, strengthens health surveillance and creates value through more timely and effective monitoring of adverse events.

results.title: FABULOS (Future Automated Bus Urban Level Operation Systems)
results.proposal: FABULOS (Future Automated Bus Urban Level Operation Systems). Many cities are interested in automated last-mile public transport, yet practical deployment depends on more than vehicle technology alone: it also requires integration with existing networks, regulatory clarity, financial viability and public acceptance. FABULOS addressed this challenge by helping cities test whether autonomous minibuses could become a realistic extension of urban transport systems rather than a stand-alone novelty. The stakeholders included municipalities, public-transport planners, technology suppliers and potential passengers, with the objective of exploring how self-driving shuttle services could improve first- and last-mile connectivity while fitting within real urban operating conditions. The solution was implemented through a Pre-Commercial Procurement process that engaged several consortia to design, prototype and pilot automated shuttle services in six European cities, including Helsinki, Gjesdal, Tallinn, Lamia and Helmond, as well as a site in Portugal. At a conceptual level, the project combined vehicle automation, service design, route integration and operational testing in live urban contexts to assess the technical, economic and societal feasibility of the model. This enabled cities to compare approaches and identify the conditions needed for broader adoption. The expected impact was improved understanding of autonomous public transport in practice, evidence on user acceptance and stronger readiness for future deployment decisions. More broadly, FABULOS created value by reducing uncertainty around automated mobility and supporting cities in planning more connected and innovative transport systems.

results.title: PILOTING - PILOTs for robotic INspection and maintenance Grounded on advanced intelligent platforms and prototype applications
results.proposal: PILOTING - PILOTs for robotic INspection and maintenance Grounded on advanced intelligent platforms and prototype applications. Ageing infrastructure such as bridges, tunnels and oil and gas facilities requires frequent inspection and maintenance, yet these activities are costly, labour-intensive and often expose workers to hazardous environments. PILOTING was created to address this operational challenge by improving how critical assets are inspected and maintained across Europe. The stakeholders included infrastructure owners, industrial operators, maintenance teams and standardisation actors, with the objective of increasing inspection quality, reducing operating costs and enhancing worker safety in sectors where asset failure can have major economic and public consequences. The solution was implemented through an integrated robotic platform combining aerial drones, ground robots, crawlers and advanced analytics within a common inspection and maintenance framework. At a conceptual level, the system brought together data capture, autonomous or semi-autonomous navigation and defect-analysis capabilities so that robots could operate in complex environments and support the detection of structural or operational issues. These technologies were validated in three large-scale pilots spanning civil infrastructure and oil and gas settings. The expected impact was safer inspections, improved consistency in asset assessment and lower reliance on risky manual intervention. More broadly, PILOTING strengthened the case for robotics in industrial inspection and maintenance, supported the development of standards in the field and created value through more efficient, scalable and safer infrastructure management.
results.memo: Proceed. PILOTING - PILOTs for robotic INspection and maintenance Grounded on advanced intelligent platforms and prototype applications is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: KIA - AI-supported assistance for digital psychosocial counseling
results.proposal: KIA - AI-supported assistance for digital psychosocial counseling. Digital psychosocial counselling services often require counsellors to assess complex enquiries quickly while maintaining empathy, relevance and consistency in their responses. As demand grows, there is a practical need for tools that can support professionals during consultations without disrupting the human-centred nature of the interaction. KIA addresses this challenge by developing an assistive system for digital psychosocial counselling that helps practitioners interpret incoming requests and respond more effectively in real time. The stakeholders include counsellors, service providers and people seeking support, with the objective of improving the efficiency and quality of digital counselling while preserving professional judgement and relational care. The solution is implemented as an assistance system that analyses counselling enquiries as they arrive and provides targeted cues to the counsellor during the exchange. At a conceptual level, the platform combines several analytical methods to identify relevant themes, interpret user needs and generate support prompts that can help structure the consultation and surface useful response directions. These outputs are designed to augment, not replace, the counsellor’s expertise. The expected impact is more efficient handling of digital enquiries, better support for counsellors in demanding interactions and improved consistency in the consultation process. More broadly, KIA creates value by strengthening the usability and responsiveness of psychosocial counselling services in digital settings while supporting professionals with timely, context-sensitive assistance.

results.title: ErLeSen - Creation and Analysis of Easy Language through AI
results.proposal: ErLeSen - Creation and Analysis of Easy Language through AI. Access to information remains uneven when official or public-facing texts are difficult to understand for people with cognitive impairments or limited proficiency in German. This creates barriers to participation in education, services and everyday social life, particularly where simplified language is not readily available at scale. ErLeSen addresses this challenge by developing tools that can convert complex German texts into Leichte Sprache so that more people can engage with information independently and effectively. The stakeholders include individuals who benefit from Easy Language, accessibility advocates and organisations seeking to communicate more inclusively, with the objective of improving societal participation through more understandable written content. The solution is implemented through open models and datasets designed to learn from pairs of complex and simplified texts. At a conceptual level, the project uses deep-learning methods based on artificial neural networks, supported by partially synthetic data generation and later refinement through reinforcement-learning techniques. This allows the models to capture patterns of simplification while improving output quality over time. The emphasis on open resources also supports reuse and broader accessibility in the field. The expected impact is easier access to information, stronger inclusion for users with specific language or comprehension needs and reduced effort in producing simplified texts manually. More broadly, ErLeSen creates value by supporting accessible communication as a scalable digital capability rather than a purely manual specialist service.
results.memo: Proceed. ErLeSen - Creation and Analysis of Easy Language through AI is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: EKAPEx - AI for precipitation forecast
results.proposal: EKAPEx - AI for precipitation forecast. Forecasting extreme precipitation accurately is a growing operational challenge, particularly as severe weather events place increasing pressure on infrastructure, emergency planning and public safety. Traditional forecasting approaches can be computationally demanding and may not always extract the full value from long-term observational datasets. EKAPEx addresses this challenge by developing improved precipitation forecasts for Germany, with a particular focus on extreme weather events and the need for methods that are both effective and resource-efficient. The stakeholders include meteorological researchers, forecasting specialists and organisations that rely on timely weather intelligence, with the objective of improving predictive accuracy while controlling computational demands. The solution is implemented through analytical models trained on a distinctive long-term dataset derived from the Global Navigation Satellite System, covering the past 20 years. At a conceptual level, the project uses these historical atmospheric and positioning-related signals to support the development of new forecasting algorithms capable of identifying patterns linked to precipitation intensity and extreme-weather formation. results.title: EdTech for Diversity in AI

The DivAI project was created to address this gap by equipping companies and employees with the skills needed to introduce human-centred digital applications more responsibly. The stakeholders include employers, staff and organisations involved in workplace digitalisation, with the objective of reducing discriminatory risk, supporting fairer adoption practices and providing an accessible learning route for organisations that may not otherwise have specialist expertise in this area. The solution is implemented through an AI-supported learning platform offering low-threshold digital training packages. At a conceptual level, the project builds on the EdTech tool developed by platform3L, using adaptive digital-learning functionalities to deliver practical content on diversity-sensitive implementation and to support skills development in real workplace settings. This allows training to be embedded into everyday organisational learning rather than treated as a one-off intervention. The expected impact is better preparedness for fair digital adoption, improved awareness of discrimination risks and stronger internal capability among companies and employees. More broadly, DivAI creates value by supporting more inclusive workplace innovation and making diversity-sensitive implementation more scalable and accessible.

results.proposal: Digitaler Erstkontakt (Digital Initial Contact) - AI for counseling services related to family and parenthood. The solution is implemented through an automated dialogue system called guide.me – smart paths to counseling, designed for deployment as both a chat bot and a telephone bot. At a conceptual level, the system uses natural-language-processing methods to interpret user input and connect it with curated response pathways and referral logic developed entirely by human experts. Unlike generative systems that produce new content on their own, this approach relies on controlled outputs, allowing organisations to retain a high degree of oversight over behaviour and service quality. Development, testing and evaluation are carried out through agile feedback cycles, enabling regular refinement. The expected impact is faster and more accurate referral to counselling, improved user experience and reduced administrative effort for service providers. results.proposal: SUMM AI - Creating accessible information: End to end automated with AI. results.title: AI.CAN: AI Citizen Science Aqua Network
results.proposal: AI.CAN: AI Citizen Science Aqua Network. The project also aims to show that collaborative, data-driven water monitoring can be transferable to other river systems and bodies of water. The solution is implemented through sensor boxes deployed by non-governmental and citizen actors, whose data are then analysed together with official monitoring information. At a conceptual level, the system combines distributed environmental sensing, citizen-science participation and analytical models to identify patterns in water-quality conditions and improve interpretation of aquatic data. The collaboration with the Leibniz Institute of Freshwater Ecology and Inland Fisheries and re:edu provides a bridge between grassroots monitoring and scientific expertise. The expected impact is broader data coverage, improved environmental awareness and stronger capacity to detect and understand water-quality issues. More broadly, AI.CAN creates value by making aquatic monitoring more participatory, scalable and evidence-based, while strengthening cooperation between citizens and scientific institutions in environmental stewardship.

results.title: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Trento (Italy)
results.proposal: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Trento (Italy). Emergency call audio is often one of the most difficult speech environments to process reliably, as conversations may include screams, overlapping voices, weak connections and high background noise. The Trento PSAP pilot examined whether automated transcription could still be useful under these demanding conditions and whether it could support future enhancements in emergency-call processing. The stakeholders included call takers, PSAP managers and the technology provider, with the objective of testing the practical value of transcription tools on live emergency calls and understanding how such outputs might support broader operational improvements. The pilot was conducted on approximately 2,500 emergency calls between mid-August and the end of September 2024, and user experience was assessed through several methods, including focus groups. The implementation used Gladia’s transcription tool as a support layer within the call-handling process. At a conceptual level, the technology sought to convert speech into text in real time, creating a basis for later integration with tools capable of summarising calls, suggesting actions or automatically populating CAD systems. In practice, call takers found that transcription quality was not yet sufficient for emergency audio conditions and rated the service poorly. However, the pilot still generated useful insight: it confirmed operational interest in transcription, identified the audio-quality barriers that must be addressed and highlighted downstream opportunities for large-language-model applications. Gladia reported that some issues found during the pilot were corrected in an October 2024 update, suggesting potential for future improvement.

results.title: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Ludwigshafen (Germany)
results.proposal: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Ludwigshafen (Germany). Ludwigshafen PSAP explored whether advanced language and call-assistance technologies could improve emergency-call handling in situations where operators must work quickly, accurately and sometimes across multiple languages. Emergency communication centres need tools that support understanding without compromising reliability, privacy or operational control, especially when handling sensitive and time-critical calls. The pilot therefore involved call takers, management and the technology provider, with the objective of evaluating whether automated language services and AI-supported call guidance could improve the operator experience and strengthen information capture during emergencies. The trial tested LiveReader’s ALTERNIS solution for simultaneous language detection, translation and transcription, alongside the NOTITIA tool, which proposes questions and extracts call data to support operators. At a conceptual level, the system combined offline, on-premise detection and transcription for security, browser-based translation without data storage, and AI-assisted prompts to help structure calls. The pilot involved 184 participants working on 1,319 simulated cases, providing a substantial testing base. Participants rated the solution positively, with an average score of 4.1 out of 5, and particularly appreciated the interface and the AI-generated hints. However, the beta version was not considered ready for live operational use, especially because of limitations in generative support and insufficient medical knowledge. Even so, the pilot showed clear value in secure, supportive AI tooling for PSAPs and identified a credible path for future operational maturity.

results.title: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Basque Country
results.proposal: AI pilot in Public Safety Answering Point (PSAP) in Basque Country. Emergency call centres in multilingual environments must capture vital information accurately even when callers speak quickly, switch language or place calls from noisy settings. The Basque Country PSAP pilot explored whether transcription technology could help improve the effectiveness of emergency communications by supporting operators with faster and clearer access to spoken content. The stakeholders included call takers, PSAP managers and the solution provider, with the objective of understanding the practical value of automated transcription in real emergency-call scenarios and identifying the conditions under which it might become operationally useful. The pilot focused on more than 25 simulated calls in Spanish and evaluated the quality of transcription produced during the exercises. The implementation used Cestel’s NatalíA language-processing solution, with attention centred in this case on the transcription service rather than the full multilingual feature set. At a conceptual level, the tool functioned as a real-time aid, converting speech into written text so that operators could track and review key information more easily during a call. The results showed good punctuation, spelling and speaker separation in many cases, indicating real promise. However, the system struggled with institution names, certain Basque characters and, crucially, the effects of background noise, especially in hands-free conditions. The pilot therefore demonstrated that transcription can add value in PSAP contexts, but also made clear that better accuracy and stronger chronology handling are needed before the solution is suitable for operational deployment.

Even so, the pilot demonstrated operational potential and gave clear direction for improvement, particularly around transcription quality and service cohesion. The expected value lies in faster, more accessible multilingual communication, but only once robustness improves sufficiently for demanding emergency-call conditions.

results.title: Good Public Space for Walking pilot in multiple dutch Municipalities
results.proposal: Good Public Space for Walking pilot in multiple dutch Municipalities. The solution is implemented through an interdisciplinary methodology that combines classical spatial analysis with behavioural studies and digitally supported citizen participation. At a conceptual level, the approach compares the intended function of a place with observed patterns of use, while AI-enabled participation tools help structure and incorporate residents’ views into the assessment process. This produces a richer evidence base for design decisions. The expected impact is more user-centred urban planning, better-targeted improvements and stronger alignment between public-space investment and actual community use. results.title: DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Cluj-Napoca use case
results.proposal: DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Cluj-Napoca use case. Cluj-Napoca has experienced rapid population growth and increasing pressure on its transport system, making it harder for the city to maintain efficient, sustainable and coordinated mobility services. Although the city already offers real-time public-transport information through a user-friendly mobile application, a key challenge remains: limited data sharing and coordination between the various public and private operators serving the city and surrounding communes. The Cluj-Napoca DELPHI use case addresses this fragmentation by aiming to create a more integrated and data-driven mobility ecosystem. The stakeholders include the Public Transport Company, municipal authorities, surrounding localities and other mobility-service providers, with the objective of improving planning, interoperability and user responsiveness across the transport network. The solution is implemented through the development of a centralised IT platform capable of aggregating and standardising data from buses, trams, bike-sharing systems and parking facilities in line with open-data standards. At a conceptual level, this platform combines data integration, monitoring and user feedback to support better coordination between services and a more coherent picture of mobility demand and supply. These insights can then inform network adjustments, service improvement and long-term planning. The expected impact is more efficient public transport, improved accessibility and stronger coordination between modes and operators. More broadly, the pilot supports sustainable urban mobility, better use of infrastructure and a more responsive transport system for a growing city.
results.memo: Proceed. DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Cluj-Napoca use case is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Attika Use Case
results.proposal: DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Attika Use Case. Freight movement in the Athens metropolitan area is heavily affected by congestion on the Attiki Odos ring road, yet road and metro systems currently operate as separate domains with limited real-time coordination. This disconnect reduces flexibility for logistics providers, especially when delivery services need to respond quickly to traffic incidents or peak-period slowdowns by shifting to faster transport options. The Attika DELPHI use case addresses this lack of integration by creating a dynamic multimodal alternative for urban freight movement. The stakeholders include Attikes Diadromes, which operates and maintains the ring road, STASY, which manages Athens’ fixed-track public transport network, and logistics operators seeking more resilient delivery routes. The objective is to enable on-demand rerouting from roadway transport to metro-based logistics when traffic conditions make this advantageous. The solution is implemented through a coordinated mobility framework that links traffic and transport information from the road and metro systems and supports route suggestions based on current conditions. At a conceptual level, the pilot uses real-time data exchange, multimodal routing logic and operational coordination to redirect deliveries to designated metro stations, where goods can be loaded onto specialised metro carriages for onward movement. This model is designed for flexible, on-demand use rather than fixed metro freight schedules. The expected impact is faster and more reliable deliveries, better adaptation to congestion and improved use of existing transport assets. More broadly, the pilot strengthens multimodal resilience and supports more efficient urban freight operations.
results.memo: Proceed. DELPHI - Coordinated mobility for passengers and freight - Attika Use Case is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Fluently - the essence of human-robot interaction
results.proposal: Fluently - the essence of human-robot interaction. Modern manufacturing increasingly depends on effective collaboration between people and machines, yet many industrial systems still require specialised knowledge to operate and can place unnecessary cognitive or physical strain on workers. Fluently addresses this challenge by making human-robot collaboration more intuitive, inclusive and productive in real manufacturing settings. The use case involves shop-floor operators, production managers and industrial technology providers, with the objective of enabling workers of different skill levels to interact more naturally with robotic systems while improving operational performance and worker wellbeing. Rather than requiring users to adapt to rigid machine interfaces, the project seeks to make robots more responsive to human communication and easier to integrate into dynamic factory environments. The solution is implemented through an interface that allows robots to interpret speech and gestures, supported by perception, language-processing and interaction models that translate human signals into machine actions. At a conceptual level, the project combines multimodal interaction, collaborative robotics and a dedicated Robo-Gym training environment where human-robot interaction can be developed and tested before deployment. These capabilities are then validated through real-world industrial pilots. The expected impact is smoother human-robot cooperation, lower barriers to use, improved production efficiency and better worker experience. More broadly, Fluently supports safer and more adaptive manufacturing, increases the practical usability of robotic systems and creates value by aligning automation more closely with human capabilities and needs.

results.title: Circular TwAIn- AI Platform for Integrated Sustainable and Circular Manufacturing
results.proposal: Circular TwAIn- AI Platform for Integrated Sustainable and Circular Manufacturing. European manufacturers are under growing pressure to reduce waste, improve resilience and make production systems more sustainable across the full product lifecycle, yet industrial data and decision-making often remain fragmented across suppliers, plants and recovery processes. Circular TwAIn addresses this challenge by helping manufacturing organisations move from linear production models towards more circular and interoperable operations. The use case involves industrial partners in both discrete manufacturing and process industries, with the objective of improving sustainability, flexibility and resource efficiency while strengthening Europe’s position in advanced manufacturing. Its approach spans three industrial pilots, each tackling a different circularity challenge: batteries, waste electrical and electronic equipment, and petrochemical production. The solution is implemented through an integrated platform built around interoperable digital twins, trusted data-sharing mechanisms and advanced analytical models applied across the product lifecycle. At a conceptual level, the platform connects operational, recovery and lifecycle data so that sustainability-related decisions can be supported from design through use, reuse and end-of-life processing. In the battery pilot, it supports new circular value-chain nodes; in the WEEE pilot, it improves recovery and reuse pathways; and in the PETRO pilot, it connects digital intelligence with established industrial processes. The expected impact is more efficient circular manufacturing, better reuse and recycling outcomes, stronger resilience and improved industrial coordination. More broadly, the project enhances scalability, supports trustworthy digital transformation and creates value through more sustainable and competitive production systems.
results.memo: Proceed. Circular TwAIn- AI Platform for Integrated Sustainable and Circular Manufacturing is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: ELIAS - European Lighthouse of AI for Sustainability
results.proposal: ELIAS - European Lighthouse of AI for Sustainability. ELIAS addresses a strategic challenge facing Europe: how to accelerate advanced technological research and application in ways that contribute directly to sustainability goals while also respecting ethical and societal considerations. Climate change, the energy crisis and related environmental pressures require new forms of collaboration between academia and industry, yet the pathway from research excellence to deployable solutions is often fragmented. This use case therefore brings together researchers, emerging talent, industrial partners and innovation stakeholders with the objective of building a strong European ecosystem for sustainability-oriented technological development. The project seeks not only to advance research, but also to ensure that resulting solutions generate practical value for society and the environment. The solution is implemented through a programme that combines fundamental academic research, industrial application work, talent development and partnership-building across Europe. At a conceptual level, ELIAS creates a collaborative structure in which advanced methods are developed, tested and translated into seven pilot use cases over the project’s duration, while also supporting the broader research community and strengthening links between scientific and commercial actors. This model is intended to foster both technical progress and responsible innovation. The expected impact is stronger European leadership in sustainability-focused research, improved pathways from research to application and a more capable innovation ecosystem. More broadly, ELIAS creates value by aligning scientific excellence, industrial relevance and societal benefit around pressing environmental challenges.

results.title: AI4Citizens - Supporting ethical and effective AI governance in European cities and regions
results.proposal: AI4Citizens - Supporting ethical and effective AI governance in European cities and regions. Cities and regions face growing pressure to modernise public services through advanced digital technologies, but adoption can be hindered by uncertainty around governance, ethics, risk management and the practical design of enabling policy mechanisms. AI4Citizens addresses this challenge by helping local and regional governments strengthen their ability to introduce such technologies safely and effectively, while ensuring that implementation serves the public interest. The stakeholders include local and regional policymakers, public-sector organisations and partner institutions engaged in interregional cooperation, with the objective of improving and creating policy mechanisms that support responsible adoption and, in turn, enhance citizens’ wellbeing and regional vitality. The solution is implemented through interregional exchange, co-creation and learning processes focused on good practices, innovative solutions and governance models relevant to public-sector deployment. At a conceptual level, the project draws on key elements of governance frameworks and implementation processes, enabling partners to compare approaches, identify gaps and develop policy improvements suited to their own institutional contexts. This process is designed not merely to share examples, but to drive concrete policy change and better governance arrangements. The expected impact is stronger governance capacity, more robust and ethical policy instruments and improved readiness for adoption at local and regional level. More broadly, AI4Citizens creates value by supporting safer innovation, more coherent public-sector transformation and a more trustworthy relationship between digital progress and citizen benefit.

results.title: Enaibler - AI for ethical policies and services across European regions
results.proposal: Enaibler - AI for ethical policies and services across European regions. Public authorities increasingly recognise the strategic importance of advanced digital technologies, yet many regional and local administrations still lack the practical capacity, frameworks and confidence needed to translate this potential into better public policies and services. ENAIBLER addresses that institutional challenge by helping public-sector organisations across Europe strengthen their readiness to adopt advanced tools in an open, transparent and ethically grounded way. The project brings together nine partners from six EU regions, including regional and local authorities, development agencies and a university, all of whom are involved in shaping or supporting policy instruments linked to digital transformation. Its objective is to empower the public sector to unlock the benefits of these technologies while improving the quality, ethics and transparency of the services and policies delivered to citizens. The solution is implemented through interregional cooperation, policy learning and capacity-building activities aimed at supporting organisations in the design and adoption of appropriate approaches. At a conceptual level, the project combines policy exchange, institutional support and shared experimentation to help partners strengthen governance, implementation capability and ethical practice across their territories. The expected impact is better-informed public administrations, stronger regional policy instruments and more responsible deployment of advanced digital services. More broadly, ENAIBLER creates value by improving public-sector capability, supporting trustworthy innovation and helping regions embed more transparent and citizen-oriented approaches to digital transformation.
