results.title: Corpus Viewer: NLP and ML-based Platform for Public Policy Making and Implementation
results.proposal: Corpus Viewer: NLP and ML-based Platform for Public Policy Making and Implementation. Corpus Viewer was developed to help public administrations make better-informed policy decisions by analysing large and complex bodies of textual information that would be difficult to process manually. Policy design and implementation increasingly require evidence drawn from diverse sources such as patents, scientific publications and public-aid records, yet these datasets often combine structured metadata with large volumes of unstructured text. The use case therefore involved decision-makers and policy implementers who needed a clearer, more navigable view of the research and innovation landscape in order to support evidence-based action. Its objective was to enable the analysis of this information space in a way that reveals themes, relationships and patterns relevant to public policy. The implementation used natural language processing, machine learning and machine translation techniques to process multilingual textual corpora and associated metadata. At a conceptual level, the platform combined topic modelling, graph analysis and large-scale text exploration to support the discovery of connections across documents and sources. It was developed through collaboration between research groups and companies, and is used by several public administrations, including SEAD, FECYT and SEUIDI. The impact includes improved analytical capacity for policy teams, more robust evidence for decision-making and a more scalable way to explore large knowledge domains. In practical terms, it strengthens policy design, supports implementation oversight and improves the usability of complex R&D information.
results.memo: Proceed. Corpus Viewer: NLP and ML-based Platform for Public Policy Making and Implementation is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: VI-DAS – Vision Inspired Driver Assistance Systems
results.proposal: VI-DAS – Vision Inspired Driver Assistance Systems. VI-DAS addressed the need for safer, more adaptive driver-assistance systems by focusing on contextual understanding of driver behaviour and road situations using non-invasive sensing. Many road incidents are linked to human error, yet traditional vehicle systems do not always interpret behaviour, environment and risk in a sufficiently integrated way. The use case therefore involved vehicle manufacturers, drivers, road-safety stakeholders and system designers seeking to improve safety, comfort and efficiency through better situational awareness and more personalised driver support. Its objective was to understand scene dynamics and driver behaviour in real time, and to provide the most appropriate response through vehicle interfaces that guide safer decisions. The implementation combined computer vision and machine-learning methods with inexpensive and widely available sensors, primarily cameras, to monitor the driving context and model driver behaviour. At a conceptual level, the system generated predictions about likely outcomes in a scene and used these to drive a personalised human-machine interface that recommended appropriate actions. A cloud platform supported large-scale storage and analysis of data, improved the design of sensors and algorithms, and enabled the use of connected and cooperative vehicle systems. The impact was improved safety support, more effective anticipation of risk and stronger potential to reduce incidents linked to human error. It also offered benefits in comfort, efficiency and scalability, while recognising important legal, liability and ethical considerations associated with advanced driver-assistance technologies.

results.title: ARSI – Aerial Robot for Sewer Inspection
results.proposal: ARSI – Aerial Robot for Sewer Inspection. ARSI addresses a difficult operational challenge for urban infrastructure management: inspecting sewer networks safely, efficiently and in sufficient detail to detect blockages, sediment build-up and structural defects before they compromise system performance. Sewer environments are hazardous, constrained and costly to inspect manually, which limits the frequency and breadth of conventional inspections. The use case therefore involves infrastructure operators and maintenance teams seeking more effective ways to assess sewer condition, monitor system performance and collect environmental samples from hard-to-reach locations. Its objective is to support earlier identification of compromised sewer segments and improve maintenance planning through more capable and less intrusive inspection methods. The implementation uses an aerial robotic solution designed to operate within sewer environments and assess infrastructure condition while carrying out additional monitoring functions. At a conceptual level, the platform combines onboard sensing, navigation and inspection capabilities to identify sediments, detect structural defects, monitor sewer conditions and collect samples of water, air and sediments for further analysis. The impact is improved inspection coverage, reduced reliance on labour-intensive manual procedures and stronger support for preventive maintenance. In operational terms, the solution offers better scalability, improved safety for inspection activities and greater reliability in monitoring critical underground infrastructure.
results.memo: Proceed. ARSI – Aerial Robot for Sewer Inspection is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: SIMPATICO Platform for PS iN Spain
results.proposal: SIMPATICO Platform for PS iN Spain. The SIMPATICO Platform was developed to simplify how citizens and companies interact with public services by improving the usability and relevance of digital administrative systems. In many cases, public e-services remain difficult to navigate, creating barriers to adoption and reducing the efficiency gains that digital transformation is meant to achieve. The use case, deployed in Galicia, involved public administrations, service managers and end users, with the objective of making existing systems more understandable, more personalised and more responsive to citizen needs. It sought not only to improve individual service interactions but also to enable the continuous optimisation of services and administrative processes over time. The implementation used advanced technical components layered onto existing public administration systems to adapt content, support personalised interactions and improve the delivery of customer-centric services. At a conceptual level, the platform combined service integration, user-oriented adaptation and process-improvement mechanisms to reduce complexity and strengthen engagement with digital public services. The impact was better user experience for citizens and businesses, higher accessibility and improved uptake of e-services. More broadly, the platform supports efficiency in service delivery, enables continuous improvement of administrative processes and strengthens the public sector’s ability to provide scalable, user-centred digital services.

results.title: Madrid - AI for saving lives of Psychiatric patients
results.proposal: Madrid - AI for saving lives of Psychiatric patients. This use case focused on supporting clinicians in identifying suicide risk and other serious health threats among psychiatric patients more rapidly and consistently. Conducted through field trials involving San Carlos Hospital in Madrid, Fujitsu Laboratories of Europe and Fujitsu Spain, the project addressed a high-stakes clinical context in which doctors must make fast decisions based on complex and often fragmented medical information. The stakeholders included psychiatrists, hospital teams and clinical researchers, with the objective of improving diagnostic support and helping professionals recognise relevant risks earlier in the care pathway. The implementation led to the development of the Advanced Clinical Research Information System, which combined anonymised medical histories from more than 36,000 patients with a large body of external knowledge, including over one million medical papers. At a conceptual level, the system used analytical models to examine this integrated knowledge base and present possible health risks relevant to an individual patient. The impact was improved clinical decision support, faster access to relevant evidence and stronger capacity to identify patients requiring urgent attention. In qualitative terms, the solution enhanced the usefulness of available data, improved the consistency of risk assessment and delivered significant potential value in protecting vulnerable psychiatric patients.

results.title: Optimum - decision making for efficient integration of transport modes
results.proposal: Optimum - decision making for efficient integration of transport modes. OPTIMUM was created to support urban authorities in making better decisions about the integration of transport modes across interconnected mobility systems. In complex city environments, travellers depend on a combination of transport options, yet fragmented information and rapidly changing traffic conditions can make it difficult for operators and planners to maintain quality, accessibility and efficient system use. The use case involved urban mobility stakeholders participating in pilot studies, with the objective of facilitating proactive decision-making through a smart multimodal transit concept that would improve the coordination and utilisation of different transport modes. The implementation combined multiple transport information sources with advanced real-time predictive analytics to create a complex model of current traffic conditions and a short-term forecast of how those conditions were likely to evolve. At a conceptual level, the system integrated multimodal data streams, predictive models and decision-support capabilities to provide a dynamic view of network conditions and support more effective operational and planning choices. The impact was improved integration of transport services, better accessibility and more efficient use of interconnected mobility networks. More broadly, the use case supports higher service quality, stronger responsiveness to changing conditions and a more scalable approach to managing multimodal urban transport.
results.memo: Proceed. Optimum - decision making for efficient integration of transport modes is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Semantic analyser - Document analyser for the public administration
results.proposal: Semantic analyser - Document analyser for the public administration. This use case was initiated by the Ministry of Public Administration, in cooperation with the Faculty of Computer Science and Informatics of the University of Ljubljana, to improve how public administration bodies compare and analyse unstructured textual documents. The operational problem was that conventional text comparison methods tended to rely heavily on statistical similarity or keyword overlap, which limited their ability to identify documents expressing the same ideas in different wording. The use case therefore involved public-sector organisations handling large volumes of documents and seeking more accurate ways to identify similarities, overlaps or related content across texts. Its objective was to enable comparison based on meaning and context rather than surface-level word matching alone. The implementation used semantic text-analysis techniques to compare unstructured documents according to their content and intended meaning. At a conceptual level, the solution relied on language-processing methods capable of recognising contextual similarity, semantically related expressions and documents containing equivalent or closely aligned concepts even where vocabulary differed. The impact was improved document analysis, more effective retrieval of related texts and stronger support for knowledge-intensive administrative work. In practical terms, the tool increases efficiency in handling unstructured information, improves consistency in text comparison and provides a more scalable basis for document management within public administration.

results.title: Case Fiva (RPA) - Support the Financial supervisory Authority
results.proposal: Case Fiva (RPA) - Support the Financial supervisory Authority. This use case was developed to support the Financial Supervisory Authority in carrying out time-consuming administrative tasks more efficiently in a context of limited resources and high accuracy requirements. One of the authority’s operational challenges involved manually entering information on investment services offered by European companies into a database, based on notifications exchanged between authorities. The task required significant staff effort, was repetitive in nature and presented substantial scope for human error. The objective was therefore to reduce manual workload, improve processing accuracy and allow supervisory staff to focus on higher-value activities while maintaining the reliability of regulatory information handling. The implementation combined robotic process automation with rule-based processing to capture, validate and enter structured information into the relevant database. At a conceptual level, the solution replicated a clearly defined administrative workflow that could be standardised and executed consistently by software, with appropriate integration into the authority’s existing data-management processes. The impact was improved operational efficiency, a marked reduction in human error and better use of constrained supervisory resources. Qualitatively, the solution increased reliability, reduced the burden of repetitive work and demonstrated a scalable approach for automating similar back-office tasks in financial supervision.

results.title: WISDom - Water Intelligence Data
results.proposal: WISDom - Water Intelligence Data. WISDom addresses a core operational challenge for water utilities: how to turn large volumes of network and consumption data into practical insight that improves service continuity, reduces losses and supports reliable water supply in both quantity and quality. The use case involves water-network operators, planners and technical decision-makers who need stronger visibility over consumption patterns, infrastructure failures and abnormal events in order to manage increasingly complex systems more effectively. Its objective is to improve network management by enabling earlier detection of problems, more accurate forecasting and better-informed operational decisions across the water cycle. The implementation combines exploratory data analysis with predictive and spatial modelling techniques applied to Water Intelligence System data. At a conceptual level, the solution covers five analytical capabilities: understanding historical patterns, forecasting water consumption, locating pipe breaks spatially, identifying and anticipating anomalous events, and delivering a prototype recommendation and decision-support system for end users. These components are integrated into a unified analytical framework that supports both monitoring and planning activities. The expected impact is lower water loss, faster identification of incidents, more efficient network management and improved service reliability. In practical terms, the project supports better resource use, greater scalability in operational control and stronger decision-making for maintaining resilient water services.
results.memo: Proceed. WISDom - Water Intelligence Data is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: GADgET - Online Gambling Addiction Detection
results.proposal: GADgET - Online Gambling Addiction Detection. GADgET was designed to help the gambling control authority identify problematic patterns of online gambling behaviour more effectively by making better use of the large volumes of behavioural data generated every day on digital gambling platforms. The operational challenge is that harmful gambling behaviour can be difficult to detect early through manual review alone, especially at scale, despite the importance of timely intervention for consumer protection and regulatory oversight. The use case therefore involves the gambling regulator and associated supervisory stakeholders, with the objective of modelling user behaviour, detecting patterns associated with addiction risk and enabling proportionate follow-up actions where necessary. The implementation uses behavioural data captured from online gambling activity to build detection models capable of identifying behavioural signals associated with addiction. At a conceptual level, the solution combines user-behaviour analysis, pattern-modelling and integration with the authority’s existing operational system so that flagged cases can be reviewed and acted upon within current supervisory processes. The impact is improved detection capability, more efficient monitoring of large user populations and stronger support for targeted regulatory intervention. In qualitative terms, the project enhances scalability, improves the consistency of oversight and contributes to better protection of vulnerable users, while also increasing the effectiveness and responsiveness of the authority’s control mechanisms.

results.title: IPSTERS - Remote Sense Data
results.proposal: IPSTERS - Remote Sense Data. IPSTERS focuses on the challenge of processing very large volumes of remotely sensed data for land applications with minimal manual intervention. Public-sector and research stakeholders increasingly depend on satellite and other remote-sensing data, yet the scale and complexity of these datasets make traditional processing workflows slow and resource-intensive. The use case brings together stakeholders interested in environmental monitoring and land-information products, with the objective of improving the efficiency and autonomy of data digestion and generating level-3 products suitable for operational use. It also explores the practical boundaries of advanced analytical methods when combined with accelerated hardware. The implementation uses accelerated processing hardware within the IPSentinel framework and investigates two complementary approaches: one based on active learning and another based on fuzzy logic. At a conceptual level, the system is designed to automate the interpretation and transformation of large remote-sensing datasets into higher-level analytical products while reducing the need for continuous human intervention. The expected impact is faster processing, improved scalability and greater consistency in producing land-related outputs from remote-sensing data. More broadly, the project supports better exploitation of Earth-observation information, enhances operational efficiency for data-intensive workflows and provides a foundation for more responsive environmental and territorial analysis in the public sector.

results.title: ModEst - Student Flow Modeling
results.proposal: ModEst - Student Flow Modeling. ModEst addresses the need for better planning and policy support in the Portuguese education system by producing reliable estimates of student movements across the system at NUTS 3 regional level. Education authorities must understand how learners progress through different stages of education, where dropouts occur and how admission patterns evolve over time in order to design effective policies and corrective measures. The use case therefore involves education planners, public administrators and policy stakeholders who need robust forecasting to support decision-making across the six stages of education. Its objective is to model student flows more accurately and provide a structured evidence base for planning interventions, resource allocation and policy design. The implementation decomposes forecasting into segment-specific models corresponding to each education stage and estimates variables such as admissions, progressions and dropouts on an annual basis. These models are enriched with contextual socio-economic data from sources including the National Statistics Institute and Pordata, enabling regional patterns and external influences to be incorporated into the analysis. At a conceptual level, the solution combines predictive modelling, segmentation and contextual data enrichment. The impact is improved planning precision, stronger policy insight and a more scalable way to monitor educational dynamics over time. In practical terms, it supports earlier identification of risk areas, better-targeted interventions and more informed use of public education resources.

The stakeholders include general practitioners, dermatologists, hospital teams and healthcare administrators, all of whom require a more effective screening and prioritisation process. The expected impact includes improved referral consistency, better prioritisation of higher-risk lesions, reduced pressure on specialist services and a smoother user experience for clinicians. results.title: OpenJustice - Open case law, pseudonymization and enrichment of court decisions
results.proposal: OpenJustice - Open case law, pseudonymization and enrichment of court decisions. The French open-data programme for judicial decisions addresses a structural tension between transparency and privacy: courts must make case law more accessible and reusable, while ensuring that parties and other individuals mentioned in decisions are adequately protected. Led by the Court of Cassation and the Ministry of Justice, the objective is to enable broad publication of court decisions, support legal innovation and legal-tech reuse, and strengthen consistency, accessibility, and public confidence in the judiciary. The implementation combines rule-based and machine-learning techniques to detect and pseudonymise identifying information before publication, within the wider open-data infrastructure for judicial decisions. Official French sources state that the Court of Cassation is responsible for implementing the release of decisions, while the Ministry of Justice describes an ongoing publication rollout and public reporting notes that the release calendar runs by court branch and jurisdiction type, with deployment continuing through the different court systems. This makes the programme a staged implementation rather than a single completed launch. The impact includes wider public access to case law, more reusable legal data for research and legal-tech services, and a more scalable publication process than manual redaction alone. It also creates long-term value by embedding privacy-preserving automation into judicial transparency at national scale.

results.title: GenerativeAI @ LDS
results.proposal: GenerativeAI @ LDS. Europe’s language-technology ecosystem needs much larger volumes of trustworthy language resources if it is to support strong multilingual LLMs and generative-AI applications across official, regional, and minority languages. The European Language Data Space addresses this challenge by building a data market and exchange infrastructure for language resources, with the generative-AI dimension focused on making those resources available as an enabler for European language technologies. The objective is to assemble a broad user and provider community, improve access to language data, and strengthen the foundations for a more inclusive European LLM and GenAI landscape. The implementation centres on the LDS platform and marketplace, which are being developed under the EU Data Strategy as infrastructure for sharing language data and models between public and private actors. Current official sources show that the platform is live, that versions continue to be released, and that the infrastructure and user group are still growing, which matches the description of an initiative still in build-out rather than fully complete. The impact includes improved availability of multilingual language resources, stronger support for European language technologies, and a more scalable market structure for exchanging data needed to train and improve future language models across Europe.

results.title: GenerativeAI @ TEMS
results.proposal: GenerativeAI @ TEMS. Public-service media organisations need trustworthy, rights-aware ways to engage with generative AI, especially where questions of data use, attribution, verification, and audience trust directly affect their core mission. Within the Trusted European Media Data Space, the GenerativeAI @ TEMS activity addresses this by creating a framework for discussion and collaboration around the use of AI in media-data environments, with the EBU treating AI as a strategic priority. The objective is to help media actors adopt generative AI responsibly, protect rights and provenance, and ensure that high-quality media data can support trustworthy AI systems. The implementation is not a single chatbot or model, but a coordinated initiative involving publications, stakeholder engagement, data-space development, and collaboration with companies such as Mistral. Recent TEMS and EBU materials show that the topic remains active in 2025, including discussion of AI governance priorities and the role of TEMS as an enabler of trusted, rights-cleared media content for AI-related use cases. The impact lies in shaping governance, data access, and collaboration conditions for future AI deployment in public-service media, creating strategic value through standards, interoperability, and trusted data practices rather than through one direct end-user service.

results.title: OpenGPT-X - 35 GenAI usecases
results.proposal: OpenGPT-X - 35 GenAI usecases. Europe faces a strategic need for large language models and related infrastructure that are developed within its own technical, regulatory, and linguistic context rather than relying only on external providers. OpenGPT-X was created to cover the full generative-AI value chain, from training data and scalable GPU infrastructure to model development and practical prototypes, so that European actors could test and build productive use cases from the beginning. The objective is to advance research, strengthen digital sovereignty, and enable industry partners to explore practical generative-AI applications through proofs of concept and deployable models. The implementation was a consortium project funded by the German Federal Ministry for Economic Affairs and Climate Action from January 2022 to 31 March 2025, combining research institutions and industry partners. Official Fraunhofer sources confirm that the project has ended, while also showing that its outputs continue through model families such as Teuken and through published use-case and code materials. The impact includes open multilingual model assets, stronger European capability across the generative-AI stack, and reusable technical results that can support future industrial and public-sector applications even after the formal project period has finished.

results.title: A Public Administration Canvas for Ethical AI implementation
results.proposal: A Public Administration Canvas for Ethical AI implementation. Public administrations often need structured help to assess legal, ethical, organisational, and technical issues before adopting AI, especially under evolving European regulatory requirements. The objective is to help administrations design AI solutions that are compliant, accountable, and ethically robust from the outset rather than treating ethics as a late-stage add-on. The implementation takes the form of a reusable canvas and guidance framework that prompts users to consider issues such as bias, privacy, accountability, and regulatory fit in a structured way. Current public sources from FBK and the project repository indicate that the tool is available, has been published for broader reuse, and is still being further developed and validated based on the Trento experience. The impact includes better governance readiness, stronger alignment with EU requirements, and a more scalable way for public bodies to assess AI projects consistently before deployment, thereby reducing implementation risk and improving trustworthiness in future AI adoption.

results.title: SOLARIS - Democratic responses to the challenges of deepfakes and infodemics
results.proposal: SOLARIS - Democratic responses to the challenges of deepfakes and infodemics. Generative adversarial networks (GANs) are generative AI models capable of reproducing realistic images, videos and voice outputs. Because they have the potential to create highly realistic content, they can also pose a threat to democracies through the creation and circulation of deepfakes, which spread false information and undermine trust. In this context, the EU-funded SOLARIS project will focus on the challenges and opportunities posed by GANs in the context of democracy. It will study how deepfakes circulate and are trusted by users, thus threatening democratic processes. It will also develop regulatory guidelines about GANs and generative AI for the promotion of democratic engagement. The project will involve three use cases to simulate the circulation of threatening content, and co-create value-based GANs content to enhance digital citizenship.

results.title: Alliance for Language Technologies (ALT-EDIC)
results.proposal: Alliance for Language Technologies (ALT-EDIC). Europe’s language-technology landscape is fragmented by market size, linguistic diversity, and unequal access to high-quality data and infrastructure, which makes it difficult to build competitive large language models and related tools across all European languages. ALT-EDIC addresses this challenge by creating a common European infrastructure for language technologies, with a particular focus on strengthening the foundations for large language models while preserving linguistic diversity and cultural richness. The objective is to improve Europe’s competitiveness, expand the availability of European language data, and support interoperable language-technology capacity across participating states. The implementation uses the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium model, allowing member states to pool funding and resources in a coordinated structure. Official ALT-EDIC and related language-data-space materials describe activities including linguistic-data production and curation, evaluation and normalisation support, adaptation of models to user needs, and advice to the wider ecosystem. The impact includes stronger shared infrastructure, more reusable multilingual resources, and better conditions for developing European language technologies at scale. It also creates long-term strategic value by supporting common standards, reducing fragmentation, and reinforcing Europe’s capacity to develop language AI aligned with its regulatory, linguistic, and public-interest goals.

results.title: Autonomous Fawn Tracking System - AROS
results.proposal: Autonomous Fawn Tracking System - AROS. Farmers and wildlife-protection volunteers have only a short time to locate hidden fawns in fields before mowing begins, and manual searches with thermal drones can still be labour-intensive, weather-sensitive, and dependent on multiple people. AROS was designed in Schleswig-Holstein to address this by automating more of the detection and localisation process so that fawns can be found and rescued more efficiently. The objective is to protect wildlife, reduce dependence on scarce human resources, and enable more reliable pre-harvest scanning of fields across different conditions. The implementation combines autonomous drone flight, thermal and visual sensing, computer-vision models based on convolutional neural networks, and geolocation functions that send the detected animal’s GPS position and aerial view to the farmer and hunter for intervention. Technical reporting describes an autonomous fawn-tracking system with high positioning accuracy, while project material presents the solution as a collaboration between nAIture and public actors in Schleswig-Holstein. The expected impact is faster rescue, better field coverage, and a more scalable wildlife-protection workflow during mowing season.

results.title: 120 Words per Minute - a Training App for Basal Automated Reading
results.proposal: 120 Words per Minute - a Training App for Basal Automated Reading. Primary schools face a persistent literacy challenge, as a substantial share of pupils do not reach fluent reading speed by the end of primary education and often struggle to recover later. In Schleswig-Holstein, the “120 Words per Minute” project was conceived to support the “Lesen macht stark” programme by converting a printed diagnostic and training approach into a more flexible app-based tool for schools. The objective is to improve reading fluency, make diagnosis and support easier to use in everyday teaching, and enable children to practise independently or in pairs while giving teachers a more continuous way to monitor progress. The implementation centres on an app that digitises the phases of the existing reading-support programme and uses speech-to-text methods to automate the level check that children would otherwise complete manually. Public descriptions of the project present it as a digital education solution intended to support classroom use from the earliest training stages and to simplify the practical application of the methodology in school settings. The expected impact includes improved reading fluency, more practical use of diagnostic support at school level, and a more scalable method for early literacy intervention, especially for children at risk of falling behind.

results.title: Starting up smoothly: chatbot service (Virtual Agent Network) for foreign entrepreneurs in Finland
results.proposal: Starting up smoothly: chatbot service (Virtual Agent Network) for foreign entrepreneurs in Finland. Starting a business as a foreign entrepreneur can require interaction with multiple agencies covering immigration, registration, patents, and tax, and this fragmentation often creates confusion, duplicated effort, and avoidable delays. In Finland, the “Starting up Smoothly” initiative was designed to reduce these barriers by connecting the conversational services of the Immigration Service, the Patent and Registration Office, and the Tax Administration into a more seamless user journey. The objective was to break down agency silos and give entrepreneurs a more coherent route through immigration, business-registration, and taxation questions. The implementation linked three virtual agents—Kamu, PatRek, and VeroBot—through a shared conversational network, using natural language understanding to detect when a user’s question fell outside one bot’s scope and hand over the conversation within the same chat window to the most relevant agency bot. However, Finnish official material from the start of the project described the inter-agency cooperation as a trial ending in June 2019, and Migri later announced that Kamu itself was discontinued after 31 October 2024, even though PRH still operates its Trade Register chatbot. The impact of the original project was to demonstrate smoother inter-agency digital support, but its current status is best described as partly absorbed into successor services rather than still running unchanged.

results.title: AI tool to spot undeclared swimming pools in France
results.proposal: AI tool to spot undeclared swimming pools in France. Property-tax compliance is difficult to enforce comprehensively when local authorities depend on declarations that may omit features affecting taxable value, such as swimming pools and other built structures. In France, this use case was developed to help the tax administration identify undeclared swimming pools more efficiently and strengthen property-tax enforcement using large-scale image analysis. The objective is to detect non-declared taxable features, increase the accuracy of property records, and improve revenue collection without relying solely on manual inspection. The implementation uses a computer-vision system developed with Capgemini, working with aerial photographs and comparing detected features against real-estate and tax databases. At a conceptual level, the system scans images for pool-like visual patterns, links identified locations to property records, and flags cases where a relevant address appears not to have declared a pool. This creates a targeted workflow for further tax compliance action. Reported results show that 20,356 previously undeclared residential swimming pools were identified, generating about EUR 10 million in additional tax revenue in the earlier reported phase, while later reporting noted wider fiscal gains and plans to extend checks to features such as annexes and verandas. The impact includes stronger compliance detection, more efficient tax control, and improved scalability in property-record verification.
results.memo: Proceed. AI tool to spot undeclared swimming pools in France is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Servizz.Gov Chatbox in Malta
results.proposal: Servizz.Gov Chatbox in Malta. Citizens often need quick answers to routine questions about public services, but traditional customer-service models in government can be costly to scale and may deliver inconsistent response times across ministries. In Malta, the Servizz.Gov chatbot was introduced to improve front-line digital interaction and create a shared support layer that could serve multiple ministries more efficiently. The objective is to provide more immediate access to information, achieve economies of scale through horizontal collaboration, and gradually develop a more capable citizen chatbot integrated with wider government services. The implementation uses a chatbot architecture based initially on a rule-based mechanism and FAQ content, with machine-learning elements added incrementally as user intents are captured and used to refine the model through iteration and feedback. At a conceptual level, the solution combines a central knowledge base, conversational handling in Maltese and English, and a training loop that improves responses over time. The longer-term design also envisages integration with third-party systems so that the chatbot can move beyond information provision towards more connected service support. The impact includes reduced waiting time for routine enquiries, broader 24/7 digital access, and more consistent handling of common questions. It also improves scalability across government and creates operational value by consolidating support functions into a shared conversational channel.

results.title: Automatic decision making of the Electronic Declaration System of the State Revenue Service
results.proposal: Automatic decision making of the Electronic Declaration System of the State Revenue Service. Tax administrations receive very large volumes of declarations and supporting documents, and reviewing each submission manually can limit efficiency, delay compliant cases, and divert expert attention away from higher-risk filings. In Latvia, the Electronic Declaration System of the State Revenue Service was designed to automate part of this process by verifying submitted declarations and filtering out cases that do not show signs of non-compliance. The objective is to accelerate routine processing, improve service efficiency for citizens and businesses, and allow specialists to focus on the declarations most likely to require closer examination. The implementation relies on automated verification rules within the Electronic Declaration System, which checks the correctness of document completion and informs users of the result. In the use case description, up to two thirds of declarations that reveal no non-compliance can be approved through this automated decision-making approach, while experts concentrate on the remaining cases. At a conceptual level, the system combines digital submission, validation, and compliance screening within the tax administration workflow. The impact includes shorter processing times for straightforward filings, better allocation of expert capacity, and more scalable tax administration. It also creates value by improving the user experience for compliant taxpayers and by supporting more targeted oversight of declarations where inconsistencies or risks are detected.

results.title: FITS ITEMS - Road safety
results.proposal: FITS ITEMS - Road safety. Road safety authorities need reliable ways to enforce rules on speeding, insurance, and vehicle roadworthiness, yet manual roadside control is resource-intensive and cannot provide the same breadth of coverage as automated monitoring. In Latvia, the State Public Traffic Safety Directorate adopted FITS ITEMS to improve control on the road network and strengthen preventive enforcement in support of safer driving behaviour. The objective is to detect non-compliance more efficiently, increase the effectiveness of traffic supervision, and reduce accidents through more systematic monitoring. The implementation uses automated number-plate recognition and related analytical functions to identify vehicles in relation to speed, insurance status, and roadworthiness-test compliance. At a conceptual level, the system combines roadside camera infrastructure, image recognition, and back-office processing to identify vehicles and connect them to the relevant compliance checks needed for enforcement activity. The use case is presented as part of a broader intelligent transport approach rather than as a single isolated camera tool. Reported results indicate that, by the end of 2018, road accidents had decreased by 43 per cent at roadside sections where photo cameras were installed and operating, falling from 1,084 to 613. The wider impact includes stronger road safety, more efficient enforcement operations, and better use of public resources through automated control at scale.

results.proposal: Toscana Open Research - Allows users to access information through "queries". The objective is to support more inclusive governance and easier access to information by enabling people to search and query the system without needing specialist knowledge of how the underlying databases are organised. The implementation uses an integrated data model based on domain ontology, allowing information from different sources to be linked conceptually and queried through user-oriented expressions. At a conceptual level, the ontology acts as a semantic layer between users and the physical databases, translating queries into structured access paths without requiring users to understand technical schemas or internal data relationships. This makes the portal a more accessible interface for exploring the Tuscan landscape of research, innovation, and higher education. The impact includes improved discoverability of public information, greater transparency, and a more user-friendly experience for navigating complex institutional data. It also supports reusability and interoperability of information, while creating public value through more open and intelligible digital access to knowledge about the regional innovation ecosystem.

results.title: Noovle - Management of health documentation
results.proposal: Noovle - Management of health documentation. Healthcare systems produce vast quantities of clinical documentation, and important diagnostic information is often embedded in free-text discharge letters that are difficult to process consistently at scale. In the Veneto Region, this created a need to extract clinically relevant information more efficiently so that electronic health records could better support both care delivery and regional health governance. The objective of this use case is to identify the salient parts of discharge documentation automatically, map diagnoses to standard coding systems, and make health data more usable for clinical and population-level purposes. The implementation uses machine learning techniques to analyse discharge letters and identify diagnoses according to the ICD-9-CM international classification. At a conceptual level, the solution combines document analysis, medical term recognition, and coding support to structure unstructured clinical text and feed that information into the regional electronic health record ecosystem. This creates a foundation for applications that can support clinical decision-making while also strengthening prevention, planning, and population medicine at governance level. The impact includes more efficient processing of medical documentation, improved quality and usability of clinical data, and stronger support for interoperable digital health services. It also enhances scalability in health information management and creates value by turning routine documentation into structured knowledge for both frontline care and strategic health-system oversight.

results.title: Skala - Predictive policing
results.proposal: Skala - Predictive policing. Police forces must decide how to deploy limited patrol and prevention resources across large territories, yet burglary and related offences often occur in patterns that are difficult to anticipate through manual analysis alone. In North Rhine-Westphalia, this use case was developed to support policing decisions by identifying areas with a higher probability of residential burglary based on prior incidents and spatial-temporal patterns. In Germany, this use case was introduced to support the Federal Office for Migrants and Refugees in evaluating claims about country of origin, particularly in cases involving Arabic-speaking applicants whose stated nationality could affect the asylum process. The objective is to strengthen identity assessment and provide additional evidence that can support case handling where documentary proof is missing or uncertain. The implementation uses automated speech-analysis software to examine spoken language and identify dialect or linguistic patterns associated with particular countries or regions. At a conceptual level, the system analyses audio samples alongside other sources of information, such as documentation and existing case-evaluation techniques, and its outputs may be complemented by expert linguistic opinion where necessary. The tool is therefore positioned as an additional decision-support element rather than a standalone determination mechanism. The impact lies in the potential to improve the speed and structure of origin assessment and to help officials prioritise further checks in uncertain cases. At the same time, the use case illustrates the limitations of language-based inference, particularly where vocabulary and dialects change over time, making accuracy and reliability ongoing operational concerns.

results.proposal: LaBonneBoîte - Identification of companies with a high probability of hiring. Many job opportunities are never formally advertised, which means jobseekers can miss suitable openings if they rely only on published vacancies. In France, this use case was created to help people identify employers likely to recruit in the near future, even where no vacancy has yet been posted. The objective is to improve access to hidden job opportunities, strengthen spontaneous application strategies, and increase the chances that jobseekers secure interviews by targeting firms with a high probability of hiring. The implementation takes the form of an online service that predicts which companies are likely to recruit within the next six months in a given sector and area. At a conceptual level, the tool uses predictive modelling over labour market and employer data to estimate hiring probability and then presents these employers through a searchable digital interface. Its code is reusable and an API allows the service to be replicated on other websites, increasing its portability and reach. The impact includes better targeting of job-search efforts, improved access to opportunities beyond traditional vacancy listings, and stronger support for proactive labour-market behaviour. It also enhances scalability by allowing the service to be reused across platforms and user groups, while creating clear business value by helping more people connect with employers likely to recruit in the near term.

At a conceptual level, the solution combines historical enforcement knowledge with predictive analysis to assess declaration risk and help customs officers prioritise cases for further examination. Rather than replacing investigative judgement, the model functions as a decision-support layer within a broader customs control process, enabling staff to concentrate resources where the likelihood of irregularity is highest. The impact includes improved capacity to detect fraud, faster identification of high-risk transactions, and more efficient allocation of control resources. It also supports the scalability of customs supervision, contributes to stronger border and revenue protection, and creates operational value by helping enforcement teams manage growing declaration volumes with greater precision and consistency.

results.title: AuroraAI  - Programme with many AI examples.
results.proposal: AuroraAI  - Programme with many AI examples. Public services are often organised around administrative structures rather than around the real-life situations people face, which can make it difficult for citizens to find timely, relevant support across different organisations. Within the AuroraAI programme, one experimental use case focused on the life event of moving to a place of study, where students may need help that cuts across housing, mobility, wellbeing, and local services. The objective was to understand student needs more holistically and to design a cross-cutting public service offering that responded better to the factors shaping wellbeing during this transition. The implementation combined wellbeing survey data collected in Tampere and Turku with clustering and analytical methods to identify groups of students requiring different kinds of support. The findings showed that issues such as the reliability of public transport and the quality of the natural environment played an important role in student wellbeing. Based on these insights, a bot was created to provide information on the topics students considered most important. The impact of the experiment lies less in large-scale uptake than in the lessons learned: it demonstrated the value of user insight, data analytics, and life-event-based service design, while also highlighting the need for stronger user experience capabilities and more proactive engagement if municipalities are to make cross-cutting digital services more effective and widely used.

results.title: Traffic load - Machine vision for collecting information on traffic load
results.proposal: Traffic load - Machine vision for collecting information on traffic load. Urban transport planning requires accurate information on how vehicles move through the city, yet municipalities often lack detailed, continuous data on traffic flows across key entry and exit points. In Tallinn, this created a practical challenge for planning decisions related to congestion, parking, road construction, and other transport measures, as authorities needed better evidence on how many vehicles entered and left the city each day. The objective of this use case is to generate a clearer picture of traffic load in order to support more informed and timely planning decisions. At a conceptual level, the application combines image capture, object recognition, and traffic counting to classify buses, cars, lorries, and motorcycles, with the potential to expand later to pedestrians and cyclists. results.title: Texta Toolkit - Identifying documents published without authorisation
results.proposal: Texta Toolkit - Identifying documents published without authorisation. The objective of this use case is to strengthen information governance by automating large-scale document review, supporting anonymisation, and enabling safer republication of sensitive materials where appropriate. At a conceptual level, the system combines document ingestion, text extraction, classification, and anonymisation functions within a scalable analysis environment for public-sector records. The impact includes much faster auditing of large repositories, lower manual effort, and reduced risk of unauthorised disclosure. It also improves compliance, supports open-data publication in safer forms, and creates sustained operational value by giving institutions reusable tools for document governance and privacy protection.

results.title: OTT - Predicting employment pathways
results.proposal: OTT - Predicting employment pathways. Employment services must decide how best to support jobseekers with very different skills, histories, and barriers to work, yet this can be difficult to do consistently when advisers are handling large caseloads and labour market conditions are changing. OTT was developed by the Estonian Unemployment Insurance Fund to improve understanding of client needs and to help identify the most suitable employment pathways for individual jobseekers. The objective is to support more accurate job recommendations, better targeting of retraining or reskilling measures, and more effective allocation of staff attention across client groups. The implementation uses machine-learning methods trained on more than 100,000 client records to estimate the probabilities of different employment outcomes and suggest appropriate positions or interventions based on qualifications and profile characteristics. At a conceptual level, the system combines client data, pathway prediction, and recommendation logic within a tool used by civil servants rather than as a fully autonomous public-facing service. It helps structure client segmentation, identify likely needs, and distribute workload more effectively among advisers. The impact includes more tailored support for jobseekers, improved matching to vacancies, and better-informed retraining guidance. It also enhances service efficiency, supports prioritisation of cases where intervention is most needed, and creates business value by making employment support more targeted and data-driven.

results.title: EE Parliament- A system for preparing of verbatim reports
results.proposal: EE Parliament- A system for preparing of verbatim reports. Parliamentary administrations are often required to publish accurate verbatim records very quickly after sittings conclude, yet doing so manually places significant pressure on stenographers and can limit both speed and consistency. In Estonia, the Chancellery of the Riigikogu needed a more efficient way to produce official transcripts within one hour of the end of a sitting and to open up these records for wider digital reuse. The objective of this use case is therefore to improve transcript production efficiency and accuracy while enabling parliamentary speech records to become machine-readable open data. The implementation uses a speech recognition system called Hans, developed with Estonian-language recognition technology, to transcribe speeches delivered from the parliamentary rostrum. At a conceptual level, the system converts live spoken contributions into draft verbatim text that can be processed and published more quickly than through manual transcription alone. It is integrated into the parliamentary reporting workflow and supports both operational publication and downstream data use. The impact includes reduced manual workload for stenographers, faster delivery of official reports, and improved accessibility of parliamentary proceedings. It also increases the scalability and reusability of legislative records by supporting their publication as structured, machine-readable data for use in other systems and public services.
results.memo: Proceed. EE Parliament- A system for preparing of verbatim reports is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Enhanced Care Management - Prediction model for hospitalisation/assistance
results.proposal: Enhanced Care Management - Prediction model for hospitalisation/assistance. The Estonian Health Insurance Fund, in collaboration with the World Bank, initiated a programme to improve the management of patients with chronic conditions by strengthening preventive care and reducing avoidable hospitalisations. General practitioners often face challenges in identifying high-risk patients who require intensified monitoring and intervention. The objective is to support risk-based care management by identifying patients most likely to experience adverse health events. The solution uses predictive modelling techniques applied to healthcare utilisation data, particularly medical billing records, to identify patterns associated with hospitalisation risk. Algorithms analyse patient histories and selected diagnoses to generate risk scores, enabling GPs to prioritise care interventions such as counselling and follow-up. The model is integrated into primary care workflows to support decision-making. Pilot results indicate improved targeting of high-risk patients and potential reductions in unnecessary hospital admissions and healthcare costs. However, the initiative remains at pilot stage with limited evidence of nationwide implementation.

The service was integrated into the programme’s broader digital support model and aligned with an evolving customer strategy focused on accessibility and end-to-end assistance. The impact includes faster first-response times, better support scalability, and lower pressure on human support teams. results.title: SATIKAS -  Detecting the agricultural grasslands changes
results.proposal: SATIKAS -  Detecting the agricultural grasslands changes. Agricultural agencies need reliable ways to verify whether grasslands have been mown, since this affects compliance with land-management and subsidy rules, yet traditional inspections are costly, selective, and difficult to scale across an entire country. SATIKAS was developed for the Estonian Agricultural Registers and Information Board to automate this monitoring task and improve oversight of grassland management using remote sensing. The objective is to support more efficient compliance checking by replacing or reducing manual inspection with systematic, data-driven observation of mowing activity. The implementation uses deep learning and convolutional neural network techniques to analyse satellite imagery from the Copernicus programme, particularly Sentinel data, together with reference information on farmer fields, historical inspection logs, and meteorological data. At a conceptual level, the system fuses geospatial imagery and administrative datasets to classify whether mowing has taken place on specific grassland parcels. The solution is one of Estonia’s earliest government uses of such methods and was described as still under development, with plans to expand its capabilities further. The impact includes broader and more frequent monitoring coverage, reduced inspection effort, and more consistent evidence for subsidy control. It also improves scalability and reliability in agricultural supervision while supporting better use of public resources and more targeted field verification where necessary.
results.memo: Proceed. SATIKAS -  Detecting the agricultural grasslands changes is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Camilla, Virtual assistant for public competitions
results.proposal: Camilla, Virtual assistant for public competitions. Public recruitment processes often generate very high volumes of candidate questions, and applicants can struggle to interpret open notices, timelines, procedures, and requirements without waiting for manual replies. Camilla was introduced by Formez, in collaboration with CSI Piemonte, to make information about public competitions easier to access and to reduce response times for people interested in ongoing calls. The objective is to provide always-available guidance, improve the applicant experience, and streamline the handling of repetitive questions in a high-demand recruitment environment. The implementation uses a generative-AI virtual assistant accessible through a dedicated web interface, trained and tested extensively by a Formez task force with technical support from CSI Piemonte. Formez reported that the tool went live on an experimental basis after more than 500 tests and that it operates 24/7 to answer questions about competitions managed by the institute; later reporting stated that it had already served over 5,000 users and handled around 22,000 questions, and that its scope had expanded to include ranking-related queries. At a conceptual level, the solution combines generative answering with institution-specific recruitment information in a public-facing assistant. The impact includes faster applicant support, lower pressure on manual help channels, and a scalable way to improve access to public competition information.

results.title: Three judges under suspicion of ‘cheating’ with artificial intelligence
results.proposal: Three judges under suspicion of ‘cheating’ with artificial intelligence. This case is not a public-service innovation project in the usual sense, but rather a controversy about the alleged use of generative AI in judicial drafting, which raises questions about transparency, accountability, and the acceptable role of automated tools in the justice system. In Portugal, suspicion arose after an appeal-court ruling reportedly contained odd phrasing and citations that lawyers argued might have been produced with the help of an AI system, prompting scrutiny of whether judges had relied on such tools in preparing a decision. The issue matters because courts depend on trust, legal accuracy, and human responsibility, and any use of AI in judicial reasoning or drafting can affect confidence in the integrity of judgments. The reported implementation, insofar as it can be described as one, would have involved a judge or judges using a general-purpose generative AI assistant to help produce legal text rather than a formally authorised court system integrated into judicial workflow. Public reporting indicates that the judges disputed the allegations and that the matter led to official discussion and inquiry rather than confirmation of an endorsed technology solution. The impact of the episode lies in highlighting governance risks: it intensified debate about standards for AI use in courts, the need for human oversight, and the importance of clear rules on whether and how judges may use generative tools.

results.title: CHAIN - Smart Water optimising energy consumption
results.proposal: CHAIN - Smart Water optimising energy consumption. The municipality of Aarhus sought to address inefficiencies in water and energy consumption within its water management infrastructure. Traditional systems lacked the capability to dynamically optimise operations based on real-time demand and system conditions. The objective of this use case is to improve energy efficiency and water quality monitoring through data-driven optimisation of water systems. The solution relies on sensor networks that collect detailed data on water consumption, flow, and quality parameters. Advanced analytics and machine learning techniques are applied to process these large datasets, enabling optimisation of pumping operations and early detection of anomalies. The system integrates sensor outputs with analytical models to support operational decision-making. As a pilot project, it demonstrates the potential to reduce energy consumption, improve system efficiency, and enhance sustainability in municipal water management.

results.title: Assess your entitlement to 906 aids: OpenFisca, a tool to writing rules as code
results.proposal: Assess your entitlement to 906 aids: OpenFisca, a tool to writing rules as code. Social and fiscal rules are often complex, difficult to compare, and hard for both citizens and administrations to apply consistently without digital support. OpenFisca addresses this by turning legal and policy rules into executable code that can be reused to simulate entitlements, compare scenarios, and power public-facing services such as benefit calculators. The objective is to create a common, computable representation of rules so that governments, researchers, developers, and civil society can debate, test, and deliver social and fiscal policy more transparently. The implementation uses the open-source OpenFisca framework, which models taxes and benefits through formal variables, entities, and rule logic that can be exposed through APIs and reused in services such as Mes Aides and Aides Jeunes. The current youth-oriented simulator publicly states that it can estimate eligibility for more than 1,060 aids in a few clicks, while beta.gouv.fr describes OpenFisca as a leading practical implementation of the Rules as Code movement used in multiple countries. At a conceptual level, the solution combines legal modelling, microsimulation, and software engineering to produce machine-executable policy logic. The impact includes faster and more transparent eligibility estimation, easier reuse across public services, and a scalable foundation for policy simulation, digital entitlement tools, and evidence-based reform analysis.

results.title: WISP - Road Crossing Management supported by AI - Pilot - Paris
results.proposal: WISP - Road Crossing Management supported by AI - Pilot - Paris. Urban traffic-light control often relies on static or costly automated regulation systems that do not adapt well to real-time traffic conditions, leading to unnecessary delays, higher emissions, and inefficient use of infrastructure. WISP was developed to address this problem by optimising traffic-light sequencing dynamically, with an initial field deployment at three intersections in the southern suburbs of Paris. The objective is to reduce waiting times, improve flow management, and lower the ecological and budgetary costs associated with conventional automated signal regulation. The implementation combines real-time traffic-data analysis, connected-vehicle data, optimisation algorithms, and a compact hardware module that can be installed in existing signal-control cabinets. The company states that its AI is specialised in reducing driver waiting time through real-time search for the best signal sequence and that the prototypes already showed waiting-time reductions ranging from 10 per cent to 50 per cent depending on the type of junction. At a conceptual level, the system links live digital traffic inputs with adaptive control logic and lightweight roadside hardware to support responsive intersection management. The impact includes faster vehicle movement through junctions, reduced environmental and operating costs, and a scalable model for upgrading traffic control without the expense of wholesale infrastructure replacement.

results.title: Open LLM France and LINAGORA - Open Source LLM model
results.proposal: Open LLM France and LINAGORA - Open Source LLM model. European organisations increasingly want language technologies that are transparent, locally governed, and better aligned with national languages and public-sector requirements than many closed commercial models. The OpenLLM France community and LINAGORA developed LUCIE in this context as an open-source French-language large language model intended to serve as a foundation for dialogue generation and understanding tasks. The objective is to strengthen sovereign and ethical AI capability, provide a reusable base model for French-language applications, and support uses such as meeting summarisation, virtual assistants, and document-related productivity tools. The implementation centres on a pre-trained dialogue-oriented language model developed with open and licensed training datasets, community participation, and access to French high-performance computing resources, including the Jean Zay supercomputer. LINAGORA states that the model is designed to reflect the characteristics of spoken interaction and to be fine-tuned for downstream tasks rather than treated as a fully finished product in itself. At a conceptual level, the initiative combines open model development, transparent data governance, and ecosystem collaboration to create a deployable base model for French-language systems. The impact includes greater technological autonomy, better support for French-language digital services, and a scalable open foundation for public and private innovation in language applications.

results.title: crowdHEDGE: Using AI to help governments and local authorities keep citizens safe
results.proposal: crowdHEDGE: Using AI to help governments and local authorities keep citizens safe. Local authorities need timely information on how public spaces are being used, especially when crowding, footfall, or unsafe proximity may affect public health and safety, yet traditional monitoring methods can be slow, incomplete, or costly to scale. In Turin, crowdHEDGE was piloted to help the city extract actionable insight from drone footage over parks and other public areas so that officials could understand how people were using space and respond more effectively. The objective is to improve situational awareness, support safer management of public areas, and provide public-health and city officials with evidence they can explore by location and time. The implementation uses drone video streams connected to an AI-based image-recognition and analytics system running with edge-computing infrastructure. According to Addfor, the solution processes footage close to the source, calculates metrics such as crowd size, approximate distancing, and foot-traffic levels, and presents results through a graphical interface for geographical and temporal analysis. At a conceptual level, the system combines aerial sensing, computer vision, and edge analytics in a workflow designed to reduce bandwidth demands while preserving operational responsiveness. The impact includes faster and more detailed insight into how public spaces are used, better support for local safety decisions, and a scalable model for using drone-based analytics in urban public administration.

results.title: Eduthek - The learning platform on AI for schools
results.proposal: Eduthek - The learning platform on AI for schools. Schools need accessible, up-to-date teaching materials on artificial intelligence, yet many teachers and families lack the time or specialist expertise to assemble reliable resources independently. Austria’s Eduthek responds to this by providing a dedicated digital space within the Ministry’s wider learning platform where teachers, pupils, and parents can access curated material on AI in a structured and reusable format. The objective is to improve AI literacy in schools, support teaching on a fast-changing topic, and make high-quality educational resources easier to find and apply across different levels of schooling. The implementation uses the Eduthek platform as a central repository and delivery channel for learning content, with a specific AI focus area that is continuously expanded and updated. The official course page describes the section as an overview of freely available teaching materials for lower and upper secondary education, designed to help schools address both the opportunities and the challenges raised by AI in everyday life and work. At a conceptual level, the solution combines digital curation, thematic organisation, and open access to support classroom use without requiring each school to build its own material base. The impact includes broader access to AI-related teaching resources, more consistent support for educators, and a scalable way to strengthen digital and technological understanding across the school system.

results.title: DutchCycling - Cycling Lifestyle AI
results.proposal: DutchCycling - Cycling Lifestyle AI. Streets in many cities remain dominated by cars, limited greenery, and fragmented cycling infrastructure, making it difficult for residents and planners to imagine what a healthier, more bicycle-friendly street could look like in practice. The DutchCycling Lifestyle AI project addresses this challenge by giving people a simple way to visualise how an existing street might be transformed into a greener and more cycle-oriented environment inspired by Dutch design principles. The objective is to stimulate public imagination, support discussion on liveability and active mobility, and make the Dutch cycling approach more tangible for users anywhere in the world. The implementation combines generative AI with Google Street View imagery and the expertise of Dutch cycling specialists, allowing users to enter an address, select or upload a street view, and generate alternative visualisations of a more sustainable street layout. At a conceptual level, the tool links image-based generation with mobility-design knowledge to create plausible illustrative scenarios rather than detailed engineering plans. Public project material also makes clear that the tool was designed primarily as an inspiration device and that the concept has since been made open source after the original public tool was taken offline. The impact lies in widening public engagement, making policy ideas easier to communicate visually, and providing a scalable digital method for promoting cycling-friendly urban transformation.

The implementation uses large language models developed by Heidelberg-based company Aleph Alpha and draws on publicly available information from the city of Heidelberg to generate responses. At a conceptual level, the solution combines a public information base with an LLM-powered conversational interface designed for municipal use. The impact includes easier access to city information, a more intuitive user experience, and better scalability of first-line citizen support, while also giving the city a practical way to experiment with European AI capability in public services.

results.title: Albert France Services - GenAI tool to support public servants
results.proposal: Albert France Services - GenAI tool to support public servants. results.title: Inter-municipal Chatbot MUNI - Aarhus
results.proposal: Inter-municipal Chatbot MUNI - Aarhus. Citizens often find municipal websites and self-service systems difficult to navigate, particularly when they are unsure which service they need or how to complete a process such as obtaining a passport, using MitID, or arranging childcare. MUNI was created to improve this interface between citizens and local government by offering a more conversational and accessible route into municipal services across a large inter-municipal collaboration in Denmark. The objective is to supplement or partially replace traditional self-service pathways with more efficient and user-friendly AI-supported interaction, while ensuring that people can still reach a human adviser if the automated route does not resolve their need. The implementation combines chatbot technology with integrations into municipal call-centre and self-service systems, including Puzzel and Selvbetjening.nu, and more recent descriptions present MUNI as an AI-driven chat and voicebot. Public descriptions of the project report collaboration across 36 municipalities, with the potential to expand further, and note that since launch citizens have rated the service highly, averaging 2.43 out of 3. Where the chatbot cannot provide sufficient help, it can offer a callback from a call-centre agent. The impact includes faster access to municipal guidance, better user experience, and stronger scalability of citizen support across participating authorities.
