results.title: ‘Fix the Streets’ - AI that leverages citizen-produced data to improve the streets
results.proposal: ‘Fix the Streets’ - AI that leverages citizen-produced data to improve the streets. Municipal engineering teams need timely, localised information on potholes, damaged signs, and other street defects, yet conventional inspections can miss issues or detect them only after delays. In Vaasa, the Fix the Streets initiative tackled this challenge by drawing directly on geo-located observations submitted by residents, turning citizen-generated reports into a richer operational picture of street conditions. The objective is to improve infrastructure monitoring, support faster and better-targeted maintenance decisions, and strengthen the city’s use of digital tools within its wider twin-transition and innovation agenda. The implementation combined a mobile application with a multi-format knowledge base built over two years from text, image, and video submissions. Working with Crowdsorsa, the Municipal Engineering Department used AI to analyse reported defects and linked the app with Vaasa’s digital signage and mapping systems for more precise localisation and follow-up. At a conceptual level, the solution joins crowdsourced data collection, geospatial mapping, and automated issue analysis in one workflow, while emphasising data minimisation in the handling of citizen input. The impact includes improved visibility of street health, more informed prioritisation of maintenance activity, and stronger evidence for infrastructure decisions. It also demonstrates a scalable model for combining citizen participation with digital monitoring to improve local public services.

evidence.quote: The impact includes improved visibility of street health, more informed prioritisation of maintenance activity, and stronger evidence for infrastructure decisions.

results.memo: Proceed. ‘Fix the Streets’ - AI that leverages citizen-produced data to improve the streets is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Kiri - chatbot for citizens' enquiries
results.proposal: Kiri - chatbot for citizens' enquiries. Municipal websites receive large numbers of routine citizen questions, yet residents increasingly expect immediate answers without having to wait for office hours or contact staff directly for simple matters. Kiri was introduced in this context as a pilot chatbot for several Danish municipalities, including Frederiksberg, to improve access to general information in citizen service areas such as passports and driving licences. The objective is to provide instant responses to common questions, reduce pressure on front-line service teams, and test whether conversational digital assistance can improve the overall citizen experience without handling sensitive case-specific issues. The implementation uses a public-facing municipal chatbot that interprets natural-language questions and returns answers drawn from predefined service information. At a conceptual level, the system relies on conversational language technology, structured municipal knowledge content, and website integration so that users can obtain immediate guidance directly on the municipality’s digital channels. The pilot was inspired by similar Scandinavian trials and was intentionally limited at first to frequently asked, general enquiries rather than individual case handling. The impact includes quicker access to information, more convenient self-service, and reduced demand on municipal staff for repetitive queries. It also offers a scalable support mechanism across municipalities and contributes to more consistent communication with citizens across digital service channels.

results.company: Kungsbacka municipality, Tjörn municipality, Gothenburg city, Region Skåne, Region Halland, and Västra Götaland Region
results.title: Svea - A shared digital assistant for the public sector
results.proposal: Svea - A shared digital assistant for the public sector. Public-sector organisations handle large volumes of text-based work every day, from drafting and revising documents to summarising material, classifying content, and supporting administrative processes, yet these tasks consume significant staff time and are difficult for single organisations to automate alone. In Sweden, the Svea initiative was created as a joint effort between authorities, municipalities, regions, and industry, coordinated by AI Sweden, to develop shared capability rather than fragmented local solutions. The objective is to support public employees in routine text tasks, free time for more interpersonal and creative work, and establish the conditions for national cooperation on shared AI solutions in the public sector. The implementation is organised in phases, beginning with data generation, change management, use-case identification, and prototype development, and continuing with large-scale testing and evaluation. Svea itself is a web-based chat assistant built on open-source, model-agnostic architecture running on Swedish infrastructure; it can already answer organisation-specific questions, summarise documents, extract information, and rewrite text in easy-to-read Swedish. AI Sweden states that participating organisations collectively spent 2,500 hours annotating training data for the assistant. The impact includes stronger reuse of data and effort across institutions, improved scalability of AI adoption, and better productivity in text-heavy public work, while helping organisations prepare for labour shortages and rising service demand.
results.memo: Proceed. Svea - A shared digital assistant for the public sector is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: GPT-SW3 - The first large-scale generative language model for the Swedish language
results.proposal: GPT-SW3 - The first large-scale generative language model for the Swedish language. Swedish organisations increasingly need language technologies that reflect local linguistic realities and can be developed within a national ecosystem rather than relying entirely on foreign models. GPT-SW3 was created to address this need by providing a large-scale generative language model for the Nordic languages, with a primary focus on Swedish, through collaboration between AI Sweden, RISE, and WASP WARA Media & Language. The objective is to give organisations in Sweden access to a strong domestic foundation for language applications, while also strengthening the country’s applied AI capability across public, private, and academic sectors. The implementation uses a large-scale generative model based on the same broad technical principles as contemporary transformer-based language models, trained to support Nordic-language generation and downstream applications. At a conceptual level, the project combines national collaboration, technical development, and ecosystem building through AI Sweden, which brings together more than 120 partners and is funded by both the Swedish government and public- and private-sector participants. The impact includes a stronger Swedish-language AI infrastructure, new possibilities for organisations to build local language applications, and improved strategic capability in a domain often dominated by global providers. It also creates long-term value by supporting innovation in Swedish and Nordic language technology through a shared national platform.
results.memo: Proceed. GPT-SW3 - The first large-scale generative language model for the Swedish language is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: CitiVERSE - LDT CitiVERSE EDIC
results.proposal: CitiVERSE - LDT CitiVERSE EDIC. Cities across Europe are developing digital twins to support planning and public-service innovation, but these systems often remain local, fragmented, and difficult to connect into a broader European capability. The LDT CitiVERSE EDIC initiative was created to link existing local digital twins and form the foundation of a broader European CitiVERSE, enabling more coordinated development of data-driven and simulation-based tools for urban policy and citizen interaction. The objective is to strengthen cooperation between participating countries, improve the use of digital twins in smart-city policy, and support new forms of simulation and engagement around issues such as traffic, congestion, air quality, and decarbonisation. The implementation uses the European Digital Infrastructure Consortium model to establish a shared governance and infrastructure framework for networked local digital twins. At a conceptual level, the initiative connects data, analytics, simulation, and generative AI applications so that cities can model real-time or future urban conditions and also explore virtual-reality tools that help citizens understand proposed urban changes more easily. The Commission notes that Croatia, Estonia, France, Latvia, Portugal, Slovenia, and Spain initially called for the EDIC to be established. The impact lies in stronger interoperability between local digital twins, greater capacity for collaborative urban innovation, and more scalable smart-city services across Europe, creating both public-sector efficiency gains and better-informed citizen participation.
results.memo: Proceed. CitiVERSE - LDT CitiVERSE EDIC is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: GenAI chatbot on the EU-FarmBook platform
results.proposal: GenAI chatbot on the EU-FarmBook platform. Farmers, foresters, advisers, researchers, and policymakers often need practical knowledge quickly, but relevant materials are frequently spread across projects, languages, and institutions, making them hard to find and apply. EU-FarmBook addresses this challenge by building an open online platform to support knowledge exchange across the European agricultural and forestry innovation ecosystem. The objective is to make research-based and practice-oriented resources easier to discover and use, while improving knowledge transfer between actors at regional, national, and European levels. The implementation includes an AI-powered conversational assistant developed with support from TNO, designed to help users retrieve relevant information interactively from the platform. At a conceptual level, the chatbot uses generative AI to respond to users in a conversational way while grounding its answers in the platform’s own database of contributions, tools, guides, and other materials. Recent project communications state that the AI technology is European and that the responses are based on content held within EU-FarmBook itself, supporting controlled and domain-relevant retrieval. The impact includes easier access to specialised information for users with different backgrounds, improved usability of a large cross-European knowledge platform, and more efficient dissemination of project results and practice-based insight. It also supports scalability by turning a growing repository into a more navigable and interactive service for rural communities.

results.company: Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate
results.title: GPT-NL - A language model for the Dutch language and culture
results.proposal: GPT-NL - A language model for the Dutch language and culture. Many widely used language models are developed outside the Netherlands and may not adequately reflect Dutch language use, legal requirements, or national priorities around privacy, cultural context, and technological independence. GPT-NL was launched to address this strategic gap by creating an open Dutch language model designed to strengthen national capability in AI, data science, and data spaces while supporting compliance with European rules. The objective is to improve strategic autonomy, foster domestic expertise, and provide a trustworthy foundation for language applications built around Dutch language and culture. The implementation centres on the development of an open large language model funded by the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate Policy through RVO, with EUR 13.5 million allocated to the project after the “Facility for a sovereign Dutch language model” proposal was awarded in October 2023. At a conceptual level, the initiative focuses on building and governing a Dutch-language model in line with the GDPR and the AI Regulation, with an explicit aim of avoiding training sources that infringe privacy or intellectual-property rights. The impact is expected to include a stronger national knowledge base, improved access to compliant Dutch-language AI infrastructure, and greater capacity for public and private organisations to build applications suited to local linguistic and regulatory needs, creating long-term value through sovereign digital capability.
results.memo: Proceed. GPT-NL - A language model for the Dutch language and culture is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Boosting efficiency and transparency in processing of Official Publications with AI tools - AI for thematic classification
results.proposal: Boosting efficiency and transparency in processing of Official Publications with AI tools - AI for thematic classification. Public administrations publish large volumes of official notices across multiple gazettes and journals, and classifying those notices by topic or procedure is essential if citizens and organisations are to find relevant information quickly. In Barcelona, the same service behind the provincial gazette and official documentation search tools introduced CIDOBOT to support the thematic classification of official publications and improve the accessibility of public information disseminated through the CIDO service. The objective is to reduce the manual burden of classification, increase consistency across large document flows, and make it easier for users to track procedures, regulations, grants, procurement, and other official activity. The implementation uses a neural-network-based deep-learning model trained on human-produced summaries and classifications from a range of official bulletins and journals. At a conceptual level, the system performs documentary analysis of incoming public information and assigns it to thematic or procedural categories such as public procurement, collective agreements, local regulations, grants, and personnel selection. The project documentation explains that the model was trained using classified material from several official publications, including provincial bulletins, the Catalan official journal, and the national gazette. The impact includes faster and more standardised classification, improved discoverability of public information, and stronger transparency for users of CIDO, while also creating a replicable and scalable model for modernising administrative information management.

results.title: Boosting efficiency and transparency in processing of Official Publications with AI tools - AI for summaries
results.proposal: Boosting efficiency and transparency in processing of Official Publications with AI tools - AI for summaries. Official gazettes and public-information services handle very large numbers of notices and announcements, yet preparing concise, accurate summaries of those publications manually is resource-intensive and can slow publication workflows and reduce consistency. In Barcelona, the Service of the Official Provincial Gazette and Official Documentation and Publications sought to improve the efficiency and transparency of this process by automating the drafting of short summaries for official notices published in the provincial gazette. The objective is to reduce manual effort for both submitters and staff, speed up publication processing, and improve the accessibility of official information for users of the gazette and related public-information services. The implementation uses a supervised machine-learning and neural-network system trained on a large corpus of previous publications to generate summaries automatically in Catalan or Spanish. The project documentation states that the system was trained with 275,000 publications from 2013 to 2022, processes the first two pages of an announcement, and returns a summary of up to 100 words, while also recording manual edits for later retraining. The impact includes faster summary production, lower workload, improved consistency, and better scalability as publication volumes grow. It also supports transparency by making official content easier to understand and reuse within public-information services.
results.memo: Proceed. Boosting efficiency and transparency in processing of Official Publications with AI tools - AI for summaries is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: EMi Smart Employment: Emi: AI at the service of job matching and skills development in Galicia
results.proposal: EMi Smart Employment: Emi: AI at the service of job matching and skills development in Galicia. Employment services must support jobseekers and employers in a labour market that changes quickly, where skills gaps, mismatched expectations, and fragmented information can reduce the effectiveness of matching and guidance. In Galicia, EMi Smart Employment was introduced to improve how the public employment system supports unemployed people, employers, and frontline staff by connecting individual profiles more closely with labour-market demand. The objective is to provide more personalised, higher-quality services, guide jobseekers towards the skills the market requires, and give employment-service professionals better tools for decision-making. The implementation combines big data and AI to analyse users’ abilities, labour-market information, and employment patterns in order to suggest relevant skills-development paths and better job matches. At a conceptual level, the platform offers tailored services to jobseekers and employers while also equipping staff in the Galician Public Employment Service with stronger analytical tools to interpret labour-market data and support case management. The system is therefore both a public-facing guidance service and an internal decision-support resource. The impact includes more personalised employability support, stronger skills alignment with market needs, and improved quality of matching and advisory services. It also enhances trust in the employment system by improving service outcomes, while creating a more scalable and data-informed approach to workforce development across the Galician employment ecosystem.

results.company: Ministry of Justice and Ministry of Territorial Cohesion
results.title: Mapping Portugal: leveraging Machine Learning for land registration
results.proposal: Mapping Portugal: leveraging Machine Learning for land registration. Accurate land registration is a longstanding challenge in Portugal, particularly for rural and mixed-use properties where ownership information may be incomplete, fragmented, or difficult to access. The BUPi initiative was created to modernise property management by improving the identification, georeferencing, and registration of land parcels, while also reducing regional disparities in access to information and supporting better territory management. The objective is to make property data more accessible and reliable, increase transparency, and provide a stronger evidence base for land governance, public planning, and sustainable development. The implementation combines the BUPi digital platform with machine-learning techniques that support property identification, anomaly detection, land-use classification, and faster processing of geospatial and registry-related information. At a conceptual level, the system links administrative property records with georeferenced parcel data and analytical tools so that land can be identified more precisely and processed more efficiently. Public reporting on the programme notes the scale of the task, with more than eight million land records still requiring georeferencing during the expansion phase, and highlights the use of advanced technologies to accelerate knowledge about the territory. The impact includes improved data quality, quicker land-registration processes, stronger transparency, and better support for strategic decision-making, creating a more scalable and accurate basis for understanding and managing Portuguese territory.
results.memo: Proceed. Mapping Portugal: leveraging Machine Learning for land registration is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.company: Autonomous Entitat Autònoma del Diari Oficial i de Publications (EADOP)
results.title: Application of Generative AI to the Generalitat de Catalunya to facilitate citizens' understanding of legal texts
results.proposal: Application of Generative AI to the Generalitat de Catalunya to facilitate citizens' understanding of legal texts. Legal texts are essential to public life, yet their technical language often makes them difficult for citizens to understand, limiting access to rights, obligations, and public information. In Catalonia, the Entitat Autònoma del Diari Oficial i de Publicacions and the Legal Portal of Catalonia address this issue by making plain-language summaries of legal rules available to the public, with the aim of improving comprehension, accessibility, and transparency in the dissemination of current law. The objective is to reduce the barrier created by specialist legal drafting and to help citizens navigate Catalan legislation more confidently, while making clear that the official legal text remains the only authoritative source. The implementation uses generative AI to produce unofficial summaries of Catalan legal rules in plain language for publication on the Legal Portal. The initial rollout covered 44 rules in Catalan and 44 in Spanish, with the Generalitat stating that the approach would extend to the more than 14,000 legal provisions then in force; later reporting indicated that more than 16,000 summaries had been made available. The summaries are expressly presented as informational, not as legal advice. The impact includes easier public access to legal information, faster large-scale production of citizen-friendly summaries, and improved transparency and inclusiveness in legal communication, while supporting a more scalable model for making complex public information understandable.
results.memo: Proceed. Application of Generative AI to the Generalitat de Catalunya to facilitate citizens' understanding of legal texts is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Parcel Monitoring Platform Flanders, an AI-based geo-imaging tool for data-driven policy formulation and evaluation
results.proposal: Parcel Monitoring Platform Flanders, an AI-based geo-imaging tool for data-driven policy formulation and evaluation. Public authorities increasingly need continuous, parcel-level intelligence to support decisions in agriculture, energy, spatial planning, and environmental management, yet raw satellite imagery alone is often too noisy and technically demanding for direct policy use. In Flanders, Digitaal Vlaanderen and VITO developed the Parcel Monitoring Platform to provide more precise, timely, and actionable monitoring of land parcels in support of data-driven policy formulation and evaluation. The objective is to detect relevant changes in land use and parcel conditions more effectively and to give agencies evidence that can support operational monitoring and Green Deal-related policy tasks. The implementation combines AI and geo-imaging techniques with Sentinel time series, aerial imagery, GIS layers, and field data. Raw satellite images are pre-processed in Terrascope, while the CropSAR time-series service allows users to access derived Sentinel-1 and Sentinel-2 parameters for specific parcels without performing the image processing themselves. At a conceptual level, the platform uses data fusion and change-detection workflows to generate parcel-level notifications relevant to specific policy use cases. The impact includes better monitoring coverage, faster detection of meaningful changes, and stronger support for evidence-based public action. It also improves scalability by turning complex earth-observation data into reusable services for multiple governmental domains.
results.memo: Proceed. Parcel Monitoring Platform Flanders, an AI-based geo-imaging tool for data-driven policy formulation and evaluation is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Water monitoring using AI in South Tyrol
results.proposal: Water monitoring using AI in South Tyrol. Water utilities need better visibility over the condition and performance of distribution systems, yet smaller operators in particular often lack integrated tools for monitoring, maintenance planning, and rapid response to leaks, interruptions, or inefficient network behaviour. In South Tyrol, AiAqua addresses this challenge by offering a digital platform and app designed to help operators keep their water-distribution systems under closer and more continuous control. The objective is to improve the efficiency and sustainability of water-network management, reduce waste and service interruptions, and support better operational and investment decisions. The implementation combines a mobile application with a software-as-a-service platform that includes network-modelling functions, heuristic optimisation, machine learning, and data-analysis components. At a conceptual level, the system brings together monitoring data from measurement devices, alarms, images, notes, and network-configuration information to support day-to-day operational oversight and longer-term planning. The impact includes improved water saving, energy efficiency, and maintenance management, alongside better support for renovation planning and network resilience. It also creates value by giving small and medium-sized operators access to a more scalable and integrated water-management capability than they might otherwise be able to build independently.
results.memo: Proceed. Water monitoring using AI in South Tyrol is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Erhvervsstyrelsen - Detection of errors in business statements
results.proposal: Erhvervsstyrelsen - Detection of errors in business statements. Supervising corporate filings and financial statements at scale is difficult for regulators because manual review cannot easily keep pace with the volume of submissions, while material errors and potentially fraudulent reporting may remain hidden among routine cases. The Danish Business Authority developed this use case to strengthen risk-based supervision by identifying suspicious patterns and highlighting significant errors in business and financial statements more efficiently. The objective is to improve control quality, target inspections more intelligently, and reduce unnecessary burdens on compliant businesses by focusing attention where risks are highest. The implementation uses machine learning models within the authority’s data and control environment to analyse company filings and financial statements for indicators of fraud, irregularities, or non-compliance. At a conceptual level, the solution combines administrative and statement data with digital risk-scoring methods to prioritise cases for review and support supervisory decision-making. This fits into a broader risk-based control framework used by the authority in relation to company law and accounting oversight. The impact includes more effective detection of problematic filings, better allocation of inspection resources, and stronger trust in business reporting. It also supports scalability in regulatory control, improves consistency in case selection, and creates value by enabling more proportionate and data-driven oversight across very large filing volumes.

results.title: ChatBot Assistant PosteItaliane
results.proposal: ChatBot Assistant PosteItaliane. Large service providers receive high volumes of routine customer enquiries about digital services, products, and website functions, and handling all of them through email or telephone support alone can create avoidable delays and operational pressure. Poste Italiane introduced its digital assistant to offer users a simpler self-service route for common questions without requiring direct contact with an operator in every case. The objective is to improve the accessibility of customer support, speed up resolution of routine enquiries, and reduce pressure on traditional contact channels. The implementation combines chatbot and voicebot capabilities within Poste Italiane’s assistance environment, allowing users to ask short natural-language questions and either receive guidance directly or, where necessary, be routed onwards to a human operator. At a conceptual level, the assistant uses conversational language processing and a structured support knowledge base covering products and services, and it is designed to provide support continuously rather than only during staffed service hours. The impact includes faster first-line support, better user convenience, and more efficient handling of repetitive customer-service interactions. It also improves scalability by shifting a share of standard enquiries to automated channels while preserving escalation paths for cases needing human assistance.

results.title: AI predicts cardian arrest in Copenhagen
results.proposal: AI predicts cardian arrest in Copenhagen. Recognising cardiac arrest during emergency calls is a high-stakes operational challenge, because callers may describe symptoms unclearly and dispatchers must make life-critical decisions within seconds. In Copenhagen, Emergency Medical Services introduced a real-time analytical tool to improve recognition of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest during 112 calls and provide dispatchers with earlier warning when a call matches patterns associated with cardiac arrest. The objective is to increase recognition rates, support faster intervention, and improve survival chances by strengthening dispatcher decision-making during the call itself. The implementation uses a real-time speech-analysis solution that listens to the ongoing emergency call, compares patterns in the dialogue with historical call data, and calculates the probability that the incident involves cardiac arrest. At a conceptual level, the system applies predictive pattern recognition to live call audio and feeds alerts to the medical dispatcher handling the case, functioning as decision support rather than a replacement for human judgement. Reported results indicate that the tool identifies around 85 per cent of cardiac arrests, compared with approximately 75 per cent recognised by dispatchers alone, corresponding to roughly 150 additional patients being recognised before the ambulance arrives. The impact includes faster diagnosis, better quality of emergency response, and more effective use of pre-hospital care resources.

results.title: Corti's AI - Emergency medical services real-time speech analysis for cardiac predictions
results.proposal: Corti's AI - Emergency medical services real-time speech analysis for cardiac predictions. Emergency call handlers must identify cardiac arrest within seconds, yet callers often describe symptoms unclearly and high-pressure conditions can lead to delayed recognition or missed warning signs. This use case addresses that operational problem by supporting dispatchers and call-takers during emergency calls so that out-of-hospital cardiac arrests can be recognised faster and with fewer errors. The broader objective is to improve emergency medical response, reduce avoidable mortality, and strengthen the reliability of call-centre decision-making in time-critical situations. The implementation uses real-time speech analysis on live emergency calls, applying predictive models trained to detect linguistic and behavioural patterns associated with cardiac arrest. At a conceptual level, the system listens to the call as it unfolds, analyses speech signals and conversational content, and produces immediate decision support for human operators. The approach is intended to work alongside dispatch professionals rather than replace them, feeding alerts and clinical suggestions into the emergency response workflow. Reported performance from the original deployment described detection accuracy of up to 95 per cent, and the Copenhagen implementation was sufficiently promising to support wider piloting with the European Emergency Number Association. The impact includes quicker diagnosis, reduced error rates, faster dispatch decisions, and stronger overall service quality, with clear public value in improving survival chances during medical emergencies.

results.title: Elements of AI - free online course designed by the Icelandic government
results.proposal: Elements of AI - free online course designed by the Icelandic government. Building broad public understanding of artificial intelligence requires educational offers that are accessible to non-specialists, especially if governments want citizens and workers to engage confidently with technological change. The Elements of AI initiative addresses this challenge by providing a free online course aimed at a wide audience, explaining what artificial intelligence is, what it can and cannot do, and how people can begin to understand or develop related methods. The objective is to expand AI literacy across society and lower the barriers to entry for learners without advanced mathematics or programming backgrounds. The implementation consists of a series of online courses created by MinnaLearn and the University of Helsinki and delivered through digital learning platforms designed for self-paced participation. At a conceptual level, the programme combines structured educational content, practical examples, and accessible explanations so that learners from varied backgrounds can engage with core concepts. The material is presented as open, reusable digital education rather than as a specialist technical qualification. The impact includes broader public access to foundational AI knowledge, improved digital skills awareness, and greater readiness among learners to understand the implications of AI in work and society. results.title: Artificial intelligence in Ingolstadt's transport system - KIVI
results.proposal: Artificial intelligence in Ingolstadt's transport system - KIVI. Modern transport systems often lack a complete and up-to-date view of all road users, particularly pedestrians and cyclists, which makes it harder to optimise traffic control and improve safety in mixed urban environments. In Ingolstadt, the KIVI project was developed to address this problem by building a more comprehensive, multimodal picture of traffic conditions across selected network nodes and using that information to support smarter control and warning functions. The objective is to improve traffic efficiency and safety by recognising all relevant road users, forecasting network conditions, and adapting traffic measures more precisely to real demand. The implementation combines local high-definition stationary sensors with mobile sensors from cars, buses, bicycles, and pedestrians equipped with 5G-enabled devices, and fuses these data using data-driven methods into a current digital representation of the traffic situation. At a conceptual level, the system supports network-wide multimodal forecasting, demand-based green-time allocation for different road users, a traffic-light phase assistant, and warning functions that recognise behaviour and intent and provide visual or acoustic alerts in dangerous situations. The impact includes better situational awareness, more balanced traffic control, and stronger protection for vulnerable road users. It also supports smarter urban mobility management by improving scalability, responsiveness, and the quality of data available for operational traffic decisions.

results.title: System to control social welfare recipients
results.proposal: System to control social welfare recipients. Welfare administrations responsible for pensions, housing, family, disability, and maternity-related benefits face a difficult balance between protecting public funds and respecting the rights of citizens, especially when fraud controls operate across very large populations. In Denmark, Udbetaling Danmark uses automated controls to analyse whether payments are lawful by bringing together data from multiple public registers, including tax, housing, and civil records, as well as information relating to family members and housemates. The objective is to detect irregularities, identify potentially unlawful payments, and support centralised control of welfare disbursement at scale. The implementation combines broad data integration with evolving analytical criteria, including modular checks whose partial results are combined into an overall conclusion on whether further scrutiny is warranted. At a conceptual level, the system functions as a large-scale risk and compliance engine embedded within the administration of welfare benefits, supporting investigators and decision-makers by flagging cases of possible concern. The impact is greater control capacity, faster identification of suspicious cases, and improved scalability in payment oversight. At the same time, the use case illustrates the trade-offs associated with extensive public-sector data analysis, particularly where large volumes of personal data are processed in ways that raise concerns about privacy, proportionality, and discrimination.

results.title: PCA - AI algorithms in audit methodology detecting potential fraud when prescribing medicines
results.proposal: PCA - AI algorithms in audit methodology detecting potential fraud when prescribing medicines. AI algorithms in audit methodology detecting potential fraud when prescribing medicines. Between 2014–2018, big data analysis was used to examine prescribing of two expensive ophthalmology drugs, Eylea and Lucentis, in Slovakia. The study found that 15.5% of patients were treated atypically, with high concentrations of irregular prescribing in three centres. These anomalies could stem from medical decisions, patient non-compliance, or potential fraud, with estimated savings of €1.8M if practices matched national norms. Following the analysis, health insurers tightened monitoring and restrictions for these treatments. The case highlights how big data can uncover inefficiencies and protect public resources, while final judgments must rest with medical experts.

The objective of this use case is to support more efficient procurement preparation and solution design by identifying whether in-house technology components can satisfy requirements described in procurement or offer documentation. results.title: (AILUME) - Artificial Intelligence-Based Application for the Early Detection of Forest Fire Outbreaks
results.proposal: (AILUME) - Artificial Intelligence-Based Application for the Early Detection of Forest Fire Outbreaks. AILUME is an artificial intelligence system developed to strengthen Galicia’s response to one of its greatest environmental threats: forest fires. The region’s vast forest coverage, rural depopulation, and increasing climate change impacts make early detection essential. AILUME addresses this by continuously analysing video streams from the Xunta de Galicia’s forest surveillance camera network, strategically placed across the territory. Using advanced deep learning models, optimised YOLO detectors, and vision-language reasoning, the system identifies smoke, filters false alarms, and provides explainable alerts to operators at the Central Coordination Center for Forest Fire Defense. The platform combines state-of-the-art AI with robust software architecture: a Django-based modular backend, Apache Kafka for distributed real-time processing, PyAV/OpenCV for video capture, and PostgreSQL for structured data management. It includes a human-in-the-loop feedback system, ensuring that operator validation contributes to continuous learning and higher detection accuracy. Designed for resilience and scalability, the solution can handle dozens of concurrent video streams with sub-second data latency, operating 24/7 under real production conditions. Pilot testing launched in August 2025 has confirmed its effectiveness: 86.1% detection success in real-world cases, precision of 98.2%, recall of 99.9%, and detection lead times averaging 18 minutes earlier than official notification channels. The system has already proven especially valuable in depopulated rural areas where traditional surveillance is limited, outperforming commercial alternatives in both accuracy and speed.

The solution is fully interoperable with existing internal systems, integrates seamlessly into data pipelines, and complies with GDPR, CCPA, and organisational policies. Its advanced Natural Language Processing (NLP) and Machine Learning (ML) capabilities allow context-aware recognition of PII in structured and unstructured data, outperforming traditional rule-based methods. The tool has delivered measurable impact, including an 85% reduction in data breaches involving unauthorised PII exposure, significant labour cost savings, and increased user confidence. By providing a reliable, scalable, and user-friendly solution, the AI tool strengthens operational efficiency, data integrity, and transparency, allowing secure data sharing with internal teams and external partners without compromising privacy.

results.proposal: ROSE - Route optimisation module for waste logistic platforms - Montana (BG) pilot. Municipal waste collection often runs on fixed schedules that do not reflect actual container fill levels, leading to unnecessary journeys, higher operating costs, avoidable fuel use, and excess emissions. The aim of this use case is to improve the efficiency and sustainability of urban waste collection by ensuring that collections take place only when needed and with the most suitable routing and vehicle allocation. The implementation, led by Theoremus, uses an advanced logistics routing engine that clusters waste containers according to historical fill rates, assigns the most appropriate vehicles to each cluster, and optimises collection schedules using transport data patterns. The results are already measurable: the project anticipated a 10–20% reduction in miles driven and operating cost, and in the Montana pilot weekly collection distance fell by 10.2%, from 173.03 km to 155.36 km, with fuel consumption and CO₂ emissions reduced by a similar margin. This improves operational performance, lowers congestion and heavy-vehicle presence on local streets, and creates stronger long-term value through more data-driven and scalable waste-management practices.

results.title: Visa Application Chatbot for the EU countries
results.proposal: Visa Application Chatbot for the EU countries. The European Commission, in collaboration with Member State authorities and eu-LISA, initiated the VisaChat pilot to address challenges faced by visa applicants in accessing clear and consistent information on Schengen visa procedures. Applicants often rely on fragmented or complex sources, increasing administrative burden and the risk of errors in applications. The objective of the use case was to provide a unified, accessible interface to answer frequently asked questions and improve user experience. The solution consists of a chatbot application designed to respond to general visa-related queries using predefined knowledge bases. It employs supervised learning techniques based on curated datasets of standard responses in multiple languages, complemented by machine translation and unsupervised approaches to extend multilingual capabilities. The system is modular and built using open-source technologies, allowing flexible deployment either centrally or through Member State portals. Privacy-by-design principles are incorporated, including explicit restrictions on collecting personal data. As a pilot conducted between 2021 and 2022, the project demonstrated feasibility in improving information access, but no evidence confirms transition to full-scale implementation.

results.title: IVORY – ‘AI for Vision Zero in Road Safety’
results.proposal: IVORY – ‘AI for Vision Zero in Road Safety’. Achieving major reductions in road fatalities requires more than isolated technical improvements, as road safety depends on the interaction between vehicles, infrastructure, human behaviour, governance, and public trust. In support of the United Nations target to halve traffic deaths by 2030 and the European Vision Zero strategy to eliminate road fatalities by 2050, this use case aims to build a robust framework for responsible innovation in road safety while developing specialist expertise across sectors. The stakeholders include universities, industrial partners, associated organisations, researchers, and road safety actors from ten countries. The implementation takes the form of an industrial doctoral network bringing together engineering, data science, and ethics of technology to develop new responsible AI applications for road-user assistance and infrastructure safety management. The programme integrates research training, cross-sector collaboration, and applied experimentation, with 13 researchers working on solutions that combine advanced analytical methods, domain knowledge, and governance considerations. Rather than a single product, the system is a coordinated innovation and learning platform designed to connect research outputs with real-world road safety needs. The expected impact includes stronger interdisciplinary capability, improved methods for safer transport systems, and a more scalable pipeline of expertise. It also creates long-term value through knowledge transfer, international collaboration, and more reliable foundations for future road safety innovation.

results.title: GenAI for Legislative Drafting - Prime Minister's Office
results.proposal: GenAI for Legislative Drafting - Prime Minister's Office. Analysing statements submitted during consultation rounds is a demanding part of legislative preparation, as officials must review substantial volumes of written feedback, identify recurring themes, and produce coherent summaries under time pressure. This creates an operational challenge in terms of workload, speed, and consistency, especially when consultation material is extensive and diverse in style or content. The purpose of this use case was to assess whether automated support could help the Prime Minister’s Office process consultation responses more efficiently and accelerate the preparation of summary material for legislative work. The implementation tested the Finnish Poro language model in a summarisation setting, with the experiment carried out by Silo Gen AI Oy and funded by Sitra. At a conceptual level, the approach used a Finnish large language model to generate condensed summaries from consultation texts, exploring how language technology could support document analysis in a policy environment. The trial focused on the model’s ability to synthesise large volumes of textual input into usable outputs for expert review. The results showed clear potential for increasing efficiency in the analysis of consultation rounds, even though the summaries produced were not yet of sufficient quality for operational adoption. Even so, the exercise generated valuable learning on model limitations, future capability needs, and opportunities to improve productivity, scalability, and evidence handling in legislative processes.

results.proposal: GenAI for Legislative Drafting - Ministry of Transports. In this context, the Ministry of Transport and Communications sought to improve the efficiency of drafting work while also reinforcing Finland’s strategic autonomy in digital capability. The objective of the use case was to test whether a practical support service could help drafters navigate legislative content more effectively and retrieve relevant information in a structured manner. The implementation consisted of a service demonstrator built by Futurice around Finnish-language large language models, delivered through a chatbot-style interface. At a conceptual level, the solution allowed legislative drafters to query legislation and related materials in natural language, with the model supporting information retrieval, question answering, and synthesis over large text collections. The system design explored how domestic language models could be incorporated into policy workflows while remaining aligned with public sector requirements. The results indicate potential for reducing time spent searching and reviewing documentation, improving accessibility of complex legal material, and supporting more efficient drafting processes. The wider business value includes strengthened experimentation capacity, greater technological sovereignty, and a foundation for more scalable digital support in public administration.

results.title: FloReST - Intelligent tools for urban flood resilience
results.proposal: FloReST - Intelligent tools for urban flood resilience. Increasing frequency of heavy rainfall events has exposed urban areas to significant risks of flash flooding, causing damage to infrastructure and disrupting communities. Municipal authorities require tools to plan emergency drainage routes and improve resilience, but traditional hydraulic modelling approaches are complex, time-intensive, and difficult to scale. The FloReST project, funded by the German Federal Ministry of Education and Research, aims to enhance urban flood resilience by providing decision-support tools tailored to local conditions. The solution combines hydraulic-numerical modelling with machine learning techniques to simulate and optimise emergency water drainage pathways across urban environments. These models are supported by data from terrain, infrastructure, and environmental sources, enabling scalable analysis of larger catchment areas. The project also includes user-oriented applications designed to support municipalities and infrastructure operators in planning and response. Pilot testing of a smart application with end users took place in 2024. The approach demonstrates improved modelling efficiency and usability, supporting better preparedness and risk mitigation, although full operational deployment remains under evaluation.

results.title: A2I - Networked hearing system with innovative sensors
results.proposal: A2I - Networked hearing system with innovative sensors. In audiological, occupational health, and cardiological care, clinicians often rely on fragmented observations and periodic assessments, which can limit their ability to identify emerging issues early and respond with appropriately tailored interventions. This is particularly relevant where hearing-related data may also provide insights into wider physiological conditions, yet such information is not routinely captured or connected across care pathways. The purpose of this use case is to create a user-centred socio-technical system that improves prevention, diagnosis, and care processes by using sensor-based data gathered in and around the ear. The implementation combines innovative hearing-related sensors with data analysis methods to process continuous or repeated health signals collected from wearable or ear-based devices. Analytical models are used to detect patterns relevant to audiological status, occupational exposure, and cardiological indicators, while the overall architecture links sensing technologies, health data processing, and evaluation workflows in a conceptually integrated system. The development approach is explicitly user-focused, ensuring that the technical design reflects clinical and practical needs. The expected impact includes earlier identification of health risks, better continuity of care, and more efficient clinical decision-making. Additional value lies in improved service integration, stronger preventive capacity, and the potential to scale monitoring and assessment across multiple healthcare contexts with greater reliability and personalisation.

results.title: ABILITY - Improving the accessibility of digital images for blind users
results.proposal: ABILITY - Improving the accessibility of digital images for blind users. For blind and visually impaired people, digital images often remain difficult to access in a meaningful way, because standard image analysis tools are typically designed around the assumptions and preferences of sighted users. This creates a gap between what current systems can technically describe and what users actually need in order to form an accurate and useful mental representation of visual content. The objective of this use case is to improve accessibility by developing image interpretation tools tailored to the needs, expectations, and sensory strategies of blind and visually impaired users, with these users involved directly as co-designers and evaluators. The implementation combines computer vision, large language models, and visual-assistant language models with extensive user studies, tactile interaction research, and iterative testing. The partners are also developing dedicated hardware, including a tactile tablet and a pin-display device capable of presenting simplified object outlines, zoomed elements, and other selected outputs derived from image analysis. The system concept therefore links multimodal models with tactile interfaces and user-centred evaluation methods. The anticipated results include more relevant and nuanced image descriptions, improved usability and trust, and a more inclusive digital experience. More broadly, the project supports accessible design innovation, stronger user adoption, and better alignment between emerging image technologies and real user needs.

results.title: AI4Justice, Intelligent assistant to support judges in drafting sentences by locating texts of previous judgments and jurisprudence
results.proposal: AI4Justice, Intelligent assistant to support judges in drafting sentences by locating texts of previous judgments and jurisprudence. The time dedicated by judges to search for precedents and legal foundations to write a sentence is high and an impediment to being more agile in the drafting of sentences, causing a high response time and a sense of slow justice. Currently, the location of paragraphs of interest of legal or procedural references, of any documentary information or the entirety of the magistrates' own judgments or resolutions previously issued, which may be applicable or reusable in the drafting of new judgments or resolutions, becomes a manual and costly process that causes magistrates to spend a lot of time locating, remembering, and reviewing previous judgments, relying on their memory, both for their content and the date they were issued. In Catalonia, the judge usually performs a manual search in the procedural management application for justice (eJusticia.cat), in the archive of the magistrate's own judgments, or through the Judicial Documentation Center (CENDOJ), depending on the General Council of the Judiciary (CGPJ), as well as other repositories or jurisprudential databases. The search is more or less effective depending on what the magistrate remembers at that time from similar cases or parts of an old judgment that may be applicable to the current one. The unmet need is to locate reusable information within judicial documents, such as sentences issued in any instance and jurisdiction, in order to speed up and facilitate the drafting of new sentences by judges. Currently, the location of paragraphs of interest (headings, legal foundations, dispositive part or judgment), legal or procedural references or the entirety of the judges' previous sentences, that are applicable or reusable in the drafting of new sentences, becomes a manual and costly process that causes judges to spend a lot of time locating, remembering and reviewing previous judgments, based on memory, both of their content and of the date they were issued. The solution proposed is an assistant to judges and magistrates that, by entering an open text or prompt, can quickly, accurately, and relatedly obtain all applicable historical information for the sentence being drafted. In the same way, the assistant must provide the applicable legal foundations and sentence draft for a better management of mass litigation cases with hundreds of very similar claims accumulate that has also similar resolutions. It is important that the judicial powers have the necessary resources to ensure agile and efficient justice, such as having digital tools that facilitate the location of reusable information from previous sentences and jurisprudence to draft new sentences.

results.title: MODUL-F: empowering public administration through low-code/no-code
results.proposal: MODUL-F: empowering public administration through low-code/no-code. Public administrations in Germany face persistent challenges in digitising internal procedures, often relying on fragmented, manual, or paper-based processes that slow service delivery and burden staff. Developing custom IT solutions is costly and time-consuming, especially for smaller authorities. MODUL-F addresses this challenge by enabling administrations at federal, state, and local levels to digitise internal specialist procedures quickly and consistently. The objective is to support end-to-end digital workflows in line with the Online Access Act (OZG) while reducing dependency on bespoke software development. MODUL-F is implemented as a cloud-based software-as-a-service platform using a low-code/no-code approach. Administrative staff can create digital procedures by assembling pre-programmed, reusable modules that represent common administrative functions and rules. These modules can be shared across organisations, ensuring standardisation and interoperability. The platform is rule-based, allowing consistent execution of procedures without complex programming. As a result, administrations can digitise processes faster, lower development and maintenance costs, and improve consistency across jurisdictions. MODUL-F increases scalability, empowers non-technical staff, and accelerates digital transformation, delivering measurable efficiency gains and supporting sustainable modernisation of public administration.

results.title: Predicting Image Quality Degradation in Digital Radiology
results.proposal: Predicting Image Quality Degradation in Digital Radiology. Optimal design of medical x-ray imaging systems is essential for delivering maximum image quality while minimizing radiation risk to patients. The performances of imaging devices could degrade over time. For this reason, quality control (QC) programs are in place in the health systems to verify that the clinical image quality remains acceptable over the years guaranteeing the diagnostic capability. The Medical Physicists (MP) is the responsible for the QC program, ensuring high standards in medical diagnostics and maintaining the reliability and safety of medical imaging. Currently MPs perform constancy quality checks on Digital Radiography (DR) system, acquiring radiological images on phantoms and extracting specific information (e.g., non-uniformity). The results are then compared to baseline values and any deviation is evaluated. In such scenario the QC tests only provide a “snapshot” of the system performance at a specific moment over time, until the next inspection or service event not allowing to anticipate malfunctions. The objectives of the project are two-fold: automating processing of radiological image, conducting images analysis using in-house software macros and bash script and discovering trends on an ongoing basis with the aim of detecting and fixing DR system performance problems before clinical operations are affected. Performance characteristics of 19 DR systems from 5 manufacturers have been analyzed over 10 years of monthly and annually QC test. Study has been focused on non-uniformity test, based on 4 image parameters and their tolerances: Local signal non-uniformity, Global Signal non-uniformity, Local Signal to Noise Ratio non-uniformity, Global Signal to Noise Ratio non-uniformity. 1825 images were analyzed running the in-house software macros and bash script on each image to calculate the 4 baseline metrics. The second step was developing a predictive model for assessing the degradation state of DR system using the automatically images-processed database. The model has to predict the pass/no-pass label for each image. The building process involves leveraging the combined strengths of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) and Long Short-Term Memory Networks (LSTMs) to analyze sequential radiological images from a images-processed database, grouping images into sequences for effective analysis akin to video sampling. By analyzing the sequential radiological images, this model aims to preemptively identify trends in equipment degradation. This capability is crucial for maintaining high standards in medical diagnostics, ensuring reliability and safety in medical imaging and patient care. The CNN architecture, based on ResNet-18, efficiently extracted spatial features, while the LSTM component, incorporating temporal data, was crucial in detecting patterns of degradation over time. Training and validation of the model were conducted on cloud based machine-learning platform, providing the necessary computational resources and scalability. Data augmentation strategies were implemented to balance the dataset, particularly addressing the scarcity of no-pass labels, thereby enhancing the model’s predictive capability. The model demonstrated a consistent training loss, indicating effective learning, and achieved a validation accuracy of 88.2% after 100 epochs, showcasing its ability to accurately classify the condition of DR systems. This level of accuracy reflects the model’s strong performance and its potential to generalize well to new data. In summary, in this project we proposed a new approach to QC test, starting from the availability of images and data stored through 10 years of activity. A predictive tool, based on AI-model was developed for non-uniformity QC test, with the result of decreasing the interval to detection of substandard performance. This type of approach, in which the primary goal is to preemptively identify trends in equipment degradation, can change the QC scenario.

results.title: Mona - Public chatbot for companies on the subject of the economy
results.proposal: Mona - Public chatbot for companies on the subject of the economy. Businesses often need rapid, reliable guidance on economic measures, employment rules, subsidies, and administrative obligations, especially during periods of disruption such as the coronavirus crisis, when demand for official information rises sharply and questions become more varied. In this context, the Federal Ministry for Digitisation and Business Location introduced Mona through the Company Service Portal to give companies a simpler and more accessible way to obtain practical support on economic matters. The objective is to reduce information barriers for firms, improve access to official guidance across web and mobile channels, and help users navigate complex topics such as financial support, labour law, short-time work, teleworking, and research-related measures. The implementation combines a public-facing conversational interface with structured information flows, enabling both free-form questions and guided step-by-step navigation through key thematic areas. At a conceptual level, the service uses natural language understanding to interpret user requests, retrieve relevant information, and deliver responses through a chatbot integrated into the national business portal. The impact includes faster access to official information, lower demand on traditional support channels, and a more user-friendly experience for companies. It also improves service scalability, strengthens consistency of communication, and creates operational value by making critical business information available in a more efficient and responsive way.

results.company: Capital Region of Denmark (Bispebjerg Hospital and Rigshospitalet) DTU and Region Zealand
results.title: WARD-HOME – Safe discharge from hospital
results.proposal: WARD-HOME – Safe discharge from hospital. WARD-HOME focuses on enabling safe early discharge of patients by addressing the risk of undetected deterioration once patients return home. Healthcare providers require continuous monitoring solutions to ensure patient safety while reducing hospital stays and associated costs. The objective is to support rehabilitation at home through timely detection of health deterioration and rapid clinical response. The solution builds on a wireless monitoring system that continuously collects vital parameters such as heart rate, oxygen saturation, and respiratory rate. These data are analysed using predictive algorithms to assess patient condition in real time and trigger alerts when intervention is needed. The system integrates conceptually with clinical monitoring platforms, enabling healthcare professionals to oversee patients remotely. The impact includes reduced hospital length of stay, improved patient safety, and enhanced quality of care. It also supports healthcare system efficiency by optimising resource utilisation, increasing scalability of remote care, and improving patient experience through home-based recovery.

results.title: Artificial intelligence to support the visitation of referrals from general practice
results.proposal: Artificial intelligence to support the visitation of referrals from general practice. The use case addressed inefficiencies and inconsistencies in the handling of patient referrals from general practitioners to hospitals, where large volumes of referrals require manual processing, classification, and routing across multiple stages. This creates delays, variability in decisions, and administrative burden for clinical staff. The objective is to improve consistency, efficiency, and patient rights by optimising the referral handling process. The solution uses natural language processing and classification models to analyse referral content and automatically assign cases to the appropriate medical specialty and local department. For selected specialties, the system further associates referrals with predefined patient pathways. It is integrated conceptually with hospital information systems to support seamless workflow automation and human oversight. The impact includes faster processing times, improved consistency in decision-making, and reduced administrative workload. This leads to better patient experience, more efficient use of clinical resources, and enhanced operational scalability within hospital systems.

results.title: Artificial intelligence for predicting exacerbations in multidisease with easy-to-understand explanation of complex results
results.proposal: Artificial intelligence for predicting exacerbations in multidisease with easy-to-understand explanation of complex results. The project focuses on improving care for citizens with multiple chronic conditions, where disease progression is complex and difficult to monitor, often leading to unanticipated exacerbations and hospitalisations. Healthcare professionals require better tools to anticipate deterioration and communicate risks clearly to support timely intervention and patient trust. The objective is to enhance clinical decision-making and patient outcomes through early detection and understandable risk assessment. The solution combines clinical data on chronic diseases with contextual information, such as epidemiological trends, using predictive modelling techniques to forecast potential exacerbations. Explainability methods are incorporated to translate complex model outputs into clear, interpretable insights for clinicians and patients, ensuring transparency and ethical use. The system is conceptually integrated into clinical workflows to support decision-making without disrupting existing practices. The impact includes earlier interventions, reduced hospital admissions, and improved patient outcomes. It also enhances trust and usability through transparent communication, while supporting more efficient resource allocation and improved quality of care.

results.company: CAMES Rigshospitalet, DTU Compute, Region Zealand, Southern Denmark and North Jutland
results.title: Better diagnostics of pregnant women using artificial intelligence
results.proposal: Better diagnostics of pregnant women using artificial intelligence. Early identification of complications during pregnancy is essential to initiate preventive measures and improve maternal and neonatal outcomes. However, variability in ultrasound image quality can affect diagnostic accuracy and limit the ability to predict adverse developments. This project aimed to enhance the quality and consistency of prenatal ultrasound examinations by supporting clinical staff, including midwives, nurses and doctors, during scanning procedures. Building on a validated prototype capable of assessing completed ultrasound recordings, the solution was further developed into a real-time decision-support tool. Advanced image analysis algorithms evaluate scan quality during the examination, providing immediate feedback to ensure that images meet predefined clinical standards. The system integrates with existing ultrasound equipment and clinical workflows, enabling seamless adoption without disrupting routine practice. By improving image quality at the point of care, the tool increases diagnostic reliability and supports earlier detection of potential complications. Expected impacts include more accurate risk assessment, improved patient safety and more efficient use of clinical resources, contributing to higher overall standards in prenatal care.

results.title: Artificial intelligence for the prevention of malnutrition and hospitalization of the elderly
results.proposal: Artificial intelligence for the prevention of malnutrition and hospitalization of the elderly. Malnutrition among older citizens is a major risk factor for prolonged hospital stays, readmissions and increased mortality, yet early identification in community settings remains challenging. The project aimed to prevent emergency hospitalisations by identifying individuals at risk of malnutrition so that timely interventions could be initiated. Health and care data were analysed using predictive modelling techniques to detect patterns associated with nutritional risk. Risk scores were generated to support care professionals in prioritising preventive measures, such as dietary support or follow-up assessments. The system was designed to integrate with existing municipal health records, ensuring that insights could inform routine care processes. By enabling earlier intervention, the solution seeks to improve treatment outcomes, enhance self-reliance and increase quality of life for elderly citizens. Anticipated impacts include reduced hospital admissions, lower long-term care costs and more proactive, data-driven management of elderly health services.

results.company: Aalborg Municipality, Syddjurs Municipality, Aalborg University
results.title: Increased continuity in elderly care using artificial intelligence
results.proposal: Increased continuity in elderly care using artificial intelligence. Elderly citizens often experience fragmented home care services involving multiple caregivers, which can reduce perceived safety and continuity of care. The project aimed to enhance transparency and improve the citizen experience by increasing continuity in the staff assigned to each individual. Building on the existing Greenforce planning solution, the system was adapted to incorporate additional parameters such as actual time spent per visit and limits on the number of different caregivers assigned. Algorithmic optimisation generated visit schedules balancing continuity, working hours and operational constraints. A feedback loop enabled continuous retraining based on user input and operational outcomes. The solution was implemented in Aalborg and Syddjurs municipalities, allowing comparison across organisational structures and urban–rural contexts. Results indicate improved planning transparency, more consistent caregiver assignments and potential reductions in travel time between visits. The initiative strengthens quality of care, supports greener routing and provides a scalable model for data-driven workforce planning in elderly services.
results.memo: Proceed. Increased continuity in elderly care using artificial intelligence is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: An effective and holistic employment effort through the artificial intelligence technology Process Mining
results.proposal: An effective and holistic employment effort through the artificial intelligence technology Process Mining. The use case addresses inefficiencies and fragmentation in public employment services, where multiple stakeholders—including job centres, administrative units, and case workers—operate across disconnected systems, limiting coordinated and citizen-centric support. The objective is to enable a more flexible and holistic employment pathway by improving transparency, identifying bottlenecks, and supporting informed decision-making across organisational boundaries. The solution applies process mining and predictive monitoring techniques to existing log data from case management and financial systems, reconstructing end-to-end citizen journeys and mapping workflows, actors, and interventions. Machine learning models analyse historical data to identify patterns in successful outcomes and predict the most effective interventions for different citizen groups, with integration into existing IT systems for continuous analysis and visualisation. The impact includes enhanced process transparency, improved coordination, and more targeted interventions, leading to increased efficiency and better employment outcomes. Additional benefits include reduced administrative burden, improved scalability, and more consistent, data-driven decision-making.

results.title: Decision support for handling municipal document access cases
results.proposal: Decision support for handling municipal document access cases. Municipalities face increasing demand for access to public documents, requiring significant administrative effort to review, redact, and process requests in compliance with legal requirements such as data protection regulations. Manual handling of these cases is time-consuming and may lead to inconsistencies. The objective is to improve efficiency, quality, and consistency in processing document access requests. The solution uses natural language processing models to analyse large volumes of text, identify relevant documents, and detect information that requires anonymisation. These models support case handlers by automating parts of the review process and enabling more efficient file searches. The system is designed to integrate with existing administrative workflows and ensure compliance with data protection requirements. As a pilot project in Sønderborg Municipality, it demonstrates potential to reduce processing time and administrative burden while improving service quality.

results.company: Julius Kühn Institute Federal Research Institute for Cultivated Plants (JKI)
results.title: AI^2 - (Aphid identification through artificial intelligence)
results.proposal: AI^2 - (Aphid identification through artificial intelligence). The AI² project focuses on improving the monitoring of harmful insects in agriculture, where timely detection is critical to prevent crop damage and ensure food security. Traditional methods of analysing insect trap data are labour-intensive and slow, limiting the ability to respond quickly to emerging threats. The objective is to automate identification and counting of insect species in monitoring systems. The solution uses machine learning and deep learning techniques to analyse images from airborne insect traps, identifying and classifying species such as aphids. Neural networks are trained on labelled datasets to recognise visual patterns and quantify insect populations. The system enables rapid and standardised analysis across multiple locations. As an ongoing development project, it demonstrates potential to significantly reduce processing time, improve consistency of results, and support early detection and management of invasive pests.

results.proposal: CONMAR - studying contaminated sites with underwater drones. The CONMAR project addresses the environmental and safety challenges posed by marine munitions and contaminated sites in coastal and offshore areas. These hazards are difficult to monitor due to limited accessibility and fragmented data across institutions. The objective is to improve understanding, monitoring, and management of such sites through integrated data and advanced technologies. The solution combines underwater drones with data integration and analysis tools to collect and process information on contaminated areas. Machine learning techniques are applied to analyse sensor and imaging data, supporting detection and assessment of hazards. The project also integrates existing datasets from research organisations, government agencies, and industry to create a comprehensive knowledge base. As a research and development initiative, the project is ongoing, with expected outcomes including improved environmental monitoring, informed policy decisions, and enhanced remediation strategies.
