results.title: Differentiation of ship types on satellite radar images
results.proposal: Differentiation of ship types on satellite radar images. Monitoring maritime activities over large ocean areas is critical for environmental protection, security, and enforcement against illegal activities such as unregulated fishing. Traditional methods rely on manual interpretation of satellite imagery, which is time-consuming and limited in scalability. The objective is to automate the detection and classification of vessels using remote sensing data. The solution applies deep learning techniques to satellite radar images, enabling the identification and differentiation of ship types based on their radar signatures. These models are trained on labelled datasets and integrated into earth observation systems used by authorities and organisations. The system supports applications such as maritime surveillance, environmental monitoring, and enforcement. The project demonstrates potential to improve detection accuracy and operational efficiency, although full deployment details remain limited.

results.proposal: Environmental monitoring of sea trouts with AI. The objective of this use case is to automate the monitoring process and improve accuracy in species identification and counting. The solution uses underwater cameras to capture video sequences, which are analysed using deep learning models trained to distinguish sea trout from other objects such as leaves or different fish species. The system processes visual data to detect and count individuals in real time or through batch analysis. This approach enables scalable and consistent monitoring across different locations. results.title: Outdoor Mobility Digital Twin at TU Delft
results.proposal: Outdoor Mobility Digital Twin at TU Delft. The Technical University of Delft developed a digital twin of its campus environment to analyse and manage pedestrian and cyclist flows during the COVID-19 pandemic. Managing crowd density in public spaces became critical to ensure safety and compliance with health measures. The objective is to provide real-time insights into mobility patterns and support data-driven decision-making for crowd management. The solution integrates data from sensors that convert visual inputs into privacy-preserving representations, combined with external data sources such as public transport locations and infrastructure status. These data are visualised in a three-dimensional digital twin dashboard, using heat maps to indicate crowd density and movement patterns. Advanced analytics are applied to identify congestion and support scenario analysis. As a pilot, the system demonstrates the potential to improve situational awareness, enhance safety, and optimise space utilisation, although no evidence confirms long-term operational deployment.

results.title: Support the integration of job seekers with artificial intelligence
results.proposal: Support the integration of job seekers with artificial intelligence. The University of Applied Sciences Kiel, in collaboration with Jobcenter Kiel and the Institute for Labour Market and Vocational Research, is developing tools to improve the integration of job seekers into the labour market. Employment services often face challenges in matching individuals with suitable job opportunities and training pathways, particularly when dealing with diverse profiles and labour market dynamics. The objective is to enhance counselling services through data-driven recommendations. The solution uses machine learning techniques, including self-organising maps and reinforcement learning, to analyse anonymised data and cluster job seekers based on skills, experience, and labour market conditions. These clusters are used to generate personalised recommendations for employment, retraining, and further education opportunities. The system is designed to complement the expertise of job centre staff and support decision-making processes. The project aims to improve matching efficiency and service effectiveness, although no evidence confirms full operational deployment.

results.proposal: AI-Supported unmanned aeriasl vehicles (UAVs) for Ecological Agriculture and Forestry. This project explores the use of unmanned aerial vehicles to support ecological agriculture and forestry management. Monitoring weeds, crop health, and forest conditions typically requires significant manual effort and may lack precision at scale. The objective is to enable automated and efficient environmental monitoring and intervention. The solution involves adapting an existing AI-based weed detection system to operate on low-power embedded hardware mounted on drones. Machine learning models process visual data captured by onboard sensors to identify weeds and assess vegetation conditions in real time. The project also investigates the transferability of these models to forestry applications. Integration with drone platforms allows flexible and targeted data collection across large areas. As a research and development initiative, the system is still being tested and validated, with expected benefits including reduced labour requirements, improved precision, and more sustainable land management practices

results.title: KI4GeoSeDa – AI-Based Georeferencing of Specialist Data Pools for Semantic Data Integration
results.proposal: KI4GeoSeDa – AI-Based Georeferencing of Specialist Data Pools for Semantic Data Integration. The Schleswig-Holstein State Office for Surveying and Geoinformation, in collaboration with the Karlsruhe Institute of Technology, aims to improve the integration of heterogeneous spatial datasets used in public administration. Many specialised databases contain location references in unstructured textual form, making it difficult to integrate them into standardised geospatial systems. The objective is to enable automated georeferencing and semantic integration of such data. The solution uses natural language processing and machine learning techniques to analyse address data and linguistic spatial references, converting them into precise geospatial coordinates. These outputs are then integrated into existing spatial data infrastructures, enabling unified access and analysis. The system supports semantic enrichment and interoperability across datasets. As a pilot project, its focused on algorithm design and validation includes with expected benefits including improved data integration, enhanced decision-making, and more efficient use of geospatial information.

results.proposal: KI4Forst - Monitoring the Forest with Satellite Data and AI. The Schleswig-Holstein State Office for Surveying and Geoinformation aims to improve forest monitoring and management by leveraging satellite data. Traditional methods for assessing forest conditions are resource-intensive and may not provide timely or comprehensive insights into environmental changes such as drought damage or pest infestations. The objective is to enable automated, large-scale monitoring of forest areas and their condition. The solution involves developing an automated processing chain that applies deep learning techniques to satellite imagery. Image classification models, based on artificial neural networks, are trained to detect forest areas and distinguish between different forest types, such as deciduous and coniferous. The system also identifies changes in vegetation health and potential damage. Outputs are integrated into geospatial information systems for visualisation and decision support.

results.title: Kora - virtual assistant
results.proposal: Kora - virtual assistant. The Municipality of Heidenheim introduced Kora, a virtual assistant designed to provide round-the-clock responses to common citizen enquiries. The objective was to improve accessibility to municipal information while reducing administrative workload. Kora operates as a self-learning chatbot integrated into the municipal website, handling approximately 70 enquiries per day with a reported success rate of 99 per cent at launch. Initial high-demand topics included weather, local events and coronavirus-related guidance. The chatbot standardises responses, shortens waiting times and ensures consistent information delivery outside office hours. By automating routine enquiries, the municipality can allocate staff resources to more complex cases requiring individual attention, enhancing service efficiency and digital engagement.

results.title: Big Data Analysis for HR efficiency improvement
results.proposal: Big Data Analysis for HR efficiency improvement. The pilot project aimed to assess how a big data tool deployed on the Governmental State Cloud Infrastructure could support advanced analysis of HR datasets. The solution integrated personnel records, performance indicators and administrative data into a centralised analytics environment, applying data mining and statistical techniques to identify patterns related to staffing levels, absenteeism and organisational performance. Dashboards and reporting tools enabled managers to explore trends and simulate scenarios for workforce optimisation. By consolidating data sources and automating analysis, the project enhanced evidence-based decision-making in HR management. Anticipated benefits include improved allocation of human resources, increased organisational effectiveness and better-informed strategies to support staff development and satisfaction, while demonstrating the scalability of cloud-based analytics within public administration.

results.title: Aeolus – Mid-altitude maritime monitoring platform for security, search & rescue and environmental monitoring
results.proposal: Aeolus – Mid-altitude maritime monitoring platform for security, search & rescue and environmental monitoring. Maritime authorities require wide-area surveillance to address security threats, coordinate search and rescue operations and monitor environmental risks, yet conventional ship-based sensors have limited range constrained by low elevation. The Aeolus project aims to extend maritime situational awareness by elevating monitoring systems to mid-altitude, thereby expanding coverage without deploying additional vessels. The platform consists of an airborne sensor system operating at approximately 450 metres above a host ship, increasing the observable area by more than eleven times compared with standard configurations. It can be deployed using different lifting mechanisms and remain operational for extended periods. Equipped with optical and radar sensors, the system transmits real-time data to onboard command centres, where information is processed and integrated with existing surveillance systems. The solution enhances detection capabilities for vessels, persons in distress and environmental anomalies, while improving operational efficiency. By increasing coverage and persistence at relatively low cost, the platform strengthens maritime safety, supports faster response times and enables scalable monitoring across diverse missions.

results.title: HOPE - Healthy Outdoor Premises for Everyone
results.proposal: HOPE - Healthy Outdoor Premises for Everyone. Urban air quality monitoring traditionally relies on a limited number of fixed stations, providing only coarse-grained insights into citizens’ actual exposure to pollution. In the Helsinki region, this limits the ability of individuals and policymakers to understand air quality variations at neighbourhood or street level. The HOPE project addresses this gap by enabling hyper-local air quality monitoring through a dense, participatory sensing network. Stakeholders include citizens, city authorities, researchers, and public health organisations. The objective is to provide accessible, location-specific information on air pollution exposure in daily life. The solution combines data from fixed monitoring stations with crowdsourced measurements collected via portable sensors carried by citizens. These data are aggregated and visualised on digital maps, providing near real-time insights into air quality across the city. The project enhances spatial coverage, raises public awareness, and supports evidence-based urban planning and health interventions. HOPE empowers citizens with actionable information, improves understanding of pollution dynamics, and supports targeted measures to improve urban environmental health and quality of life.

results.title: VDAB Chatbot for job seekers - Chatbots to better match jobseekers with the right vacancies
results.proposal: VDAB Chatbot for job seekers - Chatbots to better match jobseekers with the right vacancies. Jobseekers often need timely, practical support when searching for vacancies, yet traditional guidance channels can struggle to provide immediate and personalised assistance at scale. This creates a challenge for employment services that aim to help large numbers of users navigate vacancies, ask questions, and receive relevant direction throughout their search process. The objective of this use case is to improve the quality and accessibility of job-search support by using conversational tools that can answer questions and guide users towards suitable opportunities. The implementation involves chatbot technology designed to participate in typed conversations with jobseekers, automatically responding to enquiries and helping users progress through their search. At a conceptual level, the solution uses conversational language processing to interpret user input, provide answers, and support matching-related interactions between jobseekers and the employment service. The chatbot is positioned as part of a broader exploration of how conversational systems can strengthen vacancy discovery and candidate guidance. The impact includes quicker access to support, a more responsive user experience, and better assistance outside the limits of traditional one-to-one service models. It also increases service scalability, reduces pressure on human support channels, and creates business value by helping more jobseekers engage effectively with vacancies and employment services.

results.title: Camera System - Mobile phone usage on vehicles
results.proposal: Camera System - Mobile phone usage on vehicles. The Belgian road safety institute Vias identified the growing risk of traffic accidents caused by drivers using mobile phones while driving, particularly handheld usage. Traditional enforcement methods rely heavily on manual observation by police, limiting detection rates and scalability. This use case aims to enhance enforcement capabilities by automating the identification of such violations and supporting road safety policies. The system uses roadside camera infrastructure to capture images of passing vehicles, which are then processed using computer vision techniques to detect whether a driver is holding and using a mobile phone. Images not indicating violations are automatically discarded, while detected cases are anonymised to protect privacy before further review. Law enforcement authorities validate flagged cases before issuing fines. The solution integrates image recognition models trained on annotated datasets to distinguish relevant behaviours. The pilot demonstrates the feasibility of augmenting enforcement through automated pre-selection of violations, improving efficiency and enabling more consistent monitoring. results.title: Diagnosis Plan and Control Tool - Assessing the risk of home fraud
results.proposal: Diagnosis Plan and Control Tool - Assessing the risk of home fraud. Municipal social services must prevent benefit fraud while ensuring proportional enforcement and safeguarding citizens’ rights. In complex housing situations, case officers faced difficulties in deciding when a home visit was justified, leading to inconsistent practices and inefficient use of limited inspection capacity. The objective of this use case was to support more consistent, evidence-based prioritisation of cases where discrepancies between declared circumstances and observed living conditions suggested elevated risk, while preserving human decision-making authority. The tool aggregated administrative data, including household composition, housing arrangements, declared living costs and registered debts, and applied statistical risk-scoring techniques to generate structured risk profiles. These profiles were integrated into existing municipal case-management systems and presented as decision support indicators rather than automated outcomes. Municipalities reported more focused inspections and fewer unnecessary home visits, improving resource allocation and operational efficiency. However, concerns regarding transparency, proportionality and potential bias prompted increased regulatory scrutiny, and similar profiling tools have since been restricted or discontinued in several municipalities

results.title: LATXA: a Basque language LLM
results.proposal: LATXA: a Basque language LLM. The Basque language, as a low-resource European language, faces structural disadvantages in the development of advanced natural language processing tools, limiting digital inclusion and the availability of high-quality language technologies for public services, education and industry. Existing large language models are predominantly trained on high-resource languages, constraining their effectiveness in Basque and reducing linguistic sovereignty. Stakeholders include language technology researchers, public institutions, educational bodies and technology developers working in the Basque ecosystem. The objective of the LATXA project is to develop foundational large language models specifically pre-trained for Basque, providing a robust technical base for downstream applications rather than a direct-to-consumer chatbot. The LATXA family consists of base transformer-based LLMs trained on curated Basque corpora using large-scale self-supervised learning. Model development was conducted on in-house GPU infrastructure, with final large-scale training executed on the Leonardo supercomputer at CINECA under the EuroHPC Joint Undertaking. These open models are released for expert users who can integrate or fine-tune them for task-specific applications. Expected impacts include strengthened digital presence of Basque, enhanced research capacity, support for public-sector language tools and a scalable foundation for future instruction-tuned and domain-adapted systems.

results.title: Algorithm based quality control of presidential candidates
results.proposal: Algorithm based quality control of presidential candidates. To ensure compliance with legal requirements for presidential candidacy, Czech authorities apply statistical verification to nomination signatures submitted by candidates. Candidates may qualify either through parliamentary support or by collecting 50,000 voter signatures. In the latter case, the Ministry of Interior conducts a statistical quality control process to verify that signatories are eligible voters. An algorithm randomly selects two batches of 8,500 signatures for detailed validation against population registers. Error rates identified in the samples are extrapolated to estimate the overall validity of submitted signatures. The process resembles statistical quality control methods used in auditing, enabling efficient review of large datasets without checking every entry individually. While the approach accelerates verification and standardises assessment, it has generated debate regarding sampling design and accuracy. In the 2013 election cycle, two candidates were excluded following application of this procedure. The system aims to balance administrative feasibility with electoral integrity safeguards.

results.title: STIR - an algorithm to fight VAT fraud in Poland
results.proposal: STIR - an algorithm to fight VAT fraud in Poland. Poland introduced the STIR system to combat large-scale VAT carousel fraud and organised tax evasion that significantly reduced public revenues. Operated by the National Revenue Administration under the State Clearing Chamber, STIR collects and analyses financial transaction data transmitted by banks and credit institutions to identify suspicious economic activity and high-risk entrepreneurs. The objective is to provide tax authorities with early risk indicators enabling rapid intervention, including temporary account freezes, without prior notification to the bank or account holder. The system processes transaction patterns, account behaviour and links to jurisdictions associated with VAT fraud, applying undisclosed risk-scoring algorithms and automated decision-support mechanisms. Where risk thresholds are met, authorities may block an account for up to 72 hours, extendable to three months. Legal provisions prohibit disclosure of the algorithmic criteria, with criminal penalties for unauthorised access or publication. STIR has strengthened investigative capacity, accelerated fraud detection and enabled preventative asset freezes, contributing to improved VAT collection performance in Poland, though concerns have been raised regarding transparency, due process and proportionality safeguards.

results.title: The Sensing Project for risk assessment and profiling by the Roermond police
results.proposal: The Sensing Project for risk assessment and profiling by the Roermond police. The Roermond police developed the Sensing Project to address recurring pickpocketing and shoplifting in a shopping district, focusing on patterns described as “mobile banditry”. The operational objective was to identify vehicles and groups considered likely to commit offences and deploy patrols more efficiently. The locally developed system analyses travel-related variables, including vehicle type, number of passengers, routes taken, licence plate information and links to rental vehicles previously associated with criminal incidents. Rule-based scoring mechanisms combine these factors to produce a composite risk score. When predefined thresholds are exceeded, the system generates an alert and records vehicle details in police databases, influencing subsequent risk calculations. Officers retain discretion in responding to alerts. Critics argued that the approach risked discriminatory profiling and created feedback loops, as prior registration increased future risk scores regardless of new evidence. results.title: “Top 600” and “Top400” used for automated risk modelling
results.proposal: “Top 600” and “Top400” used for automated risk modelling. Amsterdam authorities introduced the Top 600 and later Top 400 programmes to reduce high-impact crime by targeting individuals assessed as posing significant risk. The Top 600 focuses on young adults with prior arrests or convictions for serious offences, while the Top 400 addresses minors under 16 to enable early preventive intervention. The programmes aggregate police, municipal and social service data to produce ranked lists based on predefined criteria such as arrest history, judicial records and, for minors, broader social indicators. Statistical scoring and profiling methods prioritise individuals for coordinated multi-agency action plans. Those listed may face intensified supervision, frequent checks and tailored enforcement or support measures. Authorities report reductions in repeat high-impact offences among targeted groups and improved coordination between agencies. However, civil society organisations have raised concerns about due process, transparency and the impact on employment or residence status. The initiatives illustrate how data integration can support targeted crime prevention strategies while highlighting governance and rights-related challenges in automated profiling.

results.title: Pro-Kid used for risk assessment by the Dutch police
results.proposal: Pro-Kid used for risk assessment by the Dutch police. Since 2011, the Dutch police have used ProKid to support early identification of children and young people considered at risk of reoffending, informing preventive interventions by police and youth care services. The operational problem was to prioritise limited resources and identify cases requiring attention within the youth justice system. ProKid draws on police registration data, including criminal fact and criminal opinion databases, to generate structured risk classifications. It applies actuarial scoring techniques that assign weighted values to predefined variables, producing risk categories intended to indicate the likelihood of future police registration rather than proven criminal behaviour. The output can influence referrals to youth services and protective interventions, with significant implications for children and families. An evaluation by the Ministry of Security and Justice found that around one-third of assessed cases were misclassified due to data errors or inclusion of irrelevant incidents, raising concerns about reliability and proportionality. While the tool aimed to standardise screening and support preventive action, criticism has focused on data quality, transparency and the potential for unjustified stigmatisation.

results.title: Project RAPID - Automatic Identification of Passengers Holding Traveling Documents
results.proposal: Project RAPID - Automatic Identification of Passengers Holding Traveling Documents. Portugal’s Immigration and Border Service sought to increase efficiency and security at Schengen external borders in response to rising passenger volumes and evolving document fraud risks. In 2019, EUR 4.2 million plus VAT was invested to upgrade Project RAPID and deploy automated eGates at Lisbon, Porto, Faro and Madeira airports. The system integrates electronic passport authentication, chip reading compliant with ICAO standards and biometric verification to automate border control procedures. It reads data stored in the passport chip via secure protocols, verifies document authenticity, and performs facial comparison between the stored image and a live capture at the gate. Biometric matching algorithms generate a similarity score that determines whether the gate opens automatically or refers the traveller to an officer. The system is connected to national and European border management databases for additional checks. Implementation increased passenger throughput, reduced waiting times and standardised verification procedures while maintaining security controls. Automation allowed border officers to focus on high-risk cases and improved the overall traveller experience through faster, self-service processing.

Flight operations were assessed for cost, reliability and sample integrity compared with road transport. Results showed a reduction in transport time from 20 minutes by road to 7 minutes by drone, with improved sample quality due to reduced agitation and shorter exposure duration. The solution also demonstrated increased scheduling flexibility and responsiveness for urgent deliveries. The pilot highlights the potential of unmanned aerial logistics to enhance efficiency, reliability and quality in regional healthcare supply chains.

results.proposal: State Treasury e-invoicing plans. The Finnish State Treasury is responsible for overseeing and supporting financial management processes across central government entities, including the handling of a high volume of electronic invoices. The objective of the initiative is to increase the level of end-to-end automation in public sector invoice handling, reduce manual workload and improve accuracy and processing speed across government financial operations. The planned solution combines artificial intelligence techniques and robotic process automation to analyse structured and semi-structured invoice data. Machine learning models are designed to automatically extract and validate relevant invoice fields, such as contract identifiers and payment amounts, while rule-based automation tools integrate with existing financial management systems to route, verify and post invoices. The system relies on standardised e-invoice formats and interoperability frameworks, and is embedded within the State Treasury’s digital financial infrastructure to enable scalable, centralised processing. The initiative aims to enable near real-time invoice validation, significantly reduce manual intervention, minimise processing errors and accelerate payment cycles. By improving data quality requirements and promoting standardisation among suppliers, the State Treasury strengthens the reliability and efficiency of public financial management, reduces administrative costs and enhances transparency and scalability in government accounting processes.

results.title: Kommers (KAI) semantics check tool
results.proposal: Kommers (KAI) semantics check tool. Public procurement processes in both public and private sector organisations require clear, unambiguous tender documentation to ensure fair competition and avoid misinterpretation by potential bidders. However, procurement texts often contain complex legal and technical language, which can lead to misunderstandings, increased bidder risk, additional clarification rounds and, ultimately, delays in contract award and project execution. Stakeholders in this context include procurement officers, legal advisors, potential suppliers and contracting authorities, all of whom benefit from improved clarity and reduced ambiguity in procurement materials. The objective of this initiative is to enhance the quality and precision of procurement documentation by identifying semantic inconsistencies, ambiguous phrases and unclear requirements before tender publication. The solution integrates an AI assistant into Primona’s Kommers e-procurement platform, extending its existing modules with natural language processing (NLP) capabilities. The AI component performs semantic analysis on requirement statements, specifications and other textual elements within procurement documents to detect unclear wording, potential contradictions and language that might be misinterpreted by bidders. The tool leverages trained language models and domain-specific lexicons, combined with syntactic and semantic rule sets, to highlight problematic segments to the procurement author. It is embedded within the Kommers workflow, allowing users to run checks directly within their document preparation interface and receive actionable feedback in real time. By automating semantic validation, the tool reduces the risk of ambiguous or poorly phrased procurement documents reaching the market, improving clarity and fairness in competitive tendering. This leads to fewer clarification requests, faster procurement cycles, reduced administrative burden for contracting authorities and a lower risk of bid disputes. Enhanced document quality contributes to better supplier engagement, more accurate tender responses and ultimately more efficient public and private sector procurement outcomes.

results.title: NUMEL.AI - A communication tool for neurological disorders
results.proposal: NUMEL.AI - A communication tool for neurological disorders. Neurological disorders are often difficult for patients to understand due to the complexity of medical imaging and the abstract nature of diagnostic explanations. Clinicians face challenges in communicating disease progression, anatomical alterations and treatment implications in a clear and accessible manner, particularly when relying on two-dimensional scans and technical terminology. NUMEL.AI addresses this communication gap by providing an interactive visualisation tool that enables doctors and patients to explore neurological conditions using the patient’s own medical imaging data. The objective is to enhance patient understanding, support shared decision-making and improve the quality of clinical consultations through immersive visual explanations grounded in real diagnostic data. The solution processes magnetic resonance (MR) images and other clinical imaging data imported directly from healthcare information systems to automatically generate personalised three-dimensional anatomical models. Computer vision techniques and body-tracking algorithms align these models with the patient’s body in real time using augmented reality rendering. Machine learning methods support image segmentation and the identification of relevant anatomical structures and disorder-related patterns. The system can operate locally or through a scalable, API-based cloud platform that allows secure data storage, retrieval and extensibility across healthcare environments. The tool improves the clarity and effectiveness of clinician–patient communication, enhances patient engagement and understanding of disease evolution, and supports more informed treatment discussions. Its scalable architecture facilitates integration with existing hospital systems, while automated model generation reduces preparation time for clinicians and increases the accessibility of advanced visualisation technologies in neurological care.

results.title: CLIP (Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training) for the Italian Language
results.proposal: CLIP (Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training) for the Italian Language. Many advanced multimodal models have been primarily trained on English-language datasets, limiting their performance and applicability in languages with fewer annotated resources, such as Italian. This creates challenges for researchers, public administrations and digital service providers seeking to develop image–text retrieval, content moderation or assistive technologies tailored to Italian users. The project aims to bridge this gap by developing a multimodal model capable of understanding and linking Italian textual descriptions with visual content. The objective is to provide a robust foundation model that enables accurate alignment between images and Italian language inputs, supporting downstream applications in search, accessibility and digital services. The solution builds upon the Contrastive Language–Image Pre-training (CLIP) framework, combining a pre-trained Italian BERT language model (dbmdz) with a Vision Transformer architecture for image encoding. Using approximately 1.4 million paired image–text samples, the model is fine-tuned through contrastive learning techniques that optimise the similarity between matching image–text pairs while distinguishing non-matching pairs. The resulting architecture enables joint embedding of visual and textual data within a shared semantic space, accessible through an online demonstration environment. The Italian CLIP model improves multimodal understanding in a low-resource linguistic context, enhancing the accuracy of image–text retrieval and classification tasks in Italian. By reducing dependency on English-centric models, it strengthens digital sovereignty, supports innovation in language-specific applications and provides a scalable resource for further research and public and private sector use cases.

results.proposal: Genome representation and artificial intelligence. Healthcare professionals, geneticists and researchers face challenges in rapidly interpreting whole-genome data to support personalised diagnosis and therapeutic decision-making, particularly in nephrology and other rare disease domains. To address this need, CSI Piemonte, in collaboration with the University of Turin (Departments of Medical Sciences and Clinical and Biological Sciences), the ISI Foundation and GenomSys, launched a research initiative aimed at improving genomic data analysis for clinical use. The objective is to enable faster, more accurate identification of genetic variants associated with rare diseases and to support the design of targeted diagnostic and treatment pathways. The project leverages advanced genome representation techniques to encode large-scale sequencing data into structured, computationally efficient formats. Machine learning models are developed to analyse genomic variants, detect patterns linked to specific pathologies and prioritise clinically relevant mutations. The system integrates genomic databases, clinical records and specialised bioinformatics pipelines, enabling automated variant interpretation and decision support within research and clinical environments. The initiative enhances the speed and reliability of genomic analysis, reducing the time required to reach a diagnosis and improving the precision of treatment planning. By supporting personalised medicine approaches, it contributes to better clinical outcomes for rare disease patients while increasing analytical scalability and fostering collaboration between research institutions and healthcare providers.

results.title: RPA in Södertälje - Automation of internal services
results.proposal: RPA in Södertälje - Automation of internal services. The Municipality of Södertälje faced inefficiencies and administrative bottlenecks in handling routine internal services such as absence reporting for hourly employees, termination of hourly contracts, travel service bookings and the issuance of employer certificates. These repetitive, high-volume processes required substantial manual effort from HR and administrative staff, leading to longer turnaround times, increased risk of human error and reduced capacity for strategic work. Stakeholders included municipal HR teams, front-line administrators, IT services and employees who depended on timely processing of their HR requests. The objective was to streamline internal operations, improve service reliability and free up staff time for higher-value tasks by automating rule-based administrative workflows. The municipality implemented Robotic Process Automation (RPA) technology to mimic human interactions with existing legacy and web-based administrative systems. Software robots were configured to execute predefined sequences of tasks — such as retrieving absence records, inputting employee data into HR systems, processing terminations, managing travel service requests and generating employer certificates — based on business rules and triggers. Integration was achieved without altering core systems, using automation scripts connected to the municipal IT landscape and orchestrated by an RPA management platform that schedules, monitors and logs robot activities. The introduction of RPA significantly enhanced operational efficiency by reducing processing times, minimising errors associated with manual data entry and ensuring consistent execution of administrative tasks. Employees saw faster service delivery for routine HR matters, while HR and administrative staff reclaimed work hours previously spent on repetitive tasks. Overall organisational productivity improved, internal service reliability increased and administrative costs were reduced, enabling a shift in focus toward strategic projects and citizen-centric services.

results.title: Development of the Electronic Flood Warning System
results.proposal: Development of the Electronic Flood Warning System. Existing monitoring mechanisms provide limited predictive capacity, making it difficult for crisis management services, water management authorities and municipalities to anticipate when and where flooding may occur, and with what intensity. The objective of the initiative is to strengthen early warning capabilities by delivering reliable, location-specific flood risk forecasts that support timely decision-making, resource allocation and public safety measures. The system integrates advanced data analytics and machine learning models to analyse correlations between historical and real-time meteorological and hydrological data. Supervised learning algorithms are trained on long-term precipitation records, river water level measurements and flood wave dynamics to model patterns leading to river overflow or flash floods. The solution combines sensor networks, weather radar data and hydrological stations with predictive models deployed within the existing warning infrastructure, enabling automated risk assessments and scenario simulations. The enhanced system improves forecasting accuracy and lead time, enabling earlier alerts and more targeted emergency responses. It strengthens operational reliability, reduces potential damage to property and infrastructure, and enhances public safety. Improved scalability and automation lower long-term monitoring costs while increasing resilience in the catchment area.

results.proposal: Gladsaxe Model - profiling families for early detection of vulnerable children. Municipal child welfare authorities aim to identify children at risk of neglect or social vulnerability at an early stage to enable preventive intervention. The Gladsaxe municipality developed a points-based profiling system designed to aggregate administrative indicators such as parental unemployment, mental health status, missed medical appointments and family structure changes. The objective was to support social workers in prioritising cases requiring attention and to improve early intervention outcomes. The model combined data from municipal databases and applied statistical scoring techniques to calculate risk levels. Outputs generated alerts for caseworkers to review flagged households. After review by data protection authorities, permission to continue was denied and the system was discontinued. Although subsequent research projects explored similar concepts in academic contexts, the original Gladsaxe model was terminated and never moved into full operational deployment.

results.title: European Criminal Records Information System – Third Country Nationals (ECRIS-TCN)
results.proposal: European Criminal Records Information System – Third Country Nationals (ECRIS-TCN). Cross-border crime within the European Union creates challenges for judicial authorities who must determine whether a third-country national has previous convictions in other Member States. Prior to ECRIS-TCN, criminal record checks for non-EU nationals were fragmented and time-consuming, potentially delaying judicial proceedings and undermining the principle of mutual recognition of judicial decisions. The system supports judges, prosecutors and competent authorities by enabling efficient identification of Member States holding criminal records of third-country nationals, thereby strengthening cooperation in the Schengen area and enhancing public security. The objective is to facilitate faster and more reliable exchange of criminal record information across borders. The system operates as a centralised EU-wide index managed by eu-LISA, containing identity data and biometric identifiers such as fingerprints. National authorities query the system to identify which Member State holds relevant criminal records, after which detailed information is exchanged through existing ECRIS channels. The platform is integrated within the EU interoperability framework for large-scale IT systems in justice and home affairs. The system has been implemented at EU level and is operational as part of the broader ECRIS infrastructure. It enhances judicial efficiency, reduces processing time for cross-border checks, strengthens legal certainty and improves the fight against transnational crime.

results.title: ALICEM - face recognition for administrative procedures
results.proposal: ALICEM - face recognition for administrative procedures. ALICEM – Face Recognition for Administrative Procedures is a French government initiative designed to enable citizens to complete administrative processes remotely by verifying their identity through a mobile application. Traditionally, many procedures require individuals to appear physically at public offices to confirm their identity, creating administrative burdens and limiting accessibility. The objective of ALICEM is to streamline digital public services by providing secure remote authentication linked to official identity documents. The system allows users to register their biometric facial characteristics in a smartphone application, which captures and verifies facial data against official identity credentials. Facial recognition algorithms compare live images with stored biometric references to confirm identity before granting access to online administrative services. The application integrates with government digital service platforms to enable secure transactions. Following public debate and media scrutiny in 2019, the government postponed the launch, and no official release date has been publicly confirmed. The initiative illustrates efforts to modernise e-government services while raising important considerations regarding biometric data protection, public trust and regulatory oversight.

results.title: Automated surveillance through audio processing
results.proposal: Automated surveillance through audio processing. Automated Surveillance through Audio Processing concerns a planned public safety initiative in Saint-Étienne, a city of approximately 175,000 inhabitants, aiming to strengthen urban security monitoring in a disadvantaged neighbourhood. Municipal authorities proposed deploying a network of microphones capable of detecting suspicious sounds and coordinating responses with existing CCTV infrastructure and an autonomous camera-equipped drone. The objective was to enable faster identification of potentially dangerous situations, such as gunshots, and support law enforcement intervention. The proposed system relied on audio signal processing models trained to classify predefined sound categories, including gunshots, drills, sprays and whistles. Detected events would trigger alerts and potentially activate linked visual surveillance systems. Integration with municipal control centres was intended to enable real-time monitoring and response coordination. However, the project was placed on hold after the French data protection authority determined that the deployment did not comply with applicable legal requirements. The case highlights both the potential of automated acoustic monitoring to enhance situational awareness and the critical importance of ensuring legal and data protection compliance in public sector technology deployments.

The project develops advanced image analysis models capable of extracting quantitative biomarkers from standard radiological examinations. These computational tools analyse imaging features alongside clinical data to estimate individual risk profiles for multiple chronic conditions. Outputs provide healthcare professionals with structured, interpretable risk parameters to guide preventive interventions and monitoring strategies. By repurposing routinely collected imaging data, the approach enhances efficiency without increasing patient burden. Anticipated impacts include earlier treatment initiation, reduced long-term morbidity and improved survivorship care planning. The project demonstrates how integrated imaging analytics can support holistic management of cancer survivors and strengthen preventive healthcare strategies.

Clinicians receive structured insights to support treatment decisions, while patients benefit from tailored guidance via a user-friendly interface. results.title: From A to B: Generalizing the mathematics of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to biological neural networks (BNNs)
results.proposal: From A to B: Generalizing the mathematics of artificial neural networks (ANNs) to biological neural networks (BNNs). Understanding why and when neural network models learn effectively remains a fundamental scientific challenge with implications for both artificial intelligence and neuroscience. This project seeks to develop advanced mathematical tools to analyse learning processes in Bayesian Neural Networks as statistical models and to explore parallels with biological neural systems. The research builds on a novel interpretation of local parameter updates in Bayesian Neural Networks as a derivative-free optimisation method, challenging the assumption that such approaches are inherently slow. Using nonparametric and high-dimensional statistical theory, the project investigates the convergence properties and generalisation performance of these models. By establishing rigorous mathematical guarantees, it aims to clarify the statistical mechanisms underlying efficient learning. Insights gained could inform the design of more data-efficient training methods and contribute to the development of neuromorphic computing architectures inspired by biological networks. The project has the potential to open new directions in mathematical statistics while strengthening the conceptual bridge between computational models and brain function.

results.title: Monitoring structure health of bridges with InSAR
results.proposal: Monitoring structure health of bridges with InSAR. Public authorities responsible for bridge management must ensure structural safety while optimising inspection budgets and minimising traffic disruption. Conventional monitoring relies on periodic visual inspections and targeted topographic surveys, which may fail to detect gradual deformations at an early stage. The project explores whether satellite-based interferometric analysis can support daily bridge management by identifying millimetre-level displacements and prioritising on-site investigations. Using Interferometric Synthetic Aperture Radar (InSAR), phase differences between successive radar satellite images are processed to calculate surface deformation over time. Different satellite data sources and processing techniques are assessed to determine their suitability for bridge monitoring, with algorithms designed to filter noise and automatically flag anomalous displacement patterns. The results are compared with ground-based measurements to validate accuracy and reliability. The approach aims to enable earlier detection of structural issues, more efficient allocation of inspection resources and reduced monitoring costs. By supporting risk-based maintenance planning and continuous remote observation, the solution enhances infrastructure safety, scalability of monitoring operations and evidence-based asset management.

results.title: AI for green roof management
results.proposal: AI for green roof management. The City of Amsterdam required reliable data on green roof coverage to support climate adaptation, biodiversity and urban planning policies, as previous mapping methods classified entire roofs as green when only partial vegetation was present, leading to significant overestimation and unreliable statistics. Municipal authorities, environmental planners and property owners needed precise measurements of actual vegetated surface across the city. To address this, a proof of concept was developed using Very High Resolution satellite imagery with a spatial resolution of approximately 30 cm, enabling detailed observation of roof composition. Geospatial image analysis techniques were applied to classify pixels according to material type and vegetation cover, allowing roof areas to be quantified accurately at pixel level. The processed data were integrated into municipal geographic information systems to update spatial datasets and support policy analysis. The approach substantially improves data granularity and reliability compared with previous estimates, enabling better targeting of incentives, monitoring of environmental performance and evidence-based investment in green infrastructure, while offering a scalable method for continuous urban monitoring.

The system combines sensor-based monitoring of physical and environmental parameters—such as vibration, humidity, and temperature—with advanced data-processing tools to analyse trends and detect early warning signals. Sensor data is continuously collected from monitored sites and processed through analytical models that identify deviations from normal behaviour. Alerts are generated when risk thresholds are exceeded, supporting targeted inspections and maintenance planning. The architecture is designed to integrate monitoring data with heritage management workflows and expert assessments. Public sources describe SIAP as a research-driven pilot demonstrated in collaboration between regional authorities and academic partners. While no evidence of nationwide deployment has been reported, the project has shown potential to enhance heritage protection, reduce emergency interventions, and support more sustainable conservation strategies through continuous, data-informed monitoring.

Stakeholders include ERSAR, regulated utilities, policy analysts, and national statistical bodies. The technological approach focuses on advanced data-processing pipelines that ingest regulatory submissions, operational metrics, and historical datasets. Statistical validation techniques and pattern-recognition models are applied to detect anomalies, inconsistencies, and outliers, supporting automated pre-validation before human review. The methodologies are designed to integrate with existing regulatory information systems and reporting workflows. As a methodological programme rather than a single tool, the initiative emphasises repeatability, auditability, and governance. While no full production system has been publicly announced, the work has contributed to more robust regulatory data practices, reduced manual effort, and improved confidence in market oversight, laying the groundwork for scalable, data-driven regulation.

The tool does not replace medical judgement but supports decision-making by highlighting cases requiring attention. Expected impacts include improved efficiency of medical checks, reduced unnecessary inspections, better targeting of controls and more consistent handling of sickness benefit claims, while maintaining transparency and proportionality.

results.title: ETIAS (EU Travel Information and Authorisation System)
results.proposal: ETIAS (EU Travel Information and Authorisation System). The Schengen Area faces the challenge of facilitating legitimate travel while managing security, migration, and public health risks associated with visa-exempt travellers. ETIAS was designed to address this by introducing a pre-travel authorisation requirement for non-EU nationals who do not need a visa to enter Schengen States. Stakeholders include EU border authorities, national security agencies, travellers, and the EU Agency eu-LISA, which is responsible for system development and operation. The objective is to strengthen external border management while reducing refusals at border crossings and improving traveller predictability. ETIAS operates as a centralised IT system that collects traveller application data and automatically checks it against multiple EU information systems, including security, migration, and health-related databases. Risk rules and screening criteria are applied to identify applications requiring further manual assessment by national authorities. Most applications are expected to be processed within minutes, while a minority may take up to 30 days. Although initially planned for earlier deployment, ETIAS has been postponed and is now expected to become operational in 2026, with transitional measures foreseen. Once active, ETIAS is expected to streamline border checks, enhance security cooperation, and improve the overall efficiency and reliability of Schengen border management.

results.proposal: Machine vision AI solution for better traffic management in Tallinn. results.title: Face recognition tool for the Slovenian police
results.proposal: Face recognition tool for the Slovenian police. The Slovenian police began using facial comparison software as early as 2014 to support criminal investigations involving images from open sources such as social media and online platforms. The tool, known as Face Trace, was used to assist investigators in identifying suspects by comparing facial features across image datasets. However, for several years the use of this technology lacked a clear legal basis and was only formally regulated in 2019, five years after its initial deployment. The system is intended to generate investigative leads rather than definitive identifications, with results requiring verification through traditional investigative methods. Following legal scrutiny and public debate, the use of facial recognition by the Slovenian police has since been significantly constrained, with stricter requirements for authorisation, documentation and oversight. This case has become emblematic of broader European concerns regarding the lawful, transparent and proportionate use of biometric technologies in policing.

results.title: VicomTTS - Quality synthetic voices
results.proposal: VicomTTS - Quality synthetic voices. VicomTTS was developed to address the limited availability of high-quality digital services in the Basque language, which can hinder its everyday use in public, educational and personal contexts. The service provides citizens, learners and institutions with a reliable tool for converting written Basque text into clear, natural-sounding speech, supporting linguistic inclusion and accessibility. Built as a digital public service, VicomTTS uses neural speech synthesis models implemented in Python and executed via the PyTorch framework, trained on Basque-language datasets to ensure accurate pronunciation and intelligible prosody. The system is deployed as an online service designed for low-latency performance and high reliability. While initial uptake was lower than anticipated, the service has steadily gained popularity and is now processing approximately 5,000 requests per day. Performance metrics indicate that around 50% of requests are handled in under one second, with a reported success rate of 99.7%. VicomTTS demonstrates how advanced speech technologies can contribute to the preservation and digital normalisation of minority languages while delivering a scalable and dependable public-facing service.

results.title: RADAR-rechts | Assessing the risk of violence by far-right extremists
results.proposal: RADAR-rechts | Assessing the risk of violence by far-right extremists. Following a series of fatal right-wing extremist attacks in Germany in 2019 and 2020, federal and state law enforcement authorities faced increasing pressure to strengthen the prevention of politically motivated violent crime. To support a more systematic and person-centred approach, the Federal Criminal Police Office (BKA) developed RADAR-rechts, a structured risk assessment instrument designed to prioritise individuals known from the right-wing extremist spectrum who may pose an acute threat of committing life-threatening violence. The tool supports police forces nationwide by enabling consistent prioritisation of so-called dangerous and relevant persons and identifying cases requiring more detailed individual risk analysis. Its introduction represents a significant step towards standardised, evidence-informed approaches in the person-oriented prevention of far-right extremist violence.

results.proposal: Signalen - AI Categorisation of Public Space Reports. results.title: Automated border control via Easypass Registered Traveler Program - biometric face recognition system
results.proposal: Automated border control via Easypass Registered Traveler Program - biometric face recognition system. International airport border control in Germany faced growing passenger volumes requiring faster processing whilst maintaining security standards and compliance with Schengen external border regulations. The Federal Police implemented EasyPASS, an automated border control system using biometric facial recognition developed by Bundesdruckerei, secunet, and Cognitec to verify travellers' identities against their e-passport chip photos. The system is deployed at Frankfurt, Munich, Hamburg, Hannover, Düsseldorf, Stuttgart, Berlin Brandenburg, and Cologne/Bonn airports, available to EU/EEA citizens aged 12+ and registered third-country nationals from the USA, Hong Kong, South Korea, Taiwan, and the UK. Travellers place their e-passport on the document reader, then proceed through gates where cameras capture facial images for 1:1 comparison against stored biometric data, with information also checked against Schengen databases. Data is stored for 48 hours (extendable to 30 days for police investigations), and the system strictly limits facial recognition to identity verification purposes under the Passport Act.

results.title: EnMAP - Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program
results.proposal: EnMAP - Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program. Traditional satellite imagery captures only a limited portion of the electromagnetic spectrum, restricting scientists' ability to detect subtle environmental changes in vegetation health, water quality, soil composition, and mineral deposits essential for climate monitoring and resource management. EnMAP (Environmental Mapping and Analysis Program) is Germany's first hyperspectral satellite mission, launched in April 2022 aboard a SpaceX Falcon 9. The satellite carries a dual-spectrometer instrument capturing 230 spectral bands from 420 to 2450 nanometres at 30-metre ground resolution, enabling detection of biochemical and geochemical signatures invisible to conventional sensors. Operating in sun-synchronous orbit at 653 kilometres altitude, EnMAP records up to 5,000 kilometres of imagery daily with 4-day revisit capability. The German Research Centre for Geosciences (GFZ) leads scientific coordination whilst DLR manages operations. In 2024, the SpectralEarth dataset was released, comprising 538,974 image patches for training AI foundation models in hyperspectral analysis. EnMAP provides unprecedented environmental monitoring capability for agriculture, forestry, water management, and geology applications. The mission supports Copernicus services and contributes to climate protection initiatives by enabling precise characterisation of ecosystem changes. Data is freely available to the global scientific community through DLR's ground segment.

If it is determined with a certain probability that the wrong documents may have been uploaded, the application portal issues a warning message.

results.proposal: X-PIDER - an electonic investigative tool in the field of e-commerce used by the German tax authorities. Traditional audit methods cannot efficiently monitor the vast volume of internet commercial activity, creating opportunities for tax evasion through e-commerce platforms and social media. The German Federal Central Tax Office (Bundeszentralamt für Steuern) deployed X-PIDER, an AI-powered web crawling and scraping system to automatically identify taxable business activity online. X-PIDER can identify internet pages suggesting business transactions and collects taxpayer-related data for cross-referencing with tax records. The system can be deployed anywhere on the internet and autonomously navigates web content to build comprehensive profiles of online commercial presence. X-PIDER supports the regional tax authorities by providing centralised intelligence on potential tax non-compliance. The system complements other AI initiatives in German tax administration including the Steuerchatbot virtual assistant (extended nationally and to English and French in 2024), nudging tools that adapt communication based on taxpayer risk profiles, and automated verification systems for processing tax returns. These tools collectively strengthen enforcement whilst reducing manual investigative workload.

When anomalies are detected, automated alerts trigger specialist review to determine whether observed increases represent genuine outbreaks requiring public health response. The platform has operated since 2015, providing early warning capabilities that complement traditional epidemiological surveillance methods and supporting Germany's capacity to detect and respond to infectious disease threats.

results.title: The AI algorithm that blew up Italy’s school system
results.proposal: The AI algorithm that blew up Italy’s school system. Italy's education system faced the annual challenge of assigning approximately 100,000 teachers to schools across diverse regions, a complex optimization problem that had historically relied on manual processes prone to errors and delays. The Ministry of Education implemented an algorithmic system to automatically assign teachers to schools based on preferences, qualifications, and regional needs, processing massive datasets to generate placements within compressed timeframes. However, the 2020 deployment generated significant controversy when thousands of teachers received assignments to schools far from their preferences or in regions they had not selected, with some relocated hundreds of kilometres from their homes. The algorithm's logic and decision criteria remained opaque, preventing affected teachers from understanding or effectively challenging their placements. The case became a prominent example in debates about algorithmic accountability in public administration, highlighting tensions between efficiency gains and transparency requirements in automated government decision-making.

results.proposal: Reference Index Recherche Onderzoeken en Subjecten - Detection of unusual transactions. Stakeholders include financial institutions, law enforcement bodies, and investigative authorities. The objective is to support criminal investigations by identifying whether reported unusual transactions are linked to existing police investigations. Transaction data flagged by reporting entities is compared through a partly automated process with entries in the VROS. The system does not autonomously label transactions as criminal but acts as an investigative signal within a broader legal process. VROS is formally embedded in Dutch legislation and remains operational as part of the national framework for combating financial crime. Its use has improved investigative efficiency by enabling faster cross-referencing of financial intelligence, reducing manual searches, and supporting coordinated law enforcement action, while maintaining procedural safeguards and human oversight.

results.proposal: Leveraging Large Language Models for Topic Classification in the Domain of Public Affair. Public affairs documents shape regulation, compliance and democratic oversight, yet their volume and complexity make systematic analysis challenging for both public institutions and private organisations. This research pilot investigates how large language models can support the classification of public affairs texts. Stakeholders include policymakers, regulatory analysts, companies and researchers. The objective is to improve transparency and accessibility by enabling structured analysis of large document collections. A dataset of over 33,000 public affairs documents, comprising more than 22.5 million tokens, was compiled using automated collection techniques. results.title: Generative Ai for German Public Administration
results.proposal: Generative Ai for German Public Administration. Federal, state and municipal authorities have begun piloting generative language technologies to support administrative tasks. Stakeholders include federal ministries, regional governments, municipalities and civil servants. The objective is to improve service quality and productivity while maintaining data protection, legal certainty and public trust. These pilots, often developed with startup Aleph Alpha, focus on tasks such as summarising documents, drafting internal notes, supporting correspondence and assisting research. Systems are deployed in controlled environments, typically hosted within Germany to meet sovereignty requirements. Outputs are reviewed by civil servants, and usage policies define acceptable applications. Early results show time savings in text-heavy processes, improved consistency in communication and better support for staff handling complex information. The pilots also surface organisational and skills-related requirements, informing broader digital transformation strategies. While not yet operational at scale, the initiatives provide valuable insights into how generative technologies can responsibly support public administration without automating decision-making or compromising accountability.

results.title: Usage of Generative Ai in Spain justice
results.proposal: Usage of Generative Ai in Spain justice. Judicial systems face growing workloads, complex legal texts and increasing expectations for timely communication with citizens. In Spain, pilot initiatives have explored how generative language technologies can support judicial professionals without compromising legal safeguards. Stakeholders include courts, judicial staff, justice ministries and citizens seeking accessible legal information. The objective is to improve internal efficiency and external communication while maintaining judicial independence and accountability. The pilots, discussed within the framework of the European Commission for the Efficiency of Justice (CEPEJ), focus on two main applications: assisting communication with citizens on legal procedures and summarising lengthy judicial documents. Language models are applied to structured legal texts and official documentation, with strict human oversight and defined usage boundaries. Systems are deployed as decision-support tools rather than automated decision-makers, ensuring that judges and clerks remain fully responsible for outcomes. Early findings indicate improved drafting speed, clearer public-facing explanations and reduced administrative burden for routine tasks. At the same time, limitations related to accuracy, bias and explainability are explicitly acknowledged. The pilots contribute to European best practices by clarifying where generative tools add value in justice systems and where legal or ethical constraints require careful restriction.

results.title: PORO an LLM for Finland
results.proposal: PORO an LLM for Finland. European public institutions, researchers and companies increasingly rely on language technologies, yet most large language models are developed outside Europe and inadequately support smaller European languages. The PORO initiative was launched to strengthen European digital sovereignty by providing open, high-quality language models trained on European data. Led by startup SiloGen, in collaboration with the University of Turku and HPLT, the project aims to democratise access to advanced language models while ensuring alignment with European values, research openness and linguistic diversity. The first PORO model, a 34-billion-parameter system, focuses on English, Finnish and programming code, with plans to expand coverage to all official European languages. The models are trained using large multilingual datasets and high-performance computing resources from the LUMI supercomputer, combined with a dedicated software stack optimised for large-scale training. Open-source checkpoints enable reuse, fine-tuning and transparent evaluation by public and private actors. The initiative delivers strategic benefits by reducing dependency on non-European providers, improving language coverage for public services and research, and enabling innovation across sectors. PORO establishes a scalable foundation for sovereign European language infrastructure.

results.title: AI for Emergency information system
results.proposal: AI for Emergency information system. Emergency departments face increasing pressure due to high patient volumes, time-critical decision-making, and limited medical staff, raising the risk of delayed or missed diagnoses. This project proposal aimed to explore a new emergency information system to support faster and more accurate triage and intervention. Stakeholders included hospitals, emergency responders, healthcare professionals, and regional authorities. The objective was to improve the overall rescue process by enhancing early assessment of patients’ conditions before or during emergency intake. The proposed system would analyse facial expressions and vocal characteristics captured during emergency interactions, combining these signals with contextual information to identify potential indicators of distress or medical urgency. Conceptually, the system would integrate real-time data capture with analytical models and clinical workflows, providing decision-support signals to medical staff rather than automated diagnoses. Despite its inclusion in Interreg Europe’s project ideas, the initiative remained at the exploratory and proposal stage, with no evidence of operational deployment. Nonetheless, it highlighted emerging directions in emergency care innovation and contributed to policy-level discussions on the responsible use of advanced analytics in high-risk healthcare settings.

results.title: Algorithmic Transparency Standard
results.proposal: Algorithmic Transparency Standard. Public administrations increasingly rely on algorithmic systems, creating a growing need for transparency, accountability and public understanding. Cities lacked a shared, practical framework for explaining how such systems are used, for what purpose, and with what safeguards. The Algorithmic Transparency Standard was developed to address this gap by providing a common structure for documenting algorithmic use across local governments. The initiative involves municipalities, civic technology organisations and researchers, with the objective of enabling meaningful transparency for citizens while supporting internal governance. The standard defines a shared set of information categories, such as system purpose, data sources, decision impacts, oversight mechanisms and risks. These are published in open, machine-readable formats (CSV and Excel), allowing comparison across systems and jurisdictions. The standard can be integrated into existing registers or disclosure portals without requiring new technical infrastructure. Its impact lies in improved comparability, easier public scrutiny and stronger internal documentation practices. Cities using the standard benefit from clearer governance processes and reduced duplication of effort, while citizens gain accessible insight into algorithmic decision-making. The initiative supports trust, accountability and responsible digital transformation in public administration.

results.title: Pensioners prove they are alive via face or voice recognition
results.proposal: Pensioners prove they are alive via face or voice recognition. Each year, thousands of Portuguese pensioners living abroad must prove they are alive to continue receiving benefits, traditionally requiring in-person visits to consulates or paper-based processes. This creates administrative burdens for both pensioners and public authorities, particularly for elderly individuals with mobility constraints. Caixa Geral de Aposentações launched a pilot to simplify this process using remote identity verification, initially in Macau. Stakeholders include pensioners abroad, welfare administrators and consular services. The objective was to reduce costs, improve convenience and maintain trust in pension disbursement. The system allows pensioners to submit proof of life remotely using biometric verification, based on facial or voice recognition through a digital interface. Captured biometric samples are matched against previously registered references to confirm identity, after which confirmation is transmitted securely to the pension authority. The pilot showed clear efficiency gains and was positively received by digitally confident users. However, feedback also highlighted usability challenges for some elderly participants unfamiliar with digital tools. The project demonstrated both the administrative benefits of remote verification and the need for inclusive design and alternative channels.

results.title: BorderSens - Border detection of illicit drugs and precursors by highly accurate electrosensors
results.proposal: BorderSens - Border detection of illicit drugs and precursors by highly accurate electrosensors. Customs and border authorities require fast, reliable tools to detect illicit drugs, precursors and cutting agents during inspections, often under time pressure and with limited laboratory access. Existing methods can be slow, costly or prone to false positives, creating operational inefficiencies. The EU-funded BorderSens project aimed to address this challenge by developing a portable, low-cost and user-friendly device for on-site drug detection. Stakeholders included border guards, customs officers, forensic experts and research institutions. The objective was to enable accurate identification of a wide range of substances within seconds, supporting frontline decision-making. The solution combined electrochemical sensing with selective nano-Molecularly Imprinted Polymers (nanoMIPs) and advanced nanomaterials to capture and enrich chemical fingerprints. These signals were processed through analytical models to distinguish drugs, precursors and adulterants with high precision. The prototype targeted results within 45 seconds, with reduced rates of false positives and negatives. The project demonstrated strong potential for improving border inspection efficiency, lowering operational costs and enhancing reliability compared to traditional field tests, while supporting safer and more effective enforcement activities.

results.title: BOM - Biometrics on the Move
results.proposal: BOM - Biometrics on the Move. European border authorities face constant pressure to improve passenger flow efficiency while maintaining high security standards at external borders. Long queues, manual document checks and fragmented procedures can negatively affect both traveller experience and border operations. To explore alternatives, Frontex, together with the Portuguese Immigration and Border Service and Lisbon Airport Authority (ANA), launched the voluntary “Biometrics on the Move” (BOM) pilot at Humberto Delgado International Airport in October 2019. The objective was to test whether travellers could cross borders more smoothly without repeatedly presenting physical documents, while still complying with border control requirements. The pilot relied on biometric enrolment of participating passengers, who consented to the use of their facial image and fingerprints. These biometric identifiers were captured once and then used at subsequent checkpoints, where automated gates matched live biometric scans against enrolled templates. The system integrated with existing border control infrastructure and operated alongside traditional procedures. The pilot demonstrated the technical feasibility of near-seamless border crossing, significantly reducing interaction time at checkpoints and improving passenger experience. While limited in scope and duration, BOM provided valuable insights into operational performance, user acceptance and data protection considerations, informing future EU-level discussions on biometric border management.
