results.title: Swedish police used face recognition until 2019 at the Skavsta airport
results.proposal: Swedish police used face recognition until 2019 at the Skavsta airport. As part of Operation Rimfrost, aimed at combating organised crime, the Swedish Police tested facial recognition tools to identify suspects across images from crime scenes and CCTV footage. The objective was to enhance investigative capabilities by quickly identifying recurring individuals across large image datasets. Stakeholders included law enforcement units, oversight authorities and the public. The police used the Clearview AI application during pilot deployments, including at Skavsta Airport. The system compared images against a large external database to suggest potential matches for investigative follow-up. In 2021, the Swedish Authority for Privacy Protection ruled that the use of the system violated the Swedish Criminal Data Act, citing unlawful processing of personal data. As a result, the pilot was terminated and all personal data were required to be deleted. The case had significant impact by clarifying legal boundaries for biometric technologies, reinforcing data protection obligations and influencing future governance of digital tools in law enforcement.

results.title: DELIA | Algorithm to predict location and perpetrator of crime
results.proposal: DELIA | Algorithm to predict location and perpetrator of crime. Law enforcement agencies in Milan sought more effective ways to prevent and investigate serial crimes, particularly commercial and bank robberies, which had significant social and economic impacts. Traditional policing methods struggled to identify patterns across large volumes of crime data over time. The City of Milan’s Questura began long-term field trials of predictive crime analysis tools developed by startup KeyCrime, with the objective of supporting investigative work and targeted prevention strategies. Stakeholders included police analysts, operational units, judicial authorities and academic evaluators. The solution analysed historical crime records, spatial and temporal patterns, and offence characteristics to identify links between incidents and likely future scenarios. Over successive trial phases, the system evolved into the DELIA platform, improving usability, analytical performance and pattern-linking capabilities. Results were reviewed by the Italian Ministry of Justice and independently evaluated by the University of Essex to ensure objectivity. The impact was significant: between 2008 and 2019, commercial robberies in Milan decreased by around 58%, while bank robberies in the wider province fell by approximately 89% between 2009 and 2019. The project demonstrated strong operational value in crime prevention and investigation.

results.title: Intelligent Wellness Platform Experiment
results.proposal: Intelligent Wellness Platform Experiment. The City of Espoo sought to improve preventive social, healthcare and education services by better understanding citizens’ needs before problems escalated into costly or irreversible social exclusion. Traditional service planning relied on siloed data and reactive interventions, limiting the city’s ability to act early and in a targeted way. In collaboration with Tieto (now Tietoevry), Espoo launched an experiment to test whether large-scale data analysis could support more timely, citizen-centric welfare services. Stakeholders included municipal social and healthcare departments, education services, policymakers and the city’s residents. The objective was to assess whether predictive insights could inform service planning and resource allocation while respecting strict data protection requirements. The solution integrated longitudinal data from social services, healthcare and education covering the years 2002–2016, representing around 520,000 residents and over 37 million service interactions. Data were anonymised at source, encrypted in transit and processed in a secure analytical environment. Predictive models were used to identify risk patterns associated with social exclusion and future service needs, with results fed into planning processes rather than individual-level decisions. The experiment demonstrated that data-driven insights could support earlier interventions, more efficient service planning and new preventive service pathways. Qualitatively, it showed strong potential for improving wellbeing outcomes while reducing long-term social and healthcare costs.

results.title: Nantes Solidarity Transport Pricing
results.proposal: Nantes Solidarity Transport Pricing. Public transport affordability is crucial for social inclusion, yet fixed-price ticketing can exclude low-income residents from mobility services essential for employment, healthcare access, and social participation. Nantes Métropole implemented an algorithmic system for solidarity transport pricing (Tarification Solidaire Transports) on its Naolib public transport network. The algorithm determines eligibility for free travel or discounts up to 50% on unlimited annual passes based on household income and family composition. All households with a family quotient of 900 or below qualify for solidarity pricing. Users apply at their local town hall, where agents collect supporting documents and enter information into Deltas, software developed by Nantes Métropole. The algorithm processes data in real time, immediately notifying applicants of their entitlement level. Benefits apply to all household members regardless of age. Since May 2023, the eligibility threshold was raised from 600 to 900 family quotient, significantly expanding coverage. The solidarity pricing programme extends beyond metropolitan residents to include commuters from surrounding areas who travel within Nantes Métropole. This ensures transport affordability for the most vulnerable populations whilst supporting labour market access and social cohesion across the metropolitan region.

results.title: Nantes Social Water Pricing
results.proposal: Nantes Social Water Pricing. Access to affordable water is a fundamental right, yet low-income households often struggle with utility costs. Traditional means-tested assistance programmes require complex application processes and frequently miss eligible beneficiaries who are unaware of available support. Nantes Métropole developed an open-source algorithm to determine eligibility for its social water tariff (Tarification Solidaire de l'Eau), guaranteeing that no household spends more than 3% of income on water for reasonable consumption of 30 cubic metres per person annually. The algorithm calculates eligibility based on household income and family composition using data from the Caisse d'Allocations Familiales (CAF). For CAF beneficiaries with family quotient below the threshold, assistance is granted automatically. Other residents can apply at their town hall, where agents enter information into Deltas software developed in-house by Nantes Métropole. The algorithm processes data in real time, providing immediate eligibility determination. The source code is published under the CeCILL-B open-source licence. In 2024, 5,866 households benefited from the social water tariff, receiving €407,153 in total assistance. Since January 2025, reformed Agence de l'Eau charges have been integrated into the pricing structure. The open-source approach supports transparency in public decision-making and enables other municipalities to adapt the algorithm for their own social pricing programmes.

results.title: AI to support decision-making processes in social services
results.proposal: AI to support decision-making processes in social services. The municipal social services deal with an average of 50,000 initial visits every year ranging through a variety of issues (from financial or addiction problems to gender-based violence) and are handled by a team of over 700 professionals. An algorithm provides the staff with digital support in the decision-making process. Having been trained with a corpus of 300,000 interviews, it suggests the appropriate resources for each case. results.title: AI Beach Capacity Monitoring
results.proposal: AI Beach Capacity Monitoring. The City Council has contracted the services of the company DatActions to implement the DasEyes application, whose function is to sectorize the beaches in multiple virtual areas in order to detect the number of people in each sector. On weekends, when there is more confluence and traffic on the beach, municipal agents are provided with tools to monitor capacity; these agents patrol to make sure there are no problems and ensure order in the areas. In addition, to make it easier for them, Artificial Intelligence methods make it possible to predict when the beaches will be filled. Depending on the data, the agents open and close the different sections to the public in such a way that there will always be a safe capacity in all areas.

results.title: Intelligent layout of areas for optimal school districts design
results.proposal: Intelligent layout of areas for optimal school districts design. School districts should be designed in such a way that schools have as even a capacity as possible and the distances to school for children are short. At the same time, it is important to achieve a social mix among the students. In order to achieve these goals, school office employees in the Berlin district of Tempelhof-Schoeneberg have invested a lot of time. Streets had to be walked through one by one, information was recorded in Excel spreadsheets. This work is now done by an algorithm that automatically outputs a first draft of the cut based on the available data from the State Statistical Office.

results.title: Pilot project to support the future development of photos with AI
results.proposal: Pilot project to support the future development of photos with AI. Municipal archives often hold vast photographic collections that are difficult to index and search due to limited metadata and manual cataloguing processes. The Heilbronn City Archive launched this pilot to improve access to its digital photo collections and enrich historical documentation. Stakeholders include archivists, researchers, local historians and the general public. The objective is to increase indexing depth and accelerate the availability of detailed information about archived images. The pilot trains image analysis systems to recognise approximately 1,500 individuals and around 200 distinctive buildings using existing labelled photographs. The resulting metadata is integrated into the HEUSS online archive database, enabling faster and more detailed tagging of images. The impact includes significantly reduced manual indexing effort, richer search functionality and improved public access to cultural heritage materials. Qualitatively, the project enhances the long-term value of archival assets and demonstrates scalable approaches to digital heritage management.

results.title: Data-driven water infrastructure maintenance in Burgas
results.proposal: Data-driven water infrastructure maintenance in Burgas. Ageing water infrastructure causes significant water losses, threatening sustainability, service reliability, and public resources. In some regions, leakage rates reach critical levels, requiring proactive detection and maintenance strategies. The Burgas municipality addresses this challenge by modernising water network monitoring to reduce losses and optimise asset management. Stakeholders include municipal utilities, maintenance operators, and residents. The objective is to detect leaks early, improve water supply reliability, and reduce long-term operational costs. The solution deploys vibration sensors along water pipes to continuously monitor acoustic patterns associated with leaks. Large volumes of sensor data are analysed using predictive models that distinguish normal operation from leak signatures in real time. Continuous automated monitoring enables faster detection than manual inspection methods. The project delivers reduced water losses, improved maintenance planning, and more efficient use of public funds. It strengthens resilience of water infrastructure, enhances service continuity, and supports sustainable water management, offering a replicable model for municipalities facing similar challenges across Europe.

results.title: Public AI Challenge - Hub Innovazione Trentino - Overtourism detection
results.proposal: Public AI Challenge - Hub Innovazione Trentino - Overtourism detection. Overtourism places pressure on environmentally sensitive areas, leading to congestion, ecological damage, and reduced quality of life for residents and visitors. The Province of Trento sought tools to anticipate tourism peaks and manage mobility proactively. This use case addresses the need for data-driven forecasting to support sustainable tourism management. Stakeholders include regional authorities, transport planners, local communities, and visitors. The objective is to detect and predict overcrowding in specific areas and support timely mitigation measures. The solution integrates heterogeneous datasets, including road traffic data, mobile network activity, and weather information, to estimate visitor volumes and characterise tourism patterns. Data preparation and harmonisation enable effective analysis, while predictive models identify days and locations at high risk of overtourism. The impact includes improved forecasting accuracy, better traffic management decisions, and reduced environmental pressure on sensitive areas. The initiative supports evidence-based tourism governance and demonstrates how advanced analytics can help balance economic activity with environmental protection and quality of life.

results.title: Autonomous Road Inspection for Bizkaia Regional Council
results.proposal: Autonomous Road Inspection for Bizkaia Regional Council. Maintaining road safety requires frequent inspection of infrastructure such as signs, markings, barriers, and work zones, yet manual inspections are costly, infrequent, and expose personnel to risk. The Bizkaia Regional Council faced the challenge of improving road asset monitoring while increasing coverage and responsiveness. The Autonomous Road Inspector addresses this need by enabling continuous, automated assessment of road conditions. Stakeholders include regional authorities, infrastructure operators, and road users. The objective is to enhance safety, optimise maintenance, and support proactive road management. The solution deploys vehicle-mounted sensing systems that capture visual and environmental data during normal traffic operations. Automated analysis identifies damaged or missing signs, degraded markings, unsafe barriers, construction zone conditions, and hazards such as slippery surfaces. Predictive functions support early detection of deterioration and risk. The impact includes more frequent inspections, reduced operational costs, improved worker safety, and faster response to hazards. The pilot demonstrates how automated monitoring can modernise road management, improve public safety, and deliver scalable benefits for regional infrastructure authorities.

results.title: Z-Inspection – Assessment for Responsible Artificial Intelligence
results.proposal: Z-Inspection – Assessment for Responsible Artificial Intelligence. Governments adopting automated systems face complex ethical, legal, and social considerations that cannot be addressed through technical evaluation alone. The Z-Inspection pilot in the Province of Fryslân addresses the need for holistic assessment methods that support responsible adoption across public administrations. Stakeholders include policymakers, civil servants, citizens, and interdisciplinary experts. The objective is to identify risks, ethical dilemmas, and governance gaps early in the lifecycle of automated systems and to build institutional capacity for responsible use. The solution applies the Z-Inspection methodology, bringing together experts from multiple disciplines to analyse the purpose, design, data use, and societal impact of a concrete system. Structured discussions explore conflicts of interest, accountability, and alignment with public values. The outcomes are documented as lessons learned and shared across government. The impact includes improved understanding of responsible deployment practices, increased digital awareness, and a practical framework for assessing future systems. The pilot supports more confident, transparent, and trustworthy use of advanced technologies in the public sector.

The solution integrates a network of webcams, sensors, and data sources into a unified platform that enables real-time monitoring and analysis of urban environments. Advanced analytics support the detection of suspicious patterns and events, while shared dashboards improve coordination between operational units. The pilot nature of the project allows solutions to be tested and refined before replication in other cities. The impact includes improved detection and prevention of criminal activity, more efficient investigations, and strengthened trust in public safety services. ME@GIS demonstrates how integrated digital infrastructures can enhance urban resilience and deliver measurable public security benefits.

results.title: FreshRegio – making the quality of fruit and vegetables measurable
results.proposal: FreshRegio – making the quality of fruit and vegetables measurable. Quality assessment of fruit and vegetables is critical for regional agriculture and efficient food supply chains, yet traditional inspection methods are often subjective, labour-intensive, and limited in predictive power. FreshRegio addresses this challenge by enabling objective, data-driven evaluation of product quality and shelf life. Stakeholders include farmers, distributors, retailers, and consumers. The objective is to strengthen regional food systems by improving transparency and reducing waste. The solution combines near-infrared sensor technology with analytical models to assess internal quality attributes of produce non-destructively. Measurements are processed to predict freshness and remaining shelf life, supporting informed decisions along the supply chain. The system simplifies quality control processes and enables consistent evaluation across batches. The impact includes reduced food waste, improved product differentiation, and stronger trust between producers and buyers. FreshRegio contributes to more sustainable food systems by aligning quality measurement with regional agricultural value creation.

results.title: DynAWI - Predict extreme weather situations reliably and region-specific
results.proposal: DynAWI - Predict extreme weather situations reliably and region-specific. Extreme weather events increasingly threaten agricultural productivity, yet timely and region-specific assessment tools are often lacking. Farmers and public authorities need reliable indicators to anticipate yield impacts and support risk management decisions. DynAWI addresses this need by developing a process chain for monitoring and analysing extreme weather conditions in agriculture. Stakeholders include agricultural agencies, researchers, and private sector users of environmental data. The objective is to provide scalable, regionally differentiated indicators that link weather extremes to crop yield outcomes. The solution integrates geospatial datasets within a scalable data infrastructure and applies analytical models to derive dynamic agricultural weather indicators. These indicators capture the intensity, duration, and spatial extent of extreme conditions relevant to crop development. Outputs are made available through standardised interfaces for integration into national and European data spaces. The project improves early warning capabilities, supports impact assessment, and enhances planning under climate uncertainty. DynAWI contributes to more resilient agricultural systems and informed adaptation strategies in the face of climate change.

results.title: BoniKI - plant-specific assessment by autonomous systems
results.proposal: BoniKI - plant-specific assessment by autonomous systems. Assessing plant health, growth, and pest infestation is essential for sustainable agriculture, yet manual inspection is labour-intensive, costly, and dependent on expert judgement. Sampling-based methods provide limited resolution and may miss early signs of stress or disease. The BoniKI project addresses this challenge by enabling automated, plant-level assessment at scale. Stakeholders include farmers, agronomists, and agricultural service providers. The objective is to increase efficiency, transparency, and sustainability in crop monitoring and decision-making. The solution uses unmanned aerial systems to capture high-resolution imagery of agricultural fields. Data processing pipelines separate crops from weeds and background elements, followed by automated assessment of plant condition using trained analytical models. The system derives relevant scoring parameters and generates actionable insights for field management. The project aims to deliver an integrated, user-friendly solution for routine agricultural use. The impact includes reduced monitoring costs, earlier detection of stress or infestation, and more targeted interventions. BoniKI supports precision agriculture and contributes to more resource-efficient and resilient farming practices.

results.proposal: AI-TEST-FIELD – Semantic Environment Perception for Intelligent Sensor Systems. Current sensor systems often struggle to deliver consistent and certifiable outputs under varying conditions, limiting deployment in safety-critical contexts. AI-TEST-FIELD addresses this challenge by developing the foundations for robust, trustworthy sensor systems. Stakeholders include industrial developers, certification bodies, and operators of automated systems. The objective is to enable sensor technologies that provide stable and interpretable guidance for action across diverse environmental scenarios. The solution focuses on semantic environment perception using learning-based approaches that fuse data from multiple sensor modalities. Models are trained and tested in controlled environments to ensure robustness and consistency of outputs. Emphasis is placed on reproducibility, validation, and suitability for certification. The project delivers reference architectures, datasets, and testing methodologies. The impact includes increased reliability of intelligent sensor systems, improved safety assurance, and accelerated industrial adoption. AI-TEST-FIELD supports the deployment of trustworthy perception technologies in domains such as automated transport and industrial automation.

results.proposal: Data4UrbanMobility - Development of application-driven tools for mobility information. Cities often lack tools that translate large volumes of heterogeneous mobility data into actionable insights for planning and operations. Data4UrbanMobility addresses this gap by developing application-driven tools that support data-informed mobility decisions. results.title: FAKE-ID - Video analysis using AI to detect false and manipulated identities
results.proposal: FAKE-ID - Video analysis using AI to detect false and manipulated identities. The rapid spread of manipulated video content poses growing risks to trust, security, and democratic processes, as falsified or synthetic identities can be used for fraud, disinformation, and impersonation. Public authorities, media organisations, and digital platforms require reliable methods to detect such content at scale. The FAKE-ID project addresses this challenge by supporting the identification of falsified and manipulated identities in video material. Stakeholders include security agencies, technology providers, and institutions responsible for safeguarding digital integrity. The objective is to improve the detection of deep-fake videos and manipulated identity representations to strengthen trust in digital media. The solution develops advanced video analysis methods that examine visual and temporal inconsistencies in facial movements, expressions, and image artefacts. Trained models analyse video streams to identify signs of synthetic manipulation under varying recording conditions. The project establishes robust evaluation frameworks and datasets to ensure reliability. The impact includes improved detection accuracy of manipulated videos, reduced risk of identity fraud, and enhanced resilience against disinformation. FAKE-ID contributes to safer digital environments and supports the development of trustworthy media verification technologies.

results.title: MASIRI – Multi-Agent Simulation for Integrated Energy and Mobility Systems
results.proposal: MASIRI – Multi-Agent Simulation for Integrated Energy and Mobility Systems. The integration of energy and mobility systems, such as vehicle-to-grid solutions, depends not only on technical optimisation but also on human behaviour and decision-making. Traditional system models often neglect how users’ experiences, preferences, and habits influence energy and mobility usage. The MASIRI project addresses this gap by exploring how behavioural insights can improve the design and regulation of integrated energy and mobility systems. Stakeholders include researchers, system designers, policymakers, and energy providers. The objective is to understand and simulate interactions between human behaviour and intelligent energy systems to optimise resource use. The solution develops a multi-agent simulation framework in which intelligent agents represent energy users with psychologically informed behaviour models. These agents interact within simulated vehicle-to-grid environments, allowing analysis of how different incentives, regulations, and system designs influence outcomes. The project improves understanding of behavioural dynamics, supports more realistic system modelling, and informs better policy and infrastructure design. MASIRI contributes to more efficient, user-centred, and resilient energy and mobility systems that align technical optimisation with real-world human behaviour.

results.title: RePAIR – Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Cultural Heritage Reconstruction
results.proposal: RePAIR – Artificial Intelligence and Robotics for Cultural Heritage Reconstruction. Archaeological artefacts are often discovered in thousands of fragments, making physical reconstruction a painstaking and time-consuming task that requires scarce expert skills. Many damaged artworks remain in storage for decades due to the effort required to restore them. results.title: ITERATOR – Automated Detection of Pores in Rocks
results.proposal: ITERATOR – Automated Detection of Pores in Rocks. Understanding the physical properties of rocks is essential for applications such as geothermal energy, fluid storage, and geological disposal, where porosity plays a decisive role. Stakeholders include geological research institutions and applied geoscience bodies that require reliable parameters to assess heat flow, fluid flow, and mechanical behaviour of rocks. The solution applies advanced image processing techniques to scanning electron microscopy images to semi-automatically detect and characterise pores. Algorithms identify pore boundaries and compute quantitative descriptors, including size distribution and shape metrics, which are then linked to geological and petrophysical models. The results significantly reduce manual effort and increase analytical consistency. The project enables more detailed and data-driven interpretation of rock properties, supporting improved modelling, better parameter estimation, and more robust decision-making in geoscientific applications.

Stakeholders include municipal authorities, urban planners, businesses, and civil society organisations. The objective is to provide a reliable, transparent emissions information system that supports informed decision-making at multiple urban scales. The solution integrates heterogeneous datasets into a single analytical platform, where automated methods extract activity patterns from areas of interest and infer corresponding emissions. By linking observed activity to emissions factors, the system generates timely and comparable emissions estimates across sectors such as transport, buildings, and industry. The pilot improves the granularity and responsiveness of emissions monitoring, supports evaluation of policy interventions, and enhances public transparency. It demonstrates how data-driven emissions intelligence can strengthen climate governance and accelerate urban decarbonisation strategies.

results.proposal: Carbon Intelligent City - Paris. The objective is to support evidence-based climate action through detailed, science-based emissions tracking at city, district, and street level. The solution combines diverse datasets within a unified platform, using advanced analytics to extract activity signals from defined areas of interest and infer associated CO₂ emissions. Satellite imagery and other data sources are analysed to detect operational activity, such as industrial site usage, and translate these signals into emissions estimates. The pilot improves transparency, enables continuous monitoring, and supports scenario analysis and impact assessment. It strengthens the city’s capacity to manage emissions strategically and engage stakeholders in collective climate action.

results.title: ELASTIC – Autonomous Transport Network for Urban Tramways
results.proposal: ELASTIC – Autonomous Transport Network for Urban Tramways. Urban public transport systems require precise situational awareness to ensure safety, reliability, and efficient operation, particularly as cities move towards higher levels of automation. The ELASTIC project addresses this need by developing a software architecture for advanced mobility systems, with a focus on autonomous and assisted transport networks. The pilot, deployed on Florence’s tramway network, involved transport operators, city authorities, and technology providers. The objective was to enhance real-time monitoring of tram operations, infrastructure, and surrounding environments without compromising passenger privacy. The solution integrates multiple onboard and roadside sensors, including cameras, radar, lidar, and inertial measurement units, installed on tram vehicles and at stops. Sensor data is processed in real time using perception and data fusion techniques to extract information on tram positioning, obstacle detection, and movement of vehicles and pedestrians. Visual data is analysed on the fly and immediately discarded, ensuring that no personal data is retained. The pilot demonstrates improved operational awareness, enhanced safety, and better incident prevention. It provides a scalable and privacy-preserving foundation for future autonomous public transport systems in urban environments.

results.proposal: Advanced Technology for National Topographic Map Updating - Increasing spatial data accuracy with AI in Finland. In Finland, the National Land Survey sought to improve the accuracy and timeliness of spatial data while reducing manual effort. The objective of the ATMU project was to enhance object detection and change recognition for buildings, roads, and watercourses at national scale. Stakeholders include mapping authorities, planners, and public agencies relying on high-quality geospatial data. The solution applies advanced image analysis techniques to aerial and satellite imagery, using deep neural models trained for object detection and change recognition tasks. Different model architectures are applied to specific features, supported by transfer and multitask learning approaches. By the end of the project, building detection achieved an accuracy of 97.9%, and 96% of building and road changes were correctly identified. The project delivers significant improvements in data accuracy, update frequency, and operational efficiency, providing a scalable foundation for modern, data-driven national mapping services.

results.proposal: Process Mining pilot for the support service and case management of the Diputació de Girona. Stakeholders include support staff, service managers, and public sector users relying on timely and effective assistance. The solution applies process mining techniques to system event logs generated by support and records management platforms. By reconstructing real process flows from operational data, the approach reveals hidden process variants, bottlenecks, and rework loops. The pilot uncovered more than 3,400 distinct process variants within workflows previously assumed to be linear. Simulation capabilities allow decision-makers to test “what-if” scenarios, such as changing escalation paths between support levels. The results indicate potential savings of up to 16,000 processing hours per year, alongside improved transparency and data-driven decision-making. The pilot demonstrates how process intelligence can significantly enhance efficiency, service quality, and organisational learning in public administration.

results.proposal: Artificial Intelligence in the Sorting of Municipal Waste as an Enabler of the Circular Economy. The “ZRR for municipal waste” research project addresses these challenges by modernising waste sorting operations to better support circular economy objectives. Stakeholders include municipal authorities, waste management operators, workers, and recycling industries seeking higher-quality secondary raw materials. The objective is to increase recovery rates, capture valuable materials from rejected waste streams, and improve working conditions within treatment plants. The solution introduces robotic sorting systems equipped with advanced perception and decision-making capabilities, integrated into existing waste treatment facilities. These systems analyse waste streams in real time to identify and separate materials with high precision, complementing or replacing manual sorting. Operational data is used to optimise performance under real plant conditions. Results from pilot deployments, including tests in Barcelona, show higher recycling yields, improved purity of recovered materials, and reduced landfill disposal. The initiative delivers environmental benefits, operational efficiency gains, and safer working environments, demonstrating the potential for scalable, technology-enabled circular waste management.

The system integrates mobile interfaces, social networking features, and health-related data sources. The project demonstrates improved user engagement, more effective behaviour change support, and scalable delivery of personalised wellbeing services, contributing to better quality of life and reduced long-term pressure on health and care systems.

results.title: iMaging Project - WITOIL Oil spill detection service
results.proposal: iMaging Project - WITOIL Oil spill detection service. As part of the EU-funded iMagine project, the EyeOnWater initiative addresses the challenge of ensuring the quality and reliability of citizen-contributed data for environmental monitoring. Through a smartphone application, citizens submit photographs of natural water bodies such as rivers, lakes, and seas to support large-scale observation of water colour and related ecological indicators. Key stakeholders include citizens, environmental scientists, and research institutions that rely on consistent, high-quality visual data. The objective of the use case is to validate incoming images efficiently and at scale so that only suitable, scientifically usable photographs are incorporated into long-term environmental datasets. The service uses computer vision techniques to automatically assess the suitability of submitted images before they enter scientific workflows. Image segmentation and object detection models, including YOLOv8, are applied to identify whether an image contains a water body and to detect obstructions or irrelevant content. The models are trained on a labeled dataset of more than 10,000 images categorized into different quality classes. The validation pipeline is integrated into the mobile application backend, enabling near real-time processing and automated decision-making on image acceptance or rejection. The automated validation process significantly improves the consistency and reliability of citizen science data while reducing the need for manual review. Real-time filtering ensures that only high-quality images are added to long-term water colour datasets, increasing their scientific value and usability. The approach enhances scalability by allowing large volumes of submissions to be processed efficiently, supports faster data availability for researchers, and improves the user experience by providing immediate feedback on submissions. Overall, the solution strengthens the contribution of citizen science to environmental monitoring and ecological research.

results.proposal: iMaging Project - Ecosystem Monitoring at EMSO Sites by Video Imagery. This use case addresses these needs by supporting ecosystem monitoring at subsea observatory sites, involving marine researchers, infrastructure operators, and data scientists, with the objective of improving real-time understanding of marine environments. The solution is implemented through a video-based monitoring service that processes underwater imagery using deep-learning models for object detection and quality filtering. Deployed across EMSO sites including Obsea, the Azores, and SmartBay, the service identifies marine species, flags low-quality footage, and detects notable events such as prawn burrows, converting unstructured video into standardised, analysable datasets. Integrated data pipelines deliver near-real-time outputs to researchers and support reuse across observatories. The approach significantly reduces manual workload, improves consistency of observations, and enhances the timeliness and scale of ecosystem monitoring. It strengthens biodiversity assessment, supports long-term environmental research, and provides a scalable foundation for data-driven marine science.

results.title: ADMAIES Project (Improving administrative decision-making through the use of AI, experimentation, and sandboxes)
results.proposal: ADMAIES Project (Improving administrative decision-making through the use of AI, experimentation, and sandboxes). Public administrations increasingly rely on complex decision-making processes that must balance efficiency, transparency and legal certainty. However, limited experimentation spaces and unclear governance frameworks often slow responsible innovation. The objective of the ADMAIES project is to explore how experimental approaches, including regulatory sandboxes, can support the responsible integration of analytical technologies into administrative decision-making. The implementation is led by academic researchers and focuses on designing, testing and evaluating decision-support tools within controlled environments. results.proposal: AMS Berufs Infomat -  personalized career advice for job seekers. results.title: Clean Air Optimisation in Madrid Metro
results.proposal: Clean Air Optimisation in Madrid Metro. Madrid Metro sought to improve air quality while optimising energy consumption. This use case involves the metro operator, passengers, and technology providers, with the objective of dynamically managing ventilation to maintain high air quality standards. The system integrates with existing ventilation infrastructure and continuously adapts to changing conditions such as passenger density and external air quality. Passengers benefit from a healthier environment, while the operator gains a more sustainable and responsive infrastructure management approach.

For administrators, ParticipApp offers comprehensive dashboards to monitor participation, track emerging trends, moderate contributions, and measure engagement and impact. It allows barcode scanning for instant product safety checks and simplifies the submission of detailed hazard reports, including photos and descriptions, which are standardised for seamless use by regulatory authorities. Technologically, the app leverages familiar mobile, cloud, and database infrastructure, providing a scalable and user-friendly solution without requiring specialised equipment. It is designed with full interoperability in mind, adhering to the European Interoperability Framework at legal, organisational, semantic, and technical levels, ensuring seamless integration with national and transnational market surveillance systems. By increasing transparency, accountability, and public engagement, the Virtual Market Assistant strengthens trust between citizens and regulatory authorities, streamlines hazard reporting, and accelerates the removal of unsafe products from the market.

Its flexible architecture allows future expansion, including additional functionalities, AI-assisted workflows, and integration of new datasets, while ensuring alignment with organisational values and operational goals. The application reflects a user-centred design approach, incorporating continuous feedback, training, and co-creation with staff to maximise usability, trust, and impact.

results.title: RehaPlus: AI-Powered Identification of Complex Rehabilitation Cases in Public Health Insurance
results.proposal: RehaPlus: AI-Powered Identification of Complex Rehabilitation Cases in Public Health Insurance. The statutory accident insurer BG ETEM introduced RehaPlus to improve the early identification of complex rehabilitation cases requiring intensive case management. Previously, such cases were often detected late through manual reminders, leading to delayed interventions, higher treatment costs and longer recovery times. RehaPlus applies explainable machine learning models to continuously monitor case data and flag potential high-risk cases weeks earlier than before. This has replaced the outdated manual reminder process with proactive, automated monitoring, while ensuring case officers remain in control of final decisions. The result is improved efficiency, fewer documents to screen or complete, earlier interventions, and better recovery outcomes for insured workers. Since going live in 2021, RehaPlus has delivered high user satisfaction, with more than 90 per cent of staff rating it positively for improving efficiency and quality of work. Built with open-source components such as Python, XGBoost, Scikit-learn, Pandas and Docker, the solution is lightweight, explainable, cost-efficient and fully compliant with GDPR. Its modular architecture makes it portable across infrastructures and scalable to other social accident insurers, with the first reuse planned for 2026. By combining automation with transparency and human oversight, RehaPlus demonstrates how AI can create both internal efficiency gains (G2G) and societal value (G2C) through better rehabilitation outcomes.

results.company: Technical University of Applied Sciences Wildau
results.title: Pepper robot as an examination assistant and source of information
results.proposal: Pepper robot as an examination assistant and source of information. Pepper at TH Wildau is a deployed library assistant, based on SoftBank’s humanoid platform and the NAOqi software stack. The project adapts Pepper for a 24/7 academic library, where access is card-controlled outside staffed hours. The robot greets visitors, answers common questions, guides users to locations across three floors, gives short tours, and demonstrates equipment such as the printer–scanner–copier. The solution combines scripted behaviors with a lightweight NLP pipeline. Behaviors are authored in Choregraphe/Python as modular, rule-based flows for gestures, tablet prompts, and navigation sequences. Speech interaction uses an open, componentised chain: automatic speech recognition (speech-to-text), intent and entity extraction for library domains (orientation, lending, services, events), response generation from curated templates and FAQs, and text-to-speech. The team prioritises transparent, locally hosted components over closed assistants. For perception and mobility, Pepper uses classical robotics methods for localisation and path planning; autonomous driving is complemented by tablet teleoperation for safety and elevators. Two units are operated: “Wilma” serves in the library as a mobile information point; “Bernd” is used in the RoboticLab for testing and training. Content and dialogs are updated iteratively, with analytics from interactions feeding refinements to intents, utterances, and tour scripts.

results.company: Italian National Institute of Social Security (INPS)
results.title: Text Simplification for Citizens with GenAI
results.proposal: Text Simplification for Citizens with GenAI. Clear and accessible communication is essential to ensure that citizens can effectively navigate public services. INPS—Italy’s National Institute of Social Security and the largest welfare institution in Europe—serves approximately 45 million citizens through nearly 500 digital services related to pensions and welfare. The clarity of these service descriptions plays a critical role in guaranteeing equitable access and a positive user experience. To address the challenges of bureaucratic language, INPS has launched a structured simplification program aimed at making content understandable to users with a middle school level of education. Over 700 texts have been manually simplified so far, resulting in an increase in the average Gulpease readability score from 57 to 64—a substantial improvement in accessibility. However, this manual process is labor-intensive, requiring specialised linguistic and legal expertise, and is not easily scalable. The need for plain language in public administration has long been acknowledged in Italy. A 2002 directive still in force emphasizes that “all texts produced by administrations must be designed and written to be understood by those who receive them.” Yet institutional communication remains overly formal and complex, hindering citizens’ ability to fully access and understand critical services. While simplification improves transparency and public trust, it must also preserve the legal precision required for official documentation. To overcome these limitations, INPS has integrated Large Language Models (LLMs) into its simplification workflow, developing a semi-automated system—operating in a human-in-the-loop model—that is both scalable and efficient. This solution can process high volumes of content while ensuring readability, semantic accuracy, and legal compliance. A dedicated evaluation framework was introduced to measure key aspects of the output, including readability, fluency, and content preservation. User testing further validated the approach, confirming the quality of AI-generated content in comparison to both the original and manually simplified texts. The AI-based system delivers expert-level results in a fraction of the time and cost required by manual processes. It enhances INPS’s operational efficiency, standardizes quality across service pages, and ensures that content remains accessible and legally sound. Human oversight guarantees accuracy and relevance, while integrated metrics provide transparency and guide ongoing optimization. A large-scale user study involving A/B testing with 1,620 participants confirmed the model’s effectiveness. AI-generated texts were preferred in over 70% of cases when compared to the original versions and outperformed them across all measured dimensions: fluency (+14.1%), readability (+13.5%), clarity (+11.1%), and engagement (+12.3%). The AI semplified versions outperformed also the corresponding human simplified texts across all the qualitative metrics. Citizens are the ultimate beneficiaries of this transformation. By simplifying complex institutional language, INPS reduces barriers to access for individuals with limited language skills, lower educational attainment, or reading difficulties. More inclusive communication strengthens transparency, encourages greater civic engagement, and builds trust between citizens and institutions. Beyond INPS, this AI-driven approach has strong potential for adoption in other sectors where complex language limits accessibility—such as healthcare, legal services, taxation, and social welfare. Its ability to adapt to diverse regulatory and linguistic contexts makes it a powerful tool for modernising public communication across government systems. In summary, the integration of LLMs into INPS’s content simplification strategy demonstrates how generative AI can enhance accessibility, efficiency, and trust in public services—delivering clear, comprehensible, and citizen-centered communication at scale.

results.company: Italian National Institute of Social Security (INPS)
results.title: Document Review in Service Requests powered by Gen AI
results.proposal: Document Review in Service Requests powered by Gen AI. INPS provides services where users are required to submit various types of documents to support their requests, which must undergo a thorough review to verify their validity. This process involves the manual review of millions of documents annually by operators, all within a constrained timeframe. This involves a wide variety of documents (invoices, contracts, travel tickets, payment receipts, etc), making the process highly time-consuming and error prone. The goal of the project was to streamline and enhance the verification process through AI-powered automation, reducing manual workload, ensuring consistency in checks, and improving response times for citizens. To address these challenges, an innovative solution has been developed, integrating on-premise Generative Artificial Intelligence technologies designed to support operators in document analysis activities. Key features of the solution include: • Automatic classification of documents based on both type and content; • Data extraction and verification, with automated comparison between the information in the documents, the tender requirements, and the associated metadata; • Smart visualization of AI-extracted fields, with automatic highlighting directly within the document for easy reference; • Decision support, offering a detailed summary of the extracted data, flagging any discrepancies, and assisting with manual validation. This solution significantly streamlines the verification process, reducing manual effort and increasing both the speed and consistency of checks, delivering concrete benefits to both staff and citizens. Moreover, the system’s ability to adapt and learn from new data ensures continuous performance improvement, supporting progressively more effective procedure management. The solution aims to deliver benefits for both operators and citizens. Overall, the implementation of Generative AI has proven to be a transformative step in modernizing the document verification process, setting a strong foundation for future innovation and scalability. The next objective is primarily to adopt this solution for the other services within the INPS system.
results.memo: Proceed. Document Review in Service Requests powered by Gen AI is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: Robic: Inclusive AI for Special Learning
results.proposal: Robic: Inclusive AI for Special Learning. This pilot project explores the feasibility and educational impact of an AI-supported social robotics solution in a special education setting. Implemented at Colegio Gaudem in Madrid, the initiative aims to enhance the personal, cognitive, and emotional development of students with special educational needs through personalised, structured interactions using Inrobic Clinic and Inrobic Virtual. Between November 2024 and March 2025, 300 sessions were conducted involving 28 students, mostly in group formats. High satisfaction scores were reported by educators and families, with notable improvements in communication, motor skills, and engagement across subjects like math and language. Students responded positively, treating the robot as a peer and showing increased motivation. Teachers integrated the solution smoothly into their practices, and families expressed strong interest in its continuation. Early findings support the value and effectiveness of AI-assisted robotics in promoting inclusive and adaptive education.

results.title: UNA - Chatbot for process enterprise registration
results.proposal: UNA - Chatbot for process enterprise registration. Chatbot is available 24/7 and thus able to make communication between citizens and the state accessible and friendly. UNA was available on both the website of the Register of Enterprises as well as on the Facebook page as part of the Facebook messenger application. According to the first performance indicators, 44% of the questions asked on UNA were considered to be general of nature and easily taken care of by the Chatbot.

results.title: Datakalab - Covid-19 Mask wearing  detection In some French cities
results.proposal: Datakalab - Covid-19 Mask wearing  detection In some French cities. During the Covid-19 pandemic, the use of surveillance cameras was authorised to monitor whether passengers on public transport respected the requirement to wear masks. However, France’s data protection watchdog CNIL called out the practice, saying it was not governed by any legal framework and was therefore illegal. The authority began a three-month test of its software from French tech company Datakalab this week at the Chatelet-Les-Halles station in the heart of Paris, normally used by about 33 million passengers per year. Monitors will have access to a dashboard with the proportion of riders believed to be wearing masks. The plan was making mask wearing mandatory in public transport from May 2019. AI was regarded to be able to supplement enforcement agents in stations. Still, CNIL, the government body in charge of privacy, raised concerns that this type of technology carries a risk that the identity of the people being analyzed could be reconstructed.
results.memo: Proceed. Datakalab - Covid-19 Mask wearing  detection In some French cities is classified as minimal. No prohibited practice, no Annex I or III ground and no transparency trigger found: minimal risk, voluntary codes only.

results.title: ITI - Chatbot for Statistics Estonia
results.proposal: ITI - Chatbot for Statistics Estonia. The virtual assistant called ITI, created in collaboration with the Estonian start-up AlphaBlues (now AlfaChat, part of a larger company), shared knowledge regarding the population of Estonia, the size of the pay gap, average wages and consumer price changes, and many other things. Iti also assisted the data provider, whose typical questions are related to activities in the electronic data submission portal and filling in questionnaires. If Iti did not know the answer, it would redirect the query based on its content to either the customer support specialist of the data provider or the user of the statistics. Iti obtained its knowledge from the questions sent through online chats over one year and gets wiser with every query. ITI helped to find information faster thus allowing the customer support of Statistics Estonia to focus on answering more complicated and detailed queries. ITI is know not in use as it has been substituted by Bürokratt, the Estonian national chatbot.
